title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: It was observed that no employees present during today’s inspection had completed a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) course. A CFM should be present at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM is able to oversee proper employee hygiene, food handling practices, safe holding temperatures, and overall reduces the risk of food-borne illness. Ensure a CFM is present on staff during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.[C]

citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed beef/steaks to be improperly thawing outside of cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and beef was moved to walk in cooler. Ensure when thawing, any TCS item is placed in a cooler or under running water.
citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed onions in dry storage room to be resting directly on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from floor and placed at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food items is at least 6 inches off of ground.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed clean utensils to not be inverted. Discussed with PIC, utensil were put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process and inverted. Ensure any cleaned utensils are inverted to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed kitchen line prep coolers to be soiled with food debris under lids. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed leak to be present under fan unit in walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. A container was placed under leak to contain it, ensure walk in cooler is working to meet manufactures standards.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handler training to be missing for some members of staff. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff members will receive license. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the required food handlers training within 30 days of hiring. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed CFM on duty to not have allergen training completed. DIscussed with PIC, training will be completed. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, PIC will ensure a certified food manager is brought in. Ensure a certified food manager is available within the facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed kitchen hand sinks to be missing paper towels. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm Cl. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Triple sink will be used until dish machine is serviced. Ensure dish machine is sanitizing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed open juices to be stored in a cooler at 70F. Discussed with PIC, cooler is observed to be down and items were discarded. Any juices in the future will be stored in walk in cooler. Ensure any TCS item is cold held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There is observed to be soil residue accumulation in a container that holds packages of hard boiled eggs and on the outside of two containers of Barbecue sauce in the walk-in cooler. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that they will clean the container holding the eggs and the containers of Barbecue sauces will be discarded. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
There were multiple food items that were observed to be held past the 7-day date-marking: 

1. A container of cups of tartar sauces that are made in-house that had a date of 6/15. 
2. A container of cheddar garlic mashed potatoes that had a date of 6/17. 
3. A container of turkey gravy that had a date of 6/15. 

CORRECTED- These food items were discarded by the PIC. Ensure that dates on foods are routinely checked and the food is discarded if held past the 7-day allowed date-marking.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- The gaskets of the batter station cooler. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The fan covers of the three-door cooler and the milk cooler. 
5. FIRST REPEAT- The bottom of the cooler across from the batter station. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no soap to be available at the back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed multiple items to be resting within back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from hand sinks are. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used to wash hands.

(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed water bottles to be stored outside of store. Discussed with PIC, bottles will be moved back inside. Ensure water bottles are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to coming apart in the bathroom hand sinks. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop sink. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a single use 2 oz cup stored in powdered sugar and cinnamon sugar. CORRECTED- the cup was removed and discarded. The person in charge (PIC) stated they are actively reminding employees to not use scoops without handles in ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure all RTE foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

comment:

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
SECOND REPEAT: The CFM has not completed Allergen Training. Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. Certified Food Protection Managers at high risk establishments must complete Allergen Awareness training and test within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there wasn't a certified food protection manager available. A CFPM arrived shortly after the start of the inspection to correct the violation. Person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the facility will work to get the main cook food manager certified. Ensure that there is always at least one employee who is food manager certified during operating hours.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were a handful of mouse dropping observed on floor of the dry storage area. Shown to the PIC and discussed routinely cleaning of storage area. Ensure that the area is cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of droppings.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There were two containers of bread loafs stored on the floor of the indoor building. The PIC mentioned that the breads are normally stored off the floor and in a different area. Ensure that bread loafs are stored at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. Discussed with the PIC that a sanitizer solution shall be present to sanitize all food contact surfaces. The facility will use a sanitizer bottle for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present during all hours of operation.

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

comment:
None of the employees working at the time of the inspection could show proof of food handler certificates. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There were various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods stored inside of the prep cooler that were probed between 45F - 50F. These items included salads, mayonnaise, cheeses, meats, and dressings. The PIC mentioned that the cooler had recently been restocked at 1:30pm after lunch. The facility was instructed to place bulk items back into the walk in cooler and to use time control for the items at the top of the cooler. The facility will discard items after four hours. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below. Will follow up on July 6, 2026.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler had an ambient temperature of 50F. See violation #22 for further details. Ensure that the prep cooler is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow up on July 6, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced or replaced.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The service prep cooler did not contain an internal thermometer to measure the ambient temperature. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that an internal thermometer is available to accurately measure ambient temperatures of cold holding equipment. Will follow-up on July 6, 2026 to see that the unit has a thermometer available.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: THIRD REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). An employee stated that they are currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: All three employees were observed to not use a barrier when turning off the faucet of the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The employees were educated on using a barrier when turning off the faucet to prevent contamination to clean hands. Ensure that staff are educated on proper handwashing procedures to prevent contamination to clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- An employee was observed to handle raw chicken with their gloves, wipe their gloves off with a towel, and then touch tongs and other items with the same gloves. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that after handling raw chicken, the gloves need to be discarded and hands should be washed before donning gloves again. 

An employee was observed to use their gloves to make a sanitizer bucket with bleach and touch the triple sink faucet handles, then proceed to prepare food. CORRECTED- The employee was educated to discard their gloves, wash their hands, and don gloves again before preparing food. 

Ensure that employees are properly educated on when to wash their hands. A handout was given that is translated to Thai and it is highly recommended to post this in the facility.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The ice scoop was observed to have the handle in direct contact with the ice in the ice machine. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and an employee to have the handle of the ice scoop stored above the ice. The scoop handle was moved to be stored above the ice. Ensure that food is protected from contamination from bare-hand contact by having the scoop handle stored above the food.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. title: Food separated and protected.

citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

3. The bottom of the three-door cooler.

comment:

citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that staff remember to wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

comment: The baffles of the ice machine was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. PIC began dumping the ice from the ice machine to get it cleaned. title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:

Duct tape is not considered smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Ensure this is completed by the next routine inspection (at least 90 days from now).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: A few spatulas were observed torn creating little crevices on the surface. Discussed with PIC. The spatulas were discarded. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:

3. (REPEAT) Inspector observed the accumulation of dust, rust, and soil on the shelvings in the dish room. Ensure that these accumulations are shelvings are routinely monitored and cleaned.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed a leakage and rots in the ceiling on the far end of the dry storage area by the walk-ins in the basement. PIC was made area. PIC informed inspector that a technician is scheduled to come and do the repairs soon. Ensure that this is repair to ensure that the facility is in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training certification during today’s inspection. PIC said that those documents were locked away and they had no access to them. Inspector told PIC to have copies of certifications in a folder accessible for inspection purposes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify allergen training due to the restricted Acces to paperwork at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the paperwork is provided or the training done to be in compliance. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed dumped ice in the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware. And education was carried out. Ensure that employees are aware to use all handwashing sink for handwashing purpose only at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

The sanitizer was retested after the repairs and it tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the sanitizer in the dish machine is always tested and maintained within an appropriate concentration range at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The standing cooler in the kitchen was observed not holding the appropriate temperature range.  PIC was made aware. PIC informed inspector that the food items in the cooler were placed in the cooler on 6/14/2026 (two days prior to the inspection). The food items in the cooler was discarded. The cooler was repaired and the ambient temperature collected was 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was no hanging thermometer present in the standing cooler in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC provided a hanging thermometer for the cooler. Ensure that there is always a hanging thermometer present in all cold holding units at all times.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. An accumulation of grease and dust were observed dangling from the hood filters in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that the third-party company that usually clean the hood were scheduled to be at the facility a couple days before but canceled due to scheduling conflicts. Hence, they are scheduled to be in the facility within a day.  Ensure that the filters are cleaned to avoid the contamination of food.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The PIC stated a cooler has not been obtained. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/29/26. Contact the inspector as soon as the new cooling unit has been obtained to verify proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed a staff member wash their hands, then fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided. Ensure the use of a barrier after completing hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed ground beef at 119F. CORRECTED- it was verified that the food had been in the unit less than 4 hours, and the unit was turned from “1” to “3”. Food was then observed to have an internal temperature of 140F. Ensure hot holding units are always set so that hot temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods have an internal temperature of 135F or higher.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed TCS foods in the standing cooler (nearest the door) to have internal temperatures between 45-50 (hotdogs and hamburgers respectively). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit less than 4 hours were moved to a working cooler or implemented under time as control (items are to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Items housed in the unit over 4 hours were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods (including all animal proteins, house made products using mayo as an ingredient, cut tomatoes, and shredded lettuce) are cold held at or below 41F, or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. [P]

citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the beginning of this inspection there was not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and called the owner during the inspection. They arrived to correct the immediate violation. They were instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section.

1) A container of salsa in the walk-in cooler was observed with an incorrect date. The cook stated that the sticker would not come off when washed. 2) A container of pico was observed without a date marking in the walk in cooler. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and corrected during this inspection. Ensure that date marking is correctly managed by all employees in the facility at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A bag of onion were observed stored on the floor in the kitchen. The cook was shown and the onions moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to prevent possible pest concerns and contamination from the floor.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The sink in the bar area is leaking from both the faucet connection as well as the drain pipe. The PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all plumbing fixtures in the facility are maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee’s can of sprite was observed in the standing cooler next to open salsas ready for service. The PIC was consulted and instructed to store employee foods separate from foods intended for consumers moving forward. Store employee belongings in such a way so that there is not a concern for contamination of consumer foods.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
The metal board sealing the door of the walk-in cooler was observed not properly sealing the gap under the walk-in cooler door. This gap was observed during facility’s routine inspection on 6/4/2026. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the  gap will be fixed allowing the door to seal cooler properly. 
Ensure that this gap is closed to avoid food spoilage and a damage to the cooling unit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a metal scrubber stored in the basin of the hand sink next to the ice machine. The person in charge (PIC) was informed and the scrubber was removed. Ensure staff are using the triple sink or utility sink to scrub dishes and never the hand sinks. This violation was corrected on site.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed the egg rolls to be stored in direct contact with a washing cloth. This cloth was heavily saturated with water. The PIC stated that the egg rolls release water as they thaw and become soggy in the metal container. Inspector recommends using a straining insert to keep the egg rolls dry and prevent cross-contamination. Ensure egg rolls are stored properly to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.13 Linens and Napkins, Use Limitation. LINENS, such as cloth napkins, may not be used in contact with FOOD unless they are used to line a container for the service of FOODS and the LINENS and napkins are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new CONSUMER.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed a knife to be stored in the crevice between the prep cooler and stainless steel countertop. The PIC was informed that this crevice is not easily cleanable. Therefore, the knife cannot be stored here. The inspector recommends purchasing a magnetic knife block to attach to the shelf of the prep cooler for safe storage. The knife was moved to the dish area during today’s visit. This violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak coming from the hand sink to the left of the grill. The leak is coming from the connection between the PVC plumbing and the metal sink basin. Wastewater leaks pose a cross-contamination hazard, especially located so close to the cook line. A follow-up will be conducted on Monday, June 22, 2026 to ensure the leak has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.

CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection and these violations were corrected during the inspection. The CFPM was observed to educate staff on these violations. citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

Ensure that staff are educated on when to wash hands and on proper handwashing procedures. Further education will be conducted regarding handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The trash can in the kitchen was observed to be in front of and obstructing the only handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the employees. The trash can was moved to another spot. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
There were multiple instances where food was observed to be in a package that exposed it to potential contaminants: 

1. There was observed to be raw meat stored directly in a grocery bag. CORRECTED- The raw meat was switched to be in another container. 
2. There was observed to be an open can of tomato purée, an open can of jalapeños, and an open can of chipotle peppers. CORRECTED- These food items were moved into another container. 

Education was conducted with the PIC. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and food should never be stored directly in them. After the can of an acidic food item is opened, the can is no longer meant to protect the integrity of its contents and the food item can be adulterated. Ensure that food is stored in a container that does not expose it to adulteration or to potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was observed to be raw, shelled eggs above yogurts and other ready-to-eat food items in one of the double-door standing coolers in the kitchen. In the same cooler, there was also observed to be raw sirloin tip on top of a pan of cooked meat. CORRECTED- The raw eggs and the raw sirloin tip were moved to be on the bottom shelf of the cooler, below other ready-to-eat food items. A storage order handout that is in Spanish was provided and an English one is already posted on a cooler. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were multiple containers of food that were observed to not have a cover on them in the double-door standing coolers. This was discussed with the PIC. Saran Wrap is observed to be used to cover some of the containers and it was recommended continue this practice with all of them. Ensure that food is stored in a package, a covered container, or is wrapped to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
comment: There was a pan of cheese sauce that was probed to be at a temperature of 97F on the steam table. The employees stated that it was being reheated on the steam table. CORRECTED- The PIC and the employees were educated that reheating should be done on the grill or the stove to make sure that the food item reaches a temperature of at least 165F. The cheese sauce was placed on the stove to be reheated. The probe thermometer was observed to still be in the package and the PIC was educated that this should be in use to make sure the reheated food is reaching the correct temperature. Steam tables are not typically made to be able to rapidly reach a temperature of 165F, which is why they should not be used for reheating. Ensure that food is being reheated to at least 165F before being placed in hot holding.
citation_text: 3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of cheese sauce, a container of cooked meat, and a pan of cooked meat that were observed to not have any date-marking on them. CORRECTED- The employee stated that the food items were made yesterday and the foods were date-marked. Date-marking was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods that are kept for more than 24 hours are date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day. Further education will be conducted regarding date-marking.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The bleach that was being used to make sanitizer buckets was observed to be a bleach that is not EPA-Registered and is meant for “whitening and brightening”. Ensure that chemicals used for sanitizers are EPA-Registered and are safe to use on food-contact surfaces. Ensure that staff are educated on this.

Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed multiple buckets in the hand sink obstructing handwashing. Education was carried out. The buckets were removed. Ensure that the hand sink is always available and accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

citation_text: 2-402.11 Effectiveness. (A) Except as provided in (B) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair, that are designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

Education was provided on proper cold holding expectations, and facility will be using a Time as Control for the vegetables. PIC is unsure if this will be a permanent addition, however inspector provided facility with paperwork and education if facility would like to continue. Ensure any TCS item is being cold held below 41F or discarded after 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and items were dated. Ensure after 24 hours, any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed TCS item in walk in cooler to be resting on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any TCS item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.

(A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

[Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

PIC was informed that the sink should be serviced. Inspector will Follow Up to see that this handwashing sink is dispensing hot water. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are equipped to provide hot water.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a buildup of residues in the ice machine in the front area. PIC was informed that the ice machine should be cleaned. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that the ice machine is clean to sign and touch. Ensure that the ice machine’s food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items that were held beyond 7 days from their initial preparation date, per their datemark: sliced tomatoes, and hotdogs. PIC and Inspector discussed the 7-day rule (day 1 is date of opening or preparation of RTE or TCS foods, and day 7 is the date the food item should be either used or discarded). PIC made a plan for when TCS & RTE food should be prepped every week, and when it should be discarded, so as to align with the 7 day rule. This included preparing appropriate amounts of food to meet customer demand during those 7 days.

(A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.

Ensure that single-service and single-use articles are stored so that the food-contact surfaces are are protected form contamination, including through inversion, underneath a shelf, or inside their original packaging.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed raw chicken being stored above raw fish, and raw fish being stored above ready-to-eat foods (sauces and sliced peppers) in the 2-door stacked standing cooler and the bottom of the prep cooler. CORRECTED: The raw chicken was moved below the raw fish, and the ready-to-eat foods were moved to a separate part of the prep cooler so that they were not stored below raw meat. Inspector and PIC discussed keeping meat in separate doors of the prep cooler. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods, and that meats are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with the highest temperature on the bottom: fish & shrimp & eggs (135 F), whole intact beef and pork (145 F), ground beef and pork (155 F), and chicken and poultry (165 F) always on the bottom.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed several food items stored inside the 3-door standing cooler that were well above the cold holding temperature of 41°F. CORRECTED: PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a calibrated stem thermometer and either discarded items or moved items to working coolers: 
- items that were too warm and were prepared outside of the safe cooling time window were discarded; 
- items that were still cooling inside the safe cooling time window were moved to working coolers to continue cooling.
Items voluntarily discarded included: ~6 containers of raw chicken (47-52°F), 2 containers of raw steak (52°F), a 2 containers of cooked chicken (49-85°F), and 3 small containers of cooked potatoes (50°F).
PIC will work on getting the 3-door standing cooler repaired (see Violation #33) and will confirm with Inspector before resuming food service in the cooler. Ensure that all TCS Foods are cold held at temperatures of 41°F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed the 3-door standing cooler was no longer cooling or cold holding, with several food items measured at temperatures above 41°F. PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a stem thermometer and discarded or moved items as determined by temperature and cooling time (see Violation #22). Inspector will Follow Up to check the progress of repairing the 3-door standing cooler. title: Food handler training
comment:
At least four of the individuals working at the time of the inspection had expired food handler certificates. Be sure to get employees re-certified and compliant with food safety guidelines. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
The following plumbing repairs requirements were observed.
1. The left faucet on the triple sink was observed leaking. 
2. The faucet on the dump sink was observed leaking continuously.
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the plumbings is in good repair according to the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of grease build up was observed on the sides of the  fryers. 
2. The coving trim tile under the drink station was observed coming off the wall. 
3. Inspectors observed a hole in the trim edge of the door to the dry storage. 
Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspectors that the areas mentioned will receive the relevant corrections. Ensure that these corrections are made to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The deli/bakery walk-in cooler is observed to have ice accumulation on the ground and coming from the fan units. Ensure that the issue causing the ice build-up is repaired and that all the ice is scraped off to allow the floor to be smooth and easily cleanable. Due to this being a third repeat violation, a follow up is scheduled for 7/13/2026 to ensure that this violation is corrected. 

2. The shelf closest to the door on the left side of the deli walk-in cooler is observed to be significantly rusted on the bottom shelf. Ensure that this shelf is repaired or replaced to prevent contamination to food from rust. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
The following plumbing systems are in need of repair: 

1. There is a leak coming from the kitchen triple sink’s left faucet. 
2. There is a leak coming from the handles of the faucet of the kitchen handwashing sink. 

Ensure that these leaks are repaired. Plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The hood baffles. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The floor under the fryers in the kitchen of the deli is observed to have an accumulation of grease and food debris on them. Ensure that these floors are being regularly cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soil residues. 
3. The wall and baseboard under the kitchen triple sink. 
4. The dish shelves to the right of the kitchen triple sink. 
5. The floor to the right of and behind the Henny Penny in the kitchen of the deli. 

Ensure that physical facilities are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

A small amount of slime/mold is observed on the underside of the ice chute of the fountain drink machine. The inspector wiped the area to show the PIC. Ensure that this is maintained clean at all times moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any soap available at the hand washing sink near the dish room. A new bag of soap was added to the soap dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The machine was cycled and primed several times without a change in concentration. The facility was instructed to sanitize all dishes in triple sink until the dish machine can be serviced. Ensure that machine is serviced and sanitizing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration. Will follow-up 6/15/2026.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There were storage racks inside of the walk in cooler that contained a fuzzy debris on the outer surfaces. Shown to the PIC. Suggests that racks are taken outdoors to be power washed during down time. Ensure that racks are cleaned as frequently as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back food preparation area is nonfunctional. The PIC mentioned that the wiring has been stripped and was unable to provide water to the hand-sink. Ensure that all hand-sinks are functional and are able to meet the needs for adequate handwashing. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026 to ensure that the sink has been serviced.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite being if full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer solutions available. Discussed with the PIC and a solution was prepared and tested at 300ppm (quat). Violation corrected on site. Ensure that sani solutions are available to sanitize food contact surfaces during operational hours.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor directly in front of the utility closet is starting to bubble. The PIC mentioned that there hasn’t been any recent water damage to the facility. See that the flooring is lifted and repaired to ensure a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is ice build-up coming from the fans in the bakery walk-in freezer that is being caught on a green tray. Ensure that the issue is repaired and that the ice is removed. 
2. There is a slow leak coming from the ceiling of the bakery walk-in cooler. Ensure that this leak is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is missing coving to the right of the bakery walk-in freezer. Ensure that this coving is replaced and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The sealing on the bakery handwashing sink is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this is re-sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
