title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT - Inspector observed raw shell egg stored above cut tomato and mushrooms in the top of the prep cooler. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and the eggs were moved to the bottom of the prep cooler

Paper receipt was also observed on the cut tomatoes in the top of the prep cooler. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the receipt was removed. 

Ensure foods are protected from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing through the back door. The PIC was instructed to have the gap sealed with weather stripping. Ensure the gap is covered to prevent potential entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. The chest freezer gasket was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The fan blade covers in the walk-in cooler were observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The non-functional oven in front of the walk-in freezer was observed to have food debris and dust accumulations.
4. Food debris accumulation was observed on clean dishes at the dish area. 

The PIC was informed. Ensure the areas mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The shelves in the walk-in cooler were observed to be rusted. The PIC was instructed to have the shelves coated. Ensure the shelves are kept free of rust by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT - The following areas were observed to be in need of caulking/sealing:

1. Gaps were observed between the walls and the hand washing sinks.
2.  The caulking on the three-compartment sink in the kitchen was observed to be peeling off.

Openings between fixed equipment (sinks) and walls can allow for the entry of water and harborage of mold or bacteria. Ensure the gaps are sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple employees change tasks without hand washing. Discussed the need for ongoing education with the staff regarding times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure hands are washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils, after touching cell phones, when switching tasks between handling raw food and ready to eat (RTE) foods, before donning gloves, and after engaging in any tasks that may contaminate the hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a cup being used as a scoop, submerged in sugar. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the scoop with a gloved hand, and placed a scoop with a handle to be used for scooping sugar in a clean plastic bag. Ensure all ready to eat foods are handled with cleaned gloves hands, or utensils that have a clear differentiation between the hand contact surface and food contact surface.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach maximum heat plate temperature of 145, after 4+ cycles. Neither wash or rinse temperature gauges on the outside of the machine were moving during the cycle. Inspector directed the facility to use the triple sink to wash-rinse-sanitize all food contact surfaces until the dish machine has been repaired, and observed sanitizing at a minimum temperature of 160F. Inspector will return on 03/02/26 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple plates and bowls at the serving station stored with the food contact side upwards. CORRECTED- the plates were inverted after the inspector discussed the need for the food contact surfaces to either be covered or inverted when not actively serving to prevent contamination of the food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact and nonfood contact surfaces in disrepair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Two spatulas hanging in ready to use position on the cook-line were chipped around the perimeter. CORRECTED- spatulas were voluntarily discarded. 
2) The gaskets along the triple door cooler, as well as the warmer (next to the hood system) were frayed or fragmented.
Ensure utensils are checked for integrity to prevent contamination of food. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable. Gaskets should be replaced by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The condensers of the coffee machines contain an accumulation of soil debris.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The black, (3) segmented container holding ready to use utensils at the island across from the hood contains food debris. 
* Line item #2 was previously noted as violation #44, and has since been moved.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket. Inspector discussed proper mop storage with the PIC. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry, to prevent the growth of microorganisms.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair:
1) There is no caulking between the hand washing sink (in front of the office) and the wall.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine contains an accumulation of debris, and is fragmented or absent in multiple areas.
3) Coving between the floor and wall is peeling in the chemical storage closet (directly to the right of the entry).
Fixed equipment should be sealed to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) A tray of cooked dumpling was observed being stored underdressed raw chicken to cool. Education was carried out and the dumpling tray was removed. Ensure that proper storage order is practiced to avoid cross contamination. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Multiple soda nozzles were observed with soil accumulation. PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed water chestnuts being stored in the can after opening inside the prep cooler. Education was carried out. The chestnuts were placed in the appropriate storage container. Ensure that food items are stored appropriately to avoid contamination. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, therefore recontaminating their hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure that the hand washing procedures in the facility protect freshly washed hands from recontamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing prior to food service/handling. Education was conducted and they are instructed to review hand washing with employees. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several items in the storage area used for cleaned dishes are observed with remaining food debris or stickers on them. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to the dish area for re-cleaning to correct. They are instructed to review with all dish washers acceptable levels of cleanliness for the food contact equipment and conduct oversight as needed to ensure that the dishes are cleaned appropriately at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The two display coolers next to the ordering line were observed to be holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 49F-51F. When discussing with the PIC the items in the coolers were mostly placed into these coolers the day before the inspection in the morning. The only exception were the cannolis which arrived in the cooler approximately 5 hours prior to the inspection. The TCS items observed include multiple containers of ricotta filling, parmesan cheese, roast beef and several slices of cheese cake. The cannolis were allowed to remain until 4pm (six hours) and then be discarded. The remaining TCS items were discarded immediately to correct the violation. The PICs cleaned the filters on the front and back of the coolers to hopefully fix the overall issue. They also stated that they had contacted the owners who were having a company come to ensure that a more in depth maintenance scenario was not needed. The violation is considered corrected at this time with the caveat that the inspector will return in the morning to check if the remedial actions taken during the inspection were sufficient. The PICs are aware that tomorrow’s visit could ensure violations requiring follow ups in the future.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

Two employee cell phones were observed on a counter used for food preparation. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the phones moved to correct the immediate violation. Ensure employee possessions are stored in locations where contamination of foods or food contact surfaces is not a concern.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: There wasn’t any bleach available for responding to a vomit or diarrheal event. Discussed with PIC that bleach should be purchased in order to properly respond to a Norovirus event. The bleach must contain an EPA registration number. Ensure that bleach is purchased and available by the March 2, 2025 followup date.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the dish room lacked paper towels and also hand soap. Discussed with the person-in-charge that every handsink shall be stocked with the essentials for proper handwashing. Ensure that every handsink has warm running water, handsoap, and paper towels at all times. Will follow up on March 2, 2026.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a temperature measuring device available for the heat sanitizing dish machine. A temperature measuring device is necessary for ensuring that the machine is effectively sanitizing food contact surfaces. The person-in-charge mentioned that the facility will purchase thermo stickers in the near future. Ensure that a temperature measuring device is available to monitor sanitizing temperatures. Will follow-up on March 2, 2026.
citation_text: 4-204.115 Warewashing Machines, Temperature Measuring Devices. A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; and (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Various surfaces of the fryer were observed heavily accumulated with grease and food debris. Shown to PIC. The surfaces included inside of the fryer, the outer surface of the fryer, and underneath and around the walls of the fryer. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is an unused steam table stored across from the serving line, as well as an unused cabinet that is stored inside of the dry storage room. Discussed with PIC that items that are no longer needed for operation shall be removed from the premises. Ensure that items are removed, as this may create a harboring environment for unwanted pest and insects.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Food handler training
comment:
None of the employees, other than the only employee who holds a food manager certificate, could produce a copy of their food handler certificate. Discussed with the person-in-charge that all employees who handle clean dishes or food must obtain food handler certificates. Ensure that every employee has a food handler certificate on file by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed four dented cans in the dry storage shelf of the kitchen space. The PIC was informed and the cans were removed from use. In the future, set aside any dented cans and return to distributor. Dented and damaged cans can cause bacterial growth which leads to botulism contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of a cleaning:
1. The interior of the cabinet freezer on the cook line which stores the chicken fried steak.
2. The piping of the hood system above the fryers have accumulated oil and debris which is developing drips.
3. The interior of the hot box has an accumulation of food debris.

Ensure these surfaces are clean to sight and touch during the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
Inspector observed the following freshwater leaks in the facility:
1. The hand sink next to the dish area has a slow leak from the faucet handle.
2. The wall faucet with a hose connected has a considerable leak from the handle.

Ensure these plumbing concerns are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the mop head stored in the bottom of the mop bucket. This storage method does not allow for proper drip drying. The PIC was informed and stated that hanging hooks are located above the mop sink for proper storage. The PIC plans to reeducate staff on proper storage.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed the following areas to be soiled with food debris/soil:
1. The walls of the dish area
2. REPEAT - Floor under ice machines
3. REPEAT - Floor of walk-in freezer
4. Ice accumulation on floors, walls, and ceilings of walk-in freezer

Informed PIC that these areas are in need of a deep clean. Soil accumulation can promote both food-borne pathogen growth as well as potential pest harborage. Ensure floors in facility are cleaned frequently to avoid soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

The following canned food items were observed to have dents around their seams:

2. Whole peeled potatoes x2

CORRECTED - The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Ensure dented cans are removed from the shelf due to potential contaminants from exposure.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. Bottom of the 3-door cooler at the back storage area has soil accumulation.
2. Shelf for storing clean pots at the walk way has dust accumulation.
3. Shelf for storing clean plate at the salad bar has dust accumulation.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Employee was observed handling non ready to eat food from the prep cooler with their bare hands. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was provided. Ensure education about glove usage and  proper hand washing times are reviewed with new staff.
citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Sanitizer for food contact surfaces were observed to be outside of their recommended range in the following locations:
1) FIRST REPEAT The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer at the bar was observed to be at 100 ppm at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the sanitizer was remade and tested to be at 200 ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 
2) The kitchen’s Chlorine bleach sanitizer bucket was observed to be “bleaching out”- indicating too high of a concentration of bleach. CORRECTED- the bucket was diluted to 200 ppm.
Ensure that sanitizer is frequently tested using the facility’s test strips, and remade if not at the label-recommended concentration (200 to 400ppm for Quaternary ammonium and 50-200 ppm Cl for bleach).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the dry storage above the mop sink. CORRECTED- the item was identified as baking soda, and labeled accordingly. Ensure white powders (which may be easily mistaken for each other) are labeled once removed from their original container.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the kitchen prep counter. CORRECTED- the cloth was moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria with high water activity. Dry wiping cloths may be used, as long as there are replaced at least every 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food Handler certificates on file were observed to have been expired. Ensure Food Handler Certificates are renewed every 3 years and maintained on file. New employees should obtain a Food Handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIRD REPEAT- The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed multiple dishes to be resting in hand sink. Discussed with PIC, ensure hand sink is solely being used for hand washing. Dished were removed from hand sink.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking behind the kitchen sinks to be cracked. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: FIRST REPEAT - Ambient thermometer was not observed in the walk-in cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to provide an ambient thermometer. Ensure an ambient thermometer is available in the warmest part of the cooler by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The interior white coating of the microwave was observed to be peeling, exposing the underlying material. The PIC was informed. Ensure the microwave is repaired or replaced so that all surfaces are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The surface area around the soda machine nozzles was observed to have soil accumulation. The PIC was informed and instructed to clean the area. Ensure the surface area around the soda nozzles is maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. Corrective Action: The PIC was informed. Ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. The inspector will follow up on 02/23/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ceiling tile above the mop sink in the dry storage area was observed to be missing. The PIC was informed. Ensure the missing ceiling tile is replaced before next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ceiling tiles above the three-compartment sink and mop sink at the dry storage area were observed to be soiled. The PIC was informed. Ensure the ceiling tiles are replaced before next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket next to the mop sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure water from mopping is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was an open container of Barbecue sauce that was observed to be on a table in the kitchen and not in refrigeration. This sauce states to “Refrigerate after opening”. CORRECTED- The PIC discarded the Barbecue sauce and was educated to read labels of sauces. Ensure that food items that are Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a table that has pans holding it up. The PIC stated that the end of the table needs repaired. Ensure that this is repaired. 
2. The dish table to the right of the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking and needs re-sealed. 
3. The handle of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be broken and is in need of being replaced. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair and that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The small fan in the dish area. CORRECTED- The PIC removed it to be cleaned. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. The bottom shelf holding sauces and plates across from the pizza oven on the cook-line. There is observed to be an accumulation of dust and soil residue on it. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of pink soil accumulation on the front baffles of the ice machine. Empty the ice machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to have no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the recommend concentration and process for testing. Sanitizer was observed at a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is made and tested at a frequency to verify the proper concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed to go to cups of cheese sauce to be hot holding at 119F (verified via stem thermometer). CORRECTED- the 2 cups of cheese sauce were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Discussed long term solutions with the PIC (either using time as control [foods are used or discarded within 4 hours and marked accordingly], OR filling the bulk container to ensure the warm water is transferring to multiple sides of the container, and then moving it into a to-go container at the time of service. Ensure any temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are hot held at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple TCS food/ drink items without date marking (PIC verified they had been opened or prepared in days prior):
1) Orange juice at bar cooler
2) Salsa at kitchen standing cooler.
CORRECTED- both items were marked with the dates they were opened and prepared. Ensure all TCS foods being held over 24 hours are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed an in-use knife stored between a cutting board and wet cloth. CORRECTED- the knife was brought to the dish area for ware washing. Education about wet wiping cloth/ in use utensil storage was provided. Ensure all in use utensils are stored in a manner that prevents the contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.[C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of debris on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) Rust on the shelves in the walk in cooler 
2) Rust on the shelves to the right of the dish machine.
3) Dust on the monitor cords above the service station in the kitchen.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Shelves should be resealed or replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, which may contaminate ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple instances of coving not sealing to the wall:
1) Cracked tile beneath the dish machine
2) Loose coving on the South wall of the mop room.
Inspector showed these areas to the PIC, and education was provided. Ensure these areas are repaired by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Dead bugs were observed on the floor close to the emergency exit door and the side of the soda cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated it was due to the gaps in the door at the emergency exit. Ensure the dead bugs are cleaned from the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing through the corner of the emergency exit door at the back. The PIC stated an order will be put in to have the door well-fitted. Ensure the gaps are covered or sealed to prevent pests from entering the facility.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handwashing sink in the employee bathroom was observed to have gap between the wall and the handwashing sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the handwashing sink was caulked to the wall during the inspection. Ensure the gap is sealed so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A zesty orange sauce with “Refrigerate After Opening” was observed on the shelf in the dry storage. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Disinfectant spray and All purpose cleaner with bleach were observed on the ice machine close to the restroom. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the chemicals were voluntarily moved to the chemical storage area. Ensure poisonous or toxic materials are not stored above food or food equipment to prevent chemical contamination of food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Ice buildup was observed in the silver double door cooler. The PIC was instructed to have the cooler defrosted and cleaned to prevent more ice accumulation. Ensure the cooler is defrosted and cleaned to sight and touch by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the bar to only dispense cold water- the hot water faucet was nonoperational. All sinks designated for hand washing should be able to reach a minimum temperature of 85F. Inspector will return on 02/24/25 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contact an accumulation of debris:
1) The soda nozzle at the bar banquet room
2) 2 ladles handing in ready to use position with an accumulation of food debris on the food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- items were moved to the dish machine for ware washing. 
3) The water fountain in the hallway contains a significant amount of limescale and biofilm.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Inspector will return on 02/24 to check that line items 1 and 3 have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.  [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple pieces of equipment to be in disrepair:
1) The gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator are frayed.
2) The hinges along the pizza prep cooler are not holding the lid in place.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in need of physical repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The hand-sink at the (main) bar should be sealed to the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the West wall of the dry food storage is peeling.
3) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the wall directly to the right of the entryway of the chemical storage room. Coving is also peeling on the North side behind the water heater.
4) Coving in the Southwest corner of the dry storage is absent.
Items that cannot be moved easily for cleaning should be adhered to the wall. Seal items to wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple cell phones stored on the prep counter of the kitchen. Ensure personal belongings are kept in a designated area, separate from food and nonfood contact surfaces used to serve food to the public to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The sanitizer solution in the sani bucket at the deli bar area was measured at 0 ppm at the beginning of the inspection. Staff was educated and the sani bucket was remade measuring at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani bucket is monitored and changed at a regular frequency to ensure that food-contact surfaces are appropriately sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed washing hands and turning off the faucet without using a barrier. CORRECTED - The employee was educated by the inspector on proper handwashing procedures, and the person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to review proper handwashing practices with all employees. Ensure a barrier, such as a paper towel, is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Cleaned cooking utensils stored on the dish rack were observed to have food debris remaining on the surfaces. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the utensils were returned to the dish machine for re-washing. Ensure all cooking utensils are properly washed and maintained free of food debris before being stored for use.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Chicken in batter (a time/temperature control for safety [TCS] food) was observed in the walk-in cooler with date marking exceeding the maximum allowable holding time of 7 days. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the product was voluntarily discarded. Ensure date marks on TCS foods are routinely monitored and all TCS foods are discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Food debris accumulation was observed in the corners inside the cappuccino machine.
3. Food debris accumulation was observed at the bottom of the container used to store customers’ knives at the server station. CORRECTED - An employee placed the container in the dish machine for cleaning.
5. Soil accumulation was observed on the surface around the juice machine nozzles. CORRECTED - The surface was cleaned during the inspection.
7. Food residue accumulation was observed on the interior top surface of the middle microwave (of three stacked microwaves) across the cook line. CORRECTED - The microwave was cleaned during the inspection.
8. Food debris accumulation was observed on the top surface of the dish machine.

The PIC was informed and instructed to ensure the remaining areas are cleaned prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to be in need of repairs:

1. The left side of the handwashing sink at the order station needs to be caulked.
2. The bottom of the wooden shelf across the juice machine is bare and needs to be covered. 

The PIC was informed of the areas mentioned above. Ensure the areas mentioned above are repaired so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM was not available in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have a CFPM available at all times that the facility is in operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The only hand sink in the bar area was observed with a pitcher in it as well as a pair of blenders in front of it preventing access and use. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain the hand sinks in the facility accessible at all times. The items were moved to correct.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The faucet to the triple sink had a plastic bag wrapped around it to prevent a leak from spraying out. This is not an approved method to repair plumbing. The PIC was instructed to have a plumber repair the faucet prior to the scheduled follow-up. The follow up was pushed back from the usual three days because of the weekend and holiday.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) (REPEAT x2) On arrival the dish machine would not register on the inspector’s CL test strips. The quat test strips showed a little color change but was not sufficient for quat sanitizing either. The PIC was consulted and replaced the jug of quat concentrate with a CL concentrate jug. Once primed the registered correctly on both the inspector’s and facility’s test strips. 2) On arrival the sani bucket would not register correctly on the inspector’s test strips. The bucket was remade by staff to correct. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are at effective levels at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed multiple dead adult roaches on the floor in dry storage. PIC stated the Pest Control Log is in the main office. Advise updating log for Pest Control Provider. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned in their entirety to better monitor pest activity.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated that employees will sign the forms. The inspector provided blank copies to the PIC for each employee to sign. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/20/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
It was observed that the operator was unable to properly communicate basic food handling safety as related to the nature of the operations. The facility is acidifying rice, using time as control, and serving raw fish. These are incredibly high risk food handling behaviors that can quickly cause a food-borne illness outbreak if not properly controlled. Staff should be aware of cold and hot holding temperatures. Staff should be able to acknowledge that foods held at room temperature should be used or discarded within four hours. There should be documentation of the prior handling of sushi fish so that everyone is aware of parasite destruction prior to use. Operator should also be able to demonstrate basic hand washing and control how staff wash hands. 
Proper hand washing should be demonstrated by all staff at the follow-up inspection. 
Staff should be aware of safe food handling strategies such as time as control, parasite destruction, and proper cold/hot holding.

The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The operator then used soap for a two second scrub before turning off the faucet and reaching for paper towel. Finally, inspector interfered to demonstrate proper hand washing using a scrubbing timeframe of 10-15 seconds, rinse, dry with a paper towel, and used the towel to turn-off the faucet. SCDPH will be performing spot checks and education throughout the year to ensure proper hand washing.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature (Spicy Miso Mayo and Chili Spicy Mayo). Previously,  the operator mentioned keeping the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. Previously, the recommended solution of using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours was discussed. 
Today, sauces were again left on the counter and initially no one was quite aware of how long sauces stayed on the counter. Ensure that staff (there are only three) are educated on the proper time-as-control policy for house made sauces, spoons in water, tempura batter, and dry cloth on preparation counter. 
The aforementioned items should be removed/discarded and fresh created every FOUR HOURS. A Time As Control policy was created during the inspection. Discussed the bulk storage of sauces in the back cooler and movement of bulk product over 7 days.
Store homemade sauces, tempura batter, water and spoons, and dry cloth at room temperature for only FOUR HOURS.

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

comment: Inspector observed salmon in the standing double door cooler to be lacking date marking. The PIC stated the salmon was thawing. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are marked with the date they are brought into thawing in the future.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility was unable to provide Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. All employee who handle are serve food are required to obtain a Food Handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire. Inspectors provided a list of ANSI-approved programs that offer Food Handlers courses. Ensure all employees obtain a Food Handler Certificate by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed not using an adequate amount of soap and not properly rubbing hands together before rinsing and drying. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated and instructed to review proper handwashing procedures with employees. Ensure sufficient soap is used during handwashing and hands are vigorously rubbed together for at least 10 to 15 seconds before rinsing and drying with a single-use paper towel. Employees must also use a paper towel to turn off the faucet to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during this inspection is unaware of any completed allergen trainings at this facility. They recalled a previous conversation. title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The sanitizer test strips at the facility were observed to be wet and unusable. The PIC stated the test strips were accidentally dropped in water over the weekend and new test strips have been ordered. Ensure sanitizer test strips are available and usable at the facility at all times. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas were observed to have accumulations of dust and soil:

1. FIRST REPEAT - Dust accumulation was observed on the fan guard in the walk-in cooler.
2. Debris accumulation was observed on the walk-in cooler floor, especially under the food shelving.
3. Debris accumulation was observed in the corner area near the thermostats under the pizza oven.
4. Soil accumulation was observed on the food shelving in the walk-in cooler.
5. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the utensil holder container located by the three-compartment sink.
6. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the container used to store pizza cutters for customers at the server station.
7. Food debris accumulation was observed on the top surface of the oven. 
8. FIRST REPEAT - Soil accumulation was observed on the inside of the ice machine baffles.
9. Soil accumulation was observed on the soda gun holster.

The PIC was informed of the above conditions and instructed to clean the listed areas to sight and touch. Ensure all nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained free of dust, soil, and food debris accumulation to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Ice accumulation was observed on the walk-in freezer floor and behind the fan casing. The PIC was informed and instructed to remove the ice buildup to prevent further accumulation. Ensure all ice buildup is cleared and the walk-in freezer is maintained free of ice accumulation by the next routine inspection.

citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection did not have a CFPM and did not know of any others in the area that did. The normal person that does have one was off that day. Ensure that there are enough CFPM’s available to cover all shifts.

comment: Inspector observed paper plates used for catering service stored with their food contact surface facing upwards in the dry storage. comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.

Ensure physical facilities are maintained in proper repair.

comment: Inspector observed the hand contact surface of tongs touching a baguette. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the tongs into a separate container and discarded the baguette. Ensure all utensils are stored in a manner that prevents bare hand contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.

(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

4) The top interior of the microwave on the cook-line.
Ensure all equipment is maintained in proper repair. Repair or replace equipment by next routine inspection.

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a broken tile on the coving between the bakery room and drive thru area. Ensure repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.
