title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed the following food items being stored on the floor during inspection. 
1. Multiple lotus containers in cardboard boxes stored directly on the floor next to the double doors standing milk cooler in the back.
2. Multiple boxes of smoothie mix in cardboard boxes stored on the floor at the entrance of the dry storage area. 

PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that they are currently overstock at the moment however, they would ensure that the above mentioned food items would be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from splash, pest, and other forms of contaminations. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed mold accumulation to be present at the wall behind soda dispensing nozzles. Discussed with PIC, area will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevent mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. DIscussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager to present within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back room was observed to have a container of graffiti remover in it. CORRECTED- The inspector removed the graffiti remover from the sink basin and educated the PIC that handwashing sinks should always be maintained accessible at all times for employee use. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times and are only used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back room was observed to not have any paper towels at it. CORRECTED- An employee placed paper towels at the handwashing sink and the PIC was educated that all handwashing sinks should always have paper towels at them. Paper towels are necessary to allow for proper handwashing and the use of a barrier when turning off the faucet.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: The facility is observed to be selling hot dogs and tornadoes on roller grills during today’s inspection. The facility does not have a grease trap and the current one is concreted in. A new grease trap would need to be put in and the facility would need to be moved to a Medium Risk to allow these roller grill items to be served in the facility. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they will cease selling the hot dogs and they were all discarded during today’s inspection. A spot check will be conducted in the future to ensure that the equipment has been removed from the facility and that these roller grill items are no longer being sold.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the Bunn coffee machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. A follow up is scheduled on 11/3/2025 to ensure that the top of the inside of the Bunn coffee machine has been cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are frequently cleaned and are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were pre-packaged sandwiches that were observed to be in the cooler that did not bear any date-marking on them. This was discussed with the PIC. The PIC stated that the sandwiches arrive frozen and that they are placed into the cooler upon arrival. The PIC stated that these items were placed in the cooler on Tuesday. It was discussed with the PIC that these must be date-marked when put out and discarded if not sold within 7 days. CORRECTED- The sandwiches were date-marked during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: There were bottles of a bleach cleaning spray observed to be above boxes of cereal. CORRECTED- These boxes of cereal were moved to another shelf, where they were not exposed to contamination. Ensure that chemicals are never stored above food items. Food items should be protected from contamination during storage and display.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach that the facility is observed to be using for food-contact surfaces does not have an EPA Registration Number. A follow up is scheduled for 10/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has obtained an EPA-Registered Bleach. This was discussed with the PIC.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There were single-service forks and knives that were observed to be in cups with their food-contact surface being exposed to contamination. CORRECTED- The utensils were inverted by an employee and the PIC was educated that these should be displayed inverted to protect them from contamination. Ensure that single service articles and utensils are handled, displayed, and dispensed to protect the food-contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not register on the inspector test strips (CL sanitizer). The concentrate jug was observed empty and replaced. The new jug would not register on the test strips either, even when the jug itself was tested. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed pasta salad on an ice bath to be probed at 49F. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) stated the serving had been sitting out for approximately one hour, so the item was moved into a cooler. Education about ice baths occurred with PIC. Ensure items moved out during busy periods are either; held at or below 41F, are in an ice bath which surrounds the bottom and sides of the container, or time as control for food safety (TAC) is used.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items without date marking (caramel iced latte, milk, and sour cream). CORRECTED- the caramel iced latte is not currently being used, but education about date marking occurred. Milk and sour cream were both opened or prepared yesterday, and were marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all TCS items are date marked with the date they are opened, prepared, or thawed, and used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect control device over foods in hot holding. CORRECTED- PIC moved the light away from food storage. Ensure all pest control devices are installed away from areas of food storage and preparation to prevent insects from contaminating food.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer cloths being stored on counters in both the bar area and the kitchen. CORRECTED- education occurred with PIC and staff. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution when not in use to prevent the growth of pathogens on the cloth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed Certified Food Protection Manager’s (CFPM/CFM) Allergen awareness training to be expired. Allergen awareness training must be maintained and renewed every 3 years for facility’s CFMs. Ensure CFMs receive Allergen Awareness training by ANSI accredited program by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: The leak coming from the pipes under the triple sink is still present and has not been repaired. The PIC stated that they have a company coming this week to repair the leak. A follow up is scheduled for 10/24/2025 to ensure that the leak has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees on the cookline were not washing hands between removing gloves and putting on new ones. The employees on the cookline were educated that hands must be washed before donning gloves to initiate tasks that involve working with food. The PIC will be continuing to educated employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that employees always wash hands when switching gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Observed fried rice stored in a steamer from yesterday. The steamer was turned-off overnight and the food was temped at 50F today. Owner stated that he was going to discard the product, however, the facility should remove old food at the end of the night. Close properly to allow for proper opening. Leaving food overnight is a potential concern for pests. Leaving the old food also means the steamer may not be cleaned properly before being reintroduced to service. During the inspection, the rice was discarded.  
SCDPH will continue to spot check so this behavior of overnight storage is corrected. 
Food code does allow you to store hot food (over 135F) for an indefinite period of time (until quality becomes a concern). Either remove the food and clean containers nightly, or store at temperatures of 135F or above.

comment:
Inspector observed sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to not be reaching the sanitizing concentration benchmark set by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm of quaternary ammonia). 1) The facility has adjusted the water heater to reach 75F to allow quaternary ammonia sanitizer tablets to dissolve.
2) Facility has obtained unscented bleach (with an EPA registration number and label indicating use for food contact surfaces) to use as sanitizer. Facility has test strips for both sanitizers, so either are acceptable means of sanitation for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a large container of rice was stored on the cookline with an internal temperature of 50F. The PIC stated that the rice was removed from the cooler at 11 AM. When asked, the employees on the cookline stated that they were planning to put the rice back inside the cooler after lunch ended. The inspector explained the importance to the PIC and employees of keeping rice outside of the temperature danger zone (41-135F). They cannot leave large quantities of rice at room temperature for several hours and then put the unused rice back inside of the cooler for future use. The rice was put under a time-as-control policy and was discarded at 3 pm. The PIC and inspector discussed removing smaller quantities of rice that can be used during the lunch rush in the future. The inspector will follow-up on 10/21/2025 to check that only small quantities of rice are being removed from the cooler during lunch.

Nine roach sightings have been reported during the past month in the binder in areas including the bar, near the water heater, in the manager office, as well as in areas where ready-to-eat food is held. On 10/07/25 the pest control technician noted that the areas in the pest log had been chemically treated, and gel bait was applied.

Remove all conditions for harborage, including spilt food and beverages, as well as cardboard. Write the date on glue traps to better monitor pests. The frequency at which pest control is providing services to the facility is currently inadequate. Increase services to biweekly treatments. The inspector will return on 10/29/25 to check pest control management. title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.

2-103.11(O) Person In Charge. All of the portion of Code applying to knowledge of person-in-charge are applicable at this facility. The manager has a certified food protection certificate, however, is unable to demonstrate proper safe food handling and cannot impart knowledge onto staff. While language is a concern, the evidence of proper knowledge should be able to be seen in the cleaning and general maintenance of the facility. Overall, there is no apparent effort to maintain food as required in the Food Code. SCDPH has discussed the future operations of this facility and has the following solutions: 1) the facility will be upgraded to a Class I facility to insure multiple visits throughout the year; 2) the facility will be on a two week rotation of inspection by the director of EH and facility inspector to insure compliance with Code and that knowledge is being gained and applied; and 3) following a few months of follow-ups, the facility will be routinely visited by the SCDPH health educator to fill education gaps and to insure safe food handling between SCDPH visits. Inability to observe improvement will result in a suspension of permit until knowledge of proper food handling can be demonstrated. 
The food manager class is great education for all involved in the operations. Having multiple employees complete the training can only benefit Almadina operations. Please see that those employees that work any amount of time in the kitchen are at least food handler trained. But ideally food manager certificates should be obtained for employees. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (O) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD safety, including FOOD allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. FOOD allergy awareness includes describing FOODS identified as MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS and the symptoms that a MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN could cause in a sensitive individual who has an allergic reaction.

2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. Observed staff to not be able to demonstrate proper hand washing. Employees in the facility were not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing hands. Discussed with operator and employee and demonstrated proper technique. The employee interacting with SCDPH was on his phone at least five times during this educational meeting. Discussed washing hands after answering phone calls and handling food. Continue to educate available staff on proper technique. 

 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. The facility is observed cooling and reheating almost every protein served at the facility. As a Class II facility, the act of cooling/reheating is not allowed. As the kitchen is cooling over eight different items, the upgrade to Class I will occur. Furthermore, the facility is struggling to demonstrate safe food handling. The inability of the facility to proper clean, maintain, and handle foods dictates the upgrade. 


(A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. Observed a covered container of cooked/cooled potatoes to be molded. Potatoes were discarded during the inspection. 

FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. The bulk containers show no signs of proper cooling: covered, large amounts, and no date marking. The chicken on the counter is temped at 90F which implies possible improper cooling and the obvious improper reheating/hot holding (see violation #21). 

COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER. 

(A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. There are multiple items being held on counters and not in proper hot holding units. The facility has a hot holding display, a steam table, and a warmer available. None of these items are in-use today. During the inspection, chicken (cooked yesterday) was observed on the counter at 90ish F. The operator could not immediately explain why food from yesterday and just brought to the counter within the last 15 minutes was temping at 90F. See violation #20. The proper hot holding of foods was discussed as was the proper reheating behavior. A warmer was plugged-in and made available for use. 

HOLD FOODS AT 135F OR ABOVE ONCE COOKED.

REHEAT FROM COLD TEMPERATURE TO 165F WITHIN TWO HOURS. 

USE A PROBE THERMOMETER TO INSURE THIS PROCESS IS PROPERLY CONDUCTED. 
This hot holding practice will be monitored by SCDPH staff over the next few weeks to insure proper education to staff. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. Nothing in the kitchen bares a date mark. There are multiple containers of rice and proteins cooked prior to today, without a proper date mark. If nothing is date marked, then the facility cannot know when to discard foods after seven days. Date mark prepared foods once created and date mark TCS foods once opened.



(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Thawing. Full tub of raw, frozen chicken is observed thawing on a counter in the back room. Discussed thawing under running water, in refrigerator, or as part of cooking. During the inspection, chicken was placed under running water at the triple sink. SCDPH will continue to monitor thawing practices to insure education is gained.


Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. The facility does not have a probe thermometer available. A probe style thermometer shall be provided to allow for the proper cooling, reheating, and cooking of foods within the facility. Provide a stem thermometer and learn how to use and calibrate the thermometer. 

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(A) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. There were no sani-cloths being stored in the available sanitizing solution. Cloths were observed on various counters around the kitchen. The available sani-bucket was shallow. A larger bucket was created - use a bucket that can fit your hands and the available cloths. 

(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills from TABLEWARE and carry-out containers that occur as FOOD is being served shall be: (1) Maintained dry; and (2) Used for no other purpose.

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text:
3-304.15(C) Gloves, Use Limitation. The facility is observed donning gloves without a proper hand washing. Also, it appears that gloves are being used to protect hands and not food as the staff are observed touching multiple surfaces with gloved hands without changing. Discussed glove use at length. The facility will have this education included in the ongoing training that will occur over the next few months.  


(C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with READY-TO-EAT FOOD that will not be subsequently cooked if the slash-resistant gloves have a SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent outer surface; or if the slash-resistant gloves are covered with a SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent glove, or a SINGLE-USE glove.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-401.11(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. 

There is immediate concern over the lack of cleaning in this facility and the potential for cross-contamination. As a bare minimum, safe food handling should include a routine cleaning schedule that maintains surfaces clean. The facility does not have a single surface that is observed free of accumulated grease and soil. A follow-up for the following surfaces will be conducted in two weeks:
1) hood system - the hood has not been serviced since 2023. The baffles are observed coated with grease and ready to drip onto the food of the cook line - clean the baffles, the Ansul system, and service the hood.
2) Shelving in the walk-in cooler is coated with food debris and mold. The shelving should be removed and power washed to remove all access grease and soil. 
3) The dry storage shelving is observed coated with a dusting of powder from the various spices held on the shelves. The side brace is nearly yellow from powder from spices.
4) Fryer, flat top, steamer, and vertical broiler are observed thickly coated with accumulated grease. This appears to be a potential fire hazard. Clean the cooking surfaces.
5) Throughout the facility, in-use cooking utensils are not being removed every four hours for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. There were observed soiled knives and peelers under the prep cooler from previous days use. Discussed cleaning. This is one of the topics that will be covered in future educationals. Staff appeared to be unaware as to proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing practices. 
6) preparation cooler interior and exterior is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. 

Clean the aforementioned surfaces paying attention to maintaining these surfaces clean once the initial task is completed.  


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, EQUIPMENT, a cabinet used for the storage of FOOD, or a cabinet that is used to store cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be located: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

Also, there was no knowledge of how a triple sink was to be properly created and used. Discussed sanitizing at the moment. Steamer was cleaned-in-place using a bleach solution to complete. Will continue to educate on future inspections. 


When used for WAREWASHING, the wash compartment of a sink, mechanical warewasher, or wash receptacle of alternative manual WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT as specified in 4-301.12(C), shall contain a wash solution of soap, detergent, acid cleaner, alkaline cleaner, degreaser, abrasive cleaner, or other cleaning agent according to the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions.

 Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer available in the kitchen during food preparation. An employee was informed of the requirement for sanitizer availability and a spray bottle was prepared, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is available at all times of food preparation and service.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

comment:

comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese sauce to have an ambient temperature of 125F, and was probed to have an internal temperature of 126F. CORRECTED- the liquid cheese was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Liquid cheese was moved to used time as a control for food safety (TAC). The outside of the container was marked with a discard time 4 hours past when the bag was opened. Other options may include using a ladle for liquid cheese until the hot holding unit is serviced or replaced. Hot holding units for hot TCS items must be maintained at or above 135F.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper utensils storage:
1) Both the chopped tomatoes and onions contained single service bowls with no handles in the food.
2) The ice scoop handle was touching the ice in the drive-thru.
CORRECTED. The single service bowls in the produce were discarded, and the ice scoop was moved to its holder. Scoops with handles should be stored so that the nonfood contact surfaces (the handle, which is touched) is stored above or separate from the food to prevent bare-hand contamination. Do not reuse bowls as scoops, as there is no differentiation between the food-contact surface and the hand contact surface. Either Immediately discard bowl after use, or obtain scoops with handles for produce.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to inspect quesadilla grill cleaning.

comment: Inspector observed no paper towels at the hand washing sink. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed paper towels at the hand washing sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only, and are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature. The PIC said that they keep the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. The inspectors and PIC discussed possible solutions. The recommended solution is using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours. This system allows the sauces to be left on the counter for convenient use during preparation. The inspectors will return on 10/15/2025 to check that the TCS sauces are being stored correctly.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed several prepared foods (i.e, various seafood salads) were observed in the prep cooler bottom without proper date marking. The PIC stated that the foods had been prepared yesterday and they will be used for several days. During the inspection the salads were date marked. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum (the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1, food is discarded after 6 additional days).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items were out of proper cold holding temperature. The ambient temperature of the open air cooler was initially observed at 51F, and went down to 41F (no indication of defrost on cooler). As a result, multiple TCS items were probed for internal temperatures:
1) Three cheeseburgers were probed at temperatures of 48(X2) and 45F.
2) Three Chobani yogurts were probed at 48(X2) and 47F.
3) Two steak and jalapeno burritos were probed at 49 and 51F.
4) Two beef and bean burritos were probed at 48 and 46F.
5) One country fried chicken was probed at 47F.
6) One smoked ham and turkey club was probed at 48F.
7) Two smoked ham and swiss sandwiches were both probed at 48F. 
8) Two egg and sausage burritos were probed at 50 and 51F.
9) One Italian wrap was probed at 48F.
10) One chicken and Ceasar wrap was probed at 47F.
11) One buffalo chicken wrap was probed at 47F.
12) Two packaged of creamer in the dispenser were also observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Creamers were voluntarily discarded.

Three items not listed in numbers 1-11 were probed from the open air cooler and had internal temperatures below 41F. CORRECTED- due to all of the previously mentioned foods being prepackaged, they had to be discarded to be probed. The inspector notified the person in charge (PIC) of the need to probe and discard foods due to high temperature readings. The PIC stated they check cooler temperatures at the end of the shift daily. Inspector encourages use of a daily temperature log to monitor temperatures for cold holding units. Ensure TCS foods are kept at or below 41F to prevent the growth of microorganisms that may cause foodborne-illnesses.

comment: Inspector observed water pooling on the floor behind the soda machines. The source of the leak appeared to be a carbonator below the soda machines. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed two wet mops on the floor. Discussion between the PIC and inspector occurred regarding storage of mops. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows for air drying in the future.

comment: Two containers of ground beef were observed in the walk-in cooler at 46F and 48F, probed. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the out of temperature ground beef. Ensure time/temperature controlled for safety foods are held at 41F or below at all times.

[P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The walk in cooler was observed with an ambient temperature of 45F using inspector’s probe thermometer. Ground beef was observed at 47 and 48F and was voluntarily discarded. title: Food handler training
comment:
There were two employees working at the time of the inspection, one employee was a certified food protection manager and the other employee did not have any food certificates. Discussed the need of at least a food handler certificate if handling food, drinks, or clean dishes. Be sure that all employees obtain a food handler certificate within 30 days of hire if not already a certified food protection manager. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The facility is observed to be in a poor state of cleanliness and is continuing to worsen - many of the violations present during today’s inspection are REPEAT violations. There does not seem to be a cleaning schedule in place that is being followed. Floors, walls, drains, and equipment are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. There are a number of cleaning repeat violations that have not been corrected since previous inspections. Attention to cleaning is needed in the facility. The poor state of cleanliness has caused soil and molds to accumulate throughout food storage and preparation locations and this poses a threat of contamination to food. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/10/2025 to ensure that cleaning is being done, the facility is improving in cleanliness, and that a regular cleaning schedule has been implemented and is being FOLLOWED.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handler licenses to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, staff will all take steps to get licenses . Ensure all members of staff that handle food have the required food handlers license. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

comment: Inspector observed two opened containers of creamer without date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC knew when the creamer downstairs was opened and placed the corresponding date on the container. The creamer upstairs was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with their opening date if held for more than one day. Use or discard TCS items within seven days.

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector and PIC observed multiple ants on the soda nozzle in the upstairs satellite bar. CORRECTED- the PIC cleaned and sanitized the soda nozzle, and stated that it should have been soaking. Ensure pest control is obtained (or verified) and monitored to prevent the contamination of drinks and garnishes.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed neither of the upstairs bathroom doors to contain self-closers. Provide self closers on all restroom doors to prevent the contamination of potable beverages.
citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (SECOND REPEAT) Inspector observed the floor at the back walk-in-cooler to contain spots of bare wood, as well as chipping into the surface of the floor near the door. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Wood is highly absorbent and may allow for the entry and harborage of mold. Seal or repair floors by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers certificates during today’s inspection. All employees who handle food or drinks must obtain a Food Handlers card; and renew it every three years. Course completion reviews safe food handling practices and cold holding temperatures, among other important food safety standards. Ensure all bar tenders obtain a Food Handlers certificate, and maintain a copy on file to be made available during future routine inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (Repeatx2) Observed mold accumulation to be present on the caulking to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being checked regularly for black mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee turn off faucet without using a barrier. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing techique, employee rehashed hands. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(B) Compliance with Food Law. (B) FOOD prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

This facility is licensed as a Class-III (low risk) facility. The complaint stated that they were serving food prepared at home to customers. This was confirmed by the PIC during this inspection who appeared unaware that this is not allowed. The distinction between a private event and serving to the public was made. Education was conducted and they are instructed to either upgrade their risk classification to Class-II (medium risk) or pull temporary event permits moving forward. In either situation the food would need to be prepared on site. This situation is considered corrected with education to the PIC. The current practice is being ceased at this time.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There were a couple leaks dripping from a pipe above the right table of the dish machine. The facility is aware of the leaks and is in the process of repairing the leaks. The facility mentioned that the ice machine on the second floor is causing the leaks in the kitchen area. In the meantime, the facility is instructed to place a bucket underneath the drip to catch contaminated water. A follow-up will be scheduled for 10/8/2025 to ensure that leak is repaired and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The spray bottle in the meat room would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation showed that the dispensing machine was not dispensing at correct concentration. The bottle was refilled from a different machine in the facility to correct the immediate violation. A check of the machine will be conducted on the scheduled follow up in ten days related to flies in the facility (refer to line item #38).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives in the produce prep area are observed with remaining food debris on them and in storage in the knife rack. Per the PICs these knives are damaged (observed chipped) and are being discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are thoroughly cleaned and sanitized prior to storage in the facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple locations in the facility are observed with gnats/fruit flies/drain flies. Locations include: 1) the dairy mop sink; 2) the trash can in the produce area; 3) the mop sink by the back receiving door. The PICs were shown and instructed to contact pest control for maintenance. Ensure that all pests are removed from the facility and the facility is maintained free of pests moving forward.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
(REEPAT) 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple partially consumed drinks are observed throughout the stock areas of the facility. The PICs were shown and discarded the items during this inspection to correct. Ensure that employee foods are only consumed in areas that do not allow for possible food contamination.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspectors observed the Certified Food Manager Certificate (CFM) on file to have expired in March of this year. The person in charge (PIC) stated that they have not retaken the test since then. Inspector provided PIC with a handout on accredited institutes through which they may retake the exam. A CFM must be on site at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM helps to oversee proper food handling and cold holding temperatures to ensure facility is in compliance with safe food handling and preparation. Retake the test by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The PIC was unable to produce signed Employee Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. The inspector provided the PIC with a blank copy of Sangamon County Department of Public Health’s Employee Reporting Agreement. The inspector will return on 10/16/25 to ensure all employees have signed and read the agreement. Ensure these documents are kept on file to be produced during inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed multiple items (pork belly, Mackerel, Tilapia) to have torn packaging, or be outside of their packaging in the sliding chest coolers & freezers. CORRECTED- items were re-wrapped. Ensure all temperature control for safety (TCS) food items that are packaged on site retain their seal to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed the sliding chest cooler in front of the food prep area to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the PIC added an ambient thermometer to the cooling unit. Ensure all cooling units contain an ambient thermometer to measure the temperature at the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility ensure all cooling units are working properly to hold items at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: 1) Inspectors observed mouse droppings on the floor and between boxes in the back dry storage area (shipping container). 
2) Inspector also observed a dead bug on a noodle package on the top shelf of the open air cooler. CORRECTED- this item was removed from service by the PIC.

The facility uses Sonny Adams for Pest Control once monthly. Droppings should be cleaned up, but large pallets of food will need to be moved to properly clean. Contact pest control operator, and monitor the area for evidence of pest after clean up, and check shipments for pests during delivery.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of brown rice being stored in a cardboard box, with an open top in the back dry storage area. Foods in dry storage should be completely covered in a food-grade package or container to prevent the contamination of food. This storage method also may attract pests (see violation #38). Ensure foods are protected from contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed a bare wood countertop over the triple sink. Wood is highly absorbent and may allow for the entry and harborage of mold. Seal or paint this shelving unit to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates during today’s inspection. Three people were observed to be packaging food during today’s inspection. Ensure all workers who handle or prepare food have and maintain their Food Handler’s Certificate every 3 years. Food Handler’s must have a certificate on file within 30 days of hire. Ensure these documents are available upon request during future inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket along the cook-line tested below 100ppm (quat). The sani solution was changed and retested at 200ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer's recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The gap in between the triple sink and the wall is need of recaulking. The current caulk is filled with debris and must be repaired. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are sealed to avoid buildup of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning in the following areas:
- Floors throughout the kitchen (underneath and behind equipment)
- Outer surfaces of equipment
- Walls and ceilings throughout the entire facility
When time permits, be sure to clean physical facilities at a frequency to prevent buildup of grease and food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

6-101.11(A)(1) Inspectors observed a build up of ice in the walk-in cooler at the bottom of the door of the walk-in freezer. A build up of ice was also observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the building up will be cleaned. Ensure that the build up is clean to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A THRICE REPEAT VIOLATION. There was no sanitizer bucket (s) available on the cook line at the beginning of today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. The sani bucket was made immediately. The final measured of the sanitizer concentration was 200 ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are made at the appropriate temperature at all times during food prep.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed several food items in the walk-in cooler not properly date marked. Some of the items are but not limited to an opened jug of milk, sauces, dumplings fillings, cooked meat, and etc. PIC was made aware and education was carried out. Ensure that all food items are properly dated when they are being stored for future use. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Ensure that the above mentioned handwashing sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

Ensure that the above mentioned handwashing sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The back door of the establishment was observed propped open upon arrival. The PIC mentioned that the facility baked cookies earlier in the morning and the door was propped open to allow fresh air inside. The door was closed to correct the violation. Ensure that outer doors are never propped open, unless there are effective methods to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
citation_text: 6-202.15(D) Outer Openings, Protected. (D) Except as specified in (B) and (E) of this section, if the windows or doors of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, or of a larger structure within which a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is located, are kept open for ventilation or other purposes or a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is not provided with windows and doors as specified under (A) of this section, the openings shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) 16 mesh to 25.4 mm (16 mesh to 1 inch) screens; (2) Properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or (3) Other effective means.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hand soap to be present at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was refilled. Ensure soap is present at all hand sink to ensure proper hand washing is practiced.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure any TCS item is kept no longer than 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.

(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed tubing to be in contact with ice at bar. Discussed with PIC, plans are in place to move hose unit to one ice bin so the other can be used. Facility will be using a separate ice bin for ice at the bar. Ensure tubing is not in contact with ice.
citation_text: 4-204.16 Beverage Tubing, Separation. Except for cold plates that are constructed integrally with an ice storage bin, BEVERAGE tubing and cold-plate BEVERAGE cooling devices may not be installed in contact with stored ice.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up at bar or kitchen. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer buckets were set up and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure sanitizer solution is set up and available during all hours of operation.
