The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) REPEAT: There were gaps observed between the front hand sink and the wall. Clean off existing caulking and re-seal the front hand sink to the wall.
2) REPEAT: There is a horizontal gash in the wall above the front hand sink. Fill in or patch the damaged wall.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee remove gloves and put on new gloves without hand washing. The PIC will be educating staff about proper glove use. Additionally, the inspector will be reaching out to the PIC in about two weeks to schedule hand washing education with the SCDPH health educator and Spanish translator. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC will be educating staff about the proper hand washing procedure. Additionally, the inspector will be reaching out to the PIC in about two weeks to schedule hand washing education with the SCDPH health educator and Spanish translator. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. The PIC scheduled service for the dish machine. Until the dish machine is serviced the facility will be washing and rinsing in the dish machine but sanitizing in the triple sink. The inspector will follow-up on 7/24/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the ice machine baffles have an accumulation of soil residues. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets on the cookline and bar were testing at 0 ppm (Cl). The PIC was informed and the sanitizer buckets were changed during the inspection. The inspector suggests increasing the frequency that sanitizer buckets are changed throughout the day. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-200 ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of queso sitting on top of the containers inside the steam table with an internal temperature of 81F. The queso container has a label indicating that is was prepared at 7:30 AM. The inspector asked the PIC about the queso and they stated that it should have been put inside the steam table. The PIC voluntarily discarded the queso during the inspection. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination: (1) Uncovered containers of chips, tortilla bowls, and taco shells on the cookline by the entrance door; and (2) Uncovered deserts on the top shelf of the double cooler. The inspector educated that foods must be protected from contamination during storage when not being used. Ensure that foods are properly covered during stoarge by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the ice scoop in the server area stored with the handle within the ice. An employee was notified and the ice scoop was moved into the holder during the inspection. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: (1) The food residue on the floor beneath the grill on the cookline; and (2) The debris on the magnetic knife holder above the steam table on the cookline. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The preparation cooler was observed to be holding at 70F (cut tomatoes). CORRECTED- The prep cooler was unplugged and the PIC plugged it back in. The prep cooler lowered to under 41F and the food had only been in there for around 30 minutes. Ensure food is kept at 41F or below if it is a TCS food.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The PIC was using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer spray bottle (a premade solution) but only had Chlorine test strips. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and he stated that he will cease using the Quat sanitizer and use the Clorox bleach they have on the mobile unit. Ensure that there are always test strips available for all types of sanitizers that are being used.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT- The floor is observed to not be caulked to the wall and trim. Ensure that this is caulked/sealed to the wall and trim. This was discussed with the PIC. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand sink at the bar being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- employee moved the dump tray to the triple sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are being used for hand washing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw meat was observed to be stored on top of a ranch container in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC moved the raw meat beneath the ranch. Ensure that raw food is stored beneath ready-to-eat food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
1) FIRST REPEAT- Both bar soda nozzles were observed to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned the soda nozzles. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
2) Knives on the magnetic strip in the kitchen were observed to contain food debris. CORRECTED- person in charge moved the knives to be cleaned and sanitized. All food contact surfaces that will be used on ready-to-eat foods must be clean to sight and touch.
3) Magnetic strip for the knives contained grease and debris. Non-food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch. A follow up inspection will occur on 07/28/25 to ensure that the knife strip are cleaned or sanitized. 
3) Ice baffles at both the north and south ice machines were observed to contain a significant amount of soil accumulation behind the door hinges. Food-contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch. A follow up inspection will occur on 07/28/25 to ensure that baffles are cleaned or sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: Inspector observed chicken cooling in the walk in freezer to be stacked in a tub. Education occurred with the person in charge regarding the need for shallow pans for food to have the surface area to properly cool. In it’s current configuration the chicken will not reach cooling temperature benchmarks in the required time.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Lime juice and whipping cream located at the bar reach in cooler did not have date marking. CORRECTED- Education occurred about date marking and dates were placed on the whipping cream and lime juice. Ensure items being held for more than 24 hours are marked with the date the container was opened, so that they may be used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect stun light above single service articles at the entry of the kitchen. Ensure that insect control devices are stored away from single service items to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed chicken bouillon with an open lid to be located on the floor of the dry storage area. All food items should remain covered when not in use, and must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect items from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) FIRST REPEAT- Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler is soiled or rusted (straight across from the door and to the left when you walk in the cooler). Wire shelving over the prep counter (above the under-counter freezer) is dusty. Clean dusty/dirty shelves. Replace rusted shelves that are no longer smooth/easily cleanable.
2)  Significant amounts of food debris were observed on the floors in the walk in freezer and throughout the kitchen. 
3) The floors of the walk-in freezer and bar walk-in cooler were wet from the cooling system dripping.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1) 2nd REPEAT: The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked.
2) 1st REPEAT: There are holes in the wall above the hand-sink and the triple sink that need caulked.
3) 1st REPEAT: The kitchen handwashing sink needs re-caulked.
4) A hole was observed in the east wall of the dry storage above the water heater.
5) The hand sink in the south men’s bathroom was not adhered to the wall. There is also not a large enough gap to easily clean between the sink and the wall. The sink should be sealed to the wall to be smooth and easily cleanable.
6) Both walk-in coolers appeared to be dripping water from their compressors (see violation #49). The bar walk in cooler contained several ready-to-eat items, including cut fruit, red peppers flakes, parmesan cheese, and milk. This provides an opportunity for cross contamination. 

Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The CFM was unable to show inspectors allergen awareness training certificate. All CFMs must obtain allergen awareness training within 30 days of employment. Inspector gave allergen certification information to the CFM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink after washing hands. PIC was informed that a barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off the hand sink to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure all staff members are properly hand washing at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to wash their hands before donning new gloves to portion food for the dessert bar. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper handwashing. Ensure staff are washing their hands before putting on new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed knives and a pair of scissors stored inside of counters or equipment which is not considered easily cleanable. Ensure utensils are stored in designated areas to avoid contamination. The PIC was informed and the utensils were sent to the dish area.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed the triple sink in the dish washing area to be leaking from the drainage plumbing. PIC was informed that waste water must be properly conveyed and plumbing must be maintained in good repair. A follow-up will be conducted on July 24, 2025 to ensure the plumbing has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-103.11(I) Inspector observed multiple priority and priority foundation violations during this inspection. See violations below. Staff education is needed regarding cold holding temperatures, handwashing procedures, and other safe food handling practices.

Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Inspector observed an employee using the triple sink to wash hands. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that employees only use the handwashing sink to wash hands. This helps to prevent cross contamination. Inspector will return 7/24/2025 to reevaluate hand-washing procedures.

Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed many of the foods in the walk-in cooler to be above 41F. Foods probed include: Carnitas (50F), Cheese Sauce (50F), Consommé (51F), Raw Beef (51F), Raw Hamburger (50F), Cheese Sauce x2 (52F), Bacon (51F), Refried Beans (51F), Milk (51F), Raw Beef (52F), Cheese Sauce x3 (54F), Sour Cream (48F), Cut Lettuce (53F), Egg Rolls (53F). All out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are kept at 41F or below. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate cold-holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

Items in coolers are as follows: Raw Chicken (53.5F), Raw Beef (52F), Raw Marinated Chicken (51.5F), and shredded cheese (55F). All items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed 3 TCS items being stored out of refrigeration. The items were: Barbecue Sauce (Ambient temperature), mayonnaise (75F), feta (54F). All were voluntarily thrown away. The barbecue sauce was open on a shelf at room temp, and had been there for a while. Facility was attempting to store the mayo and feta in an ice bath. When preparing an ice bath, ensure that food containers are submerged to the top of the container in ice. Ice must then be replenished as needed to keep foods at or below 41F. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate the cold holding of these items.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Inspector observed a spatula being used to scoop carnitas in the walk-in cooler to be stored improperly. The spatula was sitting on the shelving in the cooler next to the carnitas. Ensure that while utensils are in use they are stored in the food being served with the handle sticking up. Alternatively, utensils may also be stored on a clean and sanitized work surface while not in use.

3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed 2 utensils in need of repair or replacement in the kitchen. The first utensil in need of replacement or repair was the juicer. The paint on the juicer is flaking from the surface. The second utensil is the fine mesh strainer hanging in front of the ice machine. Loose wires are sticking off the side of the strainer basket. citation_text: 4-502.11(A) Good Repair and Calibration. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed several instances of a #55 violation at the establishment.

1) The floor of the kitchen was covered in water and food debris upon the inspector’s arrival. Ensure that the floor is kept free of large amounts of water and food debris.

2) The cold-water outlets in the floor behind the sink have been sealed into the floor with a material that is not smooth and easily cleanable. The material was observed to hold food debris and soils. Ensure this material is either smoothed or replaced to make it easily cleanable.

3) The walk-in cooler compressor is leaking water on the floor of the walk-in cooler and possibly foods inside. Ensure this is repaired to prevent the contamination of other surfaces and items in the cooler.

Ensure these areas are maintained and kept in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a jug of milk that was opened yesterday and a container of horchata (ready-to-eat milk based drink) that was prepared yesterday were not date marked. The PIC was educated and the milk and horchata were date marked during the inspection. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods held at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: 2-103.11(L) The operators are knowledgeable of the food code but are struggling to apply these safe food handling practices. New staff is not being trained on proper hand washing. And the practices of general cleaning, maintenance, and storage have lapsed. See that education to staff is completed prior to them starting to cook and handle food. See that staff does not forget to practice the knowledge known for safe food handling. Will revisit safe food handling during the ten day follow-up. 


Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure.  Observed new employee to be nearly unable to understand how to properly wash hands. Demonstration of proper hand washing occurred multiple times, the staff member was asked to wash hands, and it took nearly five attempts to observe a successful handwashing. The lack of knowledge was discussed with the owner. The owner was encouraged to have an education session with the employee (see violation #1). The employee speaks Spanish and language is a barrier. SCDPH will bring a Spanish-speaking interpreter to facilitate education. Employee was present for five days. 


(B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

comment:

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that proper hand washing procedures are enforced at the facility. Food handlers should only wash their hands in the designated hand washing sinks.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

All of the Allergen training certificates available at the facility have expired at the end of last year. The PIC was notified and instructed to have the current CFPMs retake the course/renew the certification. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility maintain current allergen training certifications at all times.

comment: PIC has not demonstrated knowledge of food safety practices. PIC has continued to operate without essential equipment (pH meter) or other interim measures in place. citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Sushi rice is not acidified, nor is a Time as a Control policy in place to maintain food safety while rice is held on the countertop to make sushi rolls. Discussed the use of Time as a Control with PIC. If sushi rice used from cooking, rolls created from that rice need to be created and sold within 4 hours of rice being removed from the rice cooker. If sushi rice is cooled to 41F within 6 hours (and logs are maintained), sushi rolls created from that rice need to be sold within 6 hours of the rice being removed from cold-holding. Sushi packages need to be labeled to indicate the time that they should be consumed by.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control. [Pf]

citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility maintenance issues that could impede proper cleaning.
1. A buildup of frost on the refrigeration unit and fan in the walk-in cooler.
2. Few broken tiles under the fryers in the kitchen area. 
3. Dust accumulation hanging off the fan on the floor on the cook line in the kitchen.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned areas are cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to be out of compliance with food allergen awareness training. PIC was made aware and PIC had no knowledge of the possible location of the certification if any was available. Ensure that facility is compliant with this law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the three compartment sink without caulking. PIC was made aware and PIC ensured inspector that the three compartment sink will have the necessary caulking done.  Ensure that the three compartment sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observe that there was only one employee with proof of food handler certification at the facility during the inspection. PIC said that everyone else does have valid food handler certifications however, was unable to provide proof as they may have been locked in a cabinet that is not accessible to them. PIC does not have access to the digital copies either. PIC ensured inspector that they will have the certifications printed out  making them available when needed. Ensure that all employees with the exception of those of the certified food protection manager certification acquired their food handler certification within 30 days of employment.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 55-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: shredded cheese 56F, colby jack cheese 55F, mozzarella cheese 55F, cheese slices 54F, cream cheese x3 50-54F, sour cream 53F, ground beef 57F, mayo 55F, salami 58F, sausage 49F, beef 55F, cooked vegetables 55F, ham x3 55-50F, ranch 56F, cheese sauce 55F, and cheddar cheese 58F. All foods has been inside the cooler for over four hours. During the inspection all temperature control for safety (TCS) were voluntary discarded by the PIC (the above mentioned were the TCS foods discarded). There was a package of sausage, steak, and multiple pizzas that were recently purchased that had temperatures below 41F; these were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. The non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. unopened ranch, unopened mayo, uncut tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce in the harvest cut, and bread). The PIC was instructed that they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holing foods at 41F or below. The inspector suggests immediate service for the cooler. The inspector will follow-up on 7/14/2025 to check that the cooler is functioning properly.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The buildup of frost on the standing freezer fans - the freezer must be defrosted. 

(2) The buildup of frost on the reach-in freezers - the freezers must be defrosted.

(3) The cardboard lining the shelf above the sushi prep cooler - the cardboard must be removed. 

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The food debris on the bottom of the standing freezer. 

(2) The grease and food debris on the wall and floor to the right of the fryers. 

(3) The debris on the silver shelves above the prep cooler. 

(4) The debris on the white shelves surrounding the kitchen triple sink. 

(5) The dust on the hood system. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the mop was stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The employee working in the kitchen was informed and they hung the mop during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to airdry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was between 50-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: parmesan cheese 54F, mozzarella cheese 51F, caesar dressing 53F, cut tomatoes 49F, and cream cheese 47F. The temperature control for safety (TCS) foods inside the temperature danger zone were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. There were several TCS foods recently brought to the double cooler from the walk-in cooler that had internal temperatures below 41F and these foods were immediately moved back into the walk-in cooler. All non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC was instructed that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holding foods at 41F or less. The inspector suggests getting immediate service for the double cooler. The inspector will return on 7/14/2025 to check on the temperature of the double cooler.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect trap placed above clean dish ware (on storage rack between office and mop sink). PIC was notified to have pest control company move trap away from food-contact surfaces to prevent contamination. Insect control devices should not be located over areas where food is being prepared, or where clean equipment is being stored. [C]
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed ice bucket faced upwards towards the ceiling- where the food contact surface can be exposed to contaminants.  CORRECTED- Education was provided to the PIC regarding potential contamination of food contact surfaces. Ice bucket was inverted. Food contact surfaces should be stored where they are not exposed to contamination. [C]
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Multiple employees were observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to actuate the paper towel dispensers. Multiple options were discussed with the PIC for handling this situation but the primary idea is that the bare hands should not be used to actuate this machine. Education conducted to correct. Ensure safe hand washing procedures are used at all times.

citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The soap dispenser in the men’s bathroom is observed empty during this inspection. The dispenser was replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

comment: Observed the left sink at the sushi station that is used for hand washing did not have hand washing signage. The right sink that is used for dumping was labeled with hand washing signage. The signage was removed from the designated dump sink and the PIC was given new hand washing signage for the designed hand washing sink. Ensure that signage that notifies employees to wash hands before returning to work is available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the dump sink (to the left of the reach-in freezer). Stored behind the faucets the cutting board can be contaminated by water splashes, food residue, and other debris dumped into the sink. The cutting board was moved to a different location for storage during the inspection Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. The employee working the dish machine drained the water and the dish machine tested at 100 ppm (Cl) afterwards. The PIC stated that the dish machine repair company suggested draining the water every two hours at the last visit. The inspector reminded that PIC that the dish machine must be tested regularly to make sure that it is functioning correctly (test strips are stored on top of the dish machine). Ensure that the dish machine is always properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the fried rice in the warmer across from the dish machine had an internal temperature of about 125F. The PIC stated that the rice was put inside the warmer at 11 am when the facility opened. During the inspection the temperature of the warmer was turned up and the rice had an internal temperature of 178F when the inspector re-checked. A time-as-control policy was implemented for the rice. The facility closes at 2:30 pm and any leftover rice will be discarded at this time. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are maintained at 135F or higher.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several pans of cooked rice in the back walk-in cooler stacked together that did not all have date marking. Each item must be individually labeled in case the pans are separated. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed the large containers holding various un-packaged white powders were not properly labeled. The containers did not have labels that matched the food inside (ex. flour was in the container labeled corn starch). The PIC stated they will be removing the old labels and creating new labels that match. Ensure that all easily mistaken foods not in the original container are properly labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination:

(1) Uncovered fried tempura on the sushi prep line; the lid was put onto the container during the inspection. 

(2) Uncovered cut vegetables in the walk-in cooler; saran wrap was put on to cover the containers during the inspection. 

(3) A hammer stored on top of foods in the dry storage area; the hammer was moved into the personal storage bin. 

The PIC was reminded that foods not being used must be covered to prevent the risk of contamination and that personal items must be stored away from food. Ensure that foods are always protected from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to drop a bottle of mayonnaise on the ground, pick it up, and then continue preparing food. CORRECTED- The inspector instructed the employee to sanitize the bottle of mayonnaise, wash his hands, and then don gloves to continue preparing the food. The employee was educated on when to wash his hands. Ensure that food employees are washing their hands and exposed portions of arms after engaging in activities that contaminate their hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were dishes that were observed to still be soiled after being washed that were being placed on the rack with the clean dishes. Ensure that dishes are thoroughly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The individual washing the dishes should be checking the dishes to ensure they are properly cleaned before they are placed on the rack with the other clean dishes. A follow up is scheduled on 7/16/2025 to ensure that dishes are being thoroughly cleaned before being placed with the clean dishes.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a bottle of regular mayonnaise and a bottle of spicy mayonnaise that were observed to be held on the table next to the preparation cooler, where they were out of cold holding. The PICs thought they could be left out of cold holding. CORRECTED- The guidelines were read by one of the PICs for the mayonnaise and they stated that they can either be at ambient temperature for four hours (Time as Control) or kept in cold holding. The bottles had been made at 11am and had only been out for around thirty minutes during a rush. The bottles were placed back in the preparation cooler and the PICs were educated to make sure that they are being either cold held or left out for four hours and then discarded. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are held at 41F and under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was a bottle of water that was in the standing freezer across from the cook line. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the bottle of water was discarded. title: Food handler training
comment:
REPEAT- The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the prep cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The hanging internal thermometer was reading at about 55F. The following internal temperatures were recorded: jalapeños 53F, chicken 51F, turkey 50F, ham 53F, burger patty 49F, chorizo 49F, parmesan cheese 52F, monterey jack cheese 55F, southwest sauce 56F, spicy mayo 58F, sour cream cups 58F, and salsa cups 53F. Non-temperature control for safety (TCS) foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. onions, jalapeños, pickles, various non-dairy based sauce, strawberries, corn mix, avocados). Some of the TCS foods were put inside the cooler at 8:30 am and other TCS foods has been inside the cooler since last night. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since last night and were voluntarily discarded: turkey, ham, feta cheese, parmesan cheese, burger patties, dairy bases sauces (southwest, spicy mayo, and mayo), sour cream cups, and salsa cups. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since 8:30 am and were put under time-as-control (TAC) to be discarded at 12:30 pm: lettuce, cut tomato, all cheeses, chicken, and chorizo. The PIC wrote down and posted above the prep cooler the foods that must be discarded and the time they will be discarded. The PIC also mentioned that they are not busy today and will most likely close at 12:30 pm. The PIC spoke with Koady Hawkins who stated they will be scheduling service for the cooler. They will be putting small amounts of TCS foods that can be used within four hours inside the prep cooler until it is serviced. They were reminded that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler without TAC until it is cold holding foods at 41F or below. For information about the cooler, see violation #33.

The majority of the foods had already been removed from the cooler and only condiments and cut vegetables were being stored in the top. While they had implemented a TAC policy they were not writing down the time when food must be discarded. The PIC was aware of the time the foods were put into the cooler and during the inspection a note pad was brought to the prep table and the foods in temperature control were recorded. The PIC stated that a new part has already been ordered to fix the cooler, but until it is serviced they will continue to use TAC. The inspector will follow-up on 7/10/2025 to check on either the TAC procedure or that the cooler is properly functioning. Ensure that foods are properly marked to indicate the four hour TAC window until the cooler is cold holding foods at 41F or below.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspectors observed facility not being in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the person with the CFPM certification will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure that at least one certified food protection manager at the facility obtain a basic allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple food service employees fail to wash hands before donning a new pair of gloves. PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure staff are washing hands before donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler next to the grill in the kitchen was observed to be inoperable during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the cooler failed overnight and all food items in the cooler were discarded. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored in the cooler are being monitored with time as a control until the cooler is repaired. Ensure TCS foods in the cooler are kept for no longer than 4 hours. Items kept in the cooler for 4 hours must be discarded; they cannot be cooled and reused. A follow-up is scheduled for July 11th to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The upright freezer in the kitchen was observed to have an accumulation of ice. The ice accumulation is at risk of contacting food in the freezer, resulting in cross-contamination. The PIC is aware of the issue and is storing food such that it does not contact the ice in the freezer. Ensure the freezer is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the back storage room off the kitchen (water heater storage closet) to have bagged flour and boxed powdered foods to be stored in the unfinished space. The ceiling is not tiled and the floor is not coved. There is slight water seepage occurring around the floor. The room was previously observed with mouse droppings around the floor. Today, no droppings are observed, however, the space should have no food stored within or should have food protected if it is going to be used for food storage. Use large plastic storage tubs if you are going to continue to use the space for food storage. Provide storage bins that can be contained and are plastic or change the storage location of powdered foods.

Several food contact surfaces in the kitchen are thickly coated with accumulated dust and grease. The baffles of the hood system are coated in a layer of dust (baffles over the chicken broaster units). The broaster units themselves are observed to be coated with accumulated grease as is the surrounding floor and wall. See that the baffles are being routinely cleaned at a frequency that allows them to be maintained free of accumulated dust and grease.  After the baffles are clean, see that the baffles are cleaned a single one at a time and then moved down so that they maintain them clean. Clean the area surrounding the broaster (wall, floor, and attached plumbing).

citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Three locations have temperature violations observed at this time. 1) The drink prep cooler in the front section of the facility is holding milk at 51F. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code.

In the walk in freezer, stacks of food in boxes are observed with the bottom boxes on the floor. These bottom boxes are saturated in ice and the dyes from the boxes appear to have soaked into the observable ice coating them. This leads to the conclusion that the food inside of these containers has been contaminated and should not be used. The PIC was notified and discarded the bottom containers of food to correct the immediate violation. The remaining boxes were then placed on milk cartons to correct the future concerns of this situation (refer to line item #39 for write up). Ensure that all foods are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Two stacks of boxes containing food are observed with the bottom boxes stored on the floor of the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and placed the stacks on top of crates to correct. The bottom boxes were discarded (refer to line item #15 for write up). Ensure that all foods are stored at least six inches above the floor at all times.

6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers (CFPM) employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The only allergen certificate currently available at the facility is held by an employee without a CFPM. None of the available CFPMs have an allergen training certificate. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and that the certificates are maintained at the facility moving forward. Ensure that all CFPMs have allergen training completed at all times.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed staff barehandling ready to eat food items during food prep. Discussed with PIC and an education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are aware to don gloves after handwashing before prepping ready to eat food at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed to the sani bucket on the cook line by the grill measuring low concentration at 0 ppm. Discussed with PIC and the sani bucket was remade. The new solution tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani buckets are monitored and tested at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the hot holding unit to not be holding temperature within the appropriate temperature range. Discussed with PIC and the hot holding unit was switched with a better performing unit. PIC mention that the unit in question sometimes malfunction with temperature holding. They will work on getting an upgrade to a more function unit. Ensure that this unit is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil and food debris within the gasket of the stainless steel four compartment cooler on the cook line opposite the fryers. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the gasket of the cooler would be cleaned. Ensure that non food-contract surfaces such as the gasket of the cooler rare cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface to prevent future malfunction to the equipment.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the PIC’s Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate expired in February 2025. The PIC was reminded that someone with a CFPM certificate must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that the PIC renews their CFPM certificate by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. The PIC added bleach to the sanitizer bucket and it re-tested at 150 ppm (Cl). The PIC was reminded that sanitizer concentrations must be tested regularly with test strips. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration.
