The PIC was shown and instructed to clean these items again and to ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage. All items were moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Dates were adjusted during this inspection to correct.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Observed cloths in-use for wiping food contact surfaces stored moist and on prep tables. Advised PIC that cloths must be stored in their sanitizer buckets between uses. This ensures that the cloth is clean and without potential contamination before each use. Cook staff placed in-use cloths to their sanitizer buckets during inspection.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored in metal tubs which were contaminated with dust and food debris. Observed single-use condiment cups to be stored with food contact surfaces exposed or without adequate coverings to protect from dust/debris contamination. Observed large sharpies to be in a container with plastic spoons. Advised PIC to keep containers holding single-use utensils clean and to keep single-use food contact surfaces covered or inverted on a clean surface such as the bottom of a container or clean work surface. Containers holding single-use utensils were washed and contaminated utensils were disposed of during inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Observed shelf of kitchen pass-through to be damaged (cleanable coating lifting from wood shelf). Observed 3-part sink in dishwashing room to have gaps between the sink and wall. Advised PIC to fix these areas such that the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Any gaps/cracks/crevices on surfaces can harbor bacteria and other pathogens.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Observed the following improper hand washing sink usage during the inspection:

(1) During the inspection an employee was observed washing the soda dispenser holder in the hand washing sink by the dish machine. When the action was observed the employee was educated that hand washing sinks cannot be used for any purpose other than hand washing.

(2) The inspector observed dumped ice in the bar hand washing sink. The PIC was reminded that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. The bar currently has two sinks designated as hand washing sinks directly across from each other. The inspector suggests designating only one as the hand sink and using the other as a dump sink to avoid improper use. The sink that will not be used for hand washing must have the ‘employees must wash hands before returning to work’ signage removed.

Ensure that hand washing sinks are never used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed caulking to the left of the dish washing machine is a dark black color and deteriorating. This portion of the dish washing area experiences a high level of moisture from the rinsing nozzle. The calking must be removed and replaced when it starts to show signs of deterioration from moisture. Ensure that the caulking is replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of ice inside the walk-in freezer underneath the fan and on the ceiling. The ice is also dripping onto the boxes of food underneath. The inspector suggests scheduling a defrost or contacting repair personal. Ensure that inside the walk-in freezer is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the ice scoop holder at the right service station had an accumulation of soil residues. The ice scoop holder was removed and washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. Suggested to PIC to get more individuals manager certified. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (CL). The bucket contained soap and water. The bucket was re-prepared and bleach was added to the solution (tested at 100ppm CL). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize surfaces.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine’s sanitizer concentration tested at 0ppm (CL). PIC contacted a technician to service the machine. The facility was instructed to use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the machine is functioning properly. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to sanitize dishes correctly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There wasn't any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerator units.
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed bar dish machine to test at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will get serviced. Any dish washing needing to be done at the bar will now be done at the kitchen dish machine. Ensure sanitizing dish machines are testing at least at 50 ppm CL.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer fan unit to have significant ice accumulation present. Discussed with PIC, fan unit will be serviced. Ensure equipment is working to meet manufacturer’s standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be present at bar. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure both kitchen and bar both have sanitizer solutions available at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed kitchen dish machine to be soiled with food debris on top. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop to be resting in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mop water will be dumped and mop was placed in strainer part of bucket. Ensure mop water is being disposed of properly and that mops are being hung to dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the following locations:
1) The front hand sink.
2) The back drain sink.
3) The back hand sink.

Discussed with PIC, caulking will get replaced. Ensure facility is checking caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to leave the kitchen wearing gloves, retrieve soap, place it at the handsink, and return to handling clean dishes without removing/changing gloves or washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PICs, who will review handwashing with employees. Employees must wash hands after any activity that may have contaminated hands (such as leaving the kitchen), and before handling clean equipment and utensils.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: No soap was available at the front handwashing sink upon inspectors arrival. Upon request, an employee provided soap to the handsink. Ensure soap is always available at all handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Sanitizer buckets throughout the facility were observed with no measurable quat concentration. Upon further investigation, it was determined that sanitizer is not being dispensed from the wall-mounted dispenser at the proper concentration. Staff will mix sanitizer by hand and use test strips to check concentration until the wall-mounted dispenser is fixed. Use test strips regularly to monitor sanitizer concentrations. Inspector will follow up to verify that the wall-mounted dispenser has been repaired and is functioning properly.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration of 200-400ppm as indicated on the manufacturer’s label. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Muffins and scones were observed prepackaged on the service counter without any labeling present. Ensure foods that are prepackaged in advance of sale are labeled with the information below.
citation_text: 3-602.11 (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; and (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Small portion cups of loose leaf tea, sealed tea bags, and containers of chai are stored under the barista prep/rinse sink. Store foods away from potential sources of contamination. Discussed storage in other cabinets or in plastic containers with lids.
citation_text: 3-305.12 FOOD may not be stored (I) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking sealing the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall is cracked, creating a surface that is not smooth or easily cleanable. Recaulk the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall so the transition is smooth, easily cleanable, and cracks/crevices are eliminated.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

There was not any soap or paper towels observed at the handwashing sink. The operator was able to provide paper towels at the sink, but did not have any soap. Ensure that there is always soap and paper towels to allow for proper handwashing at the handwashing sink. A follow up is scheduled on 2/24/2025 to ensure that the facility has obtained soap.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. 

There are prepackaged cuts of meat, smoked fish parts, and frozen produce in the facility that are not labeled with the common name of the product or the cooking instructions. All food needs to be labeled with the common name of the product and all meat needs labeled with cooking instructions. Discussed placing a general cooking instructions label on the outside of the freezers. Discussed reaching out to supplier about labels for the cuts of meat. Ensure that produce that is placed into a bag to be froze has the common name of the product. A follow up is scheduled on 3/5/2025 to ensure that all of these items have been labeled.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed there was an open jug of milk in the front clear double cooler that was not date marked. The PIC stated the jug had been opened several days ago. The milk was correctly date marked during the inspection. The inspector suggested the PIC add labeling open milk to the kitchen’s closing routine. Ensure that all ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (day 1 being the day food was opened).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the container of sugar in the dry storage room had a bowl being used as a scoop. The PIC was educated that scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle to avoid contact with food. The PIC discarded the bowls during the inspection. Ensure that dispensing utensils for ready-to-eat foods are stored with their handles not in contact with food to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the rinsing surface to the left of the dish machine is not properly sealed to the wall in some locations. There is a gap between the caulking attached to the wall and the rinsing table surface. The surface must be re-sealed (ex. caulked) to the wall to make it smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that the rinsing table surface is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that no one at the facility has a valid allergen awareness certificate. One of the PIC’s (Jason) stated he will be re-taking the test. Ensure that someone at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed a trash can to be blocking kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, trash can was relocated. Ensure hand washing stations are kept accessible to encourage hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of won ton soup to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, inspector recommended soup be moved to stove for reheating, however staff threw soup away and prepared a new batch. Ensure any TCS food being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be made upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizer solution is made and available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: PIC had copies of the employee health reporting agreements, but they were not signed. Advised that all employees need to sign the agreement and the signed copies should be kept in records. This form advises employees that if they are experiencing any of the symptoms mentioned, they should not handle food or food services, and should not come into work. Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Repeat - Observed employee place soiled fruit storage container in bar handwashing sink. Food debris observed in kitchen handwashing sink. Advised that handwashing sinks are for washing hands ONLY, no dumping of food waste or cleaning equipment allowed in handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed cut lettuce, curry sauces, and dry noodles stored with no lid. Advised to keep food containers covered at all times. Regardless of the food being stored in a fridge or freezer, coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container.  Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
The following food storage/contamination violations were observed in the kitchen: 
1. Rice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor.
2. Raw beef stored in the deli cooler above open container of cut iceberg lettuce. Advised that the juices from the beef could drip into the lettuce, resulting in contamination. Always store raw meat at the lowest shelf, and produce above. Storage order was fixed immediately.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wiping cloths used for cleaning food surfaces stored on food prep surfaces. Advised cook staff to store sanitizing cloths in sanitizer (water and bleach). This helps keep cloths clean and sanitized between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed soup and rice bowls stored with food contact surface exposed to potential contamination. Advised cook staff to store dishes upside down on a clean surface or to cover to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed fan covering in walk-in cooler to be soiled with dust/debris. Clean cooler with enough frequency to ensure no build-up of dust and debris. Dust from the fans can be blown in to soup pots/other containers in the cooler and contaminate food.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspectors observed soup bowls being handled by the inside rim of the bowl immediately after soup was put into the bowl. Discussed with PIC. On arrival and during the inspection the spray bottle used for the sanitizer in the service area is without a label. A label was added during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all chemicals not in their original containers have labeling indicating the common name of the chemical in them at all times that they are in use.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. This was noticed while the inspector was washing their hands ant the beginning of the inspection and the PIC began running water before the situation could be addressed directly. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A box of frozen meat is observed on the floor under a table in the kitchen during this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the box to a shelf in the walk in cooler to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored so that they are at least six inches above the floor at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Immediately afterwards the employee re-washed their hands using the proper procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed the single-use utensils in the student self-service station were stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The inspector educated about the importance of storing utensils in a manner that prevents students from touching the food contact portions of utensils. The PIC removed the utensils and brought them into the kitchen to correct the storage after lunch. Ensure that single-use articles are stored to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities are observed to still need repaired from the pre-opening: 

1. REPEAT- Repair the flooring that is peeled at the door in the men’s room. 
2. REPEAT- Seal wood around floor drain of triple sink. 
3. Repair hole in wall of men’s restroom. 
4. REPEAT- Seal wood base/kick on right side of double sink in kitchen. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

There were containers of lettuce observed in a standing cooler that did not have a lid on them. The fan in this cooler was observed to be soiled. Ensure that all food is protected from cross contamination by being in a covered container, a wrapper, or stored in its original, closed package. CORRECTED- Lids were placed on these containers during the inspection.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

An employee was observed to use a wiping cloth to wipe down food contact surfaces and leave it on the counter after use. Ensure that if wiping cloths are not in use that they are being stored in a sanitizer bucket that is at the label-recommended concentration. CORRECTED- The employee was educated and moved the cloth into the sanitizer bucket.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The steamer that the facility uses to prepare mashed potatoes and ribs is observed to be leaking and not working properly. It is creating large amounts of steam that is causing black mold to grow on ceiling tiles above this area. Ensure that this equipment is maintained in a state of good repair and condition. There will be a spot check on 3/17/2025 to ensure that this equipment has been repaired and is properly functioning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The following areas throughout the facility are in need of a cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The fan of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes.
2. REPEAT- The bottom of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes. 
3. REPEAT- The fans in the walk-in cooler. 
4. The bottom of the bar cooler. 

Ensure that these areas are cleaned and maintained cleaned by next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The floor of the walk-in freezer. 
2. REPEAT- The floor throughout the bar area, specifically underneath the equipment.
3. The floors underneath the cook line. 
4. The floors underneath the back prep area/sink. 
5. The floors underneath the drink station. 
6. The ceiling tiles above the steamer as there is mold growth due to the large amounts of steam coming from the steamer. This will be checked on during the 3/17/2025 spot check that is scheduled to ensure it has been cleaned. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities are observed to need repaired: 

1. The drink station needs re-caulked to the wall. 
2. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the left of the dish area. 
3. REPEAT- The handwashing sink on the end of the cook line needs re-caulked. 
4. REPEAT- There is a piece of broken coving in the walk-in freezer next to the door. 
5. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the right of the walk-in cooler entrance.
6. There are holes in the wall above the handwashing sink near the entrance door to the kitchen. These holes need caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
7. The triple sink next to the ice machine needs re-caulked. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should remain in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
4-202.18 Ventilation Hood Systems, Filters. Filters or other grease extracting EQUIPMENT shall be designed to be readily removable for cleaning and replacement if not designed to be cleaned in place. 

The facility is observed to be using a steamer that is in a state of disrepair. It is creating large amounts of steam that is leading to black mold growth on the ceiling tiles above this area. If this equipment is not repaired and is going to continue to be used, there needs to be a ventilation hood that will prevent this mold growth and allow for proper ventilation. This is combined with the 3/17/2025 spot check as this equipment either needs repaired to function properly or a ventilation hood is needed.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Pink mold accumulation was observed on the baffle of the ice machine. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized the baffle of the ice machine. Clean the ice machine as often as necessary to prevent mold growth.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: A sauce was observed stored in a 5-gallon bucket that originally contained chemicals. CORRECTED- PIC will cease the use of chemical buckets for food storage.
citation_text: 3-305.11 (A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: A piece of cardboard used to line the bottom shelf of the walk-in freezer has become soiled and needs to be replaced. CORRECTED- PIC replaced the cardboard. If cardboard is used to line shelves, ensure it is changed regularly and does not become soiled or degraded.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handsink near the dish machine is not sealed to the wall. Recaulk the handsink so it is sealed to the wall and no gap is present.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
No food handler certificate is available for the food employee working in the kitchen during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates available on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). 

It was observed that the dish machine is not reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of above 150F. A follow up is scheduled for 2/10/2025 to ensure that the dish machine is reaching a temperature of above 160F. Ensure that dish machines are properly sanitizing dishes by reaching a temperature of 160F or above.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives and pans in the kitchen are observed with remaining food debris on them as they are in storage as ready-for-use. These items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage/use. It is highly suggested that the dish washers are educated to review dishes after washing and prior to storage.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

The scoop holder for the ice machine is observed with contaminants in the standing water at the bottom. The ice scoop sits in this holder consistently throughout the day. The item and contaminants were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are cleaned regularly and specifically whenever contamination has occurred.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests.

Numerous flies are observed in the dish and hand sink areas of the kitchen. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agent (Orkin) for help in remediating the situation. A follow-up will be conducted in three weeks to allow for remediation to take affect throughout the life cycle of the flies observed.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The floor in the dry storage area has dried spills and debris observed. These areas should be cleaned often enough to prevent soilage from accumulating. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

A mostly empty gallon of milk has a manufacturers use by date of 1/29/25 and a facility date mark of 1-20. Today is day 10 since opening and one day over the manufacturers date. The PIC was shown and discarded the container during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are discarded within seven days of opening and prior to the manufacturers use by date.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a can of butane fuel stored on a top shelf above various foods (including, but not limited too, seasoning, sauces, maple syrup, icing, sugar, and flour). The butane fuel was removed from the location and moved to the dry storage area. Ensure that chemicals are always stored separate from food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service -and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bar soda nozzle holder had an accumulation of soil and other debris. The soda holder was removed from service and washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector immediately educated the employee when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier it always used to turn off the faucet to avoid contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed an employee grab toast from the toaster and place it on a plate for serving with their bare hands. The PIC was immediately notified when the action was observed. The PIC stated that the facility had recently ran out of gloves and more were on order. The inspector explained the importance of immediate action to ensure a barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods. The PIC placed a pair of tongs by the toaster and another employee went to the store to purchase gloves. The employee returned with the gloves during the inspection. Ensure that gloves or another barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw hamburger meat stored above various vegetables in the right prep cooler bottom. An employee moved the raw meat below the vegetables during the inspection. The inspector explained the importance of storing raw foods underneath any ready-to eat foods to avoid contamination. Ensure that foods are always stored according to the proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sanitizer bucket under the grill was testing at 10 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. After the PIC remade the bucket it was testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector suggests increasing the frequency that sanitizer buckets are changed. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (chlorine = 50-200 ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed two containers of soup in the walk-in cooler had exceeded the 7-day maximum. The soups had a date mark indicating the food was prepared on 1/20/2025 meaning it should have been discarded on 1/26/2025. The PIC was notified and the soup was discarded during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of discarding foods after 7 days (the day the food is prepared being day 1). Ensure that foods are always discarded when they exceed the 7-day maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the caulking behind the spray nozzle table to the left of the dish machine is not attached to the wall and is degrading in quality. The caulking must be removed and replaced with fresh caulking. Due to the area being subject to high amounts of moisture the caulking must be repaired/replaced frequently. Ensure the caulking is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness expired in August 2024. The PIC stated they were unaware it had expired and they will schedule a new training. No one else present at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the PIC has a certificate in allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: No paper towels were available at the kitchen handsink upon inspector’s arrival. Employees recognized the lack of paper towels and retrieved towels from another location to dry hands, but did not replace the paper towels at the handsink. CORRECTED- Upon request, paper towels were provided at the kitchen handwashing sink. Ensure towels are always available at handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The kitchen dish machine was found to reach a plate temperature of 143F after two cycles. On the second cycle, the dish machine began leaking suds. PIC called to request maintenance on the machine to fix the leak and adjust the rinse temperature. Ensure the rinse temperature is sufficient to reach 180F from the baffle or achieve a surface temperature of 160F, as measured on an irreversible registering temperature indicator.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a way to verify that the dish machine is reaching sanitizing temperature. Ensure that an irreversible, maximum registering thermometer or heat-sensitive stickers are available to monitor the dish machine function.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a bucket of pickles left uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC placed the lid back on the bucket of pickles. Ensure foods that are being stored are protected from-cross contamination at all times; in this case, placing a lid on the bucket is sufficient.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC had an employee start cleaning the microwave immediately. Ensure the microwave is kept clean to prevent cross-contamination between foods.
citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of food residues on the milkshake mixer arms and machine surface. Discussed with PIC. PIC had the machine cleaned immediately. Ensure all food-contact areas on equipment are kept clean and sanitary.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed several non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning. 

The hot holding in the back of the kitchen has an accumulation of soils on the machine surfaces. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the machine builds up hard-water soils as water evaporates on the machine. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly to eliminate buildup of soils.

The corner of the dish line between the dish machine and the sink/sprayer combo was observed to have a large amount of soils. Discussed with PIC, recommended a cleaning regiment that includes that area as a frequently visited spot. Ensure that this area is cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.

Underneath the dish machine was observed to have a build up of soils. Discussed with PIC and recommended a cleaning regiment that includes the dish machine area as part of regular cleaning. Ensure this area is cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soils and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed there to still be an ice-buildup problem in the walk-in freezer. The lines have been repaired, as requested in the previous inspection. However, the buildup of ice persists to a lesser extent. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the machine is serviced to prevent this buildup of ice.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the bar hand washing sink did not have soap when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided the hand sink with soap during the inspection. Ensure that every hand washing sink always has soap available for the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw meat stored over onions and cooked food in the walk-in cooler. An employee moved the raw meat below the ready-to-eat foods during the inspection. Ensure that food is stored according to the proper storage order to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the steam table was not holding foods at 135F or higher when the inspector arrived. The internal temperature of beans was 120F, queso was 125F, and rice was 120F. An employee turned up the temperature of the steam table during the inspection. When the inspector re-checked the temperatures the internal temperature of the queso was 135F and beans was 140F. The PIC was reminded that temperatures must be checked on a regular basis using a probe thermometer. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the employee cleaning dishes in the triple sink was not properly using the wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure. The employee had a bucket filled with soap which they were using to wash the dishes and then rising in clean water before air drying. The inspector educated the PIC and employee about the proper procedure. Dishes must be first washed in soap, then rinsed in clean water, and lastly sanitized in a combination of water and the chosen sanitizer at the correct concentration. After education, the employee had three buckets set up for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing and was utilizing the proper technique. Ensure that dishes always undergo the proper wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure to keep food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed butane fuel stored on a shelf above the sushi prep cooler. The PIC was educated and moved the butane fuel to a new location. Ensure that toxic materials are stored in a position where they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single-use articles.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish thawing at room temperature during the inspection. The PIC moved the fish into the cooler during the inspection. They were educated on the importance of thawing using an approved technique (i.e, under continuous running water, inside a cooler, as part of the cooking process, or in the microwave). Ensure that foods are always thawed properly.
citation_text: 3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a cell phone stored above the back prep cooler leaning against clean dishes and a personal drink stored on a wire shelf above an open container of food. The cell phone was removed from the location and the personal drink was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are always stored away from food and food prep areas.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed the employee working does not have food handler training completed. The PIC was instructed that all employees hired over 30 days ago must receive training in food handling principles. Ensure that the employee completes the training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the front cold holding cooler to be at 58F. Discussed with PIC, cooler was not turned on. Cooler was turned on and ran a temperature of 41F. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. After adding a capful of bleach the sanitizer bucket was testing at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded the PIC of the importance of testing sanitizing solutions on a regular basis and re-making them as needed. Ensure that sanitizing solutions always test between 50-200 ppm (Cl).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed the beach at the facility does not have an EPA registration. The inspector educated about the importance of using food grade bleach at the facility. The inspector will follow-up on 1/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has bleach with an EPA registration.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several foods stored in cardboard boxes or containers directly on the floor. The locations of food stored on the floor included the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and underneath the front counter. The PIC stated they are in the process of purchasing more shelving and pallets. During the inspection some pallets for underneath the front counter arrived. Ensure that foods are always stored at least 6-inches above the floor to protect food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed the single use utensils by the takeout window were stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces. During the inspection the utensils were moved into a different container to allow the handles to be stored vertically. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored properly.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:

The PIC and inspector had a conversation about sealing (ex. paint) all the exposed wood to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. They were also reminded that any other bare wood exposed throughout the facility due to ongoing construction must also be sealed. Ensure that all surfaces remain smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

(2) The edging piece that is coming off the wall to the right of the front hand washing sink must be re-attached to the wall.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

comment:
Facility could not provide proof of food handler certifications for employees. Ensure that employees who are not manager certified obtain a food handler certification if handling food.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.

citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored with food contact surface faced upward along the cookline. Discussed with PIC proper storage technique. Ensure that clean utensils are stored with the handles facing upward to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(B) Kitchenware and Tableware. (B) Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and by CONSUMERS if CONSUMER self service is provided.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The back outside door was observed propped open. Discussed with PIC and door was shut. Ensure that doors are never propped open top avoid the entry of unwanted insects and pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Chicken in a sink was observed to be thawing improperly. There wasn’t a constant flow of running water. Discussed with PIC and running water was provided. If using the running water thawing method, be sure to always have a constant flow of running water at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
