Shredded mozzarella and mushrooms were observed to be improperly stored on ice. The ice method is being used to cold hold these food items. The containers of food were pushed further down into the ice so that the bottom and sides are
covered with ice. Be sure that containers are completely covered with ice to ensure that foods are at the proper cold holding temperature.
citation_text: 301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food separated and protected.

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the behavior and reminded PIC to wash hands, which they did, then donned gloves to continue work. Ensure employees wash hands after any task that may have contaminated them and before donning gloves.

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [Pf]

citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education is conducted in house for dish washers to ensure that food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the front portion of the left roller had ambient food temperatures of about 68-74F. Upon investigation the PIC noticed that the front portion was turned off. The back portion of the roller was turned on and had an ambient air temperature of about 150F. The PIC discarded the food on the front portion of the roller and turned on the roller during the inspection. When the roller was checked at the end of the inspection the ambient air was 180F. Ensure that temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed the pizzas at the front were not properly marked for time-as-control. When pizzas are brought from the back a sticker is placed above which indicates when the pizza was prepared and when it must be discarded. The pizzas currently on display did not have a sticker. The PIC and inspector discussed the importance of identifying the 4-hour window for time-as-control. The PIC voluntarily discarded the pizzas during the inspection. The newly made pizzas were properly marked with a sticker. Ensure when using time-as-control the time is marked to indicate when the 4-hour window has passed and food must be discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several foods stored on the floor throughout the facility. The foods stored on the floor included: (1) Boxes of sliced banana peppers and various cans on the floor adjacent to the back hand sink; and (2) Boxes of food (including, but not limited too, creamer and pastries) stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler. Ensure that foods are stored at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One of the kitchen employees isn't food manager or food handler certified. Ensure that employees who handle food are handler certified if not manager certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. 

There are prepackaged cuts of meat, smoked fish parts, and frozen produce in the facility that are not labeled with the common name of the product or the cooking instructions. All food needs to be labeled with the common name of the product and all meat needs labeled with cooking instructions. Discussed placing a general cooking instructions label on the outside of the freezers. Discussed reaching out to supplier about labels for the cuts of meat. Ensure that produce that is placed into a bag to be froze has the common name of the product. A follow up is scheduled on 2/19/2025 to ensure that all of these items have been labeled.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Daylight is visible along the bottom edge of the back door. Weather stripping is missing from that area. Replace the weather stripping on the back door so it is tight-fitting and daylight is not visible along the edges.
citation_text: 6-202.15(C) Outer Openings, Protected. (C) Exterior doors used as exits need not be self-closing if they are: (1) Solid and tight-fitting. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
PIC present at the beginning of this inspection has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. CORRECTED- A CFM with allergen training arrived near the end of this inspection. Ensure a CFM with allergen training is present during all shifts of food prep and service.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the PIC dump a bucket of water containing food debris into the hand washing sink. The PIC was educated about only using the hand washing sink for washing hands. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed several dented cans on the can holding rack outside of the walk-in cooler. The cans were set aside and the PIC was educated about the importance of removing dented cans during the inspection. The PIC was instructed to remind all employees on the facility’s procedure for removing dented cans. Ensure that packages are always in good condition to protect food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several foods (including, but not limited too, cooked chicken, cooked rice, and cut vegetables) stored uncovered in the walk-in cooler. The uncovered items were covered during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always covered to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:
(1) The baffles of the ice machine were soiled with debris. The baffles were cleaned to sight and touch during the inspection. The baffles must be cleaned regularly to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
(2) Cutting boards stored behind the faucets of the triple sink and dump sink. Storing cutting boards in this position presents the risk of contamination from food debris or water splashes. The cutting boards were removed from behind the faucets and were placed in new location away from potential contamination. 
Ensure that food contact surfaces are always kept clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed fryer and oil cleaner stored above clean dishes and WD-40 stored adjacent to food. Both of the chemicals were moved to shelves where they cannot pose the risk of contamination during the inspection. Ensure that toxic materials are stored separate from food and utensils.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, and tempura batter) in large containers without a label. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that foods not in their original packaging and easily mistakable are always labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed single-use utensils at the front service area stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The PIC corrected the storage during the inspection. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to avoid contaminating the food contact portion. Ensure that single-use utensils are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the floor directly underneath the fryers has an accumulation of grease and food debris. The inspector suggests pulling out the fryers to clean underneath. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal employee drinks stored on shelves intermingled with and above various food products and clean dishes. The PIC removed all the personal drinks and placed them on a bottom shelf which will be designated as the ‘personal storage shelf’. Ensure that all personal employee items are placed in designated areas.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training is expired. No one else at the facility has completed the training. Ensure that the PIC completes training in basic allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the hand sink by the juice machines was observed to have running water flowing through a catch tray that appears to be from one of the juice machines. Designated hand sinks are to be used for only hand washing and no other task per code. The PIC was shown and removed the tray to correct. Education is suggested for staff to ensure that this situation does not persist in the future.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

A package of raw chicken is observed on top of a package of pre-cooked chicken in the walk in cooler. The PIC saw it and removed the RTE chicken immediately to correct the violation. Education was conducted. Ensure that RTE TCS foods are stored above raw items in the coolers.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(F)(1) and (2) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket available in the kitchen at the time of this inspection would not register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure all in use sanitizers in the facility are maintained at effective levels at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a broken piece of framing around the AC unit in the 4th floor dry storage room. This leaves an opening to the outside through which pests could enter the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to have repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. 

The gasket on the door for the walk in freezer is pulling away from the door. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Of the kitchen staff that does not have a CFPM only one has food handler training on file. A conversation took place with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all food handlers that do not have a CFPM have completed food handler training prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels available at the kitchen handwashing sink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Upon request, staff refilled the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Grease or food was observed spilled on the lower shelf of the clean equipment shelves near the mop sink. Clean this area.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Three mops were observed stored with the mop-ends piled in the mop sink basin. Another mop was observed stored in dirty mop water in a nearby mop bucket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use, and that mops are stored to promote air-drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Food debris was observed under the counter in the multi-use hallway area near the soda syrups. Sweep and clean under equipment.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The bottom of the yogurt cooler was observed to have an accumulation of trash on the lining. The facility uses a paper lining at the bottom of the coolers. The facility is getting new coolers soon and it was recommended to make sure that the bottom of those coolers stay clean and that the lining is changed more often. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained cleaned.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager.

A the time of this inspection there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. The PIC was consulted and stated that the one they have on staff starts next week. A copy of the known local courses is being attached to this report and the PIC is instructed to insure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW.

During this inspection the PIC could not produce verification that employees were notified of their responsibility to report illnesses and symptoms related to foodborne illness. A copy of the Reporting Agreement given out by this facility was found in the paperwork given during the pre-opening. Another copy is being attached to the email of this report. The PIC is instructed to have all food employees sign a a copy and maintain the copies at this facility moving forward.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans of foods are observed with significant dents. Education was conducted with the PIC and the noted cans separated out for discard/credit. Ensure that all food packaging is in good condition until use.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw chicken is observed over raw vegetables in the three door cooler in the prep room. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-aranged during this inspection to correct. A hand out is being attached to the emailed report for an added visual.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

A bus tub of onions is observed on a shelf under cleaners, degreasers and bleach. Storage was discussed with the PIC and the container moved to correct. Ensure that all chemicals are stored in a manner that does not pose a risk of contamination for foods.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location.

Two knives are observed being stored in the gap between two coolers. This gap is not able to be cleaned/sanitized. Education was provided and a new storage practice will be needed for these items. The items were moved to dish to correct the immediate violation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

A CL (bleach) based sanitizer is used in the facility. Only test strips effective for use with Quat sanitizers are available for checking the concentration of sanitizer solutions. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that the test strips and sanitizers match prior to the follow up.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Ceiling tiles above the bathroom, sink, mop sink and prep areas are of the acoustic type and are not acceptable for food preparation or moist locations. The PIC was consulted and will be replacing as able moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The triple sink has a small gap between it and the wall that could allow for moisture and mold growth. The PIC was consulted and instructed to seal (caulking suggested) prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

A the time of this inspection food handler training certificates are not available for the food handlers in the facility. Training was discussed and the PIC is instructed to have the training completed by the staff and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs).

Allergen awareness training certification is not available for the only CFPM available at the facility. Education was conducted and a pair of hand outs attached to the emailed report. Ensure that the CFPMs at this facility have also completed allergen awareness training and the certificates are available moving forward.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) Dust on the walk-in cooler fans; and (2) Grease in between the fryers on the cook line. Ensure these areas are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed an employee storing their cell phone on a shelf adjacent to the pizza & salad prep cooler holding clean plates and utensils. The employee was educated and they removed their phone from the location. Ensure that personal items are stored away from food prep areas to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The facility continues to have gaps around the base of the back door, specifically on the bottom right. There was discussion of using a solid material along the outside of the door instead of steel wool (which was repeatedly falling out). The door needs to be repaired to prevent the entrance of pests. The door is not used for deliveries and is able to be relatively sealed.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Paint around the front counter handsink is chipped and deteriorating. Repaint the walls around the front counter handsink so the wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a leak in the ceiling in the middle of the kitchen (not over any food prep/storage). Per PIC, the landlord has been notified and is getting estimates for repairs. In the meantime, a bucket has been placed to catch the drip. Repair the ceiling to eliminate the leak.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. REPEAT- The soda nozzles in the buffet area have a buildup of black soil residue on them. The facility stated in the past that the syrup causes this buildup. It is recommended to reach out to Coke to see if there is a way to fix this issue or it is recommended to scrub them daily to avoid this build up. Clear soda nozzles are also a recommended option to be able to easily see this build up to clean it. CORRECTED- These soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. 

 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. There is not an air thermometer in the coolers in the grab and go section or in the yogurt cooler in the buffet area. Ensure that there is always a temperature measuring device in all refrigerated and hot food storage units to measure the air temperature. 

(A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. There are single service plates by the buffet area and bowls by the cereal area that were stored in a manner that exposes them to contamination. CORRECTED- These items were inverted during the inspection. Ensure that all single service articles are stored inverted to protect them from contamination. 

 (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: 1st REPEAT: A carton of raw shell eggs was observed on the top shelf of the 2 door cooler, above bread, cream cheese, and salad dressing. CORRECTED- PIC removed the eggs and voluntarily discarded them. The eggs were delivered by accident and are not used in the facility. Ensure raw shell eggs are stored below ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Foods in the countertop cooler were observed above 41F. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. PIC stated that the sliced cheese, veggie sausage, and ham were stocked in the cooler about 30 minutes prior to initial checks. Temperatures had not changed 30 minutes later, 1 hour after foods were placed in the cooler. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were moved to a functional cooler to quickly cool to 41F or below. Ensure TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A spray bottle of Clorox Scentiva disinfectant was observed stored on the countertop in the back kitchen area, where food is prepared. CORRECTED- The spray bottle was moved to storage away from food prep surfaces. The disinfectant is used on the cash register countertop, not for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The countertop cooler is not holding foods at 41F or below. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. Discussed turning down the cooler temperature or moving TCS foods to the nearby prep cooler that is holding foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: 1st REPEAT: An ice scoop in the small ice bin was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Discussed proper storage with staff and PIC. Store ice scoops so that the handle does not touch the ice, and the scoop can be used without touching the ice.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: No prepared sanitizer bucket was available during this inspection. CORRECTED- Upon request, a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure sanitizer buckets are prepared before beginning to engage in food prep, and refreshed as needed throughout the day.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a bare wood 2x4 on the wall holding a syrups rack on the wall. Paint or otherwise seal the bare wood so it is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. The sani buckets in the facility do not register on the inspector test strips at the beginning of the inspection. title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment:

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Three buckets and one pan of cheese sauce were not cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours. The cheese sauce was finished cooking at 11:30am. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands briefly (approximately 5 seconds) and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. The observed procedures also only rubbed the palm and palm side of the fingers. Proper hand washing was discussed with the PIC (and employee) and they are instructed to ensure that safe hand washing takes place at all times. Wash all of the hands to include between fingers, under fingernails and the top of the hands to ensure that all possible contaminants are removed. Then use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet in order to prevent recontaminating the hands prior to food handling.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
All staff members were observed practicing improper handwashing technique and frequency. Hands were washed in non-handwashing sinks, without using proper barriers, for durations too short to be effective, and without proper hand soap usage. Hands were not washing following potentially contaminating actions and activities such as touching head/hair, putting hands in pockets, using personal phones and other devices, blowing/wiping noses, and others. 

Inspector is present due to the concern of a foodborne illness being contracted as this establishment. Viruses and other pathogens are easily spread by touch from the contaminated hands of staff. To prevent additional illness from occurring, the facility MUST enforce proper hand washing procedure and frequency as follows:

- Hands must be washed EVERY TIME contamination has occurred. Discuss with staff the need to be aware of what they are touching, if the surfaces they touch are cleaned and sanitized, and if not, that hands are immediately washed. Personal devices, insides of clothing, and areas of the body are not cleaned and sanitized surfaces and once touched ALWAYS requires that staff wash hands afterward. Wiping noses is an EXTREMELY hazardous behavior and should NEVER occur in the kitchen and must ALWAYS be followed up with proper hand washing.

- Hands must be washed with active scrubbing for a minimum of 20 seconds.
- Hand soap must be used every time hands are washed.
- Hands may only be washed in designated hand washing sinks, never a triple sink, dump sink, disk sink or utility sink. 
- A barrier such as a paper towel must be used to turn off the faucet. If staff fails to use a barrier to turn off the faucet, hands must be immediately rewashed.

** Gloves are NOT an alternative to proper hand washing.

title: Food separated and protected

- Multiple staff members were observed touching body parts or clothing and continuing to work with food and/or food-contact surfaces.
- Exiting the facility and returning without proper hand washing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed staff preparing drinks with bare hand contact of the food-contact surface of single-use plastic cups without proper handwashing occurring. Discussed with person-in-charge the need to wash hands frequently and/or avoid bare hand contact with any food-contact surfaces. Inspector observed these behaviors during an extremely busy rush which has been taken into consideration during the preparation of this report. However, it is during these rushes when the greatest number of consumers are served and the need for hand washing and avoiding bare-hand contact is most necessary. Discuss with staff the proper frequency for hand washing, even during such rushes, and the need to avoid any bare hand contact with the lips of cups where consumers place their mouths to drink to prevent hand-to-mouth contamination. Person-in-charge verified that the discussion would be held with staff and that the behavior will be corrected. Corrected-on-site. No follow-up required. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wiping cloths (bar rags) must be stored in sanitizer when not actively being used. These rags may never be stored on countertops or other surfaces during food (drink) service. Wet rags allow bacterial growth to occur rapidly in the rags which are then used to wipe surfaces. These rags are also handled by staff members who were not washing hands frequently during service and then touching the lips of single-service cups used to serve customers. Any bacteria or other pathogens present on these rags are then transferred to the lips of cups. This contamination is a source of foodborne illness. Ensure that wet wiping cloths (rags) are stored properly in sanitizer which has been tested to ensure proper concentration of chemical sanitizer in the solution. Inspector discussed this requirement with person-in-charge who confirmed understanding and assured future compliance with this requirement. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Mold is observed int he soda gun holder with the soda gun nozzle stored in it. Although the soda gun holder is a nonfood-contact surface requiring less frequent cleaning, the soda gun nozzle is a food-contact surface and requires frequent cleaning and sanitization to prevent contamination of foods served to consumers. Ensure that the soda gun holder and soda gun are cleaned and sanitized and remain as such. Additionally, the white upright freezer at the bar used to store glasses has a large accumulation of ice on the shelves. Operator states that this freezer is manually defrosted on a weekly basis and it cannot be defrosted daily. Inspector instructed operator to store glasses in the freezer with the lips of the glasses out of the ice to prevent contamination of this food-contact surface. However, operator must keep in mind that if these glasses are stored face up and ice is allowed to accumulate above them, this constitutes a violation as well because food-contact surfaces must be stored in a manner that protects from contamination. It is recommended that facility replace the freezer to ensure future compliance. A follow-up is issued for 01/02/2024 to determine compliance with food-contact surface cleaning and sanitization.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed several areas of concern in the back room where the triple sink and soda are stored. Under the triple sink, inspector observed a dead mouse amongst many droppings and nesting material. To the right of the dead mouse was a hole approximately 2 inches wide and 3/4 of an inch tall where mice have been able to enter and exit the room. Near the soda boxes, inspector observed large amounts of soda syrup splashed on the floor, walls, ceiling and ceiling vents. In this area, x3 dead and decaying mouse corpses were observed. One of the three was stuck to an old, heavily soiled glue trap. One was stuck to the back of the right-rear leg of the soda shelving. And the third was on the floor under the shelving. Enormous amounts of mouse droppings were observed on these shelves and at the floor/wall junction in these areas. A drain in the area was heavily soiled with residue/debris and mouse droppings. A dead mouse was also observed behind numerous stacked boxes of liquor along with mouse droppings too numerous to count near the rodent corpse and along the floor/wall junction in this area.

Due to these observations, inspector contacted the SCDPH Environmental Health Director (AA) and requested additional assistance with enforcement. AA arrived at the facility. Inspector AM arrived shortly after. 

AA spoke with operator. Operator stated that pest control is present on a monthly basis. A report was provided from 12/8/2023 which showed that pest control was presented and treated for multiple pests/insects including the placement of glue traps and bait.

Inspector pointed out additional areas of concern including numerous shelves, boxes and countertops with mouse droppings observed in both the back room and the section behind the soda counter where the soda fountain drain is located. At this time, due to the severity of the rodent infestation within the facility, SCDPH Environmental Health Director (AA) informed the operator that the facilities permit to serve food is being suspended effective immediately until the pest problem is under control and cleaning has occurred. Facility may continue to serve fully pre-packaged foods but the soda fountain, slushy machines, and coffee machines MAY NOT be used until approval is granted by SCDPH. Operator is to contact third-party PCO and contact SCDPH inspector to ensure that inspector can be there for planning and/or discuss plans with the PCO. Inspector will return on 12/26/2023 to evaluate progress and discuss plans for elimination of pests within the facility.

Additional mouse droppings, insects and harborage conditions were observed ubiquitously throughout the rest of the facility.

THIS IS A REPEAT VIOALTINO FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 9/13/2022.

Caulking has not been completed on the back of the triple sink as cited during the previous inspection. Surfaces subject to food/water must be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable to prevent hard-to-reach areas from becoming soiled. Ensure that all surfaces subject to food/water are SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 12/08/2021. 

Inspector observed mop heads stored on the base of the utility sink. Mops must be stored in a manner which prevents contamination and facilitates air drying. Mops may be stored in the top portion of the mop bucket and/or hanging inverted along the wall. Ensure that mops are stored properly by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink at the start of the inspection was observed to be blocked by various items. When this was noted to the PIC, all items in the hand sink were removed, thus resulting in the hand sink being accessible. Ensure the hand sink remains accessible during all hours of operation and is only used for hand washing. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: At the start of the inspection, the cutting boards were observed to be stored against the back portion of the double sink faucet which is a contamination hazard for the surfaces being stored on them and a potential contamination of hands touching the surface of the cutting boards when the sink is used. The PIC has moved these boards from this location to a more appropriate location to not pose a contamination hazard. The PIC will be finding a new place to store the cutting boards to air dry without posing a contaminants hazard. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: There was a knife observed stored between the magnetic knife strip and the wall. This knife was removed and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that knives are stored properly on the magnetic strip to prevent contamination of the food contact surface.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

Ensure that a sanitizer bucket is readily available during all hours of operation and tested to ensure proper concentrations.  
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Two employees were actively working in the kitchen during the inspection. One staff member washed hands one time. The other staff member did not wash hands at all despite repeatedly switching from cleaning to food preparation throughout the inspection AND returning from smoking. Hand washing MUST BE occurring frequently to prevent contamination of foods in the facility. A discussion was held with operator who will discuss with staff the importance of hand washing. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

Sanitizer buckets in the kitchen and at the sushi bar measured 0 ppm (cl) during inspection.  PIC added more bleach to the buckets, bringing the concentration to 100 ppm. title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:

Rice was just recently prepared and labeled during inspection. PIC was advised to ensure staff are properly labeling sushi rice as soon as it is removed from the cooker and placed in the sushi prep area for use. Time control is used, and time must be properly tracked for each portion prepared during hours of operation.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control.

comment:

comment:

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
Staff were observed drinking from plastic bottles in the kitchen and near the food prepared in the cashier area during the inspection. Ensure that personal food/drink is not consumed in any food service areas of the facility.

comment:
Inspector did not observe ANY hand washing occurring during the inspection despite staff switching tasks repeatedly. Gloves were used but gloves are not a substitute for hand washing. title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

Inspector observed three hand sinks in the facility. The second hand sink was to the right of the fryer and behind a metal table completed inaccessible and dry indicating it has not been used. The last hand sink was in the bathroom which was stocked with hand soap but no paper towels. None of the three hand sinks were properly stocked and/or accessible to employees to ensure hand washing is occurring. Facility was provided with hand washing signs and have chosen to designated the right hand sink and bathroom hand sink as designated hand sinks. title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Inspector did not observe any date marking on thawed products in the cooler. Thawed, prepared products held for longer than 24 hours must be properly date marked to indicate when thawed/prepared and/or a date by which to discard. This date marking must be consistent. When asked if the product was cycled within 24 hours, operator responded by saying that the product usually used within 24 hours. Usually means that the item is not consistently used within a 24 hour period and must be date marked accordingly. A follow-up is issued for 12/20/2023 for date marking within the facility.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

comment:
Chemical sanitizer was kept in an unlabeled metal container with no distinction between the sanitizer container and containers used for food service. A follow-up is issued for 12/20/2023 to ensure that sanitizer is labeled properly.

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Inspector observed the thawing of shrimp in a metal container in the utility/hand washing sink to the left of the fryers/cooler. Utility sinks used for mop buckets and dumping are not appropriate for thawing of foods. Additionally, foods thawed in water must be retained below 41 degrees in running cold water. The water in the sink was not running on arrival. Ensure that proper thawing occurs at all times. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. comment:

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Inspector observed temperature via infrared in the dairy cooler exceeding 41 degrees F. Temperatures ranged from 45 to 50 degrees F via probe. Items held out of temperature include but are not limited cheeses, yogurts, Jello and other dairy products. Inspector checked different areas of large yogurt containers to determine if foods have exceeded 41 degrees for an extended period of time. Operator contacted technician who arrived and stated that the cooler has been in defrost since approximately 1:00 pm. The cooler is scheduled to defrost at this time for x1 hour. However, the cooler malfunctioned and was "stuck in defrost" since 1:00 pm. Temperatures were checked by inspector at approximately 2:30. No food temperatures exceeded 50 degrees F and all temperatures following corrective action were trending downward. Technician ensured that the cooler is now functioning properly. Additionally, operator spoke with technician and informed inspector that the monitoring temperature on the coolers was set to notify them at 60 degrees F. This has been corrected so that facility will be notified if temperatures exceed the 41 degree threshold. Violation has been corrected on site. No additional follow-up required.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Inspector observed cartons of milk in the milk cooler adjacent to the dry storage area to be holding between 45 and 55 degrees F for an unknown period of time. Logs indicate temperature abuse with no corrective actions on 11/3 (42F), 11/6 (45F), 11/9 (42) and 11/13 (45). A hanging thermometer was placed in the cooler but was damaged and not functioning properly. comment:

comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed mouse droppings throughout the facility. The droppings had a lustrous appearance indicating that they are fresh and were accompanied by evident mouse footprints present in the foods in the dry storage area. Mouse droppings were observed in plastic containers of dry foods, on boxes of dry foods, on an open plate with a dry food in the employee food storage area, on pans and other cookware, in the corners of the walls/floors in the kitchen and dry storage areas, on countertops, and diffusely through the junk storage area. The smell of urine was observed by both inspector and SCDPH supervisor in the dry storage and junk storage areas. Due to the ubiquitous presence of mouse droppings throughout the facility, SCDPH EH director AA was contacted to visit the facility to establish next steps. AA discussed with PIC the conditions at the facitlity, preventive measure and corrective actions. AA advised PIC that the facility may remain open but must deep clean all areas with mouse droppings and adjust the frequency of cleaning and pest control to eliminate the rodent problem within the facility. Inspector observed several holes/gaps in the front and rear doors to the facility that are sufficiently large to allow entry of pests into the facility. The facility must seal these holes to prevent entry from these exterior areas. Foods must be sealed properly in plastic containers to prevent further infestation. comment:
(P) 2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handle of dispenser was touched to dispense paper towels after handwahsing occurred, and paper towels were used to shut off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. Handwashing technique was discussed. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process and use paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the manual faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if additional towels need to be dispensed. Elbows and forearms may also be used to touch the handle to dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
(Pf) 3-501.19 (A) & (B) Portions of fried chicken pieces and fried tofu were not being properly hot held. Products were observed out on a prep table with surface and internal temperatures ranging from 83F-97F. PIC indicated the intent was to prepare small portions and hold them at room temperature for use. PIC stated the products are typically gone within an hour or a little longer. Based on information provided, tofu was fried around 12pm and chicken was fried around 1pm. Foods were labeled with the time and were to be used or discarded within 4 hours. PIC was advised a time control policy will be established and a copy will be provided at the followup inspection in 10 days. 
Except as specified under (D) of this section, if time without temperature control is used as the public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food before cooking, or for ready to eat TCS food that is displayed or held for sale or service: (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request that specify: (a) Methods of compliance with Subparagraphs (B)(1)-(4) or (C)(1)-(5) of this section; and (b) Methods of compliance with § 3-501.14 for food that is prepared, cooked, and refrigerated before time is used as a public health control. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) The food shall have an initial temperature of 41F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control; (2) The food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; (3) The food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready to eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; and (4) The food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

comment: Styrofoam containers on the outside table are stored with the food contact surfaces facing up/ exposed. The items were flipped over to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the 3 compartment sink in the kitchen to have 0 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Several tests were taken with test strips with multiple fills/disposal of the basin. Inspector showed PIC. New bucket of sanitizer was put on recently. It appears the line is not pulling the sanitizer through to the dispenser. Discussed with PIC. PIC is contacting maintenance to rectify the issue. Inspector will follow-up on 10/10/23.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E).

Discussed with employee. Discard bread. Ensure all staff is aware that naan bread must be handled with single-use gloves. COS.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used.
