Observed no hot water at the kitchen hand sink. The hand sink has a broken cold water faucet. The hot water faucet is working; however, the water is coming out as a small stream, not at full force, and the water is cold. No hot water appears to be available at the hand sink. Hand washing can still occur. A plumber needs to repair the hand sink so it functions correctly. Cold water faucet should be repaired and the hot water tap should provide hot water. Water pressure should be akin to a regular hand sink’s water pressure. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 10/17/23 (facility is closed on Monday’s).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces to be soiled with debris:
1. The ceiling of the ice machine has a layer of black and pink mold. Inspector showed PIC. The ice should be removed and the basin (including the ceiling) should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
2. The soda gun nozzle was stuck to the gun itself. Mold was visible on the gun once removed. The soda nozzle holder also had a layer of mold. Inspector showed employees both issues. 

Discussed areas of mold growth with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean these areas: wash, rinse, sanitize. Clean as needed to prevent mold accumulation. Inspector will follow-up on 10/17/23. Staff was actively beginning to clean the above areas during the inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed many items within the walk-in cooler to lack date marking. Employee/cook walked with Inspector and could tell Inspector when items were made. Inspector asked employee to date mark all items (ex: chicken, curry, etc.). Employee date marked the items. Ensure staff is actively date marking food items and discarding within a 7-day period. Inspector will follow-up on 10/17/23 to verify staff is date marking foods.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

(REPEAT) Observed chicken (and potatoes) in large containers to be directly on the floor of the walk-in cooler under the shelving units. Cease practice. Ensure all food items are at least 6 inches off the floor and on top of the shelving units of the walk-in cooler. Discussed with employee/cook. Employee moved the chicken (and potatoes) to the bottom shelves of the walk-in cooler. COS.

Ensure the lids are placed on the chicken. Several had lids, several did not. Food should be protected against cross contamination. Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the walk-in freezer to have several issues:
1. The gasket/seal is coming away from the door. Repair.
2. The fan is dripping water and there is ice ponding. 
3. The door handle is being held closed with a screw driver. Repair the door handle.

Discussed issues with PIC. The majority of the shelving has a layer of ice. It could be from the door not properly sealing (gasket is broken, door handle is being held shut with a screw driver). Ensure repairs are conducted before the next routine inspection.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no active sani buckets during the inspection. Inspector asked PIC to create a sani bucket. PIC created a bleach bucket - 200 ppm. Ensure staff is aware to create a sani bucket prior to engaging in food manipulation behaviors. Facility should have an active sanitization bucket before food prep begins. Ensure frequent changes of the sani bucket to maintain concentration - 50 to 200 ppm of bleach. Facility has bleach to perform testing procedure. Ensure staff is aware how to utilize test strips and knows the active concentration levels of bleach. Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning:
1. Several metal dry storage shelving units throughout the kitchen have a layer of dust and flour debris (next to walk-in freezer next to tandoori oven, shelving next to hand sink near where naan bread is being cut on a prep table). 
2. Top of dish machine has debris.
3. Interior of dish machine has hard water inside (including interior doors) - needs scrubbed and de-limed. 
4. Dish machine has black moldy water on the walls and underneath the dish machine on the walls - clean the walls.
5. The wok/grill line needs the equipment pulled away and cleaned underneath. Some grease and food debris was present - mop area.
6. The wall at the end of the wok/grill line (on the same wall as the 3 compartment sink) has food splash and grease debris. 
7. The vents above the wok/grill line (attached to the hood system) have dust. 
8. The top of the stove top (with oven attached, next to tandoori oven) is soiled with a layer of food debris.
9. The side of the tandoori oven and the stove/oven have a layer of grease debris and dust.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Items #1-6 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 3/15/23. Ensure the above areas are cleaned (wash, rinse, sanitize). The entire wok/grill line area needs a deep cleaning. There is considerable grease/food splash/debris on the sides of the wok/grill line, walls, under the equipment, in the bottom holes (appears to be bottom access to woks), etc. Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of repairs in order to make smooth, easily cleanable, corrosion-resistant, and non-absorbent:
1. Men’s bathroom hand sink is missing caulk from sink to the wall. Caulk the sink to the wall. Several times are missing in the wall within this bathroom and need replaced - wall is not smooth and easily cleanable.
2. The shelves above the 3 compartment sink are wooden and need sealed with paint and/or sealant in order to make non-absorbent and easily cleanable.
3. Dish machine has moldy caulk around the perimeter - re-caulk the dish machine to the wall after removing moldy caulking.
4. Mop sink has moldy caulking around the basin - remove the molded caulking and re-caulk mop sink to the wall.
5. The coving is broken at the door frame entrance (next to dish machine). The coving under the dish machine area is coming away from the wall and needs re-caulked.
6. The wall behind the ice machine is damage - repair the dry wall and paint/seal.

Discussed with PIC. Items #1-4 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 3/15/23. Ensure repairs are conducted before the next routine inspection.

(REPEAT) The ceiling throughout the kitchen is heavily dyed black by the smoke from the wok/grill line and the tandoori oven. All ceiling tiles throughout the kitchen have been stained black. The entire kitchen tile system needs to be replaced with time. Ceiling tiles should be the original color (white) and be durable/smooth/easily cleanable/non-absorbent (non-porous tiles - no holes - smooth tiles). Inspector discussed this again with PIC as no work has been conducted since the last routine inspection (looks same). PIC indicated the landlord wanted to keep the ceiling black by painting them black. Landlord stated the ceiling will only turn black again after repairs due to the woks and tandoori oven. Inspector texted Food Program Manager, CK, about situation during the inspection. The ceiling tiles need replaced to appropriate white ones and routine cleaning should occur every week to keep the black smoke off the ceiling tiles (wash, rinse, sanitize). CK confirmed this is the correct next procedural step for the ceilings. Discussed this with PIC. Per CK, the permit holder (PIC) will have suspension of permit for failure to comply if work is not at least started. Follow-up will be in a month on 11/7/23 (closed Monday’s) giving ample time to start addressing the ceiling issue. If no work or next to no work is completed, permit suspension will be discussed between SCDPH and the permit holder (PIC).

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses for the facility. All have expired. Discussed with PIC. This was an issue during the last routine inspection on 3/15/23. Discussion was held at that time regarding all employees completing food handler’s licenses. All kitchen staff and wait staff must have an active food handler’s card. Valid for 3 years. Discussed again with PIC today. PIC was in compliance to have staff complete by next routine inspection. Ensure printed copies are available at the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed no allergen training certification for the only CFPM for the facility. Discussed with CFPM/PIC. Ensure PIC completes the allergen training certification before the next routine inspection and prints a copy for the facility. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/15/23.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Food service employee working in the kitchen has a food handler certification but does not have a food manager certification. Food service employee is the designated person in charge (PIC) as they are the person preparing and handling food, answering questions during inspection, and performing their duties. Information about food manager course was provided for food service employee and director of the facility to obtain certification. Ensure the person working in the kitchen is a certified food manager. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique.  Employee touched handles to dispense paper towels for drying after faucet was shut off. Handwashing signage showing proper technique is posted adjacent to the sink. Ensure proper handwashing technique is used every time hands are washed. Have paper towels dispensed and ready to use and/or use an elbow/forearm to touch handles when shutting off the faucet and dispensing paper towels. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-202.12 Bleach solution was prepared and observed at a concentration above 200ppm. Test strip was bleached out when used to check concentration. Solution was diluted to 100ppm. Maintain bleach solutions for product being used at 100-200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.  
Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

citation_text:

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for cross contamination and glove use. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at followup inspections.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.15(A) PIC switched tasks from working with an electronic device for inventory at the sandwich prep cooler to preparing orders without a glove change. Gloves were changed at request of inspector. Ensure gloves are immediately changed when switching tasks and prior to handling food after touching general surfaces with gloved hands. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Fruit flies were observed on clean dishes and shelving to the left of the dish machine. All dishes were to go through ware washing process again, and shelving needs to be cleaned and sanitized. Fruit flies were also observed on surfaces throughout the drive thru cabinet including around packaged single service articles. Management was encouraged to relocate single service articles until flies are no longer present in the drive thru cabinet. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Quat sanitizer is currently connected to the dispenser at the 3 part sink, and facility has labeling, test strips, and infographics posted at the 3 part sink for Sink and Surface Cleaner Sanitizer, which has different active ingredients of DDBSA/lactic acid. PIC did not realize the wrong product was connected to the dispenser and plans to confirm ordering of correct sanitizer with order that will be placed tomorrow for Saturday delivery. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 1) Facility has an active fruit fly population. The majority of flies were observed in the dish area and within the cabinet under the counter along the north wall at the drive thru. Dozens of fruit flies were observed under the sprayer sink on the plumbing and around the floor drain where heavy accumulation of mold and other debris was observed. Fruit flies were also observed on the walls around the dish machine, the clean dish shelving and dishes to the left of the dish machine, and surfaces to the left of the clean dish shelving. Dozens of fruit flies were also present under the soda machine ice bin in the drive thru cabinet and throughout the entirety the cabinet on shelving/brackets and surfaces of equipment said to be unused.
2) The current conditions in the dish area and the cabinet at the drive thru, specifically the absence of proper drainage from the ice bin, are contributing factors to the issue with fruit flies. The need for cleaning and general maintenance to aid in fly management were discussed. PIC was also advised on use of an enzymatic drain cleaner to remove buildup in floor drains that could be contributing to the fly issue.
In addition to cleaning and maintenance, management needs to get in touch with pest control operator for service. 
The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the premises by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the premies for evidence of pests; (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

comment:

The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the upstairs sani bucket at the bar (that was in the hand sink - see violation #10) to be 0 ppm. PIC asked waitress if the bucket was re-made today. It appears the sani bucket was from the day before. Ensure staff is aware that sani buckets should be frequently changed out to maintain concentration - every 4 hours or so. Quaternary ammonium (sanitizer type facility is using) should be maintained at 200-400 ppm. Facility has test strips to verify concentrations of sanitizer. Ensure staff frequently changes sani buckets and utilizes test strips to verify concentration ranges. Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

(REPEAT) Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. The can opener blade in the kitchen (attached to a prep table) was soiled. Employee stated she had not used the can opener today. Ensure staff cleans can opener blades every 4 hours or as needed to maintain a clean blade. Discussed with staff. Can opener blade was brought to the dish machine to wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.
2. The ceiling vent above the dish machine area where clean utensils are stored has dust on it. Clean. Repeat violation since last routine inspection on 2/15/23.
3. The clean cooking utensil shelf under the large vent at the rear kitchen hand sink has a layer of visible dust hanging from the grates. The vent above it previously was very dusty and blew the dust over the clean cooking utensils. Ensure the vent and shelving unit is frequently cleaned to prevent dust (should not be dusty where clean utensils are stored).
4. Main level bar soda gun holder was soiled with mold. Discussed with PIC. Employee washed, rinsed, and sanitized. COS.
5. Upstairs bar had a moldy soda nozzle. Inspector showed PIC. Employee washed, rinsed, and sanitized. COS. 
6. The ice machine in the kitchen had a layer of mold along the interior baffle. Inspector showed main CFPM for kitchen. Facility began pulling all the ice from the machine in order to wash, rinse, sanitize the interior basin and ceiling, plus baffle. COS.

Discussed the above food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning is observed in order to prevent mold, debris, food splash, etc. accumulation. Inspector will follow-up regarding the above areas on 10/16/23.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  

Observed the hot holding steam table to have all food at barely above cold holding temperatures (65F) or roughly ~100F for some items. Food appears to be being heated directly in the steam table. Cease practice. Inspector questioned the employee making food in this area and he stated the food was directly put into the steam table. And reheated food needs to be cooked at 165F on the cook line, then brought to the steam table where it remains 135F or above. Discussed with employee and PIC. Inspector asked the employee to reheat all items on the stove top. COS.

Discussed with employee who was working in this area. Ensure more active managerial control for staff. Cooking, cooling, and reheating practices (see above violation as well) may cause significant food borne illness if done improperly. Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed roach infestation at the facility. All stages of roach life cycle were present: babies, juveniles, and adults. Inspector noted activity by babies and juveniles. Significant areas of issue were in the dish room, under the noodle steam table at the prep line, under pizza prep cooler (minor), and in the soda line room next to the bar (babies noted). Bacon’s Pest Control has been notified of the issue and has been to the facility twice in the last 3 weeks. Inspector asked PIC to have Bacon’s come weekly to the facility until the issue is resolved. Per PIC, Bacon’s has sprayed, left powder, and put down sticky traps. The facility should purchase their own sticky traps and replace every few days as needed around the perimeters of the hot spot areas listed above. 
Dish Room: Walls need scrubbed of food debris and mold, re-caulk the dish machine, 3 compartment sink, and hand sink in this area (moldy, coming away), top and underside of the dish machine needs a good cleaning (food debris build-up), coving around the perimeter of the dish room is coming away (roaches were coming from behind coving) and needs to be repaired/caulked, all holes in the walls in this area need caulked.
Steam Table: pull the equipment away and clean, replace the sticky traps. Discuss with Bacon’s the most appropriate way to remove the roaches from the machine (open the doors, babies and juveniles are underneath inside). 
Soda Room: clean the flooring, put sticky traps around the perimeter.
Pizza Prep Table: maintain nightly cleaning by pulling the cooler away and cleaning/mopping behind this cooler, replace sticky traps around perimeter, clean food splash from walls. Clean the dough prep areas in this area - roaches are attached to the flour dust.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine chlorine final rinse concentration was observed at 0ppm. Owner primed the sanitizer line continuously for 3 full cycles resulting in a concentration of 100ppm present briefly on the drain board while the concentration on the dish rack was still at 0ppm. After running additional cycles all surfaces were observed without a presence of chlorine residual and consistent concentration of 0ppm was noted. Call for service was made and technicians arrived to provide service during inspection. Tubing was changed and other components of the dish machine were checked to verify proper function.  Final rinse concentration after repairs was at 100ppm.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:

Rice was reheated to 167F, and maintaining the temperature setting above 135F to allow for proper hot holding was discussed. Setting for warmer was placed above 140F to proper hot hold rice after reheating.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Crock of gravy was observed with an internal temperature of 57F-60F in the chicken walk-in cooler. PIC noted the crock was removed from hot holding unit around 10:30am and put in the cooler around 12pm. Best practices were discussed for quick chilling process. Gravy was placed in an ice bath and stirred to help product reach 41F within the remaining ~2hrs of time frame for cooling. Educational handout for cooling was provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs. One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Numerous insects are observed in the grate by the old dish area. It is possible that the crack in the coving next to this location could be a breeding/ egg laying location and the grate is supplying food for the young flies. The flies appear to be in the early stages of development/adulthood. The PIC is instructed to contact Orkin for service to remedy this situation. It was suggested to repair/seal the coving to deny the potential breeding ground and clean the grated area thoroughly to ensure that any possible food source is removed. Follow up will be conducted in two weeks to ensure removal of the insects.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Did not observed any hand washing during the inspection. Ensure employees frequently wash hands, particularly when changing gloves or changing tasks that could contaminate the hands. Facility utilizes mainly raw chicken. Hand washing should be frequent and through. Discussed with manager. Ensure staff is reminded frequently to wash hands to prevent food borne illness outbreaks and/or cross contamination of hands and food. Set timers for staff to wash hands, if needed. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the quaternary ammonium at the 3 compartment sink to be 0 ppm. Discussed with the dish washer. Dish washer acknowledged that the quat should be changed out after lunch. Inspector asked the dish washer to drain the basin and re-fill with fresh quat sanitizer. Ensure staff is aware to routinely change out the sanitizer in order to maintain concentration - 200 to 400 ppm for quat. Facility needs test strips in order to verify. See violation page.

Inspector is aware of the high volume of food product and amount of grease the facility utilizes - ensure a nightly cleaning schedule is adhered to - wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 9/18/23 regarding the cleaning of the above areas.

comment:

Inspector asked employee to wash hands and don single-use gloves. COS.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
The hood system over the hood has been a continual source of dust, dirt and grease residue which has been allowed to accumulate on the ceiling tile of the deli. During the inspection today, inspector observed a visible amount of smoke in the entirety of the building but most prominently throughout the deli area where the fryers and stovetops are actively functioning. Although the hood appears relatively clean with no visible drips developing or buildup of debris, the exhaust is not able to properly disipate materials from the equipment underneath. This poses an imminent public health hazard, nuisance and may constitute unlawful discharge of hazardous materials. Smoke is hazardous to the health of building occupants and may contain other hazardous materials which, when not ventilated properly, will accumulate on items inside the building including food and nonfood-contact surfaces. Lastly, failure to dissipate heat from the equipment below the hood in concert with an accumulation of potentially flammable materials poses a significant fire hazard. Due to the severity of the violation and the imminent health hazard posed by the malfunctioning hood, resolution is required immediately. Per conversation with the general manager, a third-party hood cleaning company is to be secured to investigate the cause of the problem by the end of the day. Failure to have a functioning hood will result in continued enforcement including but not limited to closure of the deli/referral to fire department and/or building and zoning.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed hand washing practices at the facility and observed the following:

-- Hand washing frequency is inconsistent from one staff member to another. Obtain and post an SOP for handwashing either from the franchisor or develop a facility specific one, however, all staff must understand when hand washing is required.

-- The facility is short staffed and unable to manage hand washing with busy operations. Two employees and a manager were present on arrival. During this time, inspector observed an employee preparing food at the front grill with a slice of cheese in hand who then returned to the fryers, cheese still in hand, to turn off the alarm (using a glove hand to touch a soiled NFCS) on the fryer. Staffing must be sufficient to ensure that cross-contamination at the facility and two employees plus a manager is insufficient with any significant amount of business at the facility. The employee was immediately instructed to stay in one area, but this is not feasible with only two employees present. Failure to properly staff the store results in an inability to wash hands during appropriate intervals and the separation of activities required to prevent cross-contamination from occurring. Ensure that staffing is sufficient at all times to ensure food safety.

-- Inspector observed an employee return from cleaning activities to food preparation without hand washing between activities. Gloves are NOT a replacement for proper hand washing. When switching activities that result in the potential contamination of the hands, such as cleaning the dining room, gloves must be removed, hands must be washed, and new gloves must be donned before working with food. Ensure that staff is aware that any activities in the dining room such as cleaning, picking up consumer trays, and so forth must be followed by hand washing due to potential contamination from consumers visiting the facility.

Pizzas are sold to customers, and customers use the pizza oven located in seating area to bake their own pizza. Hotdog roller was shut off, and bartender stated they would leave it off for the remainder of operations. No hotdogs were on the roller for service at the time of inspection. title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Person-in-charge (PIC) has several repeat and/or priority/priority foundation violations during the inspection today. 

PIC advised inspector that the majority of accumulation had occurred prior to her appointment as CFM at the facility which is correct. This violation was observed during the previous inspection and corrective actions were required as of today's date. Further, PIC advised inspector that a list of all areas requiring cleaning was not itemized in the previous report. As noted in the previous report, cleaning is required underneath ALL pieces of equipment in the facility. The PIC must be able to identify areas which do not comply with 2017 FDA Food Code as part of the responsibilities of a CFM. The responsibility for identifying all areas of the facility which require cleaning does not fall on SCDPH but on the facility.

Due to the priority/priority foundation and repeat violations observed during the inspection today, a 30-day follow-up is issued to evaluate the overall state of compliance at the facility. Ensure that no priority or priority foundation violations exist in the facility at that time. Inspector will return on 08/25/2023.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM 08/25/2022.

Inspector did not observe any hand washing occurring during the inspection today. Inspector put a crease in the corner of the paper towel roll at the front hand sink after washing hands at the start of the inspection. The crease was still present in the paper towel roll at the end of the inspection indicating that hand washing had not occurred at that sink. Inspector did not observe any hand washing at the back hand washing sink. Several glove changes occurred without hand washing between glove changes. Inspector observed an employee go from taking orders and accepting payment to working with food without hand washing, although gloves were changed between activities. Ensure that hand washing is occurring immediately before working with food AND any activites which may have contaminated employee's hands. A follow-up is issued for 07/28/2023 to observe hand washing practices within the facility at that time.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Foods in the prep cooler along the south wall of the kitchen where sandwiches are made was observed to have temperatures around 50 to 55 degrees F. Temperatures in the prep cooler must be maintained at 41 degrees or below. The facility does not have a time-as-a-control policy which states that items in the cooler are discarded after 4-hours in the prep cooler. The lid to the prep cooler was left open on inspector arrival allowing foods to warm to within the critical range above 41 degrees. Inspector closed the lid during the inspection. Ensure that staff are aware to keep the lid to the cooler closed. If the lid is to remain open and foods are observed to be out-of-temperature, establish a time-as-control policy and discard all TCS foods in the prep cooler at the end of 4-hours. Ensure that ALL TCS foods not covered under a time-as-control policy are kept at 41 degrees or below at all times. A follow-up is issued for 07/28/2023 to ensure cold-holding temperatures in the prep cooler are below 41 degrees and/or establish time-as-control policy.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 03/21/2023.

Inspector observed the floors underneath all pieces of equipment in the kitchen to be soiled with grease, refuse and debris. The majority of the accumulation observed during the inspection today was also observed during the inspection on 03/21/2023 prior to the current CFM taking over as person-in-charge (PIC). 

Heavily soiled areas include but are not limited to underneath and behind the cash register counter, the reach-in coolers to the left of the grill, the grill, the steam table, the corner counter reaching to the drive thru, the counter to the right of the drive thru, the fryers, and the prep cooler to the right of the fryers, the double upright fry freezer to the left of the fryers, and the dish machine. Underneath/beneath each of these items (and any others within the kitchen itself not explicitly listed) is large accumulation of soil that has been present since prior to the previous inspection. These areas are required by 2017 FDA Food Code as adopted by the State of Illinois to be clean often enough to prevent such accumulation from occurring. 

The severity of the soil accumulation is of serious concern for the harborage of pests in the future as well as the growth and spread of pathogens as the accumulation worsens. PIC has stated concerns with being able to move the equipment to clean. Food code requires that equipment be constructed in a manner which allows it to be easily cleanable.

A follow-up is issued for 08/04/2023 to allow time for cleaning to occur. Ensure that corrective actions have been taken to bring the facility back into compliance by this date. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
Person-in-charge (PIC) has not completed allergen awareness training as required by this statute. Ensure that allergen awareness training is completed by the PIC by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: At the start of the inspection, the QUAT dispenser at the triple sink was tested utilizing appropriate test strips and was recorded at 0ppm. After trouble shooting, it was recognized that the dispenser tubing had been crushed under the metal holding shelf under the sink. After removing the shelf unit and freeing the tubing from its crushed nature, the sanitizer dispenser worked as required and was retested and recorded at 200ppm QUAT. Ensure after cleaning that the tubing is free of obstruction and ensure testing is performed regularly to have confidence in the sanitizing solution.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Crepes were observed with surface temperature of 55F-58F and internal temperature of 85F in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler. Cook stated crepes were made at 6am, and it was a little after 9am when temperature was checked. GM stated the cook starts at 6am, but crepes were likely made around 7am. Process for cooling allows for 30 minute rest period at room temperature prior to placing product in a cooler for chilling. A couple dozen plus crepes were stacked together, which could have also impacted the rate at which product was cooling. GM was advised the prep cooler is not ideal for cooling cooked TCS foods, especially the prep cooler at the west end of the cook line that is in constant use with cooks getting in and out of the cooler throughout operations. Crepes were discarded during inspection. Ensure proper cooling and consider quick chilling smaller stacks or single layers of crepes in the walk-in cooler prior to placing product in the prep cooler. Time stamps are encouraged for working supplies of product that was just prepared and is still in the process of cooling.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

On arrival, the steam well used for hot holding of cooked burgers and hot dogs is observed to not be holding foods at correct hot holding limits. The steam well does not appear to be turned on. It was activated and was observed at correct temperatures later in the inspection.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Pork chops, brots and hot dogs are observed sitting out to thaw by the grills. Education was conducted as to the safe ways to thaw TCS foods. It was suggested that instead of two freezers, it may be better to have a freezer and a cooler at this location. Inspector also suggested thawing under refrigeration in the walk in cooler across the walkway. Brots are observed still frozen at this time. PIC indicated that the other items had been sitting for less than half an hour  when observed. All items were moved back into the freezers to correct.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: At the start of the inspection, multiple food items in the walk-in cooler and the cooler in the kitchen were observed without a date mark present. Most of the food was prepped today, but some was not. If a food item is in the facility longer than 24 hours, then it must have a date mark placed on it stating the date of creation/prep. PIC informed employees about this and date marks were placed on all the containers. Ensure date marks are placed on food items appropriately.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Proper disposition of returned, previously served, reconditioned and unsafe food
comment:
Inspector was notified of complaint number 23-0309 which states that "complainant claims they are reusing chips. Sat near the back of the restaurant and noticed a bucket near the trash they were dumping chips in."

Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed the bucket in question filled with chips near the trash at the back of the dining room. Immediately upon announcing my presence to staff, the container was taken back to the kitchen and the chips were dumped into a larger container on top of the single door upright cooler. Person-in-charge at first told me that these chips were fresh chips and were not being used. After some questioning regarding where the chips came from and why they were first in the dining room if they were fresh, person-in-charge state that "maybe" they are being reused. Foods previously served, even if not eaten, may NEVER be reused and served again to consumers. These foods must ALWAYS be DISCARDED after service. 

The chips were discarded during the inspection.

Complaint is founded and a follow-up is issued for 7/14/2023. 

3-306.14: (A) FOOD that is sold or served to CONSUMER may not be offered for human consumption if returned. (B) non-TCS FOOD can be offered if FOOD is protected when dispensed or if FOOD is in an unopened original PACKAGE and in sound condition.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:

comment:

Reference 2-501.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. 7-301.11: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be separated from one another for RETAIL sale. (B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be located in area not above FOOD or FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed a shallow metal container containing what appeared to be flour used to bread meat sitting on the floor underneath the counter on the west side of the kitchen. The food was immediately removed and person-in-charge affirmed understanding that foods should not be stored on the floor nor under countertops which are not cleaned/sanitized. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. Ensure that foods are protected from contamination at ALL times. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
Facility is using deep containers to cool soup during operations. The facility possesses ice wands to rapidly cool soups. Discussed with chef and person-in-charge the need to use the ice wand each time when cooling due to the depth of the containers and the temperature at which they are cooked. Foods cooling for x1 hour retained temperatures of 135 to 140 degrees F when stirred. They have 1-hour to reach a temeprature of 70 degrees. Ice wands will help ensure proper temperatures are reached within critical limits. Consider using logs to track the exact times foods are placed in cold-holding, 1-hour temperatures, 2-hour temperatures, and 6-hour temperatures. Foods must cool to 70 degrees or below within the first 2 HOURS. Foods must cool to below 41 degrees F within the next 4 HOURS. Ensure that proper cooling procedure is followed at all times and that staff are aware of requirements for cooling. A follow-up is issued for 07/03/2023 to ensure compliance. 

3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

comment:

comment:

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) PIC was not following the requirements of the company HACCP plan and did not have a copy of any necessary documentation to discuss the requirements in detail. Missing documentation included, but was not necessarily limited to, the company HACCP plan, letters of guarantee for sushi fish, and employee health documents. Daily log book showed information written down for pH of sushi rice and calibration of pH meter and thermometer, but information was documented without the processes actually occurring based on the information provided. PIC has been working at the facility for ~2 months and stated they’ve never calibrated the pH meter or used it to verify pH of acidified rice. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 White rice in the walk-in cooler cooked prior to inspector’s arrival was observed with surface temperatures of 79F-102F and internal temperatures of 111F-124F. Rice was said to be mixed with rice vinegar and sugar prior to placing it in the cooler ~30 minutes prior. Rice pH was not verified and cooling process was not being monitored. Plastic container was tightly sealed with a lid on top. Lid was left partially askew to allow for faster chilling of product, and PIC was advised on quick chilling of cooked rice. Company HACCP policy requires proper cooling of sushi rice if it will not be used immediately. Cooling will be discussed during training and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Workers washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handwashing process was less than 20 seconds. Proper handwashing was discussed. PIC re-educated staff on proper handwashing technique. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

Handwashing upon arrival and prior to doing any tasks was discussed. PIC advised workers on when to wash hands. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Facility currently has an active roach population. Adult and juvenile roaches of various sizes, including a white roach that recently molted, were observed in the compressor compartment of the upright reach-in freezer (next to seafood freezer). Several dead roaches were also observed in the freezer compressor compartment as well as in the compressor compartment of the residential fridge on the cook line. A hatched egg case was also observed in the compressor compartment of the residential fridge. A glue trap containing dead and live roaches was observed under the seafood freezer. Two additional glue traps on the floor behind the grease trap also contained several roaches, and a few dead roaches were observed along the wall under the 3pt sink and the handwashing sink. Cleaning and repairs were discussed. PIC was asked to contact pest control company for service. PIC was advised to request service as soon as possible and let technician know service is needed before the follow-up inspection in two weeks. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment:

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wet wiping cloths were observed sitting on countertops in the kithen and warewashing areas. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Inspector observed operator using a wiping cloth which had been sitting on the top counter of the prep cooler during food preparation. The wiping cloth was used to wipe hands and knives during use. The wiping cloth was then brought over to the triple sink where it was rinsed off. Following rinsing, operator folded the wiping cloth and began wiping off food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces on and along the prep cooler including knives and cutting boards. Inspector tested the water on the wiping cloth and ther was zero concentration of sanitizer in the wiping cloth following rinsing and thus no sanitizer used in wiping off food-contact surfaces such as the cutting boards and knives. Inspector had a detailed discussion with operator to educate on proper use of wiping cloths. Wet wiping cloth must be placed in sanitizer solution between each use and may not be allowed to sit on surfaces such as counter tops. If rinsed, wiping cloths must be returned to the sanitizer bucket prior to using the wiping cloths to wipe down food-contact surfaces. Operator stated understanding of this requirement and wiping cloth was immediately placed in the sanitizer bucket with a quaternary ammonium concentration of approximately 200 ppm per inspector test strips. Corrected on site.

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands and after handling soiled dishes and prior to handling clean dishes.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Multiple prepared foods were once again observed with date marks indicating a time frame for use longer than 7 days. Dates were corrected at the time of inspection and staff were re-educated about date marking. An educational spot check will be conducted at the end of the month to revisit date marking and ensure foods are properly dated.
Except as specified in (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in  (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

Additional chlorine test strips were provided for use at the facility. Ensure chlorine test kits are maintained and available for use. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-203.14 Leaks were still present at the first and middle basins of the dish area triple sink. Look below the basins. Leaks appear to be along the handle for the drain plug and possibly other junctures within the plumbing. Provide proper repairs.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:

Ensure all staff complete food handler certification and that copies are maintained on-site.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:

All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items were observed for cross contamination, hot holding, date marking, and chemical storage. See violations 15, 21, 23, & 28 for details. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

One of the managers made reference to washing their hands at the 3 part sink. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was discussed. PIC was advised to revisit proper handwashing and where to wash hands with all staff.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Empty dish detergent bottle was observed in the basin of the handwashing sink. Bottle was removed and discarded to allow for access to wash hands.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

All sinks not used for handwashing should not be supplied with handwashing aids/devices.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Fountain soda nozzles and diffusers were observed with varying amounts of mold buildup, with some nozzles having chunky buildup indicating a lack of cleaning for quite some time. Fountain soda machines were taken out of service. Soda nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during inspection.  
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Cheese sauce and chili sauces were observed with internal temperature of 110F and 113F for dispensed product. Chili sauce and cheese sauce were placed in the dispenser as of 6/8, and both products were removed and discarded after being wasted for inventory.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Open packages of hotdogs and smoked sausages were observed without date marks in the walk-in cooler. Exact date when products were opened was unknown. Items were wasted for inventory and discarded upon request of inspector. Ensure open packages of hotdogs and sausages are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days.
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of pink liquid without a label was observed in the front lobby with other chemicals. PIC confirmed it was glass cleaner and placed the product in a properly labeled bottle.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-201.11 Spray bottles of Purell Food Service Sanitizer and Bathroom Tuff Stain Remover were stored on top of and next to Red Bull products in the hallway across from the walk-of cooler. Chemicals were relocated to proper storage area. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:

Equipment for cooling and heating food, and holding cold and hot food, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Two metal stem thermometers were reading at 60F and 70F at ambient temperature. Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the bases of the reach-in coolers in the back (for curbside pick up orders) to have debris. Clean the bases routinely to keep clean. Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
comment:

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
CFM certification is expired and was brought to attention during last inspection.  PIC states she plans on retiring in 2023, no definite date is determined for retirement yet.   Ensure CFM certification is obtained.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 1) Trim and base coving directly behind the dish machine are still in need of repairs. Ensure proper repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
Plastic base coving and wall trim to the right of the dish machine beneath the sprayer sink were repaired.
2) Walls were soiled with general buildup under and around the dish machine. Ensure walls are cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.16: Observed mop head to be stored head down in bucket filled with dirty water.

  After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

Observed the mop sink to be missing caulk. Caulk the mop sink basin to the wall. Correct both areas by next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Several dozen fruit flies were observed in the dish area on surfaces under the dish counters, the dish machine, and the 3 part sink. Dish area was cleaned and repairs were made since the last routine inspection, but fruit flies persist. Fly strips may be used to help aid in fly management as long as they are placed in locations that do not pose a potential risk of cross contamination, such as the areas mentioned above. Also, the floor drain under the garbage grinder and sprayer sink has drain lines down inside, which does not allow for scrubbing/cleaning in the drain. Consider disassembling drain lines to allow for access to thoroughly clean the drain. Operator plans to call for additional pest control service as well.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-202.15 Light from the outside was visible at the bottom left corner of back door where weather stripping was damaged and missing. New door sweep is available to install for the back door.  
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, and tight-fitting doors.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 1) Two door cooler used for noodle storage was observed with torn gaskets. Per kitchen manager, gaskets are on order. Repairs will be made once parts arrive.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Walk-in cooler shelves had varying amounts of food splash and debris accumulation. Clean the shelves as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:

White cloth towel was observed in the bottom left side of the cooler to try and minimize the amount of condensation dripping out the bottom. Per kitchen manager, a part is on order to make repairs.  
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floor tiles were missing around the drain to the left of the salad cooler. Replace missing floor tiles or seal the area to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface where tiles are missing.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Food allergen certifications were not available for certified food managers working at the facility. Ensure CFMs also complete an allergen course and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

(P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. comment:

comment:

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, operators advised the inspector that the walk-in freezer had failed completely and walk-in cooler is functioning but unable to maintain a temperature sufficiently low to ensure food temepratures are maintained at 41 degrees F or below at all times without frequent recharging of the condenser. Chest freezers have been brought in to supplement the failed equipment until repairs can be made. Foods are maintained within proper temperatures and all frozen foods have remained frozen. Foods were discarded by staff prior to the inspection if out of temperature as a result of the equipment malfunction. title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Inspector observed several temperatures throughout the facility that exceed the 41 degree maximum for cold-holding. Foods in the prep cooler along the cook line were the warmest with temperatures between 55 and 65 degrees F. Foods in the reach-in below were 45 to 47 degrees F. Foods in the sushi prep cooler were 46 to 48 degrees F. Foods under the sushi prep cooler were 44 to 46 degrees F. Facility is currently operating during busy lunch hours with food preparation occurring frequently. The lid to the prep cooler along the line was left open during service resulting in high temepratures. There is no indication of equipment failure but there is evidence of temperature abuse occurring with TCS foods in the facility.

Person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring that staff keep lids closed and monitor temperatures to maintain foods at 41 degrees or below at all times. Work with staff on minimizing the times lids and doors are spent open allowing cold air to be released. Especially during busy periods, work with smaller quanitities of food to allow for time-as-a-control if temperature controls are not sufficient when facility is busy. 

Person-in-charge had a discussion with staff and immediately took corrective action. Ambient temperatures of the coolers are 41 to 42 degrees with the doors being opened and foods will return to appropriate temperatures. title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Multiple priority items were observed during the inspection today. See violations 8, 9, 13, 15, 16, 19, 22, & 23 for details. title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

Enough staff with food manager certifications need to be available so one is present and working at the facility during all hours of operation, including morning prep prior to opening.
