title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were said to be in the office but PIC was unable to unlock the door during inspection. Owner and management need to ensure access to employee health documents for ease in reference during inspections. Documents need to be available for viewing by inspectors at time of follow-up inspection.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure for responding to diarrhea/vomit incident was not available with other employee health documents. Owner and management need to ensure access to employee health documents, including cleanup policy for norovirus. Cleanup policy needs to be available for viewing by inspectors at time of follow-up inspection.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Approximately 6 bottles, coffee cups, and glasses with personal drinks were observed throughout prep areas intermixed with food and equipment. One of the cooks was also observed actively drinking from their beverage as they were taking tortillas to the walk-in cooler from the cook line. Handwashing and personal beverage consumption were discussed as was proper storage of personal drinks. All drinks were removed from the prep area and discarded. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

2-301.14 Employees were not washing hands between tasks as needed and missed several opportunities for handwashing. Another employee was also observed using a cloth apron to wipe their hands. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and employees were later observed washing hands during inspection. When, where, and how to wash hands will be revisited at a later date during an educational inspection as well.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands

All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen certification was not available for staff. Ensure all certified food managers also complete an allergen course, and maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed a staff member touch an ear bud, put gloves on, and continue working with food. Hands must be washed ANY TIME contamination may have occurred.

Work with ALL staff to ensure compliance with hand washing procedure and frequency. Procedure includes a) wasing hands for AT LEAST 20 seconds b) using soap and warm water c) turning off the faucet with a paper towel as a barrier between the hands and the knob on the faucet. 

Inspector observed operator educating staff members of hand washing and education has been provided. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time.

If hand washing signage in a language beside English would be helpful to ensure compliance, contact your inspector immediately and materials will be provided. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Inspector provided education to operator regarding accessiblity of hand sinks within the facility. The facility is small and provides limited space for food preparation activities. During the spot-check, inspector observed a staff member preparing meat patties at a short table immediately next to the hand sink with the employee sitting on a stool directly in front of the hand sink blocking access. 

Hand sinks must be available for employees to wash their hands at all times with no exceptions. Hand sinks cannot be used for any purposes apart from hand washing. Hand sinks must remain stocked with paper towels and appropriate hand soap at all times. 

During the inspection, operator had food preparation moved from immediately in front of the sink to adjacent to the sink. This is not ideal because hand washing activities will result in water spray potentially contaminating the food. Work with staff and determine a better location for preparing meat in the facility moving forward and ensure that hand sinks remain accessible during all operational hours. Coach staff on appropriate locations for food preparation.

If signage in a language beside English would be helpful for ensuring compliance with hand washing requirements, reach out to your inspector immediately and materials will be provided to assist with compliance. 

The hand sink was stocked and accessible at the end of the spot-check today. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

A bottle of Microban is observed to be used for spraying surfaces in the kitchen. At the time of the spraying a freshly cleaned rack of food contact utensils is observed in the immediate area being sprayed. The bottle of Microban indicates that it is intended for only no-food contact surfaces. A discussion took place and the bottle of bleach solution will be the only surface sanitizer used in the kitchen moving foreword. Ensure that any chemical used on food related surfaces is intended for food contact.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P), conditions of certification (if applicable) (P), and additional conditions (if applicable) (C).

The bottle of bleach solution used in the facility is observed to bleach out the inspector’s test strips. This indicates a concentration significantly to strong for safe use in a kitchen. Education took place and the bottle remade during this inspection to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

1) The counter above the dish machine is warping and exposing the particle board underneath. Repair prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The junction between the dish sink and the wall is pulling away from each other. Seal the wall/counter junctions prior to the next routine inspection. Caulking suggested.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
A box of shelled eggs in the walk-in cooler was sitting directly under the left edge of the condenser unit where water was actively dripping. Inspector observed water inside the box and splashed on eggs in the corner of the box. The box of shelled eggs was immediately discarded by the person-in-charge. The box below the discarded box was immediately moved to prevent further contamination. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. Ensure that all foods are protected for any sources of contamination at ALL times. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM 10/12/022. 

During inspection on 10/12/2022, facility was cited for hand washing sinks not being caulked to the walls creating surfaces which and not easily cleanable. During the inspection today, no caulking had been performed and the hand sinks remain out of compliance. All surfaces subject to food and/or moisture must be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable at all times in areas where food preparation, storage and service occurs. Ensure that all areas of the facility comply with this requirement by the next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: The magnetic knife holder is observed to be visibly soiled at the start of today’s inspection. PIC removed the items from the magnetic strip and placed them into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. While the items were removed, PIC performed a CIP of the magnetic strip with a sanitizing step before replacing the items to the strip. Ensure this surface is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean to sight and touch. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
3-304.14: The facility was observed to be using reusable cloths when utilizing a spray bottle of sanitizer. Corrective action and education have been given to utilize disposable paper towels when using a spray bottle of sanitizer. A solution has been determined that the sanitizer bucket will be available to store the wiping cloth and then the cloth will be removed form the bucket when in use with a spray bottle. Once finished wiping the surface, the wiping cloth will be placed back into the sanitizer bucket until it is ready to be used again with the spray bottle.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: The mop sink is observed to have pulled away from the wall enough to create a visible gap. This gap needs to be resealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Eggs stored above ready-to-eat foods in the fridge (on the top shelf). CORRECTED- Storage rearranged to prevent potential cross contamination. Store raw foods below RTE. Ref. 3-302.11 [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Tuna salad observed without any date-marking. CORRECTED- PIC made salad on Friday and labeled it accordingly. Ensure all foods that will remain in the facility for more than 24 hours are labeled with the date prepared/opened. Ref. 3-501.17 [Pf]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for barehand contact, cross contamination, cold holding, hot holding, sanitization, and date marking. See violations 9, 15, 16, 21, 22, & 23 for details. In addition, chlorine test kits were not available for checking final rinse concentration at dish machines, and an active fruit fly population was observed in the dish area under and around the dish machine. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 1) Two ounce portion cups were observed in pans of salt and hot giardiniera relish at the cook line. Portion cups were removed and discarded. Ensure scoops with handles are used when dispensing ready to eat foods.

2) Employee was observed having barehand contact with basil being prepped for garnish at the server prep cooler. Employee was advised on glove use in addition to handwashing when handling ready to eat foods, such as garnish. Basil handled with bare hands was discarded. Employee just washed their hands so gloves were put on to finish prep with fresh product.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in  (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signs were not posted at handwashing sinks in the kitchen. Kitchen manager noted paper towel dispensers were recently replaced, and handwashing signs were located on old dispensers. Ensure handwashing signs are posted at kitchen handwashing sinks to replace signs that were removed with the old paper towel dispensers.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Shaker of seasoning was observed sitting inside pan in direct contact with onion topping on the cook line. Outer surface of seasoning shaker was soiled with general buildup from use. Onion topping was discarded. Outer surface of shakers and containers are not considered clean surfaces and should not be in direct contact with other foods. Cease this storage practice.

2) Containers of pickles in the walk-in cooler were uncovered on the bottom shelf. The shelf above was soiled with general buildup and mold. In addition, plates and parchment paper were observed down inside the pickle containers. All pickles were discarded during inspection. Ensure proper storage of foods covered between uses and without unnecessary items, such as parchment paper and plates, inside products. 

3) Can opener blade was heavily soiled with encrusted debris and white powder that appeared to be flour or another breading material. Can opener was taken to dish area for ware washing. Ensure can opener is cleaned and sanitized between uses and not left in prep area for use when soiled.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Kitchen dish machine was observed with final rinse concentration of 0ppm chlorine. Product appeared to be weakened from exposure to air in the top of the container. Inspector’s test strip showed product was not fully concentrated as test strip was a dark purple black color when product was checked straight out of the container. Concentrated product should register on a test strip as clear liquid with a dark purple/black edge. New sanitizer product was connected to dish machine, and sanitizer line was primed multiple times before and during cycles. Concentration remained at 0ppm after running over a half dozen cycles. GM placed a service call during inspection. Dish machine can still be used for ware washing for wash and rinse steps. Until dish machine is repaired and functioning properly, manual sanitizing will occur at the 3 part sink with quat sanitizer after dishes are ran through the machine. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Cheese sauce in hot holding unit in server area had internal temperatures it 111F and 100F. Product was said to have been reheated on the stove above 165F prior to placing in holding wells. Products were uncovered and in double pans with hot water in the pans beneath observed at 153F and 155F. Water in hot holding unit was also around 150F. Cheese sauce was placed back on the stove to be reheated back to 165F/above prior to hot holding. Kitchen manager put more hot water in the pans intended for hot holding to aid in maintaining product at 135F/above after reheating. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) 1) Lettuce was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 60F and 57.5F respectively. Pan of lettuce was located on the top left side of the cook line prep cooler. Other TCS foods were observed with internal temperatures of 41F and 47F for tomatoes that were just sliced. It was unclear as to why lettuce was so warm, but it could have been due to the lid being open and air circulation from exhaust. Lettuce was discarded.

2) Open bottles and boxes of Bloody Mary mix and juices that require refrigeration after opening per product label were observed at 56F and 57F when dispensed to check temperature with probe thermometers. Products were located in the middle reach-in cooler at the bar, which was holding above 50F. All open products that indicated refrigeration was required after opening were discarded by bartender. Juices and other mixers that contain juice will be held in other reach-in coolers holding at 40F/below.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Tarter sauce and garlic mayo portions prepared in the facility had date marks of 4/22 and 5/14 in the 2 door reach-in cooler in the server area. Products were discarded during inspection. Ensure all TCS foods and sauces prepared on-site are used or discarded within 7 days. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Three spray bottles at the bar containing yellow and clear liquids were not labeled. Front of house manager confirmed the products were general cleaners used to wipe down tables and the bar top. Spray bottles were labeled as to the contents. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Middle reach-in cooler at the bar was holding above 50F and unable to maintain products at 41F/below. Products requiring refrigeration were discarded (see #22 for details). Call for service will be made. Until cooler is repaired or replaced it will only be used for storage of non-TCS products, such as simple syrup.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Fruit fly activity was observed in the dish area under and around the dish machine where cleaning and general repairs are needed. Management noted detail cleaning and repairs were planned for the dish area, but the exact time frame was unknown. Ensure cleaning and general repairs are completed for temporary fix until full detail cleaning and repairs can be accomplished. Contact pest control operator for additional service as well.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Duct tape was observed as a repair material on the kitchen ice machine lid where insulation was exposed and along the top right side of the machine. Tape is not an approved repair material. Provide proper repairs to the dish machine. See general comments for additional information. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Chlorine test kit was not available for checking final rinse concentration at dish machines. 
 A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided. Obtain and use chlorine test strips to verify proper function of dish machines.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Leaks were observed at the following fixtures:
1) faucet of kitchen handwahsing sink by ice machine - water continues to drip when handles are in off position; and
2) faucet at sprayer sink in dish area - water steadily dripping beneath right faucet handle.
Provide repairs to eliminate leaks.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 REPEAT 1) Plastic base coving was unattached along the wall behind the kitchen dish machine.
2) Wall trim behind kitchen dish machine was loose and falling off the wall.
3) Caulking was loose and/or missing resulting in a gap at the handwashing sink to wall juncture in the north restrooms.
Provide repairs in the aforementioned areas.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 A) Floors were soiled in the following areas with food, general debris, and/or grease:
1) under and around the dish machine;
2) under kitchen ice machine, especially along the wall by the floor drain;
3) under soda machine in server area;
4) under shelving in dry storage; and
5) under fryers and table to the right of fryers. 
Ensure cleaning under and around equipment throughout the facility as needed to eliminate buildup.

B) Walls and attached plumbing were soiled in the following areas with dust and/or splash and general buildup:
1) at the kitchen ice machine;  and
2) under and around the dish machine.
Ensure walls and attached plumbing are cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed a food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Caulking along the rear edge of the triple sink along the back wall next to the entrance to the dry storage area. The sink appears to have shifted pulling it away from the caulking. Re-caulk the sink and ensure that all surfaces subject to food and/or moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Bags containing loaves of bread were stored on top of raw beef in the bottom of a reach-in cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage with bread away from raw meat.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Two metal stem food thermometers were available for use, with one reading around 80F and the other reading around 70F at ambient temperature. Based on information provided, thermometers were last calibrated approximately a year ago. Owner expressed knowledge on the calibration process for ice point method and verifying 32F in ice water. Thermometers were set aside to be cleaned and calibrated to ensure accuracy.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 One of the owners had a food manager certification that expired during the pandemic. At minimum a food handler certification is required. Ensure completion of the online food handler certification or manager certification by the next routine inspection. All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for barehand contact, cross contamination, sanitization, and cold holding. See violations 9, 15, 16, & 22 for details. A food thermometer is not available for use in the kitchen. Food handler documentation and allergen certification for CFM were unable to be provided at time of inspection due to staff not having access. Employee health documentation was not readily available. Owner will compile all necessary documentation to ensure it is available at the follow-up inspection in June.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health reporting agreements were not readily available, and staff were unsure where they might be located in the office. Inspector spoke with owner briefly on the phone, and owner noted they discussed employee health policy with staff but didn’t recall having them sign a form. Copies of employee health reporting agreement were reviewed and signed by staff working at the time of inspection. Ensure all staff not present at time of inspection also review and sign copies of the reporting agreement. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) 1) Small portion cups were observed in diced onion and tomatoes in the top of the salad cooler. Portion cups were removed and discarded. Cease the practice of using portions cups as scoops.

2) Spoon was stored in a container of escargot butter and noted to have the handle down in the product. Spoon was removed for cleaning.

3) PIC in kitchen had barehand contact with lettuce while discussing setup and function of the salad cooler. Per request of inspector, PIC washed hands, put on gloves, and discarded the portion of lettuce just touched.

4) PIC at bar was observed having barehand contact with drink garnishes (fruit/olives) while preparing beverages. Use of tongs and/or gloves in addition to handwashing was discussed when handling ready to eat foods.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Pizza slicer was stored in the crevice between the prep table and the wall. When removed from the area the slicer was soiled from use the previous evening. Pizza paddle on top of the oven was also soiled with food debris from the previous operating day. Both items were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.

2) Inner surfaces of soda gun nozzles were observed with heavy mold buildup. Nozzles observed to be soiled were on the east and west sides of the bar, and staff noted the soda gun on the north end of the bar is the main one used most frequently. Ensure cleaning and sanitizing of all soda guns and nozzles daily/as needed regardless of how often they are used. PIC at bar cleaned nozzles during the inspection. 

3) A long hair was observed on an ice scoop at the soda machine in the server area. Scoop was given to employee in dish area to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Plastic bags of pasta noodles were stored so outer surface of bags were in direct contact with noodles in containers located in the ice bath setup at the cook line. Bags of noodles were removed and portions of noodles in contact with bags were discarded. Outer surface of plastic food bags are not considered clean surfaces. Ensure proper storage with barriers between bagged foods and foods in other containers.

2) Small pan with diced onion was observed inside container of lettuce in top holding compartment of salad cooler. Outer surfaces of pans are not considered clean surfaces once in use, and a barrier is needed between the bottom/sides of pans and foods in other containers. Onions were relocated to allow for proper storage, and a small portion of lettuce was discarded. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket at bar was observed with concentration of 0ppm when checked with quat and chlorine test strips. PIC at bar noted they added water after dispensing the sanitizer. Fresh quat solution without added water was provided and observed at 400ppm. Ensure all staff know and understand the chemical dispenser is setup to dispense sanitizer at proper concentration and adding water will dilute product and weaken the concentration of sanitizer.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 Back side of slicer was soiled with stuck on food debris. PIC in kitchen noted it would have been used the evening prior. Staff began to disassemble slicer to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all slicer food contact surfaces that cannot be taken to the dish area for ware washing are manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized as well.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize the slicer between uses.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) 1) Diced ham and lettuce in the top holding compartment of the salad cooler had internal temperatures at 47F and 48F-50F respectively. PIC in kitchen noted all products are held in the bottom of the cooler overnight and placed in top holding compartment once it is turned on for service each day. Temperatures were checked again after and observed going up to 50F-52F. PIC realized the top compartment was actually turned off. All TCS foods in the top of the cooler in question were to be served or discarded by the end of lunch service. Ensure the top of the cooler is on, properly chilled, and able to maintain cold TCS foods at 41F/below prior to stocking for service.

2) Plastic bags of spinach fettuccini and spaghetti noodles stacked on top of containers of noodles in an ice bath at the cook line had surface temperatures at 70F-80F and internal temperatures ranged from 49F-71F. PIC in kitchen discarded one bag and placed another in a cooler. Remaining portion was to be used or discarded by the end of lunch service. Best practices of additional ice baths and/or storage in cooler and retrieving as needed were discussed.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food thermometers were not available for checking temperatures. Obtain and use digital food thermometers or stem thermometers with a temperature registering range of 0°F-220°F to verify proper cooking, cooling, reheating, hot holding, and cold holding temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Dozens of small flies that appeared to potentially be both fruit flies and drain flies were observed in the dish area under the counter along the east wall where the sprayer sink is located. title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to enter the kitchen, don gloves and begin food handling without washing hands. Education conducted to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Employee was advised on proper technique. Ensure hands are dried prior to using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet. If paper towels are used to shut off the faucet prior to drying hands, then discard the used paper towels and retrieve new paper towels to dry hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Ice scoop was observed with handle down in contact with ice in the bin of the ice machine. PIC noted the scoop is to be stored with the handle extended up out of ice and repositioned the scoop to allow for proper storage.
 Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of food thermometer was soiled with stuck on food debris. PIC removed soil and wiped down the food thermometer with sanitizer solution during inspection. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of food thermometer between uses.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. If quat solution is used to wipe stem after immediate use, ensure stem is cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

3-501.16 (A)(2) Almond milk and whipped topping sitting out for use at room temperature had surface temperatures above 45F. Cold holding versus time control were discussed. A time control policy was established during inspection (see general comments for additional information) .

Best practices for hot holding were discussed.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Container of shredded potatoes in an ice bath on cook line had an internal temperature of 39F for product in the bottom in contact with ice bath. Product further up in the container that was not in contact with ice bath was observed with an internal temperature ranging from 58F-62F. Potatoes were removed from cook line and placed in the walk-in freezer to quickly chill prior to cold holding in the prep cooler up front. Best practices were discussed for use of ice baths to cold hold TCS foods.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Tuna salad was observed with a date mark of 5/8 in the bottom of a prep cooler at the cook line. Chicken salad had a date mark that was partially torn making it difficult to know the date of prep. Products in question were discarded. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Portion of sliced potatoes were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 104F and 88F respectively. Potatoes were blanched in the fryer ~30 minutes prior to temperature check. Potatoes were in a covered container on ice at the cook line, but only the bottom of the container was in contact with ice intended for chilling. Potatoes were removed from the cook line and placed in the walk-in freezer to quickly chill product. Best practices were discussed for quick chilling cooked TCS foods.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Multiple spray bottles labeled as sanitizer (Shurguard and Kay Quat II) were observed with concentrations of 0ppm and 100ppm. A freshly prepared sani-bucket was also observed with a concentration of 0ppm quat. Another fresh solution was prepared for the sani-bucket and observed at 200ppm. Fresh solutions in spray bottles were initially observed at 0ppm. Quat solution was not consistently dispensing at 200ppm. Store manager ran the dispenser for several seconds at which time the concentration was then observed at 200ppm. Restaurant manager was advised to allow the dispenser to run for several seconds prior to filling bottles and buckets. Allow foam to settle before using test strips to check the concentration of liquid. Verify proper concentration of quat solutions prior to use. Also, ensure quat solitons in spray bottles are checked with test strips frequently to verify proper concentration and fresh solutions are provided as needed.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Sausage gravy cooked the day prior on 5/11 did not cool properly. Gravy was observed in 22qt containers in the walk-in coolers (one in the main walk-in and three in the bar walk-in). Condensation was on the inner surface of lids, indicating product was placed in the coolers and covered during the cooling process. Surface temperatures were at 46F-49F, while internal temperatures were observed at 55F, 59.5F, and 60.5F. Gravy was prepared between 10am-12pm the day prior. Employee helping with prep stated the blast chiller was not used, and product was placed directly in walk-in coolers. All gravy was discarded during inspection. Proper cooling was discussed, and educational handout was provided for management to re-educate staff.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

Best practices were discussed. Ensure only the amount of needed product is removed for prep from coolers. Promptly use TCS foods and/or place them back in cold holding when interruptions in tasks occur to limit temperature abuse.

Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

comment:

citation_text:

Flies were also clustered around a soiled dust pan by the mopsink and in a floor drain beneath the cafeteria garbage conveyor belt. General cleaning and repairs to help aid in fly management were discussed. Management already requested additional service with their pest control company, and PCO is currently scheduled to come in once a week at this time for service. Re-inspection will be conducted in ~2hrs to check on the status of pest control.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-403.12 Drain line to ice machine bin was slightly askew and draining on the floor underneath. Adjust the drain line to allow for proper drainage in the floor drain. 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law. Route waste to public sewer system per Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Floor drains throughout the dish area were soiled with varying amounts of debris and general buildup. 
2) Buildup of splash and debris were observed on the floor, wall, and components of the garbage disposal at the dish room 3 part sink.
3) Floor under conveyor belt between pulper and dish machine was soiled with food/general debris after a backup that occurred in the early morning hours (see general comments for additional information).
4) Food and general debris were observed under dry storage shelves. An old glue trap was also noted by the electrical access door. 
5) Floor under ice machine was soiled with accumulation of single service cups.
6) Floor between drink cooler and pizza station at cafe was soiled with an accumulation of food debris and general buildup.
Clean the aforementioned areas.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 1) Gap was observed at the floor to wall juncture under the 3 part sink just past the garbage disposal. Heavy fruit fly activity was observed in the area. Provide repairs to this location and any others in the area that could hold moisture/debris and serve a harborage location for pests.
2) Floor flashing in front of the cart washer on the side adjacent to the pulper was loose and moisture accumulation was noted in the area. Clean and dry the floor beneath the flashing and provide repairs to re-seal it to the floor. 
3) Piece of ceramic wall tile was missing by the mopsink. Provide repairs to the wall at the mopsink.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items were observed for reheating, sanitization, and proper disposal of waste water. A cooler with an iced up condensing unit was being used for cold holding but observed holding at 51F during inspection. PIC did not have employee health documentation and copies of certifications were not available for staff. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection in 2 weeks.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were not available at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Reporting agreements were signed by staff during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
301.11 Soap was not available at the dish room handwashing sink. Soap was provided.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sinks at the front bar counter and in the dish room were without handwashing signs. Handwashing signs were provided to be posted.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-702.11 While discussing ware washing process in the dish room, the cook began to use the wall mounted chemical dispenser to fill the sanitize basin. Inspector advised the chemical jug for sanitizer was empty. Cook was unaware the product was empty. Quat tablets were used to prepare sanitizer solution. Ensure concentration of 200-400ppm as required by instructions on manufacturer’s label and a contact time of at least 30 seconds on all surfaces prior to air drying. 
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.12 (B) Inside microwave was soiled with food splash, some of which appeared encrusted from previous operating days. Clean the microwave as needed to eliminate buildup.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Gravy and cheese sauce out on prep table were observed with internal temperatures of 78F and 83F respectively. Products were said to be held in he prep cooler overnight and just pulled recently to reheat. PIC briefly placed pans in the tabletop warmer but were removed by the cook to reheat products in the microwave some time prior to inspector’s arrival. Cheese sauce and gravy were reheated above 165F prior to hot holding. Ensure foods are left in the cooler until time to reheat. Use equipment intended for reheating to quickly and properly reheat TCS foods. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Reach-in cooler in kitchen was observed with heavy ice accumulation at the ceiling condensing unit. The hanging thermometer was reading near 50F. Frozen foods (fries, potatoes, tater tots) had internal temperatures at 32F-41F depending on how long they were in the cooler, and bacon pulled from the freezer to thaw overnight was observed with an internal temperature of 39F. Other foods included heads of lettuce and a whole whole tomato. All foods were relocated to coolers holding at 40F/below. Cooler door was kept closed for over 30 minutes and temperature was confirmed at 51F. Cooler will not be used until it is serviced and able to maintain temperature. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 1) Counter under microwave was soiled with food debris/general buildup.
2) Base of waffle iron and baking sheet beneath were soiled with food debris.
Clean under equipment and general surfaces daily/as needed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Old, dirty mop water was observed in the mop bucket by the mop sink in the dish room. Cook noted they mopped the day prior. PIC discarded the mop water during inspection. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave sitting in the facility overnight, as waste water can serve as a potential water/food source for pests.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for staff. Server completed training through previous employer and was advised to check with them about getting a copy. If copy cannot be obtained then server needs to complete another food handler course for certification. Cook has a food manager certification, but copy of certification was not available. Ensure copies of all food handler and manager certifications are available and maintained on-site by next routine inspection.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC has not completed food allergen certification. Certification needs to be completed by next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of allergen certification along with all other certifications for staff on-site.
All certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: There is observed visible soil on the inside wall of the ice machine. The internal walls of the ice machine were cleaned and sanitized during today’s inspection. Ensure the food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
4-904.13: The tableware at the walk up window were observed to be stored with the handles and ends of the spoons mismatched in the container. These utensils were removed during today’s inspection and all the tableware was placed inverted in the container with the handles facing up. Ensure the tableware remains stored inverted where the hands of the employees will not come into contact with the food contact surface of the utensil.
4-904.13: (A) TABLEWARE shall be protected from contamination if preset (wrapped, covered, inverted). (B) Preset maybe exposed if: unused settings are removed when consumer is seated  or settings are cleaned and SANITIZED before further use.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-601.11: The inside bottom shelf of the single door freezer with the chicken strips is observed to have an accumulation of breading and other food residues. Ensure this freezer is cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: The outlets near the milk cooler were observed to have a visible gap where the outlet cover has pulled away from the wall. The outlets were pushed back into the wall during today’s inspection. Further repairs are necessary to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface by securely attaching the outlet covers to the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of caulking: mop sink is missing caulking (caulk sink to wall), women’s bathroom hand sink needs re-caulked (coming away from wall and sink), and the coving at the base of the walk-in cooler needs caulked to the wall (gaps where grout and caulking should be). Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

PIC was unable to provide some form of verification for employee illness acknowledgment during this inspection. A copy of the reporting agreements given out by SCDPH were given. They are instructed to make copies and ensure that all food handlers (including bartenders) sign a copy and that the copies are maintained at the facility moving foreword. Inspector will follow-up in 2 weeks for compliance.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

On arrival, hand soap was not available at the sink in the bar area. Soap was provided during the inspection to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The potato slicer is observed soiled with dry food debris. PIC indicated that it was probably from last night. Food contact items should be cleaned after use, or at a minimum of 4 hours. The slicer was taken apart for cleaning during the inspection to correct. 2) The right soda gun is observed with pathogenic slime inside of the nozzle. The bartender was consulted and the item cleaned during this inspection to correct.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

On arrival, raw chicken is observed thawing in standing water in the kitchen’s large sink. A conversation took place in relation to thawing practices and it is suggested to place chicken (or other thawing foods) in a cleaned/sanitized bucket that would allow water to flow into it, overflow and then drain. Chicken was moved during this inspection to correct.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

There is a tube running out of an unused air unit in the kitchen, that terminates in the large sink used for thawing. During this inspection the tube is in contact with the standing water that is containing thawing chicken (refer to line item 35). This is a potential source of cross contamination and should be managed. The tube was removed from the sink to correct the violation. If it is non-functioning it is suggested to remove the item.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

Soil accumulation observed under shelving and in corners in the walk-in cooler. Clean as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
There was no Certified Food Protection Manager at the establishment at the start of the inspection. Ensure a CFPM is at the establishment during all hours of food preparation. This includes when hot holding of foods is occurring. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
Motor oil, antifreeze and other chemicals are stored next to and close to sugar, coffee, and other food or food contact surfaces (like paper towels and cups). Ensure these chemicals are stored in a location to prevent potential contamination of food. Additionally, a barrier can be put between chemicals and food so spilled chemicals cannot contaminate food. The oil and antifreeze were moved over a few inches to avoid possible contamination. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Water bottles cases were observed stored outside near the wall of the establishment. This is not considered a clean, dry location for the water bottles. Ensure the water bottles are moved to a clean, dry location where they are protected from possible contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
The tea dispenser did not have a lid covering the top of the dispenser. Ensure the lids are replaced after tea is brewed to protect tea from contamination. The lid was placed over the tea during the inspection to protect it from contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
The burrito and cheeseburger hot holding unit was not holding temperatures properly. The cheeseburgers and burritos were holding temperatures between 105F and 112F. The foods were discarded. After looking at the hot holding unit, the manager noticed that the unit’s had been turned off. After turning it on, the hot holding unit started functioning properly. This corrected the violation. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple wire shelves in the standing cooler next to the 3 part sink are observed with developing mold colonies on them. All foods in this cooler are sealed and not a concern for contamination at this time. PIC is instructed to clean and maintain clean.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed opened packages of turkey and ham cold cuts to not have a date mark. Items were date marked during inspection.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Observed 2 pairs of tongs hung from Ansul system above fryers in kitchen. Tongs were moved during inspection. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Floors in the facility kitchen and behind the bar are soiled with grease, food debris, bottle caps, other litter and soil. Clean floor areas more frequently and maintain free of accumulated soil.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Observed wet mop head stored head down in mop bucket. Hang mop after use to allow for drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
Observed CFPM on duty to not have additional allergen training certification. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Multiple employees observed to use a paper towel to turn off the faucet and then use the same paper towel to dry their hands. Education conducted. PIC instructed to review proper hand washing and ensure that good practices are enforced.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Doors of ice cream display cases were observed with cracks and areas of disrepair along edges of handles. Owner is working on repairs to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Multiple priority violations were observed during this inspection: handwashing, bare hand contact, and cold holding. Inspector will follow up to see that these practices are being addressed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Food service employees were observed to enter the kitchen, don gloves, and begin handling foods without first washing hands. Provided some education, but PIC should review when to wash hands with staff.
citation_text: 2-301.14 Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Employee observed to wash hands, then turn the faucet off without using a barrier to prevent recontamination of clean hands. CORRECTED- Provided education. Ensure employees use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

comment: Food employee observed to use bare hands to place a pickle on a plate. Discussed preventing bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat foods. citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed to have no measurable concentration of quat sanitizer. CORRECTED- Bucket was emptied and new sanitizer solution was prepared (200ppm quat).
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

comment:

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

title: Thermometers provided & accurate

Ambient thermometers in the cooler under the grill observed to read 45F and 65F. Foods in the cooler observed to be 49-57F. Ensure ambient thermometers are accurate. Calibrate or replace thermometers.
4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
No CFM was present at time of inspection.  Ensure a CFM is present during hours of operation.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Cheese sauce in clear door cooler was not date marked.  Discussion with employee revealed an employee had just filled the container with cheese sauce from a larger container that was properly date marked.  The container was placed in the cooler for a short time before being heated up on stove.  Inspector advised employee to always date every container that contains food to ensure employees know the date the food was prepared in the event the container does not get used the same day.  Cooking logs are also kept of foods cooked and cooled for future use.

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

-By the back door

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged Atlantic salmon was in various stages of thawing in the walk-in cooler. Proper thawing of reduced oxygen packaged fish was discussed. At minimum, packaging needs to be cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. If packages are thawed under running water, the fish much be removed from packaging as soon as thawing is completed. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in  (B) of this section.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Tubs of thawing fish were stacked so a tub with holes in the bottom allowed for running water to fill the tub of fish below. Kitchen manager placed fish in tub without holes and rearranged both tubs of fish to allow cold running water to flow over all surfaces of thawing fish via a split hose on the 3 part sink faucet. Best practices for thawing were discussed with kitchen manager.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

comment:

(B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]
