title: Food separated and protected
comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed a prep cooler with a large amount of mold growth on the inside of the cooler. The mold and lime scale has covered all surfaces inside the cooler. The cooler has pools of water on all lower surfaces with visible white, green and black mold growth. Black mold growth is observed on the upper surface and dripping down towards the lower edges of baffles, potentially dripping onto foods below it. Foods within the cooler were uncovered. All foods were removed from the cooler immediately. Water must removed from the cooler and the all surfaces within the cooler must be cleaned and sanitized and inspector must provide approval before foods may be stored in the cooler again. Inspector will return in three days to follow-up on the status of the cooler unless contacted earlier by operator. Foods must be protected from contamination at all times. Ensure that foods are stored in a manner that prevent ANY cross-contamination at ANY time. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022.

At the rear of the facility, inspector observed a large dough hook used to prepare fresh dough in the facility stored, dirty, directly on a wire rack for continued use. The dough hook was potentially contaminated immediately upon placing it on the dirty, unsanitized wire rack. The hook must be cleaned, sanitized and stored in a manner that prevents contamination. As long as the hook remains in use for only the single purpose of preparing raw dough, cleaning does not need to occur between use but it may only be stored on cleaned and sanitized surfaces between uses.

Also on a wire rack at the rear of the facility was an in-use cutting board placed underneath the dirty, unsanitized wire rack directly on the external, potentially contaminated, containers of flour. The cutting board was soiled with raw dough. The cutting board must be cleaned, sanitized and stored in a manner that prevents contamination as long as it remains used for the same purpose. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces being stored between uses are stored ONLY on cleaned/sanitized surfaces and remain protected from any form of contamination.

Inspector will return on Thursday 04/20/2023 to evaluate corrective actions.

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022. 

There are approximately ten flies at the rear of the facility near and within the hampers containing wet wiping cloths and soiled mop heads. Aramark collects these items for laundering once per week. This may not be suficient to prevent harborage of pests within these items. Ensure that the premise is inspected for pests and insects, especially flies, often and that harborage conditions such as sacks of wet soiled linens are eliminated from the facility to prevent worsening pest/insect problems. Contact third party pest control if store efforts to remove them are unsuccessful. Improve cleaning practices to further eliminate harborage conditions. 

Inspector will return on 04/27/2023 to evaluate progress towards eliminating insects from the facility.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
The far east display cooler was observed to contain foods at temperatures between 48 and 52 degrees F. Facility provided hanging thermometers indicated a temperature at the vent of 52 degrees F while actively blowing. Inspector had facility immediately cease serving foods from this cooler and discard foods. No logs are kept to determine if foods had been in the cooler for less than 4 hours and could still be used. Foods stored in the walk-in are mixed with remaining food in containers in the display cooler negating the possibility of using foods which have been in the cooler for less than 4 hours. title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment: Inspector observed cooling lo mien noodles in a medium sized metal bowl stored on the back shelves of the walk-in cooler. The noodles were approximately 78 degrees based on a digital probe-style thermometer reading. No logs are kept to record cooling times and temperatures to verify the two-hour mark had not been surpassed. Per 3-501.14 of the 2017 FDA Food Code, foods must be removed from heat and cooled quickly to prevent the growth of dangerous pathogens known to cause foodborne illness in cooling TCS foods. Foods must cool from an initial temperature of 135 degrees F after cooking to a temperature of 70 degrees F within 2 hours. Foods must cool from 135 degrees F after cooking to a temperature of 41 degrees F within 6 hours. Ensure that the facility adheres to these time/temperature requirements when cooling foods within the facility. Inspector will re-evaluate on 04/14/2023.

(G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
A shallow metal container of shelled eggs was stored on the top shelf of the upright cooler along the west wall of the kitchen. Several foods including raw beef and raw scallops were stored directly below this container of eggs. A recent complaint for possible foodborne illness indicated that one affected individual consumed scallops prior to the onset of symptoms. Storage order of raw animal products contributes to cross-contamination and is a potential source of illness. The container did not have a lid or any other covering to prevent contamination from the eggs to items beneath them. Stored raw foods must be stored in a manner, based on cooking temperatures, which prevents cross-contamination. Fish and pork must be cooked to a lower temperature of 145 degrees F for 15 seconds and thus should be stored above all other raw animal products but below ANY ready-to-eat foods. Beef must be cooked to 155 degrees F for 15 seconds and should be stored below fish and pork but above poultry. Poultry (including eggs) must be stored below other food items to prevent cross-contamination because it requires the highest cooking temperature of 165 degrees F. Ensure that staff are aware of proper storage order and the reason for separation and that foods are all separated in a manner that prevents contamination during storage. Should the facility require handouts or further education regarding proper storage order, reach out to Sangamon County Department of Public Health (SCDPH) immediately.

Operator immediately removed the container of shelled eggs and placed it on the bottom shelf next to the carboard container of other shelled eggs already located on the bottom shelf. Corrected on site. No follow-up required.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Inspector observed the following over the course of the inspection today:
- The hand sink in the deli as immediately after the entrance to the deli was not stocked with paper towels or soap. The soap dispenser was empty and open. Per operator, the paer towel dispenser is not functioning. 
- The second hand sink in the deli between the bakery and the deli was stocked with soap but was not stocked with paper towels.
- The hand sink in the meat processing area of the meat department was stocked with soap but not paper towels. Per the meat department operator, he had requested x4 times to have the paper towels stocked and they had not been stocked yet.

In both instances, operators were aware the sinks were improperly stocked. The person-in-charge of the deli left the facility to get chicken tenders from another store. The person-in-charge of the meat department had unfulfilled requests to have the paper towels stocked. 

The combination of violations during the inspection today is incredibly concerning. Staff was completely unable to wash hands WHILE participating in highly risky behavior with a high likelihood of contamination. Hand sinks in this facility have been a recurring problem. Facility fails to treat hand washing as a priority. Facility has been issued a repeat letter and notice to comply already for previous hand washing sink violations.

title: Proper cooking time and temperatures
comment:
A white sauce was observed cooking in a crock pot on the countertop in the southwest corner of the kitchen. A crock pot is not a proper piece of equipment heating/reheating food as it does not heat rapidly and allows foods to remain outsid critical limits for extended periods of time during food preparation. Foods must be cooked/reheated on a stovetop and may be hot held at 135 degrees in a crock pot AFTER heating to 165 degrees. A follow-up is being issued for 03/20/2023 to ensure the facility is following proper cooking procedures including times, temperatures and equipment. 

3-401.11: (A) Heat all parts of food to: 1) 145F for 15 seconds (raw eggs for immediate service, fish and intact meats); 2) 155F for 17 seconds (injected meats, raw eggs, and comminuted meats); 3) 165F for <1 second (poultry, stuffed meats/pastas/stuffing). (P)  (B) Whole roasts should follow cooking log (P) and have oven preheated (Pf).  (C) Undercooked if 1) NOT HSP; 2) whole, intact beef; 3) steak top and bottom cooked to 145F (C).  (D) Any raw foods if 1) NOT HSP (C), 2) not comminuted to kids (Pf), 3) Consumer Advisory, 4) Variance with HACCP plan approved (C).

2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Employees were not following requirements of the company HACCP plan. Sushi products prepared prior to inspector’s arrival were observed with internal temperatures above 50F in the display cooler, indicting they were not properly chilled to 41F/below prior to placement in the cooler. PIC confirmed products were placed directly in the display cooler after preparation. Sushi is to be chilled properly in the walk-in cooler or freezer prior to placing items in the display cooler or transporting to other stores. 
Sushi products prepared within the last 2hrs were sitting at room temperature in the prep area, and a California roll had an internal temperature of 64F. Sushi products should be placed in the walk-in cooler or freezer as soon as possible after preparation to ensure proper chilling and limit time in the temperature danger zone. 
Daily logs sheets for previous operating days show documentation, but PIC noted information for the current operating day was not yet written down. The pH meter is to be calibrated each day prior to use, and the pH of sushi rice should be checked prior to use to confirm a pH of 4.1 or below. Food handler stated sushi rice had a pH of 3.9 when checked this morning. Employees were advised to write down information as they go to ensure proper documentation.
Thermometer available for use has a probe to take internal temperatures and also has the ability to take surface temperatures via an infrared option. PIC stated they use the infrared option for temperature documentation. The thermometer has not been calibrated recently to ensure accuracy. Per HACCP information the thermometer should be checked at minimum weekly. PIC was advised to use the ice point method to calibrate the probe thermometer (32F) and use the probe thermometer to verify internal temperatures of foods during daily temperature checks. 
Facility is currently without a certified food manager, as both the PIC and other employee have expired certifications. 
Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at a follow-up inspection in 2 weeks.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Tempura shrimp was observed with an internal temperature of 63F-68F in pan sitting at room temperature on top of the prep cooler. PIC confirmed the shrimp was fried around 7am and was sitting out at room temperature to cool prior to use. Shrimp was used to prepare sushi products starting around 8:30am. Shrimp was taken to walk-in cooler to chill until it was needed again to prepare products.
Best practices were discussed for cooling and cold holding cooked tempura shrimp. Shrimp should not sit at room temperature for hours while cooling and during preparation of sushi products. Ensure shrimp is placed in the walk-in cooler or walk-in freezer in a loosely covered or uncovered pan protected from cross contamination to allow for quick chilling. Remove shrimp from cold holding when it is time to prepare sushi containing tempura shrimp, and place shrimp in the cooler when not in use. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of manual faucet were touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Eggrolls and fried chicken pieces were observed cooling at room temperature. Products were said to be cooked within the last 30 to 35 minutes prior to inspector’s arrival. Internal temperatures ranged from 79F to 105F for eggrolls and 91F-127F for chicken. A portion of fried chicken still at the wok had an internal temperature ranging from 99F to 133F at the bottom where product was near heat source. Best practices were discussed, as well as monitoring time and temperature during the cooling process. All foods were placed in the walk-in cooler to finish rapid chilling. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

3-501.15 Ground beef cooked this morning to be used for spaghetti on another day was tightly covered with plastic wrap and aluminum foil in the walk-in cooler. Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 
 When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet and obtain paper towels for drying hands. Proper technique was discussed, and educational handout showing proper handwashing process was provided. Best practice would be to have paper towels ready prior to beginning handwashing process and use paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the manual faucet and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser if additional towels need to be dispensed. Elbows and forearms may also be used to shut off the faucet and touch the handle to dispense paper towels. Ensure proper handwashing occurs between tasks and prior to food preparation and service. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee exited the restroom and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to begin food prep. Employee was asked as to the use of a barrier when exiting the restroom and confirmed a paper towel was not used to touch the door handle. Employee re-washed hands at the kitchen handwashing sink and put on a new pair of gloves upon request of inspector. Ensure hands are properly washed upon re-entering the kitchen after using the restroom and prior to putting on gloves to handle food. Best practice would be to wash hands again in the kitchen after exiting the restroom even if a barrier was used to touch the handle of the door. However, using a paper towel to touch the door handle after properly washing hands in the restroom would negate the need for an additional hand wash in the kitchen as long as no other general surfaces were touched prior to beginning food prep or other tasks. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the kitchen after using the restroom, before putting on gloves to handle food, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

comment:

Complaint is valid. Whole frozen turkeys in the open top freezer case are observed to have areas where meat was soft to the touch. The unit is functioning properly. The issue is from portions of the turkeys sticking up above the freeze line for too long. Turkeys in the case were evaluated for soft spots. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Breakfast corndogs in individual portion bags were out in the service area upon arrival of inspector and later observed in the walk-in cooler. Surface temperatures were observed at 92F-76F, and the internal temperature for one of the breakfast corndogs was observed at 101F-103F. PIC noted corndogs were out for ~1hr prior to placing in the walk-in cooler. Product was still within the first two hours of cooling process based on information provided. Best practices were discussed. Bags were loosened to allow for heat transfer, and baking sheet was moved to the walk-in freezer to finish quick chilling. PIC noted product had an internal temperature of 42F after being in the freezer ~30 minutes. Educational handouts on proper cooling were provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Surface temperature of brown rice was observed at 46F-49F and internal temperature was 52.3F. Rice was in a covered plastic container in the walk-in cooler. PIC indicated the rice was made around 8am and placed in the cooler around 9am to begin cooling process. Based on information provided, the rice had another 30 minutes to reach 41F/below. Rice was placed in the walk-in freezer to finish rapid chilling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Although violations from the previous routine inspection have been corrected and no new priority foundation/priority violation were observed during the inspection today, facility has a history of severely hazardous violations and recurrent high-risk behaviors that resurface when further inspections are not anticipated. As such, an additional 30-day follow-up is being issued to ensure continued compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code requirements and to encourage continued improvement and the development of health-oriented habits at the facility. Ensure that all staff are washing hands FREQUENTLY throughout the course of operations. Work towards developing the habit of hand washing at all activity changes and anytime contamination may occur. Ensure that sanitizer is made at all times of operation and that ALL food-contact surfaces are sanitized with bleach water at least every 4-hours if not more often. Work on establishing managerial control and developing practices for the facility to remain in compliance without the anticipation of inspection. Operators have demonstrated an understanding of Food Code requirements but must show continued compliance. 

Inspector will return on 02/09/2023 to evaluate progress at that time. 

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. 

1) Multiple items in the steam table along the main kitchen walkway are observed between 112F and 120F. Items were prepared fresh this morning at approximately 7 am. The steam table has been turned up and the TCS items will be discarded at 11 am (4 hours). Items include cheese sauce, gravy and sausage. 2) Chili is observed with an internal temperature of 123 in the steam table to the right of the fryer. Foods in the other lines are observed at correct temperatures. Investigation indicated that the water was nearly out in the bottom of the line and is believed to be why the equipment was not functioning correctly in this spot only. Water was added to correct the situation and the chili is observed at correct temperatures at the end of the inspection. Chili will still need to be discarded by 11 am (4 hours) due to temperature abuse.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:

Information was provided for food manager courses. Ensure enough staff have a food manager certification to cover all hours of operation. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC was observed touching the edge of pizza with unwashed hands. This happened while discussing the cook time and documentation of time for pizzas that sit at room temperature after baking. Prior to touching pizza PIC was holding a pen and order pad and had not washed his hands at the designated handwashing sink since inspector arrived at the facility. Handwashing was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink between tasks and prior to food handling. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:

Employee was also observed filling a cup with water for a customer at the handwashing sink after being advised the handwashing sink was to be used only for handwashing. PIC later used the handwashing sink to prepare a bleach solution to soak soda nozzles. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed and reiterated multiple times. Ensure handwashing sink is used only for handwashing and no other purposes. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

citation_text:
6-301.12 Men’s restroom paper towel dispenser was empty. Paper towels were provided during inspection.

PIC was advised the can opener requires a full wash, rinse, and sanitize like all other food contact surfaces. Can opener was placed in the dish machine and ran through proper ware washing cycle.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Some mold buildup was observed in the ice machine on the baffle. The buildup long the top where the baffle attaches to the ceiling was hard/encrusted. Some buildup was also noted to be encrusted in the gap at the hinge of the door. These were areas that would need to be addressed when the machine could be shut down to remove ice and allow for thorough cleaning. 
The baffle had some mold as well but was minimal and able to be wiped down with a bleach solution to remove buildup at the time of inspection. A clean pan was used as a barrier while wiping the baffle, and a layer of ice was removed once wiping was done. 
Ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate mold buildup. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Sauces were observed in a unplugged food warmer. Surface and internal temperatures were at 50F-51F and 49F-50F respectively. PIC noted sauces were held in the unit and heated to order as needed, and PIC sometimes sets up an ice bath. Ice bath was not provided for holding unit today. Sauces were placed back in the walk-in cooler, which was holding at 34F. PIC was advised to ensure a proper ice bath is maintained for sauces or to use time control and discard after 4hrs of use at room temperature.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19 Pizzas were observed with surface temperatures ranging from 74F (individual slice) to 103F (partial pizza) and 107 (whole pizza). PIC noted all pizzas were just made within the last hour or less. Documentation of time for pizzas held at room temperature was discussed. PIC provided documentation during inspection.
Ensure proper documentation of the time for all working supplies of baked pizzas and sauces held at room temperature. Pizza sauce just removed from the walk-in cooler was on the prep table at room temperature and observed with internal temperature of 45F.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F/below when removed from cold holding or 135F/above when removed from hot holding; (2) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; (3) the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready-to-eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; and (4) food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Two (approx 1 gal each) containers of cheese sauce observed in the walk in cooler at 80F (probed). All three containers were without time stamps. Per PIC, cheese was placed in the walk-in cooler at 11:30pm. Containers had been in the walk-in cooler for 2.5 hours at the time of inspection. Ice baths were used to speed the cooling process. At 3:30pm, inspector checked temperatures again. Both containers were observed to be 75F (probed). CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling. Ensure containers are labeled with time stamps when the cooling process began.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Mops were observed to be stored in the base of the mop buckets with no way for the wet mops to air dry and/or drain. Mops must be stored in a manner that allows for air drying and prevents contamination. Ensure that mops are hung inverted along the wall or that they are stored in the upper portion of the mop bucket to facilitate draining and drying and prevent contamination. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
The hand sink along the east wall of the kitchen near the register and bread pans did not have any paper towels in the dispenser or nearby. All hand sinks must be stocked with paper towels at all times to facilitate hand washing. Ensure that hand sinks are stocked with paper towels and soap at all times. Operator immediately added paper towels to the dispenser. Corrected on site. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
The dish machine sanitizing stage did not register any chlorine concentration on SCDPH test strips or facility test strips. Operator made multiple attempts to correct the problem including priming but was unable to get the dish machine functioning within required limits. As such, facility has been instructed to cease use of the dish machine for sanitizing operations. Machine may be used for cleaning but all items washed through the dish machine or sink must be sanitized in the third (sanitizing) basin of the triple sink prior to use/storage. Operator states that the dish machine concentration is tested on a daily basis. Operator has been instructed to call SCDPH inspector when repairs have been made by EcoLab and prior to using the dish machine for sanitizing operations. If no corrections have been made prior, inspector will return on 01/06/2023 to evaluate progress of repairs and ensure that facility continues to utilize the triple sink for ALL sanitizing operations. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Inspector observed individually packaged containers of sliced meat stored in a broken box on the floor of the walk-in freezer underneath shelving. Foods must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. Foods may not be stored under sources of contamination (i.e. underneath shelving units). Ensure that foods are protected from contamination by storing in a dry, clean location at least 6 inches above the ground at all times. Operator immediately removed food from this location and discarded it. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
Baking sheets throughout the facility which are used for baking bread in-house are observed to be soiled/worn to the point that cleaning of the sheets is no longer possible. Baking sheets are brown to black in color due to long-term use and are visible soiled with accumulated burnt residue and debris. The accumulation of residue on these baking sheets creates a surface which can no longer be cleaned easily.  Baking sheets must be cleaned or resurfaced to be free of residue or replaced by the next routine inspection which will occur in mid-2023. Per conversation with person-in-charge, facility has been trying to power wash these pans to remove residue and debris. Inspector observed that pans which were power still had residue and debris present and had scoring as a result of use and the power washing process.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The right-hand cabinet underneath the lemonade counter in the dining area is observed to have a significant amount of spilled lemonade accumulating on both top and bottom shelf of the cabinet. This cabinet must be cleaned. Ensure that non-food-contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of residue and debris and that spills are cleaned up at the time they occur. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Inspector observed that the broom/dustpan combination were stored immediately leaning on pans which held packaged containers of bread and other items. Brooms, mops and other maintenance items must be stored in a location which does not pose the risk of the contaminating food. Ensure that maintenance tools are stored properly between uses. Inspector moved the broom so that it no longer touched packages of food during the inspection and discussed with person-in-charge. Corrected on site. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Areas of the floor along the base coving tile in the walk-in freezer are observed to have a significant amount of residue and debris accumulating. Clean underneath these shelves by the next routine inspection. Ensure that the areas underneath shelving and equipment are cleaned on a regular basis to prevent the accumulation of soil throughout the facility.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
The following areas need to be repaired/re-caulked/replaced to ensure smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surfaces. 
- Behind the large dump sink in the west portion of the kitchen.
- Small holes in the walls throughout the facility where food preparation occurs.
- Holes and exposed wood on the cabinets under the front registers.
- Cracked floor tiles to the left of the bread ovens.
Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable and those subject to food and moisture are non-absorbent prior to the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed an employee at the register who needed assistance with the processing of a consumer debit/credit card. The person-in-charge assisted the employee with the process but was observed to return to food service/preparation immediately after touching the debit/credit card without switching gloves and washing hands. Ensure that hands are washed between activities that may have contaminated the hands/gloves. Discuss with employees the need to wash hands between such activities. Inspector immediately instructor person-in-charge to wash hands before returning to food service. Person-in-charge washed hands immediately. Corrected on site. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter immediately to the east of the drive-thru window. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution at all times when not actively being used to wipe surfaces and may not be stored on countertops or other surfaces. Ensure that all employees are aware that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution (buckets) between uses. The wiping cloth was removed from the counter immediately and placed in sanitizer solution. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

Test strips must be available and used for all sanitizers used in the establishment. Test strips were provided from the inspector to correct the violation. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

2. Both ice machine baffles were soiled with pink, slime-y mold. Inspector showed PIC. PIC washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware of the above listed places as frequent cleaning areas - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

Observed no heat temperature test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer in order to accurately measure the temperature of the dish machine. PIC ordered a maximum register thermometer during the inspection. Inspector will follow-up on 1/6/23.

comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 Table top dicer was observed with food debris stuck on the blade and push block. Dicer was set aside for cleaning.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the only allergen training certification available to be expired. See that all CFPM’s have up-to-date allergen certification (valid for 3 years). Print copies for the public health binder. Discussed with PIC. Ensure by next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed the CFPM to not have proof of licensure. Discussed with PIC. PIC is having issues with the company he took the course with in order to schedule examination. Ensure the exam is completed and proof of license is available at the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 10/4/22.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the bar hand sink upon Inspector attempting to wash hands. Bartender provided new paper towels. Ensure hand sinks are stocked so proper hand washing may occur (need to dry hands and utilize a barrier to turn off the faucets). Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed the fried rice hot holding to have a surface temperature of 110F. Observed the cheese sauce hot holding to have a surface temperature of 125F. Discussed hot holding temperatures being 135F. PIC rapidly reheated the items to 165F on the grill line/wok line per Inspector’s request. Hot held items had not been on the hot holding units for very long (facility opens at 4 PM). Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed the food handler’s licenses to not be available at the facility. Ensure all staff obtains a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Ensure copies are left at the facility. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 10/4/22.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Cook was observed chewing gum while working in the kitchen. Gum was discarded at request of inspector.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Spatulas removed from the dish machine were dried with a used, damp wiping cloth. Proper air drying of utensils and equipment after ware washing was discussed. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage. Spatulas were placed through additional ware washing cycle prior to setting aside to air dry. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in sani-buckets in kitchen and front service area were a 100ppm. Fresh solutions were provided at 200ppm. Staff were advised to consider pre-wetting wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to placing in fresh solutions as sometimes wiping cloths will draw sanitizer out of solution depending on the type of cloth.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 TCS foods in the kitchen prep cooler had internal temperatures at 45F/above. Pasta salad and cantaloupe in the bottom of the cooler were observed with internal temperature of 62F and 49F-50F respectively. Products were discarded. Other foods had internal temperatures of 45F-47F in the top and bottom of the cooler, including diced/sliced tomatoes, feta cheese, sour cream portion, and chicken salad portions. Cooler was holding around 43F per inspector’s calibrated food thermometers. Benefit of doubt for foods at 45F-47F was given based on foods just being restocked and being in and out of the cooler for food service. TCS foods with internal temperatures above 45F at the close of business were to be discarded. See general comments for additional information.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer in the bottom of the prep cooler was reading around 30F, and the cooler was holding at 43F. New hanging thermometers were provided.
Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Small coolers used for milk storage in cabinets at coffee counter had severely torn gaskets. Replace the gaskets as soon as possible. The torn gaskets in combination with staff being in and out resulted in the specialty milk cooler holding at 44F. All milks should be stored in the 2 door drink cooler by the ice machine overnight until the gaskets are replaced to allow for consistent cold holding at 41F/below.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer available for use was observed at 20F when checked for accuracy with ice point method. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F in ice water. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 Wall mounted slicer used to make fries was soiled with old food debris. Slicer was removed and taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Raw shrimp was observed in a pan of water on the ledge of the kitchen prep sink. Pan was placed under cold running water to finish thawing. Best practices for thawing were discussed. Ensure proper thawing of TCS foods.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee entered the kitchen and was observed via the pass-through window going straight to the fryers/cook line without first washing their hands. Literally seconds prior the employee was seated at the designated staff break table in the dining room with the owner (PIC). PIC was advised as to what was observed and stated the employee was planning to wash their hands at the back handwashing sink in the kitchen. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed. Ensure all staff are washing their hands after breaks before entering the kitchen and prior to food preparation.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Front handwashing sink should not be used to fill water pitchers and/or discard liquids. Do not store pitchers or any other items in the basin of handwashing sinks for any reason.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:

If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. comment:

1. Paint on wall near the hand sink in the kitchen is chipped and peeling. Ensure all paint on the kitchen walls is smooth and repaint any additional areas as needed.
2. The right of the dish machine by the corner is in need of caulk.  The rest of the dish area has been caulked.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Facility should be smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent regarding materials of walls, ceilings, and floors.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 

Time as a control policy written today as a flat of eggs is observed to be sitting out at room temperature. Cook says that the eggs need to be room temperature for proper cooking in dish. Time was written on egg flat. Eggs will be used or discarded by 2:30pm.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed boxes of tea on the floor at the smoothie bar. Boxes of food are observed on the floor of the walk in freezer. Store all food a minimum of 6 inches above the floor.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Observed a purse and personal water bottle on the table in the hall of  dish area. Also, an unopened bottle of water is observed on the cart at the cook line. Finally, personal drinks and items are observed on the back of the smoothie bar. The items were moved to the top shelf of the metal shelves under the coffee and hot water/hot tea station. Store employee belongings properly at all times.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Facility has several priority/priority foundation violations and several repeat violations. Operator appears able to take corrective action when violations are observed but does not appear to understand the inherent risks of the violations observed. Ensure that facility is in compliance with all priority/priority foundation items, that employees are educated on proper food handling, cleaning and hygiene practices, and that repeat violations do not occur. A 30-day follow-up will be assessed to evaluate active managerial control and efforts towards compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code Requirements. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed virtually no hand washing occurring in the facility. At the sushi bar, both operators were observed to be standing with their arms crossed, hands underneath arm and body, returning to the preparation of raw, ready-to-eat sushi without any form of hand washing. No hand washing was observed during food preparation in the back of the house. Inspector observed two operators return from outside without washing hands prior to returning to work. Hand washing is a recurring problem at the facility. Ensure that hand washing is occurring often and that all employees understand the frequency and procedure of hand washing required. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
The hand washing sink at the sushi bar, in the middle, is observed to be missing paper towels. Ensure that paper towels are provided at both hand washing sinks at the sushi bar. This is a repeat violation.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
The middle hand washing sink at the sushi bar is observed to be missing soap. Soap is available at the sink at the end of the sushi bar, but these are not adjacent sinks and do not qualify for exemption. Ensure that all hand washing sinks are properly stocked with soap at all times. This is a repeat violation.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
comment:
Several cans on the rolling rack are observed to be dented along the upper/lower seam and/or with severe dentals along the outer edge which continues to the upper/lower seams. Ensure that cans received from suppliers are in good condition. All cans identified with potentially hazardous dents must be discarded immediately. Discarded items include x4 cans of pineapple juice and x1 can of bamboo shoots. Items are voluntarily discarded by operator during inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed food stored underneath a countertop. The underside of the countertop was heavily soiled with loosely attached dust and debris. Food may never be stored underneath dirty surfaces. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by storing in clean locations away from sources of contamination. The food was removed from the area; corrected on site. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed a personal phone sitting on top of an open box of single-use gloves which operator confirms are used in food preparation at the facility. The top layer of gloves in direct contact with the personal phone was discarded immediately. The phone was removed. Ensure that single-use gloves and other food contact surfaces used to work with RTE food are protected from contamination. 

3-304.15: (A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Inspector observed countertops which food is prepared on being wiped down with water that had no sanitizer present. An operator immediately added two capfuls of bleach to the water with a Cl concentration of 100 ppm and the counter was wiped down properly. Corrected on site. 

The dish machine was observed to be operating with a bleach concentration greater than 200 ppm chlorine. No label is present on the machine to indicate operating parameters for bleach concentration. The machine is serviced by GFS. Contact GFS to ensure that proper bleach concentrations are being used in the dish machine. 

Two sanitizer buckets in the facility were observed to have concentrations of sanitizer too low to measure using SCDPH test strips. Concentrations high enough to register on facility test strips were obtained by soaking and stirring the test strips in the water. Ensure that test strips are used properly and that sanitizer meets concentration requirements. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Inspector observed cleaned/sanitized bowls in a soiled container and with a piece of green onion sitting on top of the bowls. Dishes must be protected from contamination and must be cleaned/sanitized properly when contamination occurs. 

The blade of the can opener was observed to be soiled with old, dry food. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized often. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Date marking was inconsistent throughout the facility. The upright cooler to the right of the triple sink was observed to have no date marking at all. All other coolers had a mix of date marked items and items missing date marking. Ensure that date marking is occurring throughout the facility on all items requiring date marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wet wiping cloths were observed sitting on counters throughout the facility and in buckets with too low a concentration of sanitizer to remain sanitary. Wiping cloths, when not in use, must be stored in sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths are ONLY stored in sanitizing solution between uses. This is a repeat violation. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The facility is in need of deep cleaning throughout. Most pieces of equipment are heavily soiled in all hard-to-reach areas. Easily reached areas appear to be cleaned regularly but details are frequently missed allowing residue and debris to accumulate throughout the facility. Ensure that all equipment is cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of residue and debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Physical facilities appear clean ONLY is easy to clean places. Underneath all equipment and most corners of the kitchen and sushi bar there are large amounts of debris on the floor and particularly in corners. Deep cleaning must occur in underneath ALL equipment by the next routine inspection and must remain clean. Cleaning must occur at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of residue and debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
All sinks in the kitchen have damaged/missing/deteriorating caulk. Ensure that all sinks are caulked to create a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Inspector observed that the ice machine had a buildup of red residue along the lower edge of the baffle. Operator observed the same. The baffle was immediately cleaned and sanitized. Corrected on site. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Inspector observed a reach-in cooler which had foods at 65 degrees F using infrared. The temperature readout on the external gauge showed a temperature of 65 degrees F. All foods inside were immediately discarded and replaced; facility will use time-as-a-control and toss all foods in the cooler every 4 hours until repaired. Operator will call to have the cooler serviced. A follow-up is issued for 12/27/2022 (due to holiday schedule and willingness of operator to make necessary changes until repairs are made) to ensure that foods in this cooler are in safe condition and that the cooler has been repaired/replaced to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Eggs which were in the cooler were removed and no meats are stored in the cooler at this time. Discussed with operator the hazards of processed/cut produce. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
The triple sink is observed to have deteriorating and/or molding caulking along the back edge of the sink against the wall. Re-caulk these surfaces to ensure a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. Ensure that all ares of the facility subject to food or moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Hand washing frequency has improved at this facility from previous inspections this year. However, inspector observed two instances of improper procedure specifically less than 20 seconds of washing and failure to use a barrier. Hand washing is has been problematic in the past and corrective action is required. Educate all employees on proper hand washing procedures. Ensure that all employees are washing hands for the required time and with proper procedure. Discuss with staff the importance of hand washing to food borne illness prevention. This is a repeat violation from the previous routine inspection. A follow-up is issued for 12/27/2022. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed a personal vape sitting on the shelf above the food preparation area across from the hand sink on the east side of the wall. Vapes contain nicotine and thus pose a contamination hazard when stored near/above food preparation surfaces and food itself. Ensure that vapes are stored in designated areas away from food preparation and food itself. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
The door handle of the silver upright cooler on the east wall of the facility is damaged and partially missing. This was a problem during the previous inspection. This handle must be replaced. Equipment must be maintained in good repair. Further, the missing handle creates areas of the equipment which are not smooth and easily cleanable and are touched regularly which poses a contamination hazard. Ensure that the handle of the cooler is repaired by the next routine inspection. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The fan near the cook line on the south wall is visibly soiled with dust and debris. Should the fan be turned on, this would be a potential source of contamination for food along the line. Ensure that the fan is cleaned and all non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned regularly. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
The base coving underneath the hand sink and underneath the drying portion of the triple sink is observed to be peeling from the wall. Reattach or replace the coving to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud.
