title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
A slightly wet mop is sitting on the floor next to the mop sink. The mop must be stored off the floor in a manner which allows it to air dry including in the top portion of the mop bucket or inverted hanging along the wall. Ensure that mops and other maintenance tools are stored properly. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
Manager was not present during the inspection. Food was actively cooking on the roller grills. Food was removed and food preparation ceased immediately. Ensure that a certified food manager is present during all food-preparation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
The sanitizer bottle next to the microwave at the front of the facility was observed to have a concentration which exceeded the testing parameters of the test strips (bleaching). Sanitizer was dumped; corrected on site. Operator was unaware of where test strips are in the facility. Ensure that sanitizer is maintained at proper food-contact concentrations and that operators are aware of testing procedures and criteria. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) New cook that started at the facility as of 12/16/22 did not have a signed copy of the employee health reporting agreement on file. Employee health policy was discussed with PIC and copies of documents were provided. New hire reviewed and signed reporting agreement. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

PIC was advised to ensure soiled equipment is removed from service area and at minimum placed at 3 part sink at the end of operations to ensure soiled items are not potentially available for use the next day. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Prepared foods leftover from Sunday in the walk-in cooler did not have date marks, including but not limited to, white rice, sweet and sour chicken, and General Tso chicken. Thawed shrimp eggrolls and portion of sweet and sour chicken in the reach-in cooler were also without date marks. Foods were properly dated during inspection and kept for use. Date marking and options for tracking dates (piece of notebook paper posted on cooler, etc.) were discussed.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Open #10 can of Ketchup from Sunday was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. Proper storage was discussed. Acidic foods need to be stored in plastic or stainless steel containers after opening if they will not be used within the current operating day. Inner lining of cans may corrode off into foods when acidic foods are left inside the original can after opening. Ketchup and Hoisin sauce were were placed in stainless steel containers during inspection.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

Otherwise, provide a durable, easily cleanable liner, such as baking sheets or hard plastic.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed person in charge wash hands and turn the faucet off without a barrier. When washing hands, a paper towel or other barrier must be used to prevent re-contaminating hands. Ensure that hand washing follows proper procedure. 

This is a repeat violation from 8/31/2022. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Upon arrival, the hand washing sink was accessible. During the inspection, operator moved equipment in front of the hand sink blocking access. Ensure that hand sinks are not blocked at ANY time during operations to facilitate FREQUENT hand washing. 

This is a repeat violation from inspection dated 8/31/2022. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed food sitting on the floor uncovered, food sitting underneath shelving uncovered, and food sitting in the walk-in (on the floor and on shelving) uncovered underneath surfaces which are not cleaned/sanitized. Food may not be stored on the floor. Food must be protected from contamination at all times. Ensure that food is protected during operations. Inspector will return on 12/12/2022 to check on food protection. 

This is a repeat violation from 8/31/2022. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Chicken was observed at 51 degrees on the trash can. Chicken was immediately returned to the walk-in cooler. Beef was observed sitting out on the floor at 63 degrees. The food was placed in the smoker to cook. The beef had been sitting on the floor since 11:00 AM. Food was discarded. Imitation crab was observed sitting on top of equipment in a pan at a temperature of 68 degrees F since around 10:30 AM to 10:45 PM per PIC. Imitation crab was discarded. Ensure that foods which are are required to be cold held are stored at 41 degrees F at ALL times except during ACTIVE cooking/preparing. When preparing food, a maximum of two hours may be taken for food preparation. All food that is out of temperature must be discarded after 4-hours. 

This is a repeat violation from 8/31/2022. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:

This is a repeat violation from 8/31/2022. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food items including but not limited to a bag of cooked beef, pans of chicken, and open containers of sauces stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler. These items must be stored at least 6 inches off the floor. Ensure that all foods are stored at least 6 inches off the floor and in clean, dry locations at all times. 

This is a repeat violation from 8/22/2022. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Inspector observed in use utensils stored on soiled counter tops, on soiled shelves, and behind pipes which are visibly soiled. Utensils must ONLY be stored in clean, dry locations and food contact surfaces may only come in contact with cleaned and sanitized surfaces. Ensure that utensils are stored properly. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:

Inspector observed that the counter tops, shelving underneath counters, and other portions of the equipment to be soiled. Cleaning must occur regularly throughout the facility to preclude the accumulation of soil and debris. Ensure that cleaning is occurring as often as required and to a sufficient degree to prevent contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:

This is a repeat violation from 8/31/2022.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 
Cheese sauce (2 large pans full) is observed in the walk in cooler at 74F. The cheese sauce was made last night at 7pm according to manager. Cooling temperatures are not documented. At 11:30am the cheese sauce is still 74F. The large pans were stacked on top of each other. The pans were not more than 4 inches deep individually and were covered with pan lids that do not have holes to allow heat to escape. Recommend filling the pans only half full (2 to 3 inches maximum) and cooling items must be separated  and loosely covered so that heat can move away from the food. Use mindful cooling practices. The pans of cheese sauce were discarded.

comment: 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. Another large pan of cheese sauce about 1/2 full was on top of the cheese sauce at 74F. The internal temperature of this pan was 58F. One gallon of milk and two flats of eggs were also in the walk in cooler.  Milk and eggs were both 58F.  Pans of cheese sauce and eggs were discarded in the garbage. Milk was poured down the drain.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: 3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). Observed small pan and large pan of cheese sauce half full to be date marked 11.26.22. Today is 10 days in the establishment. The cheese sauce was discarded. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C
Pans of cheese sauce cooling in the walk in cooler have tight fitting covers and are stacked so that heat transfer can not readily take place. Use proper cooling practices. Suggest putting less cheese sauce in each pan and leaving uncovered or loosely covered. The foods can also be placed into the walk in freezer for a few hours to knock the temperature down. Stirring regularly during the cooling process is also helpful in rapidly moving the temperature of cooling foods through the temperature danger zone.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Observed foods in the upright to the right of the prep counter to be held at temperatures between 41 and 45 degrees. The internal thermometer and built-in thermostat read 44 degrees F. Operator instructed to move foods from cooler if the cooler cannot be fixed rapidly. Ensure that foods are held at proper temperatures at all times. comment:

No foods within the walk-in coolers were out of temperature or appeared to be spoiled. Facility will use items without date marking immediately and will label foods in the walk-in cooler. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C). 3-501.15 (A)(2) 1. Carafes of dressings were observed in the top left side of the salad cooler sitting on the edges of pans. Internal temperatures were at 67F to 68F for blue cheese and chipotle ranch. title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Kitchen manager was observed using a wiping cloth to wipe their hands after previous discussion of proper use. Improper handwashing technique was later observed when the manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and the handle to the paper towel dispenser was touched after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing was discussed. Ensure proper technique is used every time hands are washed. Always use disposable paper towels for wiping hands and not wiping cloths/common towels.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

3-304.11 1. Plate used for storage of ice scoop on top of the ice machine was soiled with discolored splash and grimy buildup. After cleaning and sanitizing the plate was stained and had stuck on buildup. Plate was discarded by manager.

2. Soda gun holder at banquet area bar was soiled with crusty buildup and possibly dried out mold. Holder was removed to be cleaned and sanitized. 

3. Mold accumulation was observed on the metal baffle in the bin of the ice machine and along the top above the baffle. Mold was also observed inside the bin on the ceiling behind the baffle. Ice machine will be cleaned and sanitized, and follow-up will be conducted to check the machine on 12/9/22.

Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

Chlorine strips are needed for the dish machine and any bleach solutions (100-200ppm) used for wiping down surfaces. Quat strips are needed for sanitizer tabs at the bar and product now being used in the kitchen.
 A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:

comment:

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Observed hand washing performed twice without a barrier and for less than 20 seconds. Discussed with PIC and PIC discussed with staff. Ensure hand washing is done for at least 20 SECONDS and with a BARRIER. Educated staff immediately. Corrected on site. Ensure that hand washing continues regularly throughout operations and with proper procedure.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Inspector observed wiping cloths which were moist sitting on the countertop in the middle of the room (with the can opener). Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer when not in use. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored appropriately.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
The sugar scoop handle was observed sitting in the sugar itself. Handles must be stored upright. Ensure that the handles of utensils stored in food are not in contact with the food.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

comment:

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

Employee left the area before inspector had a chance to discuss handwashing. PIC was made aware and advised to revisit proper handwashing between tasks with all kitchen staff. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, between handling soiled and clean equipment and utensils, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Employee was observed touching toast with bare hands. Employee noted the plate prepared was for a staff member. Use of a barrier when handling ready to eat food was discussed. Ensure gloves or another proper barrier are used when handling ready to eat foods for residents and staff.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Sliced almonds and sunflower seeds were not properly covered in the dry storage area. Lid was off of the sliced almond container, and the sunflower seed bag was open. PIC provided proper covers for both items during the inspection. Ensure lids are secured on food containers and food bags are properly sealed between uses.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open packages of deli meats were without date marks. PIC noted the deli meats were opened for use over the weekend. Deli meats were dated and kept for use. Ensure proper date marking of foods.
Except as specified in (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

comment:

comment:

Reference 2-501.11.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
The facility has been observed to have three repeat priority/priority foundation violations from the previous inspection. Person-in-charge is a current Certified Food Protection Manager (21556549). Operator was able to answer questions adequately. Although violations were corrected on-site, all three violations are repeat violations from the previous inspection. Per 2017 FDA Food Code, the person-in-charge must be able to prevent the occurrence of priority/priority foundation violations through active managerial control of the facility. The establishment has not been able to adequately prevent such violations from occurring. As such, a follow-up is issued for 30-days to ensure continued compliance with food separation and protection, cleanliness of food contact surfaces and date-marking. Ensure that these items remain corrected throughout all operations. This is a repeat violation from routine inspection dated 10/27/2022. Inspector will follow-up with facility on Wednesday 12/28/2022. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed black, slimy mold growth on the baffle of the ice machine. During the previous routine inspection, the facility was instructed to discard all contaminated ice and clean the ice machine. This was completed satisfactorily by the follow-up on 11/07/2022. During the inspection today, mold growth is observed due to an insufficient cleaning frequency. Water drips from the center of the baffle regularly. This dripping water is observed to be coming from the molded section of the baffle. As such, all ice in the machine must be considered potentially contaminated by the mold on the baffle. The ice was immediately discarded. Corrected on site. Ensure that food (ice) is protected from all sources of contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
The baffle of the ice machine is observed to be soiled with slimy black mold. The baffle of the ice machine is in contact with food and also allows dripping water to land on the ice below. As such, this surface must be cleaned at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of mold and other residue which has the potential to contaminate the ice below. The facility has not maintained a cleaning frequency which is sufficient to ensure compliance with this requirement. Ensure that the baffle and areas behind the baffle of the ice machine are cleaned daily to prevent recurrence of mold growth. This is a repeat violation from previous routine inspection dated 10/27/2022. The baffle has been cleaned with sanitizer; corrected on site. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Inspector observed cut celery in the upright cooler across from the ice machine which did not have date marking. Once foods are prepared (cut) dates must be applied and foods must be discarded within 7-days. Discussed proper date marking procedures with person-in-charge who understands that this is a requirement. Ensure that all items prepared and needing to be refrigerated are date marked with the date opened/prepared and/or the date to be discarded. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection dated 10/27/2022. Dates were applied to the cut celery during the inspection; corrected on-site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Discard forks already available to customers. With clean, gloved hands, arrange single service utensils so that handles are up.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment: Facility is operating outside of their permit by cooling and reheating cheese sauce and two types of soup (actions not allowed under a Class II Medium Risk permit). Cease cooling and reheating or upgrade to a Class I High Risk permit. CORRECTED- Previously cooled foods in the facility may not be served as cooling violations were also observed during this inspection. Foods will be voluntarily discarded.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Container of cheese sauce observed to be 125F (probed) at 4:30. Per PIC, cheese sauce began cooling at 2PM. Cheese sauce did not cool to from 135 to 70 in two hours. CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling time & temperatures as well as cooling methods. Additional education will be provided if facility decides to upgrade permit and continue cooling/reheating.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
An open gallon of milk was observed without date marking indicating the date it was opened. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who labeled milk with the date it was opened. Label foods and use or discard within 7 days of opening.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle of clear liquid observed in a bucket of other chemicals in the kitchen. PIC was unsure what was in the container, opened and smelled it, and determined it to be water. She indicated that the bucket is the janitor’s supplies. CORRECTED- Spray bottle was labeled to indicate contents. Ensure chemicals (or what may be mistaken for chemicals) are labeled to indicate contents and avoid confusion.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
Cheese sauce observed cooling in the kitchen cooler, covered and with no other additional cooling methods used. Cheese sauce had not met the time/temperature benchmarks. Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling methods. Inspector will follow up to verify that cooling has ceased, or to provide additional education if cooling will continue.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [Pf]

comment:

comment:
Two packages of mozzarella observed with manufacturer expiration dates of 10/28/22. One package observed with visible mold. Foods are used or discarded within 7 days of opening, and nothing is kept past its manufacturer expiration date. CORRECTED- Out of date mozzarella was voluntarily discarded.

If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container
comment:
Unlabeled plastic container of white powder observed near the microwave. Food employee indicated the contents to be salt. Label working containers of easily mistakable foods.
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment:
Facility is a medium-risk facility. Inspector observed a clear plastic container properly date marked indicating that the container held “gravy mix” which had been prepared on 11/17/2022 and was to be discarded on 11/20/2022. Using an IR temperature gun, inspector obtained a reading of 97 degrees F indicating that the gravy mix had been cooked and was in the process of cooling. Operator stated that the food was prepared around 8:00 AM today and was intended to be reheated on Saturday, 11/20/2022, for service. Facility was immediately advised that operation under a medium-risk permit is limited to same day service and that cooling and reheating is not allowed within the scope of their current permit. The gravy mix was immediately discarded voluntarily by the facility. Inspector had a long discussion with both operators regarding permit limitations and alternate procedures. Corrected on site. Facility will cook gravy daily as needed for service and will discard upon completion of food service. Establishment will not be upgrading to a high-risk permit. Ensure that food preparation occurs within the scope of the facility’s permit with Sangamon County. No follow-up is required at this time. 

3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled. (E) WHOLE-MUSCLE BEEF shall be from approved source and acceptable from AUTHROITY. Pf (D) FISH must be frozen if consumed undercooked. (F) Meat and Poultry shall be properly labeled. (G) Eggs shall be properly labeled. C

comment: 6-501.111: Observed several fruit flies (20+) by the front counter and prep cooler area in kitchen. Advised PIC to contact Ecolab for assistance with pest control. PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

2) Observed floors under oven and prep table in kitchen to be soiled with food debris.
3) Observed floors under 3 compartment sink to be soiled with food debris.

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
The facility has several priority/priority foundation violations and repeat violations from previous inspections. Person-in-charge has failed to ensure that hand washing sinks remain accessible and are used for no other purposes which inhibits operators from washing hands as frequently as required to provide a safe food operation. Food has not been protected from contamination throughout the course of operations. A follow-up is being issued for 30-days to evaluate the operation and ensure that person-in-charge is properly managing compliance with priority and priority foundation violations. Ensure that all priority/priority foundation violations are corrected and the facility remains in compliance. Inspector will return on 12/15/2022 to check on the status of these corrective actions. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
The hand washing sink to the left of the drive thru does not have a supply of paper towels and/or the dispenser is not working. Each hand washing sink must be supplied with paper towels. Ensure that hand washing sinks are always stocked with paper towels. A follow-up is issued for 11/28/2022 (due to Thanksgiving scheduling) to check for compliance. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
On arrival, hand washing sink was observed to have a spoon and frosting in it. The hand washing sink may not be used for dumping, filling or any other purposes except hand washing. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection on 10/13/2021. A warning letter/notice to comply will be issued. A 10-day follow-up is being issued for 11/28/2022 (due to Thanksgiving scheduling)  to ensure compliance. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed the ice scoop at the front ice bin under the “coffee & espresso” sign to be stored in a visibly soiled plastic blender container. Operator was advised the the container for the ice scoop must be cleaned every four hours or whenever soiled, whichever occurs first. Ice in the bin was observed to have brown food residue assumed to be coffee. Ice scoop was removed from the container and the container was cleaned. Ice was removed from the bin. Bin was cleaned and refilled. Corrected on site. No further follow-up required at this time. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Using a brown paper towel from the nearby hand sink, inspector was able to remove a significantly thick layer of mold from the bottom edge of the baffle in the ice machine. The baffle is a food-contact surface and must be clean to sight and touch at all times. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. A follow-up is being issued for 11/28/2022 (due to Thanksgiving scheduling) to ensure compliance. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed wet wiping cloths sitting on counters throughout the facility including the front register counter, the counter near the dump sink under the “coffee and espresso sign” and the drive thru. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution when not actively being used. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer between uses or paper towels are used and disposed of as needed. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
The handle of the scoop in the powdered sugar tub at the rear of the facility is observed to be stored handle down in the powdered sugar. The handle must be stored out of the food to prevent contamination. Ensure that food handles are not contacting food in containers during storage. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The base of the double upright cooler at the rear of the facility is observed to be soiled with debris. This is a repeat violation from the inspection dated 10/13/2021. A warning letter/notice to comply will be issued. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris on these surfaces. 

The hood above the fryer is observed to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure that this surface is cleaned at a rate sufficient enough to preclude the accumulation of dust and grease. The current cleaning frequency is not sufficient to preclude the accumulation of debris and poses and contamination hazard to the food being processed beneath it. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Inspector observed that the caulking behind the hand sink in the back where the donuts are being prepped is deteriorating and must be re-caulked. The triple sink has caulking which is deteriorating and molding. Ensure that these areas are re-caulked to create a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:

Ensure that these are cleaned prior to the next routine inspection and are added to the establishments cleaning rotation.

comment:

A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

comment:
3-501.14: (A) Observed cooling rice (large bin) at 164F (probed) under shell eggs and stored in the double glass-door cooler. Discussed proper cooling strategies and proper wash, rinse, sanitize using equipment too large for the triple sink. The owner stated that the rice would be used within the dinner service period. Four hours at any temperature below 134F.

(D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Multiple TCS foods observed stored at room temperature - stored beneath the grill top - at ambient temperature. Today the food is observed below 41F as is the ambient temperature. The food is not labeled for four hours and the knowledge of proper cold holding was not demonstrated. It is the behavior of the staff to hold cooked noodles and raw animal proteins under the flat top for convenience of handling, See that staff is educated on proper time-as-control/cold holding before they leave food out of the cooler for ease of handling. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Observed nothing in the coolers to be date marked. There are minimal concerns over the present foods, see that vegetables and opened/frozen items are properly date marked. Properly date mark foods within coolers. 
Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19: (A) Observed no time-as-control strategies in-place for foods stored on-the-counter or foods to be cooled.  The facility needs to implement labeling to control for time allowed for on-counter storage and to monitor cooling. See that the time is indicated on foods left on counters during busy periods for ease of cooking. OR, keep foods in coolers between service. 
Get in-the-habit of indicating the time of foods stored beneath the flat top. 

If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

comment:

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

comment:

comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed a can which was dented sharply along the upper seam in the rolling can storage rack. Inspector discussed the need check cans prior to accepting delivery to prevent costs associated with disposing of cans and ensure consumer safety by preventing the use of compromised cans. Cans dented along the seam where the integrity of the can is in question can be a source of botulism. The dented can observed by the inspector was immediately tossed. During a quick look of the remainder of the cans no dented cans were immediately apparent. Ensure that all cans are checked and that cans dented along any seem are not allowed into the rotation. A follow-up is being issued for 10-days (11/21/2022). Go through all cans in the facility to ensure that none are dented along a seam.

Wet wiping cloths quickly lose sanitizer concentration and may grow bacteria which could contaminate food contact surfaces. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer buckets between uses. This is a repeat violation from inspection dated 7/14/2021.

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed the two creamer boxes in the cold holding creamer unit to have no date marking. Discussed with employee. Utilize a date marking system for the cold holding creamer unit. Inspector will follow-up on 11/14/22.

comment:

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:

Ensure that facility is in compliance with test-strip requirement and ensure that education is occurring internally so that all employees can verify food contact surfaces are being sanitized appropriately. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
Facility uses quaternary ammonia sanitizer. No test strips are available. Test strips are on-order and an invoice is available. Operator has been to GFS and Sam's Club to find test strips. Operator states that none were available at either supplier. Test strips must be available at all times that food is being prepared. A second follow-up is being issues for 10-days to ensure compliance. This is a repeat violation for 10/26/2022 routine inspection performed by inspector AD.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Inspector did not observe any active pests/nest or other indication of cockroaches in the facility. Operator states that he has not seen any cockroaches in the establishment. Although no pests were observed, there were some concerning harborage conditions at each hibachi grill. Each grill, along both sides from the front to back, is heavily soiled in the area underneath the baffling of the grill. These areas have a large amount of food debris and grease which has begun to pile up. This is a harborage condition for pests and must be eliminated immediately. Inspector checked each of these areas and no insects were observed. Underneath the triple sink and dish machine of the facility is a large amount of soil along with underneath the grill and fryer in the kitchen. These are also harborage conditions for pests. Pest prevention is reliant on good cleaning practices. Ensure that moving forward, cleaning of these concerning areas is performed routinely. A follow-up is being issued for 10-days. At that time, these areas must be clean to sight and touch. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

Observed bottom reach-in coolers of prep line to still be dirty - food debris and splash build-up, grates of shelving, ledge inside coolers, base of coolers. PIC, Alex, began to wash, rinse, sanitize on site. Ensure area maintains food contact surfaces clean. COS. 

No further action.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 PIC at time of inspection was chewing gum while working in the kitchen. Gum was discarded at request of inspector. Ensure staff are not eating while working in in the kitchen, including chewing gum and/or eating candy.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee helping with dishes entered the kitchen after exiting the restroom and did not wash hands prior to removing a clean pot from the dish machine. Hands were just washed in the restroom but need to be re-washed upon entering the kitchen prior to handling clean equipment and/or working with food because door knobs were touched to exit the restroom and enter the area leading to the kitchen. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Ensure hands are consistently and properly washed between tasks as needed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the kitchen, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet and handle to paper towel dispenser were both touched between washing hands and getting paper towels to dry hands. Handwashing process also happened relatively quickly and lasted less than a total of 20 seconds. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing

title: Hands clean and properly washed

comment:
Inspector observed several in-use utensils including multiple whisks stored on top of the smoker. The smoker top is not a cleaned and sanitized surface. Operator indicates that space is limited but will find a better location for the utensils. Ensure that utensils are only stored on cleaned/sanitized surfaces or hanging to prevent the cooking surface of the utensil from touching other surfaces.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Food separated and protected

Gloved hands were also wiped with a napkin instead of changing after soup splashed on hands while portioning. Proper glove use was discussed as well as periodic handwashing between glove changes. Employee changed gloves before continuing with next task.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food separated and protected

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:

It would appear the soup and meatballs may have never reached a minimum temperature of 135F and were discarded. 
Ready-to-eat TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

comment:
