title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: The ice scoop holder and the can opener were observed soiled at the start of the inspection. Each items was removed form service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that food contact surfaces remain clean to sight and touch. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11: The baffle of the ice machine is observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residues along the metal fold and the edges of the baffle. Ensure this surface is properly cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111: The fry building is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings along the interior walls of the back room, galley room, and main room. Fidelis is the facility PCO and should be contacted and made aware of the observations and discuss plans for eradication. A follow-up is being issued for Monday, November 7th, 2022 to observe the eradication and prevention process.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
3-304.12: At the start of the inspection, the tongs to utilized to remove fish from the fryers were observed stored with the contact surface in contact with a very soiled metal piece. The tongs were removed from this location and placed properly on the food basins. Ensure utensils intended for food contact are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
comment:
5-403.11: It was confirmed in the fry building that the mop water is dumped outside and not through a proper disposal system. This practice should stop and the mop water should be disposed of utilizing the public sewer. Ensure workers are educated and the effort is established to properly dispose of waste water.
5-403.11: SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: Facility is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings, dead insects, and other various debris/soils in the fry room back room, galley room, and main room. Ensure that equipment is pulled away from walls and that the premise is cleaned with the removal of the droppings, insects, and various debris/soils.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Open can of soda was observed on shelving used for clean dish storage. Employee helping in kitchen noted it was their personal beverage. Soda was relocated to the counter by the service window away from clean dish storage and food prep area. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-202.14 Restrooms in hallway between classrooms and front office were observed with broken self-closers. Owner noted the doors are hollow and require special plates to be installed on the backside of the door that will allow for re-attachment of and proper function of the self-closers. 
A toilet room located on the premises shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight- fitting and self-closing door.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 A certified food manager was not present upon arrival of inspector. The manager on duty with certification was on break, and the employee working did not have certification. CFM came back from break and noted they were the PIC to oversee operations until close of business today. Ensure a CFM is on-site during all hours of food service and operation. **See general comments for additional information)
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between tasks and did not wash hands between operating the cash register at the order window and handling clean dishes at the 3 part sink. While moving the dish rack at the 3 part sink a utensil was loose and handled to be placed back in the rack. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks, especially after working the service window and prior to doing anything with clean dishes, single service articles, or food prep/handling. Employee washed hands prior to continuing with the next task.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Mold was observed on the lower edges of the baffle in the ice machine bin, with some surfaces in direct contact with ice. Ice was removed to allow for cleaning. Sanitizer was used to wipe down surfaces where mold was observed while using a baking pan as a barrier between the baffle and ice below. Additional layer of ice was also removed after cleaning. Cleaning and maintenance were discussed. 
2. Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed around the mixer, with some of them sitting on cutting boards. Manager noted cookies were made earlier in the day, and the area in question probably needs some additional cleaning. Cutting boards were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Portions of chicken salad located in a bag dated 10/27 in the fridge door had surface temperatures above 45F. Internal temperatures were observed at 49F-51F. Portions of chicken salad (4) were discarded during inspection. **See general comments for additional information**
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19 Open containers of half and half and almond milk were observed in the fridge. One container of half and half had a time stamp of 12:15 and was observed with an internal temperature of 43F. The other containers of half and half and almond milk did not have time stamps and dispensed portions had internal temperatures of 52F and 59F respectively. Half and half and almond milk without time stamps that were placed back in the fridge after being held at room temperature were discarded. Portion of half and half with 12:15 time stamp was removed and placed on the prep table for use. Other milks and whipped topping removed from cold holding were observed labeled with the time and left on prep table for use during inspection. Ensure foods are properly labeled and used or discarded within 4hrs. Cease the practice of placing time controlled TCS foods back in the fridge. **See general comments for additional information**
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F/below when removed from cold holding or 135F/above when removed from hot holding; (2) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; (3) the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready-to-eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control; and (4) food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Probe thermometer was used to check chicken salad and was not registering near temperatures observed with inspector’s digital probe thermometers. Ice water solution was used to check accuracy, and facility’s thermometer was observed at 40F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F with pliers used to adjust the needle. Ensure all thermometers are calibrated to verify accuracy.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-404.14 Damp wiping cloths were observed sitting on counters. One wiping cloth was dipped in sanitizer at 3 part sink to wipe tables. Sani-buckets were emptied and fresh solutions not yet provided. Quat solutions at 200ppm were prepared to allow for proper storage of wiping cloths between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 Wall behind washer/dryer and handsink had areas of disrepair and spots where gaps were present along drywall seams. Owner has plans to repair the wall/remodel the facility. **See general comments for additional information**
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.06 Employee working at the time of inspection did not have a food handler certification and confirmed they have not yet completed the course. Employee stated they were new as of July. PIC was advised on the time frame for certification. Ensure all staff that are not CFMs complete food handler certifications within 30 days of hiring. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13: Observed the surfaces of cabinet used to store cooking pans and sheets to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize cabinet surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: 2-201.11: Observed facility to not have signed reporting agreements for all food employees. Provide signed employee reporting agreements for all food employees. (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 4-602.12: Observed the interior of microwave in kitchen to be heavily soiled with food splash and debris. (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: 4-303.11: Observed sanitizer solution available to not be testable using quaternary ammonia or chlorine test strips. New sanitizer bucket was made using chlorine bleach. New solution was tested at 200 ppm Cl-.(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
Two unlabeled spray bottles observed (one in the kitchen, one behind the service counter). CORRECTED- According to PIC, spray bottle in the kitchen contains oven cleaner and was labeled as such. Counter spray bottle contained water and was emptied.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: 2-301.12: (A) Observed an employee put on new gloves without first washing hands. Wash hands before putting on new gloves.  FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: 5-203.11: (A) Observed hand sink located next to fryers to be non-operable. Repair hand sink using licensed plumbing contractor. Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: 6-202.15: (A) Observed a gap between top of back door and wall. Fix door so that no gap exists. Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: 4-202.16: Observed plastic garbage bags used as pull handles on permanent handles of walk in cooler and freezer. Remove plastic trash bags from permanent cooler and freezer handles.  NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13: Observed bottom of cooler and warmer on west wall of facility to be soiled with food splash and debris. Clean and sanitize bottom of cooler and warmer. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-601.11: Observed large Rubbermaid can used to store flour to be soiled with food splash and debris. Clean and sanitize flour container. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-501.12: Observed a significant amount of grease buildup on floor under fryers. Remove grease from floors under fryer (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-101.11: Observed metal shelving located above sink next to ice machine and three compartment sink to be pitted and rusted. Replace shelving above both sinks. (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
The hand washing sink in the all-gender restroom has a paper towel dispenser which was stocked but not functioning correctly resulting in paper-towels not dispensing as required. Paper towels must be available at all times for each hand sink. Operator corrected the dispenser and paper towels were available during the inspection. Ensure that paper towel dispensers are not just stocked but are functioning properly to allow paper towels to be obtained following hand washing. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Soda nozzles were observed to be covered in black mold by checking with a clean paper towel. Soda nozzles are food-contact surfaces. Food-contact surfaces must be cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of residue, debris and mold. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned regularly and thoroughly the prevent buildup from occurring. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
Inspector observed that the meatballs at the front prep area were stored in a steam table at a temperature of 131 degrees F or lower. Facility temperature logs show that meatballs were checked this morning and were 160 degrees immediately after removing from the microwave. Checking the meatballs immediately after cooking is a great practice to ensure that meatballs are reaching the appropriate cooking temperature, however, ensure that temperatures are checked shortly after to ensure that hot-holding temperatures remain at-or-above 135 degrees throughout the course of service. Microwaves do not cook food evenly so time must be given to ensure that temperatures are allowed to stabilize before you take temperatures. Meatballs were immediately brought to 135 degrees by increasing the temperature of the steam table. Corrected on site.  

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Inspector observed a personal mobile phone sitting on a wire shelf directly above food preparation. Operator was removing the bag from a container of spinach immediately underneath the phone. Operator was told to cease food preparation immediately, do not remove the bag and expose the food, and remove the phone from the food preparation area. The phone was removed and hands were washed appropriately immediately after. Ensure that personal phones and other personal items which are sources of contamination are not ever stored above or in contact with food. Corrected on site. 

3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Several tiles throughout the facility are cracked and/or peeling from the wall. These areas include near the mop sink/rear door, near the soda boxes at the rear of the facility, and to the left of the triple sink along the floor/wall junction. Inspector also observed that caulking around the triple sink was missing in several areas and has deteriorated across the entire wall/equipment junction leaving a gap. Surfaces in food preparation areas or areas subject to moisture but be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that tiles in the kitchen are repaired/replaced as needed and that caulking around all sinks remains intact. Correct tile and caulking by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Person-in-charge was personable but lacked understanding of 2017 FDA Food Code requirements including but not limited to paperwork, cleaning procedures, hand washing practices, and date marking. Facility has repeat violations and priority/priority foundation violations. PIC needs to focus on ensuring compliance through active managerial control in the facility and asking questions as appropriate. A 30-day follow-up is being issued to ensure compliance and provide education as necessary to ensure compliance with code moving forward.

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
Inspector discussed with operator the need to have all employees sign employee health reporting agreements. Operator was unaware of this requirement despite being a repeat violation from inspection dated 11/18/2021. Facility was provided with employee health reporting forms during prior inspection which were completed and signed during the inspection. These forms are not available upon request and new forms have not been completed. All employees must have signed employee health reporting agreements with the facility at all times. Ensure that all current and future employees are made aware of this requirement and sign the appropriate acknowledgement. Facility has been provided with another copy of the form and all employees have signed the agreement. Corrected on site. 

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Inspector observed employees washing their hands and turning the faucet off without using a barrier. Discussed this violation with person in charge who has actively corrected the behavior. Corrected on site. This is a repeat violation from 11/18/2021. Ensure that correct hand washing procedure is followed at ALL TIMES. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Inspector observed that ice in the ice machine had water contaminated from molded portions of the ice machine. The area around the outlet for the ice was heavily soiled with thick black mold and residue. In the stored ice, inspector observed small black particles and a relatively large piece of slimy molded material which had fallen from the above areas of the ice machine. Service of ice-based products including soda and other drinks was immediately halted and both the ice machine and soda machine were emptied of ice to facilitate cleaning. 

Upon further inspection of the ice machine, areas of the machine including around the outlet port are heavily molded into areas which are unreachable for cleaning. Molded areas are heavily molded due to the extensive use of abrasive materials to clean the ice machine in the past. These ares of the ice machine are not smooth or easily cleanable. Food contact surfaces must be durable, smooth and easily cleanable. Repair or replace the ice machine to ensure that the interior compartment is smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that cleaning is performed to remove all mold from the machine. If mold cannot be removed, replacement is necessary. Facility is obtaining ice from a gas station which will be stored in the freezer in the meantime. Inspector will follow-up in 10-days to ensure repair/replacement and cleaning have been completed. Ice from this machine may not be served until inspector has verified compliance.  

Ensure that ice is protected from contamination at ALL times through frequent cleaning and monitoring of containers and equipment. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Ice machine equipment was heavily soiled with mold and other residue. The baffle, sides and ice outlet had a significant buildup of residue the presented a contamination hazard for the ice inside the machine. Ice is a food. Any pieces of the equipment which touch ice must be cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of debris and residues. Ice machine was cleaned appropriately during the inspection and no additional mold is observed at this time. Continue ensuring that all food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that effectively precludes buildup from occurring.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
During the prior inspection, inspector had observed a hole in the weather strip at the bottom right of the rear door of the facility. The hole is still present. Inspector discussed this with the person in charge and explained that this is an entry point for pests to infiltrate the facility. Ensure that the external entrances are sealed to prevent pests from entering the facility. Further, an area of rust has developed on the left corner of the door frame which is severe and leaves the potential for pests to create an alternative opening when the hole on the right is sealed. It is recommended that this be repaired to prevent a second hole from developing next to the door. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection on 11/18/2021. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Inspector observed PIC leave a wet wiping cloth on the counter top next to the slicer. Person-in-charge stated that the cloth was used for sanitizing the slicing equipment. Wet wiping cloths, when not directly in use for wiping, must be stored in sanitizer solution to prevent contamination. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer when not in use. PIC tossed the cloth and got a new one during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Inspector observed the ice scoop for the ice machine being stored on top of the ice machine on arrival. The ice scoop may be stored in the ice handle-up or in a clean, sanitized container but my not be stored on top of the ice machine which is not clean and/or sanitized. The ice scoop was removed and cleaned. Corrected on site. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection dated 11/18/2021. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Shelving in the upright coolers at the rear of the facility has paint which has peeled away and begun to rust. These surfaces are not smooth or easily cleanable. These shelves must be repaired or replaced to ensure that they are smooth. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection. 

4-202.11: (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be smooth, free of breaks, cracks, sharp angles, and finished to have SMOOTH welds and joints. Also, it shall be accessible for cleaning and inspection with easy disassembling.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Inspector observed the following areas of the facility are in disrepair:

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Inspector observed three half-gallon containers of 2% milk in the silver uprights in the back storage area. All three containers of milk were open and none bore a date mark. Two of the containers had not reached the manufacturers expiration date but one had expired as of 10/15/2022. All three containers of milk were at 37 degrees F; below the 41 degree F requirement for temperature. The container of milk which had expired was discarded and person-in-charge believes the milk may have been previously frozen but was unsure. Person-in-charge will discuss with cook the need to date mark milk containers and ensure that they are date/time marked appropriately. A follow-up will be issued for 10-days at which time inspector will check for proper date marking throughout the facility. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wiping cloths were observed sitting in a shallow container with a small amount of water at the bottom of it. Inspector checked chlorine concentration of the water with tests strips and there was no chlorine present. The wiping cloths appeared to have been left out over night. The wiping cloths were not submerged in water with most of the cloth exposed to the air. Wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer (bleach water solution) at proper concentrations when not directly in use for wiping surfaces. Wet wiping cloths exposed to the air and stored in water facilitate bacterial growth and pose a contamination hazard. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored submerged in sanitizer solution and are not stored overnight when bleach concentrations of the water cannot be checked as bleach concentrations degrade over time. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Crepes, apples, and hollendaise sauce were all in different stages of the cooling process in the walk-in cooler. Crepes were separated out to allow for quicker chilling on multiple plates after one stack was observed with an internal temperature of 67F and the other an internal temperature of 83F. Crepes were within the last half hour of the 2hr timeframe for cooling. Hollendaise sauce after stirring was observed with internal temperatures of 83F and 87F. Containers were in a tub of water that consisted of a melted ice bath. Owner added more ice to the container, and based on information provided the hollendaise sauce had another hour to reach 70F/below. Apples had an internal temperature of 127F and were placed in the melted ice bath more recently. Best practices were discussed, including but not limited to separating cooling foods into multiple batches in ice baths to quickly chill foods and ensuring foods are stirred and rotated frequently to aid in chilling process. The importance of monitoring time and temperature of cooling foods was also reiterated. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of food.

Mops were observed to be stored directly on the floor.  Mops shall be placed in a position to allow air drying.  Ensure mops are stored in a way to allow air drying to prevent mold and pest accumulation.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-602.11 Mold was observed on the ceiling in the ice bin along the walls behind the baffle. Management noted the ice machine was new to the facility and leased by the owners within the last two weeks. Cleaning was discussed. Ensure surfaces that can be reached are cleaned and sanitized between full services. Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Lettuce in the top right holding compartment of the sandwich prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 50F. Manager confirmed temperature with the facility’s calibrated stem thermometer. Lettuce was washed and cut around 10am and stacked with other containers in the 2 door cooler prior to storage in the prep cooler for service within the hour prior to inspector’s arrival. All coolers were observed holding below 40F, and other foods in coolers were at proper temperature. Lettuce was in a plastic container and wrapped tightly, so that storage in combination with being stacked may not have allowed for chilling after prep. Lettuce will be served or discarded by 7:30pm.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents provided during pre-opening could not be located, and signed reporting agreements were not available for the owner and food service manager. Documents were provided, and employee health policy was discussed. Owner and food service manager signed reporting agreements during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 Norovirus disinfection policy provided during pre-opening could not be located. A new copy of disinfection policy was provided. Maintain a copy of the disinfection policy on-site.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign is not posted at the handwashing sink in the food service area. Handwashing signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw shell eggs (personal use) were stored above onions, jar of banana peppers, and cans of olives and mushrooms in the bottom of the pizza prep cooler. Carton was moved to the bottom of the cooler. Ensure proper storage of raw animal products below and separate from ready to eat foods.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Chemical spray bottle in the restroom was not labeled. Owner verified it contained Awesome cleaner, and the bottle was labeled as to the contents.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food thermometer was not available for use. Provide a food thermometer. Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-501.18 1. Handwashing sink and toilet were soiled with general buildup in the restroom.
2. Handwashing sink in the food service area was soiled with general buildup. 
Clean plumbing fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean.
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
citation_text:
5-501.16 Garbage can was not present within the vicinity of the food service area handwashing sink. Provide a small waste receptacle for disposal of paper towels at the handwashing sink.
If disposable towels are used at handwashing lavatories, a waste receptacle shall be located at each lavatory or group of adjacent lavatories.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

There are numerous flies observed in the facility. Approximately a dozen house flies are in the areas around the fryers, the manager’s desk and 1-2 in the dry storage area. Approximately 5-7 drain/fruit flies were observed in the dry storage area. PIC stated that he sprayed and killed numerous flies the previous night. He also discussed possibly using bug bombs in the facility to facilitate pest removal. Inspector cautioned him against this unless he could find ones intended for food contact areas. It was suggested to consult pest control on this matter. Orkin is the current pest control company and is conducting monthly maintenance. The most recent visit was last Friday per the PIC. Follow up will be conducted in 2 weeks.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
4-204.12: (A) cover or lid for EQUIPMENT shall overlap opening and slope to drain. (B) Opening at top of unit with cover shall be flanged upward at least two-tenths of an inch. (C) All parts extending into EQUIPMENT shall be provided with watertight join. (D) If watertight join not provided, parts shall be equipped with apron designed to deflect condensation, dust, and drips into FOOD. Openings shall be flanged. 

The equipment used for ice baths is observed with consistent drips coming from the front left corner again. This was an issue that appeared to be resolved at the previous follow up (9/27/22). At this time it has begun to leak and will need to be repaired again.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas. 

Observed four of the six light fixtures in the kitchen area to still not have adequate shielding. PIC indicated that the shielding has been acquired and that it will be put up this evening. Will follow up at the same time as the pests noted on line item #38.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: 3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) Observed Water actively dripping from ceiling tiles into plastic containers on floor. Fix roof and replace damaged ceiling tiles. Remove all food items from any areas with active leaks where contamination may occur. Discard any food products with visible water damage. FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Physical facilities are in need of ongoing cleaning throughout the establishment. Operator is aware of the need to continue cleaning efforts on an ongoing basis to prevent accumulation of residue and debris. Inspector observed a broom and dust pan being actively used to clean fresh food debris. Floors appear mopped. Hood is clear of debris. Observed female operator cleaning countertops and preparing sanitizer for cleaning activities. Inspector observed some debris still around floor/wall junctions and some accumulation of sauce on the smoker. There is some accumulation of residue and debris observed on the grill tops, scrape these as soon as debris begins to accumulate. The floor underneath grill is clean to sight and touch. Overall, continue to work on daily cleaning activities.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 
Observed the time tags on the salad bar read 2pm upon arrival. Inspector arrived at the facility at 2:40pm. Salad bar was the first area inspected. Food that did not look new was rotated out.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 
Observed several wet wiping cloth buckets to have wiping cloths hanging over the edges. Train employees to keep wiping cloths inside of the buckets when not in use.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 
Observed the caulk line at the bakery sink to be soiled. Remove caulk, clean area and seal sink to wall. The corner round at the bakery walk in cooler is pulling away from the wall and is held on by tape. Repair the corner round/wall area.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 
Observed open red bull at the area for cutting vegetables, a closed red bull at the prep cooler with noodles, and two personal drinks at the smoothie counter at the tea area. The items were removed to an area for employee belongings. Develop good habits for personal drink storage. Do not eat or drink in food preparation areas.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 
Observed an employee place carrot shreds and raw side items on appetizer plates with bare hands. The raw veggies were discarded in the garbage and plates taken to the dish area. Employee was coached on hand washing and glove use. Employee washed hands and put on gloves.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  
Observed walk in cooler to have chicken wings stored over beef on the shelves. The shelves were arranged so that the foods were in proper cooking order and protected from each other. Practice food protection by proper storage practices.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 
Five packages of ham were observed to have holes in them when removed from freezer and thawing method. The manager noticed holes in ham packages this morning, when the sheet pan used during thawing, had ham juice on it. Mor holes were observed after ham was removed from thawing in water and water was running out of the ham packages. All together 25 pounds of ham were discarded due to packaging that was not intact. Some holes were as large as a pencil eraser while others were smaller but still exposed the food inside to potential contamination. This is the first time that this kitchen has used this ham product. Normally they use turkey ham and have not had any previous issue with packaging that is not intact.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Walk-in freezer was observed to have a large build-up of ice around and outside of the door.  Discussion with PIC revealed building maintenance is aware and together have been periodically removing the ice.  The ice build up is preventing the freezer door from completely closing, but the freezer is maintaining an acceptable temperature.  Ensure freezer is fixed and in correct working order.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Juice dispenser tubes were observed to have a small amount of build-up.  Delivery tube shall be protected from contamination.  Ensure tubes are regularly cleaned and sanitized to prevent contamination.

4-204.13: EQUIPMENT dispensing liquid FOOD or ice: (A) Splash surfaces above container receiving FOOD shall be designed to divert splash and condensation from container receiving FOOD. (B) Delivery tube shall be protected from manual contact. (C) Delivery tube shall be protected from contamination through preventative measures.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Caulking of 3 part sink was observed to be detached and missing in some areas.  Exposed crevices are subject to water and moisture accumulation, allowing for mold and debris build-up.  Ensure sink is caulked to avoid mold and debris accumulation.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

comment:
Sauce observed dated 9/16. Other items in prep cooler observed without dates or more than 7 days past their date-markings. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and provided education. Staff voluntarily discarded foods 7 days or more past their date markings. See General Comments for additional information.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

3-501.13: (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

Food debris and spills observed on the floor in the dry storage area (under shelving and in the corner between freezers). Clean as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed no hand soap at the bar hand sink. Soap must be provided at all hand sinks. Soap was placed at the bar hand sink during the inspection. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
The ice machine was observed with mold and mildew build-up inside the ice machine. Water drips from this could contaminate ice. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned to prevent ice contamination from mold and mildew. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

comment:
Observed the dish machine to have a chlorine concentration of approximately 10ppm-20ppm. The dish machine must have a concentration of 50ppm and no more than 200ppm. The manager stated GFS would be called to service the dish machine. Dishes must be sanitized in the 3 part sink until the dish machine can maintain a concentration of 50ppm.

(B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

comment:
Observed no time marking on sushi rice at the sushi prep station. This does not comply with the Time as a Public Health control policy that is in place. Sushi rice must be marked with the time it was prepared. Discussed the requirements of the policy with the owner. The sushi had been changed within the last 30-60 minutes and a time marking was placed on it. 
 
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. comment:

(C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The walk in cooler fan was soiled with dust and dirt. Ensure the walk in cooler fan is cleaned frequently to prevent the accumulation of dirt and dust.  

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

comment:

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

comment:

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

Ensure sanitizer dispenser is producing the necessary concentration level of 150-400ppm as according to label recommendation.

comment:

Digital display on outside of the dish machine is not the temperature of the water as it sanitizes dishes.  Ensure a temperature measuring device is on-site and dish machine temperature is routinely checked for proper sanitation.

(B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
Ceiling tiles and vents on kitchen ceiling were observed to contain dust and mold accumulation.  Discussed with employee and PIC, non-food contact surfaces shall be routinely cleaned to prevent contamination of food and equipment.  Ensure tiles and vents are regularly cleaned to prevent accumulation of dust and mold.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

-2 and 3 part sinks.

comment:

One of the ceiling tiles over the three part sink in the prep area is missing a tile. PIC instructed to ensure that the tile is replaced prior to the next routine inspection.

comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. comment:

comment:

comment:

comment:

6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 
Observed containers of seasoning to be stored on bread crates that are not at least six inches above the floor. Crates are also difficult to clean around and often lead to other issues. Discontinue this practice and provide proper storage for these items.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 
Upon arrival the facility was beginning to deal with a hot holding table that had run out of water. They said that they could smell it burning and I observed an employee adding water to the unit. Chicken, white rice, pinto beans, fajita veggies, ground beef, steak, and adobo chicken are observed to be on the hot holding table at temperatures between 112 &142. Ground beef, brown rice, adobo chicken, and  fajita veggies were all discarded. There were small amounts of each one. Steak at 120, chicken at 117, were placed into the steam ovens for reheating. Black beans were placed in a pot on the stove top and reheated. The foods had been on the hot holding table for less than 2 hours according to management. Foods that were not discarded were reheated to 165.

title: Personal cleanliness
comment:
2-303.11: Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing FOOD, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.
Observed employees with bracelets and rings on their hands and wrists. Remove bracelets and extra (non wedding) jewelry so that hand washing can be effective and so that bracelets do not come into contact with food. Maintain violation corrected.

comment:

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. 
All employees not manager certified shall be handler certified within 30 days of hire. Facility states that they use ServSafe to certify employees. Keep certifications in a file available for inspector. Suggest doing this as a part of onboarding new employees.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Every certified food protection manager shall have allergen awareness training as well. Keep these certificates available and provide to inspector upon request.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Cheese sauce in the walk-in cooler leftover from the previous operating day was observed with an internal temperature of 54F. Cheese sauce was discarded. Owner was advised to speak with staff regarding best practices for proper cooling.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:

Diced tomatoes prepared on 9/28/22 had an internal temperature of 46F-48F and will be used or discarded by the end of lunch service today.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Dish washer was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Management was advised to speak with staff about proper technique and ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

Employee was advised on hand washing between tasks, prior putting on gloves, and upon entering the kitchen regardless of handwashing after using the restroom. Employee washed hands prior to continuing with food handling.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Ensure hands are properly washed between tasks, prior to entering the kitchen, and before donning gloves to handle food.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Inspector observed ants and flies throughout the facility. Flies appeared to congregate at the front of the store and ants appeared to be more present at the back of the store. There was no obvious nesting area for either pest. Inspector observed all corners and underneath equipment throughout the facility. Ants were present diffusely throughout the facility although not in great numbers at this time. Flies were also present diffusely but again, not in great numbers. Call Pesto-X and have them visit the facility to eliminate ants and flies. 

Several areas throughout the facility are harborage areas for pests. Underneath equipment, there is refuse that has been dropped and not cleaned up including single use items like cups and lids and other food debris. The drive thru in particular had a significant amount of residue under the soda machine. Behind the soup hot holding at the drive thru, inspector observed soup which had been allowed to drip down the wall, puddle on the floor and dry. title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Person in charge is not a certified food manager and does not appear to have managerial control of the facility. Facility is not in compliance with several priority and priority foundation items. Facility is in repeat violation of several items. Person in charge must be responsible for ensuring compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code requirements and be understanding of those requirements. Person in charge was unable to verbally explain proper cooling temperatures when asked during inspection. Person in charge must have an understanding of food handling practices, policies and procedures and be able to apply these procedures. title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Facility has cooler procedures in place which are not being followed at this time. A blue binder is kept in the premise which includes all temperature logs used throughout the day. Hot holding temperatures for chicken and other items appear to be up to date. However, temperatures for cooling are not being recorded. Discussed this with PIC who stated that employees are required to complete logs every time they begin cooling but they have not been doing it. Inspector educated on the benefits of keeping logs to allow employees, managers and inspectors to see when items began cooling to ensure compliance with the two-hour to 70 degree and 6 hour to 41 degree requirements. Because logs were not kept and no temperatures were recorded on labels or other locations, PIC and inspector had no way of determining how long items had been cooling for. A tray of meatloaf and a tray of broccoli casserole were discarded voluntarily by person in charge due to being out of temperature. The meatloaf was 100 degrees F and the broccoli casserole was 48 degrees F. Cooling must occur within proper time frames and to proper temperatures. A procedure must be in place and followed to allow for cooling within these parameters. 

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

4-703.11 (B) Upon start of inspection dishes were not getting properly heat sanitized based on initial observation of dish machine rinse gauge, final rinse surface temperature, and the manner in which the cycles were ran. Door to dish machine was opened prior to conclusion of rinse cycle with the gauge reading below 180F, and inspector’s dish temp tester showed a final rinse surface temperature of 144F. title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of deli meats were stacked above the fill line of containers in the top of a prep cooler, with some portions spilling out of the containers. Surface temperatures were observed between 58F-60F, and one portion of turkey was observed with internal temperature of 55F. Portions down in the containers were observed with surface temperatures of 37F-42F. Portions were said to be recently stocked. Cook  was advised on stocking pans in the top holding area of prep coolers and to avoid over-filling. Items above the fill line will not be maintained at 41F/below as demonstrated with products today. Portions above the fill line were moved inside the cooler to cold hold until needed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Gravy was in the process of cooling in the walk-in cooler. Gravy was observed in four plastic 6qt containers full to the top, covered, and stacked together. Surface temperatures were observed at 93F-104F, while internal temperatures in the middle were at 134F-139F. Cook noted the gravy was made around 6:30am, set on the back prep table and held at room temperature briefly prior to placing in a ice bath for ~30 minutes, and placed in the walk-in cooler around 7:00am. Temperatures were not checked during cooling process or prior to placing product in the cooler. Best practices for cooling were discussed. Gravy was removed from walk-in to further portion in multiple containers and place back in ice baths. Multiple portions were observed on the back prep table sitting at room temperature ~20 minutes later. Owner and cook were advised to place cooling portions of gravy on ice baths as soon as possible to allow for rapid chilling. **See general comments for additional information.**
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: There are no dates on foods. Prepared foods in the walk-in cooler and preparation cooler are not date marked. 
(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19:  Facility has had previous knowledge of the four hour rule and the need to label in-use foods held on the counter. There was observed foods throughout the facility and no time as control available. Chopped cabbage is observed in a tub by the preparation cooler without a time indicated. Discussed using a dry erase board, Post-It, of other method for controlling the time foods are pulled from cold holding and placed without temperature control. 
(A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 The following improperly cooled foods were observed in the walk-in cooler. 
1. Pan of Spanish rice was observed with internal temperature of 57F. Rice was made the evening prior. Rice was discarded during inspection.
2. Cooked tomatoes in a large stock pot of liquid had an internal temperature of 46.5F-47F. Tomatoes were cooked the day prior to make salsa. Tomatoes were discarded during inspection.
3. Cooked peppers and onion in a large stock pot of liquid had an internal temperature of 44F-48F. Peppers and onion were cooked the day prior to make salsa. Peppers and onion were discarded during inspection.

Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below.

2-301.12 A cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure staff are was using proper technique when washing their hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.
