title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 The following were all observed in the walk-in cooler.
1. Three containers of chicken and wild rice soup (~2.5gal each) made today were observed with internal temperatures of 49F, 45F, and 43F within the liquid portion of the soup (meat, vegetables, and rice settled to bottom). Based on cooling log, soup was prepared in the morning, had an internal temperature of 132F at 8am, and reached 51F after 2hrs. Based on the time frame of initial prep, the soup was past the 6hr time frame for proper cooling. Soup at 49F was discarded. 
2. Baking sheet with cooked rice had surface and internal temperature of 53F-62F and 61F-75F respectively. Cook stated rice was prepared around 11:30am-12pm. The first two hours of the cooling time frame was past based on information provided. Rice was discarded.
3. Cooked, shredded chicken in a covered container was observed with an internal temperature of 66F-67F. Cook noted it was cool to the touch when shredded and made around the same time as rice. Temperature was not monitored during the process. Chicken was discarded at the discretion of PIC.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Colander of thawing shrimp was observed in the back prep sink under cold running water. Water was in direct contact with only a small portion of the product and did not allow for complete submersion in water. If time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food is thawed under cold running water it must meet the requirements of FDA Food Code Section 3-501.13(B), and product needs to be completely submerged during the thawing process. PIC was advised to provide a storage container within the sink or another means to allow for thawing foods to be submerged in cold water as it is running over the product.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:

Correct concentration range for lactic acid products should be 704-1875 ppm. Inspector demonstrated test strips use with spray bottle in front of CFPM. Facility did not have test strips for the lactic acid product and was not aware. The concentration in the bottles should be lower. Front house (bar and breakfast areas) are utilizing the lactic acid spray bottles. Back house (kitchen) is utilizing quaternary ammonium from the dispensers (test strips available). After discussion with PIC/CFPM/head chef, the facility will switch back over to quaternary ammonium buckets with rags for the front house. Facility was utilizing rags with the spray bottles from what it appeared. Spray bottles should have paper towel use as the rags cannot be immersed in sanitizer. PIC indicated this practice will cease. COS.

comment:

comment:

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

citation_text:

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Manager was observed banging bagged ice on the floor to break apart frozen chunks of ice prior to placing ice on the cold line. Bag was visibly soiled and had a tear in one side. Manager noted the taco rack in question is rarely used and was advised on the concerns for cross contamination. Taco rack was removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Grease buildup was observed on the underneath surface of the table directly above the uncovered container. Covering product to avoid potential dripping of grease from soiled surface was discussed, and a lid was provided. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 (C) & (D) Two tamales were observed in the steamer on the make line. Surface and internal temperatures were at 120F-123F. Employee working on the make line confirmed the tamales were in the steamer since this morning. Tamales were discarded in the trash during inspection. Proper reheating of commercially processed, ready to eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods was discussed. Ensure proper heating of all foods. **See general comments for additional information**
RTE TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding. 
Reheating for hot holding as specified under  (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 41F and the temperatures specified under  (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Pouch of sour cream was observed out on the make line. Dispensed portion of sour cream was observed at 59F. Otherwise, management needs to establish and adhere to a time control policy. Employee on make line noted the product was in use for ~1hr. title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

comment:

comment:

comment:

comment:
Personal drinks including a Dr. Pepper and a bottled iced coffee were in the walk in cooler above food. Operator moved these drinks to an appropriate location. Personal drinks must be stored in a location away from food and food preparation areas to prevent contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

EcoLab suggested a more expensive part be ordered to fix the issue long term. The part that needed repaired today was different than the last part that was needed (see last inspection report, heat was low and EcoLab came during that inspection). COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/23/22.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: There is an opened package of hot dogs in the walk-in cooler observed with a date well past the 7 day rule. These hot dogs are removed from service and will be replaced with a fresh pack with correct date marking.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. 

On arrival, five containers of gravy are observed in individual containers on the counter. PIC indicated that they were cooling from breakfast. The procedure at the time is to wait for the pans to cool until they can be removed from the steam tables, portion into individual containers (or gallon bags), cooler to rom temperature and then be placed in the walk-in cooler. A conversation took place with the PIC that emphasized the importance of active cooling once foods reach 135F. Foods should cool from 135F to 70F in two hours and from 70F to 41F in four hours. These time/temperature benchmarks must be met and a time marking system should be in place to verify that cooling is being managed effectively. The items were believed to be approximately 45 minutes into the 135F to 70F point, so no violation is being noted for cooling today. Items were moved into the walk in cooler during the inspection to correct and time marks will be added to the same tags as the date marks moving foreword. Multiple hand outs given during the inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handle of paper towel dispenser was touched to dispense paper towels after hand washing occurred. Proper technique was discussed with staff. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 

1) Raw chicken is in the process of being prepared for the par cooking procedure used at the facility. Because of the lunch rush the chicken was left in a large wok style bowl and worked on as time permitted. Probing the chicken at different locations showed internal temperatures between 65F and 68F. PIC indicated that the chicken was only out of the cooler approximately 30 minutes to an hour. The back door is open (screen door closed) and the average temperature is in the mid 70s in the kitchen. Education took place and the chicken finished its prep process and was par cooked promptly. 

2) Par cooked chicken (after frying) is observed in several boxes (on a table) next to the back door of the facility. PIC stated that the chicken was cooling prior to placement in the walk-in. Internal temperatures are observed at 75F-77F. PIC indicated that the chicken was only out of the fryer around an hour. Education took place. Once the chicken reaches 135F in the cooling process it should be moved to the walk in cooler for rapid cooling so that it can meat the time/ temperature requirements required by the code. The chicken was moved into the walk in cooler during the inspection to correct the violation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:

title: Food separated and protected
comment:

comment:

Ensure that in use utensils are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of the food contact surface. 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, food service based on risk classification, and lack of adherence to the established time control policy. Evidence of rodent activity was also observed in the dry storage room. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection at the end of the month.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 Signed reporting agreements were not available for employees that work lunch service. Employee health policy was discussed, and reporting agreements were signed by staff. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff that work in the kitchen.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to handle portioned foods for lunches. Just prior to putting on gloves a bleach solution was prepared. Handwashing was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands and prior to putting on gloves to handle food.

title: Food obtained from approved source

Foods observed in the cooler today included portions of chicken and rice and steamed broccoli. All foods were discarded during inspection. title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19 PIC has been keeping leftover cold and hot TCS foods at the conclusion of lunch service. The school has a posted time control policy stating foods are picked up for service at 10:30am and are to be discarded by no later than 2:30pm. Lunch service is done daily by 12:30pm. All hot and cold TCS foods must be served or discarded by the end of lunch service based on this policy and lack of temperature control for foods during lunch service. Leftover TCS foods observed in the cooler included a deli meat and cheese sandwich, meatless chili portions, steamed broccoli portion, and chicken and rice portions. All foods were discarded during inspection. **See HACCP section for additional information** 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready-to-eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Evidence of rodent activity was observed in the dry storage room. Droppings were observed on the floor along walls and in corners. Droppings were also observed on a tray and in a bus tub on a cart. What appeared to possibly be urine was also observed along one of the walls. Maintenance was made aware of the issue. Pest control operator will be contacted for service.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

Ensure wiping cloths are left in bleach solution until just prior to when children will need them to wipe down tables. Provide wet wiping cloths as needed, and store in bleach solution between uses.

Handwashing was discussed with staff during inspection, and proper handwashing between tasks was observed for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Kitchen handwashing sink was used as a dump sink to discard old sanitizer solution. Proper use of the handwashing sink was discussed with the cook. Ensure handwashing sinks are not used as dump sinks.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Slices of quiche removed from the original packaging were observed sitting in direct contact with the lids of packaging. Cook was advised on storage in the original packaging or with a proper barrier between unpackaged food and the general/outer surfaces of packaging. Outer packaging is not considered a clean surface and should never be in direct contact with unwrapped foods. 
2. Pans of diced tomatoes were stacked in the top of the prep cooler so the bottom of one container was in direct contact with tomato in the pan below. Also, a pan of olives was sitting in direct contact with cheese shreds in another container in the bottom of the prep cooler. Portions of diced tomatoes and cheese shreds were discarded prior to proper storage. The bottom surfaces of containers are not considered clean and should not be stacked in direct contact with unwrapped foods. Provide lids or plastic wrap to allow for separation between the bottoms of containers and the food in other containers when products are stacked. 
3. Pan of cheese shreds from the bottom of the prep cooler was briefly set on the floor while another food item was removed from the cooler to prepare an order. Cheese shreds were placed in a new container, and the pan that touched the floor was taken to the dish area for ware washing. Cease the practice of placing pans of food on the floor when obtaining products from coolers.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in kitchen sani-bucket was at 100ppm. Cook just started their shift at 2pm and noted it was probably from use earlier in the day prior to their arrival. Fresh solution was provided at 200ppm. Ensure sani-buckets are changed as needed throughout daily operations, including at shift changes.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Cut cantaloupe in the top of the prep cooler had surface temperatures of 52F-53F. Pieces of cantaloupe in the container had internal temperatures ranging from 49F-53F. Container holding cantaloupe was stored at an angle and positioned within a smaller container in the top of the cooler, so the cantaloupe was not in direct contact with cold air. Cantaloupe was placed in the freezer to quickly chill prior to storage in the bottom of the prep cooler.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Open bags of arugula and spinach in the 2 door cooler were without date marks. Date marks were provided. Ensure proper date marking of leafy greens once packages are opened.
2. Open carton of heavy whipping cream was without a date mark in the reach-in cooler under the grill. Carton was almost empty and was discarded. 
3. Pans with portions of rice and other prepared foods were observed with date marks of 5/11. Portions of products were frozen and just pulled for thawing as of today. Label was changed to reflect proper date when products were pulled from the freezer. 
4. Chicken salad dressing prepared the day prior was without a date mark in the glass front reach-in cooler. Container had a piece of tape on it, but the date was never written down. Date mark was provided during inspection.
5. Portion of cooked, chopped chicken was observed with a date mark of 5/10 in the bottom of the glass front reach-in cooler. Cook noted the product was frozen on 5/10 and pulled from the freezer the day prior to thaw for use. Proper date mark was provided. 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

Both products were said to be received in a delivery earlier that day. Boxes of chicken breasts were moved to allow for proper storage on a racks in the freezer. Ensure box of tortilla shells gets moved to allow for proper storage up off the floor.

comment:

Two trays of bacon are observed on a shelf at room temperature. The trays have date stamps indicating they were prepared yesterday at 9:10 am and that the items are par cooked. A discussion took place with the PIC to understand the procedure in place for these items. The bacon is par cooked from raw, cooled in the walk in to 40 degrees and then allowed to be out at room temperature. This is a poor practice. Bacon is considered a TCS food until it is thoroughly cooked (which reduces the water activity to safe levels). The trays were discarded during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC is now aware that until bacon is fully cooked it must remain in temperature control, or have a time control policy in place and followed.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Bag of beef tongue in the grill cooler was observed without a date mark. PIC noted it was pulled from the freezer about 4 days prior and a date mark was provided. Ensure proper date marking of prepared foods. Properly document the original prep date when cooked, ready to eat foods are frozen and the date when cooked, ready to eat foods are pulled from the freezer to thaw for use. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Personal cleanliness
comment:

2-402.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT; UTENSILS; and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. (B) Section is not applicable to FOOD EMPLOYEES who only serve BEVERAGES and wrapped or PACKAGED FOODS, hostesses, and wait staff if they present minimal RISK.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

Develop accurate sanitizer making routine.  3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Cheese sauce made during morning prep was in the walk-in cooler in eight containers (~1gal each) in the process of cooling. Four containers with a time stamp or 10:30am had internal temperatures at 36F, 47F, 48F, and 49.5F. Four other containers that were warm to the touch and without time stamps had internal temperatures at 122F, 125F, 126F, and 130F. Based on information provided to the GM by the cook the warmer portions were prepared around 11:30-11:45am. Time and temperature were not being monitored to verify product was reaching benchmark temperature of 70F within the first 2hrs, and product was in the cooler for over 3hrs at the time of inspection based on information provided. Cheese sauce at 122F-130F was reheated to begin cooling process again. Cooling was discussed at length with GM. Ensure foods are cooling quickly and properly.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19 Pan of leaf lettuce was observed on top of the reach-in cooler. Lettuce was at 72F, and container did not have a time stamp as required by the time control policy established during the previous routine inspection. Lettuce was discarded. Ensure working supplies of lettuce held at room temperature during lunch service are labeled with a time stamp and used or discarded within 4hrs.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. The food must be served or discarded within 4 hours. The food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the walk-in cooler with packaging intact. Fish in question is only available during Lent season. Ensure vacuum packaged portions of fish are properly thawed when product is available for sale at the facility. Labeling indicates the product should stay frozen until use and be removed from packaging to thaw under refrigeration. At minimum the packaging needs to be cut to eliminate reduced oxygen environment. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

citation_text:

[C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

Manager stated that more traps and bait stations have been placed under the area and she is seeing fewer rodents. She also states that PCO has not returned. 
6-501.115: (A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Staff were observed using the kitchen handwashing sink adjacent to the dish area as a dump sink and a location for rinsing a wiping cloth. Proper use of handwashing sinks was discussed with all staff at the time of inspection. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks for other purposes.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris and was not used to open anything during prep for the current operating day. Kitchen manager took the can opener to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Some foods in the steam table were observed with internal temperatures below 135F and included mashed potatoes (117F), a portion of lasagna (97F-119F), and red sauce (124F). Other foods were observed with internal temperatures at 140F/above depending on when product was prepared and placed in the holding wells. Mashed potatoes were replaced with fresh product, which was observed with an internal temperature of 164F in the warmer. Lasagna was discarded as another portion of lasagna with an internal temperature of 143F was available for service. Red sauces were reheated to 165F prior to placing back in the steam table for service.
Water in the main holding well was observed at 170F, but products in the steam table were double panned. Double panning is not best practice if hot water is not adequate in the second pan to help maintain foods at 135F/above during hot holding. Kitchen manager stated he would change his process for hot holding at the steam table and monitor temperatures to verify best practice for hot holding.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open carton of whipping cream in the bar cooler was not date marked. Product was opened over the weekend on Saturday. Whipping cream was dated and kept for use. Whipping cream was also observed without a proper date mark at the bar during the previous routine inspection. Ensure proper date marks for all prepared TCS foods.
Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for a server and front of house manager. Course was completed awhile ago and certificates need to be printed. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Kitchen manager is currently the only person with a food manager certification and has not completed the food allergen awareness certification. Other members of the staff have the allergen certification but are not currently certified food managers. Management was advised as to the need for the certified food manager to complete the allergen course. Ensure the kitchen manager completes the food allergen certification by the next routine inspection.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, reheating, date marking, and protection of food from potential sources of cross contamination. The walk-in cooler was holding steady at 43F-45F, and the prep cooler was holding colder on the left side as compared to the right side in the bottom of the cooler. The handwashing sink by the back door was blocked upon arrival of inspector, and the facility’s hot water generation is not sufficient to keep up with demands. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the followup inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager was preparing bleach solutions upon arrival of inspector and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to work with food. Proper hand washing between tasks was discussed. Manager was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for remainder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Back handwashing sink was blocked by containers upon arrival of inspector. Accessibility was discussed, and containers were moved to allow for access. Ensure both handwashing sinks are always accessible.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing containers and/or other equipment in front of the handwashing sinks.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Plastic grocery bags were being used for storage of bread in the bottom of the prep cooler and in the walk-in cooler. Use of proper food grade bags for food storage was discussed. Bread was moved to plastic food bags for storage.
2. A churro in the reach-in freezer and tamale in the drawer of the grill cooler were observed sitting on outer surfaces of food packages. Proper storage of foods in containers and food grade bags were discussed. Churros and tamale were discarded.
3. Small portion cup of salsa and avocado skin were in direct contact with cut onions and peppers in the top of the prep cooler. Barriers during storage were discussed. Avocado and  portion cup were removed from the pan.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 A soiled butcher knife was observed in the top of the prep cooler. The knife was left from the previous operating day. Knife was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soiled utensils are properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses and at the end of operations daily. Clean and sanitize knives up to every 4hrs after continuous use.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Containers with cooked meats were uncovered in the walk-in cooler, and containers of various prepared foods were uncovered in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler. Proper storage of foods covered between uses and after cooling were discussed. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Fajita steak and meat sauce were observed with internal temperatures at 127F and 80F in the middle section of the steam table. These two food items were being reheated on the steam table. Proper use of the steam table for hot holding after reheating foods on the grill or stove was discussed. Steak and meat sauce were reheated on the stove and grill prior to placing back in the steam table for hot holding. Ground beef, shredded chicken, rice, and beans were all at 152F/above in the steam table and were properly reheated prior to being placed in the steam table for hot holding.
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods in the prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures at 44F to 54F. Pans of lettuce, pico, and shredded cheese in the bottom right side of the cooler had internal temperatures at 50F-54F. These items were stored in the cooler overnight and were discarded. Shell eggs in the top of the prep cooler were cracked to check internal temperatures, and the top layer of eggs were at 50F while the bottom eggs were at 45F. Top layer of eggs were discarded. All other foods were at 44F-46F and were kept for use, including portions of cheese sauce, salsa, pork, and cheesecake in the bottom of the cooler and guacamole, pico, lettuce, and cheese shreds in the top. Manager was advised on time control for working supplies of food in the prep cooler. All foods will be used or discarded within 4hrs.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Prepared foods were without date marks in the bottom of the prep cooler, and a bag of cooked beef in the grill cooler was without a date mark. Several foods were said to have been prepared within the last day or two. Bag of cooked beef was discarded.
A bag of beef tongue in the grill cooler had a date mark of 3/12, which was the date of prep when product was frozen. Product was pulled from the freezer on 4/9 to thaw for use. Proper date marking was discussed. An educational handout in Spanish was provided, and date marking will be revisited at the follow-up inspection on 4/25. 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 1. Prep cooler was holding foods at temperatures of 44F-54F (see #22 for details). A thermometer was not present. Inspector placed bi-metallic stem thermometers in the bottom of the cooler and observed the left side holding closer to 40F and the right side holding closer to 50F. Time control will be used for working supplies of food in the prep cooler until it is serviced and able to maintain TCS foods consistently at 41F/below. 
2. Walk-in cooler was observed holding consistently at 43F-45F. The condensing unit went down to 39F-40F briefly and then went back up to 43F-45F. Foods had internal temperatures at 44F-45F, and shell eggs had a surface temperature of 43F. 
Call for service was made for both coolers. See general comments for additional information.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer was not present in the prep cooler. Provide a hanging thermometer for the cooler and ensure all coolers and freezers have functioning thermometers for monitoring cold holding temperatures. 
Cold  holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
1. Grill cooler - drawers and gaskets (buildup of food debris);
2. Bottom inside the prep cooler (food splash); and
3. Walk-in cooler shelves (mold/general buildup).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
citation_text:
5-103.11 (B) Hot water was not available at the start of inspection. Manager noted a significant amount of hot water was just used, and in about 5 minutes hot water should be available again. Hot water was once again available later during the inspection. Manger was informed hot and cold water under pressure must be available during all hours of operation, and the plumbing system must be able to keep up with demand. Call for service and speak with a plumber about options to allow for continuous hot water supply. Perhaps a slightly larger hot water heater is needed for the facility.
 Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the food establishment.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 Steady drip was observed at the bottom right corner of the condensing unit in the walk-in cooler. A pan almost full of water was observed underneath to catch the dripping condensate. Pan was switched out with an empty container. 
Also, the hinge on the top of the walk-in cooler door does not latch properly. Staff have to manually adjust it to allow for door to shut properly and seal flush with the door frame. Call for service was made during inspection. See general comments for additional information.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
2-102.12: A certified food manager was not present at the time of inspection. Facility currently has one CFM, but that person was not present during the inspection today. Staff indicated there is intent to get more staff certified. Inspector advised that more than one person needs to have a food manager certification to ensure a CFM is on-site during all hours of operation. A CFM must be present during all hours of operation.
2-102.12: Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: Multiple employees were observed switching tasks without washing their hands before engaging in food preparation. This item has been corrected and education was shown when and how to wash hands properly. Ensure employees wash their hands after any contamination occurs. 
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: In the double door cooler, there were observed containers of chicken being stored above containers of shrimp. These containers were removed and inverted during the inspection. Reminder was provided to the staff about how to properly store food items to prevent contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: The scoop for the sugar was observed to be stored on top of the sugar tote in the dry storage. The scoop and lid of the tote were both observed to have residue/debris on them. The scoop was placed in the wash, rinse, sanitize process. Once dried, the scoop may be stored directly in the sugar as long as the handle is above the food inside the tote. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: Facility was observed to have various food items in their walk-in cooler that were not properly date marked. Facility is placing dates on the items as they were able to be identified as being prepped yesterday. Ensure that all applicable food items in the establishment are date marked appropriately where day 1 is the day of prep and day 7 the food item is either used or discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: There are various cracks and holes in the back rooms of the facility. Due to the history of pests in the establishment, it is even more reason to seal these holes and cracks. Ensure these surfaces are sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: Facility is in need of a deep clean, especially under and behind equipment where food/debris residue has accumulated. Ensure that equipment is pulled away from the wall and cleaned at a frequency necessary to keep the areas clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13: Observed marked improvement to the general cleanliness of the kitchen. Work still needs to be completed to detail cleaning of facility. The facility is observed with splash and soil on walls, counters, and shelving. See that cleaning continues. For the next follow-up, detail cleaning within the dry storage area will be the focus. See that you continue to focus on the overall detail cleaning that needs to occur on a daily basis,  NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
comment: 5-203.14: The triple sink continues to have a leak at the faucets. See that leaks are repaired so water source is eliminated.  A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT by: (A) Providing an air gap, (B) Installing an APPROVED backflow prevention device.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-101.11: The floor tiles around the dish area are missing and allowing for ponding soil and water. The entire dish machine area is observed soiled and with damaged components. Various tiles are peeled-up from floor, the mop sink is observed soiled, and the walls from mop sink to triple sink are observed coated with chicken debris. Continue to work on cleaning the dish area and see that floors, walls, and ceilings are being replaced so they are smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent. (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for potential cross contamination, sanitation, date marking, and chemical use. The facility currently has active populations of fruit flies and mice based on information provided and observations made during inspection. Active managerial controls were discussed. Corrective actions and active managerial controls will be revisited at the re-inspection on 4/18/22.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Manager was observed chewing gum upon arrival to the facility and continued to chew gum after asked to discard it in the trash. Gum should be discarded by staff upon arrival and prior to starting their shifts. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Salad plates were observed in pans soiled with food debris in the bottom right drawer of the southwest cooler on the make line. One plate was inverted allowing the food contact surfaces to be in direct contact with the soiled pan. Pan and salad plates were removed from the cooler to be cleaned and sanitized.
2. Soda nozzles and diffusers were soiled with chunky mold buildup at the soda machine by the bar. Nozzles and diffusers were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure nozzles and diffusers at both soda machines are cleaned and sanitized daily/as needed per manufacturer’s directions. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed sanitizer solutions in sani-buckets were almost 0ppm quat with very little color change to test strips. Both instant change (inspector) and litmus paper (facility) test strips were used. Management indicated the dispenser doesn’t consistently work and one of the dish washers manually adds the concentrated product at the 3 part sink prior to adding quat solution from the dispenser to get the correct concentration. This practice has occurred for ~2 weeks now. The front cover of the dispenser was loose and hanging down toward the 3 part sink. Call for service was made during inspection. In the meantime, quat solutions for sanitizer-buckets were mixed manually to provide solutions at 400ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Pan of bacon aioli in the walk-in cooler had a day dot showing the prep date of 3/31. Discard date per the label was 4/3 per company requirement. Thursday 4/7 was the last day for use per the date marking requirement of the food code. Product was discarded during inspection.
2. Container of sautéed onions was observed in the walk-in cooler without a date mark. Manager noted the product was likely leftover from the previous evening and should not have been kept. Sautéed onions were discarded.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-202.12 Hot Shot spray pesticide was observed under the counter at the south end of the bar. Manager was advised on the use of pesticides in the facility, and product was removed from the bar. Residential use products are not intended for use in a food service establishment. Ensure labeling indicates products may be used in a food service establishment and work with PCO to determine available products. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions state that use is allowed in a food establishment.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 1. Dozens of fruit flies were observed at the south end of the bar underneath counters and by the paper towel dispenser at the handwashing sink. PCO arrived for monthly service and sprayed to eliminate active flies under counters near drains at the bar. PCO advised management the floor drains need to be thoroughly cleaned before treatment of drains can occur. Drains are believed to be the main source of the issue.
2. Facility has current rodent activity. Staff noted seeing at least one mouse in the bar area in the last few days and sometimes seeing mice around the kitchen handwashing sinks in the early morning hours upon arriving to work and/or in the evening at closing time. Rodent trap was observed with a half dozen dead mice in the corner by the media box at the north end of the bar. PCO scanned the trap and noted it was not on the current service rotation, which means someone moved the trap from its original location resulting in the trap being eliminated from the service rotation. Corner where trap was located has an entry point that needs to be sealed. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
1. Bottom inside the grill cooler (general buildup);
2. Walk-in cooler shelves (varying amounts of splash/general buildup);  and
3. Under the grill, especially the back left corner (grease).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.12 BAR 1. Mouse droppings and general debris were observed on the floor in the corner where media box is stored.
2. Floor drains were soiled with buildup and debris on the south end of the bar. 
3. Grimy buildup was observed on the floor at the south end of the bar near the wall beneath the soda gun.

KITCHEN 1. Walls at dish machine and under 3 part sink were soiled with splash. Clean walls and attached plumbing as needed to eliminate buildup.

STORAGE ALLEY 1. Floor under in-use soda syrup boxes was soiled with splash.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
Outstanding items from the pre-opening inspection: Seal wall to floors around cooler, and caulk handsink to wall in employee restroom.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

Ensure raw meat and egg products are stored on the lowest shelf, under all other ready to eat foods. Inspector will re-address storage of raw product at follow-up.

title: Food obtained from approved source

Meat was embargoed at time of inspection and food program supervisor contacted IL Department of Agriculture to come inspect and evaluate meat sales at this facility. Will follow up next week with facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. Boxes of packaged juice products observed stored out in ambient air in front of counter at the front of the store. According to staff, the product arrived last night. All products bear a label of “keep refrigerated”. Food program supervisor reached out to manufacturers for more information on the product. Items should be discarded by staff after SCDPH speaks to Hani and pulls embargo from the product.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:

Additionally, a few dead cockroaches were observed under the hot holding unit and were not on glue traps. Ensure surfaces are cleaned and glue traps with dead cockroaches are removes so additional pests are not attracted. The areas were cleaned and traps were removed during the inspection. 

6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: The workers were observed switching tasks without washing their hands before engaging in food prep activities. This behavior was discussed and corrected on site with each member. Ensure hands are properly washed anytime contamination occurs.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Food separated and protected

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

3-501.15 1. Fried vegetable eggrolls were observed in the top holding area of the small prep cooler. Surface temperatures were at 80F. Eggrolls were fried within the last 30 to 45 minutes. PIC moved eggrolls to the walk-in cooler to allow for rapid chilling.

Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
4-301.11: Observed nearly sixteen Ziploc quart containers holding Spanish rice to be covered and stacked in the top of the glass sliding door cooler temped at 45-78F. It was stated the rice was cooked within the last hour or so, the rice was moved onto shallow pans, placed on the roll cart, and brought into the walk-in cooler. Foods need to be controlled during the cooling process. There is a stem thermometer and cooling log available (last dated entries were from 2021). Nicholas discussed cooling process with the cook and also discussed using the log. The facility is a Class I due to the cooling and reheating of foods. A significant number of foods are being cooled and reheated. See that cook staff is trained on cooling techniques and facility staff is all helping with this process.  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee shut off the faucet with paper towels and then continued to dry hands with the same paper towels. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed. Use soiled paper towels to touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser to get new paper towels to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

3-501.15 Portion of recently cooked shrimp was observed with internal temperature of 68F in a stainless steel bowl in the top holding area of the prep cooler. The bowl was stacked on the top edges of other pans and not in direct contact with cold air. Shrimp were in the process of cooling for ~30 minutes based on information provided. Best practices for cooling were discussed. Shrimp was portioned into additional containers and moved to the walk-in cooler to speed up the cooling process.
NOTE: The prep cooler is not intended to help cool cooked foods. Ensure proper cooling occurs with foods separated into smaller portions and placed on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler or temporarily stored in a freezer to quickly chill foods. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Four separate portions of eggrolls in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 70F; 68F; 70F; and 81F. Three portions at 70F and 68F were in slotted storage baskets, and the last batch at 81F was in a plastic tub. Eggrolls were prepared in the early afternoon and approaching the end of the first two hours for cooling. Temperatures were checked around 3:20pm. PIC was asked to move eggrolls to the walk-in freezer to speed up cooling process. Approximately an hour later the eggrolls remained in the walk-in cooler, and the batch that was at 81F had an internal temperature of 74F. Eggrolls were past the first two hours of cooling process. Eggrolls were re-fried and reached internal temperatures above 170F. Time control was going to be used, and eggrolls would be used within less than 4hrs for dinner orders. Any leftover portions at the end of the night from this batch were too be discarded.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

3-501.15 1. Five batches of fried chicken portions were observed in colander bowls on the back prep table. Surface temperatures were observed at 69F-122F depending on when portions were fried. Internal temperatures were observed at 74F, 84F, 95F, 106F, and 124F. Based on information provided the chicken portions were fried recently and within the first two hours of the cooling process. Fried chicken portions were placed in plastic tubs and moved to the walk-in cooler. Temperatures were checked around 4:30pm and observed between 48F and 58F.  
2. Four separate portions of eggrolls in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 70F; 68F; 70F; and 81F. Three portions at 70F and 68F were in slotted storage baskets, and the last batch at 81F was in a plastic tub. Eggrolls were prepared in the early afternoon and approaching the end of the first two hours for cooling. Temperatures were checked around 3:20pm. PIC was asked to move eggrolls to the walk-in freezer to speed up cooling process. Approximately an hour later the eggrolls remained in the walk-in cooler. The three portions at 70F and 68F originally were still above 60F and moved to the walk-in freezer to help aid in quick chilling.
3. Cooked lo mein noodles in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 61F and 64F. Noodles were packed full to the top in two plastic containers. Noodles were prepared around noontime and were within the last four hours of cooling. Noodles were separated so product was in four tubs instead of two. PIC was asked to place noodles in the walk-in freezer to speed up the cooling process, but the portions were left in the walk-in cooler covered and stacked. Portions were at 52F-54F when checked around 4:20pm. Noodles were moved to the walk-in freezer to finish cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Conditions at the pet food aisle are greatly improved. However, signs of pests persist. Some droppings are observed on the floor and at the end cap in the middle of the building. Also the bottom shelf with the large bags of dog food have some droppings and urine spots. According to facility management the PCO has not been in this week. Suggest obtaining written documentation from PCO to submit to corporate as proof of conditions. Maintain area clean. Call for PCO schedule and binder. 6-501.115: (A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Observed the facility to be soiled under the prep lines and on all floors at the floor wall junctures. The soil is especially heavy under the drink station #2 and to the right side of the ice machines. Under the prep line that is not in use and the fronts of equipment also have soil. 6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Observed that the floor throughout the facility is showing wear in the grout lines. Areas of low grout have the potential to hold water which facilitates bacteria growth and hold food which can attract pests. No sign of pests at this inspection. 6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:

2-301.12: (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
An open gallon of milk observed in the walk-in cooler with a printed expiration date of 2/18. CORRECTED— Out of date food voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Bar ice bin observed uncovered while not in use. CORRECTED— Discussed with bar staff. Keep ice bin covered when not in use to prevent contamination of ice.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Cardboard used in the walk-in cooler as shelf lining observed to be soiled. Discussed with PIC— remove soiled cardboard. Ensure surfaces subject to spill/splash are made of smooth & nonabsorbent materials.
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

comment:

—Utility/prep sink area has several gaps where walls meet that are not smooth/easily cleanable. Seal gaps.

comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
