title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed multiple in-use rags throughout the facility (bar, kitchen areas, server stations). Ensure rags are kept within sanitization buckets in-between uses. Ensure concentration of buckets maintains 200-400 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Use test strips to verify. Discussed with PIC.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple stacks of cups not being air dried. Ensure cups are air dried before stacking. Noted at both server stations and the bar. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violations since the last routine inspections on 1/4/20, 6/7/21, and 11/9/21.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

2. Stovetop at the prep/grill line is heavily caked with burnt food debris. 
3. Bases of multiple reach-in coolers had food debris.
4. Fan above clean dishes at the dish machine area is severely covered in dust. Fan is directly in the wall.

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces - wash, rinse, sanitize. Clean before next routine inspection.

comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/7/21 and 11/9/21.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

comment:

comment:

comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple Food-borne Illness Risk Factor violations noted on todays inspection. Staff training as well as PIC knowledge should be emphasized more.

comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the facility as well as the sink that the bucket pulls solution from are both observed low during the inspection (barely registering a color change = approximately 0-50ppm quat). Employees remade the solution during the inspection to correct the violation. A follow up will take place to verify that the dispenser is adequately supplying sanitizer in 2 weeks.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items related to temperature abuse and date marking were observed during the inspection. Best practices for cooling were not observed, and foods in the process of cooling had to be reheated to begin the process again. A section of foods in the hot deli case were observed with internal temperatures below 135F, resulting reheating and/or discard of foods. Best practices were not observed for quick chilling and cold holding after preparation of foods intended for cold storage. Soups were discarded based on prep dates from February and/or lack of date marks. Also, two of the three handwashing sinks were without soup, and one of the handwashing sinks was soiled and slow draining. Educational handouts for date marking, cooling, and proper hot/cold holding temperatures were provided. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited during re-inspection on 3/21/22. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Deli manager has an expired food manager certification and is working to get certification along with all of the managers at this location. Once certifications are completed all managers and enough assistant managers should be certified to ensure the presence of a CFM during all hours of operation. In the meantime, the produce manager was on-site during the inspection and able to show proof of a current food manager certification.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:

All foods, including candy and gum, should only be consumed in designated areas/at break time when employees are not working around food and/or clean dishes. Employee washed hands at request of inspector prior to continuing with ware washing. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:

Soap from dispenser with dead batteries was moved to the other handwashing sink, and a pump bottle of hand soap was placed at the handwashing sink in the corner. Ensure batteries are changed as needed and all handwashing sinks are properly stocked.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Knives and a spreader were stored in the crevices between storage racks and the wall above the 3 part sink. The crevices between the racks and the wall are not considered clean surfaces and are not intended for storage of cleaned and sanitized utensils. Knives and spreader were removed to be re-washed and sanitized. Cease this storage practice.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Cooked foods prepared earlier today were in the walk-in cooler and observed with internal temperatures at 106F (sausage and peppers) and 108F-115F (three meatloaves). Cooling process began around 12-12:30pm based on information provided, and internal temperatures were observed during inspection at 2:50pm. Foods were placed back in the steamer to be reheated to 165F/above and restart the cooling process. Ensure temperatures are monitored during cooling process with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Lasagna and gravy in the hot case had internal temperatures of 113F and 118F. Lasagna was placed in the steamer to reheat based on initial time of prep and gravy was discarded along with other foods the deli manager confirmed to have internal temperatures below 135F. The foods below 135F were all within the middle section of the holding case. Ensure the unit is able to maintain foods at proper temperature and consider placing the hot holding unit at a higher setting to offset for temperate loss during times when doors will be opened and closed frequently. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Several prepared foods intended to be cold held were observed on a cart in the prep area. Employee was working with and preparing multiple salads, sandwiches and other items. Surface temperatures ranged from 50F to 66F depending on how long items were out during prep within the last ~30-45 minutes. Employee was in the process of finishing prep and labeling containers. All foods were placed in the walk-in cooler to quickly chill foods. Best practice of only working with limited amounts of foods at a time was discussed. Foods should be rotated back into the the cooler to quickly chill once prep is done and prior to beginning preparation of other items.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Containers of cooked and cooled soups in the chicken walk-in cooler had prep dates of 2/27 and 2/26. One container was without a date mark. Deli manager removed all products in question for discard. Ensure prepared foods are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days, 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices

Management was advised to clean the sink and have maintenance provide service to clear any potential debris and ensure proper drainage. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

comment: Observed the steel wool to still be in the door however, light is still visible in the gaps of the door. Rob the district manager  was here Wednesday along with other members of management. title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
The complaint was concerning soft food in the freezer. The complaint does not say what type of food was soft. During inspection the employee stated that they cut meat and put it into the freezer. They have freshly cut meat in the freezer that is not yet completely frozen. This is a likely explanation of the complaint. The temperature of this meet is 28F.  Other foods in the freezers were frozen solid. The manager stated that the freezers had gone down yesterday (2.24.22). The manager stated that when they noticed the wall freezers going down they moved the new chest freezers from their storage to the facility and moved the frozen items into the individual chest style freezers. They had recently purchased the new bank of freezers for the grocery but had not yet put them into use. According to the refrigeration technician, the entire building had a single unit that controlled all of the coolers and freezers in the market. He said that they would be back Monday (2.28.22) to start work on the job and that it may take a week and a half in order to repair the unit and get the coolers and freezers up and running again. They did get one refrigeration unit working today. This unit is holding at 40F according to the independent thermometer. The staff began to stock this unit with bean sprouts and other tofu products which were observed to be on the open shelves in the facility upon arrival. Some of the other keep refrigerated items were kept in the walk in cooler according to the staff. This walk in has an integrated thermometer which was reading 45F. These bean sprouts along with the other items labeled keep refrigerated are observed to be above 41F and have been for an undetermined amount of time. We placed the tofu, egg products and noodle products into boxes to move to the back room. Several boxes of items were discarded before we could embargo them. The remaining foods have been embargoed and will be further researched in order to determine if the foods can be kept or if they will be discarded.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Cheese sauce and chili being hot held in the same food warmer were observed with varying temperatures. Cheese sauce had internal temperatures ranging from 128F-145F, and chili had internal temperatures ranging from 120F-156F. Cheese sauce was prepared and heated on the stove using a commercially processed mix prior to placing in the warmer. Chili was a reheat from the day prior and was heated to ~145F prior to placing in the warmer, with the intent to finish the reheat to 165F. Both products were placed back on the stove and reheated to temperatures above 165F before hot holding. Ensure foods are at proper temperature throughout prior to hot holding. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Signage that shows the steps of proper handwashing is posted above the kitchen handwashing for reference.

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee at service counter was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine final rinse chlorine concentration was observed at ~10-25ppm. Sanitizer jug was almost empty. After providing a new jug of sanitizer and priming the chemical line the final rinse concentration was observed below 50ppm. A call for service was made during inspection, and management was informed a technician would be able to come out for service on Thursday of this week. The kitchen 3 part sink was setup during inspection (200ppm quat). In the meantime, the kitchen manager ran the dish machine for another half dozen plus cycles, and the final rinse concentration reach 50ppm. It would appear the lower concentration during previous cycles was due to old chemical, which worked its way through the tubing after priming and running multiple cycles. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Three 5gal containers of cheese sauce in the walk-in cooler were observed with surface temperatures of 50F-55F and internal temperatures of 77F-79F. Cheese sauce was reheated to begin cooling process again. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures

3-501.16 (A)(1) Sausages in steam table were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 117F to 130F. PIC noted the staff began turning off hot holding units recently to begin the cooling process. Other hot TCS foods were observed at 133F-136F and were immediately placed in an ice bath in the walk-in cooler to begin active cooling. Some sausages were well below 135F, and PIC began to reheat sausages but ultimately decided to discard the product. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Hash browns in the bottom of a prep cooler had surface temperatures at 55F-57F and an internal temperature of 60F. PIC noted the potatoes may have been removed from the cooler for a brief period during lunch service. Time was not being tracked for the in-use supply and it was assumed the intent was to keep the potatoes cold. Potatoes were in the danger zone for an unknown amount of time and were discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Individual portions of thawed vacuum packaged salmon were observed in the bottom of a prep cooler. Other portions in the process of thawing were observed in the walk-in cooler. None of the packages were cut. PIC had employee cut the packages of thawed portions in the prep cooler during inspection. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section (under cold running water).

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Facility food thermometer was reading at a lower temperature compared to inspector’s when a hot food temperature was checked. Ice water was setup for calibration, and facility food thermometer was reading around 25F. Thermometer was calibrated to 30F-32F during inspection. PIC stated all food thermometers will be checked for calibration prior to service tomorrow morning. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for all employees. Certification was missing for one of the cooks, and the employee in the dish area confirmed they did not have a food handler certification. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Seal bare wood wall border with stain or paint by next routine inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Inspector will follow-up on 1/10/22.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee washed hands without proper technique at the bar handwashing sink. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. Ensure paper towels are used to dry hands and then used to shut off the manual faucet to avoid potential re-contamination of freshly washed hands. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.12 Carton of raw shell eggs was observed on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler stored next to and above ready to eat foods. Eggs were moved to the bottom shelf with other raw animal products. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 1. A soiled knife was observed on the magnetic knife strip adjacent to the salad cooler. Food debris was observed on the blade. Knife was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
2. The magnetic knife strip was also soiled with general buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Individual portions of thawed vacuum packaged fish were observed in the walk-in cooler. Proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish was discussed. At minimum the packaging needs to be cut on each portion to eliminate reduced oxygen environment once the fish is  removed from the freezer and and placed in the cooler to thaw. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 1. Lids for food containers were observed in a soiled storage container in the dry storage area. General debris accumulation was observed in the bottom of the tub. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
2. Storage rack above the salad prep cooler was soiled with splash and crumb accumulation. Clean plates and bowls were stored on the back ledge of the cooler beneath the rack. Single service articles were also stored on the rack. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:

3. General buildup was observed in the bottom of the convection oven located on top of pizza ovens. 
4. General surfaces of dish machine were soiled with buildup, especially on top of the machine.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Food handler certifications were not available for two of the kitchen staff working at time of inspection. One employee had proof of certification on their phone and planned to email a copy to management. The other employee (dish area) stated they had a certification that was expired and needed to take a course. Ensure staff provide copies of current food handler certifications by the next routine inspection. Staff need to complete a food handler course within 30 days from date of hire. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 1. Soda gun at the bar had mold buildup along the outer edge where the nozzle seals to the gun. The drain cup beneath the soda gun had buildup where the drain hose connected. A small amount of ponding liquid was observed where clog was present. Employee working at the bar was advised the soda gun and drain cup beneath were in need of cleaning.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

2. Mashed potato scoop was soiled with food debris from use during lunch service and stored on top of the lid to the mashed potato container in the hot holding unit. Scoop was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection. Ensure cleaning of utensils up to every 4hrs when stored at ambient temperature.
If used with time/temperature control for safety (TCS)foods, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of sloppy joes leftover from the previous operating day had an internal temperature of 46F. Pan was stacked between two other pans of sloppy joes with internal temperatures of 43F-44F. Employee that was in charge of preparing and cooling sloppy joes the day prior stated the products were cooled on ice baths, but the temperature was not monitored during the process. It was unclear as to how long the middle pan of sloppy joes had an internal temperature above 45F, and the product in question was discarded.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Portions of cole slaw made in-house were observed in a container labeled 11/27 in the walk-in cooler. Remaining portions were discarded during inspection. Ensure foods prepared on-site are used or discarded within 7 days.
2.  Open bag of pepperoni in the bottom of the pizza prep cooler was not date marked. Kitchen staff noted it was opened within the last few days and provided a date mark.
3. Leftover hotdogs in the walk-in cooler were not date marked. Kitchen staff stated they were from service Monday evening. Date mark was provided. 
4. Open bags of shredded lettuce and mixed greens were observed without date marks in the bottom of the prep cooler. Lettuce shreds were opened the day prior, and mixed greens were just opened today. Date marks were provided.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-601.11 Pizza baking tray was observed with encrusted debris. Staff working at time of inspection noted they had not used the tray in question during current operations. Tray was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 1. Hood filters above cooking equipment were soiled with buildup of dust and grease. Hood was last serviced in August 2021 and was due for another full service. Ensure filters are cleaned as needed between full service cleanings.
2. Floor under and around fryers had some buildup of grease and food debris. Floors were cleaned since last inspection but were in need of cleaning again. Ensure the floor under equipment is cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup of grease and food debris.
3. Walls on both sides of the mopsink were damaged along the top edge of base coving. Repair the walls at the mopsink.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-305.11 Jackets were observed hanging on shelving used for storage of clean equipment. Proper storage was discussed, and jackets were removed from the kitchen.
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.
citation_text:
6-303.11 Light bulbs by the back wall in dry storage room were burnt out. Provide adequate lighting in the dry storage room. 
Light intensity shall be at least 10 food candles (108 lux) at a distance of 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival, no reporting agreements are observed at the facility. PIC stated that they were in his car. Follow up will be scheduled for two weeks and they are instructed to ensure that reporting agreements are available at the facility at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11: Soda nozzles in the bar area were observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residue. Ensure these surfaces are soaked and sanitized to prevent the potential contamination of the contact surfaces with the food items being served. Ensure this process is conducted at a frequency that prevents this accumulation.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:

Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris and soil residue. This cleaning will also discourage potential pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Observed the walk in food cooler to be holding milk and juice at 45F. These items were discarded as there is no log to determine how long they have been held at 45F.  The owner is calling his refrigerator repair person and will have them out tomorrow or as soon as possible. Owner states that the beer cave should be used for milk or perishable items until the other unit is repaired. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

comment: See violations record from last routine inspection and or pre-opening inspection.

comment:
Observed boxes of prepackaged snacks to be stored on the floor in the back storage area. Provide shelving for snack storage. 
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in cook line sani-bucket was observed at a concentration below 100ppm. Solution was prepared recently, and it appeared one of the tablets may have stuck to and possible dissolved into a wiping cloth. Additional tablets were added and brought the concentration to 200ppm
Sanitizer tablets were not dissolving in the server area sani-bucket due to the use of cold water to make the solution. Kitchen manager remade the solution with warm water, and the concentration was observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures

Kitchen manager noted the warmer was turned on around the same time the products were placed inside after being made fresh this afternoon. Alfredo sauce in the warmer had an internal temperate of 144F. All products in the warmer below 135F were reheated to 165F/above prior to placing back in the warmer for hot holding. Ensure hot holding equipment is on and at proper temperature to maintain hot foods at 135F/above prior to hot holding.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the kitchen reach-in cooler. Proper thawing of ROP fish was discussed. Packaging for thawed portions of fish was cut open during inspection. Ensure moving forward that packaging is cut prior to beginning thawing process for ROP fish.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Due to the holiday, the follow-up is scheduled for 12/27/21. Facility will be closed for the holidays. Inspector instructed facility to utilize the 3 compartment sink until it is repaired. Facility has bleach for food-contact surfaces and is an approved brand.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple food items in the walk-in cooler to be out of date. Items were voluntarily discarded. Date marking of within 7 day foods was missing for some items as well. Ensure disposition of foods past 7 day date marking is habitual. Ensure date marking on all prepared and/or thawed foods. Discussed with PIC. Facility has actively improved on date marking and disposition and the issues today were minor as compared to previous inspections. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 3/12/20 and 8/4/21.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed walk-in cooler to have part coming away from the door. Ensure door is fixed so it is flush and smooth. Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC washed hands without proper technique prior to preparing an order of nachos for a customer. Soap was not used, the process lasted less than 20 seconds, and the manual faucet was shut off prior to using paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided for reference.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Observed the soda gun to be soiled. Soda gun was properly cleaned during the inspection. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: The physical facilities are in need of general cleaning around the air vents on the ceiling and under hard to reach places. Ensure these areas are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust and debris.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: Raw liver was observed to be stored above pancake batter in the silver cooler along the cook line. This item was removed and placed on the bottom shelf and the pancake batter was arranged above it. Ensure raw meat products are stored in a manner that prevents potential contamination of the food items below it. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13: Facility was observed thawing meat in a white bucket filled with water on the counter. This bucket was placed into the sink with running water during the inspection. Ensure proper thawing methods are used when thawing foods to allow the food safety to remain in tact during this process.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-303.11 The dish machine sanitizer was tested at 0ppm. MJ Kellner was called and showed up during the inspection to perform maintenance on the machine. This issue was corrected before the end of the inspection and sanitizer was properly being dispensed into the machine. Ensure test strips are used daily to ensure the integrity of the sanitizer remains.
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: The air vents above the dish area were observed to have an accumulation of dust and debris residue. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent accumulation of residues and debris.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: Area of hard to reach places, such as the shelving and behind the shelving by the dish machine, were observed to have an accumulation of soil and debris. Ensure facility is cleaned in detail to prevent this accumulation and reduce the potential of future pest issues within the facility. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: Items int he walk-in cooler were observed to be without a date mark due to their addition to the cooler today. A date marked was placed during the inspection on all new items from today. Ensure dates are applied immediately upon prep to ensure their integrity.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored on the top shelf of the kitchen fridge, over pre-cooked bacon and a large bag of tortilla chips. CORRECTED— Eggs moved to storage on a lower shelf, below RTE foods.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

comment:
