6-501.11 & 6-501.12 WALK-IN COOLER: 1. Door trim in the walk-in cooler was soiled with mold. Inner door trim was also unsealed and had exposed insulation. Clean inside the walk-in cooler and provide a proper seal for the inner door frame of the walk-in cooler.
2. Ceiling and fan covers were soiled with what appeared to be general buildup of dust. Clean the ceiling and fan covers in the walk-in cooler.
ICE MACHINE ROOM: 1. Baseboard was loose at the floor to wall juncture by the ice machine. Repair or replace the loose coving.
2. Wall had a hole in it next to the ice machine in the same area where baseboard was loose. Repair the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: 5-205.11: Observed hand washing sink in back room to be blocked by boxes.  Boxes were moved.(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: 3-307.11: Observed Freal milkshake in freezer with no lid, exposing contents to contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: 4-903.11: Observed boxes of single service cups stored directly on the ground in the back storage room. (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: The triple sink and the hand washing sink in the back room are in need of caulking where the metal meets the wall and where the sink basin meets the wall. Ensure these surfaces are sealed properly to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-101.11: The bar top black strip was observed to have spots with exposed wood. Ensure these surfaces are painted or sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment:
Facility serves pizzas without a pizza variance. CORRECTED— Completed request for pizza variance during inspection.
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Foods in the cooler labeled 10 observed to be out of temperature: gallons of milk at 48F, 14-16oz milks at 46F, and hot dogs at 45F. CORRECTED— All items in that section of the cooler were voluntarily discarded. PIC called cooler service provider while inspector was present to get cooler looked at and repaired.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

Caulking to the 3-compartment sink is old and frayed, gap between sink and wall. Re-caulk 3-compartment sink to the wall so it is smooth and easily cleanable by next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Upon inspector arrival a cardboard box holding individually-bagged servings of popcorn was observed sitting on top of handsink. Discussed with staff and PIC. Ensure handsink remains accessible at all times. Store single service equipment in an alternate location, that does not block handwashing or warewashing facilities.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

Observed staff switching between tasks/glove changes without washing hands in between. Discussed with staff and PIC. Ensure staff are washing hands when a change in tasks occurs. For busy moments during games, designating staff to particular tasks may help services run safely and efficiently.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not present in the employee restrooms, the mezzanine concession stands, and the SW main floor concession stand. Handwashing signs were provided and placed in the concession stands by kitchen manager. Maintenance will be made aware of the need to post handwashing signs in employee restrooms. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food obtained from approved source
citation_text:
3-201.11 Bags of leftover cheese sauce that were previously heated and cooled were observed in the kitchen walk-in cooler. Current risk classification of Class II medium risk does not allow for cooling and reheating of hot TCS foods. Bags of cheese sauce were discarded, and new bags of cheese sauce were heated for use. **See HACCP Topic Section for additional information**
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed on the ceiling behind the baffle in the ice machine bin. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of the ice machine as needed per manufacturer directions. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer in spray bottles at concession stands had concentrations at 0ppm and less than 100ppm. Solutions were old and in need of changing. Fresh solution dispensed for the spray bottle to be used at the NW main concession stand for today’s event was observed at 200ppm. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are checked with test strips to verify concentration and refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Chemical spray bottles pre-labeled as Purple Power cleaner contained old Quat solutions. A bottle of degreaser in the NW main concession stand was also not labeled. Proper labeling of chemicals was discussed, and spray bottles were properly labeled during inspection.
 Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water handle was stuck at the kitchen handwashing sink. Once turned to allow for cold water, there was very little pressure, and the water was discolored. The hot water, which was working prior to turning on the cold water, was then observed to also be discolored and lacking in pressure. Maintenance will be replacing the faucet and gaskets. 
Until the handwashing sink is repaired and functioning properly, the first basin at the kitchen 3 part sink will be used for handwashing. Dish soap was available at the sink, and paper towels were provided. Ensure basins are cleaned prior to setting up the sinks for ware washing at the end of food service. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook line employee was observed going between glove changes without handwashing in between. Employee was educated on handwashing between glove changes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee working at grill was observed adjusting clothing with gloved hands and continued to food handling without a handwash and glove change. Employee was educated on proper glove use prior to washing hands and putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with prep. Employee was observed changing gloves and washing hands as needed for remainder of inspection.
-Employee working at drive thru window was observed wearing gloves and then put on another pair of single use gloves on top to prepare a beverage order. Glove use policy was discussed with management, and double gloving is not in the policy. Employee was educated by manager on duty.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was at 0ppm at the front counter and 100ppm by ice cream station. Solutions were changed and observed at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. 

Dish machine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer bucket was approximately a quarter full of product, and PIC noted the amount of sanitizer in the chemical bucket was potentially too low to allow for proper suction. Changing to a full bucket and priming the dish machine sanitizer line resulted in a final rinse concentration of 100ppm.
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
No CFM present when inspector arrived. CORRECTED— CFM arrived during inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM training to cover all hours of operation.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
No handwashing signage present at either of the restroom handsinks (mens/womens). CORRECTED— Inspector provided signage to be posted. Any signage notifies food employees to wash their hands is appropriate (it does not need to be the signage provided by the health department).
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
1st REPEAT: Ice machine baffle observed with black/brown accumulation. Clean and sanitize as often as necessary to maintain clean.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Ranch and chipotle ranch in the walk-in cooler both dated use by 12/22 (more than 7 days from today). Pizza sauce in the prep cooler dated 11/22. Sauerkraut dated 11/19. Foods opened or prepared in the facility must be appropriately date-marked. See General Comments for exemptions. Discard out of date foods.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Single service spoons observed mixed directions, with many spoons food-contact-end up. Store utensils so that only handles are touched by staff or customers.
citation_text: 4-904.11 (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed half and half to be missing the date marking. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
Date mark was added to the half and half.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Observed scoops in the dry mixes with handles touching the food.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS 
Fill containers leaving enough space to include scoops without placing the handles of scoops into the food.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. They then proceeded to manipulate the paper towel dispenser with a bare hand for the drying implement. Education has taken place.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the dish machine in the kitchen is not properly sanitizing dishes. Priming the machine brought the concentration up to correct levels. PIC stated that they would contact MJ Kelner for a service call to ensure the machine functions correctly in the future.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Two containers of knives are observed stored in containers with crumbs in the bottom of the containers. Containers and knives were sent to dish for cleaning to correct.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) Class II facilities are required to have a Certified Food Protection Manager at all times that foods are being handled or prepared. 

On arrival, there was not a CFPM at the facility. A CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Both the CFPM that arrived and the PIC at inspector’s arrival did not seem aware of the requirement that the facility have one on site at all times of operation. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is on site at all times that food and food contact are handled.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (Pf) The Person in Charge shall ensure that: (O) “Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). 

No reporting agreements or other verifiable manner was observable during the inspection. A copy of the Sangamon County Reporting agreement was given to the PIC during the inspection. They are instructed to make copies and ensure that all Food Handlers have signed a copy. Follow up in 10 days.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Ice is observed with black specs both in the ice and on the surface of the ice in both the ice bin (bar) and the ice machine (back room). Contaminated ice was discarded during the inspection to correct. PIC instructed to have the ice machine cleaned and inspector will spot check in the future.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Mold accumulation was observed in the ice machine. Buildup was present along the top of the baffle behind the lid. A significant amount was observed on the ceiling behind the baffle. 
-Ice scoop was stored in a covered, plastic container that was soiled with grimy buildup. 
Follow-up inspection will be conducted on 12/6/21 to verify the ice machine and ice scoop storage container have been properly cleaned and sanitized.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was observed sealed in foil packaging and had an expiration date of 2018. Obtain a new test kit and ensure it is being used to verify concentration of sanitizer solutions. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use at the time of inspection. Sanitizer preparation and availability during hours of operation were discussed.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 WALK-IN COOLER: 1. Step inside the walk-in cooler was damaged. Trim was documented to be damaged at the 2018 routine inspection. Provide proper repairs to the step inside the cooler.
2. Door trim in the walk-in cooler was soiled with mold. Inner door trim was also unsealed and had exposed insulation. Clean inside the walk-in cooler and provide a proper seal for the inner door frame of the walk-in cooler.
3. Ceiling and fan covers were soiled with what appeared to be general buildup of dust. Clean the ceiling and fan covers in the walk-in cooler.
ICE MACHINE ROOM: 1. Baseboard was loose at the floor to wall juncture by the ice machine. Repair or replace the loose coving.
2. Wall had a hole in it next to the ice machine in the same area where baseboard was loose. Repair the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Bartender working at time of inspection did not have a food handler certification. Foodhandler FAQ and options for course information were provided. Employees need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
1st REPEAT: Pink soil observed on the baffle of the ice machine. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. CORRECTED— PIC washed and sanitized the area. Maintain clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Soiled knives observed stored with clean in the knife rack. Store in-use utensils separate from clean, not currently in-use utensils. CORRECTED— Knives removed to be washed rinsed and sanitized. Discussed proper storage and cleaning of the knife rack as well.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 1st REPEAT: Floors throughout the facility are soiled. The most heavily soiled area is behind the dish machine.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreements were not available for all staff. At least two cooks need to sign reporting agreements. Reporting agreement was also missing for one of the wait staff that arrived during inspection. Employee health policy was discussed. The server signed a reporting agreement, and additional copies were provided for staff to sign as they come in for their next shift. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff, including management. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of food thermometer was soiled with grease and food debris. Stem was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure the stems of food thermometers are properly cleaned and sanitized between uses. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Kitchen manager confirmed the can opener was not used prior to arrival of inspector, and buildup on the blade was from use on a previous date of operation. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not setup at the bar. Server working at the bar was advised on preparation and availability of sanitizer solution. Ensure sani-buckets are setup and available for use.  
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 The cook working with kitchen manager at the time of inspection did not have a foodhandler certification. Foodhandler FAQ was provided and course options were discussed. Servers did not have copies of food handler certifications available at the facility. Ensure staff that are not certified food managers complete online food handler course within 30 days of hiring. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Observed bartender to wash hands in wash section of 3 part sink. 
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.
Use the hand sink for all hand washing activities.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed the hand sink to have a box of crackers sitting in it. No hand soap was provided to the hand sink. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
The hand soap was moved back to the hand sink from the mop sink area. Cracker box was removed from the hand sink so that it is accessible.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Observed the food contact surface of the soda gun to be soiled with mold.
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 
The soda gun was washed, rinsed and saitized.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Observed chunks of black mold to have fallen out of the inside of the ice making section of the ice machine and into the ice in the ice bin. Empty and properly clean the ice machine so that it is not contaminating the food (ice) with mold. 
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed cooler in small storage room next to the bar to be holding at 50F according to the internal thermometer. Two quarts of pumpkin spice flavored cream registers 45F internally. Four pints of half and half register 45F internally. Three, four ounce portions of feta cheese register 50F internally and  two, four ounce portions of blue cheese register 50F internally. These foods were discarded in the garbage. The garbage was taken out to the dumpster. Do not store food that requires refrigeration for safety in this unit until it is either repaired or replaced. Maintain time temperature control for safety foods at 41F or below. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, proper glove use, and sanitization. Employee health documentation was also unable to be located. Educational handouts were provided for reference, and new copies of employee health documents were provided.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Person in charge (PIC) at the time of inspection did not have a food manager certification. GM is registered to take a food manager course later this week. Ensure that all supervisors who will be the designated PIC at the time of inspection have a current food manager certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee handled their cell phone to show proof of food handler certification and did not wash hands upon returning to the cooking area to put on gloves and continue with prep. Handwashing between tasks was discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling cell phones.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed touching the manual faucet with their hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employees were observed adjusting clothing and touching hats with gloved hands. Employees then continued on with food handling without a glove change. Proper glove use was discussed. Employees changed gloves before continuing with their next tasks. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-buckets were observed at concentration of 0ppm and 100ppm quat. A spray bottle was also observed at a concentration of 0ppm. All sanitizer solutions were discarded and replaced with fresh solutions at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration, and maintain solutions at 200-400ppm as directed by product label. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer available for use had a loose needle and was unable to be calibrated. GM found a new thermometer in the office, which was calibrated with ice point method and made available for use during inspection. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. Proof of food handler certification was only available for one employee working at the time of inspection. Ensure staff that are not CFMs complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Allergen training as required

4-703.11: Observed the dish machine to have a temperature of 140F. The dish machine must maintain a temperature of 160F or higher. The 3 part sink will be used until the dish machine has been fixed. 
After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
No employee health documents are on file. Inspector emailed necessary form— print one out for each employee to sign.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment:
No written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available. Inspector emailed a
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment:
Facility (with a medium risk permit) has prepared and cooled foods to be reheated for service at another time. These activities are not allowed under a medium risk permit. Inspector provided education. To continue cooling and reheating foods, facility must upgrade to a high risk permit. CORRECTED— Foods prepared outside of the current permit must be discarded.
3-201.11: (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
1st REPEAT: Raw shell eggs observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (cheese sauce, cheese slices, citrus fruit) in the kitchen fridge. CORRECTED— Since no foods appear to be contaminated, storage rearranged to prevent potential contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Cl rinse in the bar 3 compartment sink observed at 25ppm. CORRECTED— Remade sanitizer to correct concentration.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Bar 3 compartment sink observed set up to wash, sanitize, then rinse dishes. This eliminates the sanitize step, so dishes are not being sanitized. CORRECTED— Provided education. Staff set up sink to wash, rinse, then sanitize, and discussed the need to air-dry.
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
1st REPEAT: Foods observed past the 7 day date marking. In the kitchen fridge, cheese sauce dated 11/10, chili dated 11/4, and coleslaw dated 11/4. Sausage gravy in the kitchen cooler observed without any date marking. CORRECTED— Foods without date marking or 7 days past their date marking must be discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Foods and single service items observed stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Store items at least 6 inches above the floor to protect from potential contamination.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Ice scoop in the bar ice bin observed stored with handle in contact with the ice. Store scoop so that ice may be scooped without bare hand contact with the ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Person in charge (PIC) at the start of inspection was unable to answer questions about potential food service on weekends and the disinfectant available for use. A priority violation was also observed for handwashing. Facility manager arrived during inspection and was able to demonstrate knowledge.  Manager was advised to ensure all staff, regardless of the number of days they work at the facility, are able to demonstrate knowledge on all topics based on risks inherent to the establishment.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed handling cell phone and did not wash hands prior to handling and stocking single service cups and stirs at the bar. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks. Employee was later observed washing hands between tasks as needed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food obtained from approved source
citation_text:
3-201.11 Evidence was observed on the Shamrock Tavern Facebook page to indicate food service is occurring at the facility beyond what is allowed under the current permit classification. Screenshots of posts from 10/17/21, 10/24/21, and 11/7/21 were provided that showed foods such as chili, mostaccioli, and salad were served. The facility is currently permitted as Class III low risk and is not allowed to serve foods such as the aforementioned items without upgrading to a Class II medium risk permit or obtaining temporary food service permits for special events if they wish to maintain a Class III low risk permit. Temporary food permit applications were provided, and bar manager stated temporary permits will be obtained moving forward.
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Ice scoop used at main ice machine was observed with the food contact surface in direct contact with a damp, plastic grocery sack in the bottom of a rusty beer bucket. Scoop was set aside to be cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink. Proper storage was discussed. Provide another container for storage of the ice scoop. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed on the metal baffle in the ice machine. Buildup was also present in the top part of the machine where ice maker is located. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
-Mold buildup was observed around the seal of the soda gun where the nozzle attaches. Ensure cleaning as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and with enclosed components, such as ice bins a machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Four spray bottles of a yellowish colored liquid were observed at the bar. Two bottles were labeled as Buckeye Eco Neutral Disinfectant. One spray bottle did not have any labeling. The fourth bottle was a Purell food service sanitizer bottle that was being re-used. 
The two bottles without proper labeling were labeled as to the contents. All four bottles contained the same general disinfectant. Proper labeling of toxics was discussed. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Bottles of juice were observed on the floor in the walkin cooler. Store food up off the floor in the walkin cooler.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Boxes of single use cups and portion cups (shot glasses) were observed on the floor in the storage area. Store boxes up off the floor. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-202.14  Men's room door was not shutting properly. When closed it did not seal to be flush with the door frame. Repair the door so it shuts and seals properly.
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floors were soiled under and around the ice machine, mopsink, and the ice bin at the bar. Ensure cleaning of floors as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreements were not available for store manager and staff. Employee health policy was discussed. Manager and staff signed copies of the reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper technique poster is available for reference at the front handsink. Handwashing was discussed with store manager. Ensure staff are using proper technique during handwashing process. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use the paper towels after hands are dried and shut off the faucet at the last step of the handwashing process.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-202.15 A hole was present at the bottom right corner of weather stripping on the back door. Provide repairs to seal the hole.
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by providing solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Bag of onions was observed on the floor in the dry storage area. Store food up off the floor at least 6 inches. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. Proper storage in a clean, protected location was discussed. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not TCS food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.11 White baffle in the ice machine was cracked and broken along the lower edge. The baffle needs to be replaced. Manager stated they have spoke with supervisor about getting the baffle replaced. This was a repeat violation during the 2019 routine inspection. Provide a plan of action within 10 days. 
Food-contact surfaces shall be smooth; free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections; and free of sharp internal angles, corners, and crevices.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Rust was observed on shelving in the three door cooler where coating has begun to wear off. Re-surface the shelving. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floor tile by the wall on the left side of the 3 part sink was loose. General buildup and mold were observed on the underside of the tile and on the floor where tile was loose. Until repairs are done, manager was advised to keep the area clean and dry to eliminate potential food and water sources for pests. Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed under the 3 part sink adjacent to the floor tile of concern.  
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of current food handler certification was not available for delivery drivers, and one of the employees that mainly does deliveries was assisting with bread prep. All employees that do not have a food manager certification need to complete the online food handler certification, especially since delivery drivers assist with prep and may also assist with ware washing. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

An employee meal was observed on a counter in the center of the kitchen. PIC was consulted and the meal moved to an area separate from food preparation to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to eat (in the dish area) and then move directly to handling cleaned dishes without hand washing. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing takes place in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

A consistent drip is observed coming from the vent in the walk in cooler. The situation is already being taken care of for repair, but multiple foods are observed open in the cooler. The blowing of the fan is pushing drops out to land throughout an area that encompasses multiple open containers. PIC was consulted and lids/ coverings supplied to protect the foods.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside spout of the soda gun in the server area is observed with a thick accumulation of dark colored slime. The situation was brought to the attention of the PIC and the items cleaned/ sanitized to correct.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

A phone was observed stored on the wood counter in the section of the facility also containing the ice machine. The wooden counter is also used for food preparation at other times. No food prep observed at this location at this time. PIC was consulted, the phone removed and the surface sanitized to correct.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Observed the service door to the back stock room to have a large gap at the bottom and areas along the door where weather strip is missing where daylight is clearly observed. 6-202.15: 
(A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.
Repair or replace weather stripping and varmint guards on the double door to the back storage area to discourage the entrance of insects and rodents.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Locations in need of cleaning: 1) floors in the walk in freezer, 2) floors in the dry storage areas, 3) walls along the edges of the walk in freezer have peeling paint.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

1) In the dish room there is a gap between the metal siding to the left of the dish machine visibly soiled. 2) There is a hole (approximately 1.5 inch diameter) in the metal siding to the right of the dish machine that is visible soiled. PIC instructed to repair/ caulk and maintain smooth and easily cleanable.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-601.11: The pizza ovens were observed to have an accumulation of food and grease debris. Ensure these surfaces are removed from the oven and put through a wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Perform these actions at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of the debris.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: The caulking of the hand sink is no longer existent. Where the sink meets the wall there is a gap present. Apply caulking to the area to seal the gap and create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 4-602.11: (A) Observed ice machine baffles in dish room and kitchen to be soiled with debris. FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Observed clean cooking utensils stored in containers soiled with food debris. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: 2-301.14: Observed food employee put on new pair of gloves without first washing hands.  Wash hands before each new glove use. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
comment: 3-101.11: Observed moldy tomatoes in walk in cooler.  Tomatoes were discarded. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13: Observed soft serve ice cream machine to be soiled with dried ice cream residue.  NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-501.16: Observed mop head to be stored head down in dirty mop water bucket. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Facility manager and employee working at the time of inspection did not have signed employee health policy forms on file. Employee health policy was discussed, and forms were signed during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands with proper technique for the remainder of inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the front handwashing sink. Handwashing sign was provided and posted at the handwashing sink. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Meatballs in hot baine were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 109F-117F and 114F-125F respectively. Meatballs were just heated in the microwave for hot holding prior to inspector’s arrival. Internal temperature was not verified prior to hot holding. Reheating for hot holding was discussed. Meatballs were portioned and cold held since Saturday and needed to be heated to at least 165F prior to service. Meatballs were reheated to 167F prior to hot holding. 
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.  Any portions held cold after removed from original packaging and heated at a later time need to reach an internal temperature of at least 165F.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Shelves in walk-in cooler had varying amounts of general buildup and mold. Shelving unit with the most buildup was in the back left corner. Manager noted staff are in the process of cleaning all shelving in the walk-in cooler.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Observed staff member filling a frying pan with water using the handwashing sink. Discussed with PIC and staff in kitchen. See that staff use other sinks for filling/food prep, leave handwashing sinks for handwashing only.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT, and utensil is washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours. 

Observed two knives stored between prep coolers and prep tables in the cooking area. Cease practice of storing utensils between equipment crevices as these areas are not regularly cleaned and pose a contamination risk to prepared foods. Store knives on top of prep surfaces. Wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils as needed or at least every 4 hours. Discussed with PIC.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Ceiling tile missing in the kitchen dry storage area. See that tile is replaced by next routine inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open packages of diced ham and sausage crumbles were without date marks in the pizza prep cooler. Packages were opened the day prior and this morning. Date marks were provided.
Except as specified in ¶¶ (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-302. Food thermometer used for taking internal temperatures recently broke. A spare thermometer was located but was unable to be calibrated. The needle was broken and would not adjust correctly when checked with ice point method. New food thermometers will be purchased.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Flats containing canned gravy and pizza sauce were observed on the floor in the pizza kitchen. Crates were provided to store flats up off the floor. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-502.13 Tubes on bulk creamer were not cut at an angle for two of the products. Dispensing tubes were cut to be at an angle. 
Bulk container dispensing tubes shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Box of single service cups was observed on the floor in the back storage area. Crate was provided to store cups up off the floor.
 Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Cabinets beneath the fountain soda machine were cracked and damaged. Provide repairs so cabinets are smooth and easily cleanable.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed no date marking on open gallon milk container in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple Foodborne Illness Risk Factor violations observed during the inspection. Employees appear unaware of safe handling practices or anything related to sanitizing in the kitchen area. Ensure appropriate education is maintained.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

comment:

Warm water and soap should be used and the hands dried so that they do not recontaminate them after cleaning.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

1) The dish machine is barely registering CL sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips (estimated 10 ppm). CL based sanitizers in dish machines are required to be at least 50 ppm CL to be effective. The machine appears to be injecting sanitizer and the sanitizer appears to be not diluted when injected. It is believed that the machine is not metering correctly. Maintenance will be contacted by management for maintenance to be conducted. Until then, the 3 part sink next to the dish machine is being set up with a CL solution to provide effective sanitizing of dishes.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

This is a poor procedure and should cease immediately. Foods should not be held in the temperature danger zone for any reason unless Time-as-Control procedure is in effect. Items were discarded during the inspection to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

This posses a risk of contaminating the food contact surfaces or hand washing location under it. Chemicals should be stored away from these types of areas. Chemicals were moved during the inspection to correct.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:

comment:

 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:

The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.18 Open packages of smoked sausages, maple sausage links, and breakfast Tornados were without date marks in the walk-in cooler. Store manager was unsure as to when the sausages were first opened, but the Tornados were just opened this morning. Sausages were wasted and discarded during inspection. Tornados were kept for breakfast service. If Tornados were not served by the end of breakfast a date mark would be placed on the package.
-Creamers in dispenser were also without date marks. Store Manager noted they were just placed in the dispenser today and have a hold time of 3 days. Date marks are to be placed on the storage compartments where product is located when placed in the dispenser. Manager dated the creamers. **Ensure proper date marking of ready to eat, TCS foods.**
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

Color change for test strips was off the chart. Fresh solution was prepared at 200ppm. Ensure test strips are used to verify sanitizer concentration of 200-400ppm as directed on label instructions. 
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Milk in the upright cooler as you enter into the kitchen from the drive through area is observed without a date marking. PIC was consulted and stated that the container was opened this past Sunday (11/7/21). Education took place and a date tag was made during the inspection to correct.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Meatballs in hot holding well were observed with internal temperatures at 113F-137F. Meatballs in the bottom of the pan were at 135F/above while meatballs stacked higher were below 135F. Meatballs were heated this morning for lunch, and manager stated meatballs reached an internal temperature of 182F prior to service. Meatballs were initially going to be reheated to 165F. Manager decided to start with fresh product and discarded the meatballs in question. All other foods in the hot holding wells were at proper temperature or were in the process of being heated for service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Multiple pans of seafood were thawing at the kitchen prep sink. Cold running water was only in direct contact with one container at a time while other pans of seafood were observed in standing water. All pans that were not directly under cold running water were moved to the walk-in cooler. Best practices for cooling were discussed.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: 3-501.17: (A) Observed open gallons of milk in cooler to not have a date mark.  Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

comment:

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment:

Reference 2-501.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

Upon arrival to inspection, 5-gal bucket of chlorine sanitizer observed empty. Staff replaced the bucket for a new one. Facility does not have test strips for chlorine (see #48). PIC placed call to Ecolab to order new chlorine strips. In the meantime, facility opted to switch from chlorine to quaternary ammonium sanitizer so they are able to test it and verify it is sanitizing. Inspector re-primed machine with quat sanitizer and strips yielded a concentration of 400ppm. COS.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility does not have test strips for chlorine sanitizing dish machine, chlorine was the in-use sanitizer upon inspector arrival. See #16. Facility opted to use quaternary ammonium sanitizer until test strips can be ordered. 

Discussed sanitizing procedures with present staff. Test strips must be on hand at all times for working containers of sanitizers to ensure the concentration is sufficient enough to destroy pathogens. Although the container may be full, a blockage in the lines (for example) could prevent sanitizer from making it onto equipment to be sanitized. Testing the concentration at least once daily via a test strip is the only way to verify sanitizing step is working. 

Follow up issued for test strips. Text/call inspector when received chlorine test strips from Ecolab.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Cheese sauce was observed with an internal temperature of 107F in the steam table. Cheese sauce was placed directly in the steam table for reheating.
