title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Three pans of refried beans with preparation dates of 10/21/21 in the walk-in cooler had internal temperatures of 50F; 48F; and 47F. Refried beans were discarded during inspection. Owner reiterated proper cooling in shallow pans with cook during inspection. Cook noted ice bath was used, but only the surface temperature was monitored using an infrared thermometer. Ensure internal temperatures are monitored during cooling process to verify foods are cooling quickly and properly. 
Cooked TCS foods shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Utilize ice baths to chill smaller portions of foods quickly. Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to monitor cooling TCS foods during the cooling process and ensure foods are reaching temperatures as required for the bench marks of proper cooling.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Three pans of fish were thawing in the basins of the 3 part sink. Pans in the first and third basin had standing water while fish in the middle compartment was under cold running water but not fully submerged (fish was stacked above water line in the pan). Options for thawing were discussed with emphasis on planning ahead and utilizing the walk-in cooler to thaw in advance. Two pans of fish were placed in the walk-in cooler while the remaining portion remained under cold running water. If cold running water will be used, then all the fish in the process of thawing must be completely submerged during the process. 
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

citation_text:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

citation_text:
3-501.16 TCS foods in the 2 door retail cooler had internal temperatures at 46F-52F. Foods included yogurt (48.5F), multiple packages of tofu (46.5F-51.5F), soy puffs (50F), and quail eggs (52F). title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Two door retail cooler was holding above 45F. Digital thermostat was observed at 46F. Inspector placed thermometers in the cooler and observed temperatures at 48F-50F. Owner noted the cooler digital thermostat was reading at 46F for the last couple of weeks and that service was needed. All TCS foods were discarded during inspection (see #22 for details). Owner put a call in for service. Owner was advised the cooler cold not be used for storage of any TCS food until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. Owner stated he understood. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Boxes of frozen fish that needed to be separated and portioned prior to being placed in retail freezers were sitting on the floor at room temperate. Owner noted the fish was previously stored in the walk-in freezer but removed to allow fish to thaw slightly so products could be easily separated during portioning. Proper thawing was discussed, and boxes of fish were placed in the walk-in cooler.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Person in charge is not a certified food manager. Priority violations were observed for hot holding, handwashing, proper sanitizing during ware washing, and potential cross contamination during food storage. Follow-up inspection will be conducted to revisit corrective actions. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Certified food manager was not present at the time of inspection. Manager certifications posted in the facility belong to people that are not the full time manager that runs day to day operations. Manger running the daily operations has a food handler certification but needs to take a course and obtain their food manager certification (see general comments for additional information).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreement was not available for one of the workers at the time of inspection. Manager stated the individual was his son who was not a full time employee. Manager was advised all persons working in the facility regardless of full time status need to be informed of employee health policy and sign a reporting agreement. Manager’s son signed a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverage was stored on top of the ice bin at the soda machine. Beverage was removed from the area. Provide a proper storage location away from food prep and storage for personal drinks.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee began to wash hands without proper technique and shut off the faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and hands were re-washed with proper technique prior to continuing with food prep.
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager was eating upon arrival of inspector and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare an order. Another employee also began to put on gloves without first washing their hands. 
-An employee entered the building and did not wash hands prior to opening a bag of rice to place in the bulk storage bin. This same employee later went from the dish washing area to the food prep area to assist the manager and did not wash hands until asked to do so.
Handwashing between tasks was discussed with manager. Ensure employees are properly washing their hands between tasks and prior to working with food.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, upon entering the building, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee began to wash hands at the 3 part sink. Employee was directed on proper handwashing at designated handsinks. Employee washed hands at the front handwashing sink prior to continuing with next task.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Front handsink was blocked with table holding tortilla shells and chips. The table was moved to allow for access to the front handsink. Ensure handsinks are always accessible.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Do not place equipment in front of the handwashing sinks.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

6-301.11 Hand soap dispenser in the restroom was empty. Manager noted they do not have a key to change the soap in the dispenser. Aramark happened to arrive during inspection and was able to provide soap for the dispenser. Manager was advised to maintain additional bottles of handwashing soap at the facility to ensure soap is always available if they are unable to change soap in the dispenser between services. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Plastic grocery bags were being used for storage of churros in the reach-in freezer and to line pans holding rice, steak, and beef in the steam table. Manager was advised to cease this practice. Plastic grocery bags are not food grade and not intended for storage of foods. Churros were placed in a ziplock bag, and new pans were provided for storage of foods at the steam table. 
-White cloth towel was observed on top of food in the cooler beneath the grill. Cloth towel was removed. Manager was advised to use food grade items for covering foods in the coolers. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-702.11 Utensils from the grill area were washed and rinsed and then taken back to the grill. Manager was advised the utensils needed to be sanitized. Utensils were placed in bleach solution at 200ppm at the 3 part sink to allow for proper sanitization prior to use.
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-703.11 Employee quickly dunked a pan in the bleach solution at the 3 part sink during ware washing. Employee was advised of immersion in bleach solution for 10 seconds prior to removing to air dry for use. Pan was placed back in bleach solution to allow for proper contact tie.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 10 seconds for chlorine (bleach) sanitizing solutions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Rice, refried beans, steak, and ground beef in the steam table had internal temperatures at 108F-131F. Manager noted foods were reheated on the grill prior to hot holding earlier this morning. The steam table was not turned on in advance to allow for proper hot holding. Rice was replaced with fresh product, but all other foods were reheated on the grill. The steam table was turned on at the highest setting to allow for proper hot holding. Ensure the steam table is turned on in advance and able to hold foods at 135F/above prior to placing foods in the steam table for hot holding. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Three gallon size ziplock bags of chicken were observed in a pan on the chest freezer. Chicken appeared to be removed from the freezer and were in the process of thawing. Surface temperatures were observed at 31F-59F, and internal temperatures were at 33F-42F. Chicken was placed in the walk-in cooler at request of inspector. Cease the practice of thawing foods at room temperature. 
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC began drying hands with dispensed paper towels, shut off the manual faucet with paper towels, and then finished drying hands with the same paper towels. Proper technique was discussed. Ensure hands are thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed after using paper towels to shut off the faucet. Use of forearm or elbow to shut off the faucet is also acceptable.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

citation_text:

PIC described the process for cleaning up should someone become ill in the lobby and did not mention a step for disinfection. PIC noted a body fluid cleanup kit is available through the company to be used on-site and might have a disinfecting product that comes with it, but a kit was not present at the time of inspection. In the meantime, a copy of norovirus disinfection policy was provided. Maxim Lemon Detergent Disinfectant (used to inhibit mildew on carpeting/seats) is available for use if needed and is a virucide to norovirus. A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At this time, the facility is a Class-II facility. This requires a certified food protection manager (CFPM) to be present at all times. On arrival, no CFPM was at the facility. A CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct. Education took place with them in relation to the code requirements. A copy of the current available classes was given to the PIC as well as a copy of the pizza variance request paperwork.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

No reporting agreements or similar verification are available at the facility on inspector’s request. Education took place and the reporting agreements distributed by SCDPH were given to the PIC during the inspection. They are instructed to have employees sign and maintain them at the facility.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

The biohazard kit at the facility is visibly degraded in the bag and without the disinfectant. The hand out distributed by SCDPH was given to the facility and they already have bleach at the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The bars of the rack that pizzas are cooked on is observed with a thick accumulation of grease. The rack was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The scoop used for ice is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Education took place and the scoop was moved during the inspection to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

Observed employee use the three compartment sink to wash hands. Education provided. Ensure staff use a dedicated hand washing sink only to wash hands. Ensure staff do not “rinse” hands in between tasks. A complete hand washing step must occur between tasks or if hands become soiled or contaminated. COS.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Upon inspector arrival, a garbage can was observed placed in front of the hand sink. Inspector moved trash can. Ensure staff do not block the handwashing sinks at any time with garbage cans or other equipment.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Test strips not present at Halfway House. Ensure test strips are permanently kept at this location so staff on the golf course can adequately measure sanitizer concentrations throughout the day. COS. Manager brought extra quat test strips from the main house to the Halfway House.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). 

Dish machine in downstairs bar reading at 0 ppm after several attempts by inspector and staff to prime machine and correct. PIC placed a service call to Ecolab during inspection and are expected to arrive the next business day, inspector will follow up by follow up date. In the meantime bartenders are to bring dishes to the main kitchen for washing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. 

Back door to kitchen, by dry storage, is not sealed completely and sunlight is visible through the cracks. Ensure door sweeps/framing are replaced so pests do not have access to kitchen.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. 
The following areas have dust accumulated in the kitchen: 
-Fans in the walk-in cooler
-Racks in back hallway by walk-in units storing baking equipment. 
-Racks in the dish area

Ensure these areas are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation. Discussed with PIC, staff began to pull racks for cleaning during inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Several ceiling tiles in the kitchen, mainly in hallway leading to both walk-in units and dry storage, show signs of wear and tear and are buckling in some places. Ensure tiles are replaced as needed and are made of smooth and easily cleanable materials. Additionally, grates in the ceiling leading to ductwork are dusty to sight and touch, ensure these are cleaned when tiles are replaced as well.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed fryer cart to have large accumulation of dust, debris, and grease. Ensure routine cleaning of fryer cart to hinder debris and grime - wash, rinse, sanitize. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/26/21.

Several other areas are in need of cleaning due to debris build up including:
1. Grating under the prep table in the back.
2. Fan grates on top of ice machine in the back.
3. Hoods above fryers are in need of cleaning. Professional service is due soon. Facility may wash, rinse, sanitize between services or increase professional services from 2 to 3 times a year.
4. Basket attached to wall in front of fryers has accumulation of grease.
5. Cheese sauce dispenser has grime and food debris on the machine - wash, rinse, sanitize.

Ensure routine cleaning of facility - wash, rinse, sanitize as needed to hinder debris and grime accumulation.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19: Facility has a time as control policy for their food items along the prep line. This time as control is monitored by time records on a magnetic strip. Upon start of inspection, these times had not been updated. When this was brought up to the manager, they immediately corrected the violation. Ensure that time as control records are up to date when the product is placed on the prep line. 
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: The walk-in cooler was observed to not have items date marked. Ensure date marking is accomplished to ensure the integrity of the food is not compromised. This involves a 7 day life expectancy of the food items where the day of creation/preparation marks day one. For example, if food is prepared on a Sunday, that is day one. Therefore, Saturday would be day 7 and the food item is to be discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.

3-501.17 Portions of deli meats in top of sandwich/salad prep cooler were without date marks. Portions were said to be from a container that was date marked in the walkin cooler. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Cheese sauce was observed cooling in a covered 18qt container in the walkin cooler. The container was approximately half full and observed with surface and internal temperatures at 81F and 120F respectively. Cook who prepared the cheese sauce left around 2:15pm, and cheese sauce prep was the last thing the cook did prior to leaving based on information provided. Time and temperature were not being monitored for cooling cheese sauce. PIC put the container of cheese sauce in an ice bath and added an ice wand to the product to aid in rapid cooling. Ensure proper and rapid chilling of cooling TCS foods.  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.  When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Leftover portions of brown gravy, green beans, and corn were in covered containers cooling in the 3 door cooler. Internal temperatures were observed at 104F-109F for green beans, 95F-105F for corn, and 125F-134F for brown gravy. Manager noted the cook who was responsible for cooling the foods removed products from hot holding around 1:30pm. Ice baths are typically used to chill cooling foods prior to storing in the cooler. Foods in question were placed on an ice bath around 2:30pm in an attempt to quickly drop temperatures and reach 70F within 2hrs. Brown gravy had an internal temperature of 84F after 3:30pm and was discarded. Corn and green beans and internal temperatures at 68F-70F by 3:30pm and were kept in the ice bath to continue cooling prior to storage.
Ensure adequate ice baths are used and foods are cooled quickly/properly prior to storing items covered in the cooler. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 During handwashing, an employee was observed using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet and then finished drying hands with the paper towels that were just used to shut off the faucet. Employee as advised hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. If additional drying of hands is needed, use fresh paper towels to finish drying hands. 
--Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employees were observed making an effort to use proper handwashing technique for the remainder of inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Cooked pork prepared earlier today was observed in a tub on a cooling rack in the kitchen. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 94F and 102F-119F respectively. Kitchen staff indicated the pork started cooling 2hrs prior to when temperature was checked. Pork was reheated to 180F prior to restarting the cooling process. Ice baths were setup to help chill pork during cooling.  
--Spanish rice cooked earlier today was observed in several plastic containers stacked in the sliding door cooler. Internal temperatures were observed between 72F and 89F, with some portions observed at 80F and 85F. Spanish rice was past the first two hours of cooling time frame based on information provided. Cook time and temperature was not indicated on the cooling log. Rice was placed in the oven to reheat product to 165F prior to hot holding a portion and beginning cooling process again for the remainder.
-A portion of steak in the sliding door cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 86F. Steak was prepared earlier in the day. Cook indicated the steak in question was not needed and discarded it in the trash during the inspection. 
Cooked TCS foods shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Utilize ice baths to chill smaller portions of foods quickly. Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to monitor cooling TCS foods during the cooling process and ensure foods are reaching temperatures as required for the bench marks of proper cooling.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of cooked chicken in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 51F. Cook stated the chicken was heated at lunch time and then some of it was placed back in the walkin cooler. The portion at 51F was discarded during the inspection.
-Quinoa in the top holding area of one of the prep coolers had an internal temperature between 52F-54F. Quinoa was to be used or discarded by the end of operations this evening.
-A portion of white rice in the sliding door cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 51F. Warm Spanish rice in the process of cooling was placed on top of the container of white rice. Owner was advised to monitor temperatures of all foods in the sliding door cooler and use or discard the white rice by the end of operations this evening. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Cheese sauce and black beans were observed sitting out on a prep table upon arrival of inspector. Foods were still observed on the prep table an hour later. Surface temperatures were at 91F-96, while internal temperatures ranged from 131F to 153F. Ice baths were setup to start quick chill process. 
-Chile salsa bajillo (full 8qt container) and salsa picante (full 6qt container) prepared earlier in the day were in the walkin cooler and observed with internal temperatures at 112F and 89F respectively. Ice baths were setup to help cool sauces quicker.
Cooling smaller portions in ice baths and monitoring the temperature of cooling foods were discussed. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee helping in breakfast area used a gloved hand to shut the ringer off on their cell phone and continued stocking food items without changing gloves. Proper glove use was discussed.  
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of quat sanitizer in the kitchen was observed at 0ppm. Product was discarded and replaced with fresh solution from the dispenser in the laundry room. Fresh solution was observed at 400ppm. 
-Quat dispenser in the kitchen was not functioning properly. Dispensed chemical was at 0ppm. Call for service was made. Ensure all employees know to prepare quat solutions using the dispenser in the laundry room until the dispenser in the kitchen is repaired and able to dispense product at proper concentration (effective range 150-400ppm). 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-502.11 Temperature gauge on the dish machine was not functioning properly at the time of inspection. The gauge was not moving beyond 150F during a ware washing cycle. Call for service to get the temperature gauge repaired. 
Water temperature measuring devices shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Multiple priority violations were observed during the inspection today. Owner was not present at the time of inspection. Follow-up inspection will be conducted in 10 days to discuss violations and plans for permanent corrective actions.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Ice was packaged on-site to sell for the purpose of consumption. Adequate facilities are not currently present to allow for this practice (see #10), and hands could not have been properly washed prior to packaging ice due to the lack of a handwashing sink in the dispensing area. Cease the practice of packaging ice on-site until adequate facilities are available.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-204.11 Facility is not adequately equipped with a handwashing sink in the back of the facility where ice machine is located. A handwashing sink must be provided if owner wishes to sell ice packaged on-site. Cease the practice of selling cups of ice until adequate facilities are available for handwashing in the dispensing area.
A handwashing sink shall be located to allow convenient use by employees in food preparation, food dispensing, and warewashing areas.

title: Food obtained from approved source
citation_text:
3-201.11 Styrofoam cups with ice were observed in a small freezer available for purchase. Proper facilities are not currently present to allow for retail sale of ice for consumption. All cups of ice were removed from the freezer and discarded in the dumpster outside with other trash. Cease the practice of packaging ice on-site for the purposes of consumption. 
This violation was corrected immediately, but a follow-up inspection will be conducted in 10 days to discuss the situation with the owner due to the fact that this is a repeat violation that was also observed during the routine inspection in 2018. 
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with law.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice scoop is unable to be properly cleaned due to lack of adequate facilities (see #48). Cease the practice of using the ice scoop for packaging ice to be sold for the purposes of consumption. Based on the available facilities, the ice scoop may only be used for scooping ice into containers that will be used to chill bottled and canned beverages. Any other use is prohibited. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety food (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred. 

Pink mold accumulation was observed on the lower edge of the metal baffle inside the ice machine. Discoloration (possibly rust) was also observed on the ceiling inside the ice machine. Clean the ice machine as needed, and maintain it clean. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed compartments such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-702.11 Ice scoop is unable to be properly sanitized due to the lack of adequate facilities (see #48). Cease the practice of using the ice scoop for packaging ice to be sold for the purposes of consumption. Based on the available facilities, the ice scoop may only be used for scooping ice into containers that will be used to chill bottled and canned beverages. Any other use is prohibited. 
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-204.112 Thermometer was not present in the small freezer holding Hot Pockets and White Castle burgers. Provide a thermometer, and ensure functioning thermometers are available in all cold holding units used for the storage of TCS foods.
Cold holding equipment used for TCS food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-301.12 Facility is not adequately equipped with a 3 compartment sink to allow for manual wash, rinse, and sanitize of ice scoop. A 3 part sink with compartments large enough for submersion of equipment and utensils must be provided if owner wishes to sell ice packaged on-site. Cease the practice of selling cups of ice until adequate facilities are available for manual ware washing. 
A sink with at least 3 compartments shall be provided for manually washing, rinsing, and sanitizing equipment and utensils. Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of the largest equipment and utensils.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following general surfaces were soiled:
1. top of display case used for storage of personal microwave and toaster oven (dust and debris); 
2. inside toaster oven and microwave available for personal use (food debris);
3. outer surface of beer cooler doors along bottom gasket (mold); and
4. shelving inside beer cooler (mold).
Clean the aforementioned surfaces daily/as needed.    
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-501.18 Toilet basin and handwashing sink in the restroom were soiled. Ensure cleaning of restroom fixtures as needed to eliminate buildup.
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-302.11 Toilet tissue was not available in the restroom. Toilet tissue was provided. 
A supply of toilet tissue shall be available at each toilet.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Floors were soiled with dust and general debris under the ice machine and under retail shelving. Clean the floors throughout as needed, and maintain them clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 Ceiling tiles in restroom have evidence of water damage and are acoustic. Replace the ceiling tiles in the restroom with smooth, cleanable tiles. 
-Floors were in disrepair in the following areas:
1. in the restroom - damage in front of the door by the threshold; 
2. in front of the tobacco case - damaged tiles with exposed subfloor; and
3. in front of and under the ice machine - damaged tiles with exposed subfloor and warped tiles from moisture.
Provide proper repairs to flooring throughout the facility so it is smooth and easily cleanable. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.16 Damp mop was stored in the mop bucket. Store mop so it dries properly between uses. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: 5-205.11: (A) Observed food debris in basin of kitchen hand washing sink.  Employee removed food debris.  A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the can opener to be soiled with built up food debris. Ensure the can opener is cleaned routinely so it is maintained clean. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. The can opener was pulled for cleaning during the inspection.  Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Observed the dish machine in the kitchen to have a chlorine concentration of 0ppm. The dish machine must maintain a chlorine concentration between 50ppm and 200ppm. Ecolab was called and arrived to fix the dish machine during the inspection to correct the violation. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking on sauces located in the double door cooler were observed to be past the 7 day date marking. They were dated 5-28. Food should not exceed the 7 day date marking limit. Food was discarded during the inspection to correct the violation. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: Observed the fan in the walk in cooler to have an accumulation of dust on it. Ensure the fan is cleaned so dust does not blow on food stored in the walk in cooler. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: No written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided policy. Keep on file for reference when needed. Ref. 2-501.111 [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Employees did not use a barrier to turn faucet off after washing hands. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and provided education. Use a barrier to prevent recontamination of hands after washing. Ref. 2-301.12 [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Items in the 2 door cooler were without date-markings (pico, soups, gravy, among other items). CORRECTED-- PIC knew foods were prepared yesterday. PIC labeled appropriate dates. Ref. 3-501.17 [P]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Cardboard boxes (containing sprinkles, baking powder, etc) stored on the floor under counters in the kitchen and under shelving in the dry storage. Store food items at least 6 inches off the floor. Ref. 3-305.11 [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: Knife stored in the gap between 2 counters near the lunch station. CORRECTED-- Knife removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Store utensils in clean locations. Ref. 3-304.12 [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
1) Caulk around the 3 compartment sink is dirty. Clean or replace. 
2) Coving/trim around the dish area is pulling away from the wall or missing in places. Replace/repair as needed.
3) Two ceiling tiles missing over the 3 compartment sink. Replace tiles.
Ref. 6-501.11 [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: There is an excessive amount of dust accumulation on the shelving where the pizza boxes are being stored. Ensure these shelves are cleaned to reduce the dust accumulation and at a frequency to prevent the accumulation in the future.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: Observed the soda nozzles that are used more often to be soiled with gunky soda build up. Ensure that soda nozzles are routinely cleaned so they are maintained clean to sight and touch. The manager stated the soda nozzles would be cleaned today to correct the violation. 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: Observed the area behind the ice dispenser and the areas behind the soda nozzles to have old soda debris and pink mildew build up. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned routinely to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed salad dressing bottles within the salad basin of the top salad prep cooler. Cease practice. Keep salad dressing out of the loose leaf lettuce and within the bottom of the prep cooler. COS. 

Observed chopped chicken in a bowl within the hot holding crock pot resting on top of the hot held chicken. Cease practice. Do not place bowls on RTE food items like hot held chicken. COS.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed knife store in between prep coolers. Cease practice. Knife is a food-contact surface and should be prevented from cross contamination. Keep knives in clean areas. COS.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed chest freezer in kitchen to have accumulation of frost. De-frost the chest freezer to hinder frost accumulation. Clean before next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed caulking to be missing around the dish area and 3 compartment sink area. No caulk between walls and dish machine/3 compartment sink. Caulk before next routine inspection.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed large metal shelving unit used to hold dried cooking utensils (in front of men’s employee bathroom) to have large accumulation of chipped paint and rust. Replace this shelving unit before next routine inspection and/or reseal with paint.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces in need of cleaning due to dust and debris:
1. Walk-in cooler fans have accumulation of dust.
2. Spray nozzle of 3 dish machine has accumulation of grime and food debris on top of handle area.
3. Shelving unit of clean dish ware near the walk-in coolers is dusty.

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces before next routine inspection. These items were noted in the general comments of the last routine inspection on 2/4/20.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repair due to no longer being smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulking at dish machine in front of spray nozzle - in need of caulking.
2. Mop utility sink in need of caulking around top where sink and wall meet.
3. Duct tape attached to handle of walk-in cooler #2 (where milk and cooled items were being held). Cease practice. Repair so smooth and easily cleanable.

Ensure all repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

(REPEAT) Observed no heat test strips and/or maximum registering thermometer for the heated dish machine. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/31/20. Inspector will follow-up on 6/18/21.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: 5-205.11: (A) Observed food residue in handwashing sink behind fudge station, indicating that sink is being used as a dump sink.  A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13: Observed food residue present on several surfaces of the soft serv ice cream machine.  NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: REPEAT #1: PIC does not have access to employee reporting agreements for inspector to review. Ensure that staff are educated on employee health and keep signed reporting agreements on file for review during health inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11 The Person in Charge shall ensure that (O) Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). [Pf]

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: REPEAT #1: PIC does not have access to the vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy must be accessible so it may be referred to in case norovirus clean up is needed.
citation_text: 2-501.11 FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
Employee beverages observed on the top shelves of two vertical coolers (bottled sports/energy drinks) and above the back prep counter (energy drink and an uncovered plastic cup). CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and employee. Beverages were removed and discarded. Store employee drinks below/away from food and food prep areas so they don't contaminate foods/food prep areas.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Employee donned gloves without first washing hands. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Educate staff on when to wash hands, including before putting gloves on.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed employee rinse a spatula in the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED-- Discussed with kitchen staff. Utensils washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 compartment sink. Use handsinks only for handwashing.
Observed bar handwashing sink containing a blender pitcher. CORRECTED-- Pitcher removed from handwashing sink. Handwashing sinks must be maintained accessible at all times and not used for any other purpose than handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Items observed stored in the drawer coolers under the grill as follows: Top drawer- raw beef, chicken and fish; Bottom drawer- sliced bell peppers, cauliflower, and broccoli, chorizo, and raw shrimp. CORRECTED-- Discussed storage order with kitchen staff and re-arranged drawers so that raw animal proteins are stored in the lower drawer.
3-306.13: (A) Raw, unPACKAGED animal FOOD, may not be offered for CONSUMER self-service.  This paragraph does not apply to: (1) CONSUMER self-service of READY-TO-EAT FOODS at buffets or salad bars that serve FOODS such as sushi or raw shellfish; (2) Ready-to-cook individual portions for immediate cooking and consumption on the PREMISES such as CONSUMER-cooked MEATS or CONSUMER-selected ingredients for Mongolian barbecue; or (3) Raw, frozen, shell-on shrimp, or lobster. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: REPEAT #1: No date marking on two opened gallons of milk (one chocolate, one regular), as well as on multiple items in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Foods will be labeled with the dates they were opened or prepared.
citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). [Pf]

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Raw beef observed thawing in one compartment of the prep sink without any thawing technique. CORRECTED-- Beef was still 41F or below. Provided education on thawing methods. Cool running water will be utilized.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
Thermometers not observed in the vertical coolers or the prep cooler. Place thermometers inside each cooler where they will be easily readable.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. [C]

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
Probe thermometer observed to read 40F at room temperature, and 0F when placed in ice water. Calibrate thermometers to accurately measure temperature. 
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Salsas observed in two vertical coolers and walk-in cooler on middle or lower shelves without lids protecting from contamination that may fall from items stored above. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and staff. Lids added where needed.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: REPEAT #1: No sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen during inspection. CORRECTED-- Discussed with staff and PIC. Sanitizer bucket was made to correct concentration. Sanitizer bucket must be prepared at all times of food prep and service.
citation_text: 4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
PIC does not have access to food handler certificates. Ensure certificates are available for review during health inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  [C]

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
REPEAT #2: PIC has not completed allergen awareness training. Complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111: Facility shows active signs of pests still present. Sentinel Pest Control was present 5/25/2021 at 11am. Traps in place and 1 mouse has been caught. Sentinel will return on 6/25/2021. Follow-up is being issued for 7/2/2021 to see continued progress. Facility has been instructed to continue cleaning as the droppings appear in order to better monitor the situation.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was stored incorrectly between use. The mop was found sitting inside the mop sink, which does not allow it to dry properly. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. The mop was moved to an approved position during the inspection. Reference 6-501.16.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to improperly wash hands. After hand washing, a barrier must be used to turn off faucet handle (ex: paper towel). Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following food-contact surfaces and utensils to have debris and no longer clean to sight and touch:
1. Soda nozzle at the bar has mold within the nozzle. The nozzle holder is collecting mold as well.
2. Soda nozzle holder on the opposite side of the bar (customer side) has mold.
3. Ice machine at wait station has mold along the interior baffle. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 9/19/19 and 1/14/20.
4. Can opener was observed to be soiled with debris. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20. 
5. Inside of dish machine was observed to have heavy accumulation of lime and debris. Ensure routine cleaning of the interior of the dish machine. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC - wash, rinse, and sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on the above areas on 6/17/21.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (P)

Observed two large containers of cheese in stainless steel refrigerator at 133 degrees. According to kitchen staff, the food had been in there for 1.5 hours. Method of cooling is inadequate, food is not cooling quickly. This is a repeat violation. Discussed with PIC Ann and kitchen staff. Food must be rapidly cooled from 135 to 70 in first two hours, then 70-41 in the following 4 hours, equaling a 6 hour total cooling process.

Approved cooling methods include: breaking down food into shallow containers, rapidly cooling via an ice bath, or using an ice wand or ice as an ingredient in the food item (if possible, such as soups). Multiple methods may be used simultaneously as well. 
Foods in an active cooling process also may be uncovered to allow heat to escape properly, as long as the food is stored in a way it won't be contaminated by something else. 

Corrective action: food removed from cooler and placed back on stove for a rapid reheat to 165. After heating, both containers of cheese were placed into a deep ice bath. Inspector checked temperature at 15 minute mark, food observed at 135 degrees. At the 30 minute mark, food observed at 110 degrees. At the 45 minute mark, food observed at 90 degrees. After the 1 hour mark, food was placed in the walk-in cooler to continue cooling. Conduct periodic checks of cheese to ensure proper cooling time and temperatures are met.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Process lasted less than 20 seconds. Cook also began drying hands with dispensed paper towels and then shut off the manual faucet prior to fully drying hands. Cook was advised on proper handwashing. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The blade of the can opener in the kitchen is observed soiled. Discussion with the PIC reveals that the can opener is cleaned every couple days. The can opener should be cleaned/ sanitized after becoming soiled. PIC ran the can opener through the dish machine during the inspection to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. The can opener blade and ice machine drop guard are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely so that soil does not accumulate. Blade was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment: 3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.  Both chicken and fish are observed in a sink in the kitchen area thawing without an approved method. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to thaw in an approved method.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: 6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. Multiple (approximately 5-6) flies are observed in the dish area of the facility. Another pair of flies were observed by the fountain drink machine in the server area. PIC is instructed to contact pest control and ensure effective methods are being used to combat pests in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Shelves found to be soiled in the walk in cooler of the establishment. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B). Clean and maintain clean.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
2-102.12: PIC is not a CFM. CFM is not present at the facility today during the inspection. Ensure a CFM is present during all hours of operation. 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-102.11: No employee health documentation was provided. Copies of the health paperwork were left with the facility and will be observed next inspection.

(3) PIC must be able to describe symptoms associated with foodborne disease (17) PIC must be able to explain how PIC and FOOD EMPLOYEES comply with reporting responsibilities.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment:
2-501.11: Facility does not have the proper Norovirus paperwork on file today. A copy was left with the facility.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

comment:
