title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
3-304.14: Observed wet wiping cloths to not be stored inside sanitizer between uses. Wiping cloths were observed on counters, inside a hand sink, and on prep tables. Ensure wiping cloths are properly stored inside sanitizer. 
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-403.11: Observed an employee drink in the dish area and on top of a prep cooler. Ensure employee drinks are stored in a designated area. 
(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC (interim certified dietary manager) at time of inspection did not have proof of a current CFM. PIC noted he took a manager certification at one time but did not have a copy with him. PIC was advised that proof of current manager certification was required and to consider carrying a wallet card with him to provide certification in the future.  
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee prepared a sani-bucket and then proceeded to put clean dishes away without a hand wash in between. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and was observed washing hands as needed between tasks throughout the remainder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.112 Rinse gauge of dish machine was observed reading up to and above 200F during final rinse cycle. Rinse water temperature as it enters the manifold was discussed. PIC called for service during inspection (see general comments for additional information). Ensure adjustments/repairs result in the final rinse at the manifold being not less than 180F and not more than 194F, and the surface temperature at the dish rack during ware washing cycle being at least 160F.
In a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Bottom inside ice scoop holder was soiled with general buildup. Ice scoop holder and scoops were cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection. Ensure ice scoop holder and scoops are cleaned daily/as needed.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in clean, protected location if utensils, such as ice scoops, are used for a non-TCS food.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.13 PIC was unable to provide an irreversible registering temperature indicator. PIC was advised on the need for dish machine test strips or some type of maximum registering thermometer for the purpose of verifying the final rinse temperature at the surface of dishes. PIC contacted supplier during inspection and ordered test strips. (see general comments for additional information).
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Sani-bucket at the front service line had murky water in it. Solution appeared to be left from use during a previous shift. PIC tested the solution to confirm a concentration of 0ppm quat. Proper disposal of waste water after use was discussed. Old sanitizer solution was discarded during the inspection.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of used sanitizer solutions after they are no longer needed.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Package of raw bacon was observed above bottled beverages in the reachin section of the cooler. Labeling for location of raw shell eggs and bacon were observed to be above bottled beverages as the permanent location. PIC was advised raw foods must be stored below ready to eat foods. Package of bacon was moved to bottom shelf of open air cooler to allow for proper storage. Ensure raw bacon and eggs are not stored above bottled beverages or other ready to eat foods available for purchase. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 (REPEAT) Mixing wand of the F'real machine was soiled with buildup of dried on food splash. The area just above the mixing cup was also soiled with stuck on food splash. Ensure the mixing wand and surfaces around it that accumulate food splash are cleaned and sanitized at least up to every 4hrs (not more than 6hrs) after continuous use. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat sanitizer was not dispensing at proper concentration. Product observed around 100ppm, and the effective concentration is 150-400ppm. PIC was advised to call for service and get the dispenser repaired. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda nozzles were observed with varying amounts of mold buildup. Ensure nozzles and area on the machine where they attach are getting properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-702.11 PIC indicated the 3 part sink has not been used for manual ware washing, which means food contact surfaces that need to be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized were not being properly cleaned and sanitized between uses. PIC was advised the 3 part sink is to be setup and used for proper manual ware washing moving forward. 
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
Items that need to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized include, but are not necessarily limited to, the containers and dispensing components of the cappuccino machine and soda nozzles.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of Purell sanitizer had a blue liquid inside that was thought to be window cleaner. Another spray bottle that was labeled as DG window cleaner had a light pink liquid inside. The Purell bottle was for sure improperly labeled. Both solutions were discarded at the time of inspection. Proper labeling of chemicals was discussed.  
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution, etc.) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water were observed on shelving and the ground on display outside the main entrance. PIC was advised bottled water is to be displayed and stored within the building. PIC stated this is common practice for stores in the area. PIC was advised this is a bad practice and needs to cease. Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water are just like any other food item and must be stored properly to protect product from potential contamination.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Single use packets of ketchup, salt, and pepper were stored under the old handsink in the front service area. A leak occurred at some point and the packets were exposed to moisture and general splash. Packaging was soiled, and all packets were discarded in the trash during inspection. 
Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available to be used during hours of operation. A sanitizer solution should always be prepared and available for use.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:

The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit available for use had a 2018 expiration date and had never been removed from foil packaging until today. Obtain new test strips and use them for verifying sanitizer concentration. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.

A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment:
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. (P)
There is an unfinished, vacant unit to this facility next door. The unit is owned by the same person, therefore Domino's has been using it as a dry storage area for excess soda, pizza boxes, and cornmeal. The vacant unit is not a permitted site, has not had a plan review as a food service facility, and has not been subject to inspection by SCDPH, lacks important items such as sealed/finished walls, door sweep to external door, etc.Therefore, food stored here is considered "not from an approved source". Discussed with PIC at time of inspection. The facility must remove excess dry goods from the vacant unit immediately and store back into permitted Domino's by the follow up date. If the facility wishes to utilize the vacant unit for storage, they must obtain a plan review, permit, and inspection prior to doing so.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:

There are small (dead) flies present inside the cornmeal and the outside of the container contains dirt and other debris. Discussed with PIC. Cornmeal was voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
comment:
5-501.15: (A) Receptacles for REFUSE used outside shall be designed and constructed to have tight-fitting lids, doors, or covers. (B) Receptacles for REFUSE shall be installed so debris and insect and rodent attraction are minimized. 
5-501.115: A storage area and enclosure for REFUSE, recyclables, or returnables shall be maintained free of unnecessary items, as specified under § 6-501.114, and clean.

Waste haulers are responsible for emptying the dumpsters, however facility is responsible for maintaining sound condition of storage areas surrounding dumpsters. This may be a potential harborage situation for pests later on. Ensure employees maintain this area free of debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
3-501.17: No date marking was observed in the walk in cooler. Ensure date marking is accomplished to ensure integrity of the food is not compromised. This involves a 7 day life expectancy of the food items where the day of preparation marks day one. For example. if a food is made on Sunday, Sunday is then day one. Therefore Saturday marks day seven and the food items shall be discarded. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Ensure this practice continues in the future for any meat item that is being thawed.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Volunteers were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed with the lead volunteer for the day. PIC was given signage to post at the handsink that specifies the use of a barrier to shut off the faucet once handwashing is completed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow is also acceptable for shutting of the handwashing sink.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

While assisting inspector with inspection of fridge, employee lightly rinsed their hands in the middle of the 3-part sink and shut off faucet with hands. Inspector then advised employee that handwashing should only occur in handwashing sink. Employee then went to hand sink, pumped soap into hands, 3-4 seconds of washing, and then shut off the faucet with bare hands, then dried off hands on cloth rags used in food prep in kitchen. Inspector advised proper handwashing technique includes a 20-second wash, drying hands with a disposable paper towel, and using towel to shut off faucet. Employee rewashed hands for an acceptable time, then used bare hands to shut off faucet again. About a minute or two later, employee then rinsed hands under 3-part sink for a second time. Discussed need to re-train employees on proper handwashing techniques as numerous violations were observed during inspection.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) 

Cheese sauce was heating in a hot holding unit, probed at 53 degrees. Inspector asked employee how long it had been there, they stated about 10 minutes. Employee was unable to tell inspector proper hot holding temperature for cheese sauce. Discussed with PIC reheating practices. Hot holding units, unless specified by the manufacturer, are meant to keep hot food hot, not make cold food hot. TCS foods should be cooked on either stovetop or oven to appropriate temperatures (mentioned above) prior to being placed in hot holding unit. Cheese was moved to a stovetop for a rapid heat.

citation_text:
4-904.11 Forks were observed in the utensil caddy stored with the food contact surface presented out. comment:
2-301.12 Bartender washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and hands were dried with a cloth towel. Proper handwashing was discussed - cease the use of cloth towels for drying hands.  
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

2-301.14 Employee was observed wiping down surfaces and touching general surfaces prior to handling clean dishes at the dish machine. Employee was advised on handwashing prior to handling clean dishes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Ensure hands are washed prior to handling clean equipment and utensils and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands

REPEAT #2: No CFM has completed ANSI-allergen training. Complete online allergen training and keep certificate on file.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed handwashing sink without paper towels. Ensure handwashing stations have all necessary items readily available for use. Corrected. Towels replaced. Reference 6-301.11

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed seal on freezer in bad repair. Ensure all food and non-food contact surfaces are in good repair. Fix seal. Reference 4-501.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed black mold/mildew starting to build up in the ice dispenser of the soda fountain. Ensure this surface is cleaned regularly to maintain clean. Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the soda nozzles to be soiled. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Soda nozzles were pulled for cleaning. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Observed a spatula to be stored under a bread press, which is not a sanitized surface. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The soda gun on the west side of the bar is observed with a pink/red substance on the inner surface. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. The nozzle was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. 1) The hand sink in the server area needs to be sealed to the wall to its side. The wall behind has a sufficient gap so as to be easily cleanable and is not required to be modified at this time. PIC is instructed to caulk prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The hand sink in the kitchen appears to be pulling away from the wall at this time. title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 Server working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Owner stated they ran out of blank reporting agreements for staff to sign. Additional copies were provided. Owner had the employee go over the health policy and sign a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Server was observed washing hands multiple times without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to paper towels being dispensed to dry hands. Poster demonstrating proper technique was provided for reference. Owner was advised to educate employee on proper handwashing technique. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook went back to the kitchen to return to food prep after using the restroom and did not wash hands upon entering the kitchen. Cook just washed his hands in the restroom. However, only air dryers are available in the restrooms. Policy is posted above the handsink by the front counter stating "all employees must rewash hands after leaving the restroom". Cook rewashed his hands at the front handsink prior to returning to food prep.
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. 
Ensure all employees are following the posted policy and rewashing hands after leaving the restroom.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Pitcher was observed in the basin of the front counter handsink. Pitcher was removed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in sani-bucket at front counter was observed at a concentration of ~100ppm chlorine. Product in use was prepared earlier that day, and per label requirements, needs to be at a concentration of 200ppm. Solution was discarded, and fresh solution prepared at concentration of 200ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions.

Quat solution in kitchen sani-bucket was at 0ppm. Solution was prepared earlier in the day and was soiled from use. Solution was discarded, and a fresh solution was prepared at 200ppm quat. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Raw shell eggs in the top holding area of the large prep cooler were stacked above the fill line and observed with surface temperatures at 56F-57F. Internal temperature was 56F-57F for eggs in the top of the container, while an egg further down in the pan was observed with an internal temperature of 44F. Owner noted eggs were just placed in the cooler to refill after lunch service. Top layers of eggs were placed in the bottom of the cooler for cold holding. **Cease the practice of overfilling pans in the top of prep coolers.**

Bag of noodles had an internal temperature of 51F in the top holding area of the large prep cooler. Noodles were located in a pan stacked on top of other pans and not in direct contact with cold air. Noodles were moved to the bottom of the cooler for cold holding. **Cease the practice of stacking pans of TCS foods on top of other pans in the upper storage areas of prep cooler. Foods are less likely to be maintained at 41F/below when pans are stacked in this manner.** 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Fried spring rolls in the bottom holding area of the small prep cooler were observed with surface temperatures above 50F. Owner stated spring rolls were just fried recently. Time and temperature were not being tracked for cooling spring rolls.

Cooked macaroni noodles in the walkin cooler had an internal temperature ranging from 67F to 73F in tub covered in plastic wrap. Cooling process began around 2:30pm based on information provided. A significant amount of noodles were in the tub, and product had ~1hr left for the first 2hrs of the cooling time frame. Noodles were separated out into two smaller portions and left uncovered to speed up the cooling process.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the front ledge of the small prep cooler. Wiping cloth was removed and placed in soiled linen storage area. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-901.11 Server was observed drying a pan with a cloth towel after removing it from the dish machine. Proper ware washing and air drying process were discussed. In a pinch when a pan or utensil is needed immediately after ware washing, use disposable paper towels to dry the item and then discard the paper towels.
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), before contact with food.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-103.11 At least one of the kitchen staff working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Front of house manager had the cook go over the health policy and sign a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Manager also indicated some of the servers hired recently may not have signed copies on file. Manager was advised to ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Sani-buckets at server station and in kitchen prepared using quat solution from the wall mounted chemical dispenser were observed at 0ppm quat. Call for service was made to technician. In the meantime, quat tablets were used to remake sanitizer solutions (200-400ppm). 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

4-602.11 Soda gun at south end of the bar had buildup on the dispensing surface. Surface was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensers and nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Ensure soda guns and nozzles are getting cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed inside microwaves. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure. Ensure microwaves are getting cleaned up to every 24 hours or more frequently if needed.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in alcohol walkin cooler was without a date mark. Milk was likely opened over the weekend, and date mark was provided.
Portions of cole slaw in the alcohol walkin cooler had a date mark of 6/26-7/2. It would appear this was an old batch that was mistakenly left in the cooler, since fresh portions prepared on 7/3 were also observed. Kitchen manager removed the old portions for discard.
Ensure proper date marking of prepared foods and proper discard within 7 days. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111 Half dozen plus flies were observed around the mopsink and employee restroom area. A few flies were also observed around the back door. Flies were eliminated with the use of a fly swatter around the mopsink and back door. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13
citation_text:
6-202.15 The bottom hinge of the back door stopped working properly over the weekend. The door has to be pulled shut or it stays partially open, which is likely contributing to the presence of flies around the back door and the mopsink area. Provide repairs to the back door so it is self closing and closes properly.  
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Personal cleanliness
citation_text:
2-401.13 Cook was observed working between fryers and pizza prep cooler with a bandaged thumb. Single use glove was not worn on top of bandage upon arrival of inspector. Cook began to put on a glove just as inspector advised of glove use when bandages are present on hands while working with food. Ensure single use gloves are always worn over bandages. 
If used, an impermeable cover such as a bandage, finger cot or finger stall located on the wrist, hand or finger of a food employee working with exposed food shall be covered with a single-use glove.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Clean slicing utensils were observed on soiled magnetic knife strips at the pizza prep area. Slicing utensils were removed for cleaning. Magnetic knife strips were cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Ensure magnetic strips are cleaned and sanitized as needed. 
 Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed multiple to-go sauce cups as scoops in top prep coolers (cheese, diced herbs). Cease practice. Scoops should have a handle and be above the top of the food item. Discussed with PIC. COS.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at pizza prep area and dish drying area. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed several areas of facility (pizza prep area and dry dish area) where clean dishware and/or cookware was placed right-side up and thus not in protection from cross-contamination. Discussed flipping dished and pots over so food- and lip- contact surfaces are protected from contamination. This is a repeat violation since the last routine 
inspection on 1/2/20.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple fans. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed fan in cooler storage area (on floor) and two small fans in dry dish area to have accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/2/20.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be drying within the mop bucket. Mops should be hung in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. Discussed procedure with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/2/20.
citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Multiple areas were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable - in need of caulking. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed hand sink at customer bathrom (nearest kitchen) and hand sink near dish machine area to have caulk coming from the wall and sink. Discussed repairs with PIC.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed mold/soil residue present on the ice machine baffle. Additionally, the fan inside the walk in cooler had dust and other debris on it. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Observed the mop stored sitting inside the mop sink during the insepction. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Mop was inverted duirng inspection.  Reference 6-501.16.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was missing from the handsink at the front counter. Owner noted the sign got dirty and was removed. Handwashing sign was provided and posted. Extra signs were provided to replace signage as it becomes soiled and worn over time. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees. Ensure handwashing signage is always maintained at all handsinks.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Fried sweet and sour chicken pieces were cooling in three large plastic tubs in the walkin cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 56F and 71F-73F respectively. Based on information provided the food was cooked at ~11:30am, and cooling began around maybe 12pm. Time and temperature were not being monitored to know when the chicken reached 135F to know exactly when 6hr time frame began. However, owner was given benefit of the doubt that the chicken was possibly still within the first two hours for cooling. Chicken was rotated within tubs and placed in the walkin freezer to help speed up the cooling process. 
Options for rapid chilling were discussed, including placing cooked foods in smaller portions to help chill foods quickly in the walkin freezer prior to combining in larger tubs for storage.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Tubs containing cooked lo mein noodles and fried sweet and sour chicken prepared during previous days of operation were not date marked in the walkin cooler. Both products were made within the last three days. Options for date marking were discussed. Owner was advised on use of the wall calendar hanging up front. Owner intends to begin tracking dates for prepared foods on the calendar for ease in reference. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (such as cooked noodles, eggrolls, fried chicken, etc.) or after original packaging is opened (such as tofu) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked lo mein noodles were cooling in two tubs in the walkin cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were at 65F and 80F-82F respectively. Noodles were cooked within the last hour and a half based on information provided and were still in the first two hours of cooling process. Noodles were stirred and placed in walkin freezer to help speed up the cooling process.
Ensure time and temperature are monitored during cooling process to verify foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.  Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to check temperatures frequently during cooling process.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution in kitchen sani-bucket was observed at 200ppm chlorine, but the water was cloudy and contained food debris. Fresh sanitizer solution was prepared. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. An employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. PIC is instructed to review hand washing procedures with all employees to ensure correct technique.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  1) The area around the mop sink is observed with a black substance around the rim as well as along the bottom section of the pipe over the sink. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean. 2) The shelves over the 3 part sink on the left side are observed with a brown substance that has begun to accumulate drips. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Observed clean spatulas stored wedged behind a hanging rack, which is unable to be cleaned. Spatulas moved to a magnetic strip. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf)  Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely to prevent the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residues and other debris. The blade of the can opener is observed heavily soiled with food residues. The equipment was moved to cleaning during the inspection.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food should be maintained at 41°F, or less. Milk and chicken wings in the stand up cooler next to the walk in cooler are observed with temperatures ranging from 49-50°F. Foods had been stored in the cooler since at least yesterday. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Cottage cheese in the stand up cooler next to the office is without a date mark. Container was marked with Monday's date to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text: 7-102.11  (Pf) Working containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Spray bottles throughout the facility did not have any kind of label to indicate that they contained a chemical. Person in charge labeled the containers as sanitizer.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment: Bowl of ground beef observed cooling on the counter. PIC stated that it began cooling at 1PM. At 3PM, the ground beef was 100F, probed. Discussed cooling practices and benchmarks. Foods must cool from 135F to 70F in two hours, and reach 41F in a total of six hours. CORRECTED- Food was moved to shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: Bowl of ground beef (mentioned in Violation 20) observed cooling on the counter, covered by deli paper without any cooling methods being used to bring food to 70F in 2 hours, or to 41F or below in 6 hours. CORRECTED- Discussed cooling methods with PIC. Food was moved in shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
citation_text: 3-501.15 Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: REPEAT: Observed wooden utensil used to put mustard on buns. Wood is not permitted for food-contact use. Replace utensil with something other than wood. PIC removed the wooden utensil from use.
citation_text: 4-101.17 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B), (C), and (D) of this section, wood and wood wicker may not be used as a FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE. (C)

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.

Observed back exterior door to no longer be solid and tight fitting. Seal is in need of replacement. Discussed repairs with PIC.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0ppm in the front of house sanitizer bucket. 
Discussed with employee and PIC. 
Observed soap suds in the bucket, employee stated the solution was mixed with dish detergent. Discussed that a sanitizer solution may not contain soap as soap deteriorates the bleach in the bucket. Bucket was remade at inspection with only bleach and water to a solution to 200ppm per manufacturer's label.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on roast and pot of pre-boiled potatoes in walk-in cooler. PIC reported the food was prepped yesterday for today's service. Advised PIC to place a label on the items in the cooler and use/discard within 7 days.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination.
Rolled silverware for guests are rolled with eating-end sticking out. Discussed with PIC this practice must change to prevent utensils from contamination. 
Also observed containers of spoons by coffee station with eating end and holding ends mixed interchangeably. Cease this practice. Place spoons in clean containers with eating-end down, so servers may grab and go without potentially contaminating eating side. 
Will follow up on this practice at next routine inspection.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food shall be protected from contamination. Multiple Ready-To-Eat items in the walk in cooler are observed without coverings. PIC is instructed to maintain covers to ensure no contamination of RTE foods takes place.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation. 1) The microwave next to the steam table is observed with soiled surfaces. Clean often enough to prevent accumulation of soil residues. 2) Cardboard is observed under the microwave next to the steam table and to be heavily soiled with grease/oil as well as food debris. The cardboard either needs o be exchanged a maximum of 4 hours after being soiled or replaced with something smooth and easily clean able or removed.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups in the food prep area. Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the pizza prep area and then going back to food preparation. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to ensure that all employees use sealed containers with a straw. Cup was given a lid and straw during the inspection.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Observed cheese to be measured at 108F (probed). Hot holding unit was unplugged. Ensure hot held food remain at or above 135F at all times. Corrected. Food was discarded. Machine was plugged in. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed facility to lack CFPM during inspection. Only one CFPM is available at facility. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all hours of operation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
CFM has not completed allergen awareness training. All CFMs must complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. Keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Manager began drying hands with dispensed paper towels and then shut off the manual faucet prior to fully drying hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. Manager was observed washing hands properly for the remainder of inspection. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. If additional drying of hands is needed, use soiled paper towels to touch the handle of the dispenser to retrieve new paper towels to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open container of hummus in the bottom of the prep cooler was without a date mark. Store manager stated hummus was received as of Tuesday and was confident about the date it was opened. Product was dated and kept for use. Ensure proper date marking of all ready to eat, TCS foods upon opening and prep. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. Proper storage of scoop was discussed. Ice scoop was placed in the container designated for proper storage between uses. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

A) under tea maker in the dining area (dust/general buildup); and
B) prep cooler - inside bottom reach-in section (food debris).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Surface temperatures of foods in the top of the prep cooler were above 50F. Internal temperature of foods in the top holding area ranged from 49F-50F (American cheese slices; front right corner) to 56F (green relish; left side). Foods in the bottom reach-in section were observed with internal temperatures of 55F (gyro chicken; left side), 52F (dressing; middle), and 47F-48F (green relish; right side). A portion of dressing prepared the day prior were discarded. All other foods were opened, removed from the freezer, or prepared fresh this morning around 11am. All TCS foods in the prep cooler were to be used or discarded by 5pm based on information provided.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Prep cooler was not functioning properly and unable to maintain TCS foods at 41F/below. Thermometer inside the bottom reach-in section was reading between 30F-40F but was broken (see #36 for details). Inspector placed stem thermometers in the bottom reach-in section on the left side and right side. Thermometer on the left side was reading between 50F-60F, while thermometer on the right side was reading closer to 50F. Cooler was failing, and a call for service was made. Technician arrived during inspection for service. Freon was added, and the temperature dropped to 40F during service. (see general comments for additional information.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204-112 Thermometers in cold holding units were not reading accurately. The thermometer in the bottom of the prep cooler was reading between 30F-40F and when moved to the chest freezer did not move at all. The thermometer in the chest freezer was reading below -20F and was placed in the bottom of the prep cooler to check the temperature. That thermometer also read between 30F and 40F despite the cooler holding above 50F. Also, a thermometer in the freezer section of the fridge/freezer unit was not working. New thermometers will be purchased for placement in all cold holding units.
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

Observed no food handlers licenses at facility. Discussed in depth with PIC the need for all food handlers to have training, snack bar workers and party attendants. Party attendants serve food during parties with use of single-use gloves and therefore should take the food handlers course. PIC is actively working towards training staff. Inspector will spot check in the future due to the fact that the 2020 inspection has been completed after pre-opening.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 PIC and assistant were in the process of preparing crab rolls upon arrival of inspector. Preparation ceased, and PIC was advised the prep/package process could be finished so items could be placed in the walkin freezer for chilling prior to continuing with inspection. PIC indicated the product was ok sitting out. Several minutes later the internal temperature was observed at 50F. Inspector asked PIC to put crab rolls away in cold holding until prep/package process could be quickly and safely completed. Crab rolls were placed in a covered pan in the walkin cooler for holding. Chilled pans of crab and spicy crab meat had surface temperatures at 42F-43F and internal tempreratures of 39F and were allowed to remain out for use. PIC was advised to monitor temperatures and return pans of crab and other foods to the walkin cooler if internal temperatures are above 41F.
NOTE: When a significant interruption occurs, ensure products are immediately placed back in cold holding and not left in the prep room. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish was observed in the walkin cooler thawing for use. Directions on the packaging states to remove from package and thaw under refrigeration. PIC was advised on proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish. Ensure vacuum packaged frozen fish are removed from the package and thawed in a covered pan under refrigeration.
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, its thawing using cold running water as specified in the 2017 FDA Food Code.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Knife was observed in sanitizer solution located in the sani-bucket. Knife was used wtih sticky rice and placed in the bucket for storage between uses. PIC stated the knife is wiped down with a fresh wiping cloth prior to use. PIC was advised to cease the practice and to leave the knife out in the prep area on a clean surface between uses. Knife may be wiped with a sanitizer solution between uses during prep and needs to be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use along with all preparation surfaces. PIC removed the knife and placed it at the 3 part sink for ware washing.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utnesils shall be stored on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensils and the food-contact  surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

comment: Observed walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer to have inadequate lighting. Lights were either missing or not working. Ensure adequate lighting is present in food areas.

(A) HAND WASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

Reference 5-204.11

citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed a date of 2-17-20 marked on green beans which exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13  (C) Observed a bag of ground beef to be thawing in a sink full of standing water. Ground beef was immediately, voluntarily discarded. 
Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Cook began drying hands with dispensed paper towels and then shut off the manual faucet prior to fully drying hands. Paper towels just used to shut off the faucet were then used to continue drying hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed wiping hands on a dry wiping cloth. Cook washed hands after using the wiping cloth but was advised cloth towels are not to be used for wiping hands for any reason. If hands need to be wiped then they need to be properly washed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

If sanitizer solution is used to wipe stems between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Also, surface where soda nozzles attach to the soda machine were observed with black buildup. Ensure cleaning of this area when nozzles and diffusers are cleaned. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

The other half was placed in the 3 door cooler for storage.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open package of deli turkey was observed without a date mark in the bottom of the small prep cooler. Product was opened over the weekend. Turkey was dated and kept for use.

--Cooked sausage was observed in the 3 door cooler with a prep date of 2/17 and use by date of 2/24. Use by date was 2/23 the day prior. Sausage was discarded.

Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

1)Have Adams treat facility more than once a month until presence is mitigated. Possibly switch up chemicals/traps methods used per their discretion. 
2)Conduct a walk through on inside/outside of building with PCO. Note areas that provide potential access to mice and seal/spackle/treat accordingly. 
3) Establish routine cleaning schedule where larger equipment (dough mixer, fridges, dolly) is moved aside and hard-to-reach corners are deep cleaned. **Excess debris provides an environment for them to thrive. 
4)Place dry good items in sealed totes to prevent pest access, and to make it easy to move inventory around for cleaning.
PIC described some renovations planned in the dish/walk-in area in near future. Ensure this item is addressed when renovations occur.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to touching the handle of paper towel dispenser to retrieve paper towels after handwashing process was completed. Proper technique was discussed with staff, and all employees were observed washing hands with proper technique for the remainder of inspection. 
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet and to dispense paper towels would also be acceptable.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed getting a drink and did not was hands prior to continuing with various tasks, including getting wiping cloths for sani-buckets. Cook noted he was not immediately working with food. However, hands should always be washed after drinking from a personal beverage and prior to continuing with any tasks in the kitchen or service line. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

Equipment in question was placed back in sanitizer to allow for proper sanitization. 
 After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda nozzles and diffusers had varying amounts of buildup. Ensure proper cleaning of nozzles and diffusers as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked noodles were observed in a pan covered with plastic wrap in the far right holding well of the steam table. The holding well was off, and food employee stated the noodles were just cooked and cooled under cold running water within the half hour. Internal temperature was observed at 58F-59F for noodles. Options for rapid chilling were discussed including ice baths and storage in the walkin cooler until ready for use. The plastic wrap was loosened along one edge and product labeled prior to placing in the walkin cooler for storage until ready to be reheated to 165F/above for lunch service. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

4-501.15 & 4-501.110 Dish machine wash temperature did not get to 150F during inspection. After running ~8 to 9 times the wash temperature read at 116F. The final rinse temperature readout showed 192F, and dish machine testers verified final rinse temperature was over 160F. The wash temperature slowly climbed over time and was observed at 129F after consistent use of the machine for well over 30 minutes. A leak in the machine may have caused issues with the circuit board, which was covered on the inner surface of the mechanical panel with a garbage bag. The temperature log showed wash temperatures consistently below 150F. Manager was advised to call for service. In the meantime, the wash step for dishes will occur at the 3 part sink prior to placing items in the dish machine for heat sanitization. 
The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than 150F for a stationary rack, dual temperature machine.
A warewashing machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions.

3-403.11 PIC was in the process of reheating refried beans in the microwave upon arrival of inspector. Temperature was checked with a food thermometer, but the thermometer was positioned on the outer edge of the container. PIC was advised on checking the internal temperature in the center of the product. PIC was then observed moving the food thermometer around in the product from the side into the middle and back to the side of the container. Beans were stirred and placed back in the microwave for additional heating. Refried beans were placed in steam table for hot holding prior to internal temperature reaching 165F/above throughout. Inspector took the internal temperature of refried beans after being placed in the steam table and observed pockets of product below 165F with temperatures in the 140F-150F range. Upon stirring the internal temperature in the middle was observed between 158F-160F. PIC verified the temperature was checked by moving the thermometer around as previously observed.  Beans were placed back in the microwave to finish properly reheating before hot holding for service. PIC stated final reheat temperature was at least 180F prior to placing back in the steam table for hot holding. Proper reheating prior to hot holding was discussed. Ensure all foods are reheated to 165F/above throughout and internal temperature is checked in the thermal center (thickest part of food/middle of the product) prior to placing in the steam table for hot holding. The steam table is intended for hot holding after foods are properly reheated. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly to the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.
