4-501.114  (P) Dish machine is registering at 0 ppm. A strong concentration of 200 ppm is observed coming out of the hose when machine is primed, however no concentration registers on the dishes/dish rack. PIC called service tech to service machine. In the meantime, facility will utilize wash, rinse, sanitize procedure at the 3-part sink. 
**Tech came in to service machine during inspection. Machine was registering at 50ppm at end of inspection. Facility will switch to smaller buckets of sanitizer to maintain concentration.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Shaft for can opener observed heavily soiled with grease and food debris. Clean this area by follow up date.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) small number of roaches observed during inspection. Two roaches observed in/around walls by prep coolers and shelves. One roach observed on light fixture in dish area. See below violation noting non-food contact areas that allow for proliferation of pest presence. Education provided. Keep an eye out for signs of pests. For roaches, inspector observed what looks like ground pepper (roach waste) on hinges of shelves behind prep cooler. Note these "hot spot" areas to Sentinel for additional focused treatment.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  
Soil and grease residue present on multiple surfaces, which may be contributing to pest presence in restaurant. Will follow up on 2/17/2020 to ensure areas have been cleaned. 
Clean the following areas by follow up:
-Walls and shelves by prep cooler. Remove prep cooler from wall, scrub from cieling to base boards and clean shelves holding bread. 
-Wall behind toaster. 
-Warmers underneath toaster. Focus on grease build up on knobs and crevices of the warmer.
-Metal rack next to fryers. Top two racks are clean (PIC reported they are in the process of cleaning it), ensure bottom two racks are cleaned as well.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training not complete by CFMs. Ensure this is completed by next routine inspection.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil and mold build up on the plastic sheets hanging on the walk in cooler entrance. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was stored incorrectly between use. The mop was found sitting in the top of the mop bucket, which does not allow it to dry properly. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. The mop was moved to an approved position during the inspection. Reference 6-501.16.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) An in use wiping cloth was observed stored on a counter across from the oven. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. The cloth was moved to a bucket of sanitizer during the inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-501.11  (C)  Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. 1) (REPEAT) A gap was observed around the mop sink in the utility room. The PIC was instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The caulking around the hand sink in the kitchen is observed cracking and in need of repair. PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) 3) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. The floor in the walk in cooler was observed with some food debris in the corners and along the wall edges. PIC is instructed to keep clean.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Observed hand washing sink in front service area to have a scouring pad inside the basin. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Observed scoop in direct contact with sugar in container located behind fountain soda machine. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Observed cardboard used to line area behind soups.  Replace cardboard with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed two gallons of milk with manufacturer use-by date of January 27. CORRECTED- Milk was voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.17 (B) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time  combinations specified in ¶ (A) of this section and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. (Pf)

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
No CFM present has completed allergen awareness training. All CFMs must complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. A CFM with allergen training must be present at all times of food prep and service.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07 (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. (C)

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Chlorine sanitizer at 10 ppm at the dish machine. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. PIC requested service to address low sanitizer concentration. Employees will use the 3 compartment sink until dish machine is dispensing the correct concentration of sanitizer.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the 2017 FDA Food Code or on the maufacturer's label. (P)

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Popcorn shrimp in the customer hot cart was 116°F (probed). CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were discarded. Other foods in this hot holding unit were observed to be above 135°F.
citation_text: 3-501.16 TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above. (P)

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: In the deli island, prepackaged sushi was 50°F (probed) and a prepackaged hardboiled egg was 45°F (probed). CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were discarded. Other foods in this cold holding unit were observed to be above 41°F. PIC determined that the unit had been in a defrost mode. Foods probed shortly after these temperatures were taken were found to be 41°F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16 TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained (2) At 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employees were observed entering/exiting the walkin cooler and changing gloves without consistent handwashing in between. Discussed washing hands between tasks and glove changes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Food employee did not change gloves after touching the faucet of the prep sink to rinse a cutting board during vegetable prep. Employee continued wearing the same gloves to continue handling vegetables. Proper glove use was discussed. Gloves were discarded prior to employee getting a fresh pair of gloves to continue with food prep. Handwashing between glove changes was also discussed.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack a method to test heat dish machine. Discussed purchasing heat test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer. Inspector will follow-up on 2/14/20.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11  (P)  Ready-to-eat (RTE) foods stored below raw proteins. Store RTE foods above raw proteins so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

Observed several large containers of parmesan cheese within walk-in cooler to be stored below raw proteins (steaks, sausage) that were in lidded containers. Discussed storing RTE cheese above the raw proteins with PIC. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at sanitization buckets within kitchen. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed both sanization buckets within the kitchen to have low quaternary ammonium - 100 ppm each. Discussed routine changing of sanitization with PIC. Corrected - buckets were remade and tested at 300 ppm. COS.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Utensil holder and can opener food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed utensil holder container to be soiled with debris at bottom. Food contact utensils (spoons, spatulas, etc.) are in contact with bottom of container. Observed can opener to have a small accumulation of debris. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. COS.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple foods throughout facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple items throughout facility to lack date marking:
1. Walk-in cooler: milk, orange juice, pasta.
2. Bottom reach-in coolers: ravioli, rigatoni pasta, sauce in shallow metal tray, sour cream, cottage cheese.

Discussed date marking with PIC. Facility actively date marks majority of items throughout facility. Ensure all items are date marked and discarded within 7 days. This is a repeat violation since the last original inspection on 9/10/19. COS.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed several in-use utensils to be storaged incorrectly:
1. Scoops of parmesan cheese within walk-in cooler were not stored in a manner that allowed the handle to be above the top of the food. Corrected scoops and discussed with PIC. COS. 
2. Knife at prep counter was stored beneath the cutting board. Discussed knife storage with PIC. COS.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.11  (C) Tile coving in the toxic substance storage area was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed facility to have a broken tile and coving coming from wall in the toxic substance storage area. Discussed repairs with PIC.
citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

Observed build-up on soda debris near soda lines in back toxic substance storage area. Splatter was observed on walls and tile floors. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text: 6-301.13 (C) Sinks intended for hand washing cannot be used for food preparation/ disposal or utensil cleaning/ storage. On arrival, the hand sink at the north end of the deli area was observed with numerous food debris. The PIC was notified and cleaned the sink to allow for safe and effective hand washing.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Packages of fully cooked bacon were observed in the cooler below and next to packages of raw bacon. Fully cooked product was relocated to another shelf with cooked sausage to allow for storage away from raw foods.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Dairy cooler shelving and surfaces on/around doors were soiled with splash and general buildup in the milk section. Mold was observed on the lower slatted shelving as well. 
-Shelving was soiled with mold and general buildup in the Fresh Food cooler located in the back storage room. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
comment:
5-501.17 Women's restroom was observed without a lid on the garbage can. Men's room had a covered garbage can. The waste receptacles were switched so the covered garbage can was located in the women's room.
A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.
citation_text:
6-501.18 Men's room toilet was observed soiled with general buildup on the outer surfaces between the seat and the floor. Clean all surfaces of restroom plumbing fixtures daily/as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Ventilation covers in the ceilings of both restrooms were coated with dust buildup. This was also noted during the last routine inspection conducted in January 2018. Ensure cleaning as needed, and keep the aforementioned surface clean in both restrooms.
-Floor in both restrooms was soiled with dead bugs around the toilets and along walls. Clean the floor in both restrooms.
-Floor in the hallway between the restrooms was soiled with general debris accumulation under the water fountains where a push broom was stored. Remove debris from the floor after sweeping.
-Floor seam in women's room along the far wall had gaps were debris was accumulating. Clean the debris out of the floor seam and seal the seam to eliminate debris accumulation.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Partially damp mop was observed in a mop bucket in the hallway between the restrooms. Store mops to allow for proper drying between uses. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided new paperwork for facility including requirements for symptomatic employees for reporting (exclusion and restriction) and requirements for diagnosed food service employees. Inspector will follow-up regarding signatures on 2/13/20.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

Observed facility to lack appropriate policy or procedure for Norovirus illness clean-up. Provided paperwork with PIC. COS.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11  (Pf) Food employee dumped liquid foods in the hand sink in the kitchen area. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed employee to dump liquid and ice into front kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC that hand sinks are for hand washing only and items may not be poured into sink. COS.
citation_text:
6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14.

Observed facility to have no hand washing signs at either hand sink, customer bathrooms, and employee bathroom. Provided multiple hand washing signs for facility. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Metal shelving of walk-in coolers (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed metal shelving through out walk-in cooler to have large accumulation of food debris and soil. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 2/13/20.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items through out facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple food items throughout facility to be missing date marking. Bottom prep cooler in back: cottage cheese, sour cream. Walk-in cooler: milk, sliced ham in shallow tray, shreded potatoes (hash browns). Date marking of many items was observed at the beginning of the inspection. Ensure all time/temperature control for safety foods (TCS) are marked with the date of opening and held for no longer than 7 days minimum. This is a repeat violation since the last original inspection on 9/12/19. COS.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the front kitchen prep cooler. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

Observed front kitchen prep cooler to lack a thermometer. Other cold holding units in facility had thermometers. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.

Observed back exterior door to allow access for pests. Seal is no longer solid and tight fitting at bottom. Discussed repairs with PIC.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

Observed multiple food items to not be protected from contamination in various areas throughout the kitchen. 
1. Walk-in freezer: breaded fish was observed to be on a large baking tray without cover.
2. Walk-in cooler: shreded potatoes (hash browns) was observed in large pan without cover. Observed bags of shredded cabbage and carrots to be sitting directly on top of leaf lettuce for salad in the back top prep cooler. Do not store potentially contaminated surfaces in contact with foods. This is a repeat violation since the previous inspection on 9/12/19. 
3. Multiple large dressing bottles within the bottom back prep cooler were observed to have no lids and/or punctured seals with a hole (to pour dressing). Ensure dressing bottles have lids in order to prevent cross-contamination. 
4. Boxes of food are stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Store foods 6" off the floor. This is a repeat violation since the previous inspection on 9/12/19.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

1. Observed a knife at the back prep cooler to be stored in between the two lids on the top where there is visible food debris and soil. Store in-use utensils on clean and sanitized surfaces. COS.
2. Observed sugar scoop to be stored within sugar in back dry storage area. In-use utensils should be stored in a manner that allows for the handle to be above the food item. COS.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed multiple areas of facility where bowls and plates were not covered from protection. Food- and lip-contract surfaces are exposed. Discussed inverting bowls and plates or another method of protection with PIC.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15(A)  (P) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD (RTE) or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. Reference 3-304.15(A).

Observed improper glove use at time of inspection. Gloves were not be changed in between tasks - handling of RTE foods and raw animal foods and/or in-between task changes. Discussed glove changing with PIC. Discussed washing hands in-between glove changes when changing tasks. This is a repeat violation since the last original inspection on 9/12/19. COS.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-501.11 (C) Seals on the cooler door are damaged. Replace the damaged or missing seals so the cooler can hold food at the proper temperature. Reference 4-501.11.

Observed walk-in freezer to have seal coming away from freezer door. Observed seal of mini fridge in front area to be coming away. Replace damaged seals so cooler may hold appropriate temperatures.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack a manner to test the heat level of dish machine. Discussed purchasing heat test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 2/13/20.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple non-food contact surfaces throughout facility. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with debris:
1. Shelving unit of dry rack for dishes.
2. Spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink.
3. Reach-in freezer in kitchen area (bottom shelf - food debris).

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

Observed the bottom back prep cooler to have an accumulation of water pooling at base through out. Discussed repairing prep cooler with PIC.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed multiple mops to be stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops must be hung in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry such as upside down. Discussed with PIC. COS.
citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Multiple areas of facility were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed multiple areas of facility to be no longer smooth or easily cleanable:
1. Caulk at both hand sinks of kitchen were observed to be peeling and coming away from wall and sink. 
2. Edging of wall seal near drying rack (dish machine area) observed to be coming from wall. 
3. Wood seal at 3 compartment sink observed to need re-painted. 

Discussed repairs with PIC.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-303.11 (A, B, C) (C) Lighting in the waslk-in freezer area was found to be insufficient for that area. Light intensity shall be A) at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and other areas during periods of cleaning; B) At least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in areas where food is provided for consumer self-service or where fresh produce or packaged foods are sold or offered for consumption; inside equipment such as reach-in and under-counter refrigeration units; and in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, and equipment and utensil storage, and in restrooms; C) at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) in areas where employees are working with food or working with utensils or equipment where employee safety is a factor. Reference 6-303.11(A, B, C).

Observed walk-in freezer light to not function. Replace the light within walk-in freezer. This is a repeat violation since the last original inspection on 9/12/19. This violation was also noted on the 4/12/19 inspection.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

Observed facility to have expired food handlers licenses. Discussed with PIC that all food handlers must have active training and proof of certificate.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Currently this has not taken place. Handout was given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the previous original inspection on 9/12/19.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the can opener to have an accumulation of food debris around the blade. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. The can opener was pulled to the dish area during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed quat sanitizer in the sani buckets measured at 0 and 100 ppm. Quat Sanitizer must maintain a concentration between 200 and 400 ppm to properly sanitize surfaces. The sani buckets were changed during the inspection.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Observed the scoops in the flour and the sugar to be buried inside the flour and sugar. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. The scoops were moved to an approved location during the inspection. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: No Employee Health documentation for employees provided. All food employees must be aware of responsibility and provide proof. Employee heatlh documentation provided. Ref. 2-102.11 (C)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed accumulation of in handsink. Handwashing sinks must be used for handwashing only. Education provided. Sink will be used for handwashing only. Ref. 5-205.11. Corrected.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed spatula in disrepair. All food contact surfaces must be smooth and easily cleanable. Discard/Repair/Replace equipment. Ref. 4-202.11. Corrected.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) TCS foods should be maintained at 41 degrees or less for proper cold holding. 1) Chicken wings in the salad bar are observed with internal temperature ranging up to 57 degrees. The chicken was prepared at noon and will be discarded by 6 pm today. 2) Sushi in the in the next section of the salad bar (on a separate cooler apparatus) are observed at 45-49 degrees. The sushi was prepared at another store at approximately 11 am and will be discarded by 5 on today.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Milk in the walk in cooler was observed open and without a date mark. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee at service counter was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands properly for the remainder of inspection.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Three plastic containers of roasted potatoes with the prep date of 1/30 were observed with internal temperatures of 57F; 58F; and 47F in the bottom of kitchen cooler 2. All three containers had heavy condensation on inner surfaces of lids when uncovered. Potatoes at 57F and 58F were in larger containers full to the top and stacked together. The other container was smaller and stored by itself adjacent to the larger containers. The cooling process was discussed with cook that made potatoes the day prior. Potatoes were initially cooled on a baking sheet in the walkin cooler, but the temperature was not verified prior to combining in containers and storing in the kitchen cooler. Potatoes in question were discarded. Options for improving upon the cooling process were discussed including using metal pans for storage and rapidly chilling foods to 41F/below prior to combining and covering for long-term storage.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

The cooler itself was said to be in need of potential repairs but appeared to be holding foods below 45F other than the chili in the bottom, which may have been affected by location near the door and by warm potatoes that didn't cool properly from the day prior. Chili was moved to the walkin cooler to chill the product.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Beef is observed in standing water in a sink thawing at room temperature. title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. One employee was observed shutting off the manual faucet without a barrier prior to drying hands. Another employee started to dry his hands, shut off the manual faucet, and then continued to dry his hands with the same paper towels. Also, the shift manager was observed turning off the faucet with a paper towel but did not dry his hands. Hand antiseptic was applied to wet hands prior to drying with paper towels. All three employees were advised as to proper handwashing upon observation of the abovementioned practices. Proper handwasing was later observed. Store manager was advised to re-educate all staff on proper technique. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.

750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM present during spot check. Facility is aware that there must be a certified food manager available during all hours of operation. Discussed with PIC. Paperwork for courses has been left during the 1/13/20 inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

Observed PIC to wash hands improperly: turned off knob of sink before utilizing paper towels. A clean barrier must be used when turning off faucet and after properly washing hands. Discussed with PIC. COS.

citation_text:

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: No employee health documentation was provided. PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Handout has been provided. Additional handout will be provided on follow-up. Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: Observed establishment not able to produce procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Corrected. Handout provided. Additional handout will be provided on follow-up. Reference 2-501.11.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed handwashing sink to have a large accumulation of food debris. Ensure handwashing is used for handwashing only. Corrected. Education provided. Sink will be properly cleaned. Reference 5-205.11.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed raw pork to be placed above raw vegetables. Ensure foods are stored in correct manner to prevent potential cross contamination. Corrected. Pork was placed on bottom shelf. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment: Observed meat to be thawing at room temperature (still frozen, recently began thawing). Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed through a proper method. Corrected. Education provided. Product will be thawed by running water. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment: Observed no thermometer in the D. Cooler (Front). Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Obtain Thermometer Reference 4-204-112.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: Observed a large accumulation of mice droppings throughout the building around food areas. Ensure rodents are not able to harbor inside facility. Remove food sources, water, and shelter for mice. Contact PCO. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed bottoms of bowls being used in Prep Cooler (Top) to be touching foods. Ensure proper storage of foods occur at all times. Reorganize prep cooler to ensure potential contamination is removed. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: PIC stated facility does not have test strips to test Cl- sanitizer. Facility must have measuring device for sanitizer concentration. Obtain test strips. Reference 4-302.14.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed hood vent to have a large accumulation of grease. Ensure hood vent is cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Clean hood vent. Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: Observed personal items to be mixed with foods being served to customers. Ensure personal items are placed in designated area away and below foods for consumers. Reference 6-305.11.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
REPEAT #1: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text: 3-101.11  (P) Peas stored in the walk in cooler have mold growing in the container. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. The container was discarded during the inspection.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Pork is observed thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. The pork was moved during the inspection to correct.

The device will be moved prior to the next routine inspection so as not to posed a threat of contamination to foods in the facility.

comment:

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment: Beans cooling in the freezer were probed to be 103°F (p). PIC stated that beans began cooling 1.5 hours. Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. CORRECTED- Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Additional efforts were made to cool food within the 2 hour time frame.
citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
An opened gallon of whole milk in the Rockstar cooler is not marked with an in-house use-by date. CORRECTED- Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was labeled with the date it was opened. 
3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

Soup, enchilada sauce, and salsa exceed the time limit. Foods were dated 12-26-19 and 1-5-20. CORRECTED- Food was discarded. Ensure foods are not held longer than 7 days after preparation or opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.
