3-301.11 Bowl was observed in peanut storage container. Another proper scoop with a handle was also observed in the peanuts. Bowl was removed for cleaning. Ensure only scoops with proper handles are used when handling ready to eat foods. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw chicken was observed over containers of clean/cut produce in the walkin cooler. Chicken was moved to the other side of the cooler with other raw chicken.
--Egg wash was observed on the shelf above cooked spring rolls in the bottom of the small prep cooler. Egg wash was moved to the bottom of the cooler below spring rolls. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Sweet and sour chicken was observed in the top of the small prep cooler in a pot held within another pan sitting on the top edge of pans in the designated holding area. Chicken had an internal temperature of 52F and was moved to the top of the cooler for use during lunch. Chicken was discarded. Owner was advised to cease the practice of stacking pans and containers of food in the top holding areas of coolers. Products that are stacked and not in the holding compartment in direct contact with cold air are less likely to be maintained at 41F/below, especially with frequent opening and closing of cooler lids during busy service times.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle hanging on the bottom of the dish machine was without a label. Owner provided proper label during inspection.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish that were received as frozen product were observed thawing in the bottom of the large prep cooler. Labeling on package states to remove fish from packaging prior to thawing under refrigeration. Proper thawing of frozen fish in vacuum packaging was discussed. Owner stated the fish was frozen solid and unable to be removed from packaging when first placed in the bottom of the cooler for thawing. Owner was advised that packages need to be at minimum cut open prior to beginning the thawing process. 
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the small prep cooler. Proper storage of wiping cloths was discussed, and wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen bag. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) sides and underneath equipment on cook line - between wok and grill, table holding grill, etc. (grease/food debris); and
B) . 2 door freezer - bottom inside and front grate with food splash and debris.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-305.11 Purses and jackets were observed on dry storage shelving up front on top of and next to cans of soda and boxes of single service items. Proper storage of personal items was discussed. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Upon arrival for the inspection, the hand sink was blocked by a tub. The tub was moved during the inspection. No items can be placed inside the hand sink. The hand sink should only be used for hand washing only.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training to cover all shifts.
citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. (C)

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Gravy is 130°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. CORRECTED- PIC turned hot holding unit to HIGH to heat gravy to appropriate hot holding temperature.
citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57oC (135oF) or above. (P)

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
Chlorine test strips are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Inspector will follow up on 12/30/2019.
4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

No sanitizer solution observed during inspection. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Made sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Keep a sanitizer bucket on hand during all times of food prep and service.
citation_text: 4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. (C)

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
PIC at time of inspection has not completed food handler training. 
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employeed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain ANSI-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. (C)

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverage in an uncovered Styrofoam cup was observed on the lower shelf beneath the grill. Manager discarded the beverage. Ensure proper storage of personal beverages.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

Bar manager was chewing gum. Manager discarded gum at request of inspector. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Server was observed washing hands without proper technique in the kitchen. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper technique was discussed. 

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival inspector observed knives in the kitchen handsink and a crate with a working supply of lettuce on ice was in front of the handsink. Knives were placed in dish area and crate was moved to allow access to the handsink. Proper use and accessibility of handsinks were discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Two of the three food thermometers available for use in the kitchen had varying amounts of grease/food debris stuck on the stem. Thermometers were cleaned during inspection. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer are used to wipe stems between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of eggroll sauce were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 70F-75F on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Portions of salsa and sour cream in the same area were also at 70F. Portions were discarded. 
--Pitchers of dressings were out on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Ranch and blue cheese dressings were observed with internal temperatures of 57F and 76F respectively. All pitchers of dressing that were out in the salad area were discarded. A time control policy was established for working supplies of dressings/sauces held at room temperature during lunch and dinner service. 
--Working supply of lettuce stored in a stock pot on ice had surface temperatures at 46F-51F and internal temperatures of 46F-48F. Cold holding was discussed with emphasis on using a larger container for the ice bath to allow for submersion during storage. Portion of lettuce was placed in the walkin cooler for storage. 
--Pans containing portions of Italian beef, chicken wings, raw chicken strips, raw stuffed chicken, and eggrolls were held in a pan that was sitting within another pan containing ice. This is a new practice that started recently for storage of working supplies of these foods during lunch and dinner service. Internal temperatures were observed at 46F-59F depending on how much product was present and how foods were stocked in pans. All foods were placed out for service at 11:45am and were to be used or discarded by 5:45pm since foods were holding below 70F. A time control policy was established for these foods (see general comments). 
--TCS foods in the salad cooler were observed with temperatures at 52F-53F. Diced ham and turkey was checked in the top holding area and cottage cheese was checked in the bottom. Ice buildup was observed in the bottom of he unit (see #33). All TCS foods were discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Hanging thermometer in salad cooler was reading around 50F. All foods in the top and bottom were observed at temperatures above 50F. Ice accumulation was observed on the back wall in the bottom of the unit. Cooler was taken out of service. Cooler will be repaired or replaced. Do not use the cooler for long term storage of TCS foods. Use time control for working supplies of foods during service (serve/discard within 4-6hrs based on temperature during use - see time control policy for details). 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers checked with ice water were observed reading above 34F. Thermometers were calibrated to 32F during inspection. Owner also purchased additional thermometers for use. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Personal cleanliness
citation_text:
2-303.11 Employee doing food prep was observed wearing a large watch. Watch was removed from wrist upon request of inspector.
Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing food, food employees may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 Insulation and plumbing inside the wall were exposed under the kitchen 3 part sink. Options for repairs were discussed with the owner.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in food repair.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Kitchen manager with allergen awareness training had to leave and none of the other staff had proof of a current allergen certification. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM present at facility during inspection. CFM at facility is on sick leave and the license has expired while on leave. Provided additional paperwork to PIC regarding CFM license training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink and within sanitization bucket. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed 0 ppm in both the 3 compartment sink, as well as the sanitization bucket in kitchen. Discussed with PIC that all sanitization with quaternary ammonium must be between 200 and 400 ppm. EcoLab was called during inspection to repair sanitization of 3 compartment sink. COS. 

(REPEAT) 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 0 ppm chlorine concentration and 120°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed dish machine to have 0 ppm sanitization level of chlorine bleach. EcoLab was called during inspection in order to service dish machine and repair proper sanitization level. Dish machine is in need of new parts and required to be ordered and serviced. Temporary procedure created to utilize dish machine to wash and rinse as the heat level is maintaining correctly, then utilize the quat at 3 compartment sink for at least 90 seconds submerged. Inspector will spot check dish machine on 12/26/2019. This is a repeat violation since last routine inspection.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Fan within kitchen is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed fans within kitchen to have large accumulation of dust and debris. Discussed routine cleaning of fans with PIC. COS.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

Observed multiple boxes of single-use utensils (protected within cabinents under service area) to have handles not aligned in same direction in order to hinder cross-contamination when reaching for utensils. Discussed with PIC.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
1) 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed microwave in buffet area is soiled with food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

2) 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with black mold. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed food debris on the shelves of dry storage rack. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Tub of somosas was uncovered in the walkin freezer. 
Pan of butter was observed uncovered on the lower shelf of a table on the cook line. Surfaces above and around the butter were soiled with splash and general buildup. Butter was moved to the bottom of the prep cooler.
Ensure foods are covered during long-term storage. Also cover pans of food between lunch and dinner service and store foods in areas that are clean.
--Bowl with hard boiled eggs was observed sitting on top of cooked cauliflower uncovered in the bottom of the prep cooler. Provide a barrier between containers when stacking foods.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Tongs soiled from use during morning prep were observed hanging from the handle of an oven. Tongs were taken to dish area for ware washing. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

Mold was observed along the lower edge of the metal baffle inside the ice machine. Some mold buildup was starting to accumulate on the ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Manager noted the person from whom the machine is leased comes in every few months for a full service cleaning. In between those services, cleaning and sanitizing of surfaces that can be reached by staff should occur.
Enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
 
Fire suppression system over cooking equipment had buildup of grease and dust, especially over areas where significant amounts of cooking occurs. Company that cleans the hood system typically steam cleans the surfaces of the fire suppression system also. Between 6 months services, chunky buildup needs to be wiped off of the fire suppression system located over the cooking equipment.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Ceiling inside the microwave was soiled with dried on food splash. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Chicken that was removed from original packaging and cleaned was observed in plastic grocery sacks in the walkin freezer. Although the sack is a single service article it is not intended for food storage in direct contact with unpackaged or prepared foods. Use only food grade containers and bags, such as plastic food storage bags, for storage of unpackaged and prepared foods. 

Open bags of lentils were observed in tupperware containers of unpackaged lentils. The outer surface of packaging was in direct contact with the unpackaged lentils. Store open bags of lentils in sealed ziplock bags or containers of their own and cease the practice of putting open bags of dry goods in containers with unpackaged foods. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Clean equipment was observed on shelving that was soiled with general buildup above the 3 part sink and the handsink in the kitchen. Clean shelving used for storage of clean equipment and maintain it clean to protect cleaned and sanitized equipment from potential contamination. 
--Silver tongs used with water were observed in soiled storage container with food contact surfaces extended up out of the container. Container and tongs were taken to dish area for ware washing. Store cleaned/sanitized tongs with handles extended out of containers. Clean the storage containers for utensils daily/as needed and maintain them clean.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.
Sanitized utensils shall be handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Both hot and cold water at the left automatic faucet in the women's room ran for less than 5 seconds when dispensed. 
--Water filter for the ice machine had a leak. Manager stated the company that provides service for the water filtration system provided service in October. A call for additional service will be made regarding the leaking water filter. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Grout was worn down along the floor to wall juncture in the dish area along the wall where the dirty dish drain board is located. Accumulation of moisture and debris was observed in the area. 
--Floor drain and cover were soiled with buildup of food debris by the back prep table adjacent to the handsink and ice machine. Clean the floor drain and cover. 
--Wall and attached plumbing behind the ice machine were soiled with dust buildup. Clean the wall and attached plumbing.
--Handsink in back prep area by the ice machine had grimy buildup in the basin and chunky buildup on the handles. Manager noted that handsink is not used as often as the handsink at the other end of the kitchen. Regardless, the handsink is to be properly stocked, accessible and maintained clean.
Clean the handsink and all related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain it clean.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text:
6-501.114 Storage containers with unused equipment were observed in the back prep area. The unused equipment and the storage tubs were heavily soiled with debris accumulation. One container on the lower shelf beneath the 2 part sink was said to have some utensils that are sometimes used. All storage containers and items were removed from the area. Any unused and no longer needed items need to be removed from the premise. All other items need to be cleaned and sanitized and stored in a clean covered storage container. 
The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.06 Proof of current food handler certifications were not available for staff. Ensure copies of all food handler certifications are available at the next routine inspection.
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner and all staff that were certified food managers still have not completed the food manager certification. Owner stated re-certification is scheduled to occur as of January. Additional information for locations to obtain certification, including an online process, were also provided.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Styrofoam cup of orange juice was observed in the server room on top of the coffee bean grinder. Drink was left by one of the staff from the previous operating day. Owner discussed proper storage of personal beverages with servers working at time of inspection, and drink in question was discarded. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.
citation_text:
2-301.13 PIC was observed going between tasks without washing hands. A wet wiping cloth from a sani-bucket on the cook line was handled to wipe the food thermometer between temperature checks. PIC did not wash hands prior to touching mushrooms that were relocated between pans on the cook line. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and PIC was observed washing hands between tasks the remainder of inspection.,
NOTE: Placing hands in and out of sanitizer solution does not count as having clean or sanitized hands to go directly to handling food, single service articles, or clean dishes. 
--PIC was also observed wiping his hands with a wet wiping cloth from sanitizer solution while walking around the kitchen. Proper use of wiping cloths was discussed. If hands need to be wiped, then they need to be properly washed. Cease the practice of wiping hands on wiping cloths.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after doing anything with sanitizer or other chemicals and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Baked potatoes, soup, and meat sauce were observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. Shelving above food items had varying amounts of buildup (mold/general debris). PIC provided covers and noted the shelving was on the schedule to be cleaned today.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at the dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was empty. Another 5gal bucket of sanitizer was not available and needed to be ordered. Regular bleach was available to connect to the dish machine until a new bucket is available. The final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm upon connecting bleach to the machine. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Mashed potatoes were observed heating in a warmer. Potatoes were placed in the warmer around 9:45am, and internal temperature was observed at ~78F around 10:30am. PIC was advised the warmer is not intended for rapid reheating to 165F/above w/in 2hrs. Mashed potatoes were moved to the stove to reheat rapidly prior to hot holding  (See General Comments).
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly to the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 None of the staff that will be certified food managers have completed the online food allergen awareness training.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Employee with CFM had to leave prior to facility manager's return. A designated person in charge with a CFM must be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands and began shutting off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. Handle of paper towel dispenser had to be touched to dispense additional paper towels, and those paper towels were used to finish shutting off the faucet as well as finish drying hands. Proper technique was discussed with emphasis on avoiding using bare hands to touch the handles of the paper towel dispenser and faucet. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11 Kitchen handsink was used to fill a container with water. Cook was advised to use handsinks only for handwashing purposes. Handsink was observed used for only handwashing for the remainder of the inspection. Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. 

6-301.11 Pump bottle of soap at the kitchen handsink was runny from water being added to product. Staff were advised to cease the practice of adding water to soap when bottle is getting empty. A fresh bottle of soap was provided for the kitchen handsink.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the banquet room bar handsink. Paper towels were provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signs were not posted at the bar handsink or the banquet room bar handsink. Handwashing signs were provided at both handsinks during inspection.  
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Container of salt was observed uncovered on a shelf above the kitchen prep sink. Ensure lids or other covers are provided for containers of salt and other foods between uses.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or .

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in bar sani-bucket was observed around 100ppm. Solution was potentially made with water that was too hot. Fresh solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration, and make sure water temperature is set according to product directions. Also, consider pre-soaking wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths.
citation_text:
4-602.11 The following items were observed to be soiled:
A) can opener - buildup of food debris on and around the blade; 
B) food thermometers - stems and case with buildup/food debris;  and
C) pizza trays and slicer - food debris. 
All items were cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer are used for wiping stems between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Holder for soda gun at banquet room bar was soiled with buildup inside. Holder was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Equipment such as beverage dispensers and holders shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Chili from the previous operating day was observed in a stockpot without a date mark. Cook stated the chili is a special product prepared on-site by another person when chili event happens at the facility. Ensure leftover portions of foods made for special events are properly labeled if kept after the event or removed from the facility if not intended for additional service.
--Portions of sloppy Joe were observed with date of 10/29/19 in the walkin cooler. The portions were prepared and frozen on that date. Sloppy Joe portions were removed from the freezer for thawing. Ensure dates are changed accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Chili prepared today was observed cooling in a plastic 22quart container in the walkin cooler. The container had ~8quarts of chili in it and was loosely covered. The surface and internal temperatures were observed at 112F and 181F respectively. Based on information provided, the chili was placed in the cooler within the last hour. Cook was advised on options for rapid cooling. The chili was portioned and placed in an ice bath to speed up the cooling process. Parameters for proper cooling were discussed. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Food thermometer was observed to be soiled with grease and general buildup. Thermometer was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Leftover rice cooked on Sunday was not date marked in the walkin cooler. Open package of tofu was without a date mark in the bottom of the prep cooler. Rice was to be reheated for service and tofu was date marked. 
Multiple containers of fried chicken pieces were in the walkin cooler, but only one container had a date mark. All chicken was prepared the day prior. Options for date marking multiple containers of same product with one label in the walkin cooler was discussed. For example, if three containers of fried chicken pieces are prepared the same day, owner was advised to provide one label with the date and indicate 3 containers have that date on the label.  
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Frozen shrimp was in the process of thawing in the large prep sink. A small stream of cold water was running over part of the shrimp which were held in a colander. Shrimp were placed in a metal bowl and cold water was turned on to allow for a heavier flow of water over thawing product. 
If time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food is thawed under cold running water it must meet the requirements of FDA Food Code Section 3-501.13(B), and product needs to be completely submerged during the thawing process.  
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 10 ppm chlorine concentration and 106°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed dish machine at bar to have a chlorine bleach concentration of 10 ppm after multiple times running machine. The dish machine states on it that the minimum temperature should be 120°F and machine never registered beyond 106°F. Inspector checked bleach under dish machine and observed bottle to be very low. Facility staff exchanged bleach to a full bottle and machine was run again. Dish machine was still observed to be at 10 ppm and temperature under 120°F. Advised facility to discontinue use of dish machine at bar and to utilize the 3 compartment sink next to it. Advised to have a service call placed for dish machine. Inspector will spot check dish machine status. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year. COS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket of single use wipes at the front service area was observed at 0ppm quat. Bucket was removed for solution and wiping cloths to be replaced. Manager was advised to check the concentration of the product in use periodically during the 30 day period of use to ensure proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Stem of digital food thermometer was soiled with food debris in storage case. Stem of food thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer wipes are used during temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the surfaces between the baffle and where it attaches in the ice machine. All other surfaces that were observed to be soiled the previous inspection were observed to be clean. Ensure cleaning of all surfaces as needed to eliminate mold buildup.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Sausage patties in drive thru hot holding were observed with internal temperature of 121F. Sausages were discarded and fresh sausage was cooked for remainder of breakfast service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

title: Personal cleanliness
citation_text:
2-303.11 Employee doing food prep was observed wearing a large watch. Ensure jewelry such as watches and bracelets are not worn during food prep/food handling.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
A common towel is observed on top of vegetables in the walk in cooler. Do not use common towels or linens in direct contact with food. 

Food is observed stored in t-shirt bags in the back reach in freezer. Do not store foods in t-shirt bags--always make sure containers are food grade.
citation_text: 3-304.13  (C) Linens are in direct contact with food. Linens may not be used in contact with food. Reference 3-304.13.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Rice scoop observed stored in water in between use. Store scoops clean and dry. 

Knives in the kitchen are stored in between metal shelving and containers sitting on the shelves. This area is not easily cleanable and knives should not be stored in between this area.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: The handle to one of the in use knives in this kitchen is broken and there are unnecessary crevices on the handle that are no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Replace this knife.
citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces have rusted or are no longer easily cleanable. Replace with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a food service facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: a) the wire shelves in the walk in cooler are soiled with dripping grease and dust accumulation, b) the handles to all cold holding units are soiled with build up, c) the surfaces of stools, buckets, racks, shelving in the kitchen are soiled with grease and food build up. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Floors under the cook line equipment are soiled black with grease accumulation. Floors need to be cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
Cook observed preparing food while chewing gum. Do not chew gum in food prep areas. 

Observed multiple personal beverages (cups without lids or straws) stored in unapproved locations in the kitchen and wait station--on the side of the prep cooler, on the prep areas, etc. Personal beverages were removed from food prep areas during the inspection. 

2-401.11  (C) Employee observed eating in the food preparation area. Provide designated area outside for eating. Reference 2-401.11.
citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Reference 2-401.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed numerous items in the reach in cooler in the kitchen that are not date marked with the date of preparation, and two containers of salsa that are date marked 11/24 which exceeds the 7 days allowed. Date mark all time and temperature control for safety foods and hold no longer than 7 days maximum. Salsas were discarded and other items date marked during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Observed multiple personal items such as protein powders, cereals, teas, and medications that are stored in the kitchen on storage shelves above pans, on the hanging shelf above the prep cooler, and on top of the microwave. Personal items must be stored in approved areas away from food and utensils used for the public.
citation_text: 7-209.11  (C) Employees must store their personal care items in approved lockers. Reference 7-209.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed the following to be soiled or in disrepair: a) ceiling and light shield in the prep room to be soiled with food splash, b) the wall to the left of the dry storage room has a large hole, c) the wall behind the grill is soiled with dust, d) the shelf and plastic shelf liner above the steam table are heavily soiled. Clean these areas regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
comment: Hand washing sinks are slow draining. Front three compartment sink faucet is leaking when off and draining onto the floor at times. Repair plumbing.
citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: REPEAT #3 The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. PIC has taken test twice in past year. (Last date was Nov. 6). PIC plans to take test next year once class opens. Reference 750.540.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
comment: Observed lettuce to be moldy and spoiled. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. Corrected. Food was discarded. Reference 3-101.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed can opener to be soiled. Ensure equipment is properly cleaned. Clean equipment. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Corrected. Education provided. PIC will clean can opener.  Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed sausage to be datemarked with date exceeding time limit. Corrected. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: Observed employee drink in area in proximity to consumer foods. Ensure personal items are placed in areas away and below any consumer foods. Corrected. Personal item was removed. Education provided.  Reference 6-403.11.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Wet wiping cloth observed on prep surface. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) A cup with a straw but without lid is observed in the food prep area across from the woks. PIC is instructed to ensure that any drinks in the kitchen area have a lid AND a straw. The cup was removed during the inspection.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Knives are stored between the knife rack and the wall. This is not a surface that can be cleaned/ sanitized effectively. The knife was moved to cleaning during the inspection.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) 1) A thick accumulation of soil residue is present on the shelves in the walk in cooler. The PIC is instructed to clean the shelves. It is suggested to allow one section at a time get low on stored foods so as to facilitate easy cleaning, and then to cycle through different sections prior to the next routine inspection. 2) (C) The outside of the bottles used for sauce storage while cooking are observed heavily soiled. The bottles are to be cleaned often enough to prevent the build up of soilage. The containers were moved to cleaning during the inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) The wall seal behind the dish machine currently has cracking caulking and is heavily soiled with a black substance (assumed mold). PIC is instructed to clean the area and recalk the location to provide a smooth and easily clean able surface.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) Personal foods (a Dairy Queen blizzard) are observed stored in the walk in freezer alongside foods intended for service. PIC is instructed to maintain personal/employee foods in locations designated for employees that does not makes contamination of foods intended for consumers possible.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
PA 100-0367 All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

The CFPM at the facility has not yet completed an ANSI accredited allergen training course. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed them to completed the course prior to the next routine inspection. A notice to correct shall be sent to the owner following this inspection.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration in te dish machine. Facility aquired a few to get them through the  time until more could be recieved.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Multiple areas are observed soiled: 1) the floor to the left of the pizza prep station, 2) the floor in the walk in cooler, 3) the floor under the oven, 4) the metal shelf that the grill is located on, 5) the wall at the left back corner as you walk into the walk in cooler, 6) the bottom of the pizza prep cooler. The PIC is instructed to clean these areas and maintain the facility clean and free of being soiled.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverage was observed by the tea maker in the server area left from the previous operating day. Facility has designated holders for personal beverages. Management was advised to ensure proper storage of personal beverages in designated areas only. Drink was discarded. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.
--Employee was observed chewing gum while working in the dish area. Gum was discarded upon request of inspector.  
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Bartender was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and handwashing signage with technique is posted at the bar for reference. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 Paper bowl was observed in a container of wing sauce. Night shift used the bowl as a scoop and left it in the container of sauce. Ensure only proper scoops with handles are used for dispensing wing sauce and other foods.  
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Sanitizer concentration at bar dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Machine was installed new within the last 6 months, and staff were unsure as to how to prime the chemical lines. A call for service was made. Dishes ran through the machine were taken to the kitchen dish machine for ware washing. The 3 part sink was also setup at the bar, and sanitizer was observed at 100ppm for manual ware washing as directed by product label directions.
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
--Spray bottle of quat sanitizer at the bar was observed at 0ppm. Solution was discarded. Ensure spray bottles are checked daily and changed as solution loses concentration. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions at 150-400ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Digital food thermometers were observed with food debris on the probes. Thermometer probes were soiled from use the previous operating day. Probes were cleaned and sanitized prior to calibration for use. New thermometers were also provided and calibrated. Cleaning and maintenance of thermometers were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
--Whisk used for making sweet tea was observed by the tea maker from the previous operating day. Sweet tea was not made this morning. Whisk was taken to dish area for ware washing. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized at any time when contamination may have occurred and between uses. 

Nozzles and diffusers on front soda machine were soiled with buildup. All nozzles and diffusers were cleaned during inspection. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of chemical was not labeled at the bar. Spray bottle contained window cleaner and was labeled as to the contents. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.
citation_text:
7-202.12 Spray bottle at bar labeled Eco San + water was observed at a concentration well above 200ppm chlorine. Inspector's test strip was bleached out and turned white with a dark edge. Chemical was discarded during inspection. Ensure proper dilution of chlorine based product prior to use (50-200ppm).
Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Conditions of the floor drain at the south end of the bar and drain lines above said drain are promoting harborage in this area. Drain lines and floor drain were soiled with buildup, and floor drain also had old food debris in it. A half dozen fruit flies were observed around the drain lines and the floor drain during inspection. Issue with fruit flies appears to be relatively under control otherwise. Clean the drain lines and floor drain in question daily to eliminate food source.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-904.11 Dessert spoons were observed with food surfaces stored up in a utensil holder (Zone 6 outside expo). Spoons and holder were removed for cleaning. Store utensils with handles extended up in containers so food contact surfaces are not handled when utensils are retrieved. 
Sanitized utensils shall be handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-603.12 Pans were observed with a day dot and food debris stuck on them after going through a cycle in the dish machine. Items were placed back in soiled dish area to go through ware washing process again.
Also, a spoon with stuck on food debris was observed with clean dessert spoons. Spoon was removed for cleaning. Ensure proper pre-cleaning and soaking when necessary to remove gross soiled during ware washing. Repeat the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Old sani-bucket from the previous operating day was observed on the bottom shelf of the table holding the tea maker. Solution was discarded. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Old sanitizer solution is considered waste water and proper disposal needs to occur after use/at the end of operations daily.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Corner of metal flooring in the walkin freezer was loose at one edge. Re-seal the flooring in the walkin freezer.
--Metal flashing at the threshold between the walkin cooler and freezer was loose. Re-attach the flashing.
--Tiles in the alcohol walkin were damaged in the keg storage area. Repairs have been scheduled.
--Corner of ceramic baseboard by the mopsink was missing. Replace damaged baseboard.
--Floor under fryers was soiled with grease, food debris, and single service bowls.
Also, the floor under the bar soda machine had cups and general buildup underneath. Clean under equipment daily/as needed.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC on schedule to open today has not completed food allergen awareness training. Manager that stuck around to help with inspection and has certification was not on the schedule to work today. 
All certified food managers that have not already done so need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Block of cream cheese was open and without a date mark. PIC noted it was opened on the Saturday prior. Date mark of 11/23 was provided. Ensure all ready to eat, TCS foods are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days or the time frame required by corporate documentation.
Ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 PIC has a different person helping at the facility since the last inspection. That person does not have a food handler certification on file. PIC was advised the new worker, even if only helping during the holiday season, needs to complete the online food handler training. A copy of the certification needs to be maintained on-site.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner/PIC at time of inspection does not have a food manager certification. Manager certification for another employee was available, but the designated PIC must be a CFM (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Based on the conditions observed at the packaging area and in the restroom, staff have not been washing their hands (see #10 for details). Handwashing at designated handsinks between tasks with proper technique was discussed with the owner.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11 Upon arrival handsink in packaging area was blocked with soiled wiping cloths and foam food trays. All items were removed from the sink. Proper use of handsink and accessibility were discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason. 

6-301.11 Hand soap bottle was empty in the restroom. Soap at the handsink in the packaging area was watered down. Dish soap was at the far end of the 3 part sink and provided for inspector to wash hands. Maintain soap that is not watered down at both handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not located at the handsink in the packaging area. Paper towels were observed at the right drain board of the 3 part sink. Owner was advised the current location did not promote proper handwashing. Provide a paper towel dispenser and place paper towels at the handsink in the packaging area. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text:
3-101.11 Packages with moldy Shitaki mushrooms were observed in the refrigerated display cooler. All portions were removed to be discarded. 
Sliced winter melon in the walkin cooler was without a date mark and observed to be spoiled. Winter melon was removed to be discarded.
Boxes with moldy peanuts in shells were observed up by the drink cooler in the front of the store. Peanuts were said to be set aside for discard. Owner removed peanuts from the front service area. 
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Cutting board and cleaver used the evening prior for cutting and portioning raw shrimp were soiled with food debris. Also, plastic tubs, bowls, pots, and trays were observed on the floor under the 3 part sink. 
Equipment was not cleaned and sanitized after use. Owner was advised on proper ware washing of all food contact surfaces between uses. Poster showing setup for proper manual ware washing was available for reference on the wall above the 3 part sink.
--Later an employee was observed placing the cleaver in a drawer after it was washed and rinsed. The sinks were not setup, and the cleaver was not exposed to proper sanitization. Proper ware washing was discussed. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use did not have an EPA registration number on the label. Owner stated he would obtain proper bleach for use later that day. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Bags of coconuts and shelled peanuts were observed on the floor in the walkin cooler. Foods were placed on shelving during inspection.
--Boxes of foods were all over the floor in the walkin freezer. Owner was advised to provide a means to elevate the foods in the walkin freezer at least 6 inches off the floor.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Handle of scoop for unshelled peanuts was observed touching the food product. Owner repositioned the peanut scoop so the handle was up out of the peanuts. Owner was advised to consider getting some sort of holder for the scoop to encourage proper storage outside of the peanuts between uses. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Foam food trays used for portioning bulk meats were observed to be soiled with debris accumulation in the packaging area. Some of the trays were initially observed with soiled wiping cloths in the basin of the handsink. All trays in question were discarded during inspection. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Soiled cardboard was observed under the cutting board at the 3 part sink in the packaging area. Cardboard was discarded.
--Soiled cardboard and sections of a liner with a foam backing were observed lining the small metal shelves in the packaging area. Remove soiled cardboard and liners with foam backing. Provide a cleanable surface for lining the shelves. 
--Soiled cardboard was observed lining the top of a metal table that had a deteriorated surface underneath. Owner was advised to cease the practice of using cardboard. Clean and remove damaged surface on the top of the metal table, and provide a cover that is cleanable.
--Heavy ice/frost accumulation was observed along the top inside the doors of the freezer holding eggrolls. Owner was advised to defrost the freezer and maintain it in a manner that is easy to clean. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-501.14 The 3 part sink was observed to be heavily soiled with food and general debris in all three compartments. It did not appear the 3 part sink was used for ware washing any time recently. All of the compartments and the drain board needed to be cleaned. Cleaning began during inspection. 
Clean the sinks and drain board at the 3 part sink daily/as needed and between uses and maintain them clean. 
The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following items were soiled:
1) walkin cooler shelving (dust/mold); 
2) refrigerated display cooler holding eggs (general buildup/dust); and
3) packaging area - general surfaces of shelving and table holding wrap station (splash/debris).
Clean the aforementioned items and all general surfaces daily/as needed, and maintain them clean. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Puddle of dirty waste water was observed in the mop bucket. Waste water was discarded and mop bucket cleaned during inspection. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Handsinks were observed to be soiled, especially the restroom handsink which had grimy buildup. Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean. 
--Walkin cooler floor was soiled with buildup under shelving, and dust was starting to buildup on the ceiling above the fan. Clean the ceiling and the floor in the walkin cooler.
--Ceiling was damaged and falling down at the doorway between the dry storage area and the store. 
A few ceiling tiles in store were also observed with severe water damage. Owner noted repairs are needed for the roof. Provide repairs and replace the damaged tiles and ceiling in the aforementioned area.  
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-303.11 Lighting in the restroom was very dim, and one bulb was flickering. A flashlight was needed to see general surfaces clearly. Repair/replace lighting in the restroom. 
Light intensity shall be at least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in restrooms.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. Worker present at the time of inspection confirmed he did not have a certification. Employee was advised as to online course options for earning certification. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Shift manager and night manager were both observed washing hands without proper technique. Faucet was shut off with paper towels prior to drying hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then use the paper towel as a barrier to dispense fresh paper towels to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution at 3 part sink was observed at 0ppm. Sani-bucket was observed between 50-100ppm chlorine. Product label directions show an effective concentration of 200ppm. All solutions were remade and observed at 200ppm. Dishes done prior to inspector's arrival were re-sanitized after solution was changed at 3 part sink.
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Knife was washed and rinsed prior to employee taking it to the storage area. Employee was advised to always sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils prior to storage. Knife was taken back to dish area to be sanitized. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Portion of turkey in bottom of prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 50F. Shift manager was unsure as to how long it was out during portioning prior to inspector's arrival. Turkey was placed in reach-in freezer to try and drop the temperature. Store manager chose to discard the portion of turkey. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Tray of brownies covered with plastic wrap were observed sitting on the left lid of the ice cream freezer by the handsink. Splash from staff washing hands was observed on the lid around the brownies. Night manager moved brownies away from the handsink. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 & 4-702.11  Quat solution at 3 part sink was at 0ppm, and a serving utensil was observed in the solution. Utensil was removed and placed with other dirty dishes to go through ware washing process again. Old sanitizer solution was emptied and new solution prepared at 200ppm.

Change out sanitizer solutions frequently/as needed throughout the operating day. Maintain solutions at 200-400ppm as indicated on label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
citation_text:
