title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC working at the time of inspection does not currently have a food manager certification. Course work was completed on-line, but PIC has not yet taken the test for certification. Information for testing was provided (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed drying his hands with paper towels, turning off the manual faucet, and then continuing to dry his hands with the same paper towels. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 Soufflé cup was observed in an open package of dry parmesan in the reach-in cooler at the food service area. Soufflé cup was removed and discarded. Use proper scoops when dispensing foods. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser was empty at the prep kitchen handsink. Paper towels were provided. 
Later paper towels were observed to be absent from the food service area. Paper towels were provided. Ensure soap and paper towels are always available to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.
citation_text:
5-501.16 Waste receptacle was on the opposite end of the food service area, and another container was not available for disposal of paper towels after handwashing. A small metal container was provided for disposal of paper towels generated during handwashing.   
If disposable towels are used at handwashing lavatories, a waste receptacle shall be located at each lavatory or group of adjacent lavatories.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Paper boat of seasoning used for flatbread pizza was uncovered by the pizza oven. The seasoning was uncovered overnight and was discarded. Ensure that all seasonings and liquids used in food prep are covered during slow periods and for long-term overnight storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings and separating fruits and vegetables, before they are washed from ready to eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 & 4-702.11 Quat product used as sanitizer was empty. Dishes were done prior to inspector's arrival, and PIC was not certain when the product ran out. A bottle of different quat product was provided for use. When dispensed the concentration was ~300ppm, and the effective range for the product is 150-400ppm. Ensure chemical used for sanitization is always available and at proper concentration. All dishes were to be sanitized prior to use. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

4-602.1 Stems of the digital food thermometers were soiled with food debris, and one of the cases was also observed to be soiled. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed. Thermometers and cases were cleaned during inspection. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If sanitizer solution or alcohol wipes are used to wipe stems during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use. Maintain the cases clean. 

Fry baskets were observed with stuck on food debris. PIC noted the fryer is currently not in use and needs to be repaired
 Clean the fry baskets and store them in an area protected from potential contamination until the fryer is available for use again.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed inside the microwave in the prep kitchen. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open package of spinach and pans of chicken were not date marked in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler. One portion of chicken was cooked and cooled the day prior, and the other portion was cooked and cooled the Sunday prior. Date marking was discussed, and products were properly labeled. Ensure all ready to eat, TCS foods that require date marking are dated upon opening/preparation and used or discarded within 7 days. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Boxes of bread delivered on Wednesday were observed on the floor in the prep kitchen. Boxes were moved to a storage area off the floor. Ensure proper storage of foods. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food In a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and is at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled: 
A) fryer - general surfaces (grease); and  
B) oven - drip tray (food splash). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 The floor in the prep kitchen was soiled with accumulation of food and general debris under equipment and along the floor to wall juncture. Clean the floors throughout daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
--Hoods baffles were soiled. The baffles over the fryer and oven had grease and dust buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
--Light covers in the hoods were also soiled. Clean the light covers. 
--Electrical outlet cover was loose by the fryer in the food service area. Reattach the cover.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-303.11 Lights were burnt out in the hoods. Replace the bulbs.
Light intensity shall be at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) at a surface where a food employee is working with food or working with utensils and equipment where employee safety is a factor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-201.11  (C) Three compartment sink area found not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed 3 compartment sink missing caulk between sink and wall. Observed multiple small holes in wall near 3 compartment sink and back room handsink. Must be caulked in order to avoid pests and/or mold build-up. Discussed with PIC. All surfaces must be smooth and easily cleanable.

6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop with wet mop head on ground. Mops must be stored in a position that allows to drip dry in-between uses. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.

comment: Observed cup used as a scoop in the sugar container near the coffee/tea equipment. Use scoops with handles to prevent bare-hand contact with foods.
citation_text: 3-304.12 Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. (C)

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
-Observed utensils stored in container with food debris/crumbs in the dry storage area. Utensils must be stored in clean places protected from contamination. Clean storage containers as often as necessary. 
-Observed single-use utensils stored with mixed directions (food contact ends and handles). Store utensils all one direction to prevent contamination of food contact ends when picking up a utensil. Also observed metal silverware stored with food contact portions up. Store utensils inverted to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Observed employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Corrected. Education provided. Employee re-washed hands.  Reference 2-301.14.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed soda nozzle is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Corrected. Soda nozzle will be wiped down and cleaned.  Reference 4-601.11(A).

comment: Observed time policy not being practiced properly. In addition, products are being saved after time allowance. Time Control requires food to be used within certain time frame or discarded. Readjust practices to ensure foods are discarded. This includes eggs, sausage, gravy, etc. In addition, ensure the proper documentation is being recorded. Corrected. Education provided. Items will be used/discarded in time limit. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed cutting boards are severely scratched and pitted, which prevents proper cleaning and sanitizing to prevent pathogenic microorganism transmission. Ensure cutting board is repaired/replaced. Reference 4-501.12.

4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed can opener to be soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC and COS.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed in-use wiping cloths to be not immersed in sani bucket, as well as cloths within sani bucket not completely immersed in solution. In-use wiping cloths should be maintained in sani buckets and changed every 4 hours. PIC was made aware and COS.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Date marking is not on an opened gallon of milk in the first prep cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Milk was labeled with the date it was opened.
3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date).

Date of 11/7 marked on cooked pasta in the first prep cooler, and 11/3  on marinara sauce in the walk-in cooler exceed the time limit. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Foods were voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment: Baked potatoes are stored on top of the oven out of temperature control. Facility does not have a written Time as a Public Health Control policy. CORRECTED- Created written policy for using time as a control for baked potatoes.
citation_text: 3-501.19 If time without temperature control is used as the public health control for READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is held for service (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. (Pf)

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: The method of cooling rice is inadequate. Observed rice on the top shelf of the walk-in cooler covered in plastic wrap, with a sealed lid at 135F (probed). Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Rice was uncovered and labeled with the time. Advised PIC to monitor the cooling process.
citation_text: 3-501.15 (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the FOOD in shallow pans; (2) Separating the FOOD into smaller or thinner portions; (3)Using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT; (4) Stirring the FOOD in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. (Pf)

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Chili was observed thawing from frozen at room temperature. CORRECTED- Chili was placed in the walk-in cooler to thaw under refrigeration.
3-501.13 Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

Thawed fish observed still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) with a label indicating it must be removed from packaging before thawing. Thaw frozen fish according to manufacturer's instructions.
citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section. (C)

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

citation_text: 3-303.11 After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. (P)

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Manager washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and educational poster on proper technique was provided. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
**To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the back handsink by the 3 part sink. Paper towels were provided. This same issue was observed during the 2018 inspection and corrected during the inspection at that time as well. Ensure that soap and paper towels are always stocked at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Stem of the digital food thermometer was soiled with food debris. Stem was cleaned during inspection. Use and general maintenance of food thermometer were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
--F'real machines were observed with dried food splash on surfaces where shakes and smoothies are mixed. Manager noted the entire machine has a cleaning process that occurs up to every 24hrs or it doesn't work. The surfaces that are visible and can be accessed, such as the mixing wand/area around it where splash occurs, need to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use since they come in contact with time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food.
Food contact surfaces of equipment used with TCS foods shall be cleaned up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
--Nozzles and diffusers of soda machines had varying amounts of mold buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed in the microwaves. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Tube at creamer dispenser was observed to be cut straight across and holding a portion of product at room temperature in the bottom of the tip where creamer dispenses into customer cups. Manger cut the tubes at more of an angle to allow for proper draining between uses. Ensure all staff are properly trained and that tubes for creamer are cut at an angle to avoid the issue of ponding creamer in the bottom of tubes at room temperature between uses.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-803.11 Soiled, damp wiping cloths were observed on the left drain board at the 3 part sink. Manager placed wiping cloths in soiled linen storage container. 
Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags. Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

Remove the old stickers and thoroughly clean the surfaces to remove buildup and allow for proper cleaning of sinks between uses.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate

title: Food properly labeled; original container

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:

Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-603.16 Employee washed a pan and placed it directly in the third compartment of 3 part sink that was in the process of filling with sanitizer. Employee was advised on proper rinsing between the wash and sanitize steps during ware washing. Pan was placed in middle compartment to be rinsed prior to sanitizing. Manager was advised to go over proper manual ware washing steps with staff
Washed utensils and equipment shall be rinsed so that abrasives are removed and cleaning chemicals are removed or diluted through the use of water by using a distinct, separate water rinse after washing and before sanitizing in the 3 compartment sink.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Workers in the main kitchen and the cook shack were observed washing hands without proper technique. Process took less than 20 seconds, and paper towels were not used as a barrier to shut off the faucet. Poster showing proper technique is posted in both locations. PIC was advised to reiterate proper handwashing process with all workers. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

2-301.14 While discussing handwashing with one worker, another person stated he washed his hands in the restroom prior to putting on gloves. Worker was advised that handwashing upon entering the kitchen and prior to putting on gloves needs to occur in addition to washing hands in the restroom. Worker washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves. 
--Worker entered the cook shack and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to work with food. Handwashing upon entering the cook shack and prior to glove use were discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-703.11 Bartender was observed washing dishes and dunking items in the sanitizer solution briefly prior to removing to air dry. Sanitizer tablets in-use specify a contact time of at least 1 minute or time required by local governing entity during immersion sanitization. Manager and bartender were advised to ensure a contact time of at least 30-60 seconds prior to removing items from sanitizer to air dry during ware washing process. All items were re-sanitized with proper contact time prior to air drying. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized by immersion using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing a contact time of at least 30 seconds for a quaternary ammonia sanitizer.

4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink for ware washing was around 100ppm. Solution was made earlier in the day and needed to be changed. Old solution was discarded and replaced with fresh solution observed at proper concentration (200-400ppm per label directions). 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200-400ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was beginning to accumulate on the ceiling behind the baffle in the ice machine. Cleaning and general maintenance were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed multiple areas in kitchen with missing tile pieces and therefore not smooth and easily cleanable. Discussed with PIC regarding repairs.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The PIC stated that he was a Certified Food Manager, but could not find his certificate. Ensure that the certificate is available during the next routine inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed no date marking on a package of opened hot dogs. Ensure that all foods opened and not used within 24 hours are properly date marked. PIC date marked to pack of hot dogs.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test strips for bleach were not available during the inspection. Ensure test strips are ordered and available to test the concentration of bleach solutions. PIC stated he would order test strips.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.13 (A) (C) Observed no caulking or coving on the wall across from the restrooms. Ensure that caulking or coving is installed to seal the floor to the wall.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Observed food employee enter kitchen and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Corrected. Education provided. Reference 2-301.14.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed no sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14.

Observed Hand washing sink blocked equipment including trash bin and mop bucket. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Corrected. Hand sink was made accessible. Reference 5-205.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: REPEAT #1: Observed equipment used for food prep to be soiled. This included can opener and various equipment near prep table. Wash, rinse, sanitize equipment routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed several items without date marking. This included breaded chicken, egg rolls, beef, pork, and noodles. PIC stated items had been cooked with in 7 days and will be date marked properly. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Ensure all TCS foods are properly date marked. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment: Observed Time Control policy not being followed. Ensure Time control policy is being followed. Label discard time/set-up time. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
REPEAT #2 Observed shrimp to be incontact with ice or water. Food may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the food is subject to direct contact with the ice or water. Cease practice. Reference 3-303.12.
Observed multiple foods not protected from contamination in W-I Cooler and D. Cooler. Food shall be protected from contamination. Cover food. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed Cutting boards to be severely scratched and pitted, which prevents proper cleaning and sanitizing to prevent pathogenic microorganism transmission. Repair or replace cutting board. Reference 4-501.12.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
REPEAT #1: Observed black mold and frost build-up on R-I Freezer. Defrost freezer and clean. Observed C. Freezer to have accumulation of frost. Defrost freezer. Reference 4-602.13.
Observed stove top to be covered with debris. Clean stove. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
comment: Observed Inadequate hot water available to all fixtures. Hot water system must have an adequate capacity to meet peak hot water demands throughout the facility at all times of operation. Hot water system must be repaired or upgraded to provide an adequate supply of hot water at all times.  Reference 5-103.11 .

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed floor to be cluttered with boxes, food debris and other soilage. Clean facility as needed to keep facility clean. In addition, mouse droppings have been found near C. Freezer. PIC stated no pest issues have occurred in recent past. Pest Control comes frequently to treat facility. Reference 6-501.12

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
Observed personal items stored amongst items for consumers. Ensure personal items are placed below and away from food prep. Education provided. Reference 6-305.11.
Observed light over food prep area without shielding. Cover lighting fixture with shield. Reference 6-202.11.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: REPEAT #1: No CFM has allergen training certificate. Class I Facilities shall have allergen training certificate with all CFMs. Reference PA 100-0367.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No proof of certified food manager certification. Provide proof of certified food protection manager supervision during each shift. Manager and another employee will be scheduled to take this course.
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Observed boxes of candy stored on the floor in the back storeroom. Store candy and food at least 6" off the floor. 

Observed cases of water stored outside the front of the building. Water must be stored so that it is protected from contact with direct sunlight.
citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
comment: It appears as though the hand washing sink in the front near the cappuccino machines may be leaking into a container in the cabinet below. Repair plumbing and clean out this cabinet.
citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) Repair plumbing according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Blizzard mixing spindles soiled with food debris. Spindles cleaned during the inspection. 

Ice scoop on rusted cart/can opener. Scoop was washed, rinsed and sanitized during inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf)  Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm in counter sanitizer bucket. Maintain concentration as indicated on manufacturer's label. CORRECTED- Sanitizer was remade to appropriate concentration.
4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

Can opener is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. CORRECTED- Can opener was washed rinsed and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Observed hot dog to be 121F. Ensure foods hot held at 135F or above. Corrected. Hot Dogs will be used in 4 hours or less (from ~1545).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with yellow residue. Clean non-food contact surfaces as needed.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee took a drink from a personal beverage and then began to put on gloves without handwashing in between. Employee just washed hands prior to getting a drink but was advised handwashing was required again prior to putting on gloves because of personal beverage consumption. Employee washed her hands again prior to putting on gloves to help with prep.
--Employee working the drive thru window was handling money and put on gloves to make beverages without handwashing in between. Employee was advised on handwashing prior to putting on gloves and working with food and single service articles. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after eating/drinking, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Surfaces in the ice machine were soiled with varying degrees of mold accumulation on the plastic baffle, the walls, and around the openings in the ceiling where ice drops from the ice maker. Ice was in contact with the mold on the baffle. The plastic baffle was wiped down with sanitizer during inspection, and ice was removed for discard. All surfaces inside the ice machine will be cleaned and sanitized at the close of business today. Ice machine will be checked again when inspector returns to check on pest control (11/12/19). 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Diffusers of soda machines were soiled with varying amounts of buildup. Ensure diffusers that cannot be removed from the machines getting manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized in place. 
--Inside ice machine was soiled with mold buildup (see #15 for additional information).
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed compartments, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Squeeze pouch of whipped topping was observed in a styrofoam cup within a container in the top holding area of the dessert topping cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 48F and 49F-50F respectively. Product was discarded. The styrofoam cup was likely acting as an insulator and causing the whipped topping to be above 41F because the temperature down inside the container was 39F. Consider storing the whipped topping in the bottom of the cooler and/or cease the practice of stacking a cup within the container. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 A dozen plus fruit flies were observed under and around the dirty dish area and around the floor drain by the used grease bin. Manager noted treatment has been ongoing, and facility was working with PCO to eliminate flies. PCO provided a product for cleaning and treatment that was currently in use and observed on the floor behind the used grease bin and in the drain adjacent to the grease bin. Management was advised on cleaning and repairs also needed in the area to help minimize potential food/water sources (see #55 for details)
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Metal ice scoop was stored on top of a soda syrup box by the ice machine. Manager removed the scoop and took it to 3 part sink for ware washing. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee working at drive thru prepared drinks and handled money with gloved hands. Gloves were eventually discarded. Proper use of gloves was discussed. Management was advised to reiterate proper glove use with all staff.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (mold/food debris);
B) side of fryer next to freezer storage where skimmer is stored (grease buildup);  and
C) side of fryer next to fryers (grease splash).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Ponding water and debris were observed around the pipes on the left side under the small 3pt sink up front and around the floor drain directly in front of the pipes. Clean the area and re-seal low lying areas to eliminate ponding water.
--Floor drain by used grease storage bin was soiled down inside with grimy, moldy buildup. The cover to the drain also had buildup on the underside. Clean down inside the drain and the cover. 
--Floor tiles had low grout and baseboard was loose behind the used grease storage bin. Ponding water and debris accumulation was observed. Manager also noted he was in the process of treating for flies in the area, so a greenish colored liquid was also present. Clean and repair this area to eliminate ponding water and debris accumulation. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification had to leave prior to conclusion of inspection. The person left in charge only had a food handler certification. Additional staff with food manager certifications are needed. Ensure that enough staff have food manager certifications to allow for a designated person in charge with a CFM to be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.15 PIC rinsed hands at 3 part sink after handling a chemical bottle. Handwashing at designated handwashing sinks was discussed. Ensure that hands are only washed at handsinks. If hands need to be rinsed, then hands should be properly washed regardless of the next task that will occur.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink in the ware washing/back storage area. Maintain handwashing signage at all designated handsinks. Handwashing signs were provided for management to post where needed. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwasing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket at food service area was observed at 0ppm quat despite being made within the last few hours. The solution was relatively clean. The wiping cloth in use may have absorbed chemical out of solution. The solution was remade and observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain solutions from SuperSan dispenser at 150-400ppm as directed, and use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Pizza slicer was observed soiled and resting on a wet paper towel on the top ledge of the prep cooler. Slicer was taken to ware washing area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Box containing hinged food containers was observed on the floor under the prep table in the pizza kitchen. Box was placed up on a shelf for proper storage. 
Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit available for use was severely water damage. Kit was discarded. Extra test strips were available for use from Subway. Additional test kits would be purchased. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Handsink in the ware washing/back storage area was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin and along upper surfaces. Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification had to leave prior to conclusion of inspection. The person left in charge only had a food handler certification. Additional staff with food manager certifications are needed. Ensure that enough staff have food manager certifications to allow for a designated person in charge with a CFM to be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare an order after working the cash register. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling money, and before putting on gloves/between glove changes.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink up front by the make line. Maintain handwashing signage at all designated handsinks. Handwashing signs were provided for management to post where needed. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwasing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink for ware washing was observed at 100ppm. Effective concentration per product label is 150-400ppm A freshly dispensed bucket to be used on the gas station side was observed at 0ppm. Upon rerunning the solution the concentration was observed at 200ppm. Ensure the temperature of the water used to make sanitizer is cool to warm and not too hot, as the temperature can effect the concentration. Use test strips to verify concentration when making solutions. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle containing a purple chemical with a worn label that appeared to say lime away was observed in the dish area. PIC thought it was degreaser. Product was discarded. Ensure proper labeling on working supplies of chemicals.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Bag of onions was observed on the floor in the walkin cooler. Ensure foods are stored properly. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor in a clean, dry location where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 A disposable wiping cloth previously used for wiping down tables was being reused for wiping down the back prep table and was not stored properly. The wiping cloth was previously used with sanitizer dispensed from a spray bottle, and sani-bucket with quat solution was not available for storing cloth between uses. Wiping cloth was discarded. Proper storage of wiping cloths in solution between uses and/or immediate discard when used with spray bottles of sanitizer were discussed.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-501.18 Sanitizer solution in-use at knife caddy on the make line was observed to be visibly soiled. Knives were also observed stored in the solution and not the side compartment. Proper storage of knives after wiping was discussed. The knife sanitizer caddy was cleaned and provided with new solution at 200ppm. Ensure caddy is cleaned/sanitized and provided with fresh solution for wiping knifes as needed when soil buildup occurs and/or up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions shall be clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11  Floor tiles were loose and damaged between the grease trap and the floor drain under the 3 part sink.
--Baseboard tiles were damaged and/or missing by the back door and on the left side of the water heater.
Provide proper repairs in the aforementioned areas.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Damp mop was observed in mop bucket. Ensure proper storage of damp mops between uses. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment or supplies.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 New store manager has not yet completed a food sanitation course to obtain a food manager certification. Manager took over the store within the last 30 days and should be registered to attend class in the near future. Many other employees also have food manager certifications, but the PIC at the time of inspection must be a CFM.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Manager filled a cup with water to calibrate the food thermometer at the food counter handsink. Manager was advised on proper use of handsinks for handwashing only and that signage should be placed at the sink in an attempt to deter using the sink for other purposes. After discussing this the ice water solution was also dumped at the front handsink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the food counter handsink for purposes other than handwashing. Staff should do their best to advise customers on this also.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket at food service area was at 0ppm quat. Solution was remade and observed at 200ppm. Manager was advised on use of warm water, as directed on instructions for use, to ensure tablets dissolve properly.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Follow label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration of solutions.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
citation_text:
3-403.11 Hotdogs on one roller grill were observed with surface temperatures at 106F-107F. The internal temperature of one hotdog was observed at 108F. Employee noted the hotdogs in question were put on around 6-6:30am and should have already been to temperature. All products were discarded. Ensure the roller grill is turned up hot enough to thoroughly reheat the precooked, ready to eat roller grill items to proper temperature as specified on the product directions. Items should reach at least 135F prior to service. 
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in an inspected/regulated food processing plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 Several small flies were observed in the cabinet beneath the iced coffee and cold brew machines where a drain was located. Buildup of splash and debris were noted in the cabinet, which was likely contributing to the presence of pests. Store manager cleaned the area in question during inspection. Manager was advised on use of fly strips in the cabinet to help further eliminate flies. 
NOTE: Fly strips may be used as long as they are placed in appropriate areas that do not pose a potential risk of cross contamination to food, clean equipment, or single service articles. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-201.11 Water was observed leaking under the metal divider at the 3 part sink between the middle and right compartments. The divider was repaired in 2018 after the issue was cited as a repeat violation. The repair did not permanently fix the issue. The 3 part sink may need to be replaced if the divider cannot be permanently and properly repaired to eliminate water leakage between the compartments. Manager stated she would put in a work order. In the meantime, manager was advised to have staff do ware washing from right to left since the third compartment can maintain a proper sanitize solution to allow for manual submersion of 30-60 seconds as required for proper contact time prior to air drying.

Equipment shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solution prepared using sani tabs.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips for the sanitizer currently in use.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Puddle of discarded coffee was observed in a cabinet beneath the coffee makers. A leak was present in the dump tray drain pipe. Manager noted she would make maintenance aware for repairs to occur. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper technique poster is available for reference at the front handsink. Store manager was advised to reiterate proper handwashing with all staff. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use the paper towels after hands are dried and shut off the faucet at the last step of the handwashing process.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee removed a glove to handle his phone. Employee did not wash hands and attempted to put the same glove back on to continue with food prep. Inspector interjected, and the employee discarded both gloves. Hands were washed prior to obtaining a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling cell phones.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted in the men's room. Maintain handwashing signage at all handsinks, including in the restrooms. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 Mold accumulation was observed on and around the white baffle in the ice machine. Chunky buildup was observed along the crevice between the baffle and the wall and on the bottom right corner. Ice was piled up between the ceiling and the baffle and in contact with soiled surfaces. Store manager removed ice to begin cleaning, and mold accumulation was also observed inside on the ceiling behind the baffle. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure inside the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency to eliminate buildup and protect ice from potential cross contamination. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are properly cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket prepared earlier in the day was observed at 100ppm. Solution was discarded, and new solution was prepared at proper concentration of 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration, and maintain product at 200ppm as instructed on label directions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Mold accumulation was observed on multiple surfaces in the ice machine. Ice machine was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Soda nozzle diffusers (inner white pieces with holes) had varying degrees of buildup, as did the surface where nozzles attach to the machine. Clean and sanitize the soda nozzles, diffusers, and surfaces where they attach on the machine.
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-202.15 A decent size hole, which was big enough for a writing utensil to easily fit through, was observed at the bottom right corner of the weather stripping on the back door. Provide repairs to seal the hole.
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by providing solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Food employee removed a glove to handle his phone. Employee did not wash hands and attempted to put the same glove back on to continue with food prep. Inspector interjected, and the employee discarded both gloves. Hands were washed prior to obtaining a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-201.11 White baffle in the ice machine was cracked and broken along the lower edge. The baffle needs to be replaced. 
Equipment and utensils. shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-603.12 Vegetable dicer and slicer were observed with stuck on food debris and were in the clean equipment storage area. Items were placed at 3 part sink to go through ware washing process again. Manager was advised to speak with staff about precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 & 2-301.14 PIC touched soda gun nozzle without first washing hands and was observed scratching nose prior to handling the soda gun. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 
PIC came in from smoking and immediately washed hands. However, a barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
Educational handouts on technique, when to wash hands, and proper glove use were provided. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
 To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink was observed at less than 100ppm. Only one tablet was used to make the solution. Two more tablets were added to bring the concentration to 200ppm. Ensure at least 3-4 tablets are used to make sanitizing solution for ware washing, and use test strips to verify concentration is 200-400ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed on the metal baffle in the ice machine. Buildup was also present in the top part of the machine where ice maker is located. Baffle was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. A layer of ice was discarded after wash, rinse, and sanitize of baffle was completed. Detail cleaning in the upper ice maker will occur when the machine is emptied. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Sausage gravy prepared for breakfast service was observed with surface and internal temperature at 66F and 80F respectively. Cook on duty did not work the morning shift and was unsure as to the exact time the gravy was cooked and/or when the cooling process began. Time was not indicated on the label. Gravy was discarded. Tracking of time and temperature to ensure proper cooling was discussed - consider using the dry erase board to write the time/temperature and track the cooling process so there is no confusion on time frame and/or if products are cooling properly, especially between shift changes. 
Cooked TCS food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.
