3-301.11 (Pf) Food employee is not minimizing bare hand contact with foods that are not in a ready to eat form. Employee shall use suitable utensils or gloves to minimize bare hand contact with these foods. Reference 3-301.11.

Observed ice scoops in ice bin with handles inside ice. Occured at 5 locations between bar and wait staff service station.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: 6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12.
citation_text:
6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14.
Observed lack of hand washing signs at bar sinks as well as paper towels. PIC provided paper towels, COS. Three hand sinks are located in the bar area and there is no designation for which is specifically for hand washing.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11  (C) Store all foods intended to be returned separated from food that is to be served and equipment. Reference 3-302.11.
Observed blue cheese olives in bar fridge drawer that was uncovered.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-702.11  (P) Observed in-use knives to be stored on a magnetic knife strip soiled. Removed for cleaning during the inspection. Discussed cleaning and sanitizing of food storage utensils. 
Observed the ice wands stored on the floor of the walk-in freezer. This surface is going into food for cooling. Protect the food contact surface.
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Soda nozzle and holder food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Silverware observed at wait serving station soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
Employee removed silverware with debris.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on milk in wait station serving area fridge. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: 7-201.11  (P) Observed sanitizing bottles to be stored mixed within condiments. Moved during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed at least four quat spray bottles to be at a concentration of 100ppm. Pulled from use during inspection. Discussed monitoring of concentration.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15  (C) Observed alfredo sauce stored covered and in a deep container. Probed sauce at 53F. Food was placed within container last night after close. Discarded during inspection.
Observed a large tote of cooled meatballs at 48F to 60F. There are two cooling racks that are in-use. Foods are these racks are observed at 35-38F. Single layer and date marked. Some meatballs, sausages, and noodles are observed cooling on these racks. This is the standard process. Meatballs stored in tote were discarded.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at wait station near bar and wait serving station near kitchen . Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text: 4-401.11  (C) Observed papertoweling to be stored within the shelving of the employee toilet room. Cease storing papertoweling and single-service within the bathrooms.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.
Observed expired quat test strips at bar area to be expired.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text: 750.540 (C) Observed no CFM present during the inspection. A CFM must be present during hours of operation and food prep.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observe the ice machine to have debris and build up on the baffle. All food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized as frequently as neccessary to maintain clean.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Observed a spray bottle labeled as sanitizer to not test as quat or bleach. It appeared to smell like fabuloso, which is present in the building. Only approved sanitizers can be used to sanitize. Label spray bottle according to its contents.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed accumulate crumbs and debris on the outside of the dish machine. Clean surfaces as needed to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.13 (A) (C) Observed coving to the left of the dish machine pulling away from the wall. Ensure coving is sealed to the wall with no gaps.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No proof of certified food protection manager on duty at the time of the inspection. Medium risk facilities are required to be under the operation of a CFM during operating hours--this changed when the FDA Food Code was adopted.
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
1) Observed coffee maker spouts to be soiled. Wash, rinse and sanitize coffee maker spouts. 

2) Observed employee wash and rinse mixing bowl and place to air dry without sanitizing first. Quaternary ammonium sanitizer in the wall mounted unit is empty and there are no replacements on site at the time of the inspection. Facility does have bleach available but bleach does not have an EPA registration number on the label although it does say "kitchen sink" on the label. Facility will switch to this bleach in the meantime until they are able to supply an approved sanitizer. 

4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Equipment is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
citation_text: 4-702.11  (P) After cleaning, utensils must be sanitized before use. Reference 4-702.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed the following items which exceed the 7 day date marking allowed in the pizza prep cooler: taco meat (10/9), beans (10/1), spinach dip (10/2), BBQ (9/27), turkey (10/7), roast beef (9/27), pork (9/29), corn (10/2). These items were discarded during the inspection. 

Observed half and half and iced coffee in the dispensers in the customer service area to not be date marked with the date of opening. Label on iced coffee box states to refrigerate after opening and follow local health codes once open. Date marking for these items will be checked on the follow up inspection on Monday.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment:
Observed iced coffee and half and half spouts to be cut straight across rather than at the required 45 degree diagonal angle. Cut dispensing tube properly. 

Observed single service items to be stored out of the box and on the floor in the back storage area. This includes paper towels, toilet paper and boxes of cups. Store single service items at least 6" off the floor. 

4-502.13  (C) Bulk milk container dispensing tube not properly cut. The bulk milk dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than 1 inch protruding from the chilled dispenser. Reference 4-502.13.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.
Certified food manager must be present any time pizzas are being made or served.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text: 3-301.11 (P) Observed food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods (Cut lemons for drinks) . Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed ice machine baffle food contact surface to be soiled with slime mold. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text: 7-102.11  (Pf) Observed working container of sanitizer at outdoor bar not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Observed ceiling in the pizza preparation area to be not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: There are numerous juvenile and adult roaches observed throughout the facility--under/behind the ice machine, under ice cream machine, under dish machine, under back hand sink. There are glue traps on the front counter with dead adult roaches observed. Bacon's Pest Control was last here on 9/26/19 per invoice. The facility purchased gel from Bacon's and also uses a spray (not on food contact surfaces) and glue boards. Consult pest control immediately as there is rampant activity today.
citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) . The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Grout in tile in front of ice machine/to left of custard machine is deep and no longer easily cleanable. Roaches observed in this area. Also observed roaches go under black coving on wall to right of ice machine where there are gaps in the grout. Tile needs re-grouted to help eliminate pests.
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Floors, Walls and Ceilings were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands between tasks and was observed working the cash register prior to going to food service area. Employee was observed opening the lid to the roller grill and checking products. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and staff were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.11 Hand soap was not available at the handsink in the food service area. A small bottle of soap was provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsinks at the food service area or in the back by the walkin cooler. Handwashing signage was provided during inspection. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Handsink at the food service counter has been used as a dump sink based on information provided. Proper use of handsink was discussed.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the food service counter handsink as a dump sink for coffee.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Ice shoots of the soda machines were observed with pink mold accumulation on lower/back edges. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 
Food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Chili sauce dispensed from the Gehl's dispenser had an internal temperature 127F-130F. Cheese sauce dispensed from the other side of the same dispenser had an internal temperature of 135F-140F. Thermometer on the side of the dispenser was reading around 130F. Upon further investigation store manager discovered the valve for the chili sauce was not properly attached to the bag, which was allowing air into the product. Chili sauce was removed for discard. Ensure that products are properly hooked up in the dispenser to allow for consistent hot holding at 135F/above throughout the product. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open creamers in dispensers had date marks of 10/3-10/10. With product being opened on 10/3 the discard date was 10/9. All creamers were discarded and replaced with fresh product.
Open packages of hotdogs in the walkin cooler had date marks of 10/7 with a discard date indicated as 10/17. Store manager changed the date to reflect proper discarded date of 10/13. 
Ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Packages of bottled water available for purchase were observed outside the facility on display. Manager was advised the bottled water needs to be stored in the facility. Cease the practice of displaying bottled water outside the facility. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloth was observed with a spray bottle of sanitizer. Manager was advised on use of disposable paper towels when spray bottle of sanitizer is in use. Otherwise, damp wiping cloths need to be stored in a sanitizer solution between uses. Wiping cloth was moved to soiled linen storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Proper handwashing technique is not possible with the lack of cold water at this time. A temporary handwashing station with warm water will be provided to promote proper handwashing (see general comments for details).
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival the handsink was blocked by a box holding empty strawberry cartons. Box was moved to allow access to the handsink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items on top of the handsink for any reason.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Food employee touched her hair with gloved hands and did not immediately remove gloves. Inspector advised on proper glove use. Gloves were changed prior to continuing with food prep.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water is still not available at the fixtures in the kitchen. Both the 3 part sink and handsink are impacted by the issue. A part has been ordered to repair the issue (see general comments for details).
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-202.12  (Pf) Hot water at 87F at the kitchen hand sink. Provide water of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.

Observed water at the kitchen hand sink to be 87F. The plumbing company has been called.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-201.11  (P) Soap was stored above dry storage food items. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

Observed Dawn liquid soap stored above dry storage food items. PIC removed the soap from the dry storage area and brought to toxic material area of kitchen. COS.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fan in kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Large fan in kitchen near dish washing area was observed to have noticeable amount of dust. Informed PIC to clean this fan before use. Will check upon next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Food employee washed hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and food employee was observed washing hands properly for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee returned to the kitchen after placing a roll cart in the walkin cooler and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves. Handwashing between tasks and prior to glove use were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks/as needed for the remainder of inspection.
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was full and contained new product/appeared to be recently replaced. The line was primed to attempt correcting the issue, but the sanitizer was not suctioning through the line. Detergent and rinse aid were dispensing properly. A call for service was made, and a technician arrived to fix the dish machine during the inspection. Technician replaced tubing for all the chemicals at the dish machine. All chemicals were dispensing and the dish machine was functioning properly upon conclusion of inspection. Final rinse was observed at 100ppm chlorine once the machine was repaired. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 100ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Metal baffle in the ice machine had mold buildup along the side and bottom edges. All other surfaces were observed to be clean. The metal baffle was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
6-501.111 Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed under the ice bin at the bar. Moisture and debris accumulation under the ice bin were promoting their presence. Fly management strategies were discussed, including frequent cleaning and use of fly strips in appropriate locations
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by eliminating harborage conditions.
citation_text:
6-501.112 A dead mouse and debris accumulation were observed on a glue trap under dry storage shelving. Frequent monitoring and replacement of glue traps were discussed.
Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the premises at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Bucket of discolored waste water with a strong odor was observed in the banquet room keg cooler. The waste water was emptied during inspection. Manager observed a slow drip occurring at the condenser in the cooler, which was likely the source of the liquid accumulation. Ensure the bucket is emptied daily and kept clean.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor under dry storage shelving had some debris accumulation and an old glue trap containing a dead mouse. Clean the floor under the dry storage shelving.
--Moisture and debris accumulation was observed on the floor under the bar ice bin and also on the attached plumbing. Clean in this area daily/as needed to eliminate a potential harborage location for fruit flies (see #38).
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee was observed eating while working at the roller grill. Employee was advised to cease the practice of eating while working with food. Ensure employees are eating and drinking in designated areas only.
Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands between tasks and was observed working the cash register prior to going to the drink counter and preparing coffee. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and staff were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-702.11 Sanitizer was not available for use. Manager confirmed a product called CAF Multi-Surface Cleaner and Degreaser was being used for wiping down surfaces and for sanitizing at the 3 part sink. Solution in a spray bottle did not test with any type of sanitizer test strip. Quat sanitizer was in use prior to this product but has not been available for a couple months. The practice of using the CAF product has immediately ceased. Bleach is available for use and will be used for making sanitizer solutions until quat sanitizer is obtained for use. A set of bleach test strips was provided for facility, and solutions were prepared at 100-200ppm.
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Spouts of coffee makers located above grounds basket were soiled with buildup. Ensure the spout is cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is no time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred or at least every 24 hours.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open packages of hotdogs in the walkin cooler were observed with date marks of 10/2 and a use by date of 10/9. Items should have been used or discarded as of 10/8 if opened on 10/2. Manager discarded hotdogs during inspection.
Also, an open package of creamer in the dispenser had a date mark of 10/5 with a use by date of 10/12. Manager was advised the use by date will be 10/11 based on opening the Saturday prior. Ensure staff know and understand date marking and proper time frame for use on required products.  
Ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-202.12 A chemical intended for use as a cleaner/degreaser has been used for sanitizing purposes. The manager immediately ceased using the product as a sanitizer during inspection. Product is not intended for sanitizing. Bleach will be used until quat is available for sanitization. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to the law, the FDA Food Code, and manufacturer's use directions included in labeling.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 A package of thawing hotdogs was observed under a small trickle of cold running water in the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Proper thawing methods were discussed, and water was turned on to allow for full submersion of thawing product under water.  
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Packages of bottled water available for purchase were observed outside the facility on display. Manager was advised the bottled water needs to be stored in the facility. Cease the practice of displaying bottled water outside the facility. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the left drain board of the 3 part sink. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage area. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) cart holding hotdogs and creamer in walkin cooler (buildup);  and
B) walkin cooler shelving - two sets closest to the wall with milk, etc. (mold/buildup).
Clean the aforementioned items.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor around soda syrup boxes in back storage was soiled with splash. Clean the floor.
--Condenser fan covers, ceiling above, and attached pipes were observed with general buildup of what appeared to be dust and mold. Clean the aforementioned surfaces in the walkin cooler. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed food remains including ketchup packet inside handwashing sink near bar area. Ensure handsinks are for handwashing only. Corrected. Education provided. Sink will be cleaned. Reference 5-205.11.
Observed no paper towels present in handsink near dishwashing area. Ensure handwashing sinks are accessible and have proper materials available during all hours of operation. Corrected. Towels provided. Reference 6-301.12.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Observed spatula to be sitting in clean area with food debris on it. Observed in-use knife to be in between wall and prep area. Observed can opener to be heavily soiled. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed and placed in cleaned areas. Reference 4-601.11(A).
Observed several sanitizer buckets to be to weak to be effective. Ensure proper concentrations (follow label) are reached when making sanitizer bucket. Remake sanitizer.  Corrected. Buckets will be remade and dispenser is at 400ppm. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed cooked mushrooms and taco meat to be 52F(probed) and 55F(probed) respectively. Items were discarded. Other tomato(cut) mix was just made ~1 hour ago and allowed to be rapidly cooled to 41F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed food (cooked mushrooms) to be uncovered in R-I Freezer near fryers. Ice accumulation was seen in R-I Freezer with strong indications of dripping occuring. Ensure foods are protected from potential contamination. Cover the mushrooms. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed black and pink residue starting to develop on ice machine. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed to prevent build-up. Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: REPEAT #1: Observed areas under equipment to be soiled. PIC stated cleaning team comes twice a week to clean debris. Areas will be targeted for cleaning. Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Allergen training as required
comment: REPEAT #1: No CFM has allergen training. Ensure all CFMs have allergen training. Obtain certificate. Reference PA 100-0367.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed approved bleach for cleaning food contact surfaces; however, facility lacks appropriate test strips to measure sanitizing solution concentration. PIC was made aware and will purchase chlorine bleach test stripes for 3 compartment sink. Inspector will return on or before 10/21/2019 to check corrective action.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Employee was observed to put on gloves without washing hands first. Hands must be washed before putting on gloves, any time the enter the kitchen, when switching tasks, etc. Hand washing was discussed with the manager.
citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed the ice bin at the drive thru to be stored in the open position when not in use. Keep ice bin closed when not in use.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed the following items to be soiled: 1) the inside of the prep cooler holding the liquid eggs with food debris, 2) the handles of the prep cooler and microwave with soil accumulation, 3) the SPEC1 & SPEC2 hot holding units with grease accumulation. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed sauce in the reach in cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 53 F. Sauce in the adjacent reach in cooler that was just delivered and put into service yesterday was probed at 47 and 55 F. It appears as though storing dough on the top shelves of the reach in cooler is impeding the cool air from circulating through the unit. All TCS foods out of temperature were discarded at the time of the inspection. Do not use coolers until certain they maintain foods at a temperature of 41 F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed cooked meatballs and cooked sausage in the back reach in cooler to be date marked 8-28 and 9-28 respectively. There were a few items dated 8-10 also. It was reported that those items are re-dated with a thaw date when pulled from the freezer, but one had exceeded the 7 days limit and one had not been re-dated when pulled to thaw. It appears the items dated 8-10 were meant to be dated 10-8. Items were discarded or redated as needed.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed several spatulas hanging above food prep areas that have significant chips in the food contact surfaces. Replace spatulas as needed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed deli meats such as turkey and bologna in the sandwich prep cooler that were not marked with the date of opening. There was also one tub of BBQ beef in the pizza prep cooler that was dated with an open date of 9/30--this exceeds the 7 days allowed. This was discussed with the manager. Date mark all ready to eat, time and temperature control for safety foods with the date of opening and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed the collar in the drain pipe for the soda fountain machine to have soil accumulation in it. Clean this drain pipe.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food properly labeled; original container
comment: Observed an unlabeled spray bottle with water in it that is used for the bread hanging above the prep table in the back. Spray bottle was labeled during the inspection to correct the violation.
citation_text: 3-601.11  (C) Food is not identifiable. Packaged food shall be identifiable. Reference 3-601.11.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: There is no lighting in the walk in freezer or walk in cooler. Provide sufficient lighting in walk in refrigeration units.
citation_text: 6-303.11 (A, B, C) (C) Lighting was found to be insufficient for that area. Light intensity shall be A) at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and other areas during periods of cleaning; B) At least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in areas where food is provided for consumer self-service or where fresh produce or packaged foods are sold or offered for consumption; inside equipment such as reach-in and under-counter refrigeration units; and in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, and equipment and utensil storage, and in restrooms; C) at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) in areas where employees are working with food or working with utensils or equipment where employee safety is a factor. Reference 6-303.11(A, B, C).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying mops: mops must be hung in a fashion that allows drip dry. C
Corrective action: hang mops upright in mop sink. COS.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
3.307.11 Misc. Source of Contamination: cans are sufficiently dented with creases and can contribute to contamination. C
Corrective action: Do not take receipt of cans that are dented. COS.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee working at the food counter register did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare a food order. Proper handwashing prior to donning gloves and preparing food was discussed. 
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of sanitizer at the bar was at 0ppm quat. Solution was discarded. New solution was prepared and observed at 400ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-201.11 Spray bottle of water intended for use during food prep was observed hanging between bottles of sanitizer and degreaser on the edge of the counter by the doorway leading to the back room. Water was moved to proper storage area with other food prep items. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic storage caddy at the bar used for bottle openers, drink strainer, and other equipment was soiled with sticky buildup. Caddy and all items stored inside were taken to dish area in back to go through ware washing. Ensure equipment is stored in a clean location.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-501.14 Upper edges and seams of 3 part sink basins and faucet handles were soiled with grease buildup. Clean the 3 part sink and faucets daily/as needed. Ensure removal of gross debris accumulation prior to ware washing. 
The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Liquid waste was puddling in the bottom of the holder for the left beverage gun at the bar. Liquid waste was not draining properly, and a half dozen fruit flies were observed in the area due to the presence of the liquid waste. The drain hose was disconnected to remove liquid waste from the holder. GM was advised to have facilities manager work with beverage distributor to resolve the drainage issue. Ensure liquid waste is removed nightly and all surfaces are cleaned and sanitized.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Handsinks and related fixtures in front food service area and in back ware washing area were soiled with greasy/grimy buildup. Clean handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean. 
--Drains behind beverage machines where Freestyle and Icee drain lines empty were soiled with mold buildup. Clean the drains and the drain lines that empty into the drains as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
--Floor drain under Freestyle machine on the north end of the food service area was heavily soiled with buildup of popping corn kernels and debris. Clean the floor drain.
--Electrical conduit bracket behind the Freestyle machine on the north end of the food service counter was observed with an accumulation of popping corn kernels. Clean the bracket.
--Floor in downstairs dry good storage room was observed with an accumulation of spilled popping corn kernels under bulk storage area. Clean the floor under bulk popping corn storage. 
--Floor in back storage area under ice machines and other equipment was soiled with general debris accumulation. Clean the floor in the back storage area. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed handwashing sink in sushi area to be blocked by multiple containers. Ensure handwashing station is always accessible. Corrected. Education provided. Handsink will be made accessible. Reference 5-205.11.
Observed large amount of food debris in handsinks. Ensure handsinks are used for handwashing only. Corrected. Handwashing sinks will be properly cleaned. Education Provided. Reference 5-203.11.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed chicken to be stored above other lower temperature foods. Ensure proper storage occurs. Corrected. PIC has corrected issue. Education provided. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed several knives to be soiled in clean area. This includes knives on knife rack and knife stored in between prep table and table. Ensure proper cleaning and storage occurs. Corrected. Knives have been cleaned. Education provided. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed food to be without cover in different areas throughout the facility while in coolers. Ensure foods are covered.  Reference 3-307.11.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed single-service items to be stored incorrectly with food debris on items. Ensure items are placed in appropriate manner. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: Observed personal drink in Prep Cooler #1 to be above open food. Ensure personal items to be below or away from food prep areas. Corrected. Education provided. Reference 6-403.11.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: Observed workers without food handler's certificate. Ensure all food employees have food handler's certificate. Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: Observed no allergen training from CFMs present in facility. All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program. Reference PA 100-0367.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: 6.501.112 Dead insect remains observed in storage area. Ensure routine cleaning occurs. C

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed the mixer in the ice cream station to be soiled with visible food residue. This was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct the violation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Wet wiping cloths observed stored on prep surfaces and not in sanitizer solution. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: Ice scoop observed stored with the handle in contact with the ice in the ice bin. Store scoops with the handle extended up and out of the food. Scoop was adjusted and ice in contact was scooped out.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Cake freezer observed with a significant amount of ice accumulation within. Defrost cake freezer. PIC reports that new seals are on order.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification was not present upon arrival of inspectors. Employee that was the PIC upon arrival of inspectors stated manager was at the 7th Street location. Manager returned later during the inspection. Manager stated he is between the two locations at the hospital multiple times a day in addition to covering at other locations as needed (breaks, etc.). The need for a certified food manager at all times at each location was discussed.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands prior to putting on a glove to handle baked goods. Proper handwashing prior to glove use was discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed prior to putting on gloves to handle food and after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11 Evidence was observed that indicated the handsink has been used as a dump sink. Discoloration, splash, and a small amount of grounds were observed in the handsink basin. Proper use of the handsink was discussed.  
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the handsink for any other purposes.
citation_text:
6-301.13 Paper towel and hand soap dispensers were observed on the walls by the prep sink and 3 part sink. The soap dispenser at the prep sink had soap in it, while all other dispensers were empty. Manager will place a work order to remove the dispensers from the aforementioned areas. 
A sink used for food preparation or utensil washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a handwashing sink as specified under §§ 6-301.11 and 6-301.12 and ¶ 5-501.16(C).
All sinks not used for handwashing should not be supplied with handwashing aids/devices.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text:
6-501.111 A half dozen fruit flies were observed on the wall adjacent to the soda machine up front. A dozen fruit flies were observed on the mop stored damp in the mopsink basin. Fly management was discussed, including use of fly strips in appropriate locations and general cleaning.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Lid to ice machine was open upon arrival of inspectors. Employee was up front making drinks and not retrieving ice at the time. Inspector closed the lid. Ensure the lid to the ice machine is closed between uses, especially with the presence of fruit flies in the back room.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp, soiled wiping cloth was observed in the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Employee stated it was used earlier and came from the sani-bucket. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Scoop in drink powder was stored with the handle submerged in the product. Scoop was repositioned to allow for proper storage of the handle up out of product.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12 Floors throughout had varying amounts of sticky buildup, especially in the back room. Debris accumulation was observed under the ice machine, soda syrup storage rack, and the 2 door upright cooler. 
Mold accumulation was also observed on the domed cover inside the floor drain under the 3 part sink. 
Clean the floors and the drain in the aforementioned areas
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.16 Damp mop was stored in the basin of the mopsink. Ensure proper storage of mop between uses to eliminate a potential harborage location for fruit flies.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.
citation_text:
6-501.114 Unused Gold Peak tea machine was observed next to the soda machine. Remove the tea machine from the facility.
The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee that was not a certified food manager did not have proof of food handler certification available at the time of inspection. Maintain copies of food handler certifications on-site.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Observed cup used for scoop in container of nacho tortillas chips used for pizzas.  Use a scoop with a handle that does not come into contact with food to avoid contamination.  Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) (1) Observed single use cups and paper towels stored directly on the floor next to automatic teller machine.  (2) Observed a box of pizza dough stored directly on the floor in the walk in cooler. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Volunteers were observed washing hands without proper technique. One person washed hands briefly for less that 20 seconds. Another person shut off the manual faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed, and a sign explaining proper technique is posted above the handsink. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow is also acceptable for shutting of the handwashing sink.

2-301.14 Volunteer did not wash hands at the designated handsink prior to putting on gloves. 
One volunteer was handling money and putting on gloves without handwashing in the same area to handle unwrapped deli sandwiches. Handwashing between tasks was discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must be washed before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling money.
citation_text:
2-301.15 One volunteer was observed washing hands at the 2 part sink, and another volunteer with gloved hands stated she washed her hands at the 2 part sink prior to inspector's arrival. Proper handwashing at the designated hadnsink only was discussed. Volunteers were later observed washing hands at the handsink. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 Volunteer was not wearing gloves while bagging popcorn. Popcorn was spilling over his hands during the process back into the bottom of the popcorn machine with remaining product. Glove use was discussed, and gloves were put on prior to bagging more popcorn. 
Food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment:
4-903.11 Single use gloves were observed out of the original packaging on a table in the cafeteria. Keep single use gloves in their original package until they are needed for use to protect gloves from potential contamination. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.
citation_text:
4-904.11 Plastic utensils were observed in containers with food contact surfaces and handles all facing multiple directions. Children get their own utensils, and the current storage practice allows for food contact surfaces to be touched by multiple hands. Store utensils all facing one direction so only the handles are touched. 
Single use utensils shall be stored and handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Volunteers were observed wearing the same gloves to touch various surfaces other than prepared, portioned food products and did not change gloves between touching general surfaces and going back to food handling. One volunteer preparing popcorn touched cardboard boxes with gloved hands, and another volunteer handled papers in a binder. A third volunteer used the back of her gloved hand to itch her nose. All persons in the kitchen at the time were advised on proper glove use, including changing gloves between tasks and after touching anything unrelated to food prep/handling. Handwashing prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes was also discussed.
One volunteer working at the money table was also responsible for serving prepared sandwiches with toppings. Tongs were available for handing tomatoes and pickles. However, gloves were worn to handle and slice sandwiches. It appeared the volunteer was preparing to put on the same pair of gloves that were removed and sitting by the pan of sandwiches. Gloves were discarded. Handwashing after handling money and prior to putting on gloves was discussed. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.
NOTE: Best practice is to immediately remove gloves when stepping away from food prep/handling. Discard the gloves that are removed. Get a new pair of gloves after properly washing hands prior to returning to food prep/handling.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to measure the surface temperature at the dish rack during a ware washing cycle. Options for temperature indicating devices were discussed, including a dishtemp plate simulator and dishwashing temperature test strips. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

The wash gauge was slowly moving and only reading at 120F after a half dozen full cycles. If the machine was ran several more times the gauge would likely be reading at 150F/above. The rinse gauge was reading between 180F and 190F, and it took multiple cycles for the surface temperature at the dishes to reach 160F. Get the dish machine serviced to verify proper function.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Person in charge is unsure of how dishware is sanitized when it is not run through the dish machine and it is manually washed, rinsed and sanitized instead. Facility has sanitizer prepared in a spray bottle for food contact surfaces, but this is not sufficient for sanitizing of dishware and is used for counters and tables. A residential dishwasher is available, but it is reported that this is not always used as they mostly use disposable plates and utensils. Provide a sanitizer such as Sani Tabs, which use the same test strip as the sanitizer in the spray bottle. PIC states they will ensure that all dishware and utensils are run through the dish machine and that they will verify that maximum registering thermometer reaches 160F each cycle to correct this violation.
citation_text: 4-702.11  (P) After cleaning, utensils must be sanitized before use. Reference 4-702.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Cleaner spray bottles are stored next to back up sugar shaker and creamer bottle. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11. Foods were moved to proper storage location.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used

Keep sincle use items protected at all times. Cups were discarded.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by a stack of sanitizer buckets . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11. Buckets were removed.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling cut melon is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Cut melon at 45F has been placed into other reach in cooler with no time or date. Place time and date marks on all food that is TCS which is placed into the cooler above 41F.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: No hand soap was available at the back hand washing sink near the three compartment sink. Soap was provided during the inspection to correct the violation.
citation_text: 6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed time and temperature control for safety foods in the reach in cooler near the steam tables to be probed at internal temperatures of 43-50F. Chemical dispensed properly; final rinse concentration was observed at ~75ppm chlorine. Ensure that management and staff are monitoring the dish machine, changing chemicals as needed, and using test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration (50-200ppm).
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify the concentration. 

4-602.11 Food thermometer stems were once again soiled. Note was left for staff - use sanitizer for wiping stems during continuous use, and manually wash, rinse, and sanitize the stems up to every 4hrs. 
Also - store thermometers in their own pan separate from pens, walkie talkie, and other items.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. 

Pizza slicers and trays were left in the pizza area from previous use and were soiled with food debris. Note was left for staff - remove to dish area at the end of operations daily. Clean and sanitize slicers and trays up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

Holder for the soda gun at the banquet area bar were soiled with buildup. Clean the soda gun and holder as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Clean and sanitize the soda gun and all components as directed by manufacturer's instructions or at a frequency that eliminates buildup of mold and general debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Server washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels. Server was advised on proper technique and use of a barrier when shutting off the faucet. Server re-washed hands with proper technique before continuing with work. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and cook washed his hands prior to continuing with his next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Cream cheese filling and fried portions of General Tso chicken were without date marks. Products were prepared as of the Saturday prior. Date marking was discussed, and foods were dated.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used

3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish that were received as frozen product were observed thawed in the bottom of the large prep cooler. Labeling on package states to remove fish from packaging prior to thawing under refrigeration. Proper thawing of frozen fish in vacuum packaging was discussed.
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures

3-501.16 Fish that was just cooked ~1hr prior to inspector arriving was observed on the cook line. Product was sitting in the wok but not being hot held. The internal temperature was 87F-97F. Food was for a delivery order that was to go out around 3pm. This is a bad practice to heat foods in advance and not hot hold them. Best practice is to make the food just prior to the delivery going out. Fish was to be reheated to 165F prior to delivery.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: 
-placing the food in shallow pans
-separating the food into smaller or thinner portions
-stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath 
-using containers that facilitate heat transfer
-adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods.

Once one of the above items has been done, food must be monitored to ensure proper temperatures are met. RECORD temperatures of cooling so inspectors/managers/cooks know what is occurring to that food in cooling process. Use a label on the food container or keep a log/notebook detailing the following:

Time and temperature food "started" the cooling process. 
Time and temperature after 2 hours of cooling. (during this time food should have gone from 135 degrees to 70 degrees to be considered properly cooled). 
Time and temperature after 4 additional hours of cooling process. (during this time food should have gone from 70 degrees to 41 degrees or colder). 

This is 6 HOURS of cooling process total. 2 hours to get from 135 to 70 degrees, and 4 more hours to get from 70 to 41 degrees. This process should be followed and monitored at all times on labels/paper.
