Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The drop guard on the ice machine (lower left side) is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. Drop guard was cleaned on site.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on open deli ham in the bottom of the prep cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Food was date marked.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf)  Observed food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Observed sauce bottle in bar area to be soiled on the dispensing nozzle. Observed can opener to be soiled on the blade. Items were cleaned immediately.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Curry sauce is 55°F. Sauce was left out during lunch serving time. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and 
(B). Chicken for is observed to be on the counter at 57°F. This item is often cooked and then not cooled completely or cooled and then taken out to sit on the counter during lunch service. Discussed which way they wanted to handle this item with Elliot. The chicken will be cooked and properly cooled. Portions will be taken from cold holding as needed for this dish. This time the chicken was allowed to be kept until 6pm for service. From this point on it will be discarded if held on the counter out of temperature.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text: 6-501.112  (C) Observed, dead, mouse in the soda closet ceiling. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate mice, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.112. The mouse was removed.  The facility has regular pest control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed a bag of carrots and a box of cauliflower on the floor in the walk in cooler. Also observed a fly strip to be hanging over the long skinny prep table in back where sauce is being placed into containers. The fly strip is empty and was removed. Discussed proper placement of such insect control devices.
citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the order machines which is trapped by plastic wrap. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: 6-304.11  (C) Excessive [heat / vapors / obnoxious odors / smoke / fumes] were found in the facility. A mechanical ventilation system of sufficient capacity shall be provided to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Reference 6-304.11. Obnoxious odor is evident in the facility.  Have the ventilation systems evaluated for proper function and repair.
citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11. Observed an employee phone to be sitting on a prep table. The phone was moved before anything could be said. Violation was immediately corrected.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation areas. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Store personal drinks in an area where they will not potentially contaminate food or single service items.  Reference 2-401.11. Cups were removed.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P Thirteen portion cups of ranch are observed to be sitting out at room temperature.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed a box of napkins on the floor in the dry storage area. Store single use items properly.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.
No CFM present at time of inspection. This is an ongoing issue at this facility.

title: Food obtained from approved source
comment: Facility has a rub on the shelves labeled "Marty's Rub It Raw" and that is in deli style containers that are not hermetically sealed with no labeling information on where these items are processed or packaged. PIC states that it comes from Marty's Hawg Sauce--see General Comments section for contact information from label. No permitting information is available at the time of the inspection. All foods must be processed and packaged in an approved, permitted and inspected facility and it is unknown whether this product is at this time. Rubs were pulled from the shelf and will not be offerred for sale until information is received.
citation_text: 3-201.11  (Pf) Packaged foods not properly labeled. Provide proper labeling.  Reference 3-201.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
1) Carrot cakes with cream cheese frosting that is made on site is observed held at ambient air temperature next to the register. Carrot cakes were voluntarily pulled from the shelves and will not be sold. It was discussed that cream cheese frosting must be held at 41F or below at all times unless food safety testing information has been obtained on this product.

2) Ground beef in the meat department case was probed at an internal temperature of 45F. Beef was ground yesterday. Thermometer when placed between two steaks in the middle of this cooler read 42F. Thermometer at the ground beef end read 40F and the thermometer at the opposite end read 50F. PIC stated that this cooler may be in defrost. Ensure that thermometers are accurate and cooler is holding foods at internal temperatures of 41F or below at all times. Cooler will be adjusted as needed.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was voluntarily pulled from shelves and will not be sold. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed several open, in use meats in the deli that are either not date marked or marked with dates that exceed the 7 days allowed for these products. Items include: PAP loaf with a use by date of 9/13, souse with a use by date of 9/17, honey turkey with a use by date of 9/17, pineapple ham with a use by date of 9/13, and several small portions with no date. There are also two hams with use by dates of 10/4 and 10/10 which exceed the 7 days allowed for TCS foods. Items were discarded or re-dated as needed to correct the violation.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Food properly labeled; original container
comment: Baked goods next to the register do not have ingredient or allergen labeling on the products. Provide this information in addition to the information already provided on the current labels.
citation_text: 3-602.11  (C) Prepackaged baked goods are not properly labeled. Label with: 1) common name of food, 2) ingredients, 3) net quantities, 4) name and address of packager, 5) food allergens, 6) nutrition labeling, 7) salmonid fish additives used. Reference 3-602.11.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: Observed backpacks and drinks on a shelf in the dry storage. CORRECTED- Discussed designated storage areas with PIC. Personal items were moved to their designated area.
citation_text: 6-305.11 (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment: Person in charge did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the wash, rinse, sanitize process, critical control points during the cooling process or proper cold storage organization. These items were discussed with the PIC. Handouts were left as indicated.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
1) Observed raw ground beef stored above the filling for crab rangoon and whole cuts of beef in the walk in cooler. Final cooking temperatures were discussed with the PIC in relation to storage in coolers. In the process of moving this ground beef, the juices spilled on a box of broccoli. Box of broccoli was voluntarily discarded. 
2) Observed raw shell eggs and personal foods stored above cooked pork and chicken in the reach in cooler at the front. Cooler was reorganized so that personal foods and raw eggs were below all ready to eat foods and food for the public.
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Store raw animal products below ready to eat foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Third compartment of the three compartment sink was not set up at the time of the inspection and food prep and service was steadily occurring. There were numerous knives on the magnetic strip that were soiled as well as a whole pan of utensils stored on a bottom shelf that had visible food remnants on them (appeared to be raw meat remnants). Sinks were cleaned and set up during the inspection and these items were washed, rinsed and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment: Observed garlic in oil on the cook line that was reported to have been put there this morning to be probed at an internal temperature of 77F with no indication marked as to when this was removed from cold holding. A time as a control policy will need to be completed (completed during the inspection) for the house made sauces and garlic in oil mixture that is kept at ambient air throughout the day. The time needs to be marked when these are removed from cold holding and any left at the end of 4 hours will need to be discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135°F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Observed a container of medicine stored intermingled with canned goods on the dry storage shelf in the back. Store medicines in designated areas away from food storage areas. Medicine was removed.
citation_text: 7-207.11  (P) Medicines that are in a food establishment for the employees' use must be labeled as specified under 7-101.11 and located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. Removed by employee. Reference 7-207.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Rice was observed soaking uncovered underneath the three compartment sink. Rice was removed during the inspection. There are also numerous other items under the sink such as fish, what appears to be chicken, and a rice noodle but these are reported to be personal. Do not store food under the plumbing.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed numerous wet wiping cloths sitting on surfaces throughout the facility. There is one sanitizer bucket prepared at the front cook line area. It was advised that the back half of the kitchen have a separate sanitizer bucket for their cloths as well.
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
1) Observed a trowel stored with the handle in contact with the rice. Store handles up and out of the food. 
2) Observed a knife stored in the crack between the prep table and prep cooler. Knife was removed and it was discussed that this is not a cleanable area and utensils should not be stored there.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Observed an ice scoop being used for scooping rice to be cracked and repaired with a wire. The area around the wire is visibly soiled. 
2) Observed the ice scoop in the ice machine to be cracked and repaired with a wire. These scoops were discarded. Replace scoops with new scoops that do not have unnecessary crevices.
citation_text: 4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Three compartment sink had soiled, soapy water in the middle sink and the other two compartments were empty but soiled. The process for wash, rinse and sanitize was incorrectly described by the person in charge. All dishes and utensils must be washed with warm, soapy water, rinsed in plain water, and then soaked for 60 seconds in warm sanitizer water (bleach prepared to 200 ppm as indicated on test strips). Sinks were cleaned and set up correctly during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.18  (C) The wash, rinse or sanitize solution within the three compartment sink is dirty. Drain and replace solutions in these compartments so the wash, rinse and sanitize operations will not be adversely affected. Reference 4-501.18.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Walls throughout the facility are soiled--most notably to the right of the ice machine in the back. Clean the walls.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Allergen training as required
comment: No proof of allergen awareness training completion. Hand-out left.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Employee was observed to briefly wash hands for only a few seconds before handling foods. Hands must be washed thoroughly with soap and water for 10-15 seconds before being rinsed, dried, and then using paper towel to turn off faucet. Hand washing was discussed.
citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment: Employee was observed to transfer cooked chicken from one plate to another with bare hands that had previously handled raw meats. Employee was addressed and these issues were discussed. Employees may handle raw animal products with bare hands provided that hands are properly washed first. Once foods are cooked, a barrier must be used to handle ready to eat foods. Bare hand contact must be avoided with ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed the mixer to be soiled with food debris, the citrus squeezer to be soiled with buildup, and the soda guns at the bar to be soiled with a black buildup. Wash, rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces. Items were taken to dish.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Observed two bottles of medicine and a container of protein powder stored on food prep areas in the kitchen. These items were removed from the kitchen. Do not store medications in areas where they may contaminate food.
citation_text: 7-207.11  (P) Medicines that are in a food establishment for the employees' use must be labeled as specified under 7-101.11 and located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. Removed by employee. Reference 7-207.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: 1) Observed cell phone charging cords hanging from the outlet and in contact with taco shells in the kitchen. There were also taco shells stacked out of a container and resting against the wall. Taco shells were discarded and moved as neccessary. 2) Observed the ice bin in the waitress station to be stored in the open position when not in use. Ice bin was pulled closed. 3) Observed an open can of tomato sauce in the reach in cooler in the kitchen. Acidic foods such as this must be transfered to a food grade container after opening the can.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed an employee wiping gloved hands that had just handled raw animal products on two towels that were hanging from his waist. He then used those towels as hot pads to handle plates. Avoid the use of common towels--if hands need to be wiped, they most likely need to be washed. Wiping cloths used for raw animal products should be used for no other purpose and stored in sanitizer solution in between use. Towels were removed.
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser in men's restroom was empty. Paper towels were provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Washed, peeled onions were observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. Onions were stored under a soiled shelf. Onions were covered during inspection. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Lo mein noodles in the bottom of the prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 49F and 55F respectively. PIC noted the product was sitting out during lunch service since ~130pm and was placed in the cooler once inspector arrived. Owner was advised to do time control with the noodles and use or discard within 4hrs. Cease the practice of sitting food out at room temperature and then placing it back in the cooler. Cooked lo mein noodles were added to time control policy during inspection.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked foods in the walkin cooler were not dated. Fried chicken portions for sweet and sour chicken, General Tso chicken, and cooked lo mein noodles were all prepared the Sunday prior. Proper dating of prepared foods was discussed, and date marks were provided. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food and held in food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11 Plastic grocery sack for carry out orders was observed lining a pan of food in the reach-in cooler. Pan was removed to allow for proper storage. Although the sack is a single serivce article it is not intended for food storage in direct contact with unpackaged and prepared foods. Use only food grade containers and bags, such as plastic food storage bags, for storage of unpackaged and prepared foods. 
FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the counter by the front handsink upon arrival of inspector. PIC placed wiping cloth in sanitizer for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Walkin cooler shelving was observed with varying amounts of debris accumulation. Clean the walkin shelves as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Strainer was observed in the top of the far left compartment at the bar four part sink, indicating use a dump sink the evening prior. This compartment is designated for handwashing only and was stocked with handwashing supplies. Strainer was removed from the sink, and a dump bucket was provided. All staff were advised on proper use of the sink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the left compartment at the bar four part sink as a dump sink.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration for the dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. An empty sanitizer jug was located near the fresh jug that was likely hooked up the evening prior. After running several ware washing cycles and priming the sanitizer line the final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 The stem of one food thermometer was observed with stuck on food debris. Thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Proper use and maintenance of thermometers were discussed. Food thermometers need to be cleaned after use and prior to storage.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods located in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 48F-54F. These foods were located in the middle section of the cooler and included salad greens, chicken skewers, pork, and blue cheese portions. Other foods in the bottom of the cooler on the far ends had internal temperatures at 43F, and foods in the top were at 40F-41F. TCS foods above 43F were discarded. 
The middle gasket was observed to be severely damaged causing the door to not shut properly on the cooler (see #47 for details). 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish portions were in the process of thawing in the walkin cooler at the time of inspection. Directions on the packaging states to remove vacuum packaging before thawing. At least one portion was fully thawed while others were still frozen. Management was advised to make sure the packaging removed prior to thawing. 
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 & 4-501.11 Middle door on the bottom of the cook line prep cooler was not shutting properly due to a damaged gasket. The right door was slightly askew on the bottom, and the topper with hinged lids had an area of disrepair on the left end that had duct tape on it. Manager on duty stated gaskets and a new hinged lid topper were ordered to replace parts in question (w/in ~30 days). In the meantime, no TCS foods should be held in the cooler beyond use during hours of operation. Store foods in the walkin cooler overnight until repairs are completed. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Equipment components such as doors, seals, and hinges shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-603.12 An old label was observed on a pan containing portions of sliced ham in the walkin cooler. The date on the label said 9/5, but the ham was sliced on 9/15 based on a label for fat filler also located in the pan. Old label was removed. 
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives. Ensure that labels are removed and all surfaces of pans are getting properly cleaned and sanitized between uses.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Fryers were observed with buildup of grease on the sides, underneath surfaces, and in the lower compartment where mechanicals are located. Clean the fryers.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Old sani-bucket containing sanitizer solution from the evening prior was observed on the cook line alongside a fresh sani-bucket. The old solution was discarded. Ensure sanitizer solutions are emptied throughout the day as needed and at the end of operations daily. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Walls in the dish area under the dish machine and 3 part sink were soiled with splash/general buildup. The plumbing under the 3 part sink was also soiled.
In addition, insulation and plumbing inside the wall under the 3 part sink were exposed due to recent repairs. Clean the walls and repair the wall in the dish area. 

Floors under ice machines were soiled with general debris. Clean the floors under the ice machines.

Floor under/behind fryers was soiled with grease and food debris. The floor was also damaged and holding grease where tiles were damaged. Clean under the fryers and repair damaged tiles.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Plastic tub with French fries in the chest freezer was observed without a lid. Also, frozen pastry bag was observed open in the walkin freezer. Make sure containers and packages of food are covered and closed for long-term, overnight storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in a spray bottle at the front counter had a concentration of 0ppm. Owner noted the spray bottle of sanitizer does not get used; staff use the sani-bucket during hours of operation. Solution was emptied and spray bottle was discarded. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash and food debris were observed inside the microwave. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Feta cheese in the prep cooler had a date mark of 9/9, which was last Monday. Owner was advised that 9/9 starts the 7 day time frame and the product was discarded. Ensure that foods prepared on Monday and require date marking are used or discarded by the end of the business day on Saturday since facility is closed on Sunday.

Open hummus, washed/cut lettuce, thawed/pre-cooked chicken breasts, and sliced/diced tomatoes in cold holding were all without date marks. Based on information provided, all products were prepared for use as of the Saturday prior. Proper dates were provided.
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Plastic spoon was observed in open hummus with the handle down in the product. Spoon was removed and discarded.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14 A chlorine test kit was available for use, but quat sanitizer is used at the facility. Owner noted they just ran out of strips over the weekend and he must have purchased the wrong strips. Inspector had some extra quat strips for facility to use until a new test kit can be purchased later today. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not yet prepared and available for use during morning prep. Solution was made available.
Sanitizing solution shall be provided and available for use during all hours of prep and operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) catch pan under soda machine (old soda splash);
B) counter under soda machine (dust/splash); and
C) outer surfaces of counter-top fryer (grease).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Sani-bucket containing old solution from Saturday was observed. Proper disposal of waste water was discussed. Solution was discarded and fresh sanitizer prepared for current day of operation. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of sani-bucket solutions after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility overnight.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-303.11 Light in the walkin cooler used for dry storage did not turn on. Owner noted it doesn't work right and sometimes comes on intermittently. Repair the light so it works properly.
The light intensity shall be at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) at a 30 inches above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed a tub of chicken in the walk in cooler that was probed at an internal temperature of 55F and shell eggs that were 54F. It appears as though these items are being pulled for use during busy periods and held at room temperature and then being cooled down after the rush. Maintain cold foods at 41F or below at all times. This is the same for the egg roll items that were stored above pans in the top of the prep cooler. Air flow circulates from the bottom and these will not be maintained at 41F without proper refrigeration. These items were all cooled rapidly to 41F or below as they were reported to have been out for less than 2 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: 1) Observed beans and tofu in the walk in cooler that were not covered. Many items were observed being covered at the time of the inspection. 2) Observed raw beef in the reach in freezer in the back to be stored directly in a grey Wal-Mart shopping bag. Beef was voluntarily discarded and it was discussed to store foods in food grade containers.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: Observed three knives stored in a soiled container at the end of the cook line. Knives and container were taken to the dish area to be washed, rinsed and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment: Observed kitchen staff chewing gum while cooking. CORRECTED- Discussed with employee. Employee discarded gum.
citation_text: 2-401.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result. (C)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed no soap provided at the bar handwashing sink. Provide soap for handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. (Pf)

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Chlorine sanitizer at less than 50 ppm at dish machine. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Maintenance dish machine sanitizer at correct concentration as stated on manufacturer label. Inspector will follow up on 9/23/2019.
4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the 2017 FDA Food Code. (P)

Observed can opener soiled with food debris. Observed ice machine soiled with pink mold accumulation. Maintain food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch. Inspector will follow up on 9/30/2019.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Date marking is not on half gallon of milk and smoked turkey slices in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Staff will label with the date foods were opened.
citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). (Pf)

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Observed oven cleaner stored on a shelf above the stove. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. CORRECTED- Employee moved materials to separated storage.
citation_text: 7-201.11 POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. (P)

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed wet wiping cloth stored on the 3 compartment sink drainboard. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Cloth was returned to sanitizer.
citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Inspector will follow up on 9/30/2019.
citation_text: 4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Observed Single-Use Articles stored directly on the floor  . Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 Bartender was observed slicing citrus with bare hands. Gloves do not need to be worn while washing produce, but once washed, produce must be handled with gloved hands if the produce will not be cooked. Bartender was advised on wearing gloves in addition to handwashing when preparing and handling citrus for drinks. Gloves were worn for the remainder of garnish prep.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the banquet room handsink. Ensure handwashing signage is maintained at all handsinks. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the kitchen handsink. Paper towels were provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer was not dispensing during ware washing cycles (see #48 for details). After priming the line for several minutes the sanitizer would still not dispense. A call for service was made. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify the concentration. 

4-602.11 Stems of food thermometers were soiled with grease and buildup. Thermometers were also stored in a soiled container with multiple writing utensils and other items. Food thermometers were cleaned during inspection. Ensure food thermometer stems are wiped with sanitizer or alcohol wipes between uses and receive a full wash, rinse, sanitize up to every 4hrs after continuous. Also, store thermometers in clean cases and storage pans between uses. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. 

Pizza slicers and trays were left in the pizza area from previous use and were soiled with food debris. Items were taken to the dish area for ware washing. 
Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

Nozzle and holder for the soda gun at the banquet area bar were soiled with buildup. Clean the soda gun and holder as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Clean and sanitize the soda gun and all components as directed by manufacturer's instructions or at a frequency that eliminates buildup of mold and general debris.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed inside the kitchen microwave. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Thousand island dressing and burger sauce were observed with date marks of 8/31 and 9/9 in the bottom of the sandwich cooler. Both items were discarded. Pasta salad made in-house was not dated in the top of the sandwich cooler and was also discarded. 
An open package of precooked gyro meat was not dated but was opened the weekend prior. A date mark was provided.  Feta cheese with a date mark from August was observed in the 3 door coolers. Cheese was discarded. 
Date marking was discussed. Ensure foods that require a date marking are properly dated.
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. Products prepared in-house even if commercially processed ingredients are combined together must also be dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Cook did not change gloves after taking a soiled bucket used to catch leaking water under the kitchen handsink and returning to sandwich prep cooler for prep. Glove use was discussed. Hands were washed and gloves changed prior to continuing with prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-204.117 Detergent and sanitizer were not dispensing during ware washing cycles. Lines were primed and several cycles ran prior to detergent eventually dispensing. Sanitizer was still not dispensing. A call for service was made for dish machine repairs.  
Warewashing machines shall be equipped to automatically dispense detergents and sanitizer.
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use, and morning prep was underway. Cook prepared a quat solution for use (200ppm). Maintain sanitizer solutions during prep/service hours.
Sanitizing solutions shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Leak was observed at the plumbing under the kitchen handsink. Repair the plumbing. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Old sani-bucket from the bar area was left in the kitchen overnight. Ensure proper disposal of used sanitizer solution as needed throughout the day and at the end of operations daily.

Pan of water was left in the warmer from use over the weekend. Warmer is only used one day a week. Ensure the pan is getting emptied and cleaned after use and prior to storage. 

Bucket of liquid waste was observed in the banquet bar keg cooler. Ensure the catch basin for the drain line in the banquet room keg cooler is emptied daily/as needed and maintained clean. Properly dispose of all keg cooler waste liquid daily/as needed.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12  Cover was missing at the floor drain under the metal bin in the banquet room bar. Provide a grated cover for the floor drain in question. 

Floor was soiled with buildup in and an old drain that appeared to be no longer in use under the prep sink that at one time had a garbage grinder. The floor around the drain was soiled also. Clean the area in question. If the drain is no longer in use, consider providing a cover that will keep debris from getting down in it. 

Kitchen handsink had buildup in the basin. Clean the handsink and related fixtures daily/as needed.

Wall behind the soda syrup boxes had dried splash on it, and wall in dish area under sinks and counters was soiled with buildup. Clean the walls in the aforementioned areas.

Mopsink basin and walls around it were soiled. The lower wall to the right of the basin was also damaged. Clean in and around the mopsink daily. Repair the damaged section of the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner and all staff that were certified food managers have expired certifications. Owner is working on getting himself and his staff re-certified (see general comments for details)
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12, 2-301.14, & 2-301.15 Bartender was observed rinsing hands at the prep sink by the salad cooler in the kitchen and then retrieving paper towels from the handsink by the walkin cooler to dry his hands. Bartender was advised to always use designated handsinks for handwashing and to properly wash hands when needed.
Owner wiped his hands on a dry wiping cloth between tasks while working on the cook line. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and owner washed his hands at the handsink prior to continuing with preparation of a food order. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Back handsink adjacent to the dish area was used to prepare a sani-bucket. Owner was advised to cease using the handsink for any purpose other than handwashing. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration at the dish machine was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bucket was changed, and several cycles ran to eventually show a final rinse concentration of 100ppm. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Can opener blade was soiled along the edge with buildup. Can opener was placed in dish area to go through ware washing.
Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use for items such as the can opener. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Pan of alfredo sauce in the walkin cooler prepared this morning at 10am was observed with an internal temperature of 48F after 4pm. Portion in question was discarded. A smaller portion of alfredo also prepared this morning and cooled was observed at 41F. Owner noted ice baths were used prior to placing pans in the walkin cooler. Parameters for proper cooling were discussed.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Bowl of salad in the chiller was observed with surface temperatures of 46F-52F and internal temperatures of 50F-52F. Product was in use since 11am and was discarded.
Sliced tomato and cut leaf lettuce on the server line held in an ice bath had internal temperatures of 60F and 55F respectively. Only the bottom of the pan was in direct contact with the ice bath. Lettuce and tomato were discarded. Whipped butter packets in a pan at the same ice bath had internal temperatures of 41F for packets in the bottom of the pan and 84F for those in the top. Butter packets were discarded. A time control policy was established for these three items during the inspection today. 
Fettuccine in the 2 door cooler had an internal temperature of 48F-50F. Owner noted it was out for ~45 minutes during lunch service. Temperature was to be monitored and noodles discarded if they did not drop to 41F/below within the hour. 
Top portion of cooked vegetables in an ice bath on the cook line had an internal temperature of 53F, while the product lower in the pan was at 41F. Owner was advised on submersion of pans in ice baths and use of less product to help maintain colder temperatures. Top layer of vegetables were removed and discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked chicken and at least one pan of noodles in the 2 door cooler did not have date marks. Also, an open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler was without a date mark. Prep/open dates were provided. Ensure proper dates are indicated on all ready to eat, refrigerated foods that require date marking. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 A spray bottle at the bar labeled hard surface sanitizer was straight bleach (test strip bleached out when checked). Chemical was discarded by the owner. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was checked in an ice bath and was observed reading below 30F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.  

4-204-112 Thermometers were not present in the 2 door cooler and the salad cooler. Provide functioning thermometers for all cold holding units used for storage of TCS foods. Thermometers were provided.
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Magnetic knife strip at the salad prep table was soiled with dust/crumbs along the top and general buildup on the magnetic strip. Clean the knife strip daily/as needed and maintain it clean. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-303.11 Sani-buckets were not available for use in the kitchen. Owner prepared a quat solution for use (200ppm).
Sanitizing solutions shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: 410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 None of the staff that will be certified food managers have completed the online food allergen awareness training. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee in back prep area did not wash hands upon exiting the walkin cooler and prior to putting on gloves to continue with prep. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for the remainder of the inspection
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Handsink at front service/drive thru area had ice in the basin indicating use as a dump sink. Staff and management were advised to cease the practice of using the handsink for anything other than handwashing.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was at 0ppm at the front counter and ice cream station. Manager noted the solutions were prepared recently. Fresh solution was dispensed in a bucket and observed at 200ppm. Manager was advised some wiping cloths when dry and placed in fresh sanitizer solution absorb chemical out of the solution. Ensure the wiping cloths are rinsed with sanitizer from the dispenser prior to placing in fresh solution to maintain concentration. Use test strips to verify concentration. Check solutions during operations and change as needed. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. 

Dish machine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Proper suction was not occurring because the tube as pushed down to far and curled up in the bottom of the chemical bucket. Manager adjusted the tubing, provided a fresh/full chemical bucket, and primed the sanitizer line. After two full cycles the dish machine final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Stem of food thermometer available for use on the cook line was soiled with grease and food crumbs. Thermometer was cleaned and calibrated during inspection. Ensure the stems of food thermometers are wiped between uses with sanitizer and properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.
Food contact surfaces of food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storing and sanitized before use after cleaning. 

Underneath surface of heat lamp at fry station hot holding was soiled with accumulation of stuck on grease. Debris as hanging over where fried foods are held prior to service.
Clean the underside of the heat lamp as needed to eliminate buildup that could fall onto food. 

Baffle inside ice machine was soiled with mold accumulation, especially along the lower edge. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Personal cleanliness
citation_text:
2-402.11 Female employee with long blonde hair was walking around in the kitchen and front service area without hair restraint. Manger on duty noted she was in the process of setting up equipment. Staff were advised that at minimum long hair needs to be pulled back in a ponytail while working in the kitchen around food and equipment regardless of the task being performed. Employee pulled hair back in a ponytail, and all staff were observed with hair properly restrained upon opening for business.
Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair, that are designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; and unwrapped single service and single use articles.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee that opened the back door with gloved hands to allow inspector access for inspection was observed returning to dish area and continuing to work without changing gloves. Employee was approaching clean dishes and was advised to ensure gloves are changed after touching general surfaces such as the back door. Employee discarded gloved in question.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) dish machine - top/general surfaces (buildup);
B) fryers - surfaces between and underneath (grease/food debris); and
C) heat lamp at fry station hot holding - general surfaces (grease).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness training was not available for CFMs. Manager on duty contacted GM during inspection. The internal eLearning program may qualify. GM was going to check with corporate on this matter as of the previous routine inspection. An ANSI/ASTM accredited allergen awareness training certification is required for certified food managers at high risk facilities, and certifications needs to be maintained on-site along with manager certifications. 
Provide copies of allergen training certifications for CFMs by the next routine inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: 3-501.17  (P) Observed no date mark on french vanilla creamer bag. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Reference 3-501.17.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed use by date to be 09/08 on bag of whipped topping.  Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge.  Reference 3-501.17.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Observed boxes of single-use cups to be stored directly on the floor. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 & 2-301.14 Employee was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands. Employee was advised on handwashing between soiled and clean dishes.
Cook put on gloves to work at/clean around the grill side prep cooler without first washing hands. Handwashing prior to glove use was discussed.
Waitress washed hands at server area handsink without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands.
Management was advised to reiterate proper handwashing and when to wash hands with all staff. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

2-102.11 PIC was not documenting information in the daily log book as required by the company HACCP plan. When asked why no information was documented for rice preparation, calibration of tools (pH meter and food thermometer), and other required documentation, the PIC stated she remembers information and writes it down at the end of the day. PIC was advised this information must be written down as tasks are completed and she should not be relying on memory alone. Also, as tasks occur if issues arise, corrective actions need to be accurately documented.
Sushi rice was prepared around 12pm based on information provided, but the time was not documented anywhere. Sushi rice is required to be used or discarded within 6hrs of preparation and must have a pH of 4.1 or below per the company standard. Due to lack of documentation, PIC was asked to calibrate the pH meter and check the pH of the rice during inspection. Sushi rice was observed with a pH of 4.2. When PIC was advised to add more vinegar to lower the acidity, she seemed confused and asked if more rice needs to be added to change the pH. The pH was lowered by adding more vinegar and was observed with a pH of 4.0 after corrective action was taken. PIC was advised to follow the steps in the directions provided in the HACCP plan every day to ensure proper pH of sushi rice.
