The ice cream has melted and dripped onto glasses below. PIC is instructed to store employee foods separate from items intended for consumers. The drinks/foods were moved during the inspection and the contaminated glass moved to the dish machine.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program. No allergen training has been completed at the time of the inspection. PIC is instructed to have CFPMs complete an ANSI accredited course prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed dishwasher to reach 132F. However, no sanitizer was present in machine. Corrected. Employee fixed issue. Cl- 100ppm. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment: Observed chicken to be 100F in cooling process in walk-in cooler.  According to PIC, chicken had been cooled since ~1430. Corrective Action. Chicken will be rapidly reheated to 165F and recooled with proper method. Education provided. Reference 3-501.14.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed chicken and pork to be out of temperature in prep cooler (T). These were probed at 56F and 46F respectively. Ensure proper cold holding occurs for all cold-held TCS foods. Corrective action. PIC stated products were placed in prep (T) around noon(1200). Products will be cooked and sold within six hours or discarded. Repair prep cooler. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: Observed large pans being used in facility to cool products. Ensure proper cooling equipment is used to cool foods. This includes shallow pans, small amounts of food placed in containers, ice, ice wands, and other cooling methods. Implement new cooling methods to ensure adequate cooling. Reference 3-501.15.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: Observed several dead roaches in downstairs area. Ensure remains of insects and any other pests are removed from premise in timely manner. Reference 6-501.112.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed food equipment to be placed in soiled "clean" area. Ensure equipment is placed in clean area. Clean areas as needed to prevent soil accumulation. Corrected. PIC will clean containers. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
(REPEAT #1) No CFM was present during inspection. Ensure adequate amount of CFMs are present for full coverage of food operation. Obtain CFM. Reference 750.540.
(TD* #2 was changed to #1) 8/20/2019

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed walk-in freezer to have ice build-up. In addition, ice appears to drip onto food containers. Ensure frost build-up is prevented. Also, protect food from potential cross-contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed bucket of ice for customer self-service without protection from contamination. Provide a lid or other protection measures for items on the customer self-service counter. CORRECTED- Staff removed bucket of ice from customer self-service counter at time of reinspection. Staff will provide ice to customers upon request until a lid or other protection can be provided for the ice available for customer self-service.
citation_text: 3-306.11 Except for nuts in the shell and whole, raw fruits and vegetables that are intended for hulling, peeling, or washing by the CONSUMER before consumption, FOOD on display shall be protected from contamination by the use of PACKAGING; counter, service line, or salad bar FOOD guards; display cases; or other effective means. (P)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed carts blocking the handwashing sinks in the dish area and back prep room. Also observed a carafe in the back prep room handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Carts were relocated and carafe was removed. Discussed with PIC and provided education. Ensure handwashing sinks are always easily accessible to allow frequent handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: Observed forks in the back prep room stored with the eating ends up. Store utensils inverted to prevent contamination during storage and handling. CORRECTED- Utensils were rearranged to be stored inverted.
citation_text: 4-903.11 (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be stored (2) Covered or inverted. (C)

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed single-use straws stored under the buffet counter sink. Store single service utensils where they are protected from contamination. CORRECTED- Straws were moved to another cabinet.
citation_text: 4-903.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; and (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11. Owner was chewing gum while working in the back prep and front service areas. Owner discarded gum upon request of inspector.
Employees shall eat, including gum or candy, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed on the ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle and also along the lower edges of the baffle. Cleaning and maintenance of ice machine were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions in sani-buckets had concentrations of 0ppm and 10ppm chlorine. Solutions were remade and then observed at 100ppm. Label directions for product in use requires a concentration of 200ppm. Solutions remade by owner and verified at 200ppm with test strips. Employee working with owner was advised on proper concentration for product in use
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Meatballs, jerk chicken soup, and potato soup had surface and internal temperatures ranging from 120F-130F. Meatballs and soups were in the right warmer. All products in the left warmer were at 160F/above. Right warmer was adjusted to a higher setting to reheat foods to 165F. Within ~45 minutes foods were above 150F. Staff were advised to stir products and verify proper reheat to 165F prior to serving. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Cheese slices in the top holding area of the prep cooler were observed with surface temperatures above 50F and internal temperatures of 48F and 54F. Cheeses were placed in the cooler at ~1230pm. Owner was advised cheeses could be used or discarded by 630pm as long as they didn't get above 70F. If they warmed above 70F the cheeses need to be discarded by 430pm based on information provided. Cheese was to be used or discarded accordingly based on temperature of product.
Also, surface temperatures of foods were in the high forty degree and low fifty degree farenheit range due to the way foods were stocked. Owner was advised to be careful with overstocking, and products were to be re-portioned so foods were not stocked above ill lines in pans to help maintain colder temperatures. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach currently in use for sanitizing did not have proper labeling. Bleach in question was likely purchased when facility needed to buy some in a pinch. Options for locations to purchase bleach last minute were discussed. Owner was advised to make sure the staff know the label requirements (EPA registration number; instructions for use with food contact surfaces; and concentration listed in ppm for sanitizing food contact surfaces). Proper bleach was available in the storage room and made available for use. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was reading above 120F at ambient temperature. Thermometer was calibrated using the ice water method during inspection. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Leak was observed at the pipe under the handsink. Repair the plumbing at the handsink
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Allergen awareness training has not been completed by certified food managers. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager handled phone and did not immediately wash hands prior to handling utensils and thermometer to continue with morning prep. Manager was advised on handwashing between tasks and washed hands prior to continuing with prep. Manager was observed washing hands properly between tasks for the remainder of the inspection.
An employee arrived to work and did not wash hands prior to beginning setup of the 3 part sink for ware washing. Employee washed hands upon request of inspector. Manager stated he would reiterate the importance of handwashing and when to wash hands with the employee.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands and upon arriving to work prior to doing anything in the prep, service, and ware washing areas.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text:
3-101.11 Ice in the ice machine was contaminated with chunks of mold. The ice machine was unplugged and ice was removed. Manager contacted the owner to inform that the ice machine could not be used until it has been properly cleaned and fully serviced. A spot check will be conducted before the next routine inspection to check on the status of cleaning and maintenance.  
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on surfaces inside the ice machine. Cleaning and maintenance of ice machine were discussed. Ice machine was taken out of service due to the presence of mold in the ice (see #13).
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Container of egg salad in the bottom of the prep cooler had a date mark of 8/2-8/8. Egg salad was removed and discarded. 
Sliced tomatoes in the two door cooler had a date mark of 8/13-8/19. All tomatoes in the container and leftover from the previous day of operation in the top of the prep cooler were discarded. 
Prepared refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Open bottle of Gatorade was observed on top a plastic wrap box on the back ledge of the pizza prep cooler. Personal beverage was removed from the area. Consumption and storage of personal drinks were discussed.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 & 2-301.14 Cook had a wiping cloth hanging from his back pocket. When asked about the use of said cloth, cook noted he uses it to wipe his hands. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage upon request of inspector. Cook was advised if hands need to be wiped then they should be properly washed at a designated handsink, and disposable paper towels need to be used to wipe hands upon completing handwashing. 
Cook handled his a cell phone and then prepared to put on gloves without first washing hands. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 
Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. The process took less than 20 seconds, and a barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Cook was advised on proper handwashing. Proper handwashing technique poster was observed at the kitchen handsink. 

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.  To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text:
3-101.11 Chicken wings in the walkin cooler were spoiled. A strong odor was present when the lid was removed. Employee noted he forgot to throw the wings out the day prior, and the container had a date from late July on it. Wings were removed from the cooler and discarded during inspection. 
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Stem of digital food thermometer was soiled with old food debris buildup. Use and general maintenance of thermometers were discussed. Thermometer in question was set aside for cleaning. Another food thermometer was available for use. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer solution are used to wipe the thermometer probe during temperature checks, make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Small pizza trays and pan holding trays were soiled with food debris. Pan and pizza trays were placed in dish area to go through ware washing.
Clean and sanitize pizza trays and the storage pan daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of food and other debris.
citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer concentration was observed at 0ppm chlorine at the bar dish machine. Very little product remained in the sanitizer jug that was currently in use, which resulted in the lose of suction within the chemical tubing/product not moving through the chemical line. A new bottle of sanitizer was connected and the machine was primed. The concentration of the final rinse was then observed at 100ppm. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Ensure the final rinse concentration does not drop below 50ppm and is no stronger than 200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Two containers of cheese sauce were observed in the walkin cooler, one dated 8/8 and the other dated 8/14. The cheese sauce dated 8/8 was removed to be discarded. Cheese sauce that was being reheated for lunch service was from the 8/8 container and was removed from the cook line for discard. Cook began to reheat a new portion of cheese sauce from the container dated 8/14. 
Open package of deli meat in the bottom of the pizza cooler did not have a date mark. Deli meat was opened earlier in the week and provided with a proper date mark. 
Ranch dressing portions made in-house had a prep date of 7/30. Portions of ranch dressing in question were discarded. 
Italian beef portions in the bottom of the prep cooler had a date mark of 8/6. Beef was cooked, portioned, and frozen on 8/6 and was pulled from the freezer yesterday for use. The date on the container was changed to reflect proper date mark (5 days left for use as of today). 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on the ledge of the ice machine, which is not considered a clean surface. A container was provided for storage of the ice scoop between uses. Staff were advised to clean and sanitize the ice scoop and storage container daily/as needed.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

Chemical sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

A) walkin cooler shelves along right wall (mold/general buildup - lower shelves); 
B) inside oven (carbon buildup);   and
C) drip tray under stove burners (food debris/splash).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 An ice cream scoop and chunk of walnut were observed in the basin of the server area handsink. Both items were removed from the basin. Manager stated he would speak with servers about proper use of the handsink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the server area handsink for any other purposes.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Dish machine sanitizer concentration was observed at 0ppm chlorine. A full bucket of sanitizer was observed connected to the machine. An air bubble was present, and product was not suctioning properly through the line. A call for service was made, and dishes were manually sanitized at the 3 part sink (200ppm quat) until the dish machine was repaired. A technician arrived for repairs during the inspection. Upon checking the chemical lines and priming the machine the sanitizer concentration was observed at 50-100ppm.
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain sanitizer at the dish machine to allow for proper sanitization of dishes, and use test strips to verify concentration of final rinse. 

Quat solution in one of the sani-buckets at the AL dining area was observed with a concentration of ~100ppm quat. New solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions as directed by the label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Can openers were observed with buildup along the edge of the blades. Can openers had not been used during prep today. Both can openers were taken to the dish area to go through ware washing. 
Milkshake machine was observed with dried food splash on surfaces above mixing wands from the day prior. Proper cleaning and sanitizing of milkshake machine food contact surfaces was discussed. Manager noted the machine would be cleaned and sanitized by servers prior to being used today.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Soda nozzle and diffuser at the server area soda machine were observed with mold buildup. Manager stated all nozzles and diffusers would be cleaned by servers prior to lunch time use.
Beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Date marks of 8/8 and 8/12 were observed on pre-cooked seafood and noodles in the bottom of the grill prep cooler. Both items were removed for discard. A pan of deli turkey in the bottom of the grill cooler was observed without a date mark. Turkey was just prepared and labeled with a proper date mark.
Open cartons of liquid egg whites and heavy whipping cream were observed without date marks in the bottom of the sauté cooler. Items were opened over the weekend and provided with proper date marks.  
Commercially processed and prepared, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, once opened and prepared if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Sani-bucket in the prep area was observed with a wiping cloth hanging over the edge and not properly submerged in sanitizer solution. Wiping cloth was placed in the solution for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee did not change gloves after removing a soiled can opener from the prep area and returned to vegetable prep. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were changed before continuing further with prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

Floor drain under the dirty dish drain board at the 3 part sink had buildup down inside. Clean the floor drain as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

comment: REPEAT #1: Employee present does not have food handler's license. Ensure all food employees have food handler's training certificate. Obtain certificate. Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed blue cheese dressing in the pump dispenser in the prep cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 68F. This was congruent with the thermometer inside the bottom of the unit also. There were also numerous bags of this dressing in the produce walk in cooler that were probed from 53-60F. These bags may possibly have been stored in the bottom of the prep cooler before being placed in the walk in--these dressings were all discarded at the time of the inspection. citation_text:

Clean and sanitize food thermometers between uses and before storage

Clean the pizza oven at the end of operations daily.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 All food thermometers were checked with ice water to verify accuracy after one digital thermometer appeared to be reading much higher than all the other thermometers. Digital thermometer in question was reading between 31F-32F, but two metal stem thermometers were observed reading below 30F in ice water. Thermometers were calibrated to 32°F in an ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

citation_text:

Thermometers should be clean when placed in the storage cup and need to be protected from potential contamination between uses.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
No CFM has completed allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Staff working at time of inspection had food handler certifications but none had a proof of a current food manager certification. The new manager is scheduled to attend a course and get his manager certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed quickly washing hands for less than 20 seconds. The faucet was shut off without a barrier, and the handle of the paper towel dispenser was touched to retrieve paper towels after process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and all staff working in the front service area re-washed hands properly. Educational handout on proper handwashing technique was provided.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
 To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11 Women's room handsink was observed to be extremely slow draining. As water was running the sink filled up and standing water remained for several minutes. Once water drained it was possible to see buildup in the grated drain cover. The buildup, which appeared to be mold, was causing the issue. A toothpick was used to clean out the drain cover holes enough to allow for proper drainage, and cleaner was poured down the drain. Clean the handsinks, including the drain covers, daily/as needed and make sure they are draining properly.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times.
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at handsinks in the back prep area, the front service area, or in the women's room. Handwashing signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in sanitizing compartment of 3 part sink was observed at 100ppm. The label directions for the bleach used at the facility shows a required concentration of 200ppm. Solution was freshly prepared and ware washing just started for a knife and the slicer used during morning prep. Additional bleach was added to the solution to bring the concentration to 200ppm. 
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee was observed drinking from a personal beverage with gloved hands and proceeded to the front service area. Employee opened the prep cooler and moved utensils to the make line to begin preparing an order. Employee was advised on proper glove use. Gloves were discarded. Hands were washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food preparation. Educational handout was provided on proper glove use.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Online food allergen awareness training has not been completed by management. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Can opener had chunky buildup on the blade. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned between uses, any time contamination may have occurred, and up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

Measuring spoon for seasonings at wok was soiled with buildup. Measuring spoon was set aside at 3 part sink to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Surface inside the lid of the prep cooler was soiled with general buildup. Clean the inner surface of the lid on the prep cooler daily/as needed. Sanitize the lid after cleaning. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred or at least every 24hrs. 

Nozzle of soda gun at the bar had mold inside the tip. Nozzle was taken to 3 part sink to be cleaned and sanitized. Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed on the ceiling inside the microwave.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Rice in small warmer set aside to make fried rice had an internal temperature of 116F. The small portion of rice observed below 135F was just removed from the large cooker of rice within the hour that was observed holding product at 177F. The small warmer accidentally got turned off. Warmer was turned back on to begin heating the rice, which was going to be fried and then hot held. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Pan of cooked pork in the walkin cooler was observed without a date mark. Owner stated the pork was cooked and frozen within the last couple days. The pork was just pulled to be thawed for use today. Date mark of 7/24 was placed on the pan, and staff were advised the pork needs to be served or discarded within 6 days counting today as day 1 of 6. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41ºF/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach without proper label was available for use. Employee went to store and purchased bleach with a proper label that had an EPA registration number and instructions for sanitizing food contact surfaces with a concentration listed in ppm. Bleach without proper label was set aside to be used for general cleaning and disinfecting purposes. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

Repair the screen door so it is protected against the entry of pests.

Reference 3-304.12.

Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of cooking temperatures. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Provide designated area for drinking.  Reference 2-401.11.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Hand washing sink in the kitchen is not operational at the time of the inspection. Cook was advised that the hand washing sink at the bar should be used until the kitchen hand sink can be repaired and inspector demonstrated this practice. Cook was not observed to wash hands in at the bar but actively began putting on gloves and making during the inspection. Hand washing was discussed but was not observed properly at the hand sink at the bar.
citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
1) Hand washing sink is being replaced during the inspection and there is no water hooked up to it or drain pipe at the beginning of the inspection. Cook states that he is using the three compartment sink in the kitchen to wash hands. Hands may only be washed in a designated hand washing sink and must be washed before food handling. Plumber is on site repairing the sink at the time of the inspection. 

2) Observed ice in the hand washing sink at the bar. This is a 4 compartment sink with the left sink as the hand washing sink. Use mop sink off kitchen as dump sink or dump into a bucket that is emptied at the end of each night or as often as needed to prevent pests. 

5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.
citation_text: 5-202.12  (Pf) Provide water of at least 100 deg F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored above ready to eat dressings in the reach in cooler in the kitchen. Raw shell eggs were moved to an area below ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw meat products to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
1) No sanitizer buckets were prepared in the kitchen or the bar area despite active food handling and serving occurring. Sanitizer buckets must be prepared before food prep and service to sanitize surfaces and keep wet wiping rags stored in. Sanitizer bucket was prepared in the kitchen and bar. Storage of this bucket was discussed. 

2) Observed the pizza pan rack where the in use pizza slicer was stored to be soiled with grease and food debris. Wash, rinse and sanitize these items.
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment: Cheese sauce in the steam table since 3 pm was probed at internal temperatures that varied from 130-150F. Cook reports that he had put it on the stove for a short period of time to reheat before being placed in the steam table. He stated that reheat temperature was 135F and had not taken the temperature of it. Cheese was pulled and placed on the stove to rapidly reheat to 165F at the time of the inspection. Reheat temperature discussed.
citation_text: 3-403.11  (P) Food was not reheated to 165°F within 2 hours, before being placed in hot holding. Reviewed reheating requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Food was reheated to proper temperature. Reference 3-403.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Foods in the top section of the prep cooler were probed at 48-50F. Raw beef in the bottom was probed at 41F. Cook states he had just sliced the tomatoes and ham so it was hard to determine if the top was holding foods appropriately at 41F or below or not. 

2) Meatloaf, tuna salad and all TCS foods in the walk in cooler were probed at internal temperatures of 45F. This was noted on the previous routine inspection as well. Coolers must maintain TCS foods at 41F or below at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed two bags of sliced deli turkey (one very dry and hard on the ends) without date marking and two bags of sliced deli ham with dates that had rubbed off in the reach in cooler in the kitchen. These were discarded. There was also meatloaf, tuna salad and an open gallon of milk in the walk in cooler that were not date marked with the date of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
1) Observed containers holding items such as tomatoes, and bags of cheese stored in direct contact with mushrooms and onions in the containers below. Do not stack container bottoms in direct contact with ready to eat foods. Top containers and bags were pulled during the inspection and placed in the cooler below. 

2) Observed a bag of onions stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. Store foods 6" off the floor.
citation_text: 3-305.14  (C) During preparation, unpackaged food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-305.14.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on top of the reach in cooler at the bar. No sanitizer bucket was prepared and it was discussed that this needs to be prepared to store wet wiping cloths submerged within sanitizer solution.
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored

Pizza slicer was moved and then was placed in sanitizer solution that cook had prepared for the sanitizer bucket for the kitchen. Remove slicer and wash, rinse and sanitize in the three compartment sink. Store slicer clean and dry or time control so that it is washed, rinsed and sanitized every 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

citation_text: 5-202.11  (P ) Plumbing is not designed , constructed and installed properly. Contact a licensed plumber to repair/replace to comply with Illinois Plumbing Code. Reference 5-202.11.

Reference 6-101.11.

Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C). Cups were moved up off of the floor immediately.

title: Allergen training as required

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

Reference 2-401.11.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: Several live adult roaches are observed in the dish area of the kitchen. There is a corner to the left of the dish machine with caulk that is not smooth, and a couple adults were observed sitting in this area with one dead adult in the water on the table below. There was also a live adult on the dish machine itself. When looking through other areas near the kitchen, there is a large mechanical room where the hot water heaters are located that is warm and dark and numerous live adult roaches are observed in this room that is just off the kitchen. Adams Pest Control was reported to be here and treated on 7/11 and again this past Wednesday. A call was placed for pest control service at the time of the inspection and they should be here at some point today. 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Pasta salad prepared prior to inspector's arrival was observed in a covered plastic container in the walkin cooler. The surface and internal temperatures were observed at 83F and 105F respectively. Time and temperature during cooling process was not being tracked, but based on information provided the product was still within the first 2hrs of the cooling process. Pasta salad was stirred and container left uncovered to allow for more rapid chilling. The pasta salad was checked about an hour later and observed below 70F. Cooling practices and monitoring the time and temperature during cooling were discussed. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling chicken fajitas, beef, and beans is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

Observed multiple pans of beans, chicken, and beef cooling at room temperature in the back of the kitchen area. PIC noted that coolers are very small and cooling these containers in the cooler would raise the internal ambient temperature of the cooler, therefore they cool outside first for two hours. Inspector advised that while foods are cooling outside the walk-in, ice baths, ice paddles, or ice as an ingredient must be used to rapidly reduce the temperature. Also, food should be MARKED with the time and temperature in which cooling process begins to ensure the cooling parameters are properly met. Inspector provided cooling handouts to PIC.

Employees stated the carafes were switched around 2pm and the time was documented as such. Make sure the time is written down every time carafes of half and half and milks are switched out. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, the time shall be tracked to identify the time frame for use, and products must be served or discarded within 4 hours.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Rice on trays covered with plastic wrap in the kitchen 2 door cooler were observed with internal temperatures at 61F. Rice was initially chilled in the walkin freezer after cooking and prior to wrapping to place in the kitchen cooler. Soup prepared earlier was also observed in a covered container at a quantity of 4qts in the cooler with an internal temperature of 52F-53F. Soup was chilled with an ice wand prior to covering and placing in the kitchen cooler. Both products were within the last 4 hours of 6 hour time frame for cooling based on information provided, but the time and temperature were not being monitored to ensure proper cooling. The quantities and manner in which products were being stored were not allowing for rapid chilling. Two large trays of rice were separated out into additional pans and soup was placed in a large 2 inch hotel pan. Rice and soup were then placed in the walkin freezer to finish the cooling process.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk was observed without a date mark in the walkin cooler. Bartender thought it was brought in by someone for personal use. Milk was less than 1/3 full and discarded during inspection. 
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Manager was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. 
Also, a few times wait staff were observed using paper towels to start drying hands, then shut off the faucet, and then continued using the same paper towels to finish drying hands.

Management was advised to discuss proper handwashing procedure with all staff.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked chicken breasts were observed on a baking sheet cooling at room temperature upon arrival of inspector. Chicken had an internal temperature of 73F and was said to have been fully cooked to 165F within the last hour. Chicken was still in the first 2hrs of cooling based on information provided. Staff were advised to cease the practice of cooling at room temperature. Options for rapid chill with ice baths or use of the freezer in the outdoor prep kitchen were discussed. Staff were also advised to monitor the time and temperature during cooling to ensure foods are properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2hrs and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4hrs (total time must not exceed 6hrs). Chicken was placed in the prep cooler to finish cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

PIC stated longest item in fridge was jelly. Jelly was probed to be 48F. Corrected. All TCS foods were voluntarily discarded from R-I Cooler. This included 2 containers of cream cheese (16oz), 12 containers of yogurt(27lbs), and 2 bottles of ranch (44fl oz). All other foods will be moved to other cooler. Cooler was turned down.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and was not properly cleaned and sanitized after use the previous operating day. Can opener was placed in dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned and sanitized at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred, between uses, and up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 One of the metal stem food thermometers used at the facility was not accurate. Two thermometers were reading at 68F-70F at room temperature, while the other thermometer was reading closer to 80F. All thermometers were checked with ice water, and the thermometer that was not accurate was calibrated to 32F. The other two thermometers were observed to be at 32F without the need for adjustment. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the restroom handsink. Paper towels were stocked in the dispenser, and a spare roll was provided by custodial staff. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not getting hot enough to allow for proper heat sanitization at the surface of dishes. After a half dozen plus cycles of the dish machine the wash gauge was reading around 140F and the rinse tank was below 160F. The Final rinse temperature gauge was reading above 180F, but the surface temperature at the dish rack in the machine was observed at 134F, 140F, and 135F using a dishtemp dishwashing tester. Manager stated another call for service would be made. (See general comments for additional details).
All dishes currently being washed and rinsed in the dish machine and then manually sanitized in quat solution until the dish machine is working properly.
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature tank.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Back surface of the baffle in the ice machine soiled with mold accumulation remains to be cleaned. 
Clean and sanitize the baffle as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Salad cooler was observed holding around 64F at the time of inspection. Products are being chilled in ice water baths during service until the cooler is repaired and able to maintain foods at 41F/below (See general comments for details).
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to check the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine other than the built in gauges. Owner ordered a dish machine tester for checking the surface temperature at the dishes, but it has not yet been delivered. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Provide proof of food handler certifications for all staff that are not certified food managers by the next routine inspection. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed the online food allergen awareness training.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-202.12  (Pf) Hot water at employee hand sink in employee restroom is below 100F at the hand sink. Provide water of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.  Provide hot water in 10 days.
6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink at the smoothie bar. Soap was provided at smoothie hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.
citation_text: 6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14. Signs were provided. Please post signs.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16  (P) Observed the following foods out of temperature: Beef at 47F (piled too high in the prep top) scallops at 45F in bowl on top of prep top cold holding, crab sticks at 46F in bowl on top of prep top cold holding.  Chicken on counter top at 60F during lunch. Moved to ice and remained at 64F. Chicken was and was disard.  Do not put foods in bowls on top of the inside of prep top. Do not hold food at room temperature without a time as a control policy. Garlic in oil mixture observed to be held at room temperature is 60F and was discarded. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employees and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F in reach in cooler or discarded.  Reference 3-501.16.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location on the floor in the kitchen. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11. Put food away as soon as it is delivered. The foods were moved to proper storage.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly in that a tub of dirty water for soaking soiled utensils is over clean pots and pans. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Proper area for soaking utensils was discussed and the soaking container was removed. Correct this process.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Walls in the dish area and the prep area are found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11. Repair the walls in these areas. Areas were shown to the owner and FSSM on duty.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: 410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 - Food managers do not have allergen training. Information was provided to manager to ensure that all food managers take the Allergen training certification.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine 10ppm and 120°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114. Test machine daily before use. 
Technician came over with chlorine and adjusted the machine accordingly. Now 50ppm Cl.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination in the drawer withmeasuring cups. Clean utensils shall be handled in such a way that they are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11. Observed measuring cups to be stored in a container in the drawer that is soiled with dust and crumbs.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text: 4-501.114 A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, P and shall be used according to manufacturers lable insturctions. The tube carrying sanitizer from the bucket to the machine was pulled out. The tube was replaced and machine primed. Violation corrected.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 (C) (P) To avoid recontaminating their hands, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HAND WASHING.
The temporary hand washing station set up for the cooks outside by the grill did was set up using a gatorade pitcher where the button needed to be continuously depressed in order to disperse water. Temporary hand washing stations should be set up so that there is free flowing water and the user does not need to recontaminate their hands when using. The container was changed out with a switch type jug to correct.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 (A) (C) The person in charge shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

During the inspection, the CFPM's shift ended and they left the property for the day. Their replacement did not have a certification from an accredited course available to view at the time of the inspection.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-305.11 (B) (C) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

1) Phones were observed stored next to the popcorn machine. 2) A woman's clutch was observed on the cleaned dishes in storage. Both items were moved to a container stored under and away from food and food contact surfaces.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 (C) (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. 

The container used for storing single service knives for self service by consumers was visibly soiled on the bottom. The container was cleaned during the inspection.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15  (B) (C) PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be maintained in good repair.

The backflow prevention device on the faucet at the mop sink was observed damaged during the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to repair and maintain the backflow prevention devices in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed cut melon on the top shelf of white mini fridge to be 47F (probed). CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, fruit cups were voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.16 (A)(2) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained at 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed egg products in kitchen cooler without date markings. CORRECTED- PIC stated that items were received on 5/21. Items were labeled with appropriate dates.
citation_text: 3-501.17 (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. (Pf)

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed single service plastic utensils for customers stored in such a way that allows contamination of eating ends when utensils are picked up. Utensils must be stored all going the same direction, allowing one utensil to be picked up without touching the eating-end of other utensils.
citation_text: 4-903.11 (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. (C)

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Non-food contact surfaces such as the carts in the dry storage have what appear to be a few rodent droppings on them. District pest control operator was on site yesterday as reported by PIC and as evidenced by dates on new glue traps for routine treatment. He did not notify of any issues. This appears to be a cleaning issue rather than an active pest issue. Clean carts and any remaining droppings and monitor. Alert pest control as needed.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

Observed bartender pick up drink granish with bare hands and place into customer's drink. Ensure gloves/tongs/single-use toothpicks are used to pick up garnishes to prepare drinks.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) pizza oven food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed large pizza oven behind bar (next to coffee maker) and two stacked pizza ovens (next to decorative chalkboard) to be heavily soiled with grease and food pieces. Ensure ovens are cleaned frequently to prevent soil accumulation. Will follow up with facility to ensure cleaning has occurred. Follow up: 6/5/2019.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on 1/2 gallon of milk and half-filled half and half. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of clear liquid in milk crate under handsink not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

Observed a bottle of clear liquid with other cleaners/sanitizers unlabeled. Ensure all toxic substances are labeled appropriately.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-303.12  (C) Exposed food stored in contact with ice or water at bar area. Food may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the food is subject to direct contact with the ice or water. Reference 3-303.12.

Observed a bin of ice with a scoop for drinks overflowed with an adjacent container filled with ice housing canned beverages. Protect food (ice scooped for drink) from contamination by not storing canned/bottled beverages with it.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.
Observed damp cloths throughout bar area. All damp cloths must be stored in appropriate sanitizer bucket with appropriate concentration to prevent growth of pathogens.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed bakery handsink soiled with icing. Ensure handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Icing was wiped out of the sink.
citation_text: 5-205.11 (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (Pf)

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

citation_text: 3-202.15 FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. (Pf)

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:

Observed employee fill a beverage order after drinking personal drink/handling mail without washing hands first. Ensure hands are washed properly before handling customer orders.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0 ppm. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration (or quat) sanitizer bucket during hours of operation Reference 4-501.114.

No sanitizer solution made at time of inspection. All-purpose cleaner is not an approved sanitizer for food contact surfaces. Ensure properly concentrated quat or chlorine bucket/bottle available for use at all hours of operation.

Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date).Reference 3-501.17.
