title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment: 2-102.11(B) (Pf) PIC is not a certified food manager. Provide proof of Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification.  Reference 2-102.11(B).
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of proper handwashing and sanitizing procedures. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Neither worker present at time of inspection is a CFPM. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed food employee changing gloves without washing hands in between making sandwiches for multiple customers. Ensure hands are washed in between glove changes and in between tasks.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.
Facility is moving a bottle of dishsoap in between handwashing station and the 3 compartment sink. Ensure handsoap is kept at handwashing sink at all times. Do not use dish soap as a replacement of handsoap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 4-501.114  (P) No sanitizer bucket is in use at facility to properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces in between sandwich orders. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration sanitizer bucket during all hours of operation. Reference 4-501.114.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
Observed heavy mold buildup dripping into ice in ice machine out back. Ensure all existing ice is discarded and the entire interior of the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items in deli display case. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was relabeled. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple sliced lunch meats without a date mark, along with sliced vegetables. PIC stated they were prepared the evening before. Inspector explained applicable sections of the food code and food was labeled appropriately.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.
Observed employee wiping down cutting board in between sandwich orders with a soiled rag. Ensure rags are kept in a properly concentrated sanitizer bucket to prevent bacterial growth.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Food employee was cleaning dirty dishes at hand washing sink. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

Mid-inspection, observed employee draining and cleaning coffee makers in handwash sink. Addressed with person in charge and handwash only sign provided to the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by a step ladder and several mop buckets. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed ladder and mop blocking hand sink at time of inspection. Also observed unopen can of pepsi on handsink. Ensure sink is designated for handwashing only with no extra, obstructing objects placed on it.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) soda nozzles and ice coffee nozzles is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Ensure nozzles and remaining fixed pieces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized nightly.
citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Sanitizer at 0 ppm. Reference 4-501.114. 

Observed no made sanitizer bucket/bottle. Bleach bottle is empty as well as hydrogen peroxide sanitizer. Ensure facility has methods of sanitization during all hours of operation.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of hydrogen peroxide not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Reference 7-102.11.

Sanitizer did not have proper EPA label instructions with appropropriate concentration requirements. Ensure all materials intended for food contact surface sanitation have appropriately labeled instructions for use.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

No test strips available for H2O2 sanitizer, ensure proper sanitizer is used and appropriate test strips available.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed debris build up in soda nozzles at the beverage station. Ensure nozzles are washed/rinsed/sanitized frequently to prevent soil accumulation

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Hand sink near the high temperature dish machine noted with large bag of detergent sitting in sink basin, blocking accessibility. 
Hand sink near the high temperature dish machine noted without paper towels. Food debris noted in sink basin. 
Hand sink located in the back hallway near the walk-in coolers found with potato boxes sitting in sink basin, blocking accessibility. 
Hand towels not provided at hand sink located near the ovens on the South end of the kitchen. 
Hand towels not provided at hand sink located in the broil room. 

->Hand washing sink blocked. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.
->Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Nozzle of the soda gun located behind the bar found soiled with white mineral accumulation.
Quaternary ammonia sanitizer measured with concentrations below 150 ppm located in wiping bucket in the kitchen area.

->Food contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Ensure sanitizers are maintained with proper concentrations. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Garlic in oil located in walk-in cooler noted without proper date marking of when item was prepared or when to be discarded.

->Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Observed pan of shrimp thawing at room temperature located in container of water in the food preparation sink located in back hallway near walk-ins. Water was turned on and allowed to run over product. 

->Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment:
Knife found stored between crack of table and wall in the meat cutting room. 
Wall-mounted magnetic knife holder located in the meat cutting room found soiled with food debris.

->Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
2 door upright freezer near the breading station located on cookline noted with dried food debris soilage on bottom shelf. 
2 door make table across from breading station noted with food accumulation on the inner shelf and bottom of internal unit. 
Shelf directly above raw cut meats in the display cooler in the broiler room noted soiled with accumulation of grime and dust.

->Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Floors in the following areas found accumulated with dirt, dried food debris, and pooled water: floor in dry storage near wall junctions and corners, alcohol walk-in cooler floor, floors underneath speed rack near the walk-in freezers.

->Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
Observed employee cell phone stored on top of box of gloves located on food preparation in back kitchen area. 
Observed employee back pack stored on table in the dish room.

->Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Person in charge needs to complete the food manager certification course and provide proof of certification by the next routine inspection.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not getting hot enough to allow for proper heat sanitization at the surface of dishes. Wash gauge was once again observed below 160F after running a dozen cycles. While the rinse tank temperature gauge was reading around 150F, and the final rinse temperature gauge was observed around 190F. A dishtemp dishwashing tester was placed through two cycles at different times and observed at 153F and 154F. A call for service was made to have additional repairs (see general comments for details). Until the dish machine is properly heat sanitizing, utensils and equipment need to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Dish machine may also be used for an initial wash prior to manual sanitization at the 3 part sink. 
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature machine.
citation_text: 4-602.11 Back surface of the baffle in the ice machine soiled with mold accumulation remains to be cleaned. Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Salad cooler was not holding foods at 41F/below. Shredded cheese just placed in the cooler after being held in the walkin cooler overnight was observed at 47F-49F. Inspector's stem thermometers were placed in the cooler to verify temperature and were later observed at 50F-51F. Cook noted the cooler was open so food could be iced down once the cheese was observed out of temperature. The cooler is holding at least in the high 40F range based on observations made. Kitchen manager stated a call for service will be made today to get the cooler repaired. Utilize ice baths to help hold foods at 41F/below until the cooler is repaired and able to maintain proper temperature. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
4-204-112 A thermometer was not present in the salad cooler. Provide a thermometer for the cooler
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to check the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine other than the built in gauges. Owner has ordered a dish machine tester for checking the surface temperature at the dishes. The dish machine tester should be available for use by the next inspection
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: 410 ILCS 625 Provide proof of food handler certifications for all staff that are not certified food managers by the next routine inspection. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed the online food allergen awareness training. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Chili put to cool at 11am is 107°F. Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.  Three half pans of chili between 107 and 114F were discarded in the garbage. No time or temp on the itmes. No cooling temperature logs kept. Use active methods to properly cool chili in the future.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) Hamburger in the low boy is observed to be 54F. Gyro meat is observed to be held at 56F. Impossible burgers observed to be 56F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadaquiately held food was voluintarily discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2). 28 big burgers, 5 reguarl sized burgers, 7 impossible burgers and approximately 3 pounds of gyro meat were discarded. Technician was called to repair the low boy. Do not use this unit for TCS foods until it is repaired.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 4/30 marked on chili on hot holding unit exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling chili is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Keep cooling logs and or place temperature date and time on the food so that time in the temperature danger zone can be adequately evaluated. Food was discarded.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are observed to be stored in sanitizer that is not proper strenght. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Sanitizer bucket was remade to have proper chlorine sanitizer concentration.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text: 4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at the wait service area. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-501.12  Floors behind pipes in the kitchen are soiled. (under hand sink and next to walk in door) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Observed employee to move from handling soiled dishes and cleaning a cart to working with clean dishes. Employee was stopped and coached concerning propert hand washing between tasks. Employee washed hands and proceeded to handle clean dishes. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Observed employees to share a knife that had been used to open a raw steak. Observed knife on the cutting board. When asked about the knife, employee stated that it was used to cut baccon for baccon bits.  Employee stated that the baccon pieces were not used but discarded because it was not needed. Use separate equipment/utensils when preparing ready-to-eat foods and raw meats. Reference 3-302.11. The cutting board was also removed and placed through dish. Training in this area is recommended.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) Observed chicken tenders to be between 42F and 47F when probed internally. The food is stored in the drawers under the grill line.  Also observed the dressing on the salad cooler to be 45F when probed. Dressings were discarded. Dressing dispensers were placed into a deeper pan with holes so that are can circulate more easily around the conatiners. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was voluntarily discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2). Keep drawers properly closed at all times.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Observed single use lids to be stored at wait station in holders with crumbs and dust in the bottom. Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly in soiled containers. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the following non-food contact items: 1) salad cooler doors, inside around seals 2) table at food processor 3) under low boy drawers (in unused area) 4) under grill tops (at unused area) 5) fronts of hot holding area 6) under microwaves. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Observed cooked asparagus to be stored below raw, uncooked, uncleaned vegetables. Asparagus was moved to ready to eat, cooked item storage area. Observed a box of celery to be stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Box was moved up onto the bottom shelf.  Store food properly at all times to protect it from potential cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Observed milk in the wait cooler up front to be 62°F.  Observed black bean burgers in the fry cooler to be 47F. Observed carmelized onion in the broil cooler to be 48F. These foods were discarded. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food shall be maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) Observed Madera sauce and BBQ sauce, both house made, to be on the sauce rail at room temperature. Sauces were in the 60°F range. Observed whipped butter on the wait line to be 65F. When a maximum time period of 6 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from temperature control and the FOOD temperature may not exceed 70°F during the 6 hours. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Time tag was placed on the sauces and butter in question. Reference 3-501.19. Switching to cold holding for sauces. Butter will be held with time as contol.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Finito is stored behind the bar above bottles of liquor and sugar cubes. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on walls behind the ice maker, wall to the right of the prep line, bottom shelf of bar prep cooler, vita mix at bar, speed rail at bar, and walls at the dish room. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket to be 0ppm. In addition, quat dispenser registered to be 0ppm. Upon further investigation, quat line had blockage preventing water and chemical to mix. Corrected. Quaternary chemical line was fixed and dispenser was fixed. All buckets were re-filled.
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm in sanitizer bucket. Maintain concentration indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed Prep line near handsink to be turned off. All foods were above 50F. Corrected. All TCS foods were discarded from cooler. This included tomatoes and sauces. Lettuce was just placed in cooler. PIC discovered prep cooler was turned off. Prep cooler was turned on.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Tomatoes, mayonaise, and other food items were above 50F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed food debris in walk-in freezer. In addition, ice accumulation can be seen in walk-in cooler. Clean floor areas.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Reference 6-501.12

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in spray bottles found below 150 ppm. Staff indicated sanitizer is used to clean tables after lunch in the cafeteria. Staff indicated sanitizer is mixed and stored in bulk containers by janitorial staff and working bottles are filled from bulk. Bulk is estimated to be re-mixed every 2 weeks. Test strips were provided.

->Ensure sanitizer has proper concentrations when using to clean non-food contact surfaces. Check sanitizer concentrations with test strips. Quatnernary ammonia sanitizer must be between 150-400 ppm. Chlorine sanitizer must be between 50-200 ppm. Reference 4-602.13.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment:
Observed staff touch ready-to-eat sandwich with bare hands while holding to cut sandwich in half with a knife. Discussed the importance of preventing bare hand contact with ready to eat foods to prevent the spread of illness. 

->Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Hand washing sink behind the bar was not provided with hand towels at the time of inspection. Hand sink was restocked during inspection. 

->Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels, hand soap, and hot and cold water at hand washing sinks to facilitate proper hand washing practices. Reference 6-301.12.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment:
Pan of pulled pork measured at 66F in the upright hot holding cabinet. Staff indicated items were reheated in the oven and transferred to hot holding cabinet just prior to inspection.

->Food must be reheated to 165°F within 2 hours, before being placed in hot holding. Reviewed reheating requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Food was reheated to 165F in the oven. Reference 3-403.11.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Baked potatoes measured at 56F on pan on a speed rack in the walk-in cooler. Pan of ribs measured at 46F-53F on pan on a speed rack in the walk-in cooler. Pans were noted stored closely together. Staff indicated items were cooked the night prior, estimated around 9 pm. Staff indicated items had been in the walk-in cooler all night and day. Items were discarded. 

->Discussed allowing space between pans of cooling items to allow adequate air flow to assist the cooling process. 

->Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.14.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Salmon found completely thawed in ROP vacuum sealed packages in the bottom pull-out drawer cooler across from the stove top. Discussed introducing air into vacuum sealed packages for proper thawing practices.

->Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Door gasket on the bottom pull out drawer found in disrepair and pulled away from the door (also heavily soiled) located in the 2 door pull-out cold holding unit across from the stove top.

->Replace the damaged or missing gaskets so the cooler can hold food at the proper temperature. Reference 4-501.11.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed damp cloth stored in handwashing sink near the ice machine. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and cloth was removed.
citation_text: 5-205.11(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (Pf)

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket at a concentration of 100ppm quaternary ammonium (manufacturer label states concentration must be 200-400ppm). CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Sanitizer was remade to correct concentration (observed 200ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed damp wiping cloth stored on the counter. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and cloth was removed.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Bleach needs instructions for use on food contact surfaces as well as the EPA number. Clorox will be called a Germicidal bleach. Will check at next event.
citation_text: 7-204.11  (P)  Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm. Provide 100-200 ppm bleach or prepare according to label. Bucket was remade. 4-501.114  (P) Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Raw shell eggs and raw shrimp noted stored above container of ready-to-eat butter packets in the 2 door make table cooler near the bar pass thru window. Items were rearranged at the time of inspection with raw items stored on the bottom shelf.

-> Please store raw food items by cooking temperature and below ready to eat foods to prevent possible contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
Fish such as salmon and cod, which are received frozen, were found thawing while in ROP vacuumed sealed packaging on the speed rack in the walk-in cooler and in the 2 door undercounter cooler across from the deep fryers at the time of inspection. Discussed scoring the packaging to allow air into the packaging. 

->Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wet wiping clothes noted on preparation tables in the kitchen area. Discussed keeping wiping cloths in sanitizer solution with proper concentrations. 

->Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
The following containers were noted in disrepair and missing pieces of plastic:
Blue lidded container in the bottom area of the salad make table cooler
Lid of container used for breading in the 2 door make table near the bar pass thru window
Lid of container used for ravolis in the make table cooler across from the deep fryer

->In-use equipment and/or utensils in disrepair. Remove from use and replace with equipment that is durable and easily cleanable meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI standards. Reference 4-201.11.

2-301.12 (C) (P) (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HAND WASHING SINK.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded at a maximum of 7 days. ->Working container of ***** not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Wet wiping cloths were noted stored at room temperature on counter across from display case in the deli.

citation_text:

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12, 2-301.14 & 2-301.15 Cook was observed rinsing his hands at the sprayer in the dish area and then proceeded to wipe his hands on his apron prior to retuning to prep area. Cook then handled sliced pineapple prior to returning to the cook line and wiping his hands on wiping cloths. Owner was advised as to what was observed and was asked to have a conversation with the cook on proper handwashing, when to wash hands, and where to wash hands. Cook was later observed properly washing hands at a designated handsink between tasks. Hands were not observed to be wiped on aprons or wiping cloths for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food Employees shall properly clean their hands and exposed portions of their immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.11 Pump bottle for hand soap at the handsink in the kitchen was broken. Another bottle of soap was placed at the handsink to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Open package of baking powder was observed in the bottom shelf of a prep table at the end of the cook line. Inner surface of the package was soiled with food splash, and a piece of dried pepper was observed in the baking powder. Proper storage was discussed, with the option of using a clean, stainless steel pan that can be covered between uses if the original package does not seal properly. Baking powder was placed in a clean container for storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of marinated chicken wings was observed on the prep table upon arrival of inspector. Surface temperature was observed at 58F-60F. Wings were just prepared and marinated prior to inspector's arrival based on information provided. Prompt storage of foods to avoid time-temperature abuse was discussed. Wings were portioned in pans and placed in the 2 door freezer for storage. 

Beef, sliced tomatoes, tofu, and noodles in the top holding area of the large prep cooler had internal temperatures at 47F-49F. Owner thought elevated temperatures were due to the lid being open during lunch service. Mahi mahi and scallops in the bottom holding area had internal temperatures of 47F and 48F/50F respectively. A pan of recently prepared raw chicken had an internal temperature of 55F. Cooler was not holding at proper temperature (see #33 for details). All foods that were in use since the start of lunch were to be served or discarded by 5p. Owner chose to discard foods and start with fresh product. Proper use of time control was discussed for temporary storage until cooler is able to maintain foods at 41F/below.

Sweet and sour chicken in the bottom of the small prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 47F-48F. Chicken was in a pan that previously up in the top holding area of the cooler but not in direct contact with cold air. Chicken was discarded during the inspection. Owner was advised to cease the practice of stacking pans and containers of food in the top holding areas of coolers. Products that are stacked and not in the holding compartment in direct contact with cold air are less likely to be maintained at 41F/below, especially with frequent opening and closing of cooler lids during busy service times.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 A generic chemical spray bottle hanging on the bottom rung of the dish machine was not labeled as to the contents. Owner thought it was a general cleaning/degreaser used for cleaning general surfaces under and around the dish machine. Owner was advised on proper labeling of chemical spray bottles. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
4-301.11 Stem thermometer in the bottom of the large prep cooler used to monitor the temperature was observed above 40F. Thermometer was calibrated with ice water prior to placing it back in the cooler along with inspector's calibrated stem thermometer to verify cold holding temperature. Large prep cooler was observed holding around 48F. Owner called for service and stated a technician should be out sometime later this evening to service the cooler. Do not use the large prep cooler for long-term storage of any TCS food until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13 Package of frozen pork was observed in the 3 part sink. Owner noted it was being thawed slightly so it would be easier to cut when preparing pork chops. Owner was advised to thaw it under cold running water or to place it in the walkin cooler until it was able to be sliced for prep. Pork was placed in the walkin cooler to finish thawing.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.
citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged, completely thawed mahi mahi was observed in the bottom of the large prep cooler.  Proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish was discussed. Owner was advised to make sure packaging is at minimum cut once thawing is complete. Fish were removed from packaging and placed in a pan for storage.
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-302.12 The only stem thermometers available for use at the time of inspection were being used for monitoring temperatures in the walkin cooler and the large prep cooler. A thermometer was not available for checking food temperatures. Obtain and use food thermometers that register temperatures in the range of 0°F-220°F to verify proper cooking, cooling, reheating, hot holding, and cold holding temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the prep table. Wiping cloth was placed back in the kitchen sani-bucket for proper storage Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Walls and pipe around and behind cooking equipment were soiled with grease accumulation. Clean the walls and attached pipes. 
Hood above cook line was also starting to accumulate grease on the baffles. Clean the hood.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Manager was observed touching the manual faucet with her hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands were properly washed prior to continuing on to the next task. An educational handout showing proper technique was provided, and kitchen manager was advised to discuss handwashing with all staff.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 & 6-301.13 The 2 part sink was observed being used to fill water jugs during the inspection. One of the compartments had mounting on the wall for a soap dispenser and a handwashing sign posted above it. A paper towel dispenser was observed on the wall to the right of the sinks as well. Manager noted the sinks in question have not been used for handwashing since the soap dispenser broke, but the left compartment was used for handwashing at one time. However, the sinks are obviously used for multiple purposes. Manager plans to use the 2 part sink for food prep only from this point forward. Manager was advised to remove the signage and soap from the wall; paper towels may stay on the wall for general use only. Use the designated handsink for handwashing only from this point forward. 

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. 
A sink used for food preparation or utensil washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a handwashing sink.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and some accumulation of metal shavings in the crevice around the blade. Cleaning between uses/as needed was discussed. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils used with non-TCS food shall be cleaned and sanitized up to every 24 hours or whenever they may have been contaminated.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machine in the dining area had some mold accumulation on surfaces around ice tray and mechanicals. Cleaning frequency of ice machines was discussed.
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of 1% milk had a date mark of 4/26. Last date for use was 5/2. Milk was discarded during the inspection 
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop for the ice machine in the dining area was observed in a storage container that had debris and water accumulation in the bottom. Scoop and holder were cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee was observed itching his face with gloved hands. The same employee, while discussing hot water temperature/usage at the handsink with inspector, also put his gloved hand under running water and turned the handsink faucet off. The employee then proceeded to the walkin cooler to retrieve bagged lunches. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were discarded.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.13 Heat sanitizing dish machine digital readout was showing a wash temperature of 160F. The final rinse temperature was observed at 176F-177F after more than a half dozen full cycles. Inspector used a dish simulating tester to verify proper heat sanitization at the surface of dishes. Maximum temperature on the dish temp tester was at 172F. Manager did not have a way to verify the surface temperature of dishes if the digital readout was questionable. Options for measuring the final rinse temperature were discussed. Two Thermolabels were provided for manager until facility is able to purchase a dish machine tester or temperature strips of their own.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves - left side by back wall (general buildup/mold);
B) cooler in food storage area - bottom inside, lower section of doors, and tracks (debris/mold);   and
C) drip tray under stove burners (food debris/splash).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 A leak was observed on the underside of the dish machine when the machine was running a cycle. The cause of the leak was not apparent (possible plumbing and/or equipment issue). Get the dish machine checked and repaired.
Floor under the dish machine was observed with accumulation of moisture and debris. Clean the floor under the dish machine. 
Walls in the dish area, attached pipes, underside of drain boards, and general surfaces of the dish machine were soiled with dust and general buildup of splash. Clean the aforementioned items.
Exhaust fan in the dish area had heavy dust accumulation. Clean the exhaust fan.
Kitchen handsink was observed with grimy buildup in the basin and along the upper edges. Clean the handsink daily/as needed. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee was observed touching the handle of the paper towel dispenser upon completing handwashing process. Employee was advised to use paper towels as a barrier to touch the handles of the manual faucet and handle of the paper towel dispenser once hands are washed to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink and paper towel dispensers. Use of forearms and elbows to dispense paper towels would also be acceptable.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed in the ice machine around the ice tray. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate

4-203.11 Metal stem thermometer was reading at 20°F when checked in ice water. Thermometer was properly calibrated to 32°F in the ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.

Wall and pipes behind cook line were soiled with grease. Clean behind the equipment daily/as needed.

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No Certified Food Manager (CFM) present at time of inspection. Medium-risk facilities must have a CFM present at all times of operation. PIC stated that employees are in the process of becoming CFMs through an online class and proctored exam.
citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored

citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Bleach that is being used in the three compartment sink is a lemon scented bleach. This is not approved for use in food service. Provide an approved sanitizer as discussed. 7-204.11  (P) Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed boxes of toilet paper stored on the floor in the mop sink room. All single service items must be stored at least 6 inches off of the floor.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed a package of raw chicken stored in the walk in cooler on a top shelf above ready to eat foods such as vegetables and noodles. Chicken was moved to the bottom rack where the rest of the chicken was stored. Store ready to eat foods above raw meats to protect from contamination. 3-302.11  (P) Store ready to eat foods above raw meats to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed a container of cooked pork and a container of a cooked sausage stored in a pan that was sitting on top of the containers in the top of the prep cooler. Pork and sausage were probed with a recently calibrated digital thermometer at an internal temperature of 63F. It was discussed that these should be discarded and in the future, foods such as carrots or asparagus may be stored in this pan, but all time and temperature control for safety foods must be stored where the refrigerated air is able to keep them at 41F or below. 2) Observed cooked chicken in the walk in cooler that was probed at 63F. This chicken was reported to have been cold, taken from the walk in cooler to use through lunch near the fryers, and then placed back in the walk in after lunch service. This is abusing the temperature of the food. Pull only what you need at that time and keep the rest of the chicken temperature controlled until use (or place on a time as a control policy as discussed). These items were to be voluntarily discarded. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed the condenser unit in the walk in cooler to be dripping onto the floor right in front of the food storage shelves. Repair walk in condenser unit so that if it drips, the water is not contaminating the food stored below.
citation_text: 3-305.12  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. Reference 3-305.12.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: 1) Observed a bowl being used as a scoop and stored within a container of crushed peanuts. Do not use bowls as scoops--use a scoop with a handle and store extended up and out of the food. 2) Observed rice scoop being stored in water in between use. Store rice scoop clean and dry or within rice as long as the handle is always stored extended up and out of the food.  Observed 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: 1) Observed the microwave in the kitchen to show signs of rust along the interior frame when door is open. 2) Observed the top of the chest freezer to be heavily damaged with an accumulation of rust visible. Repair or replace these items so that non-food contact surfaces are smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable. 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces have rusted or are no longer easily cleanable. Replace or repair equipment  with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a food service facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 1) Observed the outsides of some of the bulk containers, lids of containers, handles of containers, and handles of coolers to be soiled with food debris and grease accumulation. 2) Observed old date marking labels to not have been removed from working containers of food in the prep cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently and remove old date labels after use. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment: Observed a couple of sweatshirts/jackets stored on the dry storage shelves intermingled with packaged food. Store employee clothing in designated areas away from food. 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 (A)  (P) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70°F), (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41°F) or less.

A container in the walk in cooler of chicken salsa was observed with a date from the previous day (5/1) and an internal temperature of 42 degrees. This puts the RTE foods outside of the time/ temperature requirements for cooling. Cooling procedures were reviewed and the container was discarded during the insepction.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (A)  (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TOEAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded at a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.
Cottage cheese in the front reach in cooler was observed opened and without a date mark. Discussion with employee suggested that the container was opened 3 days prior. A date mark was provided to correct.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (A)  (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TO EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded at a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.
Cottage cheese in cooler 1 was observed opened and with a date mark of 4/23. Discussed with the PIC and the container was discarded during the inspection.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
comment:
Observed unlidded employee beverage stored on pizza cutting prep table upon entering establishment. Noted utensil storage and active food preparation on same table. Drink was discarded by staff. 
->Provide designated area for drinking. Store in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food preparation areas, and clean utensils.   Reference 2-401.11.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Large container of marinara sauce measured at 55F stored on preparation table in back area. PIC indicated sauce is luke warm water mixed with Dominos prepackaged sauce mix, which is then left out for 2 hours until it is moved into cold holding.  Discussed proper cold holding temperatures/procedures with PIC. 
->Food items must be maintained with temperatures below 41F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
Unlidded spray bottle of bleach and water mixture found stored on preparation table. Bottle noted without lid and being stored on table where active food preparation was observed. Staff indicated bleach is used for the bathrooms and other general cleaning. Please obtain bleach test strips if bleach is to be used as sanitizer. 
->Toxic materials must be used so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles.  Reference 7-202.12.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text:
3-202.15  (Pf) Can of artichoke is dented and in poor condition. Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15.

Observed can of artichoke with severe denting on the side. CFPM set can aside for vendor refund. Inspector informed CFPM on acceptable versus unacceptable dry goods upon delivery from vendors, ensure damaged goods are rejected at future deliveries.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B) (P) blu cheese and shredded chicken are 68 and 66 °F at cold-hold at hot pass. Also observed cole slaw and potato salad in vertical cooler by server pass at 54 and 55 degrees.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with CFPM (A)(2) and (B).

Observed cold-held food items at hot pass and server pass at inadequate temperatures. CFPM removes lids to cold-hold periodically for busy rushes at restaurant, less than 2 hours. CFPM placed lids on and lowered temperature of cooler during inspection. Inspector checked temperatures at both locations at 4PM to ensure temperatures have lowered. Temperatures observed at 4 PM include: cheese at 45 degrees, chicken at 56 degrees, Potato salad and cole slaw at 55 degrees. Cheese was kept because temperature decreased during inspection. Food items that maintained temperature chicken, cole slaw, and potato salad discarded. Ensure coolers are kept at lower temperatures in hot areas.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

3-305.11  (C) Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

Observed containers of potatoes soaking in water on floor of walkin cooler #1 behind restaurant. CFPM stated he is working with vendors to provide additional storage racks for coolers.

Observed cutting boards throughout kitchen with deep grooves, no longer easily cleanable. CFPM stated new cutting boards are at the facility and need to be installed in the kitchen.

Observed 3 sweaters, a tank top, and a ball cap being stored in the dry storage area with food. Ensure employees are provided a designated area to store their personal items while they are working. Ensure employees are not changing clothing, or removing layers in the kitchen.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Observed several drain flies in the dry storage/ 3 compartment sink area . The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate drain flies , using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: REPEAT - 3-307.11  (C) Observed rolling racks in the walk in cooler (holding cooled and thawed foods) are observed with mold growth on the sides. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed food and soil residue present on rack on prep line used to store clean mixing bowls. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

comment:
Observed cart blocking handsink near cook line. CORRECTED- PIC moved the cart so that handsink is easily accessible.
5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

Observed front handsink with paper towel dispenser jammed. CORRECTED- Maintenance was called to ensure paper towels are provided.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with (A) Individual, disposable towels; (Pf)

comment: See 4/29/19 inspection for details.

comment: See 4/29/19 inspection for details.
