comment: See 4/29/19 inspection for details.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Active managerial control is lacking in the facility today. PIC was unable to designate employees to handle other tasks so that he could address Foodborne Illness Risk Factors identified during the inspection, and was unable to correctly instruct dish person on how to prepare and utilize the three compartment sink for manual wash, rinse sanitize process. PIC stated to wash, rinse and air dry. 
2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of of numerous sections of the food code . Discussed related sections of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).
citation_text: 2-102.11(B) (Pf) PIC is not a certified food manager. Provide proof of Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification.  Reference 2-102.11(B).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No certified food protection manager is present at the time of the inspection. PIC showed inspector the half paper from renewing his FSSMC in 2009 but had no other proof of CFPM. Provide proof of successful completion of a valid CFPM course for the PIC during each shift. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Observed a server wash hands, use bare hands to turn off the faucet, dry hands and then scratch face with clean hands. Other employees on the cook and make lines were observed to be doing other tasks, enter the cook/make line area and immediately put on gloves and handle food without proper hand washing first. Hand washing and glove use was discussed with the PIC. 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment: Observed the employee in the shake station taking the tickets out of the printer and with bare hands placing the paper ticket down in the whip cream on the top of the shakes. Employee was addressed and this practice was discussed--avoid placing tickets in shakes, especially since they are handled with bare hands that are doing multiple tasks without proper hand washing. 3-301.11 (Pf) Food employee is not minimizing bare hand contact with foods that are not in a ready to eat form. Employee shall use suitable utensils or gloves to minimize bare hand contact with these foods. Reference 3-301.11.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed raw sausage stored above packets of ready to eat sauces on the speed rack in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods above raw foods. 3-302.11  (P)   Store ready to eat foods  above raw foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: 1) Multiple sanitizer buckets tested at 0-100 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. The wall unit dispenser was also testing at 0-100 ppm quaternary ammonium. PIC was unable to step away and call EcoLab because he was on the make line. Sanitizer buckets need to be re-made and prepared manually if dispenser is not working appropriately, but PIC does not exhibit that this is possible as no liquid sanitizer is able to be located during the inspection. 2) Observed the dish machine, which was in use, to be testing at 0-10 ppm on the first time it was tested. Subsequent runs provided 25 ppm according to their EcoLab test strip, and inspector's maximum registering thermometer read 140F for the rinse cycle. pH of the water is unknown. EcoLab chlorine sanitizer states to dispense at 50-100 ppm, and it is not at this time.  3) The slicer at the back prep table is soiled with what appears to be food debris and mold. Wash, rinse and sanitize the slicer. Inspector spoke with Nick from EcoLab on the phone and explained the situation and he will be here to correct the sanitizer concentrations. 4-501.114  (P)  A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Cooked chicken tenders hot holding on top of the heat lamp were probed at 130-131F. Hot time and temperature control for safety foods must be hot held at 135F or above. This was discussed and chicken will be discarded. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Shell eggs in a pan in the cold holding insert area next to the grill were probed at 50F. Eggs were discarded during the inspection. Cold TCS foods must be held at 41F or below. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: There are numerous chemical spray bottles in EcoLab bottles in the mop sink area that do not have any sort of labeling on them. All chemicals must be labeled with the common name of the contents. 7-102.11  (Pf) Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: Observed single portion cups of chili in the top of the pan in the prep cooler that were probed at 80F. Employee states she just portioned these before inspector arrived, and stocked them in the cooler. There is a pan of the same in the cooler underneath the prep cooler. Older, cold portioned chili was observed in the bottom of the pan in the top of the prep cooler. Hot chili cups were removed and placed in the walk in cooler to cool. Use adequate refrigeration that will cool TCS foods rapidly. Cooling method for single portion chili is inadequate. 3-501.15  (Pf) Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment: No thermometer is observed in the milk dispenser in the wait station and the outside thermometer reads that it is in the temperature danger zone when the milk within is 33F. Provide an accurate and conspicuously placed thermometer in each cooling unit. 4-204-112  (C) Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment: Observed numerous fruit/drain flies throughout the facility. Most notably, flies are observed in the dish room, in the shake area and near that adjacent hand washing sink, and in the waitress area. Provide effective pest control. 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate fruit/drain flies, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: Observed a pile of wet wiping cloths stored within the front hand washing sink at the beginning of the inspection. Cloths were removed. Store sanitizer cloths in the appropriate area. 3-304.14  (C) Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: 1) Observed the handle to the fry scoop to be stored in contact with the fries. 2) Observed the handle to one of the sauces in the prep cooler to be stored with the handle almost completely submerged in the food itself. Store in use utensils with the handle extended up and out of the foods. 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: There are a couple of sleeves of cups and a couple of boxes of single service items on the floor in the dry storage area in the office, and coffee filters stored unprotected in the wait station. . Store single service items at least 6" off of the floor and covered and protected from contamination. 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Boards that are used to hold burgers and sandwiches as they are moved from the grill to the dressing station have edges that are rough with multiple different layers of the material exposed on both the ends and in the middle of some of the boards where they have seemed to have chipped. Food contact surfaces must be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable and free from unnecessary ledges or cracks. Replace boards. 4-202.11  (Pf) A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: When dish machine was not testing correctly, three compartment sink was uncovered to be used and sinks were observed soiled with mold, moldy foods and other debris. Sinks were scrubbed during the inspection. 4-501.14  (C) Manual warewashing three compartment sink is soiled with food debris. The three compartment sink should be cleaned before use, as needed throughout the day, or at least once every 24 hours to ensure proper sanitizing of equipment and utensils. Clean the 3 compartment sink in the frequency listed previously. Reference 4-501.14.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the heat lamp for the fries with grease accumulation, 2) the weights on the wrappers with food debris, 3) the inside of the shake reach in freezer with food spillage, 4) the handles to the shake reach in freezers are sticky, 5) the top and sides of the dish machine with limescale accumulation, 6) the undersides of the tables in the dish room with debris (this is not helping the fly issue) and 7) most of the reach in freezers have significant soiled ice accumulation within. Clean these non-food contact surfaces. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Walls and floors throughout the facility were observed soiled as well as the floor drain underneath the dish machine. Walls in the dish room need a thorough scrubbing as well as floor to wall junctions throughout the facility. Clean walls, floors and floor drains. 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.15 Owner rinsed his hands at the 3 part sink in the dish area. Owner was advised that if hands need to be rinsed or wiped then they need to be properly washed at a designated handsink regardless of the next task to be done. Owner was also advised to make sure employees working in the dish area are properly washing their hands at a designated handsink between handling dirty and clean dishes. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Half of a small bread loaf was observed uncovered sitting on the top shelf in the reach-in cooler on the cook line. Cook noted it was likely left from only needing a portion for a half order the evening prior. Bread was discarded in the trash. 
Plate of baked potatoes was uncovered in the walkin cooler. Owner was advised to have staff cover foods after cooked foods are properly cooled. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings and separating fruits and vegetables, before they are washed from ready to eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not working properly. Wash temperature never went beyond 140F according to the gauge. The final rinse temperature was at 188F according to the rinse gauge, but Thermolabel heat strips verified the final rinse was not reaching 160F at the surface of the dishes. The heat strips did not turn black (4 separate strips were used at different times). A call for service was made. Until the dish machine is properly heat sanitizing, utensils and equipment need to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Dish machine may also be used for an initial wash prior to manual sanitization at the 3 part sink. 
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature machine.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and metal shavings in the crevice around the blade. Can opener was left soiled from previous use and not yet used during operations today. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Stem of the food thermometer and the case had some stuck on food debris. Thermometer and case were cleaned during the inspection. Sanitizing between uses and manual wash, rinse, sanitize up to every 4 hours after continuous use were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. 

Back surface of the baffle in the ice machine was soiled with mold accumulation. Owner noted the ice machine was cleaned and sanitized after the last inspection. Ice machine needs to be cleaned an sanitized as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Leftover foods from the previous evening were not properly cooled. Stacked pans of lasagna, manicotti, and sausage had internal temperatures of 50F-51F. The inner surfaces of the lids had condensation buildup on them. Also, a medium sized stainless steel pan full to the top with mashed potatoes had an internal temperature of 55F. All foods leftover from the previous evening were discarded. Proper cooling was discussed. 
Cooked TCS food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135ºF to 70°F and within an additional 4 hours from 70°F to 41°F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135ºF to 41°F/below. Utilize one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled to allow for rapid/proper cooling: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the steam table between uses. Wiping cloth was used to wipe the stem thermometer between temperature checks. Proper storage was discussed. Sani-buket was moved to the cook line to allow for proper storage of the wiping cloth between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 Cook was observed wearing a glove to prevent contamination from a bandaged finger. Glove was not being changed between touching unclean surfaces and using the oven mitt. Cook was also observed wiping his gloved hand on his apron. Proper glove use was discussed. Employee began changing his glove more frequently and washing hands between glove changes. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to check the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine other than the built in gauges. Owner was advised to purchase and use either dish machine heat strips or some type of maximum registering thermometer for monitoring and verifying the temperature to ensure proper function of the dish machine.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions. A chlorine test kit that had been purchased online was the only set of test strips available for use. Quat strips were purchased at a local restaurant supply store during the inspection and provided for use. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
citation_text:
5-103.12 Hot water was not available at the back handsink in the kitchen. This same handsink had issues with water pressure during the previous routine inspection. Owner noted a part had to be ordered a few weeks ago, and the whole faucet has to be replaced. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. Proof of a current food handler certification was not available for the cook or waitress working at the time of inspection. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed the online food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Observed deli employee put on gloves without first washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed proper glove use and handwashing habits with PIC.
citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. (P)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
Observed deli handsink not to be functioning. CORRECTED- PIC replaced batteries in motion-sensor and handsink was observed to be functioning properly.
5-202.12 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 38oC (100oF) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. (Pf)

Observed handsinks in the deli and butcher shop to be blocked. CORRECTED- PIC moved equipment to make handsinks easily accessible.
citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
comment: Observed clean utensils stored in containers with crumbs and food debris and knife rack to be soiled with crumbs. Prevent contamination of clean utensils in storage and ensure clean utensils are stored in clean containers.
citation_text: 4-903.11 (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE USE ARTICLES shall be stored (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)

title: Gloves used properly
comment: Observed deli employee serve customers, adjust handsink, and return to serving customers without washing hands or changing gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure that gloves are used for only one task and that gloves are changed when tasks are changed.
citation_text: 3-304.15 (A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. (P)

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed a few vegetables spilled on the floor in the meat walk-in cooler. Observed food debris in a grocery cooler under packaged chorizo. Surfaces must be cleaned as frequently as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. (C)

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text:
3-101.11 (P) FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

Onions were observed spoiled in the racks on display in the produce section of the facility. All spoiled produce items were removed for discard during the inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Operator was observed washing hands without proper technique at the front handsink. Faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and operator was advised to reference proper handwashing posters located at handsinks for reference.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.
citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee was observed rinsing hands at the 3 part sink after working with raw chicken. Operator was advised that proper handwashing is to always occur at a designated handsink. Employee washed his hands at the kitchen handsink proper to next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Baskets of cooked, cooled eggrolls were uncovered in the walkin cooler. Operator was advised to provide covers once eggrolls are finished cooling and prior to long-term storage.
Bottle of tomato color was without a lid in the dry storage area. Product was removed from dry storage for discard.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions just made prior to inspector's arrival were at 0ppm and less than 10ppm. The issue with concentration was likely due to the type of bleach being used (see #28 for details). Solutions were remade with correct bleach at proper concentration and observed at 150ppm.
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain bleach solutions at 150ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Scoop in bulk corn starch bin was observed with buildup on it, especially around the handle. Scoop was removed for cleaning.  General buildup of debris was also observed on the upper portion inside another bulk powder. Cleaning frequency for bulk storage containers was discussed.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned any time contamination may have occurred or up to every 24hrs depending on use.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Operators were in the process of rolling vegetable eggrolls when inspector arrived. Operators stopped working with the eggrolls as soon as the inspector arrived and left wraps and egg in bowls out on prep tables. Cracked egg was observed at 54F/63F and eggroll wraps were observed at 57F/66F after sitting out for ~1hr. Prepared eggrolls were fried and remaining product was used. Operators were advised it is a bad practice to leave foods at ambient temperature if prep is stopped for an extended period of time. Place foods back in coolers if prep is stopped for longer than a few minutes.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked foods in the walkin cooler and bottom of the prep cooler did not have date marks. Foods included eggrolls, noodles, General Tso chicken, and sweet and sour chicken. All foods were cooked within the last one or two business days per information provided. Foods were labeled and kept for use. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Lemon scented Great Value brand bleach was available for use. Concentration of bleach solutions were likely effected by the type of bleach being used (see #16 for details). Proper bleach intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces was provided during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.12 Five gallon soy sauce bucket was observed under the prep sink plumbing. Soy sauce was not opened, but operator was advised it is not a good practice to store any food, regardless of packaging, under plumbing in case the plumbing would leak. Soy sauce was moved to the dry storage area. 
Food may not be stored in under anything that may be a source of contamination.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the front counter by the handsink. Wiping cloth was placed in bleach solution for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.11 Debris that appeared to be small, dead flies was observed inside the open packaging that had to-go boxes in the dry storage area. Packaging and to-go boxes were discarded. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Cardboard was used to line shelving in storage areas and on the bottom of the rice cooker table. Some of the cardboard was soiled with general buildup and splash. A soiled cardboard box was also observed being used for storage on the shelf behind the rice cooker. Options were discussed for cleanable, plastic tubs and other re-usable materials to be used for storage and lining shelving. Start replacing the cardboard.
Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (general buildup/food debris); 
B) dry storage shelving (general buildup);  and
C) chemical storage shelves by 3 part sink (general buildup). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-302.11 Toilet paper was not available in the women's room. Toilet paper was provided.
A supply of toilet tissue shall be available at each toilet

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text:
6-305.11 Personal items were observed sitting on bottled water packages and hanging on aprons on dry storage shelving. All items were moved to proper storage areas. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 One of the employees has not obtained his food handler certification. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employee was later observed using proper technique during handwashing. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands and also wiped his hands on a wiping cloth observed hanging from the corner of shelving in the dish area. Employee was advised on handwashing between handling the soiled and cleaned dishes and to also cease the practice of wiping hands on cloth towels. Soiled wiping cloth was placed in laundry bag, and the employee washed his hands prior to continuing dish washing tasks. 
Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
citation_text:
3-301.11 Soufflé cup was observed as a scoop in marinara. Cup was removed and discarded during inspection.
Food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler had use by date of 4/17 and no date mark. The gallon of milk in question was discarded. Another open gallon of milk used to make chocolate milk with syrup in house was not labeled but was not past the product use by date. Person in charge provided a proper date mark for the chocolate milk.  
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Caddies used for storage of clean utensils in the dish area were soiled with food crumbs. Clean the storage caddies daily/as needed, and maintain them clean to protect clean utensils from potential contamination.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-202.16 Soiled cardboard was observed as lining on the shelf used for storage of milk in the walkin cooler. PIC noted it is used to keep the smaller jugs of milk from falling over and breaking in the cooler. Use of a cleanable alternative, such as a baking sheet, was discussed. 
Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) box fan in dish area (dusty); 
B) speed rails at the bar (general splash/buildup);   and
C) top ledge of beer coolers used for cup storage (debris/splash under liners). 
Clean the aforementioned items. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 Half of the employees had expired food handler certifications. Owner sent information at the time of inspection to all staff that needed to renew certifications. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 PIC has not yet completed online food allergen awareness training. PIC was aware he needs the certification and is in the process of completing the course. 
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. The whole process took less than 10 seconds, and the manual faucet was shut off without use of a barrier. CFM was advised of the issue and was asked to reiterate the importance of proper handwashing with all staff. An educational handout showing proper technique was provided to be translated to Punjabi for future reference. 
Employees shall use the following method to clean their hands: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply cleaning compound; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water;  and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
5-205.11 Kitchen handsink in the back prep area was blocked by a laundry bag. Laundry bag was moved to allow for ease in access to the handsink. Proper use and accessibility of handsink was discussed.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the kitchen handsink in the back prep area. Handwashing sign was provided and posted during inspection. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Pans of various foods were uncovered on the cook line, in the walkin cooler, walkin freezer, and in the bottom of the prep cooler. Multiple foods in the walkin cooler were uncovered, and the shelving above was soiled with general buildup of food debris and dust. A few sections of shelving also had peeling paint 
Shelving in the bottom of the prep cooler was soiled with food splash over a pan of uncovered, cooked cauliflower.
Also, pans with butter and fresh, cut onions and green peppers were uncovered in an area on the cook line where the surfaces above and around the pans were soiled with splash and debris.
Proper storage was discussed. All pans of food were covered during the inspection.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.11 Some mold buildup was starting to accumulate on the ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Also, the diffusers of the soda nozzles had some buildup.
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
citation_text:
4-602.12 Ceiling inside the microwave was soiled with dried on food splash. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Cooked and shredded potatoes were observed on a prep cart by the back door. Potatoes had surface temperatures of 55F-61F. Potatoes were cooked and cooled in the walkin cooler earlier today based on information provided. Potatoes were said to have been removed for additional prep within the half hour prior to inspector's arrival. Nobody was working with the potatoes at the time of observation. Potatoes were placed back in the walkin cooler until staff had time to finish preparation for dinner service. Temperature abuse was discussed; CFM was advised to limit time food is out of cold holding during prep. Also, place foods back in cold holding if prep is interrupted and will not immediately resume. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Prepared foods in the walkin cooler (spinach saag, lamb dish, and rice pudding) and in the server area cooler (chutney) were not labeled. All foods were prepared earlier this week. Foods were dated and kept for use. Educational handout on date marking was provided. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41ºF/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use did not have proper labeling. Directions on the label had general cleaning and laundry instructions but no directions for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Owner purchased proper bleach during the inspection. Product label for approved bleach shows concentration of 150ppm; operator was advised to use test strips and verify proper concentration when solutions are prepared. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Two pans of tarka (onion and tomato) prepared earlier today were cooling in the bottom of the prep cooler. Pans were labeled with the time of 2:00 and temperatures of 120 and 140 on the pans. Internal temperatures were checked by inspector at 3p and observed at 127F-128F. Product had ~1hr to drop below 70F. Portions were split in half and placed in the walkin freezer to rapidly chill the product. Cooling methods were discussed, and educational handouts were provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 Large serving spoon was observed submerged in a container of raita (yogurt based sauce) in the walkin cooler. Only a small portion of the top of the handle could be seen. Serving spoon was removed from the sauce.
Pitcher with greasy water was observed storing serving utensils on the cook line. CFM noted the spoons and storage pitcher are cleaned up to every 4hrs. Pitcher and utensils were removed for cleaning.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, may be stored in foods with the handles extended out or in a container. Utensils may be stored in water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container and utensils are at least every 24 hours or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Pan used for storage of clean utensils was soiled with food debris and splash. CFM noted the utensils are typically cleaned again prior to each use. CFM was advised to clean the storage pan daily/as needed to protect clean utensils fro potential contamination. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-603.12 Vegetable chopper was observed in storage area with food debris stuck in the grooves of the push block and on the cutting surface. Chopper was cleaned after the last use, but food debris remained. Precleaning and repeating the wash, rinse, sanitize process for heavily soiled equipment were discussed. Chopper was taken to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized again.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Both hot and cold water at the left automatic faucet in the women's room ran for less than 5 seconds when dispensed. CFM noted the faucet has to be replaced, and a new faucet will be purchased within the next week for installation by a professional plumber. The right faucet in the women's room works properly. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Grout was worn down along the floor to wall juncture in the dish area along the wall where the dirty dish drain board is located. Accumulation of moisture and debris was observed in the area. Repairs have been scheduled.
Electrical cover under the dirty dish drain board was broken. Replace the cover. 
Surface under the dirty dish drain board was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the surface under the drain boards at the dish machine. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

6-5011.8 Kitchen handsink between the dish area and cook line was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin. Handles of both kitchen handsinks had varying amounts of debris accumulation. Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures. 
Plumbing fixtures such as handsinks shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Observed raw beef stored next to lettuce and deli meats in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods separated from raw so they are protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Chili is 125°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. The chili had been hot holding for approximately 2 hours. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Observed deli meat packages to be thawing at room temperature on the prep table in the kitchen. Time and temperature control for safety (TICS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13. Properly thaw foods for safety. Foods were placed into the cooler for thawing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Observed, live mouse in the back storage area. Also observed small flies in the appartment upstairs in the kitchen and restroom attached to the kitchen. Also, some small black ants are observed on the floor in the dry stoarge. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate all pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Observed the two part sink in the upstairs kitchen to be used for washing of food contact utensils. The utensils are taken downstairs to sanitize. Washing upstairs will be discontinued and all dish washing will take place in the three part downstairs. 4-301.12(A) (C) A sink with at least 3 compartments shall be provided for manual washing, rinsing, and sanitizing of food contact equipment and utensils. Reference 4-301.12(A)

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil residue present on counters and shelves in the upstairs kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12 (A&B) Observed floors in the dry stoarge in back, the dry storage upstairs and ktichen upstairs to be heavily soiled. The soil is even greater in hard to reach areas. Clean and maintain clean. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).
citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) Observed a ceiling tile to be missing from the restroom downstairs. Replace ceiling tile. Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.  Reference 6-501.11.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: Managers are not allerge trained. Provide allergen training befor next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: Arrived to facility with no CFM present. CFM arrived at facility shortly after. Ensure CFM is always present during hours of preparation.
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed several knives to be soiled with debris laying in "designated" clean area. Ensure all equipment and utensils are cleaned properly and placed in clean areas. Corrected. PIC will clean equipment.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
Observed food handler license expired. Ensure all food employees have food handler's license. Obtain certificate. 
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Food employee touched salmon and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed CFPM place on gloves without washing hands first to handle a pan of raw salmon. Corrected on sight. Salmon was discarded due to date-marking issue explained in violation #23.

title: Proper date marking and disposition

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
The following items were measured with temperatures greater than 41F (located in the South facing 3 door make table cooler): sliced salami 47F, roast beef 52F, ham 45F, turkey 47F, cut lettuce 50F, sliced tomatoes 53F. Staff indicated food items were placed into cooler less than 2 hours to inspection. Lid was observed open during busy times during inspection. Ambient temperature of cooler measured 39F. 
->Please monitor cooler temperatures to ensure food item temperatures are maintained less than 41F. All cold holding food item temperatures must be below 41F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
Bottle of Ortho Home Defense Bug Killer found stored on bottom shelf of tiered metal shelf located across from walk-in freezer at the time of inspection. 
->Pesticide discarded by the person in charge. Manufacturer's label instructions must state that use of the product is allowed in a food establishment. Domestic pesticides are not approved in retail kitchens. Approved commercial grade pesticides are allowed with proper storage provisions to prevent contamination. Reference 7-202.12.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 (A) (C) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection, there was not a certification for a certified food protection manager. The PIC was instructed to ensure that there is always a CFPM  at the facility when food handling is taking place. Follow up in 90 days.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: Chlorine bleach used for sanitizer does not have instructions for use on food contact surfaces (such as dishes, silverware) on the label nor does it have instructions on how to prepare for parts per million (ppm). Replace light. 6-303.11 (A, B, C) (C)  Light intensity shall be A) at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and other areas during periods of cleaning; B) At least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in areas where food is provided for consumer self-service or where fresh produce or packaged foods are sold or offered for consumption; inside equipment such as reach-in and under-counter refrigeration units; and in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, and equipment and utensil storage, and in restrooms; C) at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) in areas where employees are working with food or working with utensils or equipment where employee safety is a factor. title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Upon completing handwashing process, an employee was observed drying hands with paper towels prior to shutting off the manual faucet. The same paper towels were then used to continue drying hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee and management.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. The last step of handwashing upon drying hands with paper towels should be to shut off the manual faucet. However, if additional drying is needed, then employees need to get new paper towels to finish drying hands. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Eggs and sausages in the hot holding wells at the drive thru were below 135F. Eggs were observed with internal temperatures of 113F and 126F, while sausage had internal temperatures of 103F-113F. All product was discarded and replaced with freshly prepared food.
Options for maintaining hotter temperatures at the drive thru hot holding wells were discussed. Cool air blowing in from opening the drive thru window may affect the holding temperature. However, the holding unit was observed set at 3, the products were double panned, and the pans with foods were not in direct contact with hot water. All of these were likely factors that resulted in the hot holding temperature dropping below 135F. Management was advised to work with staff to monitor and improve upon hot holding process at the drive thru.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Products in the Turbo Chef station cold rail on the make line were observed with temperatures above 41F. Sliced tomato was initially observed at 47F-48F. Manager noted the products were just placed in the cold rail prior to inspector's arrival. Upon checking temperatures in the Turbo Chef cold rail at the drive thru station those foods were observed at 36F-43F, and the rail was frosted up to help maintain temperature. The cold rail on the make line was not frosted. When temperatures were checked again ~30 minutes later tomatoes had an internal temperature of 50F; cheese was observed at 52F. All foods were moved to the cold holding drawer beneath, which was holding bean paste at 35F. Management will be calling for service to get the cold rail checked. Until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below the cold rail on the make line Turbo Chef station will not be used. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

Hand washing was discussed. 2-301.14  (P)  Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Batter also splashed on the box of broccoli when doing this. Separation of prep areas for raw and ready to eat foods was discussed and raw chicken was moved to other areas. An employee also washed knives but did not sanitize them before placing them back on the magnetic strip. All dish ware must be washed, rinsed and then sanitized. 2) Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm bleach. No sanitizer was available in the facility as in Violation #48.  4-501.114  (P)  Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed garlic in oil mixture on the wok line at room temperature. It was discussed that this is a time and temperature control for safety food and must be held at 41F or below. This was discarded. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: Observed numerous items in the cooling process in the facility such as chicken, rice and steamed broccoli. Chicken at the front prep table near the fryer was probed at 76F and was reported to have been cooked at 11:30 am. Rice in the walk in cooler was in a large bowl with a smaller bowl within and was probed at 119F after being cooked at 12:30pm. Chicken that is being cooked and cooled is in large heaps on the tray rack and probed at 195F. It is hard to have a clear understanding if these items are cooling properly because no time or temperatures are being written down. Most of these items are cooked well above 165F and cooled at room temperature in large batches before being placed in the walk in cooler eventually. Cooling should be done in small batches, single layers uncovered and rapidly so that foods reach 70F within the first 2 hours of the cooling process. It is unknown if this is occurring or not since foods are inadvertently being hot held for some time before they cool from cooking temperature to 135F. 3-501.15  (Pf) To cool rapidly, use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

Do not store the bottom of of containers in direct contact with food. 3-305.11  (C)  Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

This was discussed before the employee left. 4-303.11 CHEMICAL SANITIZERS shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment: There are approximately 8 employees at the time of the inspection and facility only has 3 food handler certificates available. title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Several foods in the walkin cooler and the sandwich cooler were observed without date marks or with dates that indicated they were past the 7 day time frame for use. All foods in question were discarded. Proper date marking was discussed, and an educational handout provided for reference. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41ºF/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. Products prepared in-house even if commercially processed ingredients are combined together must also be dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
citation_text:
3-501.15 Two pans full to the top with cheese sauce prepared during the morning shift were observed sitting on the prep table cooling. Surface and internal temperatures were at 90F/100F and 107F/108F respectively. Cheese sauce was held on the stove in a double boiler until removed for cooling around 130p based on information provided. Temperature was not checked at any point during the process. Cook had ~20 minutes to get product below 70F per the time frame indicated. Cheese sauce was portioned into four pans to allow for shallower amount of product in each pan, and pans were placed in a freezer to flash chill the product. Methods for proper cooling were discussed, and cook was advised to monitor the temperature during cooling to ensure foods are cooling quickly and properly. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

title: Approved thawing methods used
citation_text: 3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish were in the process of thawing in the walkin cooler at the time of inspection. Directions on the packaging states to remove from package and thaw under refrigeration. Staff were advised to make sure the packaging is at minimum cut once thawing is complete. Per the 2017 FDA Code, under Thawing, Section 3-501.13 Part E (E) frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

citation_text:
3-501.15 Multiple foods were in various stages of the cooling process in the walkin cooler.
Stuffing prepared prior to inspector's arrival was tightly covered with foil in stainless steel pans. Product was ~20 minutes into the cooling process based on information provided and had an internal temperature of 76F.

Soups and sauces were placed in shallow pans (~4" deep) uncovered in the walkin freezer on speed racks, with ice wands also utilized in some products, to speed up the cooling process. Stuffing was also uncovered in the walkin freezer to finish rapid chill.

Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4)
Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6)
Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be:
(1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 10 ppm in kitchen sanitizer bucket. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration for adequate sanitizing in kitchen. Replace sanitizer solution every 4 hours as the chemicals naturally break down and become less effective over time. CFPM made a new sanitizing solution on site. Reference 4-501.114.

Inspector advised that prepared food shall be quickly moved to the cooler for cold-holding before beginning another prep task. TCS food should be maintained at 41 or below for cold holding or 135 and above for hot holding. Both items were corrected immediately and transferred to walk-in cooler.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation. Inspector observed dust and debris accumulated on fan grate in the walk-in cooler. Clean surface frequently to prevent blowing of dirt onto refrigerated items. Reference 4-602.13.

2-401.11  (C) B. A food employee may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of (3) Exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, and linens; and unwrapped single service and single use articles Reference 2-401.11.

Observed a proper beverage container (closed with lid and straw) above a food prep area. Ensure personal beverages are on the lowest shelf possible to prevent contamination of customer food.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: 1) Observed raw Italian sausage stored above hot dogs and sauerkraut, and raw shell eggs stored above corned beef in the prep cooler. 2) Observed raw pork sausage stored on top of and in the same pan with a package of pre-cooked beef in the walk in cooler. Coolers were rearranged and ready to eat foods moved above raw foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Observed white cheese sauce on the steam table to be probed at an internal temperature of 128 and meatballs in the steam table to be probed at 120F. Both of these items were in the middle section of the steam table. Sauce in the meatball pan was probed at 140F, however, the meatballs are not down in the sauce and were only 120F. It appears as though the cheese may have been reheating but possibly was not reheated rapidly on the stove first. Surface temperature at the end of the inspection was 153F.  3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed hot dogs dated 3/20 and spaghetti dated 3/17 in the prep cooler, a pan of cooked pasta and a pan of cooked beef in the walk in cooler with no date, and a container of cooked meatballs dated 3/12 in the walk in cooler. These are either outside of the 7 day date marking or not dated appropriately. Date mark all ready to eat, time and temperature control for safety foods and hold no longer than 7 days maximum with the date of preparation counting as a full Day 1. These items were discarded or dated during the inspection. 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed several pans and containers of sauces in the walk in freezer that are frozen solid but have not been covered yet and remain stored uncovered. Cover foods once they have cooled to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment: Observed the following: 1) paper and tape on the top corner of the microwave door, 2) dusty cardboard covering the condensor unit on the reach in freezer in the kitchen, and 3) hood baffles missing in the ventilation system for the pizza oven. Repair these non-food contact surfaces. 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA 100-0367 Facility has not completed allergen awareness training. Each certified food manager will need to complete an ANSI approved allergen awareness training.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Cook has a food handler certification. Cook and principal were advised that a manager certification is now required for the person in charge of food service per the FDA Food Code. Cook and any other staff that cover the lunch service when cook is absent need to be certified food managers. 

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed preparing to put on gloves to handle food without first washing hands. Multiple surfaces were touched after removing the pair of gloves he was wearing previously. Proper hand washing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves were discussed.  

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands and prior to putting on gloves to handle food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Can opener had black gooey buildup along the top edge of the blade. Cook used the can opener prior to inspector's arrival to open fruit cocktail. Proper cleaning and sanitizing was discussed. The blade was wiped down and sanitized during the inspection. Cook was advised to clean and sanitize the can opener with all other utensils and equipment at the conclusion of lunch service. 

Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned and sanitized between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-202.12 Spray bottle of bleach solution was observed at a concentration so strong that it bleached out the test strip and began to turn it white. Cook was advised on proper use of the two bleach products available. Solution was diluted to be at 200ppm chlorine. Follow label directions and use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration (150-200ppm). 

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling and in a manner that does not pose a hazard to people or risk of contamination of food, single service articles, and clean equipment.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic container used for storing knives in the dry storage room was observed to be soiled with general debris and dead insects in the bottom. Container and knives were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Cleaning of the storage container and/or use of a covered container were discussed. 

Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment: Observed a 5 lb package of ground beef thawing in standing water in the three compartment sink that was probed at 67F and was reported to have been pulled around noon. Thawing must occur in one of the approved manners (in refrigeration, under cool running water of 70F for 2 hours or less, as part of the cooking process or in the microwave if cooked immediately after). Beef was discarded at the time of the inspection. 3-501.12  (C)  Frozen Time and Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food must be held under refrigeration at 41° or less, or at any temperature during slacking if the food remains frozen before cooking. Reference 3-501.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed automatic soap dispenser in the mens restroom to be not functioning. Facility did not have extra batteries on site, but sent an employee to purchase extra batteries so the soap dispenser will properly dispense. Employee returned and replaced batteries before completion of the inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Observed quat sanitizer from dispenser to have a concentration of 100ppm (label states 150ppm-400ppm). PIC called dispenser company and a representative should be out within 24 hours. PIC will prepare sanitizer by hand and use test strips to confirm concentration in the meantime. Inspector may spot check this issue before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under §7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
comment: Observed handsink near walk-in to be leaking. Plumbing must be in good repair and without leaks.
citation_text: 5-205.15 A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Observed a missing ceiling tile in dry storage. Observed floor drain and cover under self-service soda machine to be heavily coated in mold accumulation. Observed soil on the underside of the three-compartment sink. Maintain facility in good repair and clean as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

PA 100-0367 Section 3.07

3-202.15 (Pf) FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Cans were observed in dry storage with dents along the top and bottom seams. The entrance of oxygen was via this situation and pathogenic growth was discussed with the PIC. The cans were set aside to receive credit from the company during the inspection.

(2) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. (4) Storing the FOOD in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

4-601.11 (Pf) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

The meat slicer in the facility was observed soiled with food debris during the inspection. PIC was instructed to clean the slicer after each use.

citation_text:
3-304.12 (C) During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: 1) In the foods with the handles sticking out, 2) on a cleaned and sanitized surface, 3) in potable running water, 4) in water held at 135 F, 5) in a clean, protected location.
Ice scoops were observed in both server areas stored on the grill used for trapping soda splash from the fountain drinks. This is not a clean surface. Store food contact utensils in an approved manner.

Spoons were observed stored in standing water next to the hot held soups. This is not an approved method of storing cleaned and sanitized utensils. Store cleaned and sanitized utensils in a clean dry location.
