Single service Styrofoam containers were observed stored on top of the cook line shelving with the eating surfaces pointed up. The issue was discussed and the containers flipped down to correct.

A can of corn was observed on the stove with the corn cooking in the original can. This is not a container intended for cooking temperatures. Use a container intended for cooking when cooking foods.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Observed food employee transfer a raw hamburger to grill with gloved hands, then discard gloves and proceed to continue food preparation touching clean utensils and surfaces in the kitchen without a handwash in between. 

->Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Discussed importance of handwashing after handling raw animal products. Reference 2-301.14(G).

title: Food separated and protected
comment:
Observed raw shell eggs stored directly above container of ready-to-eat pickles and squeeze bottle of ketchup in the coco-cola cooler near the restrooms. Refrigerator was reorganized at the time of inspection. 

->Store raw animal products by cooking temperature and below ready-to-eat foods to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Chlorine dish machine behind the bar found sanitizing with concentrations less than 50 ppm chlorine at the time of inspection. Test strips were provided. 
->Ensure concentrations are between 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Verify proper concentrations with test strips. Reference 4-501.114.

The following food contact surfaces found soiled: 
1. interior of chlorine dish machine located behind bar soiled with scale build-up
2. piercing tip of table top can opener soiled with food debris
->Food contact surfaces of cooking/baking equipment must be cleaned and sanitized at least once ever 24 hours. Reference 4-602.12.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Spaghetti noodles 50F, fettucine noodles 45F, spiral noodles 48F found stored in lidded plastic containers in the 3 door make table cooler across from the cookline. Staff indicated items were cooked on 3/24/19 and noodle cooling process consists of chilling cooked noodles in water bath and then transferring to containers for cold holding until customer order. 

->Discussed importance of proper cooling practices and different methods to achieve proper cooling temperatures. Ensure food items reach 41F prior to portioning into lidded containers. 
->Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food items were discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
Kitchen: Sliced tomatoes 68F-70F observed sitting at room temperature at the beginning of inspection. Staff indicated items were being sliced for lunch. Tomatos transferred into shallow pan and placed into walk-in cooler for cooling. 
Walk-in cooler: Lettuce 48F-50F in lidded, deep plastic container. Staff indicated lettuce was prepped less than 1 hour to inspection. Lid was removed for more rapid cooling. 
Customer service area in the dining room: cut lettuce 45F and tomatoes 44F on ice bath for taco toppings. Noted the items not submerged in the ice, or lids to assist in temperature retention. 

->Please ensure cold holding temperatr. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
The following items found without proper date marking, located in cooler behind the bar: cocktail sauce (prepped on 3/9,discarded), gusto sauce (Staff indicated prepped 3/22, labeled on site), 1000 island (no date, discarded).

->Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

The following non-food contact surfaces found soiled:
1. basin of handsink in the kitchen and behind bar found with accumulation of grime
2. interior walls and floor of 4 door freezer across from the dish machine found soiled with food debris
3. bottom portion underneath roller grill on oven in kitchen found heavily accumulated with food debris and splatters. Staff indicated a plan of action for this cleaning process. 
4. knife sharpener tethered to wall-mounted knife storage container located next to 3 compartment sink found soiled with food accumulation

->Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil, grime and food accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: 1) Observed raw chicken and bacon in the walk in cooler stored above celerey and cheese. 2) Observed raw chicken and beef stored above cooked chicken wings in the reach in cooler. Raw chicken was moved during the inspection so that raw foods were not stored above ready to eat foods. 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
comment: Observed nine portions of cheese/queso sitting on top of the lids of items in the steam table that were probed at 115F. Employee states that when they are busy, they pull these to warm up before they microwave them to serve. He states they pull these and use within 10 minutes but is not keeping any documentation of this. These were discarded and hot holding was discussed. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: 1) Observed hot dogs with a date of 3/15 in the prep cooler. 2) Observed coleslaw, cooked onion/peppers and spinach dip with no date and an avocado mix dated 3/15 in the reach in cooler. 3) Observed hot dogs dated 3/15 in the walk in cooler. These are all open, ready to eat foods that must be date marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum with the date of opening/prep counting as a full Day 1. These items were discarded.  3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

Salt was labeled during the inspection. 7-102.11  (Pf)  Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: Observed traditional chicken wings in a bucket cooling in the reach in cooler to be probed at 125F and boneless wings in this same cooler to be probed at 95F with no indication as to when the cooling process began. Cooling must be done rapidly as an active process where it is documented when the cooling process begins to ensure that foods are reaching 70F within 2 hours of cooling. Facility has thermometers available and will begin tracking this. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment: REPEAT PRACTICE> Observed a couple wet wiping cloths sitting on prep surfaces and cloths in the sanitizer bucket to not be fully submerged in sanitizer solution. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution in between use.  3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

In use utensils should have a handle with the handle stored up and out of the food if stored in the food in between use.  3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Crab meat observed in walkin cooler had a prep date of 3/20 and use by date of 3/28. Operator stated the product is good for 8 days and stated proper documentation was available. Operator was advised to count day of preparation as Day 1, which would mean the use by date would be 3/27 instead of 3/28. Label was changed to reflect proper time frame for service. 

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

7-204.11 Clorox splashless bleach was available for use and did not have proper labeling. This product is not approved for sanitizing food contact surfaces. A bottle of Clorox Concentrated Bleach was in the inspector's car for an example of what needs to be present on the labeling.

Bleach used for sanitizing in a food service facility must have the following information on the label: EPA Reg number, instructions for sanitizing food contact surfaces, and a concentration for use listed in ppm.

Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned

comment: Observed sanitizer buckets to test between 0 and 100 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. These are prepared from the wall mounted dispenser at the three compartment sink. Reference 4-501.114.

Reference 4-602.13.

Reference 4-101.19.

Reference 6-301.12.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: Observed the dipper wells where the spatulas for cutting the custard are stored to not be on and spatulas stored in standing water. Dipper wells were turned on during the inspection. Keep dipper wells on when storing in use utensils. 3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
comment: Observed single service items stored in the cabinet underneath the soda fountain in the dining room where the drain lines run. Do not store single service items in this area. Store them in the cabinets that do not have drain lines/wastewater running through them. 4-903.12 (C)  Single-Use Articles may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. Reference 4-903.12.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment: Observed refried beans that had been cooked yesterday, reported to have been placed in the walk in freezer for 2 hours to cool, and then transferred to the walk in cooler to be probed with a recently calibrated digital stem thermometer at 50F at the time of the inspection (almost 24 hours later). Beans are in a large multi-gallon container with the lid sealed tightly. Refried beans were discarded at the time of the inspection and cooling was discussed.  3-501.14  (P)  Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment: As above, the refried beans were in a large plastic multi-gallon container with the lid on tight in the walk in cooler. When cooling, especially with dense foods such as refried beans, large quantities must be divided into smaller portions in shallow pans for rapid cooling. 3-501.15  (Pf) Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment: Facility has an infrared thermometer, but no stem (probe) thermometer is able to be located at the time of the inspection. A thermometer for taking internal temperatures of food must be provided and used. Infrared thermometers only take a surface temperature of foods.
citation_text: 4-302.12  (Pf) A food thermometer is not available. Food thermometers shall be provided and readily accessible to ensure proper food temperatures. Reference 4-302.12.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

citation_text: 4-202.16. Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Make sure wiping clothes are properly submerged in solution between uses.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: 1) Observed par-cooked chicken cooling in a perforated bowl that was sitting on top of cardboard egg crates. Use something that is smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable. 2) Observed shell eggs stored above carrots in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products as carrots have a lower cooking temperature than shell eggs and must be stored in proper order to prevent contamination. 3-302.11  (P)   Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
1) Observed lemon scented bleach being used as a sanitizer. Bleach when used as a sanitizer must be plain bleach, and under the FDA food code it must have an EPA registration number and instructions for use on food contact surfaces on the label. Provide approved bleach.

7-102.11  (Pf) Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.
citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Meat is thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Ranch dressing labeled "keep refrigerated" is 47°F internal and 57-58 along edge. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ranch was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

A gallon and a half of ranch was voluntarily discarded.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee failed to wash hands. Staff was observed entering the kitchen from outside the building without proper handwashing. Handwashing was not observed during the course of the inspection. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12. Handwashing was discussed during the inspection.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text: 3-202.15  (Pf) Food packaging on dried chili peppers and pepper is in poor condition. The containers were discarded during the inspection.  Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15.

title: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
citation_text: 3-402.11  (P) Food establishment is serving undercooked, ready-to-eat fish that has not undergone proper parasite destruction process. The owner of the facility does not keep receipts and records for sushi fish on-site. All observed tuna is thawed and ready-to-eat. Per a phone conversation, the owner indicated the fish is received frozen. Examples of records were viewed with facility. Provide evidence/documentation that undercooked, ready-to-eat fish has been properly frozen at appropriate temperature and time to ensure parasite destruction. Reference 3-402.11.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Raw eggs are observed stored on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler over other vegetables. Also, observed personal foods being stored on the second to top shelf over produce.  Store eggs and other personal foods  so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0 ppm in bucket. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114. The facility was only using a soap and water bucket on the frontline. A sani-bucket filled with chlorine solution should be available at the front and rear of house.  4-601.11Observed four rice steamers to be soiled around the rim of the heating unit with old rice. Two steamers were in-use and two had been stored 'clean' for future use. Also, the meat slicer is observed soiled from previous use (with no current use occurring) and old, greasy paper toweling is observed within several pans used as scoops from fryers. The tongs over the lime container is soiled with a sticky red substance (pulled for cleaning).  Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Sushi rice is observed at 75°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).   Time as Control form was created and discussed with staff. Food should be held for four hours and then discarded.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text: 3-501.19  (Pf) Sushi rice is out of temperature control at 75 °F. The method of Time as a Public Health Control does not have an effective written method to record the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control to the discard time. Discussed the HACCP concepts and requirement for written procedures with the person in charge. Product discarded by person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Observed recent mouse droppings throughout the back storage room. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate mice , using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination on the top shelf over the preparation cooler. Items were changed to a second shelf location and provided with a lid. Seasonings and frequently used items should be stored in a clean and covered container.  Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.
3-304-12 Observed a portion cup being used as a scoop within ready-to-eat red pepper flakes. Removed during inspection.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Wet wiping cloths are observed on various counters on the kitchen frontline. Cloths were removed from counters, however, a proper sani-bucket was not created until the end of the inspection. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly on-the counter and soiled with food (soup ladle and salad tossing bowl). Removed for cleaning during the inspection.  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text: 4-502.13  (C) ) Observed multiple pieces of used parchment paper on baking rack by triple sink. Paper is being used to dry coconut and fried bread crumbs. Parchment paper appears to have gone through multiple uses. Cease re-use of parchment paper. Pulled from racks during inspection. Single service articles are reused. Single service articles may not be reused. Reference 4-502.13.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text:
4-201.11  (C) A large, bare wood log is being used in the kitchen as a storage counter. The log has a deep groove down the side that allows for storage of grease and debris within the groove. Cease use of this bare wood for storage. Remove from use and replace with equipment that is durable and easily cleanable meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI standards. Reference 4-201.11.
ALSO, the glass at the sliding sushi cooler is observed cracked. Replace glass.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on: (1) interior sides of preparation cooler lid; (2) rolling storage rack in the walk-in cooler. . Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) Observed a cell phone, windshield scrapper, and a magazine on a counter between a cutting board and plastic wrap (food preparation area). Moved items during the inspection. Areas designated for employees lockers shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination.  Reference 6-403.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 4-602.13  (C)  Observed soil residue present on fans in walk in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil residue present on inside of microwave. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Person in charge of food prep/service has a food handler certification but does not have a manager certification. Owner and director have manager certifications but were informed the person in charge of food service needs to be a certified food manager as well. Information was provided for food sanitation courses. 

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook went between tasks and was not observed washing hands at any point during the inspection. Food was in the process of being prepared for lunch, dishes were being washed, and various surfaces were touched. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after leaving the kitchen and upon returning prior to handling anything related to food service and after handling soiled dishes/equipment.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114  Concentration of bleach solution in ware washing sink was observed at 50ppm. Concentration required per label instructions shows an effective concentration of 100-200ppm. Can opener was sanitized in the solution based on information provided. Cook was advised to re-sanitize the can opener prior to next use and maintain sanitizing solution for ware washing at proper concentration as directed per manufacturer instructions. Solution was emptied to be remade after lunch service. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of the food thermometer was observed to be soiled with stuck on food debris. Stem was wiped with inspector's alcohol wipe. Proper use and care of stem thermometers was discussed. 

Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
citation_text:
3-501.14 Chili that was cooked in advance for lunch another day this week was observed in the fridge. Stock pot was placed in the fridge to cool after it was cooked around 7a based on information provided by the cook. Chili had a surface and internal temperatures of 75°F and 82°F respectively. Owner chose to discard the chili and will prepare chili fresh for same day service later this week. Proper cooling was discussed, and educational handouts were provided.  (See general comments for additional information)

Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135ºF to 70°F and within an additional 4 hours from 70°F to 41°F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135ºF to 41°F/below.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment:
7-102.11 Chemical bottles in one cabinet under the ware washing sinks were observed without labels. Bottles were emptied during the inspection. Proper labeling of chemical spray bottles was discussed. 

Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.
citation_text:
7-202.12 Raid insecticide was observed in one of the cabinets with cleaning supplies under the ware washing sinks. Owner discarded the product during inspection. Proper storage and use of toxics were discussed. Owner was advised to work with a pest control company to determine a proper option for insecticide use in the facility. 

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state use is allowed in a food establishment.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers were checked for accuracy with an ice water solution. One stem thermometer was reading at 25°F while the other was around 33°F. The thermometer observed at 25°F was calibrated to 32°F in the ice water solution. Calibration was discussed, and educational handout was provided. 

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Manager did not wash his hands after working the register and prior to preparing an order of nachos for a customer. Manager went directly from working at the register and immediately began preparing the order. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed. Manager was advised that hands must be washed every time when going from handling money/debit cards at the register and then preparing food for customers and handling single service articles. 

Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as  working at the register and handling money.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use in the store is not approved as a sanitizer. During the 3/6/19 routine/re-inspection Clorox concentrated bleach that had the proper label for use as a food contact surface sanitizer was available for use. That bleach is no longer present; bleach with general cleaning and laundry instructions is the only type available. Proper bleach is supposed to be purchased later today or some time tomorrow. 

Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Manger stated he was unable to find/successfully purchase a chlorine test kit. A description of what is needed was written down and provided for manager to take with him to allow for purchasing the correct test kit. Inspector provided some chlorine test strips and a picture of the PPM chart was taken by the manager for use until a proper test kit can be purchased for use. Test kit is supposed to be purchased with bleach later today or some time tomorrow. 

A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Heavily soiled garbage can was still present at the front counter by the handsink. A liner was in the can. Manager was advised the garbage can still needs to be cleaned or replaced. It is heavily soiled with a gross buildup of debris. 

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash, and general debris.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-202.14 Restroom door remains to be fixed so it is self-closing and tight-fitting.

A toilet room shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11 Hole in the floor in front of retail shelving holding grape drink and water jugs remains to be repaired. See report from 3/6/19 for additional information.

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
citation_text:
6-501.114 Unnecessary items were still present including but not necessarily limited to mufflers, head lights, and unused equipment. Some of the equipment is supposed to be going away for use or storage elsewhere. Other items will be remaining on-site. Manager was advised to organize items to show value. The current storage practice makes it appear as though all the unused equipment is junk awaiting disposal.

The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with black slime mold. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed  Date of 2/27 marked on green peppers and fish sauce in cooler exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41?F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
citation_text: 4-101.11  (P) Observed  In-use cutting board with deep gouges and grooves. The cutting board can no longer be washed and sanitized properly to prevent pathogen growth. Reference 4-101.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C)Floor in the kitchen area behind fryer was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

Steaks were observed in the cooler across from the grill area to have internal temperatures of 45-46°F. The TCS foods had been in the cooler greater than 4 hours (discussion suggested they were placed in the cooler at 10 am). The TCS foods were discarded during the inspection.

title: Variance obtained for specialized processing methods
citation_text:
8-103.11 (B) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall obtain a VARIANCE from the REGULATORY AUTHORITY as specified in § 8-103.10 and under § 8-103.11 before curing FOOD. 

No variance has been obtained at the time of the inspection for the curing process being used at this time. The paperwork used by this department was given during the inspection and the facility was instructed to complete it a return the completed form to the department prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Pizza paddle was observed with stuck on food debris. Paddle was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment between uses/up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Carbon and food splash were observed around the burners and on the drip tray of the stove and around the grill. Clean the aforementioned items.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 & 2-301.15 Employee went from handling debit cards and cash at the register and then prepared an order of nachos without washing his hands. When advised on handwashing between tasks, employee stated he washed his hands at the 3 part sink prior to working the register. Employee was advised that handwashing is to occur only at designated handsinks, and hands always need to be washed prior to handling food and preparing orders for customers. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, sch as working the register and handling money.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food preparation or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:
6-301.11 Hand soap was not preset at the restroom handsink. A bar of soap was provided from the store. 

Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the bathroom handsink. Operator stated he was out of paper towels and had to buy more. Maintain paper towels on-site to allow for backup when needed. Paper towels, as well as soap, should always be available to allow for proper handwashing at both handsinks. 

Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 Tongs used for jalapeno slices had dried cheese sauce along the edge. Operator stated some jalapeno slices feel in the cheese sauce and were retrieved with the tongs. Tongs were placed at the 3 part sink, and a clean pair of tongs were placed at the food service area. 

If only used with the jalapeno slices, then the tongs need to be cleaned and sanitized at the end of operations daily and/or any time they may have been contaminated, for example if they fell on the ground. If the tongs come in contact with taco meat or cheese, then they need to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 Various food items were observed on the floor in around the front counter, including a jar of jalapeno slices by the handsink and boxes of candy. All foods were moved or elevated off the floor to allow for proper storage.

Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Chlorine test kit was not available for checking concentration of bleach solutions during sanitization.  

A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use chlorine test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 Bottom inside coolers and tracks of cooler doors were soiled with general buildup and debris. Clean inside the coolers.
Garbage can at the front counter handsink was heavily soiled with grimy buildup inside. Clean or replace the garbage can at the front counter. 

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
citation_text:
5-402.13 Mop bucket with waste water from cleaning the previous evening was observed in the facility. Employee emptied the waste water in the mopsink during inspection. 

All sewage and waste water must be must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility overnight.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
citation_text:
6-202.14 Restroom door is not self-closing and tight-fitting. Repair the restroom door so it closes properly.

A toilet room shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
citation_text:
5-501.16 Waste receptacle was not observed in the restroom. Provide a waste receptacle for disposal of paper towels after handwashing. 

A waste receptacle shall be located at each handwashing sink where disposable paper towels are used.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.11 A hole was observed in the floor in front of the retail shelves with jugs of grape drink and water. It appeared a cover may have been removed and/or tiles were damaged. Provide proper repairs to the floor in front of the retail shelves. 

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text:
6-501.114 Unnecessary items were once again observed at the facility. Items included, but were not necessarily limited to car tires/rims, mufflers, headlights, and unused equipment. Remove all unnecessary items from the facility.

The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Provide a freeze date and a thaw date on the labels.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed several containers of fish and frog legs in walk in cooler that had no top covering.
citation_text: 3-302.11 - Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation.  Food must be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on opened gallons of milk in the reach in and walk in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer?s use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on several non food contact surfaces throughout the kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink. Maintain concentration at 200ppm or as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114. Repair the sanitizer dispenser. For now the facility will manually mix the sanitizer to 200ppm of Quat.

comment: 6-201.11  (C) Floors in the Kitchen area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily clean able. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily clean able.  Reference 6-201.11. Repair areas where the tile is pulled appart and cracked.

Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: No employee health documentation is present at facility. All employees must have documentation at facility. Corrected. Handout provided.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Observed Chicken, Green Beans, and Mashed Potatoes to be approx. 80F after 3 hours. Cooling was done incorrectly. Products were discarded. Ensure proper cooling occurs for all TCS foods. Corrected. Education provided.
Food must drop from 135F to 70F in 2 hours. Within 4 hours of dropping to 70F, the food must reach 41F. The whole process can take upto 6 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Chicken, Green beans, and mashed potatoes are approx. 80F. Food did not cool from 135?F to 70?F within two hours and from 135?F to 41?F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment: Observed R-I Cooler (Cook Fridge) to be out of temperature. Air temperature was measured to be 46F. Multiple food products were discarded. These included Spaghetti Sauce, Green Beans, Chicken Salad, cut lettuce and tomatoes. All foods exceeded 41F. All TCS foods out of temp. were discarded. Corrected. PIC stated work order has been placed on unit. Unit was leaking.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41?F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41?F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 (C) EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS or other items needing protection can not result.

A coffee cup was observed on the steam table and a glass on the counter by the woks. Neither item has a straw and the cup was without a lid. Inspector discussed the situation with the PIC and instructed them to store beverages in areas separate from food preparation. The cups were moved during the inspection.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:

A scoop was observed stored in a bucket of sauce so that only a small piece was out of the sauce. Discussed with the PIC and the scoop was moved to cleaning during the inspection.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:

Reference 6-305.11.

title: Allergen training as required

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19  (P) Observed corn dogs sitting out prior to being taken to classrooms. Observed garlic bread at room temperature and grilled cheese thawing on the counter. When using time as a control, there must be a written policy.

When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135°F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Main employee responsible for food handling/prep in the kitchen has a food handler certification but has not yet completed the food manager course. Employee is registered to take a course through MJ Kellner next month. 
Provide proof of certification.

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee entered the kitchen and did not wash hands prior to putting away clean dishes. Handwashing was discussed, and employee washed hands prior to continuing with the task. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival kitchen handsink was blocked with gallon milk jugs. Jugs were removed from the sink and discarded. Proper use of handsink was discussed.

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Can opener blade was soiled with food buildup from previous use. Can opener was last used on Friday and had not yet been used to open cans today. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized prior to use.

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses or up to every 4hrs after continuous use for items such as the can opener and other in-use equipment.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was observed at 80°F at ambient temperature. Staff noted the thermometer had not been calibrated since it was purchased. Ice water method was used to check the thermometer, which was reading around 40°F. Pliers were used to properly calibrate the thermometer to 32°F in the ice water solution. 

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions used on general surfaces in the kitchen. Some test strips were provided by inspector. Staff were advised to purchase strips for checking the quat sanitizer. (see general comments for additional information)

 A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed uncovered containers of flour and peanuts in dry storage area.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C). Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Observed dish machine rinse cycle testing at 0 ppm chlorine.  Data plate on machine calls for 50 ppm chlorine in the rinse cycle.
citation_text: 4-204.117 Warewashing Machines, Automatic Dispensing of Detergents and Sanitizers (Pf).  Reference 3-307.11

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text: 6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded or otherwise protected in the cooking area. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

comment: No employee health documentation was provided. All employees must have employee health documentation. Corrected.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: No vomit/diarrhea cleanup procedure in facility. Facility must have procedure in place. Corrected.
citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment: Several knifes on knife rack were found to be soiled. In addition, can opener is soiled with debris. Clean food equipment properly and store in clean area.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Knife rack food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
comment: Observed rice on steam table to be out of temperature. PIC stated rice is under time control policy. Rice was cooked at 11. Product was not discarded upon start of inspection. In addition, no time control policy is available. Product will be discarded. Time policy will be created.
citation_text: 3-501.19  When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41?F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135?F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food
comment: No consumer advisory was present. Ensure consumer advisory is present for patrons eating undercooked foods. Corrected. Documentation Provided.
citation_text: 3-603.11  (Pf) A consumer advisory is not provided for serving raw or undercooked food. Discussed disclosure and reminder requirements. Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. Reference 3-603.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Observed large grease accumulation on ventilation system. 
Observed salsa to be stored with no cover. Ensure food is covered to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at display cooler . Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment:
Observed ice handle to be touching ice.
Observed cup to be used for dried peppers. 
In-use utensils must be placed with handle outward preventing contamination. Ensure appropriate utensils are used.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly ice machine and dry peppers . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 ?F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed W-I freezer to be in state of disrepair. Freezer has no lighting and frost build-up. Ensure all equipmemt is in proper repair. Fix freezer.
citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) Freezer equipment was found in disrepair in the  area of the establishment. Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.  Reference 6-501.11.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 (B) (C) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

2 cups were observed in the prep areas of the kitchen without lids or straws. Discussed with the PIC and beverages were moved to cups with lids and straws.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 (A) (4) (C) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by storing the FOOD in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

An opened can of sliced mushrooms was observed in the walk in cooler still in the can and without a covering of some kind. The situation was discussed and the contents of the container were moved to a half pan with a lid.

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
citation_text:
3-502.11 (G) (Pf) A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall obtain a VARIANCE from the REGULATORY AUTHORITY as specified in § 8-103.10 and under § 8-103.11 before preparing FOOD by any method that is determined by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY to require a VARIANCE.

Yoghurt us being made at the facility without a variance or lab testing. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the information given for Key Libratory Services in Decatur.

title: Variance obtained for specialized processing methods
citation_text:
8-103.11 (Pf) When a food establishment wants to utilize a special process, a variance and/or HACCP Plan must first be obtained from the regulatory authority.

The facility is currently making yogurt in the facility without regulatory approval. The situation was discussed with the PIC and relevant information given.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 (C) During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: 1) in the food with the handle out of the food, 2) on a cleaned and sanitized surface, 3) in running water, 4) in a container of water held above 135 F.
Multiple scoops were observed stored in a bucket of water that was sitting on a table. The situation was discussed with the PIC. The utensils were moved to cleaning during the inspections and in the future the bucket will be stored on a stove burner to maintain temperature.

title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
citation_text:
4-904.13 (A) (C) TABLEWARE that is preset shall be protected from contamination by being wrapped, covered, or inverted.

The silverware preset on tables in the facility is layed out without being covered or wrapped. The issue was discussed with the PIC and instructed to ensure that preset tableware is protected.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
PA 100-0367 All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

The CFPM at the facility has not yet completed an ANSI accredited allergen training course. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed them to completed the course prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the handsink by the dish area. Paper towels were provided during the inspection.

Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in sani-bucket by the front make line handsink was less than 100ppm. Solution was discarded and new solution prepared at proper concentration of 100ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 100ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.
citation_text:
4-602.11 (E)(4) Lower left edge of the drive thru soda machine ice shoot had mold accumulation. Ice shoot was sanitized during the inspection. 
Lobby soda machine was observed with heavy mold accumulation where nozzles attach to the machine. Manager sanitized the area in question during the inspection. 

Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and ice shoots of soda machines shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee did not change gloves after handling boxes of recently delivered dry goods and prior to returning to the make line. Employee washed hands and changed gloves at the request of the manager. 

Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Low lying area under the make line where a floor drain was previously located was observed with ponding water and debris accumulation. A slight odor was present as well. Management was advised to clean under the make line and get the area repaired to eliminate ponding water. 

Men's room handsink and inside the toilet were soiled with general buildup. Clean in the restrooms daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Certified food manager on duty did not have food allergen awareness training completed. Requirements for allergen training were discussed. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
citation_text:
2-102.12 Kitchen manager has an expired food manager certification and just took a course this week. Exam was completed on 2/27 and results have not yet been received. Manager will contact SCDPH with certification number and expiration date once she has results.  

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed touching the handles of the manual faucet and paper towel dispenser without a barrier after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
Proper handwashing technique poster was observed at handsink for reference.

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink and handles of paper towel dispensers. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of bleach solution in one classroom was observed at ~100ppm. The label directions show a required concentration of 150-200ppm. Solution was discarded and new solution prepared at proper concentration of 200ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 A package of open deli ham was observed with a date mark of 2/11/19 in the cooler. Manager stated that was the day the product was received. Product was likely past the 7 day time frame for use and was discarded. Proper date marking of opened ready to eat TCS foods was discussed. 
Educational handout on date marking was provided.

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods (TCS) shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-202.12 Spray bottles of bleach solutions in three classrooms were observed at concentrations above 200ppm. Bleach strips were bleached out and began to turn white. Solutions were discarded and new solutions prepared at proper concentration.

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling. Maintain bleach solutions at 150-200ppm as directed on label instructions, and use test strips to verify proper concentration.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: REPEAT> No quaternary ammonium test strips are available for testing of the ready to use quaternary ammonium sanitizer in the spray bottle. A few strips were left with the facility and this has been added to their order for Wednesday.
citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12  & 2-301.14 Employee in back prep did not wash hands between glove changes. Employee was advised on handwashing and was then observed washing hands without proper technique. Employee shut off the manual faucet prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must be washed any time they may have been contaminated and before putting on gloves/between glove changes. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 & 4-602.11 Dicer in the prep area used for white onions and tomatoes had food debris stuck on the slicing surface. Manager stated it was last used the day prior. Dicer was taken to dish area to go through ware washing process again.  
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses. 

Quesadilla slicer in-use since start of service was observed soiled with food debris. Slicer was taken to dish area to go through ware washing. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. Properly clean and sanitize in-use food contact equipment and utensil between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the counter next to the quesadilla press. Employee noted it was used to wipe down the make line after wetting it with sanitizer at the 3 part sink chemical dispenser. Sani-bucket was emptied since lunch service and not yet replaced. Store manager prepared the sani-bucket (200ppm quat) and placed wiping cloths in the solution to allow for proper storage between uses. 

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

title: Gloves used properly
citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee was observed touching general surfaces of equipment (handle of walkin cooler door and handle of reach-in freezer) and not changing gloves prior to retrieving food from the reach-in freezer. Employee was advised on proper glove use and was later observed changing gloves between tasks
NOTE: General surfaces, such as the handles of equipment, are not considered clean surfaces, and gloves need to be changed after touching such surfaces. Educational handout was provided on proper glove use. 

Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment: Observed an employee handle a cell phone and credit card, and then put on gloves and begin working without washing her hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Food employee entered kitchen and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil and food residue present on several non food contact surfaces throughout the kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) READY-TO EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded.

Milk was observed in a cooler with two dates marked (2/19 & 2/21) both of which are longer than 7 days. Discussed with the PIC and the items were discarded during the inspection.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text:
7-102.11 Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Pf

Two spray bottles under the pizza oven were observed without labels. Discussion revealed that the bottles contained sanitizer and degreaser. The containers were labeled during the inspection to correct.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.14 (C) During preparation, UNPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

The meat slicer in the kitchen was observed with accumulated food debris dried onto the equipment. The issue was discussed with eh PIC and they were instructed to clean the slicer after each use.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
citation_text:
3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be:
(1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

The bucket used for storing wiping cloths used for tables and counters was observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. Effective sanitizing for contact sanitizers is 100 ppm. The bucket was remade during the inspection.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12 (A & B) During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored in the FOOD with their handles above the top of the FOOD and the container or on a cleaned and sanitized surface. 
1) a pair of tongs were observed on the counter by the steam tables in the kitchen. The tongs were moved to washing during the inspection. 2) A spatula was observed with the handle in contact with lettuce in the sandwich prep station. It was removed during the inspection.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
PA 100-0367 All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.
Only one of the CFPMs on record at the facility have completed an ANSI accredited allergen training. All CFPMs at a facility are required to completed an accredited course. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to complete it by the next routine inspection.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
comment: Observed dented can in dry storage area stored with other canned products. Dented cans must be separated away from other consumables. Corrected. Education provided. Can was discarded.
citation_text: 3-202.15  (Pf) Can of pineapple is dented and in poor condition. Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
comment: Observed leaking plumbing of dishwasher. Ensure all plumbing is in good repair. In addition, dishwasher should reach adequate temperature in first cycle (120F). Fix plumbing.
citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The dishwasher plumbing needs repair. Repair dishwasher according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed the handles to most equipment to be visibly soiled. Sanitize handles to equipment as often as necessary to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Allergen training as required

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
citation_text: 5-103.11  (Pf) Inadequate hot water is available to bar fixtures at certain times. title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The floor drain by the condensation line plumbing needs repair. Repair drain according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
citation_text: 6-303.11 (A, B, C) (C) Lighting in the walk-in cooler area was found to be insufficient for that area. Light intensity shall be A) at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and other areas during periods of cleaning; B) At least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in areas where food is provided for consumer self-service or where fresh produce or packaged foods are sold or offered for consumption; inside equipment such as reach-in and under-counter refrigeration units; and in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, and equipment and utensil storage, and in restrooms; C) at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) in areas where employees are working with food or working with utensils or equipment where employee safety is a factor. Reference 6-303.11(A, B, C).

comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law.
