6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the prep area handsink. Owner stated she just used the last paper towel from the roll before she began grinding meat prior to inspector's arrival. A new roll of paper towels was provided to allow for proper handwashing.  

Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11 Cartons of raw shell eggs were observed above ready to eat foods in the reach-in retail cooler and in the walkin cooler. All eggs were moved to allow for proper storage below and separate from ready to eat foods. 

Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114  Bleach solution used for wiping slicer was observed at ~100ppm. The label directions show a required concentration of 150-200ppm. Solution was just prepared recently and not yet used. More bleach was added to bring the solution to proper concentration of 150ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11 (A) (Pf) Equipment, food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch.

Multiple pans were located in a space under the island in the middle of the kitchen and appeared to be soiled with food debris that had fallen from the counter above. Discussed with the PIC and the items were moved to the dish room for cleaning. Discussed adding doors to the cubby.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (P) Except when cooking cooling or reheating, Time/ Temperature Control for Safety Food shall be maintained at 135 F or above or 41 F and below. 

Multiple items in the stand up cooler were observed at 45 F internal temperatures. Items included multiple containers of beef patties, sausage, pork and cheese sauce. Items were discarded during the inspection and maintenance will be contacted to adjust/ repair the cooler.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) (Pf) Ready to Eat, Time/ Temperature for Safety Food prepared and held for more than 24 hours shall clearly be marked to indicate when 7 days will have elapsed and the food needs to be consumed or discarded by.

In the walk in cooler, pasta was marked with 1/5/19 and sour cream was marked with 1/16/19. The foods marked would both have had their 7 days elapsed and should have been consumed or discarded prior to the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the items discarded during the inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee was observed touching the manual faucet with her hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands were properly washed prior to continuing on to the next task. An educational handout showing proper technique was provided, and kitchen manager was advised to discuss handwashing with all staff. 

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11(E)(4) The baffle and ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle were soiled with mold. Cleaning frequency was discussed with kitchen manager.
 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Clean and sanitize all components of the ice machine as needed.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 A package of roast beef deli meat was observed with a date mark of 1/2/19 in the walkin cooler. Manager stated that was the day the product was originally opened and frozen. The deli meat was pulled from the freezer yesterday and would be used today. Proper date marking was discussed. Kitchen manager was advised to make sure the date is being marked accordingly when foods are frozen and then changed when products are removed from the freezer for thawing to accurately represent the time frame by which foods are to be used or discarded.  

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solution prepared using the wall mounted dispenser. Only a chlorine test kit was available, and none of the products used in the food service area have an active chlorine ingredient. Manager ordered test strips during the inspection and noted they would arrive with an order next week. Inspector provided some test strips for use until the new strips just ordered today are available for use.

A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) under flat grill (general buildup);
B) sides of stove, flat grill, and fryer (grease);  and
C) general surfaces of dish machine (buildup).

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

6-501.12 The floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) under flat grill (grease/debris);  and
B) under dish machine (general buildup). 
Clean the floors in the aforementioned area. 

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:

A soiled spatula was observed stored in the hand washing sink between the 2 cook lines. Discussed with eh PIC and the spatula was removed during the inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(E)(4)(B) (C) Equipment shall be cleaned and sanitized often enough so as to preclude the accumulation of soil or mold.  

The inner roof of the ice maker was observed to have multiple locations where pink slime is observed accumulating. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean the item often enough so as to prevent the accumulation of soilage.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135F, or above.

Prime rib was observed in hot holding at 127 F internal temperature. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165F.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11  (C) Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. 

A container of ice cream in the walk in freezer was observed stored without a covering. Discussed with the PIC and the lid was placed on the container during the inspection.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 F.

A knife was observed stored with the food contact surface (blade) wedged in the crack between 2 coolers. There is not a way to clean the crack effectively. Discussed with the PIC and the knife was moved to cleaning.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
citation_text:
2-401.11 Open bottles of personal beverages were observed on the fridge door. Cook removed personal drinks from the fridge. Consumption and storage of personal drinks were discussed. 

Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) the EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-302.11  Carton of raw shell eggs was observed on the top shelf in the kitchen fridge above several ready to eat foods. Eggs were for personal use by a staff member and were removed from the kitchen fridge. A staff fridge is available for storage of personal foods and should be utilized to allow for the proper storage of raw eggs. 

Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  A knife with what appeared to be general buildup on the blade was observed on the magnetic knife strip with clean knives. Knife in question was removed for cleaning. 
Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use for lunch prep.

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 The floor under and next to the milk cooler was soiled with what appeared to be dried liquid, possibly resulting due to overflowing condensation from the lid under the condenser unit. Clean the floor under and around the milk cooler as needed.

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
citation_text: 3-202.15  (Pf) Food packaging on containers of beef and chicken base have mold growing on the outside of the containers. Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. The containers were discarded during the inspection.

title: Food separated and protected
citation_text:
3-304.11 (A) (P) Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that have been cleaned and sanitized per sections 4-6 and 4-7.

The metal line covering for a soda gun was observed in contact with ice used for consumer drinks. The issue was discussed with the PIC and the soda gun was stored correctly to prevent the line covering from contacting the RTE ice.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
citation_text:
3-305.11 (A) (2) (C) Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination.

A container of sauce was observed stored without a lid along the shelves at the eastern side of the kitchen. Inspector discussed the issue with the PIC and the container was discarded during the inspection.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 F.

A steak knife was stored in a water well with the blade between the well and the outer container. In this position running water was not in contact with the blade. Discussed with the PIC and knife was removed during the inspection.

The inner bottom rim of an ice scoop holder was observed to be soiled. Discussed with the PIC and the item was cleaned during the inspection.

citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands by not using a clean barrier to turn off the water. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Sliced ham is observed with an internal temperature or 47F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was moved to the walk in cooler to rapidly cool to less than 41F.

Knives were observed stored in the gap between the cold holding unit wall and containers of food on the cook line. Discussed with the PIC and the knifes were removed during the inspection.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  

The inner roofs of the microwaves in the facility were observed soiled. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-602.11 (E)(4) Ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle was soiled with mold. It appeared to be mostly soiled around the shoot where ice comes out but may also have some accumulation up inside the shoot. Mold accumulation may also be present in the upper compartment where the filter and ice tray are located. Manager was advised to work with custodial staff and/or outside company (whoever would be responsible for detail cleaning) to get all the components of the ice machine properly cleaned and sanitized. (see general comments for additional information)

Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Cheese sauce in the warmer was observed with an internal temperature of 118°F. Staff noted the final cook temperature was 170°F prior to some cold cheese product getting added just before placing product in the warmer. Some of the cold cheese pieces were still in the process of melting and were likely the reason the cheese sauce was below 135°F. Cheese sauce was placed back on the stove to reheat to 165°F prior to mixing with cooked noodles for service. Staff were advised to make sure foods are at proper cook temperature prior to placing in the warmer, especially after cold ingredients are added to cooked product. 

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 Mouse droppings were observed on the floor in the dry storage room used for school food service supplies. The majority of the droppings were in the corner under canned good storage. Clean the floor in the dry storage room (see general comments for additional information)

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of quat solution was 100ppm. Solution was prepared earlier in the week. Solution was discarded. New solution was prepared and observed at proper concentration of 200ppm. 
Check the solution in spray bottles with test strips to verify concentration is maintained during use. Change the solution in spray bottles as needed. 

Maintain quaternary ammonium compound solutions at a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler used to make ranch dressing was not date marked. Milk was opened the day prior and dated with a proper date mark of 1/24. 

Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be used or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41°F/less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Internal temperature of one portion of baked beans was observed at 129°F in the warmer; another portion of beans in the same warmer had an internal temperature of 137°F. Internal temperature for meatloaf sandwiches were observed at 114°F and 122°F. Staff noted foods were finished cooking and portioning began around 930a. Final cook temperature for both beans and meatloaf was 150°F. Staff were advised to monitor the temperature of hot foods once they are done cooking and in the process of being portioned. If necessary, place a portion of the product in the warmer and rotate as needed while portioning hot foods to help maintain foods at 135°F/above for hot holding. Lunch starts at 1120a, and all foods would be served or discarded by 1210p. 

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control hot food that requires time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No certified food protection manager certificate (as per 11/8/18 inspection). Provide proof of CFPM or contact Kevin Dreesman to apply for a variance to be a low risk establishment and serve pizza. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Wall has not been fixed yet. 6-201.11  (C) Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Still need test strips (have chlorine strips but purchased quaternary ammonium sanitizer).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed ham dated 1/15 and sausages and sauce without date marking in the walk in cooler. Ham was discarded, and sausages and sauce were date marked with their reported date of opening/preparation. All ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods must be marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17  Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41?F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Hands clean and properly washed

2-301.14 (E) (P) Employees shall clean their hands immediately before engaging in food preparation or before handling cleaned and sanitized utensils.

An employee was observed to handle soiled dishes and switch to cleaned dishes and back without washing their hands. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to review procedures with employees in relation to when to wash hands.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) TCS foods shall be held at 41 F or less to control for the growth of pathogenic organisms.

House made buffalo ranch sauce was observed to be at 47 F internal temperature (probed) in the bottom of the prep cooler used for pizza preparation. Proper cold holding was discussed with the PIC and the sauce was discarded during the inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: No documentation was provided for clean-up. Corrected. Handout Provided.
citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

comment:
PIC does not have food allergen training. Allergen training is required for all category I facilities.
PA 100-0367: All CFMs working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

4-501.112  (Pf) Hot water sanitizing rinse at dish machine is less than 180F. Repair unit so that hot water rinse is maintained between 180F to 194F. 

Dish machine on arrival was showing a fluctuating rinse temperature on the display. A maximum registering tape was used to check the temperature and would not register (no collar change). Maintenance was contacted and the booster attached to the machine adjusted to requirements during the inspection.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
comment: There are several toxic chemicals such as roach killer stored on the drainboards and shelf above the three compartment sink. Chemicals must be stored in a separate area that will not contaminate dishware.
citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed bags of ice stored on the floor in the walk in freezer. Ice and all foods must be stored at least 6" off of the floor.
citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Replace microwave with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Facility does not have sanitizer or test strips available. Sanitizer and test strips are needed to wash, rinse and sanitize the coffee pots, soda nozzles, clean the counters, etc. Provide sanitizer and test strips. Plain unscneted bleach that has an EPA registration number and instructions for use on food contact surfaces would be sufficient. Prepare according to the label.
citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Reference 4-302.14.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12(A) - Floor in the dish area was soiled with general buildup along the wall juncture an under the booster heater. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
6-305.11(B)-An employee jacket was observed hanging on dry storage shelving. Jacket was placed in proper storage area. An employee was later observed placing her coat on the same set of shelving. Manager discussed proper storage of personal items with staff, and all personal items were placed in the proper storage area. 

Food establishments shall provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
citation_text: 7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of orange cleaner not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
citation_text: 8-201.13  (C) A HACCP plan has not been provided for approval as specified under ? 8-201.14 to validate a food processing method for reduced oxygen packaging that requires a variance. The HACCP plan and variance must be approved before the food is prepared at the food establishment. Reference 8-201.13.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: All Certified Food Protection Managers must complete an approved allergen training program.

title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
citation_text:
4-903.12 Single service articles (bags and labels) were observed in the employee restroom. Proper storage of single service articles was discussed. Staff stated items would removed from the restroom and placed in the back storage area.

Single service articles may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; and 9) under other sources of contamination.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
citation_text:
5-205.15 Leak was observed at the water heater. A small plastic container was being used to catch the leak. Empty the container as needed throughout operations, and keep the area around the water heater clean. Staff were advised to have store manager place a work order for repairs.

Floor drain under the 3 part sink had standing water in it. Staff noted it sometimes has water in it but never overflows. The recessed drain did not have a grated cover over the opening inside. Debris may be causing an issue and clogging the drain. Have a plumber service the drain.

Repair the water heater and the floor drain plumbing according to Illinois and local plumbing code.

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
citation_text:
4-203.12  Hanging thermometer in the walkin cooler was reading approximately 10 degrees colder than the actual temperature. Cooler was observed at 39°F, while the hanging thermometer was reading around 29°F.  Manager was advised to replace the hanging thermometer with one that was reading accurately. 

Ambient air thermometers shall be accurate within +/-3°F in the intended range of use.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text:
4-602.13 The following general surfaces were observed soiled:
A) dairy shelving (general buildup);
B) rolling milk cart - bottom rung (dried milk splash);  and
C) bottom inside drink coolers and freezers (general buildup/splash).

Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
comment:
6-202.14  Men's room door was not shutting properly. When closed it did not seal to be flush with the door frame. Repair the door so it shuts and seals properly. 

All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.
citation_text:
5-501.17 Women's room did not have a covered waste receptacle.

Provide at least one covered trash receptacle in the women's restroom.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 (A) Dust accumulation was observed on the air exchange vent cover in the men's room and on the ceiling in the walkin cooler by the condenser closest to the dairy section. Clean the ceiling and vent cover in the aforementioned areas.

Floors were observed with a general accumulation of debris under stockroom shelves both upstairs and downstairs. Also, general debris and dead insects were observed around the stairs to the upstairs stockroom and the emergency exit by the stairs. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
citation_text:
6-301.12  - Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. 

Paper towels were not dispensing in the restrooms. Issue was immediately resolved. Paper towels were incorrectly stocked in the dispensers when replaced. Paper towel rolls were stocked to allow proper dispensing.
Management was advised to train all staff on proper stocking of paper towel dispensers and to verify towels are dispensing properly upon stocking.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text:
6-501.12 (A) - Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

Floors in the following areas were observed to be soiled:
A) in the mop closet (general buildup around the mop sink);  and
B) under metal stationary shelves in the stock room behind the walkin cooler/freezer (plastic/general debris). 
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment: Owner and PIC is not present during time of inspection. Ensure Proper management staff are present.
citation_text: 2-101.11 (Pf) PIC is not present at the food establishment during all hours of operation. Provide an appropriate number of management staff.  Reference 2-101.11.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment: No CFM is present during time of inspection. All category I facilities must have adequate coverage throughout time of operation.
citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment: No conditional agreement forms have been signed nor knowledge of exlcusion or restriction can be provided. Ensure proper knowledge is provided to employees of facility. Sign conditional agreement form.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment: Observed no vomit/diarrhea procedure present in facility. Handout provided. Corrected.
citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed food prep material and plastic from box inside of handsink. Ensure handsink is always accessible. Handwashing stations must be for handwashing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by food prep material . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

title: Food separated and protected
comment: Observed personal item (designated as meat) to be stored above cut onion. Ensure raw vegetables are stored above personal items as well as raw meats to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) cut onion stored below personal use meat . Store raw vegetables above personal items and raw meats to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment: Observed several foods to be exposed while in cold holding units. Ensure all food is covered when not in use. Cover food.
citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination in cold holding units. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
comment: Observed handle of utensil to be touching dry food product. Ensure handle is extended outward and away from food.
citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly in flour bags . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 ?F. Reference 3-304.12.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Observed sanitation bucket to be without sanitizer. Ensure sanitizer is present during times of operaiton. Corrected. Cl- 200ppm
citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Chemical sanitizers must be present during all times of operation. Reference 4-303.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: Observed grease build-up on hood vent. Observed soil accumulation on bottom of freezer. Clean non-food contact surfaces as needed to prevent accumulation and potential cross contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on hood vent and bottom of reach-in freezer. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: Observed grease and boxes scattered near stove of kitchen area. Ensure floors are kept uncluttered and cleaned.
citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) [Floors, Walls and Ceilings] in the kitchen area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on 2 opened gallon containers of milk. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer?s use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on ceiling vent in kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: All Certified Food Protection Managers must complete an approved allergen training course.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text: 2-201.11 (E) (Pf) No documentation was observable during the inspection for employees being made aware of reportable symptoms and diagnosis related to food borne illness in a food establishment. Reporting agreements were made available to the facility during the inspection and a spot check will take place 1/14/19 to review compliance.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
citation_text: 6-201.17  (C) The caulking in the eastern bathroom around both hand sinks was observed cracking and with a significant gap between the wall and sink. Attachments to walls and ceilings shall be smooth and easily clean able. Instructed PIC to repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment: Observed no paper towels at the kitchen hand sink
citation_text: 6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment: Observed several foods in small cooler in kitchen that exceeded the seven day limit for potential hazardous foods.
citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 12/31/18 marked on coleslaw exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment: Rinse water in dish washing machine tested at 0 ppm chlorine.  Rinse water must have at least 50 ppm chlorine present.
citation_text: 4-204.117  (Pf) Unable to verify if detergents and/or sanitizers are automatically dispensed in the warewashing machine. Provide a visual means to verify or install an audible/visual alarm to signal if the sanitizer or detergent is not being delivered properly. Reference 4-204.117.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text: 2-201.11(A) (P) Facility had not yet completed the reporting agreements for their employees and had not yet started tracking any potential food born illnesses. Procedures were discussed with the PIC and copies of the forms distributed by Sangamon County Public Health were given during the inspection. Most employees filled out the reporting agreement during the inspection. Inspector will follow up on the 11th for compliance with the code.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
citation_text:
2-501.11 (Pf) A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. 

The PIC during the inspection could not find the written policy documenting the procedures in the facility for the clean up of vomit or diarrhea in the facility. Inspector will follow in ten days to verify the procedures used in the facility.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored
citation_text: 3-304.12 (E) (C) During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean protected location. Particulates were observed floating in water in the bottom of the ice scoop holder in the drive through window with the ice scoop stored in the container. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent possible contamination of the in use utensil. The scoop and the container were cleaned during the inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text: 2-201.11(A) (P) Facility had not yet completed the reporting agreements for their employees and had not yet started tracking any potential food born illnesses. Procedures were discussed with the PIC and copies of the forms distributed by Sangamon County Public Health were distributed during the inspection. Most employees filled out the reporting agreement during the inspection. Inspector will follow up on the 10th for compliance with the code.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment: 6-101.11 (A) (C) Floors walls and ceilings shall be designed, constructed and maintained smooth and easily clean able. The Sink in the men's bathroom was observed to have a crack in the caulking running across the top of the sink. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to repair.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Observed food and general debris in the dry storage area as well as general debris in the walk in cooler. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
citation_text: 2-201.11(A) (P) Facility had not yet completed the reporting agreements for their employees and had not yet started tracking any potential food born illnesses. Procedures were discussed with the PIC and copies of the forms distributed by Sangamon County Public Health were distributed during the inspection. Most employees filled out the reporting agreement during the inspection. Inspector will follow up on the 7th for compliance with the code.

title: Allergen training as required
comment: All certified food protection managers must complete allergen training.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.120 - A couple small pieces of debris that appeared to possibly be mold were observed in the ice at the ice machine. Some discoloration and mold was observed on the baffle and the side walls. Ice scoop was used to remove the debris from the ice. Cleaning and sanitizing of the ice machine was discussed. Manager noted the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized a couple times a month. Manager was advised to properly clean and sanitize in the ice machine this evening.

Food shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize all surfaces in the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. The top of the ice machine is not considered a clean surface. Ice scoop was taken to 3 part sink for ware washing. Manager was advised to store the scoop in a clean container. Clean and sanitize the container and ice scoop daily.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee put on gloves without first washing hands. Employee was observed touching his face prior to putting on gloves. Proper handwashing was discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
(R) 750.650a - White baffle in the ice machine was cracked and broken along the lower edge, and mold growth was beginning to accumulate. Replace the damaged baffle.
Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine daily/as needed to eliminate mold growth.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
comment:
(R) 750.820 - Vegetable dicer and slicer were observed with stuck on food debris and were in the clean equipment storage area. Item were placed at 3 part sink to go through ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. If food debris or general soil remains after initial cleaning/sanitizing occurs, then repeat the process as many times as necessary to ensure equipment is properly cleaned and sanitized.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment:
(R) 750.810 - Sani-bucket was not available for wiping down general surfaces. Manager on duty noted they place wiping cloths in the 3 part sink sanitizer to wipe down general surfaces.
Immediately cease the practice of using the sanitizer at the 3 part sink as a solution for general wiping cloths. Use a separate container for sanitizer and store wiping cloths in the solution between uses. If it is easier to use a spray bottle of sanitizer, then use disposable paper towels and discard after individual use. 
Container with sanitizer solution was prepared for use with wiping cloths during the inspection.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Cheese and dressing had internal temperatures of 49°F in the top holding area of the salad cooler. Air temp in the bottom of the cooler was around 45°F. Ice buildup on the condenser could have been causing an issue (see general comments). Salad cooler was just stocked this morning from products cold held in the walkin cooler, and the intention was to maintain foods at proper cold temperature when they were stocked. Manager was advised to use time control for the salad cooler until it could be properly defrosted. Foods would be served through lunch service and then replaced with fresh product.

Noodles, baked potatoes, and soup in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 47°F-50°F. Shell eggs had a surface temperature around 46°F. A huge delivery was received this morning and the cooler had to be stocked (see general comments). The air temp was blowing out below 40F. Kitchen Manager was advised to monitor temperatures to make sure they drop to 41°F/below. If products are questionable after lunch, then use or discard.

Cold foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. .

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - Cook was observed carrying a damp wiping cloth in his hands and wiping hands on the cloth after placing equipment in the dirty dish area. Cook stated the wiping cloth was not intended for his hands but was used to wipe down the counters. Wiping cloth was placed in the sanitizer solution on the cook line and hands were washed.

Member of the wait staff was observed putting on gloves and did not first wash her hands. Employee was advised on handwashing before putting on gloves.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Wiping cloths are not intended for use on hands. Cease the practice of wiping hands on damp or dry wiping cloths.

title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
(R) 750.650a - Push block on slicer was damaged with gashes along one end of the food contact surface. Owner stated a new part was ordered but had not yet arrived. Kitchen Manager stated it had been a few weeks since it was used. Food debris was obseerved on the blade and back side of the slicer. Owner stated the slicer would not be used again until the repalcement part arrives. The slicer was to be removed from the kitchen for the time being. 

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets in the kitchen were at 0ppm quat by the back handsink and ~100ppm quat on the cook line. Solutions were just prepared. More sanitizer was added to the solutions to bring concentrations to 200-400ppm.
Maintain sani-solutions prepared with the product in use at 150-400ppm quat as directed on label directions.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
(R) 750.800b - Mold buildup was observed on the back of the baffle in the ice machine. Owner stated a full cleaning will occur in early January. It is simply too busy right now to empty the ice machine for detail cleaning. In the meantime, the area in question will be wiped down with sanitizer. A barrier of baking sheets wil be used when surface is wiped, and a layer of ice will be removed/discarced once the process is done.

Clean and sanitize in the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold on all surfaces.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water had low pressure at the back kitchen handsink adjacent to the dish area. Kitchen Manager tried adjusting the pressure with the water line shut off, but it did not appear to be changing the pressure. Call a plumber for service.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
citation_text:
750.100 - Brownies and cookies from Jay's Food Mart are available for sale at the facility. Proper labeling is not present on the wrapped items, nor was any other signage present. Proper labeling of baked goods was discussed.

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling. The label information shall include the following: (1) common name of the food, (2) list of ingredients and sub-ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the food, (3) accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) name of the food source for each major food allergen contained in the food unless the food source is already part of the common or usual name of the respective ingredient (Per Section 3-602.11, 2017 FDA Food code).

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
citation_text:
750.120 - Soiled tongs used for jalapeno and banana peppers were observed in an old jalapeno jar. The jar had old crusty jalapeno pieces and dried liquid inside. The jar in question was discarded. The soiled tongs were set aside to be cleaned and sanitized. A spare set of clean tongs were placed in a single service container for storage by the warmer.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize storage containers and tongs at the end of operations daily.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 514 - Based on conditions observed upon arrival of inspector and information provided by the employee on duty, handwashing was not occurring at the designated handsink. Nor was proper handwashing occurring. Soap and paper towels were not present and the basin of the handsink was blocked. The employee noted hands are washed at the 3 part sink. Proper handwashing between tasks at the designated handsink was discussed.

Employee shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Hands are to be washed only at designated handsink.

title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
citation_text:
760.820 - Three part sink basins were soiled with general buildup. Also mold was observed around the signs posted on the back of each sink designating the wash, rinse, and sanitize basins. Per a discussion with the employee working at the time of isnpeciton, it was confirmed the 3 part sink has not been used as intended. The 3 part sink was used for washing but not setup to do proper manual ware washing. Handwashing was also occurring at the 3 part sink based on information provided. Proper setup and use of the 3 part sink was discussed. All compartments were cleaned during the inspection. The drain board remained to be cleaned prior to do dishing this evening.

For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Facility did not have a chlorine test kit for checking concentration of bleach solutions. Provide a chlorine test kit.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
citation_text:
750.820 - Plain bleach was not available for sanitizing. Food contact surfaces have not been going through wash, rinse, and sanitize baed on information provided. Proper manual ware washing was discussed. Bleach was provided during the inspection.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
citation_text:
750.880 - Box of single service forks and a package of napkins were observed on the floor at the front counter. Napkins and forks were placed on the counter.
Food service containers were stored with the food surfaces up at the front counter and in the back storage area. Containers were inverted during the inspection.

Single service items shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
citation_text:
750.1130 - Bucket with dirty mop water from the day prior was observed in the storage area. The mopsink had various products in the basin, and a clear path was not available to reach the mopsink. Employee stated waste water gets dumped outside behind the dumpster at night. Employee was advised on proper waste water disposal and to cease the practice of dumping water outside. Waste water must be disposed of via the mopsink.
Items were cleared from the mop sink area to allow for waste water disposal.

Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
citation_text:
750.1120 - Front handsink was blocked with various items in the basin. All items were removed. Sink was cleaned. Soap and paper towels were also provided.

Handsinks shall be accessible to employees at all times.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
citation_text:
750.1110 & 1120 - Soap and paper towels were not available at the front handsink, and the handsink was observed to be soiled when items were removed from the basin (see #31). Front handsink was cleaned; soap and paper towels were provided.

Restroom handsink did not have a supply of paper towels. Paper towels were provided.

The toilet and restroom handsink were soiled. Also, a covered waste can was not present. Clean the restroom daily/as needed, and maintain it clean. Provide a covered waste can.

A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each handsink.
Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
citation_text:
750.1170 - Front door did not close properly. It was not self closing to be flush with the door frame, and a gap was present along the bottom when it was flush with the door frame. The employee demonstrated how the door had to be lifted and pulled shut in order to be closed all the way. The door in question was replaced recently and was installed incorrectly. A new door was ordered to replace the current door. Proper repairs were discussed.

Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

title: Toxic items properly stored
citation_text:
750.1310 - Chemicals (detergent, degreaser, all purpose cleaned, and Fabuloso) were stored above single service items in the storage area. Chemicals were moved so they were no longer directly over the single service items.

All toxic items must be properly stored to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
comment:
(R) 750.1350 - Although it would appear that most of the clutter originally observed in 2017 was removed from the storage area, there are still items being stored on-site that are not being used and/or are unnecessary for the operation of the facility. Items include, but are not necessarily limited to, the following: a four wheeler, mufflers, car tires/rims, and unused equipment (oven, freezer).

Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.

title: No Certified Manager Present
citation_text:
750.540 - Proof of manager certification was not available at the time of inspection. Upon speaking with the new owner via phone (see general comments) the need for multiple certified food managers per the FDA Food Code requirements was discussed. SCDPH food manager course schedule and contact information for other food courses in the area were provided.

Category II facilities must have certified food managers on staff. Certified food manager need to be on-site at all times of food preparation and service to help ensure proper food handling. Provide an adequate number of certified food managers

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - One of the creamers was observed with date marks indicating product was placed in the dispenser on 11/22 and had a discard date of 11/29. title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - Frozen chicken paws, whole duck, and pork stomach were sitting out on a table in the back retail area. Items were still fairly frozen, and surface temperature of duck was 32°F. Owner stated the products were in the walkin cooler overnight and placed out at ambient temperature around 10a. All products were placed back in the walkin cooler.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.
Cease the practice of sitting frozen foods at ambient temperature. Leave items in cold holding until they are intended to be used and are properly thawed.
