title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
comment: Facility without hot water. Repair or Replace water heater.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.120 - Soda gun, nozzle, and holder were observed with heavy mold accumulation, especially around the gun where the nozzle attaches and in the bottom of the holder. All items were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize the soda gun and holder daily to eliminate buildup of mold.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips were observed to be damaged and not registering concentration properly. Test strips were discarded. Obtain and use a new set of quat test strips for checking the solutions prepared with sanitizer tablets (200ppm).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
(R) 750.800b - Mold buildup was observed inside the ice machine on the front upper part and backside of the baffle. Ceiling also had some mold accumulation around the opening where ice comes out. Owner was advised on cleaning and sanitizing in the ice machine.

Clean and sanitize in the ice machine at least weekly or more often if needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
citation_text:
750.1130 - The drain hose for the soda gun was clogged and not draining properly as a result of mold buildup in the holder (see #7b above). Drain hose was cleaned along with the holder to allow for proper drainage. Maintain the soda gun holder and drain hose clean to allow for proper drainage.

Bucket used for the soda gun drain hose was observed with mold accumulation. Bucket was removed for cleaning and replaced with a new container. Maintain the bucket clean and empty it daily.
 
Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Squeeze pouch of whipped topping in the top holding area of the dessert topping cooler was observed sticking up out of the container. Surface temperature was observed at 47°F-64°F, and internal temperature was 51°F-60°F. Manager stated no shakes were made yet for the current operating day, and the product was probably placed in there the evening prior. Labeling on the pouch says "keep refrigerated". Whipped topping was discarded.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. 
Manager was advised on the option of time control for in-use pouches of whipped topping.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.120 - Mold buildup was observed inside the left ice machine around the opening in the ceiling where ice comes out. Manager immediately cleaned and sanitized the area of concern. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machines as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 

Food thermometer probe was observed with stuck on food debris. Probe was last used for morning temperature checks. Probe was wiped down with sanitizer solution. Sanitizing between uses and proper manual ware washing
up to very 4hrs after continuous use were discussed with manager.

Clean tongs hanging from shelving above the 3 part sink were observed to have water splash on them from general use of the faucet. Mold buildup was on the wall and general surfaces adjacent to where tongs were stored. One pair of tongs had what appeared to be stuck on grease/food debris. Manager cleaned and sanitized all the tongs during the inspection. Clean utensils need to be stored in a different location to avoid being exposed to splash from general use at the 3 part sink.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750.160 - Cook was observed touching general surfaces with gloved hands, including but not limited handles of coolers and buttons on fryers, and continued food handling without changing gloves. Cook was advised on proper glove use and frequent glove changes, especially after touching general surfaces and before handling ready to eat foods.

Gloves are intended for one use and must be changed when soiled, torn, or an interruption in task occurs.
citation_text:
750.512 - Employee was observed with a cell phone out on the back table where single service items (mints, ketchup packets, etc.) were being pre-stocked in paper bags. Employee did not wash hands between touching the cell phone and continuing to handle single service items. Handwashing was discussed with employee, and hands were washed prior to continuing the current task.
NOTE: Cell phones are filthy and hands should always be washed immediately after handling cell phones and prior to doing anything else in the facility. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and single service items.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket solutions on cook line were observed at ~100-150ppm quat. Required concentration for company standards is 200ppm. All sani-bucket solutions were switched out with fresh solution (200ppm).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (mold/food debris);   and
B) bottom inside reach-in cooler (food debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was observed at the front 3 part sink. Water continues to run from the faucet even when both handles are in the off position. Repair the front 3 part sink.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
(R) 750.1200 - Ponding water and debris were observed around the pipes on the left side under the small 3pt sink up front and around the floor drain directly in front of the pipes. Clean the area and make effort to keep it dry.
Make repairs to the floors throughout where needed, and minimize ponding water.

All floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
citation_text:
750.1220 - Walls were observed with mold buildup in the walkin cooler and above the backsplash of the 3 part sink. Clean the walls as daily/needed to eliminate buildup of mold and other debris.

Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
(R) 750.120 - Slimy mold accumulation was again observed in the ice machine around the opening in the ceiling where ice comes out. Condensation droplets were gathered on the mold but not dripping onto the ice. A barrier of sandwich paper was placed on the ice, and the store manager wiped the area in question with a bleach solution during the inspection. Layer of ice was removed once the process was completed. Manager was advised on cleaning and sanitizing (quarterly maintenance provided by outside company). 

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750.510 & 512 - Paper towel dispenser at kitchen handsink was empty. Employee doing dishes stated the store didn't have paper towels. Upon furhter questioning, manager stated paper towels ran out the evening prior at the kitchen handsink; paper towels were available in both restrooms. Hands were being washed in the restroom now and then. Without the presence of paper towels or even napkins at the kitchen handsink, proper handwashing was not happening between glove changes and after handling money since the dispenser ran out the evening prior. Manager sent employee to get paper towels; three rolls of paper towels were obtained from another location for use until the next delivery is received. 

Employee returned from getting paper towels and then began looking at his cell phone while changing out dish water at the 3 part sink. Employee then removed previously soaking dishes from the sanitizer solution without first washing hands. Employee was advised on handwashing and then washed his hands without proper technique. The process took less than 10 seconds, he didn't lather hands, didn't properly dry hands or use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet. Employee was advised to use the proper handwashing technique poster above the handsink for guidance; it has the proper process listed step by step. 
Handwashing was discussed at length with the store manager and maintaining supplies for proper handwashing was stressed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, upon returning to the facility/before doing anything, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Have paper towels dispensed and ready to dry hands prior to beginning handwashing process. Use paper towels to dry hands and then use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet as the final step of handwashing process.
citation_text:
750.530 - An employee was also observed eating a sucker in the kitchen prep/dish area. The employee then proceeded to clean the floor in the dining area and was eating the sucker as he re-entered the kitchen and was standing at the 3 part sink preparing to do dishes. Employee was told he should not be eating candy while working, and the sucker stick was discarded.

Employees shall consume food, including candy, gum, mints, etc., only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection. **Do not eat in the food prep and service areas**

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
citation_text:
760.1060 - Urinal in men's room was out of order. Get the urinal repaired.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
citation_text:
750.1120 - Paper towels were not available at the kitchen handsink upon arrival of inspector (see #12a).
Paper towels were provided.
Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at all handsink to allow for proper handwashing. 

Men's room toilet was soiled inside and on the back behind the seat. Clean the men's room toilet.
All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
REPEAT: Observed no Quat test kits in the facility. Provide Quat test kits.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
Observed ice buildup in the walk in freezer. Clean the floors as needed.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
Observed no time control policy being implemented during the inspection. Make sure to always have time marked on items and use within four hours.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
comment:
Observed chili at 125 F. The chili was discarded because the manager could not tell me what time or how long it has been out of temperature.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment:
Observed food stored underneath plumbing. The food was moved. Make sure to never store food under plumbing.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
comment:
Observed the Freddy's seasoning to have a single service cup stored in the container. This is not a proper practice. All bulk containers should have a scoop with the handle extended out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
Observed ponding water on the floor in the dish area. Make sure to clean floors as needed.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
comment:
Observed a missing light shield in the dry storage. Replace the light shield.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
Obeserved black debris build-up on the nozzles of two of three soda dispensing machines. Soda nozzles must be cleaned as needed to prevent build up and potential cross-contamination. Clean soda nozzles. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
comment:
Observed utensil handle touching sugar in a bin labeled "sugar". Utensils must be placed in appropriate manner to prevent potential cross-contamination. store utensil in appropriate manner. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
Observed black debris in grill surface of panini press. Clean grill atleast once a day to prevent build-up. 
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
Observed utensils to be placed in random order that allowed handle and contact surface to be touching. All utensils must be placed in manner to prevent potential cross-contamination. Reorganize knives in appropriate manner.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
comment:
Observed 10+ drain flies present in facility. No pests can be present in facility. Remove pests harboring in facility. Corrective Action: PIC stated company came and treated drains yesterday. White powder was present around drains. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
1) Observed walk-in cooler to have standing water. 
2) Observed walk-in freezer to have box of cookies open and on floor.
Clean the floors and discard cookies.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
citation_text:
750.140 - Pan of mashed potatoes in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 80°F and 82°F-92°F respectively. Product was on a roll cart and did not have any labeling. Kitchen Manager stated the product was just prepared prior to inspector's arrival and still within the first hour of the cooling process. Mashed potatoes were placed on an ice bath to speed up the cooling process.

Pan of marinara in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 54°F. Kitchen Manager stated marinara is a canned product and was just opened around 2p to prepare for dinner service. Manager was advised to monitor the temperature and make sure marinara reaches 41°F/below by 6p.

TCS foods shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Monitor the time and temperature to ensure cooked foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs & 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4 hours. Foods prepared from ingredients starting at ambient temperature must reach 41°F/below w/in 4hrs.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Vegetable beef soup in the walkin cooler was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 50°F-51°F. Kitchen Manager noted the product was out for ~45 minutes at lunch time while product was removed to be reheated for hot holding. Container was placed on ice to help quickly drop the temperature.

Pan of vegetable soup on a roll cart was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 62°F-63°F. Kitchen Manager chose to discard the product.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service. Be mindful that it doesn't take long for product temperatures to get in the danger zone above 41°F when out at ambient temperature. Promptly place foods back in coolers after retrieving the portion needed.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.130 - Raw fish products were stored below raw beef in the cook line reach-in cooler. BBQ sauce was also observed on the bottom shelf below raw meats. All foods were rearranged and placed in proper storage order with ready to eat foods on the top shelf above all other products and raw fish stored above raw meats.
 
All raw meat shall be properly stored, in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures above all other meats and those with higher required cooking temperatures stored beneath.
All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
(R) 750.650a - Push block on slicer was damaged with gashes along one end of the food contact surface. Replace the push block.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket on cook line was below 200ppm quat. Solution was remade at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Change solutions every 2 to 4hrs or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Maintain solutions at 200-400ppm quat as directed on label instructions.
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - Mold was observed on the white baffle in the ice machine and on the left side wall. Ceiling inside behind the baffle was observed to be relatively free of mold, with the exception of one small section. Cleaning and sanitizing in the ice machine was discussed. 

Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as frequently as needed to minimize the growth of mold.

title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
comment:
Observed wash gauge (which measures temperature) to be broken. Dish machine must be in proper repair. Fix dish machine. 
750-830a Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions. Automatic dispensers and liquid injectors, if any, shall be properly installed and maintained.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
Observed the temperature gauge on the dish machine to measure 103 F after the rinse cycle. Have the machine serviced.
750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
Observed the floor to have some cracked tile in the kitchen. Make sure the tiles are smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
comment:
Observed handwashing station in kitchen as well as bathroom handsink to be unable to reach 100F. Hot and cold running water under pressure shall be provided. Repair sink to provide hot (100F) water. 
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Sanitizing temperature
comment:
Observed dishwasher to be unable to reach 180F. PIC stated company told facility the dishwasher was a chemical sanitizing dishwasher. After investigation and testing, no sanitizer is attached to machine. Heat sanitizing dishwashers must reach a minimum of 180F. 
750-830 All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dishwashing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - Sliced deli turkey had a date of 7/24 in the Spring kitchen, and open cottage cheese in the Summer kitchen had a date mark of 7/23. Both products were discarded during the inspection. 
Make sure products are clearly labeled (received date versus open date) and not held longer than 7 days under refrigeration once opened/prepared. 

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - A spray bottle labeled Multi-Quat sanitizer in the Summer mop closet was at 0ppm. The main chemical bottle connected to the dispenser was empty. A new bottle was connected, and the solution was observed at 200ppm when the bottle was refilled. Also, what appeared to be a used wiping cloth was observed hanging on another spray bottle in the same mop closet. The spray bottle in question was not labeled but confirmed to be sanitizer with the use of a test strip. Wiping cloth was placed in the soiled linen laundry bag.
Maintain quat solutions at proper concentration per the label instructions and do not use wiping cloths with spray bottles. Use disposable paper towels and discard after use when spray bottles of sanitizer are in use. 

The wiping cloth in the Spring kitchen sani-bucket was not submerged in solution. The amount of solution was not adequate to allow for proper storage of the wiping cloth between uses. Make sure the sani-buckets have enough sanitizer to allow for submersion of wiping cloths in solution for proper storage between uses.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
citation_text:
750.1280 - A pair of jeans was observed to be stored on top of clean wiping cloths in the REACH mop closet. Jeans were moved to the lower shelf of the storage cart away from clean linens.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
comment:
(R) 750.1300 - Spray bottles in Spring and Summer mop closets were without proper labels. Both were verified to be sanitizer with the use of test strips. Spring bottle just had SPRING written on it twice and was labeled with the word sanitizer also. Manager emptied the chemical from the Summer wing bottle and discarded the bottle in the trash.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

title: Foods properly cooled
comment: 750-140(b) REPEAT: A number of hot foods served during lunch are observed covered and without proper time indicated on the food container. See notes in General Comments. Cooling is an incredibly important behavior and one that will take time to change. See that proper steps are taken to insure cooling is conducted appropriately.  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 750-800e The oven drip tray is observed nearly full with accumulated food spills. Also, the fry baskets are observed coated with accumulated fry crumbs.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment: 750-1220 REPEAT: Observed the baffles of the hood to be soiled with minimal grease and dust accumulation. Clean the hood system baffles. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:
Observed multiple bulk items to be without label. All bulk items removed from original packaging must have label on container. Label containers with common name of product.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
comment:
Observed eggs and uncut onions below beef in walk-in cooler. Properly store all foods in order of cooking temperature. Onions must be stored above eggs. Eggs must be stored above beef. Rearrange food for proper storing techniques. 
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
Observed bottom of pan to be sitting on broccoli. Ensure food is protected from cross-contamination. Remove pan to prevent food-contact
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment:
Observed water to be leaking from walk-in cooler pipeline. Fix leak to prevent cross-contamination. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
Observed clean utensils to be soiled with debris and placed on unclean surface. Ensure all food equipment is properly cleaned. Clean utensils.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
comment:
Observed soap bottle and sponge sitting in handwashing station. Ensure handwashing stations are accessible at all times. Remove items. 
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment:
Observed no soap available for handwashing stations. Soap must be available at all times. Retrieve necessary supplies. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
Raw Eggs stored on shelf directly above milk in reach in cooler

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

Cases of bottled water stored on the floor at the front of store

750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Fans in walk in cooler soiled with debris

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed

Single service coffee lids stored on floor in back storage room

750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
comment:
REPEAT>Leaky faucet on 3 compartment sink

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment:

750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
comment:
REPEAT>Dumpster on bare ground

75-1140 Garbage and refuse containers shall be in good repair and stored on or above concrete or asphalt.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Cheese slices were observed above the top rim of a pan in the top of the sandwich cooler. Temperatures were observed at 49F-50F. (R) 750.151 - Soup and gravy in the walkin cooler did not have date marks. Salsa portions in the bottom of the sandwich cooler had a date mark of 6/18. All products were prepared within less than 7 days based on information provided. Items were labeled and kept for use.  

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and are held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.120 - Pan holding squeeze bottles of dressings, sauces and utensils in the top of the pizza cooler was soiled with moisture and food debris. Utensils were also observed to be soiled. Utensils and pan were removed for ware washing.

Baffle in the ice machine was soiled with some slimy mold accumulation along the lower edges. Baffle was cleaned during the inspection. 

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize storage containers, utensils, and inside the ice machine

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:
(R) 750.140 - Chili prepared earlier this morning was observed cooling in the 3 door cooler. Product was labeled with the date, but time was not written on the label. Chili had internal temperatures of 127°F. Cook noted the cooling process began around 7a when product was at a final cooking temperature of 178°F and placed in the upright freezer to begin cooling. Temperature was not being monitored over time; however, the product was still within the first two hours of cooling based on information provided. Chili was separated into two stainless steel pans and placed in the freezer uncovered to continue rapid chill. Cook was advised to stir the chili frequently and monitor the temperature to ensure food cools properly. Cook was also advised to label cooling foods with the date and time.

Cooked TCS foods shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. 
Cooling is an active process and needs to be closely monitored to ensure foods are cooling properly. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to verify products are reaching benchmark temperatures in the time frame designated for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs; 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4hrs (total time must not exceed 6hrs).
Educational handouts on cooling were provided.

Freshly portioned hamburger and apple sauce were moved to the 3 door cooler, which was holding below 40°F. Thermometer in the large prep cooler was reading at 50°F. Manager made a call for service and adjusted the thermostat in the cooler to a colder setting. Long term storage of foods will not occur in the large prep cooler until it is able to consistently maintain products at 41°F/below. 
Technician arrived during inspection. Coils were cleaned, and additional service occurred. 

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service

Container for rice scoops was soiled with food debris in the bottom. Operator noted the scoops may not have been cleaned the evening prior. The scoops and container were removed and taken to the 3 part sink for ware washing. 

Green eggroll storage basket was observed on the bottom shelf of a prep table. the basket had stuck on grease and crumbs. Operator noted the baskets get cleaned after every couple uses. Eggroll baskets need to be cleaned and sanitized after every use just like all other food contact surface. Basket was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to next use. 

Operator noted all soiled items would be cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink after sinks are cleaned once raw chicken prep was finished for the day.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Properly clean and sanitize in-use food contact surfaces (e.g. cleavers, knives, cutting boards, tongs, slicer) up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Place soiled utensils and equipment at the 3 part sink for ware washing at the end of operations daily.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Open can of ketchup was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. Operator stated it was probably opened the day prior. Operator was advised that ketchup is acidic and needs to be placed in a proper food grade container once the original #10 can is opened. Ketchup was placed in a proper container during inspection.

Foods shall be properly stored at all times. Place acidic foods in a stainless steel pan or plastic food grade storage container after the original #10 can is opened. Metals and metallic flavor can leach into the food if it is stored in the original container after it is opened.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.512 & 160 - Operators were observed putting on gloves without first washing hands and not washing hands between glove changes. Handwashing and glove use were discussed.

Food handlers must properly wash their hands before putting on gloves and between glove changes.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
citation_text:
750.120 - Stem thermometers and cases were heavily soiled with buildup of food debris and grease. Thermometers and cases were set aside to be cleaned and sanitized. General maintenance of thermometers was discussed, and an educational handout on calibration was provided.

Soiled tongs were observed on the cook line hanging from the handle of the oven door. Tongs were from lunch time service. Tongs were placed in the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Use a bleach solution, designated for the thermometers, to wipe the stem before and after checking temperatures. Wash, rinse, and sanitize thermometer stems up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Maintain the storage cases clean.

title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
citation_text:
750.830 - Old labels were observed on containers of food in the walkin cooler. Make sure labels are removed and allow for proper cleaning and sanitizing of all surfaces. 

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
If labels or food debris remain after going through a ware washing cycle, then repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure removal of all soil and debris, including a pre-soak and scrape process.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment:
(R) 750.830 - Sanitizer at dish machine was observed at 10ppm chlorine. The chemical bottle was changed, and the concentration was observed at 50ppm after ~5 cycles. Routine service was scheduled to occur around 12/22/17, but a call for service was made to Auto-Chlor prior to getting the sanitizer to dispense at proper concentration. Technician is scheduled to come in for service the morning of 12/21/17.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
Use test strips to check the sanitizer concentration daily, and make sure it is maintained at 50-100ppm per the instructions on product label.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - General buildup of debris and/or grease and food debris was observed along crevices of equipment (between upper edges of coolers and prep table) and between ovens. 
Handles of coolers and other equipment were also soiled with buildup.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Make sure storage shelves in the dish area and lower shelves or tables are cleaned as needed to eliminate potential food sources for pests.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
(R) 750.151 - A) An open gallon of milk in the second kitchen fridge did not have a date mark and was less than 1/4 full. Cook stated it was open the Friday prior. Milk in question would not be used for food service; milk was labeled for personal use and kept by an employee.
B) Portions of swiss cheese and American cheese were date marked 11/10. Swiss cheese is exempt from date marking but American cheese is not. American cheese was discarded. Handouts with cheeses exempt from date marking were provided.

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time and temperature control for safety (TCS) held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - Three pans of fish were observed on a cart and the counter in the kitchen upon arrival of the inspector. Surface temperatures were observed at 31°F and 38°F. Cook noted the fish was just removed from the walkin cooler prior to inspector's arrival. Pans of fish were placed back in the walkin cooler until additional kitchen help was able to begin proper thawing under running water prior to sevice. 

TCS foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 - Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Proper handwashing was discussed as was the use of only paper towels for wipe hands. 

Employees shall properly was hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service items.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution was not setup in the kitchen for wiping surfaces. Maintain a bleach solution for wiping general surfaces during prep and food service. Store damp wiping cloths in solution between uses.
Also, use disposable paper towels and discard after use when spray bottles of bleach solution are used for wiping down surfaces.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) metal baffle inside ice machine (mold buildup along lower edge);
B)  soda gun at banquet bar (black buildup in middle opening);   and
C) soda gun holder at the main bar (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use (for in-use items such as the can opener), to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) drip pan of stove (carbon/food debris); 
B) shelf above stove (grease);   and
C) buffet area in banquet room (food debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
NOTE: Food debris serves as a food for rodents. Clean the buffet line after every event.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
citation_text:
750.880 - Storage bin for plastic utensils at the buffet area was soiled with food debris in the bottom. Clean out the storage bin as needed for utensils, and maintain it clean.

Single service items shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
750-1220 - Dead mouse and insects were observed on the glue trap behind the motor next to keg cooler at the banquet room bar. Change the glue trap.

All floors shall be maintained clean. Check on glue traps daily, and change them out as needed.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottle labeled "bleach water solution" at the bar was at a concentration well above 200ppm chlorine. The test strip was bleached out when used to check the solution. Solution was diluted to 200ppm.

Chemicals must be used in accordance with directions on the label and must not be used in a manner that poses a risk of contamination to surfaces and/or potential harm to staff or patrons. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solution is maintained at 100-200ppm in spray bottles.

title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
comment:
750. 1380b - Damp and dry wiping cloths were observed in a storage rack at the bar. Bartender on duty stated they were probably left there from the previous evening. All wiping cloths were placed in the soiled linen storage area.

Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
comment:
(R) 750.120 0 & 250 - Cheese sauce on the steam table was observed at an internal temperature of 122°F. Cheese sauce was reheated prior to being place back on the steam table for service.

Hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above at all times during storage, display and service.
NOTE: Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to check foods when they are being cooked and reheated. Verify reheated foods reach 165°F/above prior to placing on steam table for service.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Croutons and spinach bread on the top back ledge of the salad cooler were uncovered. Lids were placed on the pans during inspection.
Baked potatoes leftover from the evening prior were uncovered on plates in the walkin cooler. Potatoes were left uncovered to cool, which is fine. However, once products are cooled they need to be properly covered. Potatoes were covered.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods during slow periods and after they have properly cooled to protect items from potential contamination.

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
comment:
(R) 750.280 - Portion bowl was observed as a scoop in croutons. Portion bowl was removed. 

To avoid manual contact with ready to eat foods, proper utensils, such as scoops with handles, spoons, etc., shall be used for dispensing foods.
citation_text:
750.290 - Metal ice scoop holders on ice bins were all observed with varying degrees of dust/general buildup. Clean and sanitize the ice scoop holders daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice

title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
citation_text:
750.830 - Knife on magnetic strip had stuck on food debris (appeared to be from sliced lemons). Kitchen Manager placed knife in the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
NOTE: If items are not clean when they come out of the dish machine, then repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure removal of all food debris and soil.

title: Sanitizing concentration
citation_text:
750.820 - A) Sanitizer solution in kitchen was observed at less than 200ppm quat. A wiping cloth was dipped in the solution prior to being used to wipe down the backside of the slicer. The solution was remade to be at 200ppm. The Kitchen Manager stated the slicer would be properly cleaned and sanitized before the next use.

Clean in place equipment must be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses.

B) (R) Sanitizer at bar 3 part sink was observed at ~100ppm quat. Solution was prepared earlier in the day. Old solution was emptied, and a new solution at proper concentration was provided (200ppm).

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).
Submerge items in sanitizer during manual ware washing for at least one minute prior to setting aside to air dry.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket at the bar was observed at ~100ppm quat. A spay bottle labeled "Sani" that contained a light blue solution was at 0ppm quat. New solution was prepared in the sani-bucket at proper concentration(200ppm). Solution from spray bottle was discarded.

Maintain sani-bucket solutions at 200-400ppm quat. Change solutions every 2-4hrs or more frequently is wiping cloths and solutions become heavily soiled. 
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) slicer (food debris on backside) - taken to dish area to go through ware washing; 
B) (R) soda gun nozzle/area where nozzle attaches (mold) - manually cleaned and sanitized at the bar during inspection;  and
C) inside ice machine - white baffle (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate mold.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
(R) 750.1200 - Floor tiles under bar soda machine were damaged and holding moisture and debris. Clean and re-seal the tiles and areas where grout is low. This area could serve as a potential breeding location for pests.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment: 1) (REPEAT) Observed cheesecake bites that need to be held 41F or below. They were 60 F holding. 2) (REPEAT) Observed grilled onions to be out of temperature with no time control. The manager stated that onions were put out around 12. Make sure to time mark onions.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
Observed candy toppings stored underneath the plumbing of handwashing sink. This is not a proper practice.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
Observed lids stored on the floor. Make sure all food and single service items are properly stored at all times.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
comment:
Observed wastewater in the mop bucket in the back of the establishment. Dump mop water as soon as the task is complete.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
1) (REPEAT) A tile is cracked on the floor in front of the dish machine. It was repaired but has broken again. Repair tiles to make the floor smooth and easily cleanable. 2) (REPEAT) Observed the walk in cooler floor to be rusty. It has been deep cleaned since last inspection but should be smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: No Certified Manager Present
comment:
Observed no certified IL FSSMC during the inspection. Provide a certified food manager for next routine inspection.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
(R) 750.151 - Open packages of deli ham and turkey, open gallons of milk, and tartar sauce prepared in-house were observed without proper date marks. Food items were discarded or dated and kept for use based on when products were opened or prepared. 

Refrigerated foods that require time/temperature control for safety that are held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
citation_text:
750.120 - Cook was observed scratching head prior to handling plates that were located on the clean drain board at the dish machine. The cook then proceeded to use a wiping cloth that was sitting out on the ledge of the pizza prep table to wipe the plate. Cook was advised on handwashing prior to handling clean dishes after scratching his head, etc. and to not use wiping cloths (dry or damp) for wiping dishes. All plates were returned to the dirty dish area to go through ware washing process again.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Ice bin in the kitchen and at the bar were open and ice was not being utilized for drinks or other food prep purposes. Ice bins were closed. 

Food shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Keep lids to ice bins closed during slow periods.

title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
comment:
(R) 750.290 - Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. Ice scoop and a plastic bowl that would be used as a storage container for the scoop were cleaned and sanitized prior to being placed back at the ice machine for use.

Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handles extended out of the ice.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - Cooks were observed washing hands without proper technique; manual faucet was shut off without a proper barrier prior to drying hands. Proper handwashing was discussed.

Bartender was observed wiping his hands on a cloth towel hanging from his pocket. Bartender was advised on proper handwashing and that common towels are prohibited. Bartender removed the towel and washed hands at the bar handsink.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Cloth towels and wiping cloths are prohibited and shall not be used to wipe hands for any reason.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Staff could not locate a chlorine test kit for checking concentration of sanitizer at the dish machine and kitchen sani-bucket. Obtain and use a chlorine test kit to verify proper sanitizer concentration at the dish machine  and in the kitchen sani-bucket.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment:
750.830 - Dish machine sanitizer concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Chemical bottle was empty. New bottle was hooked up to the machine. It took several minutes of priming the sanitizer line and multiple runs of the dish machine but the concentration was eventually observed at 50-100ppm. All dishes were to be placed through ware washing process again.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
citation_text:
750.820 - Quat solution at bar 3 part sink was observed at less than 100ppm. Bartender noted it was used a few hours prior at lunch time for ware washing. Solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - A) (R) Sani-bucket at the bar was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution was remade and still observed at 0ppm. Solution was prepared with the wrong chemical. Upon using the sanitizer from the wall mounted dispenser in the kitchen the solution test at 200ppm.

Maintain quat solutions at 200ppm, per the instructions on the label of the chemical used at the wall mounted dispenser. (See General Comments)
NOTE: Allow the solution to run through the line of the wall mounted dispenser for several seconds prior to filling buckets, and make sure chemical is pulling through the line. Use test strips to verify proper concentration is present in solutions.

B) Damp wiping cloth was observed sitting on ledge of pizza prep table. Damp wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage area.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) baffle inside ice machine and wall on left side by the baffle (mold);  and
B) tongs hanging at the oven from lunchtime (food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-use equipment and utensils (e.g. can opener, slicer, etc.), to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) bottom inside warmer (heavy food splash accumulation);   and
B) walkin cooler shelves (mold).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
comment:
(R) 750.860 - Bus tubs with utensils and equipment were soiled with varying degrees of food splash and general debris accumulation in the kitchen. Maintain storage tubs clean to protect items from potential contamination.
  
Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
citation_text:
750.1130 - Pan of greasy, dirty water was observed in the bottom of the warmer, which was observed to have heavy food splash buildup in the bottom. Water and pan were discarded. 

Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage. Do not allow greasy, dirty water to sit around in the facility; it can serve as a potential food/water source for pests.

title: No Certified Manager Present
comment:
(R) 750.540 - None of the employees working at the time of inspection had proof of a current food manager certification. Provide proof of food manager certifications. (See General Comments)

All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  certified food managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of certified food managers.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
(R) 750.510 - Employee in Winter Haven washed hands with proper technique but then proceeded to wipe hands with the paper towel after it was used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper technique was discussed with the employee, reiterating the importance of avoiding re-contamination of hands. If hands need to be dried further after the paper towel is used to shut off the manual faucet, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket in the Winter Haven mop closet had a concentration of less than 100ppm quat. Employee stated the solution was just prepared recently, and the chemical bottle was changed prior to running the solution. Chemical was allowed to run through the line prior to refilling the bucket. The solution was then observed at 200ppm.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
**When chemical bottles are switched out at the dispenser, run the solution for several seconds from the dispenser prior to filling sani-buckets and spray bottles. Also, when checking the concentration of the solution make sure the foam is settled out and the liquid is getting checked. Placing a test strip in the foam can result in a false read that may indicate the solution is at proper concentration when really it is not.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle with no label that contained clear liquid was observed in the mop closet at Winter Haven. Liquid did not register a concentration when checked with a chemical test strip. Manager discarded the bottle. 

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Maintain proper labels on chemical spray bottles.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee returned to kitchen and did not wash hands prior to going to the dish area. Employee was advised on handwashing upon entering the kitchen regardless of what task is about to begin. Employee noted he took cardboard outside and then used the restroom, but he washed his hands prior to leaving the restroom. Employee was advised the doorknob was touched and is not a clean surface (all customers may not wash their hands prior to leaving the restroom). The same employee later came in from outside and began helping prepare a delivery order and did not wash hands prior to handling cups and lids for beverages. 

Two employees were observed washing hands without proper technique and had bare hand contact to shut off the faucet prior to drying hands. Both employees were advised as to proper handwashing technique.
Educational handout on proper handwashing was provided.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Employees must always wash hands after clocking in and before handling anything food related in the prep/service area.

title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
750.650a - White baffle in the ice machine was cracked and broken along the lower edge, and mold growth was beginning to accumulate. Replace the damaged baffle.
Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine daily/as needed to eliminate mold growth.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
citation_text:
750.820 - Vegetable dicer and slicer were observed with stuck on food debris and were in the clean equipment storage area. Item were placed at 3 part sink to go through ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. If food debris or general soil remains after initial cleaning/sanitizing occurs, then repeat the process as many times as necessary to ensure equipment is properly cleaned and sanitized.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment:
(R) 750.810 - Sani-bucket was not available for wiping down general surfaces. Manager on duty noted they place wiping cloths in the 3 part sink sanitizer to wipe down general surfaces. A wet wiping cloth was also observed on the ledge of the prep sink.
Immediately cease the practice of using the sanitizer at the 3 part sink as a solution for general wiping cloths. Use a separate container for sanitizer and store wiping cloths in the solution between uses.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Toxic items properly stored
citation_text:
750.1310 - Chemical bottles were observed hanging next to a clean colander in the storage area. Spray bottles were moved.

Pesticide was also observed stored with general cleaning supplies. Insecticide was moved.

All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Insecticides and general cleaning supplies shall be stored separately from one another. Properly store all chemicals.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
(R) 750.510 - Proper handwashing technique was not used by one employee prior to putting on gloves to handle clean utensils. Employee rinsed hands and did not lather with soap, and the process did not last 20 seconds. 
Another employee was observed shutting off the faucet without a proper barrier; employee used his thumb to shut off the faucet. Proper handwashing was discussed with both employees. Staff were later observed washing hands with proper technique.
***Employees must properly wash their hands every time they wash at the handsink. Properly wash hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
 (Educational handout on proper technique provided)

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
(R) 750.800b - Pink and black mold was observed starting to accumulate inside the ice machine on the lower edge of the removable baffle. The baffle was placed through a ware washing cycle in the dish machine. Once the baffle was removed it was possible to see conditions inside on the ceiling around where the ice comes out. Black mold and some lime buildup were observed on the ceiling in side the machine. Kitchen supervisor cleaned inside the ice machine during the inspection.
***Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine and the removable baffle as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and lime.

title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
citation_text:
750.860 - Utensil storage drawer and those beneath it used for storage of activity supplies were soiled with splash and general buildup. Supervisor stated the drawers will be cleaned this evening. Supervisor was advised to have the person in charge of activities properly clean and sanitize items used for food service prior to placing trays, slicers, etc. back in the storage drawers.
***Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
citation_text:
750.1060 - Water was observed leaking from the lower edge of the garbage grinder. Properly repair the garbage grinder so it does not leak on the floor.
***All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.
Observed raw foods stored above RTE foods in the walk in cooler. ( Raw beef over buckets of noodles.) Discussed with PIC and instructed to store foods correctly in regards to cooking temperatures. (left sheet for reference)

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:
(R) 750.140 - Eggrolls were in the process of being fried and cooling. Eggrolls cooling on trays by the back door were observed with surface temperatures at 120°F-160°F depending on when they were fried. No time was indicated on the trays, but the process just began within the hour prior to inspector's arrival. Eggrolls typically sit out for about an hour prior to being placed in the walkin cooler to finish cooling. Operator was advised on tracking the time and temperature of cooling foods. Eggrolls were moved into the cooler during the inspection.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Properly label cooling foods and monitor the cooling process to ensure foods cool from 135°F to 70°F/below within 2hrs and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.153 - Coke cooler was observed holding products above 41°F this morning. Owners have a time control policy posted on the cooler, but time was not indicated as to when foods were removed from the walkin cooler and placed in the Coke cooler today. Normally foods are placed in the cooler around 1030a. Today foods were placed in the Coke cooler around 930a. A piece of paper with the time stamp of 930a was placed on the cooler. All time/temperature control for safety foods (eggrolls, chicken) must be used or discarded by 130p. Owner was advised to write down the new time when foods are placed in the cooler for each batch of product. 

A tub of fried chicken pieces was also observed on a lower shelf of a prep table across from the fryers. Product had surface temperatures ranging from 37°F-43°F. Chicken in question was just removed from the walkin cooler prior to inspector's arrival. Time stamp of 1030a was placed on the tub of chicken. Fried chicken pieces will be used or discarded by 230p. 

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - Chicken was observed in tubs with standing water at the 3 part sink upon arrival of inspector. Operator noted it was chopped frozen chicken that was in the process of thawing. Surface temperature was 60°F, while internal temperature for chicken was at 44°F. Owner noted the whole process takes less than 2hrs; once chicken is soft it is then coated with sauce prior to being placed in the walkin cooler. The tubs of chicken were placed under cold running water during the inspection prior to being strained, sauced and placed in the walkin cooler for storage

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
