750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
comment:
Observed cooked chicken in the hot wells at 125-130F (probed) at approximately 11:35 AM. The chicken was cooked and placed into the hot holding at 11:00 AM. Ensure that the hot holding wells are maintaining proper temperatures to hold food at 135F or above. All other foods in the steam wells, besides violation 3c, were right at 135-140F. Ensure that the hot holding wells are working appropriately. The chicken had 4 hour time marks placed on it and will be used or discarded by 3:00 PM. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
comment:
Observed meat sauce in the hot well that was at 130F when probed. After speaking with manager, he stated he believed it was not reheated properly since the meat sauce had just been placed into service. Ensure that PHFs are reheated to 165F within 2 hours of starting the reheating process. Manager instructed the cooks to place the meat sauce back on the stove to reheat to a higher temperature.
750-210  Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher through out the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.

title: Foods properly cooled
comment:
Observed 2.5 gallons of shell pasta, 5 gallons of yellow cheese, and 10 gallons of white cheese that were made yesterday. The probed temperatures of the cheeses discarded ranged from 46-50F. The probed temperature of the shell pasta was 83F. Products listed were discarded. Ensure that shallow pans are used during the cooling process, as well as utilizing the ice paddles in the facility. Proper SOPs should be established to ensure the facility is cooling properly at all times. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
Observed single service on the cook line to be stored with the food contact surface side up. Ensure that the single service is stored in a manner that prevents potentials for cross contamination. The single service items were inverted during the inspection. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
1) Observed the dump sink in the drive thru area needing caulked to the countertop. Caulk the sink. 2) Observed the gasket ripped at the walk in cooler. Repair the gasket.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
1) Observed the side of the oven to be heavily soiled with grease accumulation. Degrease the side of the oven. 2) Observed the inside of the microwave to be soiled. Clean the microwave.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
comment:
Observed wastewater sitting in the mop bucket that had not been dumped since this morning. Make sure to dump wastewater after each use to prevent pest control.
750-1130(e) Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the kitchen upon the arrival of inspection. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
comment:
Observed multiple drain flies and house flies within the facility. Use PCO frequently to reduce flies.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
1) (REPEAT) Observed a missing drain cover at the mop sink. Replace drain cover. 2) Observed the floor near the mopsink to be soiled with debris accumulation. Properly keep floors clean to reduce pests.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
1) Observed the nudo board just outside the walk in cooler to be in disrepair. Make the wall smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
comment:
Observed mops stored incorrectly. Mops should be hung to dry or inverted to prevent pests.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - Pastrami in 2 door cooler was dated with a prep date of  6/19 and use by date of 6/25. Pastrami was past the 7 day time frame for use. Product was discarded during the inspection.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food must be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Upon arrival employee was observed handling cell phone prior to approaching the front counter and retrieving gloves. Employee was later observed turning off the faucet without a barrier during handwashing.  Proper handwashing and when to wash hands were discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles.
Educational handouts on handwashing and glove use provided.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Spray bottle of quat sanitizer was available for wiping down tables. Manager on duty stated the bottle was brought to their store by another manager that told them to use it for wiping down tables. Quat test strips are needed to check the concentration of the sanitizer provided in the spray bottle.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
citation_text:
750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed in the back of the facility, with the majority of flies, a dozen plus, noted under the 3 part sink on the wall, plumbing and around the floor drain. Another half dozen flies were observed between the wall by soda storage next to the 2 door cooler, by the computer in back, and around the mopsink. Manager on duty was advised on general cleaning and maintenance to help minimize the presence of flies. If cleaning and maintenance alone do not alleviate the issue, then contact pest control operator for service.
NOTE: Fly strips may be utilized under the 3 part sink and in other places that do not pose a potential risk of cross contamination to food, equipment, and single service articles.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
750.1220 - Floor drain under the 3 part sink had accumulation of mold down inside. Clean down inside the floor drain. Buildup of mold may be serving as a potential food source for flies.

Floors, including drains, must be in good repair and maintained clean
citation_text:
750.1200 - Plastic baseboard was observed to be loose along the floor juncture in a few spots under the 3 part sink. Re-seal along seams that are loose and may allow for an accumulation of debris/moisture, which can then contribute as a food and water source for flies and other pests.

Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
(R) 750.1210 & 1220 - DISH WASHING AREA
1. Caulk along the drain board and wall juncture on the right side of the 3 part sink was observed to be cracked and moldy. Remove moldy, cracked caulk and reseal the juncture.
2. Paint was peeling and mold accumulation was noted under the juncture where caulk has molded and cracked at the drain board and wall juncture. Clean and repaint the wall in this area.
3. Paint was bubbled, cracked, and missing at the corner under the 3 part sink. Repair and repaint the at the corner under the 3 part sink.
4. A piece of loose drywall was observed under the wash basin of the 3 part sink. It appeared to be a removable access panel. . The drywall was crumbling in a few spots, paint was peeling off of it, gaps were present, and transparent tape was observed to be used as a repair material to hold part of it in place. Make proper repairs to the wall access panel under the 3 part sink.
NOTE: Areas with mold and disrepair may contribute to the presence of fruit flies by providing a potential food source and locations for harborage. 

Walls and attached fixtures must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - Whipped topping at coffee counter was not date marked. Once placed in the dispenser, the product is good at ambient temperature for 5 days. Manager noted the product was opened 2 days prior. Benefit of doubt was given; product was dated and kept for use.

All foods that require date marks need to be properly dated and used or discarded w/in the time frame allowed for use. Make sure the whipped topping is dated when opened and placed in the dispenser and used or discarded w/in 5 days. 
Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food (e.g. hotdogs) shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
citation_text:
750.140(a) - Built in digital thermometer in the back of the sandwich cooler was not functioning. Get the built in thermometer repaired and/or provide another properly functioning hanging thermometer in the cooler.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 - Employee went between tasks and did not wash hands. Employee was working at the front register and then stocked cups at the soda fountain. Washing hands between tasks and before handling food, clean equipment, and single service articles was discussed with manager.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Educational handouts on handwashing and glove use were provided.

title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
citation_text:
750.530 - Employee drinks were observed on shelving over the 3 part sink, in the pizza freezer, and in the pizza prep area. All drinks were moved or discarded during inspection.
Proper storage of personal beverages was discussed.

A food employee make drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee's hands, the container, and exposed food; clean equipment; utensils and linens, and unwrapped single service articles. Provide cups with a lid and straw and store them in an area that does not pose a potential risk of cross contamination.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
(R) 750.830g - Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer concentration. Obtain and use a quat test kit
for checking sanitizer concentrations in spray bottles and 3 part sink during ware washing. 

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) oven in prep area - 1. bottom inside (carbon buildup), 2. edge beneath the door (carbon/food debris), & 3. counter under the oven (dust);
B) counter under equipment at food counter (dust/food crumbs);  and
C) inside cabinet under soda machine (splash/moisture).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
citation_text:
750.880 - Boxes of single service items (cups, creamers) were observed on the floor in the storage room, by the pizza freezer, in the hallway by the restrooms, and in the store across from reach-in cooler section. Some items were delivered two days prior. Manager noted she is in the process of re-organizing the storage area. Manager was advised all single service cups, creamers, food and food related items must be stored at least 6 inches off the floor regardless of packaging and current state of re-organization. 

Sleeves of cups were observed in the cabinet beneath the soda machine. The drain was soiled with heavy buildup and condensation was present in the cabinet as well as on the packaging of the cups. Cups were removed from the cabinet.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
citation_text:
750.1170 - West front door was not properly closing flush with the door frame. Gaps were present at the top and bottom on the left side of the door. Manager placed a work order; ticket number was provided during phone conversation (see general comments).

Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Trim along bottom right side of mopsink along the floor to wall juncture was damaged. Debris accumulation was observed in the resulting crevice. Clean the area and provide proper repairs.

Drain under soda machine was soiled with heavy mold accumulation. Clean the drain.

Drain by the back door for walkin cooler condensate line was soiled with buildup in the bottom. Clean all the floor drains throughout as needed to eliminate buildup.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
citation_text:
750.1210 - Ceiling in walkin cooler was soiled with dust around the fans and what appeared to be drink splash near the reach-in cooler doors. Fan covers were also soiled with dust accumulation. Clean the ceiling in the walkin cooler and the fan covers as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Restroom exhaust vent covers were starting to acccumulate dust. Clean the vent covers in the restrooms.

Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
citation_text:
750.1280 - Bottle of Frebreeze spray was observed on the back ledge of the oven in prep area. Air freshener was removed from the prep area.
Employee purse was observed on top of the pizza freezer in an area used for food prep. Purse was moved to a storage locker.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
citation_text:
750.1390 - Wet mop heads were stored on the floor next to the mopsink and in the mopsink basin. The mopsink is right next to the clean dish drain board of the 3 part sink and staff need to be mindful of proper storage to minimize potential for cross contamination as well as potential water sources for drain flies. Store mops in a manner that allows for proper drying of wet mop heads.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
Observed an employee touch a coat with gloved hands and go back to bagging bread. The employee was instructed to switch gloves.
750-530e Employees shall maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness and shall conform to good hygienic practices during all working periods in the food service establishment.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
Observed some food debris in some of the drawers in the bakery area. Clean the non-food contact surfaces as needed.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
comment:
Observed a clean knife stored in between the prep table and the wall. This is not a clean surface. The knife was pulled during the inspection to be washed, rinsed and sanitized.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
Observed the mop sink to be cracked and no drain cover in the mop sink. Replace the cover and seal the mop sink so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
Observed the caulk at the prep sink to be coming apart from the wall. Recaulk the sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
comment:
Observed a coat stored on the food prep table where an employee was bagging bread. Make sure to separate food contact surfaces from personal belongings.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:
Observed a container of dill pickles that contained a yellow substance. The yellow substance was identified to be mustard. Ensure that if the the bulk item is removed from its original container that it is relabeled with the proper label. 
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

title: Foods properly cooled
comment:
Observed the facility to be cooling ground beef on top of a soda syrup rack in a bowl. The initial temperature taken was 118F probed. The owner took the bowl and placed it into two separate containers for cooling, then placed them in the freezer. The beef started the cooling process at 11:45 per the owner. Temperature was rechecked at 13:45 with temperature findings of 78F in one container and 94F in the other. Owner stated he would take the product home as personal food. Ensure that PHFs go through the proper cooling process. They should be cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and 70F to 41F in 4 hours. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
comment:
1) Observed the owner preparing RTE food with bare hand contact. When preparing RTE foods gloves should be utilized to decrease the chances of cross contamination. 
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment:
1) Observed a container of relish being stored in the cooler. This container had a lid, with the non-food contact surface touching the relish, and a rag stored above this lid, then another container stored inside this container. Ensure that all proper measures are taken to prevent the potential for cross-contamination. Do not store rags in between containers or the non-food contact surface on top of food. Rag was moved during the inspection. 2) Weed eater was being stored in an area that was above clean rags intended to be used as sanitizer rags. Ensure that the items to be used for sanitization within the facility are not at risk of being contaminated. Weed eater was moved during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
comment:
Observed multiple occurrences where a dish item skipped a step in the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. These occurrences were identified and brought to the owners attention for proper washing, rinsing, and sanitizing. Ensure that dirty dishes go through all 3 processes to reduce the chance of cross contamination. 
750-820a For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
comment:
Observed the three compartment sink to have a leak from the faucet. Ensure that the faucet is repaired or replaced so that it is in a good working order. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
Observed the ceiling in the rear of the facility to have a hole and mesh exposed. Ensure that the ceiling is repaired so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Toxic items properly stored
comment:
Observed a canister of ant & roach killer being stored alongside the soda syrups and soda syrup rack. There are also other chemicals stored throughout the food prep areas that should be contained to one area that is below and away from food. Chemicals were moved during the inspection. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
comment:
Observed multiple spray bottles labeled "cleaner". These bottles contained multiple different chemicals that varied in colors. One of them was tested to be a quat sanitizer. There were two bottles where the chemicals were unidentifiable. These bottles were discarded during the inspection. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

title: Foods properly cooled
citation_text:
750.140 - Mashed potatoes were observed cooling in a sealed tupperware container on the kitchen counter upon arrival of inspector. Owner was unsure as to the exact time food was removed from the stove for cooling. Time and date were not marked on the container. Surface and internal temperatures were at 92F-94F and 103F respectively. Operator was given the options to reheat the potatoes to 165F and start cooling process again utilizing an ice bath or discard the product. Initially operator noted he would reheat and re-cool the food, but the potatoes were discarded in the trash when inspector advised the reheat and re-cooling process needed to occur immediately.

Cooked potentially hazardous (time/temperature control for safety) foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Time frame for cooling begins once foods reach an internal temperature of 135. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to monitor temperatures. Use an ice bath and/or portion foods in smaller quantities and utilize the chest freezer to help rapidly cool foods. Track the time and temperature during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling. Label cooling foods with date and time of prep.
Educational handout on quick chill methods for cooling foods provided.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Canned goods on lower shelf of prep table in the kitchen were soiled with sticky splash. Operator noted the cans would be wiped down prior to opening for use.
Clean and sanitize the tops of cans prior to opening.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment:
750.820d & 820e2 - Bleach solution in 3rd compartment of 3 part sink did not have an adequate amount of sanitizing solution to submerge dishes for sanitizing. Operator was advised the bleach solution needs to be enough that the dishes being manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized can be submerged completely in solution to soak for 60 seconds prior to setting aide to air dry.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Food contact surfaces of all equipment and utensils shall be sanitized by immersion for at least one minute in a clean solution containing at least 50ppm of available chlorine as a hypochlorite and having a temperature of at least 75 degrees F.
Educational handout on manual ware washing provided.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
700.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) top inside microwave (food splash);  and
B) fry baskets (grease/food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-use items such as knives, cutting boards, inside microwaves, etc., to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed and maintained
citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water at bar handsink lost water pressure a couple times and shut off all the way after a few seconds. The water would trickle and then run a little harder depending on positioning of the hot water handle. After about a minute the hot water had more pressure. Owner was advised the hot and cold water should have consistent pressure at all sinks. Get the sink repaired so it provides consistent water pressure for both hot and cold water.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
citation_text:
750.1220 - Air exchange vent cover in the ceiling above the refrigerator was soiled with heavy dust accumulation. Clean the ceiling vent covers as needed, and maintain them clean.

Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean.

title: No Certified Manager Present
citation_text:
750.540 - (R) One employee stated he has a current IL FSSMC and took the class in 2015. The proof of certification was not present at the facility nor could it be produced. Employee was advised to contact location where course was taken and given the email address for IDPH to inquire about getting a new copy of his IL FSSMC. (see general comments)

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

title: Approved source
citation_text:
750.100 - Upon inspector's arrival the employee working was unsure as to where the taco meat in the hot holding well used for nachos was prepared. Information provided via phone by the manager indicated the product may have been prepared at home and then brought to the facility for service. The taco meat was discarded in the trash. A little later another manager arrived and confirmed the taco meat was prepared at home by his mother.
NOTE: All foods sold at the facility must come from an approved source and be prepared on-site for food service. Foods can not be prepared at home and brought to the facility for service. Typically a pre-cooked/seasoned product from Restaurant Depot would be used. Make sure the pre-cooked, heat and serve taco meat is always available for use and only heated at the facility. Manager noted leftovers are discarded at the end of operations daily.

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - Open can of cheese sauce in the Red Bull cooler at food service area was not dated. Cheese sauce was dated and kept for use.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours must be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
Make sure cans of cheese sauce are dated as soon as they are opened and used or discarded w/in 7 days. For example, cheese sauce opened on 4/16 must be used or discarded by the end of the business day on 4/22. Day 1 of the 7 day time frame for use begins once the original packaging is opened.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
comment:
750.140 - Thermometers were not present in coolers and freezers used for storage of potentially hazardous (time/temperature control for safety) foods. A hanging thermometer was purchased during the inspection. Purchase 3 more and place one thermometer in each of the cold holding units - Red Bull cooler, retail cooler holdiong milk and other foods, retail freezer, and ice cream freezer.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
citation_text:
750.230 - Manager could not locate a stem thermometer during inspection. A thermometer was purchased for use at the facility. Handout on how to calibrate with ice water method and proper cleaning/maintenance were discussed.

A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
citation_text:
750.120 - Tongs for pepper rings and jalapeno slices were observed in cloudy water containing floating debris, some of which appeared to possibly be mold. Water was discarded, and tongs were set aside to be cleaned and sanitized.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Blue gloves with the brand name Med-Express were present for use. The gloves in question did not indicate anywhere on the box that they were intended for use in a food service facility. Purchase and use food grade single use gloves for food service.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Only use food grade equipment for handling and preparing foods.

title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
citation_text:
750.820 - Three part sink was soiled and clearly not being setup for proper manual ware washing process when food service equipment needs to be cleaned. The third compartment had general buildup in the bottom as well as several dirty personal dishes and damaged product cans (energy drink) and a bottle (frappuccino).  Manager noted he usually just uses soap and bleach (not present upon arrival of inspector - see #20a for details) to clean items at the first basin of the sinks. 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Debris accumulation (presumed to be flour/dust) was observed in the pizza oven hood exhaust pipe. Get the hood serviced as needed to minimize debris accumulation in the hood.

B) The grease trap and attached plumbing were soiled with dead roaches and grease. Clean the general surfaces of the grease trap and the attached plumbing.

C) Flour and cob web accumulation were observed on the wall behind the mixers and the outer wall of the walkin freezer. The condensate pump motor was also heavily oiled with flour accumulation. Clean the walls and the condensate pump motor for the walkin freezer as needed to eliminate buildup of flour.

D) Piece of fabricated plastic used for repairs was loose at the corner between the mixers and the walkin freezer. Make proper repairs and re-seal the fabricated plastic to the wall.

E) Mopsink was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the mopsink daily/as needed. Grimy buildup in the mopsink could serve as a food source for roaches.

Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
citation_text:
750.1230 - A) Walkin freezer light bulb turned on and then immediately shut off. It appeared the bulb burnt out during the inspection. 
B) Light was burnt out in the back storage area over the #10 can rack. 

Replace the light bulbs in the aforementioned areas.
Permanently fixed artificial light sources shall be installed to provide, at a distance of 30 inches from the floor at least 10 foot-candles of light in walk-in refrigeration, dry storage areas, and in all other areas.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment: (1) Observed bulk powder stored in a clear bin on the shelving unit by the walk in coolers. Management identified the bulk powder as sugar and a label was provided to correct the violation. All bulk powders shall be labeled with their common name. (2) Observed single service containers of cocktail sauce and gyro sauce that is prepared on-site without date labels.  Management and employees state that sauce was made yesterday. Label was provided to correct the violation. All sauces made on the premises are considered potentially hazardous and shall be refrigerated and date marked. All potentially hazardous date marked food shall be used or discarded within 7 days.750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment: Observed a fly ribbon hung from the ceiling by the prep table in the back by the walk in cooler. Fly ribbons must not be hung in areas of food prep and food storage. When used, fly ribbons should be hung low and away from food prep and storage areas. SCDPH recommends using fly ribbons underneath three compartment sinks to prevent any potential cross contamination. Fly ribbon was removed to correct the violation.750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment: (1) Observed bb sauce without a lid stored on the shelving unit by the walk in cooler. Sauce was provided a lid to correct the violation. (2) Observed flour stored in a bin on the floor in the prep area by the front line. Flour was picked up to correct the violation. Food shall be stored at least six inches from the floor. (3) Observed food stored on the floor underneath the shelving unit in the walk in freezer. Food was picked up and put onto shelving unit to correct the violation. Food shall be stored at least six inches from the floor. (4) Observed cheese slices stored unwrapped in the reach in cooler. Cheese was removed and wrapped to correct the violation. (5) Observed taco shell bowls stored on top of the reach in cooler unprotected. Bowls were covered with food grade plastic wrap to correct the violation. Food shall be protected at all times during storage and display.750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment: REPEAT: Observed no test strips available for chlorine or quat. Provide test strips to ensure that employees can check that sanitizer solutions used are at the appropriate concentration.750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the prep counter by the front line.  Between use wet wiping cloths shall be stored in the sanitizer solution.750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment: Observed the ice deflector shield of the ice machine by the walk in coolers to be soiled with dust and what appeared to be mold. Ice deflector shield was cleaned and sanitized to correct the violation. Ensure that the ice deflector shield is regularly washed, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross contamination.750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
comment: Observed the gyro slicer stored soiled on the shelving unit by the walk in coolers. Gyro slicer was removed and cleaned before being placed on a clean plate next to the gyro meat. Do not store clean equipment surfaces that could potentially contaminate the food contact surface. (2) Observed clean silverware wrapped and ready for service stored in a clear bin with appeared to be soiled with food debris. (3) Observed silverware stored in organizers up front that appear to be soiled with food debris. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.750-860 The food-contact surfaces of fixed equipment shall also be  protected from contamination.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment: (1) Observed the floor underneath the prep table in the back by the walk in cooler to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris. (2) Observed the floor underneath the shelving unit by the walk in freezer to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris. (3) Observed the drain by the water heater and the mop sink to not be draining water from dish washing activities. Clean and maintain floor drain to provide proper draining and avoid creating food and water sources for pests. Clean and maintain floor and floor drains.750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment: (1) Observed the prep sink in the back by the walk in cooler to be separating from the wall. Re-seal/re-caulk sink to wall to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. (2) Observed the wall by the prep table by the walk in cooler to be soiled with food splash. (3) Observed the wall by the walk in cooler to be soiled with what appears to be mold underneath the pipes. Clean and maintain walls and attached equipment/fixtures.750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
comment:
Observed no thermometer in the reach in cooler at the bar storing orange juice. All refrigeration units storing potentially hazardous foods shall have thermometers. Provide a thermometer for this unit.
. . 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment: Observed cups of popcorn and popcorn oil stored uncovered in the side room adjacent to the pop corn machine. Food shall be protected at all times during storage and display. Keep food covered to prevent potential contamination.750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment: Observed no quat test strips at the bar. Chlorine test strips were available at the bar. Quat is used as the sanitizer. Provide test strips for quat to ensure the appropriate concentration of sanitizer is used.750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment: Observed the popcorn machine to be soiled with a heavy accumulation of grease and food debris. Clean and maintain popcorn machine to prevent cross contamination. Food contact surfaces shall be cleaned after each use.750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment: Observed single service cups stored on the floor in the back storage room. Single service items shall be protected at all times during storage. Single service items shall be stored at least six inches from the floor. Cease to store single service items on the floor.750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

title: Plumbing installed and maintained
comment: Observed a leak underneath the third basin of the three compartment sink. Leak is causing the raw, untreated floor underneath the sink to warp. Repair the leak to avoid providing water and harborage for pests. 750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
comment:
(1) Observed no air gap between the drain lines of soda gun and ice bin and the drain underneath the ice bin. (2) Observed no air gap between the drain lines of the soda gun, ice bin, and three compartment sink underneath the three compartment sink.  Provide air gaps at least twice the diameter of the plumbing (minimum one inch) between the drain lines and the drain.
750-290 Ice storage bins shall be drained through an air gap. Provide an air gap.750-1060 There shall be no cross-connection between the safe-water supply and any unsafe or questionable water supply, or any source of pollution through which the safe water supply might become contaminated. Abate in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment: Observed no covered receptacle in the men's restroom or employee restroom. Provide a covered receptacle in all restrooms.750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
comment: Observed 30+ drain flies underneath the three compartment sink. Floor at the bar is raw/unsealed wood. A leak under the third basin of the three compartment sink has warped the board creating harborage for pests. Replace unsealed wood under the three compartment sink to prevent providing harborage for pests. Repair the leak at the three compartment sink to avoid providing a water source for pests. Seal and clean floor underneath the three compartment sink to prevent providing food, water, and harborage for pests.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment: Observed raw, unsealed floors through the length of the bar. Multiple gaps and warped flooring was observed. Replace or repair floor to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Seal flooring and eliminate gaps. Management states that floor is in the process of being replaced.750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
UPON NEXT REMODEL: Replace acoustic ceiling tiles above bar, restrooms, and ice machine. Provide a smooth and easily cleanable ceiling tiles in food preparation, food service, or food storage areas.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
comment: (1) Observed a red bull cooler stored in the back room unused. Cooler appears to be soiled with what appears to be mold and dust. Remove all unnecessary equipment from the facility to prevent providing harborage for pests. (2) Observed brown bowls for popcorn stored underneath the ice bin. Soiled dishware shall be cleaned nightly and stored in a manner that protects the food contact surface. Cease to store soiled dishware underneath the ice bin.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment: Observed the following: 1) Tomatoes on grill-line by the ice machine to be at 56F and not time marked. Cheese in the same area at 67F and not time marked. 2) Observed tomatoes and cheese on grill-line by drive thru that was out, and not time marked, at 54F and 57F, respectively. 3) Observed burgers on top of burger cooler at 55F with no time marking. Manager time marked all items at this time. See remarks for Time as Control policy.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Top layers of sliced tomatoes, roast beef, and cold cut combo were observed with surface temperatures of 46F-57F; 46F-60F; and 47F-52F respectively. Product above 41F was observed to be stacked above the fill line in containers at the cold baine. Surface temperatures for product deeper in containers was observed at 44F/below. Roast beef and sliced tomatoes had internal temperatures of 36F and 40f respectively for product well below the fill line of the container. Top layers of roast beef, sliced tomatoes, and cold cut combo were removed from containers to be inventoried and discarded.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
citation_text:
750.120 - Chunky mold buildup was observed on the ceiling inside the ice machine around the opening where ice dispenses. Store manager removed the cover to the top tray/filter area, and very thick mold accumulation was present throughout the machine. A sticker inside the machine showed the last date of cleaning to be in August of 2015. Manager turned off the machine to begin cleaning and sanitizing.
NOTE: The ice machine needs to be on a routine schedule for cleaning and sanitizing to eliminate buildup of mold.

Food shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Staff were observed working the register and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to return make line for food prep. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Employees began washing hands between tasks as needed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
(Educational handouts on glove use and proper handwashing provided)

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
citation_text:
750.690 - The following were observed to be in disrepair:
A) walkin cooler shelves (chipping paint/rusty);  and
B) wire storage rack above dirty dish drain board (chipping pain/rusty).
Clean and re-seal the abovementioned items.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Facility uses bleach solution for wiping down white bowls and minimizing discoloration. Chlorine test kit was not present for checking bleach solution concentration. Obtain and use chlorine test kit for checking bleach solution.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
citation_text:
720.820 - A) Sanitizer solution at 3 part sink with dishes in it was observed at 100ppm quat. Solution was murky and appeared to have been in use for some time. Quat solution was then dispensed directly in a separate container to check the concentration but was not registering above 100ppm. Manager let the chemical run through the line for several seconds prior to checking the concentration again. The sanitizer was not registering at proper concentration. Solution at 3 part sink was remade by manually mixing sanitizer to get proper concentration (200ppm). A call for service needs to be made for the dispenser. Until the wall mounted chemical dispenser is working properly all staff must be educated on manually mixing sanitizer and use of test strips to ensure proper concentration is maintained.

B) Employee rinsed a knife used for cutting bread at the front handsink, and then placed the knife back on the make line. Other knives were taken to the 3 part sink to go through ware washing and brought back in less time than it would take to properly sanitize utensils. All knives were taken to the dish area and placed through ware washing again. Employee was advised items must be submerged in sanitizer for at least 1 minute prior to removing to air dry.
Educate staff on proper manual ware washing process. (educational handout provided)

 Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
(R) 750.800b - Back of soda machine ice shoot was soiled with mold buildup. Clean and sanitize the ice shoot as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate the buildup of mold and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
(R) 750.800e - Surface of sprayer was soiled with grimy black buildup. Clean the sprayer surface daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.

Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
citation_text:
750.1120 - Restroom door self closers were broken. Repair or replace the self closers on the restroom doors.

All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
(R) 750.1200 & 1220 - A) hole was observed in the floor along the wall below the paper towel dispenser in the women's room. Re-seal the floor where disrepair is present in the women's room.

B) Coving was loose/missing along the floor to wall juncture at the south wall next to the register. Debris accumulation was observed in the area. Clean the aforementioned area and re-seal the floor to wall juncture.

C) The floor between the counter and wall at the drink counter was soiled with black, grimy buildup. Clean the floor in this area.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
(R) 750.1220 - Men's' room handsink was not sealed to the wall. Caulk the juncture between the wall and the sink in the men's room.

Walls and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottle labeled bleach had a yellowish color to it. Manager stated it was a diluted solution of bleach and water used for wiping out white bowls to help minimize discoloration. Solution bleached out the inspector's test strip and was basically straight bleach. Solution was diluted to be at 200ppm chlorine.
Maintain bleach solution at 100-200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.

Chemicals must not be used in a manner that may pose a risk of cross contamination or a potential hazard to persons exposed to the chemicals.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 7 250 - Top layers of cheese and meats in the top holding area of the make tables were above 41F. Surface temperatures for the top layers of products were observed at 47F-57F, while surface temperatures of products deeper in containers were observed at 33F-43F. Internal temperature was checked for turkey on the back line make table and was observed at 39F. Products in question were piled high above the top of containers in the make table. Limiting portions, closing lids on make tables when not in use, and use of time control were all discussed with manager. Tables were stocked between 930-10a. Store manager noted most of the product in question would be used by 11a due to catering orders. 

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 - A) Employee entered service area after going to the back hallway and began to put on gloves without washing hands. Employee was advised that hands need to be washed prior to putting on gloves and was asked if he just came from the restroom. Employee stated he had. Employee washed his hands prior to putting on gloves for sandwich prep.

B) Employee previously assembling sandwiches was observed wearing only one glove and disposing of a paper towel. Employee was then observed preparing to put on a new glove. When asked what she did with the paper towel that was just discarded, the employee stated she wiped her nose. The employee was advised hands needed to be washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Employee washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves to finish sandwich prep.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, between glove changes, after using the restroom, upon entering service area and before beginning food prep, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Handwashing and glove use educational materials were provided.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - (R) Facility did not have quat test strips for checking sanitizing concentration. Obtain and use quat test strips for checking Steramine solutions. Steramine is a quaternary ammonia based sanitizer. 

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
citation_text:
750.820 - Quat sanitizer at 3 part sink was observed at 100-150ppm quat. Solution was just prepared with Steramine tablets ~10 minutes prior to inspector checking the solution according to information provided by staff. Solution was made with 3 tablets. Another tablet was used to bring the concentration to 200ppm. All dishes that were in the process of being sanitized and/or were just placed through ware washing were to be sanitized again.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain Steramine solution at 200-400ppm as directed on label, and use test strips to ensure the sanitizing concentration is correct.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
citation_text:
750.880 - Sleeves of lids were stored under the soda machine counter. One box was on a palette while the other was in direct contact with the floor. Manager was advised to cease storage of single sue articles in the area beneath the soda machine. The product is not 6 inches off the floor, and there is potential for cross contamination if leaks were to occur with the soda machine equipment.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
citation_text:
750.1390 - Wet mop head was stored in the top of the mop bucket. Store wet mops hanging or inverted between uses to allow for proper drying.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:
Observed a container of white powder with no label. Provide a label on all unmistakable powders.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 1). Observed the tray underneath the prep line soiled with food debris. 2). Observed the bottom prep line cooler near the drive-thru area to be soiled with food debris. 3). Observed the cinnamon container top to have food debris. 4). Observed the shelves near the handsink of the right side of the facility to have dust accumulation. 5). Observed the bottom warmer door to have food splash. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.

title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
comment:
Observed the outside dumpster lid to be open. Close the outside dumpster lid to prevent rodents and waste water.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment:
1). REPEAT: Observed the floor in the walk-in cooler to be soiled with food debris. 2). Observed the floor underneath the single service storage shelves to be soiled.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment:
REPEAT: Observed the hand sink near the vacant unit needs recaulking. Recaulk the hand sink near the vacant unit.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
citation_text:
750.230 - Facility had only an infrared thermometer for checking food temperatures. GM and staff were advised on the use of a metal stem thermometer for checking food temperatures. Purchase and use stem thermometers.

A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - Tube of half and half was cut straight across. Product was puddling in the tube. Cut creamer dispensing tubes at an angle to allow product to drain from the tube and not puddle at ambient temperature between uses.

Food shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee was observed preparing to put on gloves to package cookies without first washing hands. Employee stated she washed her hands out front prior to making tea. In the meantime. other surfaces were touched, and hands needed to be washed. Staff were advised on washing hands before putting on gloves and between glove changes. The employee washed her hands prior to putting on a fresh pair of gloves to continue with food handling.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment:
750.-810 - Sani-bukcet contained a solution of Dawn dish soap and bleach based on information provided. Solution was at 0ppm chlorine. Solution was emptied from the bucket, and the bucket was cleaned. A new solution of bleach water was prepared at proper concentration (200ppm).

Moist cloths used for wiping general surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Maintain bleach solutions in the sani-bucket at 100-200ppm. Do not mix bleach water with any other chemicals, including dish soap. Use luke warm water to make the solution, and use test strips to verify the solution is at proper concentration. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solution and/or wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) F'real milkshake wand (food splash);   and
B) pizza oven (food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use (i.e. tongs; milkshake wand; etc.), to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
(R) 750.880 - Coffee filters were observed sitting out on top of the coffee bean grinder in the food service area with food contact surfaces exposed.  Store filters in the original package covered and/or in a clean covered container.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Store items in sealed, food grade bags or containers and/or inverted with food contact surfaces face down on top of clean surfaces.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
citation_text:
750.1120 - Back handsink was blocked with boxes upon arrival of inspector. Boxes were removed from the top edge of the sink.

Handsinks are to be accessible at all times to allow for proper handwashing. Do not black the handsink for any reason. Do not store items in the basin or on the edge of the handsink.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment:
(R) 750.1120 - A) Paper towels were not available at the back handsink. Paper towels were provided during the inspection. 
Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing at all times.

B) Back handsink was soiled with buildup/splash in the basin, around the faucet, and along surfaces on top of the sink. 
Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
citation_text:
750.1200. & 1220 - A)  Floor in the back room along the floor to wall juncture was soiled with general debris and buildup, especially under the fountain drink machines and in the corner to the left of the machine. Evidence of old rodent activity was also noted behind the marquee letter cubby.
Maintenance worker began cleaning in the area during the inspection. This same area was observed to have noticeable damage on the lower wall (see #37 below).

B) Plastic baseboard was loose along the wall and in the corner to the left of the fountain soda machines in the back room. Provide proper repairs after thoroughly cleaning in the area (see general comments).

Floors shall be kept clean, and junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
citation_text:
750.12210 - A) (R) Walls on both sides of mopsink were damaged. Left side had crumbling drywall that was starting to fall apart. Right side had a hole in it.
