750.100 - Styrofoam cups with portions of ice were observed in top of food freezer. Operator portioned ice from bags sold at the facility. Operator was advised the store does not have the facilities to allow for such a practice (no handsink; no 3 part sink). Ice must only be sold in original bags and not portioned for individual sale. Operator stated he understood. All cups of ice were removed from the freezer and discarded during inspection.

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
citation_text:
750.140(a) - (R) Ice cream freezer did not have a thermometer inside. Provide thermometers for all coolers and freezers used for storage of potentially  hazardous foods.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.130 - Carton of raw eggs was observed sitting on top of deli meats on a shelf in the 3 door cooler. All other eggs were observed in the bottom of the cooler, but there was not enough space to place the carton observed with the deli meats in the bottom of the cooler. Carton of eggs was moved to a cooler located by the drive thru window in the manager's office (cooler at 38F),

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
citation_text:
750.690 - A) (R) Ice cream freezer had heavy frost/ice accumulation inside. Defrost the ice cream freezer.

B) Styrofoam was observed in the bottom of the food freezer. Remove the Styrofoam from the freezer.

C) Old bubble wrap was observed around the handles of food freezer. Bubble wrap was removed during the inspection.

D) Cardboard was observed in 3 door cooler as a divider and/or shelf liner. Remove cardboard and provide another cleanable material to act as a divider and/or lining for shelves.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) bottom inside all coolers (dust/debris);
B) tracks of all sliding door cooler (debris/dust/dead bugs);   and
C) around seal and doors of ice cream freezer (debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
citation_text:
750.1110 & 1120 - A) All surfaces in the restroom were soiled with splash and general buildup of soil.  Clean everything and all surfaces in the restroom. 

Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

B) Paper towels were not available in the restroom. Provide paper towels in the restroom.

A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
citation_text:
750.1130 - Lid to dumpster was open upon arrival of inspector. Close the lids of the dumpster when it is not in use.

Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers and must be kept closed when not in use.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled under/around coolers and freezers and in the restroom. Clean the floors.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
750.120 - Chicken breasts in the bottom of the upright cooler had an internal temperature of 46F. Cook noted he was in the cooler long enough to pull out pans of food to reheat; otherwise, foods were not removed from the cooler or prepared recently. Chicken breasts were discarded in the trash. (see general comments for details concerning cooler next to grill).

Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage
citation_text:
750.151 - A) Deli ham and turkey in plastic food bags were not dated. Staff on duty were unsure as to when products were thawed and opened for use. Turkey and ham were discarded in the trash.
B) Leftover flour used for breading the previous day was observed with pieces of dried meat in it. Container was also not labeled with date. Flour breading was discarded in the trash. Sifting flour/breading up to every 4hrs during use and proper labeling for leftover portions were discussed.  

Refrigerated, PHF held at the establishment more than 24 hours must be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Dry breadings kept for multiple day use must also be dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Sift breading/flour up to every 4hrs during service.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
750.830g - Bar Manager could not locate chemical test kit during the inspection. Obtain and use a quat chemical test kit for checking concentrations of sanitizing solutions.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) hood baffles (grease/dust buildup)
B) seal around bar ice bin (mold); 
C) metal baffle inside ice machine (mold); 
D) plastic container used for storage of deli meats  (food debris) - container was set aside to be cleaned during the inspection;  and
E) shelving directly above 3 part sink (heavy buildup).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/s needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) fryers - sides and general surfaces (grease/food debris);   and
B) (R) tall freezer next to fryers (grease/buildup on side by fryer, around door seal/hinges, etc.); 
C) general surfaces of flat grill;   and
D) metal cart used for condiment storage by wait station counter (dust/debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
citation_text:
750.860 - A) (R)  Hard plastic liners and surfaces underneath on top of beer coolers were sticky and soiled with buildup of general debris. Clean glasses are stored inverted on the aforementioned surfaces. Maintain the plastic liners and surfaces underneath on coolers clean to protect cleaned/sanitized glasses and other items from potential contamination.

B) Fly strip was observed hanging near cleaned/sanitized dishes in the kitchen. Staff were advised to move the fly strip to an area away from food, clean equipment, and single service articles.

Cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
citation_text:
750.1050 - Waste water was observed backing up out of the floor drain in front of the kitchen 3 part sink when an large amount of water was drained from the sink at one time. Staff immediately mopped up the waste water. Manager noted she thought somebody was in recently trying to figure out why the strong sulfur smell is still present in the kitchen area. Waste water should never back up out of floor drains. It s possible the grease trap needs to be serviced again in addition to possibly having a plumber clear out the lines that lead to the sewer. Get the grease trap serviced and have a professional plumber clean out drain lines.
 
All water containing sewage shall be disposed of properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
citation_text:
750.1120 - Bar handsink was soiled with grimy buildup. 

Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) (R) kitchen under equipment (food/grease/debris);
B) (R) under ice machine (bottle caps);   and
C) (R) behind wait station cabinets under the order window (debris);  and
D) along walls/around beer coolers at bar (bottle caps/coasters).

Clean floors as needed, and maintain floors clean.

title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
citation_text:
750.1280 - Employee's hat was observed sitting on top of paper towels and microwave popcorn packages in the kitchen. Hat was removed from the areas.


An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

title: No Certified Manager Present
citation_text:
750.540 - None of the employees working at the time of inspection had proof of a current FSSMC. One of the cook's stated he had a food sanitation license, but he did not have a copy on him. The kitchen manager was off duty at the time of inspection. Food sanitation course information was provided for Bar Manager to look into getting more staff through a manager certification course. 

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

title: Wholesome, sound condition
comment:
750-100 REPEAT: Cut jack fruit is observed on display on the front counter. Fruit appears dull and dry. Discarded and temped at ambient temperature (80F). In addition to the unrefrigerated nature of the food, the facility does not have the necessary plumbing to properly handle the cutting of produce and other foods. Cease cutting produce until a proper three compartment sink and food preparation area can be installed. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

750-100 A number of the glass jars of kim chee are observed with opened lids. Product had spilled from the bottles and was spilling onto a baking sheet beneath the foods. Also, a number of plastic wrapped silken tofu is observed with an expiration date of July 24, 2016. These packages were also observed bulging. Finally, a container of lily bulbs was discarded due to being under pressure and bloated.  Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment: 750-250  REPEAT: The two large open air display coolers in the frozen foods room are observed holding foods at temperatures from 41F up to 71F. A number of foods were discarded (see the Order of Destruction). Foods were all stocked on the previous day. A small amount of foods were observed to indicate 'Refrigerate After Opening' on the label. These foods were allowed to stay in the cooler. Another small portion of foods on the top shelf and the lowest shelf were probed and found to be at 41F or under. These items were also allowed to be kept. There is a thick frost accumulation on the lower shelf of the tofu display cooler. The air is obviously not moving through the unit properly. DO NOT PLACE ANY FOOD INTO THIS DISPLAY COOLER UNTIL IT IS SERVICED. The second display cooler primarily houses whole, intact produce. Continue using this cooler for whole produce only. Cease storing cut melons and foods requiring refrigeration in this cooler. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
comment: 750-260 Observed the large display cooler to be holding temperatures from 41F to 71F. See violation 3a and the Order of Destruction. Cease storing food in this cooler until the unit can be serviced. Enough hot or cold storage units used for displaying potentially hazardous foods shall be provided to maintain proper product temperature requirements.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment: 750-120(a) Observed various uncovered pieces of frozen meats in the reach-in freezer. Make sure that packages are wrapped securely so the contents do not fall out.  Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment: 750-690 Observed the new wooden shelving to be constructed of unfinished wood. Seal the wood. Also, observed the reach-in freezers to be coated with a thick accumulation of frost. Defrost the reach-in freezers.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
comment: 750-820a The facility does not have a proper three compartment sink. Should Little World Mart continue to cut produce and repackage they will need a specific area designated for the washing, rinsing, and sanitizing of utensils. A three compartment sink should be provided for this purpose. For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used..

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment: 750-830g A test kit of chlorine test strips should be available for testing created buckets and sinks of bleach water. Provide bleach test strips. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment: 750-800c The facility does not have a three compartment sink available for wash, rinse and santizing. Utensils used for the cutting of produce and meats are not being sanitized. Provide a three compartment sink or cease cutting produce and repackaging meats.  Utensils should be sanitized in 50ppm Cl for at least 60 seconds. Where equipment and utensils are used for the preparation of  potentially hazardous foods on a continuous or production-line basis, utensils and the food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized at intervals throughout the day on a schedule subject to the approval of the regulatory authority.  This schedule shall be based on food temperature, type of food, and amount of food particle accumulation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment: 750-800e The gap of the plastic edging pieces of the display coolers is observed soiled with accumulated food crumbs. Clean the display cooler shelves. Also, the reach-in freezers are observed soiled with various pieces of meat, fish, and crustacean parts. Clean the reach-in freezers. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
comment: 750-1120(a) Observed the facility to not have a handsink in the food preparation area. Provide a handsink in your food preparation location.  Lavatories shall be at least the number required by law, shall be installed according to law and shall be located to permit convenient use by all employees in food preparation areas and utensil washing areas.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment: 750-1220 Flooring under all food preparation surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Place tile on the floor where food preparation is to occur. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment: 750-1210 the ceiling is constructed of acoustic tiles. Provide a smooth and cleanable surface over the area where food preparation is to occur.  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: No Certified Manager Present
comment: 750-540 Observed the facility to be operating as a Medium Risk Establishment. The facility may choose to upgrade to this classification and will then require a certified food manager. Or, the facility may choose to cease cutting produce and repackaging meat. If they cease these activities then they may stay a Retail Class C (which won't require the three compartment sink, handsink, or certified food manager. All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
comment: 750-160 Observed an unopened stack of coffee cup lids stored directly beneath the frontline handsink plumbing lines and adjacent to the mouse bait. Lids were discarded during the inspection. Discussed the proper storage of lids and other facility materials under plumbing lines. Make sure that the storage of utensils and equipment remains away from directly beneath plumbing.  Food and equipment shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment: 750-820d Observed the sani-bucket being used to wipe the probe thermometer between uses to test at 100ppm Quat. It was discovered that the wall-mounted dispensing bucket was empty of chemical product. Product bucket was replaced with a fresh and full bucket. A new sanitizing solution was created within the sani-bucket. This solution tested at 200ppm Quat. Educate staff on proper testing of solution concentration before use. Make sure that staff is aware of how the system works and to glance at the volume remaining in chemical bucket prior to use.  Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in accordance to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment: 750-810b Observed the cloth being used to wipe the probe thermometer between uses to be stored on the counter. Store cloth within sani-solution between uses to insure that cloth is being sanitized. Cloth was placed in solution during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
comment: 750-1160 Observed mouse droppings in the cabinet beneath the drive thru soda dispenser (older droppings.green from bait) and within the opened closet by the back door. This closet has become a catch for maintenance and various other sundry items. This closet is also stocked with bottle beverages so that seeing the floor is difficult. Shelving has been ordered and will be arriving within the week. Shelving will help keep the bottle off the floor. Clean the floor within this closet. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
comment: 750-1200 REPEAT: The coving to the right of the hot holding unit is observed peeling from the wall. Properly seal the base cove to the wall to eliminate areas for crumbs to accumulate and possibly become a food source for pests.   The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
comment: 750-1210 Observed a hole in the wall to the right of the island preparation cooler/hot holding side. The hole looks like it was created in order to run cable. Seal up the wall as much as possible and allow minimal space for wiring. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

title: Approved source
comment:
750-100 Observed the facility giving away homemade cookies. Cease this activity. Whether you are selling or generously giving the cookies away is not a factor. You may not have homemade cookies on the premises to give to the public. Save homemade cookies for personal enjoyment. 
Also, observed the facility operating as a Medium Risk facility. This was addressed during the last routine inspection. The facility is going to be upgraded to a Medium Risk establishment. The facility is hot holding and dipping cheese sauce for nachos. With the upgrade comes the need for a pre-opening inspection and a plumbing inspection. 
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

title: Wholesome, sound condition
comment: 750-100 Two pound containers of ground beef were observed stored in the three door glass cooler. Packages were observed damaged with finger holes. The meat was observed white and sunk into a container filled with blood. The meat packages were also dated to sell by June 6, 2016. Items were discarded during the inspection. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment: 750-130(b) Observed boxes of chips and candy being stored on the floor in the side room. Store foods at least 6" off the floor to allow for proper cleaning. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment: 750-690 Observed the two reach-in freezers to be coated with frost accumulation. Defrost and clean the freezers. Also, observed the handles on the three door cooler to be broken. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment: 750-830g REPEAT: Provide test strips for the bleach you will be purchasing to use as a sanitizing agent. Wet wiping cloths should be stored in the sanitizing solution between uses. Sanitizing bucket concentation should be 100ppm Cl. Bleach should also be used for sanitizing equipment that touches food. Your cheese sauce ladle and containers should be washed, rinsed, sanitized and dipped in a 50ppm Cl solution for 60 seconds.  A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment:
750-820d REPEAT: Facility does not have proper bleach or quatarnary ammonia on-hand for sanitizing. Provide bleach and educate staff on how to sanitize. 

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
750-880 Observed single-service containers stored on the floor in the extra storage room. Store containers up 6" off the floor. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
750-880 Observed take home containers stored food side up within the handsink. Move sindle-service items away from water source and invert the containers so the food contact side is protected from splash and possible cross contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
comment: 750-1080 Observed the hose at the triple sink to be hanging within the sink basin. Secure the hose sprayer so it doesn't hang into the basin.A hose shall not be attached to a faucet unless a backflow prevention device is installed and hangs above the fill line. Install backflow prevention device.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
comment: 750-1120(b) Observed the handsink to be obstructed by single-service takehome containers. Moved during the inspection. Cease storing items within the handsink. Keep the handsink free so hands are always able to be readily washed.  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
comment: 750-1120e Bathroom handsink is observed soiled and without a supply of paper toweling. Supply paper towels to this handsink and wash the sink. A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
comment: 750-1170 There is observed a gap beneath the front door. Seal the gap. Protect the frontdoor so that no daylight is visible around the frame.  Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
comment: 750-1300 Observed an unlabeled spray bottle of cleaning solution. Labeled during the inspection. Label all chemical bottles with contents. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

title: No Certified Manager Present
comment: 750-540 The facility is being upgraded to a Medium Risk establishment. Facility does not have a current FSSMC available. Provide a copy of certificate. Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment:

Provide label on all unmistakable powders. 3). Observed no label sriracha bottles and being reused. Provide proper labels. 
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

Observed no date marking on the items of food in the coke reach-in cooler near the chest freezer. Provide a date mark on all items of food in the coke cooler near the chest freezer.3). Store the strawberry daquiri mix in the refrigerator.

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed

citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
comment:

title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)

title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

Observed the sides of the grills in the habachi area to be soiled withh food accumulation. Clean all non food contact surfaces. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
citation_text:
750.140 - (R) Documentation of time and date was not present for any of the potentially hazardous foods that were cooked today and were in some stage of the cooling process. Foods included, but were not necessarily limited to, cooked rice, pasta (in walkin cooler and bagged portions in cook line cooler), cooked vegetables and sauces. Management and staff must work on a system for not only documenting the time and date of cooling foods but also tracking the temperature to ensure proper cooling for all cooked potentially hazardous foods. Rice, noodles, and other cooling foods should not be portioned and placed in coolers on the cook line until they have reach at least 41F/below.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. Provide proper labels for cooked/cooling foods.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.250 A) See notes in General Comments. Observed cheese shreds being stored on an improper ice bath. Ice was present, but without water in the bath, the product container only rests on the ice and cools the bottom of the container. Cheese shreds were probed and found to be 49F. Ice was added during the inspection. Cheese shreds are normally changed every shift which is four to five hours.

B) 1. Minced garlic and whipping cream were observed out in the back prep area. Surface temperature of garlic was 74F. Whipping cream had surface and internal temperatures of 68F and 54F respectively. Manager was unsure as out how long products were out in the prep area. Both items were discarded in the trash.
2. Tray of parsnips out on the cook line had a surface temperature of 73F. Manager noted the product was pulled from the walkin cooler for portioning, but the person working on portioning had to leave. Manager was unsure as to how long product was out of cold holding. Parsnips were discarded in the trash.
Do not leave potentially hazardous foods out longer than needed for use. If process is interrupted, then place the foods back in coolers to avoid temperature abuse.

All PHF shall be kept at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
citation_text:
750.250 - The right portion of the steam table (left side of the cookline) was not holding hot foods at 135F/above. Internal temperatures for sauces were observed at 126F. Sauces in question were removed from steam table to be discarded. Two butter sauces in pans stacked inside another pan on the left side of the same unit had an internal temperature of 130F. Manager stated the butter based sauces have to be maintained at 130F otherwise they break apart. Manager was advised to use time control for the sauces that will not be held at 135F/above due to quality purposes. Label product with time and use or discard w/in 4hrs.
NOTE: Rice and mashed potatoes on the left side of the hot holding unit were at 173F and 171F. Make sure both sides of the steam table are at proper setting to maintain foods at 135F/above. 

All PHF shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service.

title: Foods properly cooled
citation_text:
750.140(b) - A) Container of Bolognese in ice bath had internal temperature ranging from 68F to +100F. Manager went to check the temperature chart and observed that times and temperatures were not being tracked for any of the products today. Based on information provided Manager thought it was cooling for ~3 hours. Bolognese was placed back on the stove and reheated above 165F prior to being hot held for service. Bolognese was to be held hot until the close of business today, and leftovers will be discarded.
Maintain ice baths to allow for proper/rapid cooling. Use several smaller containers to allow for rapid cooling, and then combine into a larger storage container once foods are properly cooled.

B) Trays of cooked and baked onions and baked tomatoes were observed on a rack next to the stove in the back prep area. Temperatures were at 91F (cooked onions), 71F (baked onions), & 73F (baked tomatoes). Manager was advised cooked vegetables, pasta and all other foods must be cooling in ice baths or in the walkin cooler/freezer. Foods should not be allowed to sit at room temperature for cooling purposes. Trays of foods were placed in the walkin cooler, and temperatures began to rapidly drop.

Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Monitor time and temperature of cooling foods to ensure benchmark temperatures are reached w/in designated time frames. The only way to know foods are cooling properly is to take temperatures and monitor the products during cooling process.
(Educational handout provided)

title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
comment:
750-280 - A) Observed the handle of the tongs used at the tasting bar to be resting in the baskets of crackers. Discussed proper handling of crackers so that customers are not grabbing the crackers and tongs at the same time. Make sure that the handle of the tongs remains out of direct contact with the food. 

B) Cook was observed preparing blackened salmon appetizer and had a glove on only one hand. Salmon was already on the plate and finishing touches were occurring. Pieces of salmon were being repositioned with hands. Employee was advised to avoid touching salmon with un-gloved hand. A better practice is to have gloves on both hands when working with ready to eat foods.

Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750-510a Observed an employee washing hands and using clean hands to turn off the faucet. Use a barrier when turning off the faucet to avoid contaminating clean hands.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

750-510d Observed an employee using a common towel to dry hands after handwashing. Cease using a common towel to dry hands. Use a proper paper towel.
To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Sanitizing concentration
comment:
750-830 The dish machine at the bar was not properly sanitizing. Super Trump detergent was connected to both the detergent lines and the sanitizing lines. The Super Trump was removed from sanitizing line and proper sanitizing solution was added. The machine had to be primed for over five minutes in order for chemical to be properly drawn through the line. 

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket at south end of cook line tested at ~100ppm quat.

Maintain quat solutions at proper concentration (150-400ppm). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b - Ice machine was soiled around opening in ceiling where ice comes out (black mold), on the metal baffle (pink mold around rectangle openings); and in the groove behind the hinge of lower lid (buildup/mold).

Clean and sanitize the ice machine as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

title: No Certified Manager Present
citation_text:
750.540 - None of the employees on-site at the time of inspection had proof of IL Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification (FSSMC). One person recently promoted to management had proof of ServSafe. Manager with proof of FSSMC arrived during inspection to correct the violation. Management noted some staff are in the process of receiving FSSMCs, and some are in the process of preparing to take the manager certification course.

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Managers.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
750.120, 250 & 151 - A) 1. Squeeze bottles of dressing in metal containers on an ice bath at the lunch buffet had surface temperatures above 50F for portions not in contact with ice. The bottom of the containers had surface temperatures of 41f/below. The internal temperature of blue cheese was 58F-60F. Dressings were discarded at the end of lunch buffet service period (11a-3p). Discussed adequate ice bath for maintaining dressings at 41F/below or use of time control for dressings on lunch buffet.
2. Lite Ranch dressing in bottom of sandwich cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 56F and 58F. GM noted the dressing was out during lunch period. Dressing was discarded in trash. Labeling states "keep refrigerated". Keep the dressing in the cooler, get it out as needed, and immediately place the product back in the cooler for storage. Otherwise, get out a smaller portion and use time control for lunch/dinner hours (use/discard w/in 4hrs).

B) Container of cheese sauce being used to make pizzas was out at the pizza cooler upon arrival of inspector. Surface temperature of portion was at 59F. Staff stated it was out for ~45 minutes. Very small amount was left. Cheese sauce was discarded and replaced with fresh product.

Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be held at 41F/below at all times during storage, use and while on display. Maintain cold PHF at 41F/below or establish and adhere to a time control policy. If time control is used then foods must be used or discarded w/in 4hrs and cannot go back in cold storage after being out at ambient temperature for use.

C) Date marking of foods was inconsistent. Some products had day dots with dates written on them, and some foods just had day dots with the day of the week on them. Ham had a prep date, and sausage was observed without any date mark at all. Gm stated foods are supposed to be labeled with the date of discard on the day dots. Benefit of doubt was given for foods based on information provided. Foods were kept and dated for use. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous foods shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
**NOTE: The date marking system needs to be tweaked so it is clearly understood and done consistently the same by all staff. (see general comments)**

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - A) Bowl of croutons at lunch buffet was sitting outside of the covered, sneeze guard area of the buffet. The bowl was too large to fit within the designated area. GM discussed the use of smaller containers to allow for storage of product under covered, buffet area.

B) Pitchers of dressings and a pan of lettuce were uncovered in the reach-in salad cooler. Cover foods between uses/during storage.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods during slow periods and when products are not in use to protect items from potential contamination.
All foods on buffet/salad bar must be stored in designated area under overhead protection/sneeze guard.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 - A) Employee working cash register did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to slice pizza.

B) Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique.

Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed during inspection (educational handouts provided)
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changed, and prior to handling food, clean equipment or unwrapped single service items.

title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
comment:
750.650a - A) (R) Mold was observed inside the ice machine on the front and sides of the white baffle. The gash observed to have heavy mold accumulation during the previous inspection had slight mold buildup and still needed to be repaired. Other small pits were also observed. Clean and sanitize the baffle as needed. Make necessary repairs to eliminate gashes/pits. If repairs can not be made to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface then replace the baffle.

B) (R) Containers and lids were observed to be cracked and broken. Replace cracked/broken containers and lids.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
citation_text:
750.810 - Previously used, disposable wiping cloths were observed stored with spray bottles of sanitizer, orange force cleaner, and glass cleaner. Wiping cloths used with sanitizer musts be discarded after each use. Otherwise, wiping cloths must be stored in a bucket with sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms.

Throw away disposable wiping cloths after use or change to sani-bucket storage and store wet wiping cloths in solution between uses.
 Moist wiping cloths used for wiping general surfaces such as dining tables, counters, etc. must be cleaned and rinsed as specified in Section 750.810(b) and used for no other purpose. the cloths shall be stored in sanitize solution between uses.

title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
comment:
750.800b  - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) slicers - at pizza window (grease/food debris);   and
B) dish machine - inside doors (grease/debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. slicers, knives, can opener, etc.) must go through ware washing process up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
comment:
. 750.880 - A) (R) Toothpicks at sandwich cooler were observed with frilled and food contact surfaces intermixed in the storage box. Store toothpicks in a manner that will allow for only the frilled ends to be handled when being retrieved for use.

B) (R) Plastic utensils in storage tubs were observed with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. Store utensils all facing once direction so only handles will be touched when utensils are retrieved for use.

2. Storage containers for sauce cups and lids on top of sandwich cooler were soiled with dust and food debris.

D) 1. To go boxes at front counter were stored with the food contact surface up.
2. Sauce cups in container on top of sandwich cooler stored with the food contact surface up. 

E) Single use gloves were observed out and stored in a box with single use coffee packets. Leave gloves in the original box or in a clean, sealed food grade container.

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Keep single service covered in storage areas.

title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
citation_text:
750.1130(e) - Containers with stagnant, old moldy water was observed under plumbing at the 3 part sink and in the cabinet below the soda machine. Pans were emptied and cleaned during the inspection If leaks are present then have leaks properly repaired. Until leaks are repaired, empty and clean pans used to catch leaking water daily/as needed. Old, stagnant water is water and can serve as a food/water source for pests.

Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage.

title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

C) Floor under sandwich cooler was soiled with food/general debris.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.151 - Several foods were observed without date marks or with date marks that indicated products were past the 7 day time frame for use.
Foods included hotdogs in the dough cooler (no date on one bag; date of 10/26 on another bag); cheese sauce in the bottom of pizza cooler (no date on container or squeeze bottle); macaroni noodles in bottom of pizza cooler (no date on one container; date of 11/26 on another container). Foods were discarded in the trash.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous foods shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
**NOTE: some day dots had dates for discard and some did not. Other items had dates noted on bags with no day of the week indicated. The date marking system needs to be tweaked so it is clearly understood and done consistently the same by all staff.**

title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed

750.140 - (R) Ice cream chest freezer did not have a thermometer inside. Provide a thermometer for the freezer.
GM provided a thermometer during the inspection.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - Sealed packages of cheese sauce and pre-cooked macaroni noodles were observed in the basin of the 3 part sink. Closing manager stated items are pulled from the freezer and usually thawed in standing water. Manager was unsure as to how long items were thawing in the sink and stated they could have been in there since 11a. It was after 2p. Internal temperatures were checked. Noodles were at 39F-45F. Noodles were placed in a clean, covered container, dated, and put in a cooler for storage. Cheese sauce had internal temperature of 52F-55F. Cheese sauce was discarded in the trash. 
Do not thaw potentially hazardous foods in standing water or at ambient temperature for any reason. Preferable method of thawing is under refrigeration - plan ahead and place frozen foods in the walkin cooler to thaw overnight when possible.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

Gloves need to be worn in addition to handwashing when ready to eat foods are handled and will not be subject to cooking.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 - Diced tomatoes and shredded cheese on make line had surface temperatures of 53F/54F (tomatoes) and 60F (cheese). Internal temperatures for products were 37F/39F (tomatoes) and 49F-53F (cheese). Foods were placed out in iced holding area around 9a. Ice was not surrounding all sides of containers. More ice was added to the holding compartments. All products would be used or discarded by 1p. Use of time control for cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) on the make line was discussed with Store Manager. Also, staff were advised pans of lettuce do not have to be on ice, and other products that don't require cold holding for safety reasons could be repositioned to allow for better cold storage in iced compartments for pans of cheese and containers of tomatoes (bottom and all sides of containers to be surrounded by ice).

Cold PHF shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, unless a time control is used. If facility wishes to use time control, then a policy must be established. Time would have to be tracked for working supplies of PHF, and foods would have to be used or discarded w/in 4hrs. Foods can not go back in the cooler once they are out for use and foods can not be kept for use past 4hrs if time control is used (time control policy sheet provided).

Maintain cold PHF at 42F/below or establish and adhere to a time control policy for working supplies of foods.

Hands must only be washed at designated handsinks, and proper technique must always occur (use soap/running water, lather hands for 20sec, rinse hands, use paper towel to dry hands, and use paper towel as a barrier to shut off manual faucet to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands).

title: Sanitizing concentration
citation_text:

Store Manager emptied the sink, remade sanitizer solution (200ppm), and filled the basin to allow for proper emersion during sanitizing step of ware washing..
Proper sanitizing during ware washing was discussed.

An employee washed/rinsed the quesadilla slicer but did not leave it submerged in sanitizer solution for 60sec before setting aside to air dry. Proper sanitizing was discussed with the employee and management.

Items that can not be submerged may be cleaned and sanitized in place. Any items that fit in the 3 part sink must be washed, rinsed, and then sanitized via immersion for at least one minute.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
citation_text:

(Both products were prepared in the 11 o'clock hour this morning and had surface/internal temperatures below 70F).

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text:
750.120 & 153 - Foods were left out over lunch period and then placed back in the cooler after lunch rush. Surface and internal temperatures ranged from 53F to 70F. Foods included minced garlic (60F; bottom of prep cooler), red curry sauce (53F; 2 door cooler), and par-fried egg rolls (70F; fridge by fryers). All foods were discarded in the trash. Manager was once again advised on time control versus cold holding. Foods that are not temperature controlled and are out at ambient temperature during lunch and dinner rushes must either have time tracked and be discarded at the end of lunch and dinner or must be maintained at proper temperatures (cold foods 41f/below; hot foods 135F/above). Options for tracking time were discussed.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at proper product temperature at all times during storage (41F/below, or 135F/above) unless time control is used. If time control is used for working supplies of potentially hazardous foods, then a policy must be established for tracking time to ensure foods will be used/served or discarded in 4hrs or less. Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. 
**Establish and adhere to a time control policy if time control is going to be utilized. Track time using a dry erase board, stickers, or any other method that is easy for staff to understand.**

title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - Raw shrimp was observed in a bucket of water by the vegetable prep sink. Staff noted the shrimp were frozen and placed in the water to thaw. The internal temperature of shrimp was observed at 55F. Shrimp were placed in walkin cooler.
**Manager was advised potentially hazardous foods must never be thawed at ambient temperature in standing water. If cold running water is used, products must be placed in a cooler or used within 2hrs or less. Planning ahead and thawing foods in the walkin cooler or another functioning cooler holding at 41F/below is the best and safest way to thaw potentially hazardous foods.**

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text:
750.120 - A) Boxes with smoothie mix packets were observed on pieces of wood shelving in direct contact with the basement floor (no brackets present) adjacent to the water heater (same area where rice bags were stored during 4/21/15 inspection). Manager moved smoothie mix up off the floor.

B) Pieces of paper sugar bags were in use as a way to soak up grease from par-fried chicken in the walkin cooler and in the bottom of a tub used for rice noodle storage. Manager noted the inside surface of the bag is used for food contact. Manager was advised to have staff stop using pieces of sugar bags for soaking up grease. Use parchment paper or paper towels.

C) Salad seasoning was observed in a soiled disposable container with a plastic spoon down inside. Container, seasoning and plastic spoon were discarded. Store foods in clean containers, and do not store utensils inside foods.

D) Eggrolls were observed outside of packaging in direct contact with freezer door shelf. Store foods in clean containers, original packaging, or in a food grade storage material (i.e. plastic wrap, etc.).

E) Several seasonings and chopped nuts in kitchen were uncovered and not in use during slow period after lunch rush. Cover foods between uses during slow periods to protect products from potential contamination. Lids, plastic wrap, or aluminum foil are all acceptable options for covering containers.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Store foods up off the floor, covered/protected, and use food grade materials (i.e. paper towels, etc.) for direct contact with foods.

**Always change gloves between handling raw meats and before handling any ready to eat foods (no further cooking required).**

comment: 750-240 Observed two containers (one holding frozen carton eggs and one holding frozen packed sausage mix) to be thawing under a single stream of water. title: Foods properly cooled
citation_text:
750.140 - Pizza sauce in two door cooler prepared the previous operating day had surface and internal temperatures of 51F and 55F-56F. Sauce was in a 10gal plastic container. Sauce was discarded in the dumpster during the inspection. Owner noted the recipe requires hot water be used to prepare the sauce, so pre-chilling ingredients is not a valid option. Owner plans to use smaller pans for portioning sauce and allowing for more rapid cooling. Owner was advised to also utilize ice baths and stir the sauce frequently as well. Another option would be to portion in smaller pans and place cooling product uncovered on the top shelf in the walkin cooler or walkin freezer temporarily to help rapidly drop temperature. 

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/ w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs.
Any product prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature must be cooled to 41F/below w/in 4hrs. The only way to know foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in designated time frame is to use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor the temperature during the cooling process. Do not cool foods at room temperature.

Potentially hazardous foods were moved to prep cooler and walkin cooler for storage. Thermostat was adjusted to a colder setting, and the temperature began to drop in the unit. 
**Do not store any potentially hazardous foods in the Absocold fridge until it is holding below 41F and is able to maintain products at 41F/below. Keep the thermostat adjusted according to need and use to make sure the unit is cold enough to maintain food at proper temperature.**

title: Foods properly cooled
citation_text:
750.140 - Cheese sauce cooling in walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 84F and 95F. Sloppy joe mix, also in the walkin cooler, had surface and internal temperatures of 144F and 160F. Owner stated both products were held on the stove during lunch. Burner for cheese sauce was turned off approximately a half hour before the sloppy joe mix, and sloppy joe mix was turned off around 1:30-2p. Cheese sauce was left in the pan on the stove after burner was turned off. Temperatures were not checked prior to foods being placed in the walkin cooler. Time was not marked on the containers. Cheese sauce was discarded (cook stated it was heated and cooled a couple times already). Sloppy joe mix was placed in an ice bath to quick chill the product.
  
Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to check temperatures and ensure cooling foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in designated time frame. Do not place hot foods directly in coolers. Coolers are meant to hold cold food at 41F/below and not meant to cool hot foods. Utilize ice baths and separate foods into smaller portions to speed up the cooling process.
Use labels on containers or use the dry erase board in the kitchen to keep track of time during cooling process. Date and time must always be documented for cooling foods.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text:
750.130 - Pan of raw chicken breasts was observed on top of pans of raw beef and raw pork in a prep cooler on the make line. Raw foods were rearranged so raw chicken was not directly above raw beef and pork.

All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  All raw meat shall be properly stored in the order of cooking requirements. The meats that have the lowest temperature cooking requirement (seafood = 145F) must be stored above all other raw meats. Chicken has the highest temperature cooking requirement (165F) and must be stored below all other raw meats. Beef and pork may be stored on the same shelf below seafood but above chicken. Always store raw meats below and separate from ready to eat foods.

B) Ground chicken in walkin cooler was observed inside plastic grocery bags. Provide proper food grade storage bags or containers by next routine inspection.

C) Boxes of chicken were uncovered in the walkin freezer. Keep foods covered during storage. 

D) Eggrolls in freezer were uncovered. Plastic wrap was placed over the container. 

E) Extra stock pot of sugar water used for smoothie preparation was observed on the floor in the kitchen. Store foods up off the floor at least 6 inches, even if products are in a pot.

Properly store and protect foods at all times. Use proper food grade materials for food storage. Keep foods covered and up off the floor.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Cook handled a raw egg during cooking process and did not wash hands before continuing  with preparation (touching plates, preparing order). Manager had cook wash hands. Employee did not use proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a proper barrier after handwashing process was complete.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated, prior to handling food or clean equipment, and between tasks as needed. Always wash hands after handling raw eggs and raw meats. Proper handwashing involves the use of soap (rub hands vigorously for 20 seconds) and running water. Paper towels should be ready for use and should  be used to shut off the manual faucet after hands are dried to avoid potential recontamination of freshly washed hands.
Also, gloves are only meant for one use and must be discarded when they become torn, dirty, and/or their is an interruption in task.

title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
comment: 750-110g Multiple items are received from the Qik N EZ kitchen with a complete and proper intact label. There are muffins and cinnamon rolls that bear no labeling. title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
comment: 750-810b A number of wet wiping cloths were observed stored beneath the shelving on the counters. Manager indicated that staff likes to 'hide' the cloths under the shelving and then quickly grab,  wipe counters, and hide the cloths again. All the cloths were pulled from their 'hiding' places during the inspection. It is important to submerged cloths within sanitizing solution between uses in order to kill bacteria that grow on the warm, moist, and food-particle ridden cloths between uses. Provide a sanitizing solution bucket that will hold these cloths between uses. Store the buckets low and away from food storage (lower shelf within the cabinets). Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

Discussed using one of the numerous available plastic  soda pallets present in the back room. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
comment:
Observed facility to make their own sushi rice but has not provided a test kit to verify if sushi can be help at room temperature. Provide a pH test kit to test sushi rice. pH of sushi rice was be 4.6 or below to be allowed to store at room temperature. Until pH meter is provided, it is recommended that facility make sushi rice and store at room temperature for no longer than 4 hours once rice has been removed from 135F or above. If facility can not prove sushi rice is at a pH of 4.6 or below, do not hold below 135F longer than 4 hours. This violation should have been documented at a 3a. Until facility can prove with a pH meter that sushi rice is not potentially hazardous, it will be treated as so. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
comment:
[1] NO DATE MARKS:  Refrigerated, potentially hazardous foods found without date-marking:
(a) two containers of heavy whipping cream (prep cooler next to hand sink), 
(b) two pans of shredded cheese in prep cooler next to 3-pan sink, 
(c) package of tortillas, 
(d) small stack of American cheese in top portion of prep cooler next to 3-pan sink.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

[2] OUT OF TEMP:  
(a) Top portion of sandwich prep cooler appears to be maintaining temperatures ~48 degrees F, specifically two small stacks of Swiss cheese, one small stack of American cheese, and one small cup of mayonnaise.  CORRECTED - the three stacks of cheese and mayonnaise cup were immediately discarded.  Only bottom portion of this prep cooler should be used (where foods are ~36 - 38 degrees F) for potentially hazardous foods until staff can consistently confirm temperatures of 41 degrees or below.

(b) Foods within vertical stainless steel cooler was found with temperatures 44 - 55 degrees F.  CORRECTED - all out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded (see Voluntary Destruction Form).  Foods at proper cold-holding temperatures were moved to walk-in cooler.  Kitchen manager cleaned the fins on the unit (which had accumulated dust/dirt).  During inspection, cooler repairman came and added freon and checked for leaks.  Do not use cooler unless proper cold holding temperatures can be confirmed.

(c) While discussing fish and chicken breading, kitchen staff stated they believed breading had not been sifted in ~7 days.  Both containers of breading had fish/chicken debris and doughballs.  CORRECTED - Person In Charge (PIC) immediately, voluntarily, discarded both containers of breading.  Breading should be sifted at least every four hours.  See HACCP topic.

title: Wholesome, sound condition
citation_text: 750.100 - Moldy tomatoes were observed in a plastic storage tub at back prep area. Tomatoes were discarded in the trash during the inspection. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text: 750.120 (x4) - A) Pan of shredded cheese at prep cooler on cook line had an internal temperature of 55F. Cheese was double panned; pan holding cheese was not in contact with cold air in cooler. Cheese was discarded and replaced with fresh product. B) Top layers of individual half and halfs in the upper holding compartment of salad cooler had internal temperature 49F. Top layers were discarded by member of wait staff. Remaining packets (43F/below) were moved to top holding area, and packaged apple slices (not PHF) were placed in holding well below. **Do not over fill pans in upper holding compartment of salad cooler.** C) Container of blue cheese dressing sitting out by table mounted slicer by walkin cooler had internal temperature of 47F-48F. No staff took ownership for removing container from walkin cooler. Label on package stated "must be refrigerated at all times." Dressing was placed back in the walkin cooler by inspector. D) Three pans of steak burgers in the Blodgett brand oven at back prep had internal temperatures of 53F-60F. It appeared the oven was set to blow cooler air around the pans (possibly for thawing purposes). Manager discarded all burgers in the trash. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at 41F/bwlow at all times. Maintain PHF at proper holding temperatures.

title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
citation_text:
750.240 - A) Pans of raw steak burgers were thawing at room temperature on top of soda syrup boxes in storage area by walkin cooler. Three pans were also observed inside the Blodgett brand oven with cold air circulating around them. Steak burgers in the oven were discarded (see #3a Part D). Pans with other steak burgers (internal temperatures 35F-44F) were either moved to front line for use or placed in walkin cooler to finish properly thawing. PHF shall be properly thawed by one of the following: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.
B) Employee placed two large containers of vanilla ice cream in a bus tub on the floor in front of the sundae freezers. Employee noted she did so in order to soften the product. Employee and manager were advised ice cream must be placed in walkin cooler or another refrigeration unit to soften product before use. PHF must not be left out at room temperature to thaw for any reason and should never be stored in bus tubs on the floor.

title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
citation_text: 750.130 - (x2) A) Pans of raw steak burgers were thawing at room temperature sitting on top of soda syrup boxes in storage area by walkin cooler. Pans of burgers were moved to walkin cooler (see #6). B) Flat of raw eggs in walkin cooler was on a shelf above what appeared to be bags of commercially processed sauces. Eggs were moved to proper storage area. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination. Do not store raw eggs and meats next to, above, or on top of ready to eat foods.

title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
citation_text: 750.120 - A) Foods were uncovered in multiple coolers and freezers. Cover foods between uses, during slow periods, and during extended storage (walkin cooler, walkin freezer, etc.) to protect products from potential contamination. B) Bus tub with 2 large containers of vanilla ice cream was observed on the floor in front of sundae station freezers. Tub was moved to a proper cold holding unit. C) Cases of chili beans were observed on the floor at back prep area. Cases were placed in proper storage area. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the ground, in a clean covered container, and protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - Soufflé cups were observed used as serving utensils in containers of food on the make line and in pans of food in the walkin cooler. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use suitable utensils, such as scoops, spoons, tongs, gloves, etc. when handling and dispensing ready to eat foods.

title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
comment:
750.160b & 530a - A) HANDWASHING & GLOVE USE (x2) 1. Cook at grill was observed going between multiple orders and touching various foods and general surfaces with the same pair of gloves. When advised on proper glove use, cook changed gloves but did not wash hands. 2. Employee on food assembly line (at far end by drive thru) did not change gloves between handling a wet wiping cloth and returning to food prep/handling. Hands were being used for contact with multiple products. Employee was advised on proper use of gloves and changed gloves at request of inspector. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Employees shall properly wash their hands before putting on gloves, between glove changes, prior to handling food or clean equipment, and any time hands may have been contaminated.
B) Employee working in dish area was observed eating. Employee moved plate of food to break area and stopped eating in the dish area. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
comment: 750.530b - Personal drink without a lid or straw was observed on the bread storage shelf in the back prep area. Cup was discarded in the trash by inspector. Employees may drink from closed beverage containers with a lid and straw as long as the containers are handled to prevent contamination of hands, containers, and exposed food.

title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms between uses. If spray bottles of sanitizer are used for wiping surfaces, then disposable paper towels must be used and discarded after each use.

title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
citation_text: 750.1120 - A) Evidence of handsinks being used to rinse food utensils was observed. Upon arrival of inspector a spatula with food debris on it was noted in the back handsink. A whisk was observed in the handsink at the front counter. Food utensils were removed from sinks and placed in dish area to go through proper ware washing. B) Employee was observed emptying a chemical bottle in the back handsink. Employee took bottle to dish area to finish emptying bottle per request of inspector. Management and staff were once again advised on proper use of handsinks. Handsinks are to be used for handwashing only and must always be accessible. Handsinks are not to be used for rinsing utensils, emptying chemical bottles, filling pitchers with water, or any other tasks. The only time a handsink should ever be unaccessible is when someone is waiting to wash his/her hands because another person is already in the process of properly washing their hands.

title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
citation_text: 750.1300 (x2) A) Several chemical bottles were mislabeled or did not have a label. Bottles labeled Multi Quat had what appeared to be Power Force and other chemicals inside. A bottle labeled Power Force in the Commissary walkin cooler had a bleach solution in it (tested over 200ppm). Contents were discarded. A bottle of Multi Quat solution did not have a label. Maintain proper labels on containers of toxic materials. B) Bleach solution used for cleaning inside Commissary walkin cooler tested over 200ppm chlorine (test strip turned very dark purple to black in color). Chemical was discarded. Chemicals must not be used in any way that may contaminate food and surfaces, nor in any way that may pose a hazard to people. Use chemicals properly, and use test strips to verify concentrations of bleach and quat solutions are correct.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
comment:
Upon start of inspection, deli manager stated that hot holding for fried chicken, fried fish, etc. has not been working, and staff has been changing out food every hour or so.  While staff appear to be taking temperatures and recording them on clipboard every hour, the time the food was taken out of proper cooking is not recorded.  It appears staff is attempting to memorize the times for all the foods.  Deli manager says that proper cooking temperature is confirmed before food is taken for hot holding.  Also, hot holding cabinet in back kitchen does not appear to be holding all foods >135 degrees F.  CORRECTED - 2nd shift deli manager immediately drew a map of the hot holding and recorded the times that each food was taken from cooking equipment.  She also labeled the pan of fried chicken in the back kitchen hot holding cabinet.  Time as a Control was thoroughly discussed with both deli managers, and store manager, and a policy form was left with deli manager.
750-153(a) When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

750.130 & 140 - A) Seasoning shakers and squeeze bottles of liquids in cooking and prep areas were not labeled. title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text: 750.120 - Shredded cheese and cheese slices in top holding areas of pizza cooler and large prep cooler had internal temperatures of 50F. Containers holding products were sitting on top edges of other containers and were not down in contact with cold air. Both products were discarded in the trash. Employees were advised on cold holding and proper storage in upper holding areas of prep coolers. Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage.

title: Foods properly cooled
citation_text: 750.140 - A) Pot roast portioned in plastic baggies and stored in a large plastic container in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 84F-96F. Date on label was 10/24, but no time was indicated. Owner verified the pot roast was pulled from oven at ~1:30-2p. Temperature was checked around 2:30p. Owner was allowed to keep pot roast, and portions were placed on a backing sheet in the walkin freezer to help rapidly drop the temperature.  B) Four pans of cheese sauce with prep date 10/24 stacked together in walkin cooler had surface temperatures at 40F-45F. Internal temperatures for cheese sauce in the middle two containers were at 49F and 54F. Cheese sauce in bottom container had internal temperature of 47, and cheese sauce in top container had internal temperature of 41F-42F. Cheese sauce above 42F was discarded in the trash by owner. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Allow heat to vent off of cooling foods and do not store hot products stacked together in pans or in baggies when foods are still hot. Utilize ice baths, the walkin freezer, and ice wands to help rapidly cool cooked foods.

title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine. If food debris and/or other soil remains after process has been completed then repeat the aforementioned steps as many times as necessary to remove soil and properly clean/sanitize all surfaces.
