title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
citation_text: 750.130 - A) (R) Squeeze bottles of water next to gyro rotisserie did not have a label. B) (R) Containers used for bulk powder storage were not labeled. C) (R) Seasoning shakers were not labeled. Label all storage containers, squeeze bottles, & seasoning shakers, especially clear and white liquids and powders. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar, flour, etc. not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
citation_text: 750.120 & 151 - A) (R) Hotdogs in a plastic container, open packages of cooked turkey bacon, and open package of polish sausage were not date marked. Hotdogs were discarded in the trash. Turkey bacon and polish sausages appeared to have been opened more recently. Benefit of doubt was given and dates were placed on bacon and polish sausages. Refrigerated potentially hazardous food (PHF) shall be clearly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded within 7 days. Properly date all ready to eat, PHF and use or discard products in 7 days. B) Can of cheese sauce just opened around 10:30a today was sitting on the grill by the gyro rotisserie. Surface temp was 86F and internal temp was 82F. Label says refrigerate after opening. Can of cheese sauce was placed in 3 door cooler. Temperature began to drop during inspection. Store cold PHF at 41F/below. When labels stated refrigerate after opening for ready to eat canned foods they must reach 41F/below within 4 hrs. C) Three portion cups of ranch dressing by drive thru window had temp of 81F. Cups of ranch were discarded. Keep ranch dressing at 41F/below or use time control and use/discard w/in 4hrs. D) Blue Bunny freezer by front counter was jam packed with bags of frozen french fries. Some bags on top right side were thawed or beginning to thaw. Surface temp was +50F. Internal temps ranged from 30F/below to mid-30F range and up to 49F. Two bags were pulled to be discarded due to internal temps being at 43F-49F. Bags of fries further down and on top left side were at proper temperature. Fries from the right side that were still frozen were moved to another freezer. Fries partially thawed but still below 41F were placed in cooler to be cooked for the first orders of the day. Maintain frozen foods frozen. Do not overfill freezers to allow for better air flow.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
citation_text: 750.120 - A) Gyro meat on rotisserie was 56F/57F. Meat already cooked was sliced off and time control was being used for meat in a pan. However, meat on rotisserie needs to stay at 135F/above. Discussed proper cooking and hot holding of gyro meat with Manager, and provided a Technical Information Bulletin from IDPH regarding gyro meat. Rotisserie was turned to higher temperature to heat meat and slice as needed. B) Fries under heat lamp were at 82F. Heat lamp was turned on and fries were discarded in the trash. Maintain hot PHF at 135F/above after product has been cooked/reheated to proper temperatures.

title: Hot food at proper temperatures
comment: (A) Corn dogs and cheesy buffalo ranch sticks were found at front counter warmer at temperatures 97 - 116 degrees F (REPEAT).  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - these foods were made at 8:30.  Manager states they are normally discarded during noon hour, and that the facility's routine is to make these foods and discard them three times a day. title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
comment:

It does not have an temperature adjustment knob.  Manager states it appears it is not functioning and has called for service on machine. Do not use machine if food cannot be maintained at 135 degrees F or greater.
750-150 All hot storage units used for potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain product at 140°F or above at all times.
